parity-metronoid-first-moment-repacking.statement:
Let \(r,d\ge1\), let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^r\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, let \(a_z=|C_z|_d\), and fix a parity class \(\epsilon\in(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^r\) with \(M_\epsilon:=\sum_{z\equiv\epsilon}a_z>0\). For \(c\in\mathbb Z^r\), set
\[
S_c^\epsilon:=\sum_{z\equiv\epsilon}a_za_{2c-z},\qquad
b_c^\epsilon:=S_c^\epsilon/M_\epsilon.
\]
For \(S_c^\epsilon>0\), let \(g_z\) be the centroid of every positive-volume contributing fiber and set
\[
q_c^\epsilon:=\frac1{S_c^\epsilon}\sum_{z\equiv\epsilon}a_za_{2c-z}\frac{g_z+g_{2c-z}}2.
\]
Prove
\[
q_c^\epsilon\in\mathsf M_{b_c^\epsilon}(C_c),\qquad
\sum_cb_c^\epsilon=M_\epsilon.
\]
Consequently the atomic graph measure
\[
\beta_\epsilon:=\sum_{c:S_c^\epsilon>0}b_c^\epsilon\delta_{(c,q_c^\epsilon)}
\]
has mass \(M_\epsilon\) and every ambient closed halfspace \(H\) satisfies
\[
\mu_C(H)\ge\gamma_d\beta_\epsilon(H).
\]

parity-midpoint-domination.statement:
For the mixed-volume measure \(\mu\) of a convex body \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}\), prove a compact parity-midpoint halfspace-domination theorem containing both of the following constructions.

First, for every positive finite Borel measure \(\rho\) carried by \(C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\), average independent same-parity midpoints over all parity classes with the normalization that gives total mass \(|\rho|/2\). Prove that the resulting measure is carried by the same mixed-integer set, is dominated by \(\rho\) on every closed halfspace, and has the same normalized barycenter.

Second, for the original mixed-volume measure, form the unnormalized ordered off-diagonal same-parity midpoint measure \(\eta^\circ\). Prove its exact mass
\[
Q^\circ=\sum_rW_r^2-\sum_z w_z^2
\ge 2^{-n}W^2-MW,
\qquad M:=\max_z w_z,
\]
and the transfer inequality
\[
\eta^\circ(H)\le2W\mu(H)
\]
for every closed halfspace \(H\). State the heavy-fiber alternative and the exact conditional implication from a \(\kappa\)-deep point of \(\eta^\circ\) to a \((\kappa/4)2^{-n}W\) mixed-depth point under \(M<2^{-n-1}W\).

parity-single-level-concentration.relation_to_goal:
For a convex body \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}\), the fiber-volume root
\(g(z)=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z)^{1/d}\) is concave on the compact base
projection and
\[
W=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}g(z)^d
\]
is its total mixed-integer volume.  The registered inequality therefore
selects one positive root-volume level carrying at least
\(2^{-n-1}W\) in the product ``level height times lattice count.''  This
has the correct \(2^{-n}\) scale up to one absolute factor and replaces the
unproved dyadic/thick-thin layer selection in the attachment.

The lemma does not itself produce a point of mixed halfspace depth.  A later
step must convert the selected lattice-convex level set into one compatible
affine, simplex, or symmetric-box fiber-depth certificate.  In base
dimension two, a constant-fraction lattice-triangle extraction is a
candidate terminal bridge; in arbitrary dimension that extraction remains
open.  Thus this subgoal is a non-final structural dependency and must have
\(\texttt{target_match: null}\).
parity-single-level-concentration.statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a
nonempty compact convex set, and let \(g:P\to[0,\infty)\) be concave.
Put
\[
D:=P\cap\mathbb Z^n,
\qquad
W:=\sum_{z\in D}g(z)^d,
\]
and assume \(W>0\).  For \(s>0\), define
\[
N(s):=\#\{z\in D:g(z)\ge s\},
\qquad
M:=\max_{s>0}s^dN(s).
\]
Prove
\[
M\ge 2^{-n-1}W.
\]

partial-affine-section-depth-lift.statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}\) be a convex body of positive mixed mass, write \(C_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}\), and let \(\delta_C(z,x)\) denote absolute halfspace depth in the fiber \(C_z\). For an affine map \(s:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^d\), define
\[
q_s(z):=
\begin{cases}
\delta_C(z,s(z)),&(z,s(z))\in C,\\
0,&(z,s(z))\notin C,
\end{cases}
\qquad Q_C(s):=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}q_s(z).
\]
Prove that, whenever \(Q_C(s)>0\), there is \(z^\star\in\mathbb Z^n\) with \((z^\star,s(z^\star))\in C\) and
\[
h_{C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)}(z^\star,s(z^\star))
\ge 2^{-n}Q_C(s).
\]
Deduce
\[
\max_{p\in C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)}h_S(p)
\ge 2^{-n}\sup_{s\text{ affine}}Q_C(s).
\]
As a folded corollary for \(n=1\), prove the stronger bound
\[
\max_{p\in S}h_S(p)
\ge \frac18\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z}M(z)
\ge \frac{\gamma_d}{8}W,
\qquad
\gamma_d=\left(\frac d{d+1}\right)^d,
\]

partial-symmetry-compression-certificate.relation_to_goal:
This is a new partial-symmetry certificate, not a proposed universal
completion.

The first assertion synchronizes all same-parity scalar pair products at
one integer midpoint with exactly one \(2^{-n}\) factor.  Accepted fact
`aca624dd8874e5a5` instead constructs the full parity-autocorrelation
measure and proves target-fiber capacity; it does not select one midpoint
with the displayed \(A_m/w_m\) ratio.

The second assertion converts geometric overlap after an affine shear and
one unimodular fundamental-cell erosion directly into mixed depth.  Its
loss is the absolute factor \(1/(2e)\), independent of \(n,d,C\).  It is
different from accepted large-projection erosion fact
`0790372855abe672` and affine-selector facts `bb2b5f9519ae23e8` and
`b220933817d23295`: no large projection and no affine selector on the
lattice fibers is assumed.

The next missing implication would be quantitatively explicit.  If one
could prove, under failure of every dyadically heavy primitive slice,
\[
\mathfrak P(C)\geq\eta\,2^{-n}W
\]
for an absolute \(\eta>0\), then the present certificate would give
\[
\sup_{p\in S}h_S(p)\geq\frac{\eta}{2e}\,2^{-n}W.
\]
The complementary slice branch would retain the exact original-mass
threshold through accepted rank-drop fact `314b32bda8a0b01e`.  No such
universal lower bound for \(\mathfrak P(C)\) is asserted here.

Thus the accepted output would isolate the first unsupported step as the
passage from discrete autocorrelation or absence of a heavy primitive
slice to positive sheared eroded pair volume.  It does not restate or
close the locked target.
partial-symmetry-compression-certificate.statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, and write
\[
C_z:=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:(z,x)\in C\},\qquad
w_z:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z),\qquad
W:=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}w_z>0,
\]
\[
S:=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d).
\]
For \(m\in\mathbb Z^n\), define
\[
A_m:=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}w_z\,w_{2m-z}.
\]

Prove the following two assertions.

1. There is \(m\in\mathbb Z^n\) such that
\[
A_m\geq 2^{-n}Ww_m.
\]
In particular, the selected midpoint has \(w_m>0\).

2. Fix arbitrary
\[
L\in\mathbb R^{d\times n},\qquad
m\in\mathbb Z^n,\qquad
U\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb Z).
\]
Let
\[
T_L(z,x):=(z,x-Lz),\qquad K:=T_L(C),
\]
\[
D_{L,m}:=
\{(v,y):(m+v,y)\in K,\ (m-v,y)\in K\},
\]
\[
Q_U:=U[-1/2,1/2]^n,
\]
and define the base-direction inner erosion
\[
D^-_{L,m,U}:=
\{(v,y):(v+q,y)\in D_{L,m}\text{ for every }q\in Q_U\}.
\]
Put
\[
V_{L,m,U}:=\operatorname{vol}_{n+d}(D^-_{L,m,U}).
\]
If \(V_{L,m,U}>0\), there is a point
\[
p\in C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)
\]
such that
\[
h_S(p)\geq\frac{1}{2e}V_{L,m,U}.
\]
The conclusion must hold for every closed ambient halfspace containing
\(p\), including vertical halfspaces and halfspaces whose boundary carries
positive mixed mass.

Consequently, if
\[
\mathfrak P(C):=
\sup_{\substack{
L\in\mathbb R^{d\times n},\ m\in\mathbb Z^n\\
U\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb Z)}}
V_{L,m,U},
\]
then
\[
\sup_{p\in S}h_S(p)\geq\frac{1}{2e}\mathfrak P(C).
\]

partial-symmetry-rank-drop-dichotomy.statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, put
\[
w_z:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z),\qquad
W:=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}w_z>0,
\]
and define \(\mathfrak P(C)\) exactly as in accepted fact
`6a9b0f7ac15a23be`: it is the supremum, over real shears \(L\), integer
midpoints \(m\), and \(U\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb Z)\), of the
\((n+d)\)-volume of the corresponding symmetric pair body eroded in the
base directions by \(U[-1/2,1/2]^n\).

Prove or disprove that there is an absolute constant \(\eta>0\) such that
every such \(C\) satisfies at least one of:

1. there are \(1\leq r\leq n\), a primitive rank-\((n-r)\) sublattice
   \(L_0\leq\mathbb Z^n\), and \(a\in\mathbb Z^n\) for which
   \[
   \sum_{z\in a+L_0}w_z\geq2^{-r}W;
   \]
2. one has
   \[
   \mathfrak P(C)\geq\eta\,2^{-n}W.
   \]

The quantifiers over the shear, midpoint, and unimodular cell inside
\(\mathfrak P\) are unchanged from accepted fact `6a9b0f7ac15a23be`.

phase-deficit-cap-transfer.relation_to_goal:
This abstracts the lossless cap injection underlying accepted large-box fact
`0790372855abe672`. The signed deficit records precisely how far a general
convex body is from the phase-core property. The theorem is useful beyond a
projection box and is not implied by the large-box conclusion, but it is only
a sufficient structural interface and does not settle the locked target.
phase-deficit-cap-transfer.statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), \(m=n+d\), let
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}\) be a convex body, let
\(\mathbf q_0=(\mathbf b,\mathbf v_0)\in C\), and let \(0<\alpha<1\). Put
\[
D=(1-\alpha)C+\alpha\mathbf q_0,\qquad
\mathbf p=(1-\alpha)\mathfrak c(C)+\alpha\mathbf q_0,
\]
and assume \(\mathbf p\in\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d\). For
\(\mathbf t\in[0,1)^n\), define the compact phase-anchor set
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathbf t}
=C\cap\left[
\left(\mathbf b+\alpha^{-1}(\mathbb Z^n-\mathbf t)\right)
\times\mathbb R^d
\right].
\]
For an affine functional \(L\) on \(\mathbb R^{n+d}\), define the signed
phase deficit
\[
\Delta_L(\mathbf t)
=L(\mathbf q_0)-\max_{\mathbf q\in\mathcal A_{\mathbf t}}L(\mathbf q),
\]
with \(\Delta_L(\mathbf t)=+\infty\) when
\(\mathcal A_{\mathbf t}=\varnothing\).

Prove the exact cap-transfer inequality
\[
\mu(C\cap\{L\ge0\})
\ge
\operatorname{vol}_m\left\{
\mathbf w\in D:
L(\mathbf w)\ge
\alpha\Delta_L(\{\mathbf w_I\})
\right\},
\]
where \(\{\mathbf w_I\}\in[0,1)^n\) is the canonical fractional part of
the base coordinate and \(\mu\) is mixed-integer volume.

As a corollary, if
\[
\mathbf q_0\in\operatorname{conv}\mathcal A_{\mathbf t}
\quad\text{for every }\mathbf t\in[0,1)^n,
\]
then every closed halfspace \(H\) containing \(\mathbf p\) satisfies
\[
\mu(C\cap H)\ge
\operatorname{vol}_m(D\cap H)
\ge
\left(\frac m{m+1}\right)^m
(1-\alpha)^m\operatorname{vol}_m(C).
\]
Treat empty anchor phases, maximizing-anchor measurability, closed boundaries,
and the distinction between the actual mixed-integer image and its thickened
cell explicitly.

pk-intake-absent-planar-corner-positive-.statement:
Let $A,K,B$ be full-dimensional planar convex bodies with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$, let $v_i+v_j+v_k=0$ be nonzero spanning normals, and let $B\subseteq\bigcap_l\{v_l\cdot x\le1\}$. Write $R_l(A)=A\cap\bigcap_{h\ne l}\{v_h\cdot x<-1\}$, $U_l=|A\cap\{v_l\cdot x\ge-1\}|$, $a=|A|$, $b=|B|$, and $k_0=|K|$. Suppose $R_i(A)=\varnothing$ and choose $P_j\in R_j(A)$ and $P_k\in R_k(A)$. Put $P=[P_j,P_k]$, $w=P_k-P_j$, $G=\{v_j\cdot x<0\}\cup\{v_k\cdot x<0\}$ and
$$
\eta_j=-\max_{x\in P_j+B}v_k\cdot x>0,\quad
\delta=\min(1/2,\eta_j/(2v_k\cdot w))>0,\quad
J_B(w)=\|w\|\mathcal H_1(\operatorname{proj}_{w^\perp}B)>0.
$$
Then $|(P+B)\cap G|\ge2b+\delta J_B(w)$ and $4|K\cap G|\ge2b+\delta J_B(w)+2a-U_j-U_k$. If $A,K,B$ are the actual fibers at $-1,0,1$ and all the caps $v_l\cdot x-z\ge0$ have raw area $Q$ summed over these three fibers, the middle residual $r_i^K=|K\cap\{v_j\cdot x<0,\ v_k\cdot x<0\}|$ satisfies
$$4r_i^K\le8k_0-8Q+5(U_j+U_k)-2a-2b-\delta J_B(w).$$

pk-intake-actual-affine-root-step-budget.statement:
Put $d=6$, $r=6/7$, $\gamma=r^6$, $I=\{0,\ldots,9\}$, and $i=8$. There are positive affine arrays $(a_j)_{j\in I}$ and $(v_j)_{j\in I}$ with $0<a_j<v_j$, $v_i=1$, $a_i=r$, and $\sum_j(j-i)a_j^5=0$. Writing $B=\sum_j a_j^6$ and $M=\sum_jv_j^6$, they satisfy
$$
B\le r^6+\sum_{j<i}v_j^6,\qquad
B\le r^6+\sum_{j>i}v_j^6,\qquad
B\ge\gamma\max_j v_j^6,
$$
yet $M>2B/\gamma$.

These data occur on the ten actual fibers $v_j T$ of a full-dimensional body in $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^6$, where $T$ is a volume-one simplex centered at zero. At $(i,0)$ the realizing cap captures $a_j^6$ on each fiber, has ordinary own-fiber mass $\gamma$, and is a global minimum among all caps through $(i,0)$ with its fixed nonzero continuous normal and arbitrary real base coefficient. The two step budgets are realized by finite base coefficients in this same cap family. The actual point $(6,0)$ has raw mixed depth at least $\gamma M/2>B$.

pk-intake-actual-aligned-outer-simplex-s.statement:
Let $v_1,\ldots,v_{d+1}$ span $\mathbb R^d$ and sum to zero, $d\ge1$, and set $T=\{x:v_i\cdot x\le1\ \forall i\}$ and $\kappa_d=|T\cap(-T)|/|T|$. Suppose $A,K,B$ are full-dimensional convex bodies, $B\subseteq T$, $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$, and each $v_i\cdot x=-1$ meets $\operatorname{int}A$. Let $K_{\rm out}=\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge-h_K(-v_i)\ \forall i\}$, and write $a=|A|$, $b=|B|$, $k=|K|$. Then $b<\kappa_d|K_{\rm out}|$. If $a<b/32$ and $k\le a+b$, then
$
\frac{k}{|K_{\rm out}|}<\frac{33}{32}\kappa_d .
$
For $d=2$ this is the strict bound $11/16$.

pk-intake-actual-balanced-moment-centroi.statement:

For the base marginal, $j=0$ is the unique integer point of raw closed-halfspace depth at least $M/2$, and its marginal depth is $D_0=11/10$.

For $t>0$, let $M_t(0)$ consist of the continuous centroids of all submeasures dominated by the mixed-length measure, of mass $t$ and with base centroid zero. The feasible masses are $0<t\le6/5$. With $A=t(1-t)/2$ and $I_t=[\max(0,(t-1)/2),\min(1/10,t/2)]$, put
$$
F_+(t)=\max_{\ell\in I_t}\{(2t-17/20)\ell-3\ell^2\},\qquad
F_-(t)=\max_{\ell\in I_t}\{2t\ell-3\ell^2\}.
$$
Then $M_t(0)=[-(A+F_-(t))/t,(A+F_+(t))/t]$. Its interval centroid $y(t)$ equals
$$
\begin{cases}
-t/6,&0<t\le3/10,\\
-1/10+3/(200t),&3/10\le t\le17/40,\\
t/6-29/120+433/(9600t),&17/40\le t\le29/40,\\
-17/(400t),&29/40\le t\le6/5.
\end{cases}
$$
For every $y\in[-17/80,0]$, including every $y(t)$, the raw mixed depth at $(0,y)$ is $3/5+y$. Consequently $y(t)$ fails the sharp budget $M/4$ exactly for $2/5<t<(43+3\sqrt{13})/80$, with equality at the two endpoints. In particular at the prescribed $t=D_0/2=11/20$, the interval is $[-163/440,619/2640]$ and its centroid is $-359/5280$. The closed ambient cap $x\le -359/5280-(707/1056)z$ attains this point's raw depth $2809/5280$, below $M/4$ by $29/5280$.

pk-intake-actual-box-full-target-density.relation_to_goal: An exact family of compatible interval and full-dimensional box witnesses for a particular midpoint-density centroid selector. The normalized actual upper bounds are at the selected point, and a separate reflected point is safe.
pk-intake-actual-box-full-target-density.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $0<a<1$, $Q=[0,1]^{d-1}$ and $k=(3-a)/4$. For $d=1$ the transverse box is a point with unit counting mass. Take fibers
$$
A=[k-a/2,k+a/2]\times Q,\quad B=[0,1]\times Q,\quad
C=[k-1/2,k+1/2]\times Q
$$
at bases $-1,0,1$ of their lifted convex hull, with total mixed volume $M=2+a$. These are its exact positive integer fibers, each smaller than $M/2$. Put $s_d=((a^{1/d}+1)/2)^d$. The mass-$a$ midpoint measure $\eta$ of an explicit uniform-marginal coupling has density $(2a/(1+a))\mathbf1_{(A+C)/2}$ bounded above by $(a/s_d)\mathbf1_B$. This upper bound on the density coefficient is attained for $d=1$.

The centroid $g$ of $\mathbf1_B\,dx+[(1+a)/a]\eta$ is independent of the uniform-marginal coupling. Its first coordinate is $g_a=(5+2a-a^2)/(4(2+a))$ and all others are $1/2$. At the closed ambient halfspace $H=\{(z,x):x_1-z\ge g_a\}$ through $(0,g)$ with middle trace $H_0$, the normalized original mass and the raw auxiliary cost are
$$
\frac{\mu(H)}M=\frac{5a^2+10a+3}{4(2+a)^2},\qquad
|B\cap H_0|+\eta(H_0)=(1-g_a)(1+2a/(1+a)).
$$
Writing $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, both the original cap mass and the auxiliary cost are strictly below $\Gamma_dM/2$ for $(d,a)=(1,1/10)$ and $(2,1/100)$. In dimension one the deficits are $3/70$ and $113/1540$ respectively, and the actual endpoint pairing slack is $47/1540$. In dimension two the normalized actual deficit is $4907/161604$.

pk-intake-actual-centroid-graph-face-tra.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional Euclidean space and $P\subset E$ a nonempty finite set. For $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body, where $d\ge1$, and write $w_z=|K_z|_d>0$ and $g_z$ for its volume centroid. Let $M=\sum_{z\in P}w_z$ and $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Give the graph $T=\{(z,g_z):z\in P\}$ the atomic weights $w_z$, and write $w(F)=\sum_{(z,g_z)\in T\cap F}w_z$. The measured family has raw cap mass $\mu(H)=\sum_{z\in P}|\{x\in K_z:(z,x)\in H\}|_d$.

Fix $0<\alpha\le M$ and $y=(p,g_p)\in T$ such that every closed ambient halfspace containing $y$ has atomic weight at least $\alpha$. Let $F$ be the minimal face of $\operatorname{conv}T$ containing $y$, allowing the whole hull. Then the raw halfspace depth $h_\mu(y)=\inf_{H\ni y}\mu(H)$ is at least $\gamma_d\alpha$. Equality implies $w(F)=\alpha$ and the existence of a single unit $u\in\mathbb R^d$ satisfying
$$
|K_z\cap\{x:u\cdot(x-g_z)\ge0\}|_d=\gamma_d w_z
\qquad\text{for every }(z,g_z)\in F\cap T.
$$
In particular, $w(F)>\alpha$ implies $h_\mu(y)>\gamma_d\alpha$.

If $g_z=G(z)$ for a single affine map $G:E\to\mathbb R^d$, these two conditions also imply equality and a through-$y$ closed halfspace attains it. In this case the atomic center assumption is equivalent to weighted closed base depth at least $\alpha$ at $p$, and $F$ projects to the minimal face of $\operatorname{conv}P$ containing $p$.

pk-intake-actual-centroid-hull-contracti.relation_to_goal: Compatible finite-fiber deformation and a response identity conditional on a specified actual marked surface coupling.
pk-intake-actual-centroid-hull-contracti.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty. Let positive convex fibers $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be the exact sampled fibers of their canonical hull $C$, and let $g_z$ be their volume centroids. Put $D=\operatorname{conv}\{(z,g_z):z\in P\}$ and $D_z=\{X:(z,X)\in D\}$. For $0\le t<1$ the fibers $K_z(t)=(1-t)K_z+tD_z$ are positive, nested and exact in their canonical hull. They contain $g_z+(1-t)(K_z-g_z)$. At a surface-almost-everywhere regular old point $X$ of outward unit normal $n_z$, their inward normal speed is $v_z(X)=h_{K_z}(n_z)-h_{D_z}(n_z)$. The first total volume loss is $\sum_z\int v_z\,dS$. For a fixed ambient cap whose cuts are proper or strictly full or empty in every fiber, its first volume loss is $\sum_z\int \mathbf1_{\rm cap}v_z\,dS$, with endpoint counting measure when $d=1$.

Let $\Xi_z$ be an integrable signed density on this old boundary. Put $F_z=\int_{\partial K_z}\Xi_z n_z\,dS$ and $R_z(u)=h_{D_z}(u)-u\cdot g_z$. If $\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}\Xi_z n_z\cdot X\,dS=0$, then
$$
\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}\Xi_z v_z\,dS
=-\sum_z g_z\cdot F_z-\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}\Xi_z R_z(n_z)\,dS .
$$
If the Jordan surface marginals $\Xi_+dS$ and $\Xi_-dS$ on the actual marked normal graph admit a full physical martingale preserving the normal, the response is exactly $-J_D\le0$, where
$$
J_D=\int [h_{D_z}(u)-\mathbb E(h_{D_{Z'}}(u)\mid z,X,u)]\,d(\Xi_+dS)(z,X,u).
$$
Equality holds exactly when the roof Jensen defect vanishes in almost every positive row. For each such row, its output bases lie in a contact cell of an active affine upper plane of the centroid roof. The force formula and this sign give $\sum_z\int\Xi_z R_z(n_z)\,dS=J_D-\sum_z g_z\cdot F_z$.

pk-intake-actual-circumscribed-planar-mi.statement:
Use the actual planar three-fiber critical family of the marked-depth theorem, with arbitrary middle body $K$, total mass $M$, marked raw depth $Q$, and canonical normals $v_i$. Let $\overline K=\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge-h_K(-v_i)\ \forall i\}$, let $m=\sum_i h_B(-v_i)/3$, and set $f(m)=|T\cap(-mT)|/|T|$ for $T=\{x:v_i\cdot x\le1\ \forall i\}$. If $Q\le2M/9$, then
$$
\frac{|K|}{|\overline K|}<\frac{36f(m)}{7(m+1)^2}\le\frac67.
$$

pk-intake-actual-cone-cap-tilt-polynomia.relation_to_goal: Local tilt cell with real base-normal coefficients and a fixed unit continuous normal. The polygon pair isolates failure of the proposed weaker hypothesis.
pk-intake-actual-cone-cap-tilt-polynomia.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $C$ be a convex body with finitely many positive full-dimensional integer fibers $C_z$, $z\in P$, and let $z_0\in P$. Fix a unit continuous normal $u$ and a through-point cap with base coefficient $b$ and thresholds $t_z=u\cdot x_0-b\cdot(z-z_0)$. Suppose on an open interval $I_z$ about each $t_z$ the actual upper cap on $C_z$ is a cone cap whose positive $d$th volume root is $(u\cdot p_z-s)/h$ at threshold $s$, for fixed apex $p_z$ and common $h>0$. Write $a_z$ for the root at $s=t_z$ and assume $\sum_z a_z^{d-1}(z-z_0)=0$. For every $\delta b$ such that $t_z-\delta b\cdot(z-z_0)\in I_z$ for every $z$, the raw cap mass is
$$
M(b+\delta b)=\sum_z[a_z+h^{-1}\delta b\cdot(z-z_0)]^d.
$$
Its increment is $\sum_{k=2}^d\binom dk h^{-k}\sum_z a_z^{d-k}[\delta b\cdot(z-z_0)]^k$. The original cap is a strict local minimizer in every nonzero effective base-tilt direction in $\operatorname{span}(P-z_0)$. Single-cut homothety and fixed-normal tilt criticality alone do not imply this formula.

pk-intake-actual-convex-profile-logarith.relation_to_goal: Actual ordinary volume and exact contact rows on changing convex bodies. The example has no physical cap stress and its explicit two-plane marks fail ordinary deepestness.
pk-intake-actual-convex-profile-logarith.statement:
Let $F\subset\mathbb R^m$ be a full-dimensional compact convex polytope, $m\ge1$, and let $A\ge H>0$ be convex finite piecewise-affine functions on $F$. Write $t=x+y$ and take
$$
K_j=\{(s,x,y):s\in F,\ x,y\ge0,\ A(s)/j\le t\le1\},\qquad
L_j=c_j(t-H(s)/j+e^{-j}),
$$
where $c_j$ gives volume-mean logarithm zero. The positive parameters are concave finite piecewise affine. The bodies converge to $K=F\times\{x,y\ge0,\ x+y\le1\}$, $M_j=|K_j|\to M=|F|/2$, and $L_j\to ct$ uniformly in affine presentation, where $c=e^{1/2}$. Put $E=\{A=H\}$ and $n_0=(0,\ldots,0,-1,-1)/\sqrt2$. The weak limit of $dX|_{K_j}/(M_jL_j)$ is its ordinary density $dX|_K/(Mct)$ plus
$\zeta=(2/(|F|c))H\mathbf1_E\,ds\,\delta_{(x,y)=0}$. The weak limit of $(-\log L_j)_+$ times the actual boundary normal-position measure is its ordinary limiting trace plus
$b=\sqrt2 H\mathbf1_E\,ds\,\delta_{(x,y)=0}\delta_{n_0}$. These satisfy $-n_0 b=M(0,\ldots,0,c,c)\zeta$ after identifying their physical positions. The construction has a fixed finite set of exact affine contact rows with uniformly interior source balls, positive lower bounds on marked values, and positive limiting source weights. The original-volume rows are uniform on the corresponding actual active cells.

For $F=[0,1]$, $H=\max\{2-s,1+s\}$ and $A=\max\{2-s,17/10,1+s\}$, both defects have tangential support $[0,3/10]\cup[7/10,1]$ in one exposed zero edge. They are neither log-concave measures nor uniform measures on convex supports. The two source marks converge to $(206/1055,25/211,25/211)$ and its reflection in $s=1/2$, with limiting values $50c/211$ and weights $1/2$. For all sufficiently large $j$ these marks are shallower than the ordinary centroid. More generally any nonempty finite union of positive-length closed subintervals of $[0,1]$ occurs as the tangential support.

pk-intake-actual-coordinate-projection-d.relation_to_goal: All-cap finite discrepancy in fixed unimodular coordinates. The error can exceed the total sampled volume.
pk-intake-actual-coordinate-projection-d.statement:
Let $n\ge1$ and $d\ge0$. In any fixed unimodular integer-base coordinates, let $\pi_I$ delete integer coordinates indexed by $I\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$. For a compact convex set $K\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$, including the empty set, put $A_I(K)=\mu_{n-|I|,d}(\pi_I K)$, where $\mu_{j,d}$ sums $d$-volume over the $\mathbb Z^j$ fibers. Use $\mu_{0,d}=\operatorname{vol}_d$ and count the nonempty singleton in dimension zero. Then
$$
|\mu_{n,d}(K)-\operatorname{vol}_{n+d}(K)|\le \sum_{\varnothing\ne I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}} A_I(K).
$$
In particular, every closed ambient halfspace $H$ satisfies $\mu_{n,d}(C\cap H)\ge \operatorname{vol}_{n+d}(C\cap H)-\sum_{I\ne\varnothing}A_I(C)$. Lower-dimensional sets and boundary fibers are included.

pk-intake-actual-critical-chord-scales.relation_to_goal: A restriction on the actual geometry of three proper-A, supporting-B critical caps at one middle-fiber mark.
pk-intake-actual-critical-chord-scales.statement:
Let $A,K,B\subset\mathbb R^2$ be convex bodies at the only integer bases $-1,0,1$, respectively, with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Use planar area on each fiber. Fix $y\in\operatorname{int}K$ and nonzero spanning vectors $v_1,v_2,v_3$ with $\sum_i v_i=0$. With $h_i=\max_{x\in B}v_i\cdot x$, assume that each closed ambient cap
$$
v_i\cdot(x-y)+(v_i\cdot y-h_i)z\ge0
$$
attains the actual mixed halfspace depth $Q$ at $(0,y)$ and that its cuts on $A$ and $K$ are proper, meaning that the cutting lines meet the interiors. Its trace on $B$ is a supporting face, so $Q=U_i+q_i$, where $U_i$ is the cap area on $A$ and $q_i=|K\cap\{x:v_i\cdot(x-y)\ge0\}|$. Let $a=|A|$, $k=|K|$, $b=|B|$, $M=a+k+b$, and $D=|\det(v_1,v_2)|$. Write $a_i,k_i$ for the lengths of the respective $A,K$ chords divided by $\lVert v_i\rVert$, and set $s_i=k_i+2a_i$, $\lambda_i=1/s_i$, $\Lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i$, $p_i=\lambda_i/\Lambda$, and $t_i=a_i/s_i$.


Let $J$ be a quarter turn. Both endpoint distances of the $i$-th middle chord in the parameter $x=y+uJv_i$ lie between $s_i(1-4t_i+6t_i^2)/2$ and $s_i(1/2-3t_i^2)$, with $0<t_i\le1/3$. For each permutation of $i,j,\ell$,
$$
\frac{p_\ell}{1-2t_\ell}\le
\frac{p_i}{1-4t_i+6t_i^2}+\frac{p_j}{1-4t_j+6t_j^2},
\qquad p_\ell<\frac34.
$$
Write $Z_i=K\cap\{x:v_j\cdot(x-y)<0,\ v_\ell\cdot(x-y)<0\}$. If $p_\ell>3p_i$, then
$$
|Z_i|\Lambda^2<\frac{D}{8p_\ell(p_\ell-3p_i)}.
$$
In particular, if all $q_i\le ck$ for some $c<1/2$, put $\epsilon=1-2c$. Then $k\Lambda^2<D/[8\epsilon p_\ell(p_\ell-3p_*)]$ whenever $p_\ell>3p_*$, where $p_*=\min(p_i,p_j)$.

For distinct $i,j,\ell$ satisfying $p_\ell>p_i+3p_j$ and $p_\ell>p_j+3p_i$, put $p_*=\min(p_i,p_j)$ and
$$
T_i=\frac{2-\sqrt{6p_i/(p_\ell-3p_j)-2}}6,\qquad
T_j=\frac{2-\sqrt{6p_j/(p_\ell-3p_i)-2}}6,\qquad
X=\frac{4p_\ell(p_\ell-3p_*)T_iT_j}{p_ip_j}.
$$

In the domain of these two stronger weight inequalities, $T_i,T_j\in(0,1/3)$ and $a\Lambda^2>DT_iT_j/(2p_ip_j)$. Under the additional cap bound $q_i\le ck$ for all three indices, $a/k>\epsilon X$.

pk-intake-actual-critical-free-simplex-v.relation_to_goal: Refutes the assertion that actual critical budgets with common contact force zero variance on every freely varying stationary simplex endpoint. Stationarity holds in the indicated fixed-cap endpoint block.
pk-intake-actual-critical-free-simplex-v.statement:
For every $d\ge2$, let $K$ be a centered $d$-simplex of volume $V$, $m=d+1$, and $B=K-K$ of volume $U$. The convex hull with integer fibers $K,B,-K$ at $-1,0,1$ has actual maximum mixed halfspace depth $D=V+U/2$ attained at $(0,0)$. Writing $\lambda_i(x)=l_i(x)+1/m$ for the endpoint barycentrics, each cap $H_{i,a}=\{l_i(x)+(a-1/m)z\ge0\}$ for $0<a<1$ has mass $D$ and passes through $(0,0)$. A group with thresholds summing to one covers the ambient space. Choose $m$ groups with $a_{g,g}=1-d/(3m)$ and $a_{g,i}=1/(3m)$ for $i\ne g$. Their combined normals have rank $d+1$. Let $\ell_{g,i}=\eta_{g,i}/(1-a_{g,i})^d$, with $\eta_H=1/(3m^2)$ and $\eta_L=(3m-1)/(3m^2d)$.

Keep the caps and the other fibers fixed, impose the global budgets $D$, and vary only the simplex endpoint at $-1$. That endpoint is physically free under strict midpoint compatibility. The positive objective-one cap-volume Lagrangian is stationary there and has nonzero within-vertex reciprocal-threshold variance. With $A$ the off-diagonal vertex velocity and $c,s$ its off-diagonal column and row sums, its Hessian divided by $V$ is
$$
-\frac{m(4d-7)+1}{d(3m-1)}\lVert c\rVert^2-
\frac{\lVert s\rVert^2+\lVert A\rVert_F^2}{m}.
$$
Thus the reference endpoint is a strict local volume maximum in this fixed-cap simplex block. In $d=2$ the centered unit coordinate triangle gives $V=1/2,U=3,M=4,D=2$. The alternative thresholds permuting $(4/5,1/10,1/10)$ and multipliers $\ell_H=5/6,\ell_L=5/27$ give normalized Hessian $-(11/27)\lVert c\rVert^2-(\lVert s\rVert^2+\lVert A\rVert_F^2)/3$ with inertia $(0,0,6)$ in the order positive, zero, negative.

pk-intake-actual-critical-planar-chord-w.statement:

$$
v_i\cdot(x-y)+(v_i\cdot y-h_i)z\ge0

attains the actual mixed depth at $(0,y)$, and cuts both $A$ and $K$ properly. The trace on $B$ is the supporting face $F_i=B\cap\{v_i\cdot x=h_i\}$. Let $a_i,k_i$ be the lengths of the $A,K$ cutting chords, respectively, divided by $\lVert v_i\rVert$. Put $\lambda_i=1/(2a_i+k_i)$ and $\Lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i$.

Let $c_{A,i}$ and $c_i$ be the $u$-centers of the $A,K$ chords. Then $F_i$ contains a $u$-interval of length $a_i$ centered at $-c_{A,i}-(k_i/a_i)c_i$. In particular,
$$
k_i\ge a_i,\qquad
|c_i|\le \frac{a_i(k_i-a_i)}{k_i+2a_i}.
$$
For the single centrally symmetric body $(K-y)\cap(y-K)$, its Minkowski gauge $N$ satisfies
$$
2\lambda_i\le N(Jv_i)\le 6\lambda_i,\qquad
\lambda_i\le3\sum_{j\ne i}\lambda_j,\qquad
\frac{\lambda_i}{\Lambda}\le\frac34.
$$

pk-intake-actual-deepest-maximal-project.relation_to_goal: The largest projective-energy stratum among actual deepest points has exact marked translation equality on all its integer anchored relations, and yields a parity payment for its retained mass.
pk-intake-actual-deepest-maximal-project.statement:
Let \(n\ge0\) and \(d\ge1\). Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n\) be finite and nonempty, and let \(K_p\subset\mathbb R^d\), \(p\in P\), be convex bodies satisfying the anchored inclusions
$$
\sum_i\lambda_i K_{p_i}\subseteq K_q
\quad\text{whenever}\quad
\lambda_i\ge0,\quad\sum_i\lambda_i=1,\quad q=\sum_i\lambda_i p_i\in P.
$$
Put \(S=\bigcup_{p\in P}\{p\}\times K_p\), let \(\mu\) be the sum of fiber volumes on \(S\), and let \(D_\mu(Y)=\inf_{H\ni Y}\mu(H)\) over closed ambient halfspaces. Write \(Q=\max_{Y\in S}D_\mu(Y)\), \(D=\{Y\in\mathbb R^{n+d}:D_\mu(Y)\ge Q\}\), and
$$
E_K(y)=\inf_{a:\ 1+a\cdot(x-y)>0\ \forall x\in K}\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx
\quad (y\in\operatorname{int}K).
$$
Then \(Q>0\) is attained, \(D\) is compact and convex, and every \((p,y)\in D\cap S\) has \(y\in\operatorname{int}K_p\). The positive number
$$

Include every nonempty integer fiber in the mixed set $S$ and let $\mu$ sum ordinary $d$-volume over these fibers. For $Y\in S$ define $\Delta(Y)=\inf_{H\ni Y}\mu(H)$ over all closed ambient halfspaces, and write $\mathcal Y$ for the points maximizing this depth. All points in $\mathcal Y$ are in the ordinary interiors of their own fibers. Use the physical retained mass $T_K(y)$ and its unique optimal cap $D_K(y)$, defined by maximizing $\int_K f$ over measurable $0\le f\le1$ with $\int_K(x-y)f(x)\,dx=0$.

There is an attained positive maximum $\tau$ of $T_{K_p}(y)$ over $(p,y)\in\mathcal Y$. Its attaining stratum $\mathcal Y_\tau$ has at most one mark at each base. For any positive convex combination of marks $(p_i,y_i)$ in this stratum whose target base $p=\sum_i\lambda_i p_i$ is integral, the target $(p,y)$ with $y=\sum_i\lambda_i y_i$ lies in $\mathcal Y_\tau$, and
$$
D_{K_{p_i}}(y_i)-y_i=D_{K_p}(y)-y\quad\text{for every }i,
\qquad D_{K_p}(y)=\sum_i\lambda_iD_{K_{p_i}}(y_i).
$$
The set of its bases equals the integer points of its convex hull, and at most $2^n$ translation classes of retained caps occur.

On $\mathcal Y_\tau$, let $\mathcal Z$ be the marks maximizing the ordinary projective energy
$$
E_K(y)=\inf_{a:\ 1+a\cdot(x-y)>0\ (x\in K)}\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx.

Then $\mathcal Z$ is nonempty and finite. For each positive convex combination of its marks with integral target base, the target is in $\mathcal Z$ and
$$
K_{p_i}-y_i=K_p-y\quad\text{for every }i,
\qquad K_p=\sum_i\lambda_iK_{p_i}.
$$
There are at most $2^n$ translation classes of these centered whole fibers.

pk-intake-actual-distal-quantile-path-an.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, $d\ge1$, with positive summed integer-fiber $d$-volume $\mu(C)=M$. For $0<a<B$ let $t_i(a)$ be the rightmost threshold with $F_i(t_i(a))=B-a$, and put $t_i(0)=b_i,\ t_i(B)=\max_C\ell_i$. Define
$$
C_a=C\cap\bigcap_i\{\ell_i\le t_i(a)\},\qquad M(a)=\mu(C_a).
$$
The thresholds are nondecreasing, allowing jumps across tail plateaus. For $a>0$, $C_a$ is a convex body retaining each original deepest point and an own-fiber relative neighborhood of it. The original caps cover its entire mixed set and each has mass at most $a$ there, so its maximum normalized mixed depth is at most $a/M(a)$.

Each mixed fiber mass and the total mass are nondecreasing and $m$-Lipschitz in $a$, with $M(0)=0$ and $M(B)=M$. The positive bases $P(a)$ are lattice-complete and expand with $a$. Each originally positive base has an entry threshold in $[0,B)$ where its mass is zero and above which its mass is positive. Thus only finitely many changes in positive bases or occupied parities occur; all original deepest bases persist for $a>0$.

On the original measured mixed set define $R_i(w)=(B-F_i(\ell_i(w)))_+$. Then $\mu\{R_i>a\}=B-a$ for $0<a<B$, $\mu\{R_i=0\}=M-B$, and $M(a)=\mu\{\max_i R_i\le a\}$ on $[0,B]$. Let $N_a(w)=\#\{i:\ell_i(w)>t_i(a)\}$ and $E(a)=\int(N_a-1)_+\,d\mu$. Then $E$ is nonnegative and nonincreasing, $E(0)=mB-M$, $E(B)=0$, and
$$
M(a)=M-m(B-a)+E(a)=ma-[E(0)-E(a)].
$$

pk-intake-actual-fixed-ray-inner-body-cu.relation_to_goal: Any actual planar inner body of the indicated strict-incidence triangle, with no cap ceiling, finite-loss restriction, or polygon assumption.

pk-intake-actual-gauss-local-support-pat.relation_to_goal: Realized support paths at smooth strictly positively curved compatible families. The original compatible gaps may vanish.
pk-intake-actual-gauss-local-support-pat.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let a nonempty finite set $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ carry positive convex bodies $K_p$ with $C^2$ supports $h_p$ on the unit sphere. Assume $Q_p=\nabla_S^2h_p+h_pI$ is everywhere positive definite and $h_q(u)\ge\sum_p\alpha_ph_p(u)$ for every $u$ whenever $q=\sum_p\alpha_pp\in P$, $\alpha_p\ge0$, $\sum_p\alpha_p=1$. Let $H_p$ be the homogeneous support extension. Take $C^2$ spherical functions $\psi_0,\ldots,\psi_n$, a $C^2$ vector field $Z$ into $\mathbb R^d$, and a finite list of $C^2$ spherical functions $\chi_a\ge0$ and smooth convex functions $\phi_a(z,s)$ on a neighborhood of the convex hull of the compact support data $(p,h_p(u))$. Put
$
g_p(t,u)=H_p(u+tZ(u))+t\bigl(\psi_0(u)+\sum_l p_l\psi_l(u)\bigr),\qquad
h_p(t,u)=g_p(t,u)-t\sum_a\chi_a(u)\phi_a(p,g_p(t,u)).
$
These are supports of positive compatible fibers for sufficiently small $t\ge0$, and for both signs when the list of contractions is empty. With only the affine-in-base additions every old gap stays exactly unchanged. The canonical hull realizes the perturbed fibers at all $P$, and its lattice trace has exactly those bases if $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$.

Put $x_p(u)=\nabla_Sh_p(u)+h_p(u)u$, $J_p(u)=\det Q_p(u)$, and $\dot h_p=x_p\cdot Z+\psi_0+\sum_l p_l\psi_l-\sum_a\chi_a\phi_a(p,h_p)$. For $M(t)=\sum_p|K_p(t)|$ and any fixed nonvertical cap $H=\{(p,x):a\cdot p+v\cdot x\ge b\}$ with $\|v\|=1$, the total mass derivative is $\sum_p\int\dot h_pJ_p\,du$ and the fixed cap derivative is $\sum_p\int\dot h_pJ_p\mathbf1_H(p,x_p(u))\,du$. Jointly changing $b$ to $b+ts$ subtracts $s\sum_p\mathcal H^{d-1}(K_p\cap\{v\cdot x=b-a\cdot p\})$ from the latter derivative. All derivatives are along the available signs.

pk-intake-actual-half-cap-quadrilateral-.relation_to_goal: Classifies the three incidence alternatives under strict planar half-caps and proves exact two-corner frontier equality in the actual one-double-vertex case.
pk-intake-actual-half-cap-quadrilateral-.statement:
Let $K$ be a planar triangle or quadrilateral containing $0$ in its interior. Let three balanced spanning normals define through-source caps each of area strictly less than $|K|/2$. Use the canonical bridge triangle $T$ at the same six boundary-ray endpoints. A sector's core is the triangle spanned by its two ray endpoints and $0$. The unique sectors belong to exactly one cap in their interiors, and the double sectors belong to exactly two.

If an open unique sector contains no vertex of $K$, its intersection with $K$ is its core. If all three open unique sectors contain vertices and no open double sector does, the double sectors of $K$ are cores and $\Psi(K)\le4$, strictly if $K\ne T$. Here for a body $B$ with these ray endpoints,
$$
f_i(B)=\frac{2\sqrt{|B|Q_i(B)}}{\sigma_i\sum_{s=1}^3 Q_s(B)/\sigma_s},
\qquad
\Psi(B)=\sum_i f_i(B)^2+\prod_i f_i(B),
$$
where $Q_i(B)$ is its cap area and $\sigma_i$ is its cutting chord length divided by the norm of its normal.

In the remaining case $K$ is a quadrilateral with exactly one vertex in each open unique sector and one in a single open double sector. The three caps of $T$ strictly isolate its distinct vertices. The unique sector opposite the enlarged double sector is unchanged, and the other two unique sectors have strictly positive reciprocal losses $\ell_i,\ell_j$, where $\ell_i=1/(2X_i(K))-1/(2X_i(T))$ for the unique-sector areas $X_i$. Put $g=1/(2Y(T))-1/(2Y(K))$ for the enlarged double-sector areas $Y$. In the triangle's reciprocal sector matrix let $\lambda_i,\lambda_j$ be the positive scales of the two rank-one unique blocks, written as $\lambda_i(\beta_i,-\alpha_i)^\top(\beta_i,-\alpha_i)$ with positive kernel $(\alpha_i,\beta_i)$ normalized by $\alpha_i+\beta_i=1$, and likewise for $j$. Let $\theta_i,\theta_j$ be the entries of these two kernels at the endpoints of the enlarged double sector. Then
$$
g\left(\frac{\theta_i^2}{\ell_i}+\frac{\theta_j^2}{\ell_j}+\frac1{\lambda_i}+\frac1{\lambda_j}\right)=1.
$$

pk-intake-actual-homothetic-shell-shared.relation_to_goal: Actual mixed shell loss under one compatible inward homothety with boundary-null cone signatures. It gives a cap-loss lower bound.
pk-intake-actual-homothetic-shell-shared.statement:
Let $K_z$ be the positive $d$-dimensional fibers of a compact mixed-integer convex body, measured by the sum of their Lebesgue volumes. Fix a target base $p$, a shared source $s\ne p$, and disjoint nonempty exclusive source sets $A,B$, disjoint from $\{p,s\}$. Assume two positive barycentric relations give $p$ from $\{s\}\cup A$ and from $\{s\}\cup B$, respectively. Put $I=\{s\}\cup A\cup B$, $V_z=|K_z|$, and $V_I=\sum_{z\in I}V_z$. For $z\in I$ fix $c_z\in\operatorname{int}K_z$. Assume that replacing $K_z$ by $c_z+(1-\varepsilon)(K_z-c_z)$ for $z\in I$, with all other measured fibers fixed, is an actual compatible deformation with the same measured base set for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon\ge0$. Its total mass satisfies $M'(0+)=-dV_I$.

Let $\nu_z$ be the boundary cone probability of $K_z$ about $c_z$. Fix two couplings of these cone probabilities, one for each relation, and any one gluing of the two couplings over the common $\nu_s$. Let $Y_1,Y_2$ be the resulting continuous barycentric outputs at $p$. Take any finite family of closed ambient halfspaces $H_j$ whose boundaries have probability zero under all the lifted source laws and both lifted output laws. Write $f_{rj}=\Pr((p,Y_r)\in H_j)$ and $o_j=\Pr((p,Y_1),(p,Y_2)\in H_j)$, with the latter denoting joint membership of both outputs. Put
$$
a=dV_s,\quad b=d\min_{z\in A}V_z,\quad c=d\min_{z\in B}V_z,\quad
c_1=\min(a,b),\ c_2=\min(a,c),\ c_{12}=\min(a,b+c),\ \rho=c_1+c_2-c_{12}.
$$
The fixed-cap loss derivative exists for every $j$ and satisfies $L_j\ge B_j:=c_1f_{1j}+c_2f_{2j}-\rho o_j$. The limiting joint source and target signature law is the law of the one chosen cone gluing. The increase of $B_j$ over the best fixed independent allocation with coefficients $0\le x\le b,\ 0\le y\le c,\ x+y\le a$ is exactly $\rho[\min(f_{1j},f_{2j})-o_j]$. For prescribed nonnegative weights on the cap family, an optimizing gluing for the weighted sum of the $B_j$ exists and uses the same two relation marginals for the entire family.

pk-intake-actual-homothetic-zero-forest-.relation_to_goal: Decomposes the sampled radius graph under exact equality on prescribed forest edges. The patches need not be disjoint and no aggregate mass or general mixed-depth conclusion is asserted.
pk-intake-actual-homothetic-zero-forest-.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$ be integers and let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact and convex. Assume the nonempty set $P$ of positive-$d$-volume integer fibers is finite, and that these fibers are $K_p=a_p+r_pK$, with $r_p>0$ and one full-dimensional convex body $K$ of centroid zero. At each occupied parity choose a designated root $v_c$ in that class. Suppose the forest given by $f(p)=(p+v_c)/2$ for a nonroot $p$ in class $c$ terminates at the roots and that every edge satisfies $K_{f(p)}=(K_p+K_{v_c})/2$.

Write $G_p=(p,r_p)$ and let $F_p$ be the minimal face of the lifted polytope $\widehat Q=\operatorname{conv}\lbrace G_p:p\in P\rbrace$ containing $G_p$, allowing the whole polytope as a face. Every $G_p$ lies in a face supported from above by the graph of an affine majorant of the sampled radii. For each edge, $F_p$ and $F_{v_c}$ are contained in $F_{f(p)}$. Thus the sampled lifts of the nodes and of all partner roots on any path terminating at $v$ lie in $F_v$, and the inclusion-maximal terminal-root faces cover all sampled lifts.

For each terminal-root face $F$, base projection $\pi$ is an affine isomorphism from $F$ to $\pi(F)$. The sampled bases on $F$ are exactly $\pi(F)\cap\mathbb Z^n$. On those bases the radius is affine, and there is a single affine map on $\operatorname{aff}\pi(F)$ giving all the actual centroids $a_p$.

pk-intake-actual-interval-continuum-and-.relation_to_goal: An exact obstruction to a finite count of potential maximizers, even within a single fiber. It also calibrates the original-measure slab constant.
pk-intake-actual-interval-continuum-and-.statement:
Let $C=\{(z,x):-1\le z\le1,\ 0\le x\le3-2|z|\}$, with summed length $\mu$ on its integer trace of total mass $5$. Write $D$ for actual raw mixed depth, $F$ for ordinary raw interval depth and $P_\lambda=D+\lambda F$. At its middle fiber,
$$
D(0,x)=\min\{x+\min(2x,1),\ 3-x+\min(2(1-x)_+,1)\}.
$$
Its actual envelope is $E(\lambda)=\max\{2+\lambda,\,3/2+(3/2)\lambda\}$. For $0\le\lambda<1$ its unique source is $(0,1)$, for $\lambda>1$ its unique source is $(0,3/2)$, and at $\lambda=1$ exactly the continuum $\{(0,x):1\le x\le3/2\}$ is active. The canonical active slope jumps from $1$ to $3/2$ at one and the actual depth drops from $2$ to $3/2$. For $Y_0=(0,1)$ and $Y_1=(0,3/2)$, at $\lambda=1$, a depth-attaining cap through their midpoint has original slab mass $1/4$ upon shifting it to $Y_1$. The own-root midpoint gain is zero and $D(Y_0)-D(Y_1)=1/2$, giving equality in the one-half same-parameter slab bound. Every finite increasing subdivision of this active segment gives equality in the summed midpoint charges.

pk-intake-actual-interval-slope-breakpoi.relation_to_goal: This is a finite exact evaluation for one continuous and one real base coordinate.
pk-intake-actual-interval-slope-breakpoi.statement: Let $P$ be a finite nonempty set of distinct real bases and let $[l_j,r_j]$ be a bounded nonempty interval at each $j\in P$. Use the sum of lengths on the placed fibers as the measure. With no other base, the two nonvertical masses are constant in slope. Zero-width intervals have zero mass.

pk-intake-actual-midpoint-common-tilt-en.relation_to_goal: One direction at a time and one common physical tilt; the larger-endpoint reserve is the actual cap mass at that tilt.
pk-intake-actual-midpoint-common-tilt-en.statement:
Let $A,B$ be convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$, $0<a=|A|\le b=|B|$, and fix $u\ne0$. Use the mass-$a$ coupling $\pi_u$ with marginal volumes $1_A\,dx,(a/b)1_B\,dx$ and comonotone $u$-projections, and let $\eta_u$ be its midpoint measure. For all $h,\tau\in\mathbb R$, write $U_A,U_B$ for actual cap volumes at thresholds $h+\tau,h-\tau$, and $p=U_A/a$, $q=U_B/b$, $m=\eta_u\{u\cdot x\ge h\}/a$. Then
$$
U_A+U_B=a m+(1-a/b)U_B+E,\qquad E=a(p+q-m)\ge0,
$$
where $E$ integrates a $\{0,1\}$-valued indicator difference. This identity includes saturated thresholds. Always $\min(p,q)\le m\le\max(p,q)$, and when all cuts are proper, $Q_A(p)+Q_B(q)=Q_A(m)+Q_B(m)=2h$.

pk-intake-actual-midpoint-slab-envelope-.relation_to_goal: Actual slabs in the original measure and actual integer midpoints. Coverage of any fixed fraction is a separate assertion.
pk-intake-actual-midpoint-slab-envelope-.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body, $d\ge1$, with positive total summed $d$-volume $\mu$ on $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. Let $D(Y)=\inf_{H\ni Y}\mu(H)$ use closed ambient halfspaces, and let $F(Y)$ be the $d$th root of raw ordinary depth in the actual fiber at $Y$. Put $P_\lambda(Y)=D(Y)+\lambda F(Y)$ and $E(\lambda)=\max_{Y\in S}P_\lambda(Y)$ for $\lambda\ge0$. Take distinct maximizers $Y_i=(z_i,x_i)$ at $0\le\lambda_0\le\lambda_1$, with $\lambda_1>0$ and the two bases of equal parity. At equal parameters order the sources by nondecreasing own root. Write $F_i=F(Y_i)$, $D_i=D(Y_i)$, $\delta=F_1-F_0$, $A=D_0-D_1$, $Y_m=(Y_0+Y_1)/2$ and $\Delta=F(Y_m)-(F_0+F_1)/2\ge0$. For every nonvertical depth-attaining cap through $Y_m$, write $H=\{L\ge0\}$ with $L(z,x)=a\cdot(z-z_m)+u\cdot(x-x_m)$ and $\lVert u\rVert=1$. Then $L(Y_1)\ge0$, strictly if $\lambda_0>0$ and $\delta>0$. Set $T_H=\mu\{0\le L<L(Y_1)\}$; this is the exact mass removed by shifting the same cap to $Y_1$, and $D(Y_m)\ge D_1+T_H$. When $\delta>0$,
$$
T_H+\lambda_0\Delta\le A-\lambda_0\delta/2,\qquad
T_H+\lambda_1\Delta\le\lambda_1\delta/2.
$$
If in addition $\lambda_0>0$, then $0\le\Delta<\delta/2$, $F_0<F(Y_m)<F_1$ and $D_1<D(Y_m)<D_0$. For distinct parameters put $\lambda_*=A/\delta$ and $B=E(\lambda_*)-D_0-\lambda_*F_0$. Then
$$
T_H+\lambda_*\Delta\le A/2+B,\qquad
0\le B\le
\frac{\delta(\lambda_*-\lambda_0)(\lambda_1-\lambda_*)}{\lambda_1-\lambda_0}
\le(\lambda_1-\lambda_0)\delta/4.
$$
For equal parameters take $\lambda_*=\lambda_1$ and $B=0$. For $\delta=0$ both endpoint margins, $\Delta,T_H,A$ and $B$ are zero and one can take any $\lambda_*\in[\lambda_0,\lambda_1]$.

Write $s=L(Y_1)$ and suppose the endpoint fiber contains a centered ball of radius $r>0$. For $\kappa_j$ the unit $j$-ball volume, $\kappa_0=1$, one has
$$
T_H\ge \kappa_{d-1}\int_0^{\min(s,r)}(r^2-t^2)^{(d-1)/2}\,dt
\ge c_r\min(s,r/2),\qquad c_r=\kappa_{d-1}(\sqrt3 r/2)^{d-1}.
$$
For $d=1$ the integral expression is $\min(s,r)$. An available radius is $r=F_1^d/(\kappa_{d-1}R^{d-1})$ for $R=\operatorname{diam}C_{z_1}$. If $T_H\le\epsilon<c_r r/2$, then $|a\cdot(z_1-z_0)+u\cdot(x_1-x_0)|\le2\epsilon/c_r$. One can choose a common positive radius from the body's maximum fiber diameter and the positive slope floor $F_*$.

For a finite chain of selected sources at nondecreasing positive parameters $\lambda_j$, order equal-parameter sources by their own roots and assume successive bases have equal parity. Let $(T_j,\Delta_j,\lambda_{*,j})$ denote these quantities for each edge, and set $\eta=\max_j(\lambda_{j+1}-\lambda_j)$. Then
$$
\sum_j(T_j+\lambda_{*,j}\Delta_j)\le
\frac{D_0-D_N}{2}+\frac14\sum_j(\lambda_{j+1}-\lambda_j)(F_{j+1}-F_j)
\le \frac{D_0-D_N}{2}+\frac{\eta(F_N-F_0)}4 .
$$
The same upper budget bounds the original measure of the union of the slabs. Along canonical envelope selections the first term is half of the corresponding work integral. Parity subsequences use the successive gaps within each subsequence.

pk-intake-actual-mixed-own-depth-envelop.relation_to_goal: Scalar accounting for actual points of the original measured mixed body. The budget is in raw mixed-depth units.
pk-intake-actual-mixed-own-depth-envelop.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body, $d\ge1$, with positive total summed $d$-volume $\mu$ on $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. Let $D(Y)=\inf_{H\ni Y}\mu(H)$ use closed ambient halfspaces, and let $F(Y)$ be the $d$th root of raw ordinary depth in the actual fiber at $Y$. Put $P_\lambda(Y)=D(Y)+\lambda F(Y)$ and $E(\lambda)=\max_{Y\in S}P_\lambda(Y)$ for $\lambda\ge0$. Put $Q=E(0)$, $F_{\max}=\max_SF$, $F_*=\max_{\{D=Q\}}F$ and $D_{\mathrm{top}}=\max_{\{F=F_{\max}\}}D$. All these maxima are attained and $F_*,Q>0$. At distinct parameters $0\le\lambda_0<\lambda_1$, for any maximizing sources $Y_i$ at $\lambda_i$, write $\delta=F(Y_1)-F(Y_0)$ and $A=D(Y_0)-D(Y_1)$. Then $\delta\ge0$ and $\lambda_0\delta\le A\le\lambda_1\delta$. Every positive-parameter maximizer obeys $F_*\le F(Y)\le F_{\max}$ and $Q-\lambda(F_{\max}-F_*)\le D(Y)\le Q$.

The envelope is convex and $F_{\max}$-Lipschitz. Let $F(\lambda)$ be the largest actual active slope at $\lambda$ and $D(\lambda)=E(\lambda)-\lambda F(\lambda)$ its actual mixed depth. Then $F(\lambda)$ is nondecreasing, right-continuous, equals $E'_+(\lambda)$ and starts at $F_*$. With the right-continuous Lebesgue–Stieltjes convention,
$$
D(a)-D(b)=\int_{(a,b]}\lambda\,dF(\lambda)\quad(0\le a<b),\qquad
\int_{(0,\infty)}\lambda\,dF(\lambda)=Q-D_{\mathrm{top}}\le Q-F_{\max}^d.
$$
The limits at infinity are $F(\lambda)\to F_{\max}$ and $D(\lambda)\to D_{\mathrm{top}}$.

pk-intake-actual-moving-cap-first-stress.relation_to_goal: A selected whole-space covering tuple with actual moving caps. Its budgets need not be maximum depth, and open actual compatibility is a separate hypothesis.
pk-intake-actual-moving-cap-first-stress.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $m=d+1$, and $\gamma=(d/m)^d$. Take a finite, lattice-complete compatible family of positive $d$-dimensional compact convex fibers with an affine interior section. After translating the section to zero in each fiber, let the selected fiber $p$ be a simplex of volume $V$ centered at zero, with barycentric coordinates $\xi_i$. Its canonical caps have traces $\xi_i\ge1/m$ at $p$ and the same continuous normals through the section at all bases. Let $H_i(\theta)$ be a smooth finite-dimensional chart of ambient cap tuples covering the whole space for every $\theta$ near zero, with the canonical tuple at zero. Write $F_i(W,\theta)$ for the cap volume on the moving selected simplex with labeled barycentric vertex matrix $W$ near $I$ (column sums one), and $G_i(\theta)$ for the sum of the $d$-volumes in $H_i(\theta)$ on **all original fibers**. Assume these cap functions are $C^2$ near the reference configuration. If only the selected fiber moves, the change in the $i$th global cap budget is
$$c_i(W,\theta)=F_i(W,\theta)-F_i(I,\theta)+G_i(\theta)-G_i(0),$$
and total mixed mass changes by $V(\det W-1)$.

On zero-column-sum matrices $B$ the physical cap derivative is $f_i(B)=V\gamma[\operatorname{tr}B+(B\mathbf1)_i]$. It has the right inverse $\mathcal R$ given, for $y\in\mathbb R^m$, by $z_i=y_i/(Vm\gamma)$ and
$$\mathcal R(y)_{ii}=z_i,\qquad \mathcal R(y)_{ij}=z_i-\frac{\sum_k z_k}{d}\quad(i\ne j).$$
Set $\ell_i=1/(m\gamma)$. Then $V\operatorname{tr}B=\ell\cdot f(B)$ for every $B$ and $V\operatorname{tr}\mathcal R(y)=\ell\cdot y$. If the physical compatibility chart is open at $I$ and $\ell\cdot DG(0)$ is a nonzero functional, a local actual path increases total mixed mass and strictly decreases every selected global cap budget. There is also an increasing-mass path keeping all selected budgets exactly constant.

There is a $C^2$ path with a critical first velocity, positive total mixed mass second derivative and strictly negative second derivative of every selected global cap mass if and only if $Q(B,\eta)>0$ for some critical velocity. If $q$ is the vector of cap second derivatives on the straight path with such a velocity, adding the physical acceleration $\mathcal R(-q-\gamma Q\mathbf1/2)$ makes the mass second derivative $Q/2$ and every cap second derivative $-\gamma Q/2$.

pk-intake-actual-period-three-sector-com.relation_to_goal: Ordinary planar areas and actual fixed ray endpoints. The triangle kernel test uses signed vertex offsets at the mark. The ordinary cubic equality test uses normalized edge drops and has a different scope.
pk-intake-actual-period-three-sector-com.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a convex body with $0$ in its interior. Index its six rays by the vectors $e_i=(1,0),(0,1),(-1,1),(-1,0),(0,-1),(1,-1)$ in this order, with $i=0,\dots,5$. Write $P_i=R_ie_i$ for the actual boundary endpoint, $W_i$ for the area of $K$ between $P_i,P_{i+1}$, and $c_i=1/(2W_i)$. In the exact sector matrix $L$ of [7d1ee06fa4119930](../facts/7d1ee06fa4119930.md), substitute $z_i=R_i x_i$ and restrict to $x_{i+3}=x_i$. The resulting matrix $N$ on $(x_0,x_1,x_2)$ is positive semidefinite with nonpositive off-diagonal entries. Its coefficients, with matrix indices modulo three and ray indices modulo six, are
$$
\begin{aligned}
N_{ii}&=R_i^2(c_{i-1}+c_i)+R_{i+3}^2(c_{i+2}+c_{i+3})-2,\\
N_{i,i+1}&=c_iR_iR_{i+1}+c_{i+3}R_{i+3}R_{i+4}-2.
\end{aligned}
$$

Suppose $K$ is a triangle with vertices $V_j$ and the three canonical normals $v_1=(1,0)$, $v_2=(0,1)$, $v_3=(-1,-1)$ strictly isolate the respective vertices. Write $v_i\cdot V_i=a_i>0$ and $v_i\cdot V_j=-b_{ij}<0$ for $i\ne j$. Then $N$ is singular if and only if $b_{12}b_{23}b_{31}=b_{13}b_{32}b_{21}$. Its kernel in that case is one-dimensional, and it is positive definite otherwise.

pk-intake-actual-planar-middle-simplex-n.statement:
Let $v_1,v_2,v_3$ span $\mathbb R^2$ and sum to zero, and put $T=\{x:v_i\cdot x\le1\ \forall i\}$. Let $A,K,B$ be planar convex bodies with $B\subseteq T$, $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$, and each line $v_i\cdot x=-1$ meeting $\operatorname{int}A$. Write $V=|T|$, $a=|A|$, $b=|B|$, $k=|K|$ and assume $h_K(-v_i)\le1+\eta$ for all $i$, $0\le\eta\le1/2$. Then
$
b/V<f(\eta)=1-(1-2\eta)^2/3.
$
If also $a<b/32$, $k\le a+b$ and $k\ge(1-\xi)V$, then $\xi>5/16-(11/8)\eta+(11/8)\eta^2$. In particular the sandwich $(1-\eta)(-T)\subseteq K\subseteq(1+\eta)(-T)$ cannot hold together with $a<b/32$ and $k\le a+b$ when $0\le\eta\le(27-\sqrt{539})/38$.

If the three bodies are the measured fibers over $-1,0,1$ and the three caps $v_i\cdot x\ge z$ have a common mixed mass $Q\le2(a+k+b)/9$, then $k\le a+b$ is automatic.

pk-intake-actual-planar-simplex-containe.relation_to_goal: Rules out a deficit-to-cost bound for replacing actual planar fibers with arbitrary enclosing triangles and convexifying at the original integer bases.
pk-intake-actual-planar-simplex-containe.statement:
For $0<\varepsilon\le1/16$, let $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,(1,0),(0,1))$, $a=1+\varepsilon^2$, and take
$$
A=\{(x,y):x,y\ge0,\ \varepsilon\le x+y\le1\},\quad
B=\varepsilon^2T,\quad
P=\{(x,y):x,y\le a,\ x+y\ge\varepsilon\}.
$$
The hull of the lifts of $A,P/2,B$ at bases $0,1,2$ has exactly those three integer fibers, all of positive area. For $n\ge1$, pad the source with $[0,1]^{n-1}$ in additional integer coordinates. It has exactly $3\cdot 2^{n-1}$ positive fibers, each layer repeating the same three.

Write $\delta(K)=|K|(D(K)-4/9)$, where $D$ is maximum normalized ordinary planar closed-halfspace depth. The sum of all source deficits satisfies $0<\sum\delta(K)\le 2^{n-1}\cdot2\varepsilon^2/9$. For any triangle containing each actual fiber, the hull of the lifts of the chosen triangles at the same bases adds at least $2^{n-1}\varepsilon/16$ in actual mixed area. Thus no finite constant times the summed ordinary deficits can bound that cost even if all enclosing triangles are jointly chosen or required to be compatible.

If $W_n$ is its total mixed area, every fiber has area strictly below $(64/79)W_n/2^n$. The summed ordinary deficits relative to $4/9$ are positive and at most $2^{n-2}\cdot 2\varepsilon^2/9$. pk-intake-actual-polytopal-boundary-vari.relation_to_goal: A supplied boundary martingale yields actual transport-induced facet ownership and covariance. Flux additionally assumes the stated full section centroids and group balances. The mixed terms have no asserted common sign.
pk-intake-actual-polytopal-boundary-vari.statement:
Let $C$ be a compact polytope with positive $d$-dimensional actual fibers $K_p$ at finitely many sampled bases $p$, with $d\ge1$. Write $\mu$ for the sum of their $d$-volumes and $\eta$ for their boundary area marked with the regular outward continuous normal. Use counting area at interval endpoints. Let $\Pi$ be a given finite coupling from $\nu\ll\eta$ to $\eta$ preserving that normal and having conditional physical output mean equal to its input $w=(p,x)$.

List the nonvertical ambient facets $F_f$ with supporting equation $a_f\cdot p+u_f\cdot x=b_f$, where $|u_f|=1$ is oriented outward, working over the affine span of the base projection. At each regular input choose the first containing nonvertical facet with that marked normal. Let $\Pi_f$ be the restriction by this source label, with marginals $\nu_f,\eta_f$, and write $W_f=\eta_f-\nu_f$. These laws sum to their original marginals, the outputs stay on the labeled facet, and $\int(1,w)\,dW_f=0$. The labeled covariance is
$$
Q_f=\int ww^{\mathsf T}\,dW_f
=\int(w'-w)(w'-w)^{\mathsf T}\,d\Pi_f\succeq0,\qquad Q_f(a_f,u_f)=0.
$$
More generally, for a compact marked coupling whose conditional physical output mean given the full marked input equals its physical input, the quadratic difference identity holds after localization by every bounded Borel function of the preserved parameter.

Suppose further that $\nu=\sum_j\lambda_j\alpha_j\eta$ for finitely many nonvertical caps $H_j=\{a_j\cdot p+v_j\cdot x\ge b_j\}$, $|v_j|=1$, and $\lambda_j\ge0$. The body selector $\alpha_j$ is the usual captured bit off supporting faces. Its section allocation $\sigma_j$ is $1-\alpha_j$ at inside supporting facets and $\alpha_j$ at outside supporting facets, with full area on proper cuts. Denote the resulting effective section measure by $\zeta_j$. Splitting each $\alpha_j$ by the common source label gives $\alpha_{jf}$, with $\sum_f\alpha_{jf}=\alpha_j$ almost everywhere, while the target owner fractions $\omega_f=d\eta_f/d\eta$ satisfy $\sum_f\omega_f=1$. Thus $dW_f=(\omega_f-\sum_j\lambda_j\alpha_{jf})d\eta$. The $\zeta_j$ remain the original section allocations.

For each group $i$ of positive-section caps let $S_j=\zeta_j(\mathrm{total})$. Assume $\lambda_j S_j=t_i\rho_j$ within each group, that all its section measures have the same full physical centroid $\bar w_i=(\bar p_i,\bar x_i)$, and that $\sum_{j\in i}\rho_j(b_j-a_j\cdot\bar p_i)=0$. Set $V_j=\int(w-\bar w_i)(w-\bar w_i)^{\mathsf T}\,d\zeta_j$ in those groups and $V_j=0$ for a zero section measure. Then $V_j\succeq0$ and $V_j(a_j,v_j)=0$. If $m_p,m_x$ are the full mixed first moments and $m_{pj},m_{xj}$ their analogues restricted to $H_j$, then
$$
\begin{aligned}
d\left(m_p-\sum_j\lambda_jm_{pj}\right)
  &=-\sum_f Q_f^{pp}a_f-\sum_j\lambda_j V_j^{pp}a_j,\\
(d+1)\left(m_x-\sum_j\lambda_jm_{xj}\right)
  &=\sum_f Q_f^{xx}u_f+\sum_j\lambda_j V_j^{xx}v_j .
\end{aligned}
$$
Here $pp$ and $xx$ denote the base and continuous diagonal blocks. In zero base dimension the $pp$ blocks are absent and each continuous term on the right vanishes individually.

pk-intake-actual-positive-fiber-local-to.statement: Let $n,d\ge0$, let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex, and let $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$ be nonempty. Put $q=\dim_H S$ and let $P$ be the finite set of integer bases whose fibers $C_z$ have affine dimension $q$, equivalently whose fibers have positive $\mathcal H_q$ measure. Let $k$ be the number of coordinate parity classes occupied by $P$. Fix a finite family of closed ambient halfspaces and an integer $t\ge1$. If for every $z\in P$ some at most $t$ of the original halfspaces cover the entire fiber at $z$, then at most $kt$ of the original halfspaces simultaneously cover every fiber over $P$.

pk-intake-actual-positive-part-and-ranke.relation_to_goal: Intrinsic q-volume, actual closed cap labels, and a finite convex residual program. The contact measure can differ from ordinary fiber counting.
pk-intake-actual-positive-part-and-ranke.statement:
Let $S$ be the sampled mixed set of a compact convex body, with $q\ge1$ its largest integer fiber dimension. List its positive $q$-volume fibers $K_i$ at distinct bases $p_i$, let $V_i=\mathcal H^q(K_i)$, and let $\mu$ sum their intrinsic $q$-volumes. Suppose a finite family of original closed ambient halfspaces $H_1,\ldots,H_N$ covers these fibers. Set $A_{ai}=\mathcal H^q(K_i\cap H_a)$, $\gamma_q=(q/(q+1))^q$ and $\kappa=1/\gamma_q-2$. For nonnegative weights $\rho_i$ and thresholds $\alpha_i$, put
$$
T=\sum_i\rho_i V_i,\qquad
E_i(\alpha_i)=\sum_a(A_{ai}-\alpha_i)_+ +\alpha_i/\gamma_q-V_i,\qquad
L_a=\max(\{\rho_i:A_{ai}>\alpha_i\}\cup\{0\}).
$$
Then each surplus is nonnegative and
$$
T+\sum_i\rho_i E_i(\alpha_i)
=\sum_a\sum_i\rho_i(A_{ai}-\alpha_i)_+
  +\gamma_q^{-1}\sum_i\rho_i\alpha_i
\le\sum_a L_a\mu(H_a)+\gamma_q^{-1}\sum_i\rho_i\alpha_i.
$$
In particular, the last cap term is at most $B\sum_a L_a$ if each original cap has mass at most $B$.

Write $A_{(s)i}$ for the decreasing ranks of the actual local masses, with a fixed ordering of ties and zero padding. Write $a_s(i)$ for the corresponding original labels when present. Set $e_i=(V_i-A_{(1)i})^{1/q}$, $R=\sum_i\rho_i e_i^q$, and $E_i^{\mathrm{top}}=A_{(1)i}+A_{(2)i}+\kappa A_{(3)i}-V_i$. Define
$$
\begin{aligned}
D_a^{23}&=\max_i\rho_i(\mathbf1_{\{a=a_2(i)\}}+\kappa\mathbf1_{\{a=a_3(i)\}}),\\
D_a^{123}&=\max_i\rho_i(\mathbf1_{\{a=a_1(i)\}}+\mathbf1_{\{a=a_2(i)\}}+\kappa\mathbf1_{\{a=a_3(i)\}}),
\end{aligned}
$$
where a padded rank contributes no indicator. Then $E_i^{\mathrm{top}}\ge0$ and
$$
\begin{aligned}
T-R&=\sum_i\rho_i A_{(1)i},\\
R+\sum_i\rho_i E_i^{\mathrm{top}}
 &=\sum_i\rho_i(A_{(2)i}+\kappa A_{(3)i})\le\sum_a D_a^{23}\mu(H_a),\\
T+\sum_i\rho_i E_i^{\mathrm{top}}
 &\le\sum_a D_a^{123}\mu(H_a).
\end{aligned}
$$
If every cap has mass at most $B$, the last sum is at most $B\sum_a D_a^{123}$.

In particular the weights may be the contact weights of the finite one-cap residual optimization. Minimize $\sum_i h_i^q$ subject to $h_i\ge e_i$ and $h_j\ge h_i+g_i\cdot(p_j-p_i)$ for all distinct $i,j$. At an optimizer, let $\lambda_i$ be the nonnegative KKT multipliers of $e_i-h_i\le0$. Then the optimum is precisely the above $R$ for $\rho_i=\lambda_i$ if $q=1$, and, if $q>1$, for $\rho_i=\lambda_i/(q e_i^{q-1})$ at $\lambda_i>0$ and zero otherwise. In the latter case every positive multiplier has $e_i>0$.

pk-intake-actual-ray-two-bridge-unique-s.relation_to_goal: An ordinary planar envelope at a marked interior point for actual endpoints. The determinant tests boundedness of this two-bridge intersection. A uniform quantitative lower bound for the determinant and any compatibility across distinct mixed fibers require separate hypotheses or arguments.
pk-intake-actual-ray-two-bridge-unique-s.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a convex body with $0$ interior and actual cutting-line endpoints $(A,0),(-a,0),(0,B),(0,-b),(\rho,-\rho),(-\tau,\tau)$, all scalar radii positive. Reflect $K\cap\{x\le0,y\le0\}$ by $(u,v)=(-x,-y)$. The reflected sector lies in the nonnegative-quadrant envelope defined by
$$
(\rho-b)u+\rho v\le\rho b,\qquad
\tau u+(\tau-a)v\le\tau a.
$$
This particular envelope is bounded exactly when $D=\rho a+\tau b-ab>0$. In that case its vertices, allowing repetitions, are $0,(a,0),P_*,(0,b)$ with
$$
P_*=\frac1D\big(\rho[ab+\tau(a-b)],\ \tau[ab+\rho(b-a)]\big).
$$
Consequently the sector has area at most
$$
E=\frac{ab(a\tau+b\rho)-\rho\tau(a-b)^2}{2D}.
$$
For the other two unique sectors of $x\ge0,\ y\ge0,\ x+y\le0$, the same formulas use $(a,b,\rho,\tau)=(\rho,A,B,b)$ and $(B,\tau,a,A)$ respectively.

pk-intake-actual-seven-fiber-partial-tra.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $T$ be a $d$-simplex of volume $V$ with centroid $g$. Place $T$ at the four binary bases in two integer dimensions. Place any convex body $R\subseteq T$ of volume $w>0$ at $(-1,0)$, and the same convex body $A\subseteq T$ of volume $a>0$ at $(-1,1)$ and $(1,-1)$. Suppose either $A$ is a positive homothet of $T$ about $g$ and $\theta=2\Gamma_d$, or $A$ is centrally symmetric about $g$ and $\theta=1$. Here $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, and $\rho_d$ is the reflected simplex profile minimum of fact 53fe12b742a7608d. Assume $a\le\rho_d V$ and $w+\theta a\le\rho_d V$.

The convex hull has exactly the seven assigned integer fibers, total mixed volume $4V+w+2a$, and raw depth $\Gamma_d V+w+\theta a$ at $((0,0),g)$. Over its actual mixed-integer points the raw maximum is $\Gamma_d V+\max(a,w+\theta a)$. The maximizing set consists of $((0,0),g)$ if $w+\theta a>a$, of $((0,1),g)$ and $((1,0),g)$ if $w+\theta a<a$, and of all three at equality.

pk-intake-actual-signed-local-masses.relation_to_goal: A local convex deformation of a fixed positive family with strict compatibility and selected exposed points.
pk-intake-actual-signed-local-masses.statement:
Let $P$, $K_p$, and $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{p\in P}(\{p\}\times K_p)$ satisfy the strict compatibility hypotheses of the open compatibility lemma. Let $\mu_C$ be summed $d$-dimensional Lebesgue measure on its integer fibers and $M=\mu_C(\mathbb R^{n+d})$. Choose finitely many distinct $w_i=(p_i,v_i)$, $p_i\in P$, each exposed in $C$ by an ambient linear functional with unique maximizer $w_i$. Assume $v_i$ has a unique unit supporting normal $u_i$ in $K_{p_i}$, whose support face is $\{v_i\}$, and fix $h_i$ with $u_i\cdot h_i>0$. For each fixed real vector $\xi=(\xi_i)$ and every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ there is an actual convex body $C_\varepsilon$ with nonempty integer fibers of positive volume exactly at $P$, converging fiberwise in Hausdorff distance to $C$. The signed measure $\mu_{C_\varepsilon}-\mu_C$ is a sum of signed restrictions of mixed volume to pairwise disjoint regions shrinking to the respective $w_i$, each of exact signed mass $\varepsilon\xi_i$. In particular $M_\varepsilon=M+\varepsilon\sum_i\xi_i$. For every fixed finite family of closed halfspaces $H$ whose boundaries avoid all $w_i$, one has
$$
\mu_{C_\varepsilon}(H)-\mu_C(H)=\varepsilon\sum_i\xi_i\mathbf1_H(w_i)
$$
for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$. The same identity holds for parallel threshold changes of order $O(\varepsilon)$, comparing the two measures at the same shifted threshold and keeping the old indicators on the right.

Among canonical caps at this point excluding the other core fibers and taking each addition wholly or with zero mass, the exact least extra mass is $a$.

pk-intake-actual-smoothed-source-inside-.statement:

$$
\Psi\left(\frac{s(x-(c+t))+A(z-p)+\varepsilon\sigma f_H}{H}\right),\qquad
\Psi(q)=(q+1)_+-q_+ .

Include closed pure-base caps with their ordinary masses. The unique globally deepest mark for the infimum over these caps is $(0,Y)$ with raw depth $2+Y$. pk-intake-actual-smoothed-triangle-produ.relation_to_goal: This is the positive-width and positive-buffer depth and menu of a fixed four-fiber product. The ordinary mixed problem and any optimization over bodies have different hypotheses.
pk-intake-actual-smoothed-triangle-produ.statement:
Let $B=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0=(-1,-1),v_1=(1,0),v_2=(0,1)\}$ and let $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a triangle of area $V>0$ and centroid $g$. The actual positive-volume lattice fibers of $B\times K$ are the four copies of $K$ at $z=0,v_0,v_1,v_2$. Let $f:K\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous and concave, strictly concave in $\operatorname{int}K$, differentiable and positive near $g$, and invariant under affine barycentric permutations. Use it at each of the four bases. Let $\Gamma(u)=(u^\mathsf T\Sigma u)^{1/2}$ for the covariance $\Sigma$ of uniform probability on $K$, and let $\Psi(t)=\min(1,\max(0,1+t))$. At a mark $(p,x)$, an oblique cap $(a,u)$ with $u\ne0$ has mixed capture
$$
\sum_{z\in B\cap\mathbb Z^2}\int_K\Psi\left(\frac{a\cdot(z-p)+u\cdot(X-x)+\epsilon f(x)\Gamma(u)}{h\Gamma(u)}\right)dX .
$$
Define its mixed depth as the infimum over these caps and the ordinary closed pure-base caps through $p$. Write $\theta_{\epsilon,h}(x)$ for the infimum over $u\ne0$ of the one-fiber term at $p$ and $q_{\epsilon,h}=\theta_{\epsilon,h}(g)$.

For all sufficiently small $\epsilon,h>0$, $g$ uniquely maximizes $\theta_{\epsilon,h}$, and $(0,g)$ is the unique mixed deepest mark, of raw depth $V+q_{\epsilon,h}$, where $q_{\epsilon,h}\to4V/9$ as $(\epsilon,h)\to(0,0)$. At each exposed outer base $v_j$, the pointwise mixed depth is $\theta_{\epsilon,h}$. At $(0,g)$ there is a three-cap menu of minimizing directions $u_j$ with $\Gamma(u_j)=1$, equal positive threshold coareas, continuous balance $\sum_j u_j/3=\epsilon\nabla f(g)=0$, equal response weights $1/3$, and strip base centroid zero for every cap. Cap $j$ is saturated at one on the matched fiber $v_j$ and zero on the other outer fibers. Its own profile is the cyclic barycentric image of the first cap's own profile.

F(1-F)\le27\prod_{i\ne j}b_i.

pk-intake-actual-three-fiber-surface-mid.relation_to_goal: Repair of one prescribed three-fiber boundary martingale. It gives literal closed-halfspace credit and a single actual middle capacity. Different triples sharing a target need a separate joint capacity bound, and supporting allocations need their own implication.
pk-intake-actual-three-fiber-surface-mid.statement:
Let $K_-,K_0,K_+$ be convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, attached to physical bases $-1,0,1$ and satisfying $(K_-+K_+)/2\subset K_0$. The marked bundle records $(u,z,x)$ with $x$ in the exposed face of $K_z$ at $u$. Let $\eta_z$ be the ordinary surface measure of $K_z$ on this bundle, marked by its almost everywhere unique outer normal. Put $\eta=\sum_z\eta_z$ and $\lambda=(u)_\#\eta$. Suppose a finite source measure $\nu$ on the same bundle admits a normal-preserving martingale to $\eta$ in the physical coordinates $(z,x)$. Let $\gamma_-,\gamma_+$ be the two target crossflows from base-zero sources to the respective endpoint bases.

For the given martingale, pair its two endpoint branches conditionally at each base-zero source using any Borel conditional pairing. Let $\rho_{\rm old}$ be the resulting marked midpoint measure, using the mass of one endpoint branch. There is a replacement normal-preserving martingale with the same source $\nu$ and target $\eta$, the same endpoint-source rows and the same two physical crossflow measures. It admits a single pairing of its new two endpoint branches with a marked midpoint law $\rho\le\eta_0$. Relative to $\lambda$, for almost every $u$ the physical conditional laws satisfy $\rho_{{\rm old},u}\preceq_{\rm cx}\rho_u$. If $H$ is any closed halfspace in the physical coordinates, the same pairing gives
$$
\rho(\{(u,0,x):(0,x)\in H\})\ \le\
\sum_{z\in\{-1,1\}}\gamma_z(\{(u,z,x):(z,x)\in H\}).
$$

pk-intake-actual-three-interval-centroid.relation_to_goal: Explicit auxiliary n=d=1 buffered-depth calibration. The middle singleton violates the strict quota and the example has a compatible descent, so it is not a joint body minimum.
pk-intake-actual-three-interval-centroid.statement:

$$
\inf_{(a,u)\ne(0,0)}
 \mu\{(z,X):a(z-p)+u(X-y)+|u|\varepsilon\sqrt{L(p,y)\Sigma E_{K_p}(y)/M}\ge0\},
$$
where $E$ is marked projective energy, with its zero boundary value. Let $\beta$ be the maximum raw buffered depth divided by $M$. At $L=1$, set $\delta=\varepsilon\sqrt{55/24}$ and assume $0<\delta\le1/10$. Then the unique maximizing mark is $Y=(0,2)$, with raw value $Q=5+\delta$ and $\beta=(5+\delta)/12$. On this fixed body $L=1$ minimizes the global buffered maximum over all positive concave physical weights on the full hull with $\int\log L\,d\mu/M=0$. Moreover $\delta_Y\preceq_{\rm cx}\mu/M$ in full physical coordinates, with constant-$L$ contact label zero.

The actual centroid-hull contraction has $K_\pm(t)=[-1+t,1-t]$, $K_0(t)=[-1+t,7-4t]$, and extends as a compatible family for small signed $t$. At fixed $\varepsilon,L=1$ its unique optimizer has height $y(t)=2-t/2$ at base zero, with
$$
\begin{gathered}
M(t)=12-9t,\quad
\Sigma(t)=\frac{2(2-2t)^3+(8-5t)^3}{12(12-9t)},\\
E_t=\frac{4(3-3t/2)(5-7t/2)}{8-5t},\quad
Q(t)=5-7t/2+\delta(t),\qquad
\delta(t)=\varepsilon\sqrt{\Sigma(t)E_t/M(t)}.
\end{gathered}
$$
At zero, $\delta'(0)=-433\delta/880$ and $\beta'(0)=1/48+227\delta/10560>0$. Thus the actual forward contraction increases optimized depth despite global concave-weight optimality and the full volume martingale. The locally feasible reverse path decreases it. In the regular two-cap physical density calibration, all three fiber forces vanish and the centroid-repair integral equals $1/4+227\delta/880=M\beta'(0)$.

pk-intake-actual-tukey-facet-null-critic.statement:
Let $n,d\ge2$, $B$ be the closed unit Euclidean $d$-ball of volume $V$, $0<\varepsilon<1/2$ and $r=\varepsilon^{1/d}$. For the convex body
$$
C=\operatorname{conv}\big(([0,1]^n\times B)\cup(\{2e_1\}\times rB)\big),

pk-intake-adaptive-gaussian-active-cap-f.relation_to_goal: Existing stochastic processes with fixed conditional laws and a fixed finite cap menu. No existence assertion for a chosen adaptive feedback.
pk-intake-adaptive-gaussian-active-cap-f.statement:
Take a finite set $P\subset\mathbb R^n$, positive prior $\pi_z$ and fixed uniform conditional laws on positive compact convex fibers. Let $A_t$ be progressively measurable symmetric positive semidefinite, with $\int_0^T\|A_t\|\,dt<\infty$ almost surely for every finite $T$. Put $Q_t=\int_0^tA_s\,ds$, and assume a finite continuous solution
$$
p_z(t)\propto\pi_z e^{a_t\cdot z-z^{\mathsf T}Q_tz/2},\qquad
m_t=\sum_zp_z(t)z,\qquad da_t=A_tm_t\,dt+A_t^{1/2}dW_t,\quad a_0=0
$$
exists for Brownian motion $W$. For actual fixed closed caps $H_j$, let $g_j(z)=|K_z\cap H_j|/|K_z|$, $G_j=\sum_zp_zg_j(z)$, and $c_j=\operatorname{Cov}_{p}(g_j,z)$. Then $dp_z=p_z(z-m)^{\mathsf T}A^{1/2}dW$ and $dG_j=c_j^{\mathsf T}A^{1/2}dW$, with $d\langle G_i,G_j\rangle=c_i^{\mathsf T}Ac_j\,dt$. These are bounded martingales. All $G_j$ in a finite menu are pathwise constant if and only if $\operatorname{range}(A_t)\subseteq\operatorname{span}\{c_j(p_t)\}^{\perp}$ almost everywhere for $dt\,d\mathbb P$. The same condition is equivalent to preserving the initially active bounds $G_j(t)\le G_j(0)$ almost surely for all $t$.

pk-intake-adjacent-centroid-complementar.statement:

Both are nonempty compact convex sets. If $g_x=M^{-1}\int x\,d\mu$, then
$$
\mathcal B=\frac{g_x-\theta\mathcal A}{1-\theta}.
$$
For every $u\ne0$, the maximizing source in direction $u$ for $\mathcal A$ is unique up to $\mu$-null sets. It is the restriction to an actual closed cap with continuous normal $u$. The opposite closed cap uniquely maximizes the opposite direction for $\mathcal B$. The same finite affine hyperplane partitions $C$ into the two corresponding convex bodies with null mixed overlap.

pk-intake-adjacent-edge-lorentz-ear-firs.statement:

$$
k=|K|,\qquad Q_i=|K\cap\{v_i\cdot x\ge0\}|,\qquad
\sigma_i=\mathcal H^1(K\cap v_i^\perp)/\lVert v_i\rVert .

Use the normals $(1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1)$. The canonical vertices for row $1$ are
$$
P_1=(2v+w,-v-w),\qquad P_2=(-x,x+s),\qquad P_3=(-x,-s-w),
\qquad x,s,v>0,\quad w\ge0.

Write $p=2v+w$, $L=x+p$, $H=x+s+w+v$, $B=x+2s+w$ and $k_0=LB/2$. For $j=2,3$ write $l$ for the other index in $\{2,3\}$, and put $n_2=v$, $n_3=v+w$. For each fixed $\theta\in[n_j/H,p/L]$ and $Q_0=(1-\theta)P_1+\theta P_l$, set
$$
Q_\varepsilon=Q_0+(\varepsilon/k_0)(Q_0-P_j),\qquad
K_\varepsilon=\operatorname{conv}(P_1,P_2,P_3,Q_\varepsilon).
$$

pk-intake-adjacent-integer-top-mass-equa.relation_to_goal: An integer marginal feasibility and equality lemma for realizing adjacent mixed centroids.
pk-intake-adjacent-integer-top-mass-equa.statement: Let $Z$ have a finitely supported integer-valued probability law of mean $\theta\in(0,1)$. Among dominated sublaws of mass $\theta$, let $U$ be the largest first moment. The top selection, filling the largest sites first with at most one partially retained site, attains $U$. pk-intake-affine-arithmetic-penalty.relation_to_goal: This is an auxiliary affine-parameter extremum with a penalty. It gives geometric properness of own traces.
pk-intake-affine-arithmetic-penalty.statement:
Let $P$ be a finite complete affine-lattice base, $m=|P|$, $d\ge1$, $N=d+1$, and $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Range over all actual positive compatible convex $d$-fibers $K_z$ at $z\in P$, with volumes $V_z$, total mass $M$, and ordinary maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth $\beta_0(K)$. Let $\beta_0^*=\inf_K\beta_0(K)<b$. Assume the original sublevel $\{\beta_0\le b\}$ admits a compact positive representative frame under invertible maps $(z,X)\mapsto(z,AX+s(z))$ with $s$ affine, with $M=1$, $V_z\ge v>0$ and $K_z\subset RB_d$ in the frame. Write $L=m\kappa_{d-1}R^{d-1}$, where $\kappa_j$ is the unit $j$-ball volume and $\kappa_0=1$.

Take positive affine $\ell$ on $\operatorname{conv}(P)$ with $\sum_z w_z\log\ell_z=0$, where $w_z=V_z/M$. Put $A_\ell=\sum_z w_z\ell_z$. Let $\beta_\varepsilon$ be the maximum normalized depth using unchanged pure-base caps and enlarging every nonvertical through-mark cap at $(p,y)$ by $\varepsilon f(p,y)G_K(u)$ in its affine margin, where $f=(\ell_pE_{K_p}(y)/M)^{1/N}$, $E$ is marked projective energy extended by zero to the own boundary, and $G_K(u)$ is the pooled within-fiber covariance norm. Use the whole-base trace in rank zero.

For all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, the infimum of $J_\varepsilon=\beta_\varepsilon+\varepsilon^2(A_\ell-1)$ is attained and is in $[\beta_0^*,\beta_0^*+\varepsilon LR]$. At every minimizing pair, in the frame,
$$
A_\ell\le1+LR/\varepsilon,\qquad
\varepsilon f(p,y)G_K(u)\le\Delta_\varepsilon:=\varepsilon R(1+LR/\varepsilon)^{1/N}\quad(\|u\|=1).
$$
Put $c=\gamma_d/m$. If $L\Delta_\varepsilon<c/4$, every maximizing mark of $\beta_\varepsilon$ at such a pair has own-boundary distance at least $3c/(4L)$ and every shifted own nonvertical trace cuts the own fiber interior.
