pk-intake-affine-base-weighted-projectiv.relation_to_goal: Canonical body-tied energy, with a separately chosen positive concave base multiplier. The source chart matches the own-fiber optimizer and does not assert an orbit minimum or any row-density contact identity.
pk-intake-affine-base-weighted-projectiv.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $N=d+1$, and let $C$ be the canonical convex hull of a finite compatible family of positive-volume compact convex $d$-fibers $K_z$ at bases $P$. Write $B=\operatorname{conv}P$, $V_z=|K_z|$, $M=\sum_{z\in P}V_z$, and $E(z,x)=E_{C_z}(x)$ for ordinary projective energy, extended by zero at the own-fiber boundary. At each own-interior point let $a(z,x)$ be its unique optimal covector. In each fiber, a positive $C^1$ function satisfies $\nabla_x f=fa$ throughout its interior exactly when $f(z,x)=c(z)E(z,x)^{1/N}$ with $c(z)>0$ independent of $x$.

If $\ell$ is a positive continuous concave function on $B$, then $f_\ell=(\ell E/M)^{1/N}$ is jointly concave and continuous on $C$, vanishes at the own-fiber boundaries and satisfies this alignment. When $\ell$ is affine and $\sum_{z\in P}V_z\ell(z)=M$, its parameter domain is
$$
\ell(z)=1+b\cdot(z-\bar g)>0\text{ on }B,\qquad
\bar g=M^{-1}\sum_{z\in P}V_z z,\qquad b\in\operatorname{span}(B-B).
$$
The domain is bounded and its closure is the compact domain with $\ell\ge0$.

Write $F=E^{1/d}$. At a sampled own-interior mark $(p,y)$, let $L_F$ be a nonnegative affine upper tangent ratio, meaning $F(z,x)\le F(p,y)L_F(z,x)$ and $L_F(p,y)=1$. Such a ratio exists. If $\ell$ is positive affine, an affine upper tangent ratio for $f_\ell$ is
$$
L=\frac{d}{N}L_F+\frac1N\frac{\ell(z)}{\ell(p)}\ \ge\ \frac{\min_B\ell}{N\ell(p)}>0.
$$
On the source fiber this is exactly $1+a(p,y)\cdot(x-y)$.

Finally, for $f=(E/M)^r$, $r>0$, assume buffered cap traces on a source fiber have margins $u_j\cdot(x-y)+\varepsilon f(p,y)$, with weights $\rho_j$ summing to one and $\sum_j\rho_ju_j=\varepsilon\nabla_x f(p,y)$. Their continuous normals after the source projective map have weighted sum $\varepsilon(Nr-1)f(p,y)a(p,y)$.

pk-intake-affine-buffer-optimum-without-.statement:
At bases $z=-1,0,1$ take the actual interval fibers $K_-=K_+=[-1,1]$ and $K_0=[-1,2]$ of their lifted convex hull. Their total length is $M=7$. Write $k(T)$ for the number of parity classes occupied by $T\subseteq P=\{-1,0,1\}$. Every nonempty proper closed minor $T=P\cap\operatorname{conv}(T)$ has mass strictly less than $k(T)M/2$, and the actual fiber-centroid graph is nonaffine.

For a positive affine multiplier $\ell$ on $[-1,1]$ impose $\ell(-1)^2\ell(0)^3\ell(1)^2=1$. At a mark $(p,y)$ use the raw buffered depth
$$
b_{\varepsilon,\ell}(p,y)
=\inf_{(a,u)\ne(0,0)}
\mu\!\left(\left\{(z,X):a(z-p)+u(X-y)+
\varepsilon |u|\sqrt{\Sigma\,\ell(p)E_{K_p}(y)/M}\ge0\right\}\right),
$$
where $\mu$ is the sum of original fiber lengths, $\Sigma=43/84$ is the volume-weighted within-fiber variance, and $E_{K_p}$ is the marked projective energy. For an interval of length $V$ and center $m$, this energy equals $V-4(y-m)^2/V$ on the closed interval.

$$
\min\{5,\ U(y-\delta)+J(y-\delta),\ L(y+\delta)+J(-y-\delta)\},
$$
where $U(h)=\min\{3,(2-h)_+\}$, $L(h)=\min\{3,(h+1)_+\}$, and $J(h)=\min\{2,2(1-h)_+\}$.

For every $0<\varepsilon\le10^{-4}$, the maximum of $b_{\varepsilon,\ell}$ over admissible marks is uniquely minimized by $\ell=1$ on the entire normalized affine parameter domain. $$
t=43\varepsilon^2/1764,\qquad
\delta_\varepsilon=\frac{t+\sqrt{35t+36t^2}}{2(1+t)}.

pk-intake-affine-cone-centered-energy.relation_to_goal: A continuous affine-cone energy estimate for arbitrary probability laws on finite slopes, including unbounded support and an atom at zero.
pk-intake-affine-cone-centered-energy.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$ and $H>0$. Put $B=H+1$ and $r(z)=(H-z)/B$. On $-1\le z\le H$, $|x|\le r(z)$, take density $f(x,z)=r(z)^{d-2}/2$ with respect to $dx\,dz$. The total mass is $V=B/d$. For finite $s\ge0$, let $P(s)$ be the mass of the cap $z+sx\ge0$. Let $C(s)$ and $M(s)$ be the integrals of $f$ and $zf$, respectively, over the section $z+sx=0$ inside the support, against $d\mathcal H^1/\sqrt{1+s^2}$. The records of a probability law are the averages of $(P,C,M)$, and the law is centered if its averaged $M$ is zero. Write $C_0=(H/B)^{d-1}$ and $p_0=(H/B)^d$.

For a probability law on finite slopes, let $\phi$ be the mixture of uniform probability laws on $[-s,s]$ with the given slope weights and with $\delta_0$ at $s=0$. Put $v=\phi((-\infty,1])$, $a_0=1/B$, and $e(q)=\int_{b\le1}(1-qb)^{-d}\,d\phi(b)$ for $0<q<1$. Then $1/2<v\le1$ and the averaged records are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overline P/V &= p_0e(a_0)+1-v,\\
\overline C/C_0 &= e(a_0),\\
\overline M/C_0 &= -\frac HB\int_{b\le1} b(1-b/B)^{-d-1}\,d\phi(b).
\end{aligned}
$$

The function $e$ is convex and differentiable on $(0,1)$. Centering is equivalent to $e'(a_0)=0$, or equivalently to $a_0$ minimizing $e$ on $(0,1)$. Every such centered law satisfies $2v-1\le e(a_0)\le(2v-1)/v$.

pk-intake-affine-frustum-truncation-comp.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$, $H>0$ and $0<U<H$. Put $B=H+1$ and $r(z)=(H-z)/B$. On $-1\le z\le U$, $|x|\le r(z)$, use the measure of density $f(x,z)=r(z)^{d-2}/2$ with respect to $dx\,dz$. Set $a=r(U)$, $T=U/a$, $t=a^d=[H/(B+T)]^d$, $V_0=B/d$, and $V=(1-t)V_0$. The associated cone has the same density formula on $-1\le z\le H$, $|x|\le r(z)$, and mass $V_0$.

For a finite slope $s\ge0$, let $P(s)$ be the mass of $z+sx\ge0$. Let $C(s)$ and $M(s)$ be the integrals of $f$ and $zf$, respectively, over the section $z+sx=0$ inside the support, against $d\mathcal H^1/\sqrt{1+s^2}$. A law's record is the average of $(P,C,M)$, and a law is centered if its averaged $M$ is zero.

For $T\ge1$, let $\mu,\nu$ be separately centered probability laws on cone slopes $[0,T]$. Use $P_\mu^c,P_\nu^c,C_\mu,C_\nu$ for their averaged cone cap and coarea records. If $P_\mu^f,P_\nu^f$ denote the corresponding frustum cap records, the coareas are the same, and

$$
\begin{aligned}
\beta_c&=\frac{C_\nu P_\mu^c+C_\mu(V_0-P_\nu^c)}{V_0(C_\mu+C_\nu)},&
\omega&=\frac{C_\nu}{C_\mu+C_\nu},\\
\beta_f&=\frac{C_\nu P_\mu^f+C_\mu(V-P_\nu^f)}{V(C_\mu+C_\nu)}
       =\frac{\beta_c-t\omega}{1-t}.
\end{aligned}
$$

For arbitrary separately centered frustum laws, use their record-preserving representatives on $[0,T]\cup\{\infty\}$ and write $\lambda_\mu,\lambda_\nu$ for their finite masses. If both are positive, let $\beta_f$ in the next formula be the bounded frustum ratio of their conditional finite laws, and $C_\mu,C_\nu$ their conditional finite coareas. The ratio for the original pair is

$$
\frac12+\frac{\lambda_\mu\lambda_\nu(C_\mu+C_\nu)}
{\lambda_\mu C_\mu+\lambda_\nu C_\nu}\left(\beta_f-\frac12\right).
$$

If exactly one law has zero coarea, the ratio is $1/2$. If both have zero coarea, the literal quotient has zero denominator, and its continuous extension has value $1/2$. Each cap record in that case is $V/2$. For $T\le1$ the positive-denominator ratio for any separately centered pair is $1/2$, with the same extension at zero total coarea.

In the $T\ge1$ case, any common correction $c$ giving $P-cC\in[\beta V,(1-\beta)V]$ on the centered bounded frustum laws extends to all centered laws when $\beta\le1/2$.

pk-intake-affine-frustum-upper-tangent-d.relation_to_goal: Upper corrected-cap bound in a proved branch and a conditional upper certificate in the remaining branch of an auxiliary weighted profile.
pk-intake-affine-frustum-upper-tangent-d.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$ and $0<a<1$. Let $H=(1-a)/a$, $r(z)=(H-z)/(H+1)$ and consider the cone $-1\le z\le H$, $|x|\le r(z)$, with planar density $f(x,z)=r(z)^{d-2}/2$. For $s\ge0$, let $P(s)$ be the mass of $z+sx\ge0$, and $C(s),M(s)$ the section integrals of $f,zf$, respectively, with respect to $d\mathcal H^1/\sqrt{1+s^2}$. Put $V_0=(H+1)/d$, $C_0=(1-a)^{d-1}$ and $p=(1-a)^d$. For $s>0$ define
$$
e_s=\frac1{2s}\int_{-s}^{\min(s,1)}(1-ab)^{-d}\,db,\qquad
m_s=\partial_a e_s,\qquad k_s=\frac{(s-1)_+}{2s},\qquad v_s=1-k_s.
$$
At $s=0$ set $(e_0,m_0,k_0)=(1,0,0)$. Thus $e_s=C(s)/C_0$ and $M(s)/C_0=-(1-a)m_s/d$. A centered law is a probability law with average section moment zero.

Suppose $0<a<1/d$ and let $s_*>1$ be the unique positive centered slope. Put $R=1+as_*$, $e_*=e_{s_*}$, $v_*=v_{s_*}$ and $t_*=p/R^d$. For a cutoff $T\ge s_*$, set
$$
t=\frac{p}{(1+aT)^d},\quad \kappa=\frac{v_*+t}{1+e_*},\quad B=1+t-\kappa,\quad
\eta=\frac{aR^{d+1}(\kappa/p-1)}{d(R-1)^2},\quad
L(s)=B-\kappa e_s-k_s+a\eta m_s.
$$
For $s\ge1$ and $q=1+as$, set $\Psi(q)=[(\kappa+d\eta)q-(d-1)\eta]q^{-d}$. Then
$$
2(q-1)L(s)=\frac{\Psi(q)-\Psi(R)-\Psi'(R)(q-R)}{d-1}.
$$
If $\kappa\le p$, then $L(s)\ge0$ for all finite $s\ge0$. If $\kappa\ge p$, the same conclusion holds provided
$$
B-\kappa-(\kappa-2\eta)_+[E(a)-1]\ge0,\qquad
E(z)=\frac{(1-z)^{1-d}-(1+z)^{1-d}}{2z(d-1)},\quad E(0)=1.
$$
In either proved case, $\mathbb E[\kappa e_s+k_s]\le B$ for all centered laws on $[0,T]$. In the proper frustum with $U=HT/(H+1+T)$ and volume $V=(1-t)V_0$ this is the upper corrected-cap bound $P_f-cC_f\le(1-\gamma)V$ on the averaged records of every centered frustum law on $[0,\infty]$, for $c=(V_0/C_0)(p-\kappa)$ and $\gamma=(\kappa-t)/(1-t)$.

For a fixed $d,a$ with $\kappa_1=(v_*+t_*)/(1+e_*)>p$, the only additional test needed by this sufficient condition over the whole cutoff range is its value at $\kappa=\kappa_1$, and only when $0<2\eta(\kappa_1)<\kappa_1$.

pk-intake-affine-interval-depth.relation_to_goal: Exact optimization in the affine planar interval model.
pk-intake-affine-interval-depth.statement:
Let a planar compact convex body have exactly $N$ nonempty sampled integer fibers, at consecutive sites. Suppose all have positive length, with affine midpoint heights and affine widths. Use the sum of fiber lengths as mass, and closed ambient halfspaces for depth. Subtract the affine center graph, reverse the base when needed, and for a nonconstant width profile divide by its positive increment. Write the resulting lengths as $w_i=q+i$ for $0\le i<N$, with $q>0$. At base $j$ the midpoint attains the largest raw depth in its interval, namely
$$
D_j(q)=\min\left\{\sum_{i<j}w_i+w_j/2,\ \sum_{i>j}w_i+w_j/2,\ T_{j,k}(q)\ (k\ne j)\right\},
$$
where every sum uses $0,\ldots,N-1$ and
$$
T_{j,k}(q)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\sum_{i<k}\min\{q+i,(k-i)(q+j)/(2(k-j))\},&k>j,\\
\displaystyle\sum_{i>k}\min\{q+i,(i-k)(q+j)/(2(j-k))\},&k<j.
\end{cases}
$$
Each $D_j$ is concave and piecewise affine with rational coefficients. The normalized maximum $\max_j D_j/[Nq+N(N-1)/2]$ is piecewise linear-fractional with finitely many rational breakpoints and is monotone or constant on each piece. For constant positive widths the normalized maximum is $1/2$ for odd $N$ and $(N-1)/(2N)$ for even $N$.

pk-intake-affine-intrinsic-volume-root-c.relation_to_goal: A sharp-form lower bound weighted by the mass on a single affine volume-root contact set.
pk-intake-affine-intrinsic-volume-root-c.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact and convex, $n\ge0$ and $d\ge1$, with nonempty mixed trace $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. For each nonempty integer fiber $K_z$, let $q$ be the maximum affine dimension of these fibers, and assume $q\ge1$. Put $a_z=\mathcal H_q(K_z)$, $r_z=a_z^{1/q}$ and $M=\mathcal H_q(S)=\sum_z a_z$. Suppose an affine function $\ell:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ satisfies $\ell(z)\ge r_z$ at every nonempty integer fiber. Set $E=\{z:\ell(z)=r_z>0\}$, $W_E=\sum_{z\in E}a_z$ and let $g_z$ be the intrinsic centroid of $K_z$ for $z\in E$.

If $z_i\in E$ and $w=\sum_i\lambda_i z_i\in\mathbb Z^n$ with $\lambda_i>0$ and $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$, then $w\in E$, $K_w=\sum_i\lambda_i K_{z_i}$ and $g_w=\sum_i\lambda_i g_{z_i}$. The participating fibers have parallel affine hulls and are positive homothets. In particular $\operatorname{conv}(E)\cap\mathbb Z^n=E$, and the mixed trace of the convex hull of $T_E=\{(z,g_z):z\in E\}$ is exactly $T_E$.

If $E$ is nonempty, some $y\in T_E$ satisfies $\mathcal H_q(S\cap H)\ge\gamma_q W_E/2^n$ for every closed ambient halfspace $H$ containing $y$, where $\gamma_j=(j/(j+1))^j$. Its normalized depth is at least $\gamma_q W_E/(2^n M)\ge\gamma_d W_E/(2^n M)$. In particular $W_E=M$ when all positive fibers are contacts. If $E$ is empty, the zero lower bound holds at any actual point of $S$.

pk-intake-affine-inverse-power-boundary-.relation_to_goal: This is the sharp threshold for detecting every affine zero on a full-dimensional sampled fiber by inverse-power integration. It includes joint body and affine-coefficient limits.
pk-intake-affine-inverse-power-boundary-.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body. If $h$ is nonnegative affine on $D$ and vanishes somewhere on $D$, then $\int_Dh^{-r}\,dx=+\infty$ for every $r\ge d$. When $h$ is nonconstant, the cone lower bound has logarithmic divergence at $r=d$. If convex bodies $D_j$ converge in Hausdorff distance to $D$ and affine $h_j>0$ on $D_j$ converge coefficientwise to such an $h$, then $\int_{D_j}h_j^{-r}\,dx\to+\infty$.

For each $0<r<d$ the standard simplex $D=\{x_i\ge0,\ \sum_i x_i\le1\}$ has positive affine $h_\delta=\delta+\sum_i x_i$, $\delta>0$, with $|D|^{-1}\int_D h_\delta^{-r}\,dx\to d/(d-r)$ as $\delta\downarrow0$. Thus inverse-power-mean-one positive affine functions can converge to a finite affine function vanishing at a vertex in that exponent range.

pk-intake-affine-label-preserving-projec.relation_to_goal: Exact calculations for a fixed-label map and two cap or compatibility obstructions in the auxiliary chart model.
pk-intake-affine-label-preserving-projec.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, be nonempty compact convex fibers. Write $L(z,X)=\ell(z)+c\cdot X$, where $\ell(z)=b+\beta\cdot z$ and $L>0$ on the placed fibers, hence on their convex hull. On the fixed fiber $z$, $T_z(X)=X/L(z,X)$ has signed Jacobian $\ell(z)L(z,X)^{-d-1}$. If $\ell(z)\ne0$, its inverse on the image is $X=\ell(z)Y/(1-c\cdot Y)$ and its image is convex. Positivity of $L$ allows collapse when $\ell(z)=0$.

Assume now that $\ell>0$ at every sampled base. The label-preserving images $J_z=T_z(K_z)$ are compatible, meaning $\sum_j\lambda_jJ_{z_j}\subseteq J_q$ for each anchored relation $q=\sum_j\lambda_j z_j\in P$, $\lambda_j\ge0$, $\sum_j\lambda_j=1$, if and only if for every such relation and $X_j\in K_{z_j}$,
$$
\frac{\ell(q)\sum_j\lambda_j X_j/L(z_j,X_j)}{\sum_j\lambda_j\ell(z_j)/L(z_j,X_j)}\in K_q.
$$
Equivalently, for every $v\in\mathbb R^d$ the support $\alpha_z(v)$ is the unique solution of $h_{K_z}(v-\alpha c)=\alpha\ell(z)$, and compatibility holds exactly when $\alpha_q(v)\ge\sum_j\lambda_j\alpha_{z_j}(v)$ for every extreme anchored representation and every $v$. For polytopes the maximum defining $\alpha_z(v)$ occurs at an original vertex. If $K_z=\ell(z)K$ with $1+c\cdot X>0$ on $K$, then all $J_z$ coincide and are compatible.

A closed cap $a\cdot z+u\cdot X\ge h$ transforms on the positive chart into $a\cdot z-h+[\ell(z)u-(a\cdot z-h)c]\cdot Y\ge0$. This expression is affine if $u\beta^{\mathsf T}-ca^{\mathsf T}=0$. A positive denominator depending on $X$ can destroy compatibility even under strict proper closed-minor quotas, and it can send a cap to a nonconvex set or to traces that are not those of a single halfspace even for compatible image fibers. For a full-dimensional fiber, $T_z$ pushes $dX/L$ to $\ell(z)^{d-1}(1-c\cdot Y)^{-d}\,dY$ on $J_z$, with density ratio $(\max_{K_z}L/\min_{K_z}L)^d$. This ratio is unbounded under positivity alone. For $c=0$ the density is $\ell(z)^{d-1}$, equal across labels when $d=1$.

pk-intake-affine-log-normalization-deriv.relation_to_goal: These are conditional scalar chain rules, before applying an actual cover or an extremum principle.
pk-intake-affine-log-normalization-deriv.statement:
Let $V_z(t)>0$ be differentiable volumes indexed by finitely many bases, $M=\sum_z V_z$, $w_z=V_z/M$, and $E_z(t)>0$ differentiable fixed-mark energies. Suppose $V_z'=-D_z$, $D=\sum_zD_z$, $E_z'=-C_z$ at the old pair. Let $\ell_z>0$ be affine samples with $\sum_z w_z\log\ell_z=0$, $A_\ell=\sum_z w_z\ell_z$ and $f_z=(\ell_zE_z/M)^{1/N}$ with $N=d+1$. Rescaling a fixed affine shape by a common factor to preserve the logarithmic constraint gives
$$
s:=\ell_z'/\ell_z=M^{-1}\sum_zD_z\log\ell_z,\qquad
f_z'/f_z=(-C_z/E_z+D/M+s)/N,\qquad
A_\ell'=M^{-1}\sum_zD_z[A_\ell(1+\log\ell_z)-\ell_z].
$$
At a fixed body the geometrically normalized affine path with raw values $\ell_z+t\phi(z)$ instead gives $\ell_z'=\phi(z)-\ell_zA_\phi$ and $A_\ell'=\sum_z w_z\phi(z)-A_\ell A_\phi$, with $A_\phi=\sum_z w_z\phi(z)/\ell_z$.

pk-intake-affine-ordinary-maximal-depth-.relation_to_goal: Depth retained by positive contacts of one affine majorant of the sampled own-depth roots. The equal-depth hypothesis retains all positive intrinsic mass.
pk-intake-affine-ordinary-maximal-depth-.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact and convex, $n\ge0$, $d\ge1$. Let $P=\{z\in\mathbb Z^n:K_z\ne\varnothing\}$, where $K_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$, and let $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. Suppose $q=\max_{z\in P}\dim K_z\ge1$. For each $q$-dimensional fiber, let $V_z=\mathcal H_q(K_z)$, let $A_z$ be its raw ordinary intrinsic maximal depth, and let $g_z$ be its unique deepest point. Set $m_z=A_z^{1/q}$ on these fibers and $A_z=m_z=0$ on the other nonempty fibers.

Suppose an affine function $\ell$ satisfies $\ell(z)\ge m_z$ for all $z\in P$ and $Q=\{z\in P:m_z=\ell(z)>0\}$ is nonempty. Then $Q=\operatorname{conv}Q\cap\mathbb Z^n$. Let $k_Q$ be the number of base parities in $Q$ and $B_Q=\sum_{z\in Q} A_z$. There exists $z\in Q$ such that
$$
h_{\mathcal H_q|_S}(z,g_z)\ge \frac{B_Q}{k_Q}
\ge \frac{\gamma_q}{k_Q}\sum_{w\in Q}V_w,\qquad
\gamma_q=\left(\frac{q}{q+1}\right)^q,
$$
where the depth takes the infimum over closed ambient halfspaces containing the mark. If all contact fibers have the same intrinsic direction space, one can choose a point whose depth is strictly greater than $B_Q/k_Q$ unless the lifted graph consists of $k_Q$ vertices with weights $A_z$ all equal. In particular strictness holds in this common-direction case when $|Q|>k_Q$.

If every $q$-dimensional integer fiber has the same raw maximal depth $A_*>0$, take $P_+=\{z\in P:\dim K_z=q\}$ and let $k$ count its occupied parities. There is an actual mark with raw $\mathcal H_q$ depth at least $|P_+|A_*/k\ge \gamma_q\mathcal H_q(S)/k\ge\gamma_d\mathcal H_q(S)/2^n$. One can choose the mark with depth strictly greater than $|P_+|A_*/k$ whenever the positive fibers share a direction space and $|P_+|>k$.

pk-intake-affine-power-inner-cdf.relation_to_goal: Scalar affine-power laws only. This lemma supplies the shared numerical endpoint estimate used by the two localization arguments.
pk-intake-affine-power-inner-cdf.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ be an integer, $0\le r<1$, and let $G$ be the CDF of the probability density $f(t)=dt^{d-1}/(1-r^d)$ on $[r,1]$. Its mean is $m=\frac{d}{d+1}\frac{1-r^{d+1}}{1-r^d}$. With $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, one has $r\le2m-1<1$ and
$$
G(2m-1)\le1-2\gamma_d.
$$

pk-intake-affine-radius-pointwise-defici.relation_to_goal: One fixed halfspace through the central simplex centroid with a normalized nonnegative continuous normal and base coefficient −β for β≥0. The comparison is between exact signed cap surpluses on the same finite base list. The scalar diagonal envelope and the all-orientation actual-depth application are separate.
pk-intake-affine-radius-pointwise-defici.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and $m\ge0$ be integers. Put $T_d=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)$, $V_d=1/d!$ and $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Take finite radii $R=r_0\ge r_1\ge\cdots\ge r_m\ge0$ with $R>0$ and with the drops $r_{h-1}-r_h$ nondecreasing in $h$. At each of the integer bases $-h$ and $h+1$, for $0\le h\le m$, take the fiber $r_hT_d$. Let $\mu$ denote the sum of the $d$-dimensional Lebesgue measures of these fibers.

Fix $u\in[0,\infty)^d$ with $\sum_i u_i=1$ and fix $\beta\ge0$. With $t=R/(d+1)$, the closed halfspace $H=\{(z,x):-\beta z+u\cdot x\ge t\}$ passes through $y=(0,t,\ldots,t)$, the actual centroid at base $0$. For $r\ge0$, $s\in\mathbb R$ and $h\ge0$, put
$$
F_r(s)=\frac{\operatorname{vol}_d(rT_d\cap\{x:u\cdot x\ge s\})}{V_d},
\qquad
G_h(r)=F_r(t-\beta h)+F_r(t+\beta(h+1))-\Gamma_d r^d .
$$
For $m\ge1$ there is a slope $a\in[0,R/m]$ such that $\ell_h=R-ah$ satisfies
$$
G_h(\ell_h)\le G_h(r_h)\qquad(0\le h\le m).
$$
The slope can be chosen with $\ell_h$ between $r_h$ and the unique minimizer of $G_h$ on $[0,\infty)$ for each $1\le h\le m$. For every such choice, equality in the comparison at an index holds exactly when $\ell_h=r_h$. Equality in the sum for such a choice is attainable exactly when the original radii are already affine in $h$. For $m=0$ leave the radius unchanged.

The replacement is realized by a compact convex body with the indicated fibers at the same integer bases and no other integer fibers. It retains $y$ and the very same $H$. The original signed cap surplus relative to the fraction $\Gamma_d/2$ is $V_d\sum_{h=0}^m G_h(r_h)$, with the identical formula using $\ell_h$ for the replacement. Hence an original cap below that fraction yields a replacement cap below the same fraction, measured against the replacement's own total mass.

pk-intake-affine-rank-at-most-two-midpoi.relation_to_goal: Closure for components of the midpoint hypergraph in low affine rank. Completeness refers to the ambient integer lattice.
pk-intake-affine-rank-at-most-two-midpoi.statement: Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite, nonempty and complete, so $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$. Give $P$ a hyperedge $\{p,q,(p+q)/2\}$ for each distinct same-parity pair $p,q\in P$. If a connected component $C$ has affine dimension at most two, then $\operatorname{conv}(C)\cap\mathbb Z^n=C$.

pk-intake-affine-sampled-support-normal-.relation_to_goal: Actual polytopal mixed fibers and a supplied marked boundary martingale. The reduced law is an intrinsic volume transport with equal mass and affine moments. Deriving a new reduced boundary stress or a bound from original bulk cap budgets requires additional input.
pk-intake-affine-sampled-support-normal-.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body, $d\ge1$, and let $P$ be all its nonempty integer bases. Assume $P\ne\varnothing$ and all its fibers $K_p$ are full-dimensional compact polytopes in $\mathbb R^d$. Write $C_0=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{p\in P}(\{p\}\times K_p)$, and let $\eta$ be the sum of the own-fiber $\mathcal H^{d-1}$ boundary measures with the regular continuous outward unit normal marked. Suppose a finite source $\nu\ll\eta$ is coupled to $\eta$ by a physical martingale $\Pi$ preserving this mark.

Fix a unit vector $u$ and suppose $h_{K_p}(u)=a\cdot p+b$ for every $p\in P$. The plane $u\cdot x-a\cdot z=b$ supports $C_0$. Write $F_u$ for its exposed face and assume $\eta(F_u)>0$. The restrictions of $\eta$ and $\nu$ to $F_u$ are their entire normal-$u$ sectors up to null sets. There are zero crossings in both directions for $\Pi$, so $\nu(F_u)=\eta(F_u)$, and the restricted rows couple $\nu|_{F_u}$ to the full target $\eta|_{F_u}$.

For a linear isometry $E:\mathbb R^{d-1}\to u^\perp$, set $\Psi(z,t)=(z,Et+(a\cdot z+b)u)$ and $D=\Psi^{-1}(F_u)$. The pulled-back target is $\mu_u=\sum_{p\in P}\mathcal H^{d-1}|_{D_p}$, the intrinsic Hausdorff measure of the reduced trace, and $\widehat\nu_u=(\Psi^{-1})_\#(\nu|_{F_u})\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}}\mu_u$ with equal mass and affine physical moments. The measure identity includes zero-weight smaller faces and uses endpoint counting when $d=1$. If $\operatorname{aff}P=\mathbb R^n$, $F_u$ is a nonvertical supporting facet and $D$ is a full-dimensional polytope in $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^{d-1}$. If $d\nu=\sum_j\lambda_j\alpha_j\,d\eta$ is an actual cap-allocation law, its reduced density is $\sum_j\lambda_j(\alpha_j\circ\Psi)$. A cap $c_j\cdot z+v_j\cdot x\ge\beta_j$ restricts to
$$
(c_j+(v_j\cdot u)a)\cdot z+(E^{\mathsf T}v_j)\cdot t
\ge \beta_j-(v_j\cdot u)b,
$$
with the original allocation on coincident positive-measure boundaries and indicator agreement almost everywhere for null equality loci.

If the sampled support is affine in the base for every unit direction, the canonical fiber at every $z=\sum_p\theta_p p$ in $\operatorname{conv}P$ is the Minkowski combination $\sum_p\theta_pK_p$, independently of the representation. The boundary coupling decomposes into finitely many such unweighted-target volume transports. With full base span, each nonvertical facet is the common support face $F_u$ for its continuous unit normal $u$, projects onto all of $\operatorname{conv}P$, and has a different continuous unit normal from every other nonvertical facet. Almost every measured own-fiber boundary point then has a unique nonvertical facet owner.

pk-intake-affine-score-moment-partition.relation_to_goal: Realizes exact masses and base moments for intrinsic mixed measure. The result gives no lower bound on centroid halfspace depth and no recursive single-cut construction.
pk-intake-affine-score-moment-partition.statement:
Let $n,d$ be positive integers and let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body. Put $\Lambda=\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, $S=C\cap\Lambda$, and assume $q=\dim_{\mathrm H}S\ge 1$. Set $\mu=\mathcal H_q|_S$. For $z\in\mathbb Z^n$ put $K_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$, and let $P=\{z:w_z=\mathcal H_q(K_z)>0\}$.

Suppose finitely many labeled mass and base moment pairs $(t_i,m_i)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n$ are feasible: there are $s_{iz}\ge 0$ with $\sum_i s_{iz}=w_z$ for $z\in P$ and $(t_i,m_i)=\sum_{z\in P}s_{iz}(1,z)$ for every label. Discard the labels with $t_i=0$ and index the remaining $k$ labels by $1,\ldots,k$. Fix any vectors $u_i\in\mathbb R^d$ such that $x\mapsto(u_i-u_j)\cdot x$ is nonconstant on each $K_z$ for $z\in P$ whenever $i\ne j$.

There are finite $\theta_i\in\mathbb R^{n+1}$ such that the affine scores $L_i(z,x)=\theta_i\cdot(1,z)+u_i\cdot x$ give closed cells
$$
D_i=C\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{(z,x):L_i(z,x)\ge L_j(z,x)\}.
$$
Each $D_i$ is an ambient convex body cut from $C$ by at most $k-1$ closed halfspaces, and $D_i\cap\Lambda$ has Hausdorff dimension $q$. The cells satisfy
$$
\bigcup_iD_i=C,\qquad
\mu(D_i\cap D_j)=0\quad(i\ne j),\qquad
\left(\mu(D_i),\int_{D_i} z\,d\mu\right)=(t_i,m_i).
$$
In particular they exhaust the mixed measure. The centroid of $\mathcal H_q|_{D_i\cap\Lambda}$ belongs to $D_i$, has base $m_i/t_i$, and lies in $D_i\cap\Lambda$ if that base is integral. Suitable $u_i$ always exist.

pk-intake-affine-section-radial-layer-st.relation_to_goal: Requires a supplied affine interior section and positive full-dimensional fibers; preserves only constant-fraction cap budgets through that section. Relative rank is allowed, with only a relative convex-body conclusion in that case.
pk-intake-affine-section-radial-layer-st.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty with $\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n=P$. For $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be full-dimensional compact convex bodies, $d\ge1$, satisfying $\sum_p\alpha_p K_p\subseteq K_z$ whenever $\alpha$ is a convex coefficient vector with $\sum_p\alpha_p p=z$. Assume an affine $q:\operatorname{aff}P\to\mathbb R^d$ satisfies $q(z)\in\operatorname{int}K_z$ for every $z$. Then there are arbitrarily close compatible positive homothets $L_z=q(z)+s_z(K_z-q(z))$ preserving $W=\sum_z|K_z|$ exactly. They can be chosen so that all representations using only other bases have a uniform strictly positive support gap. There is an open product Hausdorff neighborhood of these fibers in which each family is realized by its lifted convex hull, with exactly those integer fibers and no others. Its hull is full-dimensional in $\operatorname{aff}P\times\mathbb R^d$.

In detail, after centering by $q$, choose $0<m\le h_{K_z}(u)\le M$ for all unit $u,z$. Peel successive vertex layers of the convex hull of the remaining bases, writing $\ell(z)$ for their indices starting at zero and $L=\max_z\ell(z)$. If an excluded-target representation exists, let $\alpha_*$ be the smallest positive coordinate of any extreme point of the corresponding finite collection of coefficient polytopes, and set
$$
\delta=\min(1/2,\alpha_*m/M),\quad b_z=1-\delta^{\ell(z)},\quad
\kappa=(1-\delta)\delta^L,\quad
s_z=\lambda(1+\varepsilon b_z),\quad
\lambda=\left(\frac{W}{\sum_z(1+\varepsilon b_z)^d|K_z|}\right)^{1/d}.
$$
For $\varepsilon>0$ the uniform gap is at least $g=\lambda\varepsilon m\kappa$ and independent perturbations of size $<\eta$ suffice for $0<\eta<\min(g/4,\lambda m/2)$. If all bases are vertices, take $L_z=K_z$ and any sufficiently small positive radius for the neighborhood.

For every $u\ne0$, the through-section cap $H_u=\{(z,x):u\cdot(x-q(z))\ge0\}$ retains its fraction in each fiber. If that fraction is constant over the bases, its summed cap budget is exactly preserved. This holds simultaneously for every direction with constant original fraction, in particular for all directions if the fibers are centrally symmetric about $q(z)$.

pk-intake-affine-simplex-cap-convexity-a.relation_to_goal: Quadrature for the two actual positive-normal cap functions on a normalized affine simplex leg.
pk-intake-affine-simplex-cap-convexity-a.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)$, $V=1/d!$, and $u_i\ge0$ with $\sum_i u_i=1$. Put $F_r(s)=|rT\cap\{x:u\cdot x\ge s\}|/V$ and $t=1/(d+1)$. For $k>0$ and $0\le\beta<kt$, set
$$
f_-(h)=F_{1-kh}(t-\beta h),\qquad f_+(h)=F_{1-kh}(t+\beta(h+1))\qquad(0\le h\le1/k)
$$
and extend both by zero for $h\ge1/k$. Each is nonnegative and convex on $[0,\infty)$. For either function $f$, the sum over nonnegative integers satisfies
$$
\sum_{h\ge0}f(h)\ge \int_0^\infty f(h)\,dh+f(0)/2,\qquad \sum_{h\ge0}f(h)\ge f(0).
$$
If $k\le1$ it follows that $\sum_{h\ge0}f(h)\ge(1-k)\int_0^\infty f(h)\,dh+(1+k)f(0)/2$.

Let $\Theta$ be uniform on the opposite facet $\operatorname{conv}(e_1,\ldots,e_d)$, with $\Theta=e_1$ if $d=1$, and put $U=u\cdot\Theta$. For $s>0$, $F_r(s)=\mathbb E[(r^d-(s/U)^d)_+]$, taking the integrand to be zero at $U=0$. Write $c=\beta/k$ and $B=t+\beta$. If $c>0$, then $\int_0^\infty f_\pm(h)\,dh=\mathbb E[J_\pm(U)]/[k(d+1)]$, where $J_-(U)=0$ for $U\le t$ and $J_+(U)=0$ for $U\le B$. On their respective remaining domains,
$$
J_-(U)=1-\frac{t^{d+1}}{cU^d}+\frac{(t-c)^{d+1}}{c(U-c)^d},\qquad
J_+(U)=1+\frac{B^{d+1}}{cU^d}-\frac{(B+c)^{d+1}}{c(U+c)^d}.
$$
If $c=0$ the same integral formula uses $J_-=J_+=0$ for $U\le t$ and $J_-=J_+=1-(d+1)(t/U)^d+d(t/U)^{d+1}$ for $U>t$.

pk-intake-affine-simplex-first-jets-by-a.relation_to_goal: One-sided affine jets at common-normal simplex fibers; the resulting repaired fibers may be general convex polytopes.
pk-intake-affine-simplex-first-jets-by-a.statement:
On a finite lattice-complete base with compatible positive d-simplex fibers and common unit facet normals n_i, label each active extreme anchored relation (q,a,i) by each tuple of input facet vertices x_z and put ξ=Σ_z a_z x_z. For affine fields V_z=A_zx+c_z, let L_ell(V)=n_i·V_q(ξ)−Σ_z a_z n_i·V_z(x_z). These inequalities L_ell≥0 are exactly the affine first jets realizable by compatible paths with fibers o(t)-close in Hausdorff distance to (I+tA_z)K_z+tc_z as $t\downarrow0$. If they hold, take the actual lifted convex hull of those affine images; each integer fiber contains its candidate image and differs by O(t²), uniformly on a fixed compact feasible velocity set. Prescribing independent affine normal speeds on all original simplex facets is equivalent to some affine field on that fiber.

At bases −1,0,1 take middle T_0={x,y≥0,x+y≤1} and endpoints J=(1/4)T_0+(0,1/4). Move only the middle with V(x,y)=(−y+1/4,1). All active first-jet inequalities hold. Its affine image has inequality x+ty−t²−t/4≥0, violated by the fixed midpoint input (0,1/4) by exactly t². Actual repair has Hausdorff excess at least t²/√(1+t²) and at most O(t²).

pk-intake-affine-tilt-supporting-cap-der.relation_to_goal: A local supporting-facet derivative and an obstruction to extending facet-constant finite branch LPs to arbitrary affine velocities.
pk-intake-affine-tilt-supporting-cap-der.statement: Let a positive-area polytope facet $F$ coincide with the boundary of a cap, and use physical normal coordinate zero at the old facet with positive direction the outward unit normal. Under an affine body velocity with outward speed $\psi$ on $F$, the signed coincident-facet contribution to the right cap derivative at $t=0$ is $\int_F\min(\psi,-s)\,dS$ for an inside cap whose boundary moves to height $-ts$, and $\int_F(\psi-s)_+\,dS$ for an outside cap whose boundary moves to height $ts$. pk-intake-affine-weighted-physical-row-e.relation_to_goal: Physical surface reserve for a given martingale and prescribed marked pair. The tuple discount, domination and weighted repair selection are separate.
pk-intake-affine-weighted-physical-row-e.statement:
Let $\nu(ds,du)P_{s,u}(dt)$ be a finite physical martingale with actual marked surface source and target marginals $\nu,\eta$ on a compact convex physical domain $C$. Let $q$ be positive affine on $C$, let $L$ be continuous, positive and concave there, and set $F_q=q\log(q/L)$. At a source row put $q_s=q(s)$, $V_s=\int L(t)\,dP_{s,u}(t)$, $Q_s=qP_{s,u}/q_s$, and $T_s=LP_{s,u}/V_s$. Then
$$
\int F_q(t)\,dP_{s,u}(t)-F_q(s)
=q_s\left[\log\frac{L(s)}{V_s}+D(Q_s\|T_s)\right]\ge0.
$$
For any prescribed marked pair of endpoint-average marginal $\eta$ with midpoint law $\rho$ and source-to-midpoint martingale from $\nu$, one has $0\le\int F_q\,d(\eta-\rho)\le\int F_q\,d(\eta-\nu)$, and $\int q\,d\nu=\int q\,d\rho=\int q\,d\eta$.

pk-intake-affinely-independent-source-ar.relation_to_goal: The measure consists of the supplied fibers at fixed independent bases and the mark lies over their fixed positive barycenter. The inequality is for unnormalized source depth. Extra actual fibers contribute separately in a mixed-integer application.
pk-intake-affinely-independent-source-ar.statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge1$ and $N\ge1$ be integers. Fix affinely independent bases $p_1,\ldots,p_N\in\mathbb R^n$ and coefficients $\lambda_i>0$ with $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$. Put $j=\sum_i\lambda_i p_i$. For an array $\mathcal A=(A_i)_{i=1}^N$ of full-dimensional compact convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$, let $D_{\mathcal A}=\sum_i\lambda_i A_i$. Define the raw source depth
$$
p_{\mathcal A}(y)=\inf_{H\ni(j,y)}\sum_i |\{x\in A_i:(p_i,x)\in H\}|,
\qquad y\in D_{\mathcal A},
$$
where $H$ ranges over closed ambient halfspaces and $|\cdot|$ denotes ordinary $d$-volume.

For another such array $\mathcal B=(B_i)$ and $t\in[0,1]$, set $\mathcal K=((1-t)A_i+tB_i)_{i=1}^N$. For every $y\in D_{\mathcal A}$ and $z\in D_{\mathcal B}$,
$$
p_{\mathcal K}((1-t)y+tz)^{1/d}
\ge (1-t)p_{\mathcal A}(y)^{1/d}+t p_{\mathcal B}(z)^{1/d}.
$$
The fixed-base maximum $M(\mathcal A)=\max_{y\in D_{\mathcal A}}p_{\mathcal A}(y)$ is positive and attained, and
$$
M(\mathcal K)^{1/d}\ge (1-t)M(\mathcal A)^{1/d}+tM(\mathcal B)^{1/d}.
$$
Both inequalities have homogeneous versions with any nonnegative coefficients $\alpha,\beta$ of positive sum in place of $1-t,t$, using componentwise Minkowski combinations and omitting terms with zero coefficient.

pk-intake-aligned-conditional-surface-fa.relation_to_goal: A fixed-normal measure comparison under explicit ball and face-equivalence assumptions. It also covers dimension-zero alignment and pushforward domination.
pk-intake-aligned-conditional-surface-fa.statement:
Let $r\ge1$ be an integer and let $F_A,F_B,F_K$ be nonempty compact convex sets in a Euclidean space with $(F_A+F_B)/2\subset F_K$. Let $\mu_i$ be finite nonnegative measures equivalent to intrinsic Hausdorff measure on $F_i$, with $m_i=\dim\operatorname{aff}F_i$, for $i=A,B,K$. Suppose for every pair of open balls $B(x,a),B(y,b)$ with positive corresponding endpoint masses,
$$
\mu_K\bigl(B((x+y)/2,(a+b)/2)\bigr)
\ \ge\
P_r\bigl(\mu_A(B(x,a)),\mu_B(B(y,b))\bigr),
\qquad
P_r(s,t)=\left[\frac{s^{1/r}+t^{1/r}}2\right]^r.
$$
Then for every $x\in F_A$ the map $T_x(y)=(x+y)/2$ satisfies $\mu_K\ge 2^{-(r+m_B)}(T_x)_\#\mu_B$, with the symmetric statement interchanging $A$ and $B$. The three affine hulls have equal dimension $m$ and one common direction space, and their averaged endpoint affine hull is $\operatorname{aff} F_K$.

If $m\ge1$, write $\omega_m$ for the unit $m$-ball volume and let $E_i\subset F_i$ be the full $\mu_i$-measure Borel set where the intrinsic ball-density limit $f_i(x)=\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\mu_i(B(x,\epsilon))/(\omega_m\epsilon^m)$ is finite and positive, for $i=A,B$. The Borel upper density $g^+(z)=\limsup_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\mu_K(B(z,\epsilon))/(\omega_m\epsilon^m)$ on $\operatorname{aff}F_K$ agrees with the density of $\mu_K$ almost everywhere for intrinsic Lebesgue measure. For every $x\in E_A$, $y\in E_B$,
$$
 g^+((x+y)/2)\ \ge\ P_r(f_A(x),f_B(y))
 \ \ge\ \left[\frac{f_A(x)^{-1/m}+f_B(y)^{-1/m}}2\right]^{-m}.
$$

pk-intake-aligned-planar-middle-area-cre.relation_to_goal: Geometric area credit for the exact aligned middle triangle. The sharpness example concerns these geometric hypotheses.
pk-intake-aligned-planar-middle-area-cre.statement:

With $m=\sum_i h_B(-v_i)/3$ and $f(m)=|T\cap(-mT)|/|T|$, the areas $k=|K|$ and $b=|B|$ satisfy
$$ k/b>(m+1)^2/[4f(m)]\ge3/2.$$

pk-intake-aligned-simplex-marked-depth-a.relation_to_goal: Three positive continuous fibers, prescribed genuine minimizing caps and fixed mark. The outer comparison uses the support simplex in those same directions.
pk-intake-aligned-simplex-marked-depth-a.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let the only nonempty integer fibers of a compact convex body in $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies $A,K,B$ at $-1,0,1$. Let $v_1,\ldots,v_{d+1}$ span $\mathbb R^d$ and sum to zero, and put $T=\{x:v_i\cdot x\le1\ \forall i\}$ and $\rho_d=|T\cap(-T)|/|T|$. Suppose $B\subseteq T$, $0\in\operatorname{int} K$, every $v_i\cdot x=-1$ meets $\operatorname{int}A$, and all closed ambient caps $v_i\cdot x\ge z$ attain the genuine raw depth $Q$ at the point $(0,0)$. Let $\Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d$ and $W=|A|+|K|+|B|$.

If $K=\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge-t_i\ \forall i\}$, the normalized depth $Q/W$ is strictly greater than $\Gamma/2$. More precisely, the strict lower bounds in dimensions $1,2,3,4$ are $1/4,4/17,81/376,768/3589$, respectively, and the bound for $d\ge5$ is $\Gamma/(5/3+\rho_d)$.

For an arbitrary such $K$, put $\overline K=\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge-h_K(-v_i)\ \forall i\}$. For $d\ge2$, if $Q\le\Gamma W/2$, then the strict upper bounds on $|K|/|\overline K|$ in dimensions $2,3,4$ are $6/7,12/13,690/851$, respectively. For $d\ge5$ the ratio is strictly below $3\rho_d<1$.

pk-intake-aligned-simplex-midpoint-volum.relation_to_goal: Ordinary continuous-fiber volume comparison with explicit simplex alignment and proper endpoint cuts. The sharpness example certifies the geometric factor.
pk-intake-aligned-simplex-midpoint-volum.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $v_1,\ldots,v_{d+1}\in\mathbb R^d$ span $\mathbb R^d$ and sum to zero. Put $T=\{x:v_i\cdot x\le1\ \forall i\}$, the centroid-zero simplex defined by this circuit, and $\rho_d=|T\cap(-T)|/|T|$, with ordinary $d$-volume. Write $h_D(u)=\max_{x\in D}u\cdot x$.

For a convex body $B\subseteq T$, the mean opposite support $m=\sum_i h_B(-v_i)/(d+1)$ is positive and $|B|\le |T\cap(-mT)|$. For every $m>0$ one has
$$
 |T\cap(-mT)|\le\left(\frac{1+m}{2}\right)^d|T\cap(-T)|.
$$
Equality holds in the latter inequality at $m=1$.

Let $A,B,K$ be convex bodies with $B\subseteq T$ and $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Suppose $K=\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge-t_i\ \forall i\}$ and each hyperplane $v_i\cdot x=-1$ meets $\operatorname{int} A$. Then $|K|>|B|/\rho_d$. The sharp infimum of $|K|/|B|$ under these geometric hypotheses is $1/\rho_d$.

pk-intake-all-N-thin-cone-projected-dept.relation_to_goal: An ordinary projected-depth law and geometric localization for actual hulls, with arbitrary fixed N.
pk-intake-all-N-thin-cone-projected-dept.statement:
Fix $d\ge2$ and an integer $N\ge1$. Let $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)$, $V=|T|$, $m=d+1$, $h=d/m$, $\Gamma=h^d$, and $g=\mathbf1/m$. For $0<\varepsilon<1/m$ set $E_\varepsilon=\operatorname{conv}(0,g+\varepsilon e_1,\ldots,g+\varepsilon e_d)$ and $e_\varepsilon=|E_\varepsilon|/V=\varepsilon^{d-1}(h+\varepsilon)$. For the ordinary projected measure of density $N1_T+1_{E_\varepsilon}$ the maximum raw and normalized closed-halfspace depths are
$$
N\Gamma V+\frac{|E_\varepsilon|}{m}+o(|E_\varepsilon|),\qquad
\Gamma+\frac{e_\varepsilon}{N}\left(\frac1m-\Gamma\right)+o(e_\varepsilon).
$$
The normalized maximum is strictly below $\Gamma$ for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$. Every maximizing point satisfies
$$
y_\varepsilon=g-\frac{e_\varepsilon}{Nmdh^{d-1}}\mathbf1+o(e_\varepsilon),
$$
and lies in $\operatorname{int}E_\varepsilon$ for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$. The measure is the continuous-coordinate projection of the mixed measure on the actual integer fibers of $\operatorname{conv}(([0,N-1]\times T)\cup(\{N\}\times E_\varepsilon))$. All of its projected maximizing points are interior to every real fiber over $[0,N]$ for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$.

pk-intake-all-anchor-midpoint-star-gauge.statement:
Let $T=\{X\in\mathbb R^4:X_i\ge0,\ \sum_iX_i\le1\}$, $V=|T|=1/24$, $g=(1/5,1/5,1/5,1/5)$, $K=T-g$ and $v=-g$. The convex polytope
$$
 C=\{(z,X): |z|\le16,\ X_i\ge0,\ \textstyle\sum_iX_i+|z|/17\le1\}
$$
has exactly 33 positive integer fibers. In coordinates $x=X-g$ they are $K_k=c_k+r_kK$, $r_k=1-|k|/17$, $c_k=|k|v/17$. Its total mixed four-volume is $M=571217V/83521$.

Let $p_{K_k}(y)$ denote ordinary raw closed-halfspace depth, $\gamma_K$ the Minkowski gauge of $K$, and $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. For $0<r\le s$, define $\Phi_4(r,s)=[r c+(s-r)(1-c)/3]^4$ for $s\le4r$ and $\Phi_4(r,s)=r^4$ for $s\ge4r$, where $c=(2\Gamma_4)^{1/4}$; extend symmetrically. For each integer anchor $k$ and every $y\in K_k$ consider
$$
 L_k(y)=p_{K_k}(y)+V\sum_h
 \left(1-\frac{\gamma_K(y-m_{k,h})}{\rho_{k,h}}\right)_+^4
 \Phi_4(r_{k-h},r_{k+h}),
 \quad m_{k,h}=\frac{c_{k-h}+c_{k+h}}2,\quad
 \rho_{k,h}=\frac{r_{k-h}+r_{k+h}}2.
$$
The sum uses all positive integers $h$ with both endpoints in $[-16,16]$. Every closed cap containing $(k,y)$ has raw mixed mass at least $L_k(y)$, but
$$
 \max_{k\in[-16,16]\cap\mathbb Z,\ y\in K_k} L_k(y)
 =\Gamma_4 V\,\frac{282546}{83521}
 =\frac{\Gamma_4 M}{2}-\Gamma_4 V\,\frac{6125}{167042},
$$
attained at $k=0$, $y=3v/17$. In original coordinates the actual point at base zero with $X_i=(1-17^{-6})/[6(1-17^{-5})]$ has normalized mixed depth at least $35167522/138805731>128/625=\Gamma_4/2$.

pk-intake-all-atomic-buffered-hinge-desc.relation_to_goal: Fixed positive scale, unpenalized objective, and every maximizing base bound by its pure-base depth. The normalized multiplier varies only through a common factor. No claim about mixed atomic/proper caps or an arithmetic penalty.
pk-intake-all-atomic-buffered-hinge-desc.statement:
Let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\Lambda$ be a finite nonempty complete base in an affine lattice, and let $K_z$ be positive compact convex $d$-fibers with $d\ge1$, satisfying the anchored Minkowski inclusions. Write $V_z=|K_z|$, $M=\sum_zV_z$, $g_z$ for the fiber centroids and
$$
G_K(u)^2=M^{-1}\sum_z\int_{K_z}[u\cdot(X-g_z)]^2\,dX.
$$
Take $\varepsilon>0$ and a positive sampled-concave array $\ell$, meaning $\ell_p\ge\sum_z\lambda_z\ell_z$ for every anchored convex representation of $p\in P$, with $\sum_z V_z\log\ell_z=0$. This includes positive affine multipliers. For a sampled mark $(p,y)$, take the infimum of the raw summed fiber masses of the caps with margin
$$
a\cdot(z-p)+u\cdot(X-y)+\varepsilon(\ell_p E_{K_p}(y)/M)^{1/(d+1)}G_K(u)\ge0
$$
for $u\ne0$ and of the unchanged closed pure-base caps through $p$, including the whole-base trace in rank zero. Here $E$ is marked projective energy, extended by zero on the own boundary. Write $b_{\rm base}(p)$ for closed pure-base depth, $Q>0$ for the maximum buffered raw depth and $I$ for the bases carrying a maximizing mark. For $T\subseteq P$, let $k(T)$ count the classes modulo twice the direction lattice occupied by $T$.

If $b_{\rm base}(p)=Q$ for every $p\in I$ and $Q/M<1/k(I)$, there are arbitrarily close actual positive compatible families on $P$ and scalar renormalizations of the same array $\ell$ with respect to the new volumes, at the same $\varepsilon$, whose unpenalized normalized buffered maximum is strictly below $Q/M$. If the initial multiplier is affine, its renormalizations are affine.

pk-intake-all-dimensional-affine-frustum.relation_to_goal: This is a lower corrected-cap bound for the decreasing affine frustum in the nontrivial centered-slope branch. The higher-dimensional upper endpoint scalar and the full two-law bound require a separate upper certificate.
pk-intake-all-dimensional-affine-frustum.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$ and $0<a<1/d$. Put $H=(1-a)/a$, $r(z)=(H-z)/(H+1)$, $p=(1-a)^d$, $C_0=(1-a)^{d-1}$ and $V_0=(H+1)/d$. Use density $r(z)^{d-2}/2$ on the cone $-1\le z\le H$, $|x|\le r(z)$. For $s>0$ set
$$
e(s)=\frac1{2s}\int_{-s}^{\min(s,1)}(1-ab)^{-d}\,db,\qquad
v(s)=
\begin{cases}1,&s\le1,\\ (s+1)/(2s),&s\ge1,\end{cases}
$$
with $(e(0),v(0))=(1,1)$. Let $s_*>1$ be the unique positive zero of the cone section moment, or equivalently of $\partial_a e(s)$ at fixed $s$. Write $e_*=e(s_*)$, $v_*=v(s_*)$ and $t(S)=p/(1+aS)^d$. For every finite cutoff $T\ge s_*$ put $t=t(T)$ and $\kappa=(v_*+t)/(1+e_*)$. Then for all $0\le s\le T$,
$$
1-v(s)-\kappa(1-e(s))\ge0.
$$

For the frustum obtained by cutting the cone at $U=HT/(H+1+T)$, write $P_f(s)$ for the mass of $z+sx\ge0$ and $C_f(s)$ for the integral of the density over $z+sx=0$ against $d\mathcal H^1/\sqrt{1+s^2}$. Its volume is $V=(1-t)V_0$. Set $c=(p-\kappa)V_0/C_0$ and $\gamma=(\kappa-t)/(1-t)$. Then $(P_f(s)-cC_f(s))/V\ge\gamma$ for every $s\in[0,\infty]$, with endpoint record $(P_f(\infty),C_f(\infty))=(V/2,0)$. The same inequality holds for the averages under every probability law on $[0,\infty]$.

pk-intake-all-dimensional-larger-positiv.relation_to_goal: All finite positive-coordinate scalar vectors and their nonzero closed faces.
pk-intake-all-dimensional-larger-positiv.statement:
For an integer $m\ge1$ and $0\le x_j\le h<1$ with some $x_j>0$, put $\rho=\prod_j(1-x_j)$, $E=\rho^{-1}-1$, and
$$
L=\left(1-\frac{\sum_j x_j}{E}\right)\prod_j(1+x_j/E),\qquad
R=\rho(E+h)\left[1-\frac{(E+h)\prod_j(h-x_j)}{h^{m+1}}\right].
$$

Then $L\ge R$, with strict inequality whenever all $0<x_j<h<1$.

pk-intake-all-dimensional-minkowski-uppe.relation_to_goal: Ordinary d-volume in a single continuous cap, with a fixed tested halfspace and actual Minkowski sums.
pk-intake-all-dimensional-minkowski-uppe.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $A,B\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex bodies, and let $t$ be a nonzero linear height. Let $S\subset A$ be a segment with distinct endpoint heights, and let $c\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $\min_B t\ge-c$. In ordinary $d$-dimensional volume,
$$
|(A+B)\cap\{t\ge0\}|-|(S+B)\cap\{t\ge0\}|\ \ge\ |A\cap\{t\ge c\}|.
$$
The coefficient one is sharp even when $t(A)=[\ell,h]$ with $\ell<-1$, $h>c>0$, $t(B)\subset[-c,1]$, and $S$ joins the extreme heights of $A$. The inequality can fail in dimension one.

pk-intake-all-dimensional-nested-simplex.relation_to_goal: Ordinary d-volume estimate for arbitrary simplex containers, used to control cross-fiber convexification.
pk-intake-all-dimensional-nested-simplex.statement:
For integer $d\ge2$ and $0<\varepsilon\le1/16$, set $V=1/d!$, $a=1+\varepsilon^2$, and define
$$
A=\{x:x_i\ge0,\ \varepsilon\le\textstyle\sum_i x_i\le1\},\qquad
P=\{x:x_i\le a,\ \textstyle\sum_i x_i\ge\varepsilon\}.
$$
For every $d$-simplex $R\supseteq A$ and compact convex $L\supseteq R\cup P$, their ordinary $d$-volumes satisfy
$$
(|R|-|A|)+2^{-d}(|L|-|P|)\ge\frac{\varepsilon V}{16d^2}.
$$

pk-intake-all-dimensional-smaller-positi.relation_to_goal: All finite smaller-positive scalar gap vectors and nonzero faces.
pk-intake-all-dimensional-smaller-positi.statement:
For an integer $m\ge1$ and $0\le x_j\le h<1$ with some $x_j>0$, put $\rho=\prod_j(1-x_j)$, $E=\rho^{-1}-1$, and
$$
L=\left(1-\frac{\sum_j x_j}{E}\right)\prod_j(1+x_j/E),\qquad
R=\rho(E+h)\left[1-\frac{(E+h)\prod_j(h-x_j)}{h^{m+1}}\right].
$$

Also set $Q=\prod_j(1+x_j/E)$, $B=\sum_j x_j/(1-x_j)$, $C=B/(1-\rho)-1$, and $W=(1-h)CQ$.

Then $W\ge R$, with strict inequality whenever all $0<x_j<h<1$.

pk-intake-all-minimum-base-variance-conv.relation_to_goal: Classification and depth obstruction for a specified two-piece selector on one actual rectangle. Its nonminimal partition contains a point above the locked threshold.
pk-intake-all-minimum-base-variance-conv.statement: Let $C=[-1,2]\times[0,1]$, with mixed measure $\mu$ given by the sum of lengths on its four integer fibers. Consider pairs of positive-mass closed convex subbodies covering $C$ with $\mu$-null overlap, or a single such subbody covering $C$. Require the base coordinate $j_i$ of each actual mixed centroid to be integral. The minimum of $\sum_i\mu(D_i)j_i^2$ is $2$. Every minimizer, up to labels, consists of the two complementary closed caps of $C$ whose base-one piece is cut by either $x+z/5\ge3/5$ or $x-z/5\le2/5$. The two pairs of centroids are $\{(1,7/10),(0,3/10)\}$ and $\{(1,3/10),(0,7/10)\}$. Each centroid has a containing closed halfspace of original mass $9/10$, hence normalized depth at most $9/40<1/4$. In each case the intersection of that halfspace with $C$ lies in the centroid's own piece.

pk-intake-all-normal-integer-centered-tr.relation_to_goal: The sharp target at the actual central centroid for the integer-reflected common-vertex planar triangle family of any length. Symmetric pairs are taken around an occupied center.
pk-intake-all-normal-integer-centered-tr.statement:
Let $m\ge0$, $1=r_0\ge r_1\ge\cdots\ge r_m\ge0$, with nondecreasing outward drops $r_j-r_{j+1}$, and set $r_{-j}=r_j$, $b=r_m$, and $M=\sum_{j=-m}^{m}r_j^2$.

Let $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2)$, $V=|T|=1/2$. At the consecutive integer bases $-m,\ldots,m$ take the actual fibers $r_jT$, and assume there are no other positive-area integer fibers. With the sum of ordinary areas on the fibers as measure, every closed ambient halfspace containing the actual point $(0,1/3,1/3)$ has mass at least $2VM/9$. For $m=0$ its exact depth is $4V/9$.

In the normalized coordinates, for $2/3\le a\le1$ and every $m\ge0$, the infimum over $\beta\in\mathbb R$ of the cap mass at $a x_1+(1-a)x_2+\beta j\ge1/3$, divided by $V$, is attained at $\beta=0$ and equals $[a/(2a-1)]\sum_j(r_j-c)_+^2$, $c=1/(3a)$. Each such cap has mass divided by $V$ at least
$$
\frac{a(1-c)^3}{2a-1}M+\frac{a}{2a-1}\frac{c(1-c)^2}{2m+1}>\frac M4.
$$
A common continuous dilation replaces $1=r_0$ by any $R>0$, the mark by $(0,R/3,R/3)$, and $M$ by the sum of the resulting squared radii.

pk-intake-all-occupied-fiber-affine-rank.relation_to_goal: An exact change of ambient integer dimension preserving the entire original support, with no continuous Jacobian factor. The sharp reduced bound remains conditional.
pk-intake-all-occupied-fiber-affine-rank.statement: Let $n,d\ge0$ and let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty compact convex. Let $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. If $S$ is nonempty, $\operatorname{conv}S$ is compact and has exactly the original mixed set. Suppose now at least one integer fiber has positive $d$-volume, with counting measure for $d=0$. Write $A$ for the affine hull of all occupied integer bases, $r=\dim A$, and $z_*$ for an occupied base. A lattice basis of $(A-z_*)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ gives an affine chart $F(t,x)=(z_*+Bt,x)$ from $\mathbb R^r\times\mathbb R^d$ to $A\times\mathbb R^d$. The set $F^{-1}(\operatorname{conv}S)$ is compact convex, is full dimensional in the reduced space, and has mixed set exactly $F^{-1}(S)$, including every null occupied fiber. The chart preserves summed fiber $d$-volume and every corresponding point's raw and normalized closed-halfspace depth for $r+d>0$. In particular, a reduced bound with coefficient $2^{-r}\gamma_d$ transfers with that coefficient, at least $2^{-n}\gamma_d$, with $\gamma_0=1$. For $r=d=0$ the original mixed set is one point with normalized depth one.

pk-intake-all-parity-decimations-increas.relation_to_goal: Pure-lattice d=0 obstruction to choosing a parity restriction with nonincreasing normalized maximum depth.
pk-intake-all-parity-decimations-increas.statement: Let $P=\operatorname{conv}\{(-3,-1),(3,3),(1,3),(-1,2)\}$. For every $r\in\{0,1\}^2$, the maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth over the lattice sites of $(P-r)/2$, under their uniform counting law, is $1/2$. The corresponding maximum for $P$ is $3/10$. All four decimations therefore strictly increase the maximum, although each original site has weight $1<10/4$.

pk-intake-all-point-identical-triangle-p.relation_to_goal: Two identical copies of a continuous planar triangle, measured in absolute area at a single marked point. The theorem supplies a bound for one selected pair with a common normal and opposite shifts. The locked conjecture concerns the common ambient halfspace over an entire compatible mixed-integer fiber family.
pk-intake-all-point-identical-triangle-p.statement:
Let $T\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a nondegenerate triangle of area $V$, and let $y\in T$ have barycentric coordinates $A\ge B\ge C$. Write $f_T(y)$ for the infimum of $|T\cap H|$ over closed halfplanes $H$ containing $y$, where $|\cdot|$ denotes area. For $u\ne0$ and $t\in\mathbb R$, set
$$
P_T(y;u,t)=|T\cap\{x:u\cdot x\ge u\cdot y+t\}|+
           |T\cap\{x:u\cdot x\ge u\cdot y-t\}|.
$$
Then $P_T(y;u,t)\ge 8BCV$ for every $u\ne0$ and $t\in\mathbb R$, and
$$
\min_{u\ne0,\ t\in\mathbb R}P_T(y;u,t)=8BCV=2f_T(y).
$$
The minimum is attained at shift zero, including when $y\in\partial T$.

pk-intake-allocated-buffered-log-density.relation_to_goal: Exact flux of the physical separator from a specified finite-contact cover. A nonaffine centroid radial array can be incompatible, and its formal residual is not forced to vanish.
pk-intake-allocated-buffered-log-density.statement:
Use the common finite-contact buffered separator and its same-coefficient gradient-labeled volume rows. A regular singleton joint separator with the same body terms, the stated singleton section means and the same-coefficient volume rows is included. Let $W_z$ be the allocated boundary cap load including the atomic whole-fiber contributions. Each old cap has mass $Q=\beta M$, and the cap weights $\omega_{ij}$ and atomic weights sum to one. Define $k=\Delta/(NM)$ and
$$
\Xi_z(X)=W_z(X)-\beta+\sum_{ia:p_{ia}=z}\frac{e_{ia}P_a(X)^{-N}}{NE_a}
+\frac1{2M}\sum_{ij}e_i\rho_{ij}[u_{ij}\cdot(X-g_z)]^2
-\frac{(N+2)\Delta}{2NM}-k\log L(z,X).
$$
Then $\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}\Xi_zv_z\,dS\le0$ on the same actual body cone. Let $S_{ij}(z)$ be the consistently allocated coarea in fiber $z$. The force and affine moments satisfy
$$
\begin{aligned}
F_z:=\int_{\partial K_z}\Xi_z n_z\,dS
&=\sum_{ij}\omega_{ij}S_{ij}(z)u_{ij}-\sum_{ia:p_{ia}=z}e_{ia}a_a
-k\int_{K_z}\nabla_X\log L\,dX,\\
\sum_z F_z&=0,\qquad
\sum_z z\otimes F_z=0,\qquad
\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}\Xi_z X\otimes n_z\,dS=0 .
\end{aligned}
$$
For the ordinary centroid radial array its formal response is $\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}\Xi_z\,n_z\cdot(X-g_z)\,dS=-\sum_z g_z\cdot F_z$, which is zero for an affine centroid graph. Exact composition of an actual path with a lattice-preserving fiber-affine change of variables, transporting the parameter and caps, preserves the normalized buffered response.

pk-intake-allocated-oriented-planar-sect.relation_to_goal: Conditional on the given marked normal-marginal law and its exact allocations. The orientations constrain a section body in dimension two. The triangle bound assumes homothetic caps, and the midpoint example calibrates aggregate area.
pk-intake-allocated-oriented-planar-sect.statement:
Let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, be positive-volume compact convex bodies at a finite set of bases. Let $\theta$ be a probability law of jointly measurable cap records $H=\{a\cdot z+u\cdot x\ge c\}$ and their allocated body selectors $s_H\in[0,1]$. On proper cuts use the captured old boundary and full section area. On inside supporting facets use body density $\alpha$ and section density $1-\alpha$, and on outside supporting facets use $\alpha$ for both. Strictly full and empty fibers have their usual selectors. At pure-base records allow complementary whole-fiber choices at equality and set section coarea to zero. On nonvertical records let $T_{H,z}$ be the allocated section area divided by $|u|$ and $T_H=\sum_z T_{H,z}$. Let $S_K$ denote the outer normal area measure of $K$, and suppose the mean selected old-boundary normal measure is $\beta\sum_z S_{K_z}$ with $0<\beta<1$. Set
$$
R=\int_{u\ne0}|u|T_H\,\delta_{-u/|u|}\,d\theta.
$$
An effective area measure is the ordinary measure for a positive-volume cap, zero for an empty cap or a touch of dimension below $d-1$, and $m(\delta_{u/|u|}+\delta_{-u/|u|})$ at an outside supporting facet with allocated area $m$. At a pure-base equality take the effective measure according to the allocated whole-fiber choice. The mean effective cap and complementary cap measures are, respectively,
$$
\beta\sum_z S_{K_z}+R,\qquad (1-\beta)\sum_z S_{K_z}+R^-,
$$
where $R^-$ is the reflection of $R$. The complement uses $1-s_H$ and the same allocated section. In particular $\int T_Hu\,d\theta=0$.

If $d=2$, put $B=\sum_z K_z$ (Minkowski sum). There is a compact convex $J$, possibly a point or segment, unique up to translation with $S_J=R$. There are translations $q,q'$ with
$$
J+q\subseteq(1-\beta)B,\qquad -J+q'\subseteq\beta B.
$$
In particular $J-J\subseteq\min(\beta,1-\beta)(B-B)$ and $|J|\le\min(\beta,1-\beta)^2|B|$.

Suppose in addition that the same law satisfies the selected old-boundary normal-marginal identity tested against $\omega(z)\phi(n)$ for every affine $\omega$ on the base and continuous normal test $\phi$. For a nonnegative affine weight $\omega$ on the finite base set with positive sum, put $\lambda_z=\omega(z)/\sum_y\omega(y)$, $B_\lambda=\sum_z\lambda_z K_z$ and
$$
R_\lambda=\int_{u\ne0}\sum_z\lambda_z|u|T_{H,z}\,\delta_{-u/|u|}\,d\theta.
$$
Then $R_\lambda=S_{J_\lambda}$ for a planar convex $J_\lambda$, and there are translations of $J_\lambda$ and $-J_\lambda$ inside $(1-\beta)B_\lambda$ and $\beta B_\lambda$, respectively. If $p=\sum_z\lambda_z z$ is integral and the bodies are the actual fibers of a convex set there, both containments hold with $K_p$ in place of $B_\lambda$.

pk-intake-ambient-affine-maximality-with.relation_to_goal: An explicit failure of an objective-one ambient-contact certificate under ambient affine maximality.
pk-intake-ambient-affine-maximality-with.statement:
In $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R$, let
$$
C=\{(z,x):0\le z\le2,\ |x|\le\sqrt z\},\qquad
D=\{(z,x):0\le z\le3/2,\ |x|\le\sqrt z-z/2\}.
$$
The identity is a determinant maximum among base-preserving affine ambient fits of $D$ into $C$. Their only ambient contact is $(0,0)$, where every supporting normal has continuous component zero. Consequently no stress supported on these ambient contacts has continuous tensor one. The only positive integer fiber of $D$ is $[-1/2,1/2]$ at $z=1$. Retaining $C_1=[-1,1]$ in an ambient convex body inside $C$ doubles the mixed mass with true integer-base centroid and local normalized closed-halfspace depth $1/2$.

Its continuous coordinates sum to $q=310337/387828$. Write $a=25/798$ and $W=20/21$ for the relative endpoint and middle fiber volumes in units of $|T_5|$. The closed cylindrical cap $\sum_i x_i\le q$ through this centroid has normalized mass $(q^5+2a)/(W+2a)<\Gamma_5=(5/6)^5$. The centroid of the base-$2$ fiber has normalized mixed depth at least $\Gamma_5 W/(W+2a)=59375/157464>\Gamma_5/2$.

pk-intake-ambient-simplex-closed-knot-sl.relation_to_goal: Actual unnormalized d-volume at every real height with one integer base coordinate. The ordinary tail integral by itself gives no closed endpoint convention.
pk-intake-ambient-simplex-closed-knot-sl.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional $(d+1)$-simplex with $d\ge1$, $m=d+1$, ambient volume $V$, and vertex heights $h_0,\ldots,h_m$. Write $w(s)=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_s)$ for its actual closed height-$s$ slice. For $\min_i h_i<s<\max_i h_i$,
$$
w(s)=Vm[h_0,\ldots,h_m](t-s)_+^{m-1}.
$$
The divided difference is in $t$, with confluent values at repeated knots and the continuous slice limit at interior knots. For distinct heights the divided difference equals $\sum_i(h_i-s)_+^{m-1}/\prod_{j\ne i}(h_i-h_j)$. Off the height interval $w=0$. At each extreme height use the inward limit, which equals the actual closed endpoint volume and is positive precisely when $m$ vertices have that height. Also $\int_{\mathbb R}w(s)\,ds=V$.

pk-intake-ambient-simplex-duplicated-kno.relation_to_goal: First moments for the original full d-volume fiber measure with one integer base coordinate.
pk-intake-ambient-simplex-duplicated-kno.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional $(d+1)$-simplex of ambient volume $V$, with $d\ge1$, $m=d+1$, $N=d+2$, vertices $v_i=(h_i,\xi_i)$, barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i$, and actual closed section volumes $w(s)=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_s)$. Write $h^{(i)}$ for the height list $h=(h_0,\ldots,h_{N-1})$ with one extra copy of $h_i$. Let $f_{h^{(i)}}$ be the scalar height density under uniform barycentrics with this duplicated list, with continuous values in the interior, zero outside, and inward values at the endpoints. Then the actual section moments satisfy
$$
J_i(s):=\int_{C_s}\lambda_i(s,x)\,dx
 =\frac{V}{N} f_{h^{(i)}}(s)
 =V[h_0,\ldots,h_{N-1},h_i](t-s)_+^m.
$$
The same endpoint convention applies to the divided difference. One has $\sum_iJ_i=w$ and $\sum_ih_iJ_i=sw$. When $w(s)>0$ the centroid is $\sum_iJ_i(s)v_i/w(s)$. When $M=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}w(j)>0$, the mixed centroid is $M^{-1}\sum_i v_i\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}J_i(j)$, and it belongs to the mixed trace exactly when its base is integral.

Its ambient volume is $V=1/180$. The positive five-volume integer fibers $K_1,K_2,K_3$ have normalized mixed weights $(139,144,9)/292$. The actual integer fibers at zero and four have zero five-volume, and $K_2=(K_1+K_3)/2$. For the ordinary fiber centroids $g_1,g_3$, the point
$$
y=\left(2,\frac{g_1+g_3}{2}\right)
=\left(2,\frac{1763}{15012},\frac{1763}{15012},\frac19,\frac{161}{1251},\frac{161}{1251}\right)
$$
is actual. The closed ambient cap $\{z-x_3-3x_4-3x_5\ge1\}$ contains $y$ and has normalized mixed mass $1677/9344<(5/6)^5/2$, an absolute deficit of $(48739/2239488)V$ relative to the raw target. The parallel cap through $y$ has normalized mass $4150356952177626013/28629870146058409344$.

pk-intake-ambient-simplex-lattice-count-.relation_to_goal: Full d-dimensional mixed volume. A lower-dimensional fiber may acquire an orientation-dependent Hausdorff Jacobian.
pk-intake-ambient-simplex-lattice-count-.statement:
Let $C$ be a full-dimensional $(n+d)$-simplex in $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ with $n\ge0$ and $d\ge1$. Choose $n+1$ vertices with affinely independent base projections and let $Q$ be their projected $n$-simplex. Let $h_1,\ldots,h_d$ be the other projected vertices and $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ their barycentric coordinates. The map to $(z,x)$ fixes the base $z$ and is an affine bijection taking $C$ to
$$
\mathcal C=\{(z,x):x\in T_d,\ z\in\textstyle\sum_jh_jx_j+(1-S)Q\},\qquad S=\sum_jx_j,\quad T_d=\{x\ge0:S\le1\}.
$$
The image volume is $n!|Q|/(n+d)!$ and the absolute continuous-coordinate Jacobian is $J=n!|Q|/((n+d)!|C|)$. It multiplies full $d$-volume on each integer fiber and every mixed closed cap mass by $J$. For positive mixed total mass, it transports normalized depth and the mixed centroid. The continuous projection of raw mixed measure in these new coordinates has density
$$
N(x)=\left|\mathbb Z^n\cap\left(\textstyle\sum_jh_jx_j+(1-S)Q\right)\right|\qquad(x\in T_d)
$$
and zero outside $T_d$. For $n=1$ choose the extreme projected vertices $a<b$. The interval has endpoints $\ell(x)=a+\sum_j(h_j-a)x_j$, $u(x)=b+\sum_j(h_j-b)x_j$, with width $(b-a)(1-S)$. Its count is $\max(0,\lfloor u(x)\rfloor-\lceil\ell(x)\rceil+1)$. For $n=0$ use $|Q|_0=1$ and $N=1$ on $T_d$.

pk-intake-ambient-simplex-nonlogconcave-.relation_to_goal: Counterexample to log-concavity of the full-volume continuous marginal even in the ambient-simplex class.
pk-intake-ambient-simplex-nonlogconcave-.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$. The ambient simplex $C\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ with vertices $(0,0),(4,0),(2-\varepsilon,e_1),(2+\varepsilon,e_2),(2,e_3),\ldots,(2,e_d)$ has exactly three positive integer fibers. At bases $1,2,3$ they are, respectively,
$$
A=\operatorname{diag}((2-\varepsilon)^{-1},(2+\varepsilon)^{-1},1/2,\ldots,1/2)T_d,\qquad
B=\{x\ge0:2\textstyle\sum_i x_i+\varepsilon|x_1-x_2|\le2\},
$$
and $A$ with coordinates $1,2$ swapped, where $T_d=\{x\ge0:\sum_i x_i\le1\}$. The integer fibers at $0$ and $4$ are singletons. The positive volumes, divided by $|T_d|$, are $a,W,a$ with $a=2^{2-d}/(4-\varepsilon^2)$ and $W=2/(2+\varepsilon)$. The endpoint simplices at bases $1$ and $3$ are nonhomothetic, and $B$ is not a simplex. The continuous projection of the full $d$-volume mixed law has no log-concave version of its density.

pk-intake-ambient-simplex-sampled-vertex.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional $(d+1)$-simplex, $d\ge1$, with actual closed section volumes $w(s)=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_s)$. $$
(1-c)^d\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z} w\left(\frac{j-ch_i}{1-c}\right).
$$
For $c<0$ its mass is the full mixed mass, and for $c\ge1$ it has zero mixed mass. The formula includes vertical caps and closed boundary fibers.

pk-intake-ambient-unit-hinge-degeneratio.relation_to_goal: The example concerns the ambient normalization of cap margins and a fixed count of actual source covers.
pk-intake-ambient-unit-hinge-degeneratio.statement: Fix $n,d\ge1$ and let $C=[0,1]^n\times K$ for a full-dimensional $d$-simplex $K$ of volume $v$. Its mixed source has mass $M=2^n v$. Write $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$ for the barycentric coordinates and $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. For $0<t<1/(d+1)$, $A>1$, $p\in\{0,1\}^n$, and $0\le j\le d$, use the cap with unscaled margin $\lambda_j(x)-t-Aq_p(z)$, where $q_p(z)=\sum_{\ell=1}^n[(1-p_\ell)z_\ell+p_\ell(1-z_\ell)]$. The $2^n(d+1)$ cap interiors cover every point of the mixed source. Each cap has mass $v(1-t)^d$ and, after normalization of its full ambient normal to length one, hinge integral $v(1-t)^{d+1}/((d+1)\sqrt{nA^2+\lVert\nabla\lambda_j\rVert^2})$. Consequently for any $\tau>2^{-n}\gamma_d$ there are such covers with individual cap masses strictly below $\tau M$ and total normalized hinge tending to zero. The limiting closed vertical cap at each $(p,j)$ has mass $v$.

pk-intake-anchored-affine-recession-and-.relation_to_goal: Depth uses full residual fibers on a fixed canonical graph. The limiting maximum is for those fibers and their actual closed ambient halfspaces.
pk-intake-anchored-affine-recession-and-.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite base and let the positive compact convex fibers $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compatible, $d\ge1$, with diameters at most $D$. Let $T$ be the matrix of the rows $e_z-(\lambda_w)_w$ associated with the vertices of the anchored coefficient polytopes, let $m$ be its number of rows, and write $\sigma$ for its least nonzero singular value when $T\ne0$. The centroid array $c=(c_z)_z$ has Euclidean distance at most $D\sqrt m/\sigma$ from $L(P)\otimes\mathbb R^d$, with distance zero if $T=0$. Its orthogonal projection $g$ to this space makes $R_z=K_z-g_z$ compatible and contained in a common ball. On the fixed canonical lift $B=\Phi_P(P)$ there is an affine function $G$ with $G(\Phi_P(z))=g_z$. If $\pi$ is the affine base projection, the map $(b,x)\mapsto(\pi(b),x+G(b))$ preserves fiber masses, sends the lifted residual union onto the original union, and gives the inequality of normalized point depths
$$
\delta_{\rm original}(z,x+g_z)\ \ge\ \delta_{\rm lift}(\Phi_P(z),x).
$$
If $P$ itself is canonical, the recentering is an affine shear on its original ambient space and preserves depth exactly.

For a sequence of these residual families in a common ball $R\mathbb B_d$ and with simultaneous Hausdorff limit of positive total $d$-volume, maximum normalized lifted depth converges to the limiting maximum, and the liminf of the original maxima is at least that limit. Here each limiting fiber is nonempty compact convex and may have zero $d$-volume. For a fixed residual family of total volume $M>0$, the normalized depth within a base fiber is Lipschitz with constant $|P|\kappa_{d-1}R^{d-1}/M$, with $\kappa_0=1$.

pk-intake-anchored-box-compatible-center.relation_to_goal: Describes the actual centroid choices for the stated box geometry on a lattice-complete base.
pk-intake-anchored-box-compatible-center.statement:
Let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite nonempty, $d\ge1$, and $w_p>0$ with $w_p\ge\sum_j\lambda_jw_j$ for every anchored representation $p=\sum_j\lambda_j p_j$. For $c\in\mathbb R^P$, set $K_p(c)=[c_p-w_p/2,c_p+w_p/2]\times[-1/2,1/2]^{d-1}$. The convex hull of the lifted boxes has exactly the prescribed integer fibers if and only if all anchored representations satisfy
$$
|c_p-\sum_j\lambda_jc_j|\le\frac12(w_p-\sum_j\lambda_jw_j).
$$
Only the extreme anchored representations need be tested. Let $L_0$ contain the extreme rows with $w_p=\sum_j\lambda_jw_j$. The feasible center polyhedron is contained in $\ker L_0$ and contains a relative neighborhood of zero there, so its dimension is $\dim\ker L_0$.

pk-intake-anchored-cap-quantile-exact-ci.relation_to_goal: An exact comparison cover for any given positive anchored circuit; it does not assert that the moved cover masses equal the moved actual depths.
pk-intake-anchored-cap-quantile-exact-ci.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty finite set and $K_w(p)\subset\mathbb R^d$, $w\in P$, be compact convex bodies depending locally Hausdorff-Lipschitz on a finite-dimensional parameter $p$ near $p_0$. Write $\mu_p=\sum_{w\in P}\delta_w\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_w(p)})$ and $M(p)=\sum_w|K_w(p)|$. Use a finite list of closed caps

$H_j(b)=\{(w,x):v_j\cdot w+u_j\cdot x\ge b\},\qquad |u_j|=1.$

At the old family suppose each $H_j(b_j)$ passes through the same mark $(z,y)$ with $z\in P$, $y\in\operatorname{int}K_z(p_0)$, and has the same raw mass $\tau_0$. Suppose $\rho_j>0$, $\sum_j\rho_j=1$ and $\sum_j\rho_j u_j=0$, and set $A=\sum_j\rho_j v_j$.

Each function $F_j(p,b)=\mu_p(H_j(b))$ has a unique local inverse in the threshold, $Q_j(p,\tau)$, for $(p,\tau)$ near $(p_0,\tau_0)$. It is locally Lipschitz jointly and locally uniformly decreasing and bi-Lipschitz in $\tau$. There is a unique nearby locally Lipschitz mass $\tau_c(p)$ with

$\sum_j\rho_j Q_j(p,\tau_c(p))=A\cdot z.$

The shifted closed caps at these thresholds all have raw mass $\tau_c(p)$ and cover the whole plane $\{z\}\times\mathbb R^d$. In particular the new restricted maximal normalized depth over $z$ is at most $\tau_c(p)/M(p)$.

pk-intake-anchored-components-and-maxima.relation_to_goal: Finite arithmetic describing anchored components and the number of maximal occupied faces.
pk-intake-anchored-components-and-maxima.statement:
For the finite complete lattice set $I$ in the maximal-minimal-face lemma, join two of its maximal minimal faces when they intersect. For each connected component let $J_c$ be the union of the sites of $I$ in its faces. These $J_c$ partition $I$ and are exactly the components generated by the positive-coefficient convex representations in $I$ whose target belongs to $I$. Each $J_c$ is lattice-complete, and their occupied parity classes are pairwise disjoint. If $m_c$ is the number of maximal minimal faces in component $c$, $k_c=k(J_c)$, and $r$ is the number of nonsingleton components, then
$$
k(I)=\sum_c k_c,\qquad m_c\le k_c,\qquad
m_c=k_c\ \Longleftrightarrow\ |J_c|=1,\qquad m\le k(I)-r.
$$

pk-intake-anchored-positive-fiber-diamet.relation_to_goal: A fixed component and a uniform positive volume floor are used for the diameter bound. The normalized positive-limit support assertion uses compatibility alone.
pk-intake-anchored-positive-fiber-diamet.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set and let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$, $z\in P$, be compact convex fibers with $d\ge1$, compatible under all anchored representations on $P$, and with volumes in $[v,V]$ for some $0<v\le V$. Choose one representation at every nonvertex using all other sites of its minimal face with strictly positive coefficients. For a nonsingleton dependence component $P_i$, let $\lambda_*$ be the smallest coefficient among its chosen representations. After one common continuous affine map with linear determinant one, all fibers in $P_i$ have diameter at most
$$
2\sqrt d\,(d!V)^{1/d}
\left[\frac{2}{\lambda_*}\left(1+\frac{2dV}{\lambda_*^d v}\right)\right]^{|P_i|-1}.
$$
The anchor bound $2\sqrt d\,(d!V)^{1/d}$ suffices on a singleton component. Also, in any sequence of positive compatible families on fixed $P$ with convergent normalized fiber volumes, the set of sites with positive limiting normalized volume is closed in $P$.

pk-intake-anisotropic-seven-fiber-quadra.relation_to_goal: An explicit mixed source with two integer and two continuous dimensions. Its small fibers converge weakly to a centroid atom, and the response uses the surviving normal motion at scale square root of t. Its normalized depth is above 1/9 for small positive t.
pk-intake-anisotropic-seven-fiber-quadra.statement:
Let $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2)$ in $\mathbb R^2$ have area $V=1/2$ and centroid $g=(1/3,1/3)$. Write $\Gamma=4/9$, $\kappa=2/3$, $\eta=1/10$, $M_\eta(v_1,v_2)=(v_1-\eta v_2,v_2)$, $B=M_\eta(T-g)$, and
$$
E_t=g+\operatorname{diag}(t^{3/4},t^{1/4})B.
$$
Place $T$ at each of the four binary integer bases, and $E_t$ at $(-1,0),(-1,1),(1,-1)$, and take their actual convex hull. Let $A_{6,t}(y)$ be raw closed-halfspace mixed depth at $((0,0),y)$ in the hull after omitting the fiber at $(-1,0)$. Define $l_1(v)=v_1$, $l_2(v)=v_2$, and $l_0(v)=-v_1-v_2$. Let $x_*$ be the unique root in $(0,\eta)$ of $(1-x)(1-x+\eta)^2=1$, or equivalently $100x^3-320x^2+341x-21=0$. It satisfies $6553/100000<x_*<3277/50000$. Put
$$
\Delta=\frac V9\left(x_*^2+\frac{2(x_*-\eta)^2}{1-x_*+\eta}\right)>0,
\qquad J_0=J_2=2\Gamma V,\qquad J_1=2\Gamma V+\Delta.
$$
For every convergent bounded sequence $v_t\to v$,
$$
A_{6,t}(g+tv_t)=\Gamma V+t\min_{0\le i\le2}\{J_i-\kappa l_i(v)\}+o(t).
$$
At marks with $y=g+t(\Delta,-\Delta/2)+o(t)$, every six-fiber through-mark cap sequence within $o(t)$ of the minimum and with continuous normals approaching the canonical $l_1$ direction has $\delta_t/\sqrt t\to x_*$ under positive normalization of those normals to $(1,\delta_t)$.

For all sufficiently small $t>0$, the global maximum in the seven-fiber source is attained, every maximizing point has integer base $(0,0)$, and its continuous mark is $y_t=g+t(\Delta,-\Delta/2)+o(t)$. With total mixed mass $M_t=4V+3tV$, the raw and normalized maxima are
$$
D_t=\frac29+t\left(\frac{17}{18}+\frac\Delta3\right)+o(t),
\qquad
D_t/M_t=\frac19+t\left(\frac7{18}+\frac\Delta6\right)+o(t).
$$
At the core centroid with base $(0,0)$ the raw first-order coefficient is $17/18$, and the other three core centroids have smaller coefficients.

$$
D_t=\Gamma V+t(a+L_*)+o(t),\qquad
\frac{D_t}{4V+3ta}=\frac{\Gamma}{4}+t\,\frac{4(a+L_*)-3\Gamma a}{16V}+o(t).

For $L=1/6,H=1$, one has $v_*=(1/10,1/10)$, $L_*=3/5$, $D_t=2/9+(19/15)t+o(t)$, and $D_t/(4V+3ta)=1/9+(47/90)t+o(t)$. A_{6,t}(g+tv_t)=\Gamma V+t\mathcal L(v_t)+o(t),\qquad

pk-intake-arbitrarily-many-maximizing-ba.relation_to_goal: A faceted ordinary-depth example disproving any bound on the number of maximizing integer bases in fixed dimensions.
pk-intake-arbitrarily-many-maximizing-ba.statement:
For each integer $s\ge1$ set $r=4s+2$, $R=7s+4$ and
$$
C_s=\{(p,q,x):-1\le q\le1,\ |p|\le r-(r-s)q,\ |x|\le2+q\},
$$
with integer coordinates $p,q$. It has $24s+15$ positive integer fibers and total mixed length $M_s=72s+44$. The exact raw closed-halfspace maximum is $T_s=24s+14$ and its maximizing marks are precisely $(j,0,0)$ with $j=-s,\ldots,s$.

For every $d\ge2$ and every centrally symmetric convex body $L\subset\mathbb R^{d-1}$ centered at zero, $C_s\times L$ has mixed volume $M_s|L|$ and raw maximum $T_s|L|$. Its maximizing integer bases are precisely $(j,0)$ with $-s\le j\le s$, with a maximizing mark at continuous coordinate $(0,0)$ over each such base. In each dimension the normalized maximum is $T_s/M_s=1/3-2/(3M_s)>1/8$. Thus a count of maximizing integer bases depending only on $n,d$ is impossible for arbitrary faceted mixed bodies.

pk-intake-arbitrarily-small-full-rank-ga.relation_to_goal: Actual caps with bounds tight at their own common budget; partial menus need not cover the mixed set or contain globally deepest marks. No obstruction is claimed for a rule retaining only globally justified cap constraints.
pk-intake-arbitrarily-small-full-rank-ga.statement:
For a finite base $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ of full affine rank, $n\ge1$, positive compact convex $d$-fibers, $d\ge1$, and positive prior $\pi_z$, fix $\alpha>0$. Choose $n$ affinely independent vertices $v_i$ of any facet of $\operatorname{conv}P$ and $0<q<\min\{\alpha,\pi_{v_1},\ldots,\pi_{v_n}\}$. There are actual ambient closed caps $H_i$ of original mass $q$ with capture fractions $g_i(z)=(q/\pi_{v_i})\mathbf1_{\{z=v_i\}}$. Their base covariance vectors span $\mathbb R^n$ at every positive posterior. Preservation of these active $q$-bounds forces $A_t=0$ in any existing adaptive Gaussian process of the stated type.

On $[0,2]\times T$ for the ordinary triangle, the caps $\lambda_j(X)-z\ge1/3$ have probability $4/27<2/9$, cover only the index-zero fiber, and each has scalar base covariance $-4/27$ initially and nonzero covariance at every positive posterior. On $[-1,1]^n\times T$ for a $d$-simplex, all $3^n$ original base probabilities are $3^{-n}<2^{-n}$. At the $n$ corners $v_0=\mathbf1$ and $v_i=\mathbf1-2e_i$ for $1\le i<n$, use the $d+1$ caps $\lambda_j(X)+v_i\cdot(z-v_i)\ge1/(d+1)$. They cover their respective selected fibers and have common original budget $\Gamma_d/3^n<\Gamma_d/2^n$, with full covariance rank at every positive posterior. The original point $(0,g_T)$ has normalized depth at least $\Gamma_d/2$.

pk-intake-arbitrary-law-two-capacity-bou.relation_to_goal: A pair of scalar capacities and the associated at-most-two-row stochastic stratum, not arbitrary row counts or mixed-integer depth.
pk-intake-arbitrary-law-two-capacity-bou.statement: Let $d\ge2$ be an integer, $p=d/(d-1)$, and $U,V$ nonnegative random variables on a probability space with $U+V\le1$ almost surely. Let $a=\inf_{t>0:\Pr(U\le t)>0}t/\Pr(U\le t)^{1/d}$ and define $b$ with $V$ in place of $U$. Then $a^p+b^p\le1$, including laws with atoms. Consequently, for any integer $d\ge1$ and any nonnegative $(d+1)$-square column-stochastic matrix $X$ with at most two nonzero rows, its row capacities $\phi_d(X_i)=\inf_{t>0:\Pr(X_i\cdot\Xi\le t)>0}t/\Pr(X_i\cdot\Xi\le t)^{1/d}$ for uniform barycentric $\Xi$ belong to $D_d$, the downward set of off-diagonal row geometric means of zero-diagonal column-stochastic matrices of the same size.
