pk-intake-dominated-midpoint-center-set-.relation_to_goal: Optimizes one fixed group of actual source fibers with exact dominated selections and one fixed receiving fiber. It gives no simultaneous physical capacity allocation across overlapping groups.
pk-intake-dominated-midpoint-center-set-.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$ and let a compact convex set in $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ have positive-volume fibers $A_1,\ldots,A_k$ at integer bases $z_1,\ldots,z_k$, with $k\ge2$ and $m=k^{-1}\sum_j z_j\in\mathbb Z^n$. Let $K$ be its actual $m$-fiber, with volume $b>0$ and volume centroid $g_K$. Consider couplings whose marginals $\sigma_j\le \mathbf1_{A_j}\,dx$ all have mass $t$, and whose arithmetic-mean pushforward satisfies $\eta\le\mathbf1_K\,dx$. Let $Y$ be the set of centroids of $\mathbf1_K\,dx+k\eta$ over all such couplings, including the zero coupling. For $t>0$ put $Z_t(A)=\{t^{-1}\int x\,d\sigma:0\le\sigma\le\mathbf1_A\,dx,\ \sigma(A)=t\}$.

Then $Y$ is compact, convex, and contained in $K$. Its part obtainable at fixed mass $t>0$ is exactly
$$
 Y_t=\frac{b g_K+tZ_t(A_1)+\cdots+tZ_t(A_k)}{b+kt},
 \qquad 0<t\le\min_j|A_j|,
$$
and at $t=0$ it is $\{g_K\}$. At fixed marginals the center does not depend on the coupling. For every $u\ne0$, $h_Y(u)=\max_{y\in Y}u\cdot y$ is the unique real root in $h$ of
$$
 D_u(h)=b(u\cdot g_K-h)+
 \min_{\sum_j v_j=0}\sum_{j=1}^k \int_{A_j}(u\cdot x-h+v_j)_+\,dx.
$$
The inner minimum is attained at finite multipliers. At any minimizer the $k$ selected strict positive-part caps have equal mass, and their volume restrictions maximize the corresponding primal equal-mass objective. The outer function is continuous and $D_u(h_2)\le D_u(h_1)-b(h_2-h_1)$ for $h_2>h_1$. For $u=0$ the support is zero. In particular for $k=2$ the multiplier vector is $(v,-v)$ and the same formulas give the exact two-source center set and its one-scalar inner minimum.

For every closed ambient halfspace $H$, write $H_z=\{x:(z,x)\in H\}$. Every feasible coupling gives $\eta(H_m)\le\sum_j \sigma_j(H_{z_j})$. When the source bases are pairwise distinct and different from $m$, $|K\cap H_m|+\eta(H_m)$ is therefore a lower bound for the original mixed cap mass.

with no rate-zero defect. Thus $N_e$ is the uniform-rate kernel image of the surface defect with the normal forgotten.

pk-intake-effective-cap-count-profile.relation_to_goal: Ordinary continuous cap volumes. The result may be used in the affine hull of one positive-dimensional mixed fiber. pk-intake-effective-cap-count-profile.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^D$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body of volume $V$, with $D\ge1$. $$
\sum_{i\in I}(A_i-\alpha)_+ + \frac{\alpha}{\gamma_{\min(\rho,j-1)}}\ge V,
\qquad x_+=\max(x,0).

Consequently, with $s=\min(D,m-1)$,
$$
\sum_{i=1}^m(A_i-\alpha)_+ + \frac{\alpha}{\gamma_s}\ge V
\quad(\alpha\ge0),
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^m A_i-V\ge (m-1/\gamma_s)\min_i A_i .
$$

pk-intake-effective-three-fiber-section-.relation_to_goal: Intrinsic effective-section measure with per-fiber Hausdorff dimension $d-1$. Its overlap bounds concern these sections and supply no ambient shape derivative or ambient mixed-volume cap budget.
pk-intake-effective-three-fiber-section-.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let convex bodies $K_{-1},K_0,K_1\subset\mathbb R^d$ at the indicated bases satisfy $(K_{-1}+K_1)/2\subseteq K_0$. Fix $y\in\operatorname{int}K_0$, a unit vector $u$, and $v\in\mathbb R$. In the ambient plane $P=\{u\cdot(x-y)+vz=0\}$ let $\tau$ be the sum of the ordinary central section measure and endpoint submeasures dominated by the respective $H^{d-1}$ section measures. Assume the endpoint masses are both $s\ge0$ and $\int x\,d\tau=S y$, where $S=S_0+2s$ is the total and $S_0>0$ is the central section mass. Write $\Gamma_q=(q/(q+1))^q$ for $q\ge1$ and $\Gamma_0=1$. Every closed halfspace of $P$ containing $(0,y)$ has $\tau$-mass at least $\kappa S$, where $\kappa=\Gamma_{d-1}/2$. If $d\ge2$ and $s=0$, the lower bound improves to $\Gamma_{d-1}S$. If $d=1$, the exact depth fraction is $(1+s)/(1+2s)$.

For any closed ambient through-$(0,y)$ cap $H'=\{u'\cdot(x-y)+v'z\ge0\}$ with unit $u'$, set $p=\tau(H')/S$ and $b'=\tau(\partial H')/S$. Then $\kappa\le p\le\min(1,1-\kappa+b')$. If $u'$ and $u$ are nonparallel, $b'=0$. If $u'=\epsilon u$, $\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, and $v'=\epsilon v$, then $p=b'=1$. Otherwise in the parallel case
$$
p=\frac{S_0+s}{S_0+2s}\in[2/3,1],\qquad b'=\frac{S_0}{S_0+2s}.
$$
In a finite family of such anchored caps, the average cap indicator on any one's effective section is at least $\kappa+(1-\kappa)\lambda_j$ in normalized section mass, where $\lambda_j$ is that section's own cap weight in the probability mixture.

pk-intake-ehrhart-first-two-coefficient-.relation_to_goal: A lattice-point dilation estimate in the saturated affine lattice. It does not assert a mixed center.
pk-intake-ehrhart-first-two-coefficient-.statement:
Let $Q\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty lattice polytope of affine dimension $s$, and let $N=|Q\cap\mathbb Z^n|$. For every integer $m\ge1$,
$$
|mQ\cap\mathbb Z^n|\ge B_m(s,N):=\binom{m+s}{s}+(N-s-1)\binom{m+s-1}{s}.
$$
For $s=0$, both sides equal one.

pk-intake-eight-base-original-exact-uppe.relation_to_goal: Exact finite geometry of one original radius profile. The graph Helly obstruction is compatible with a positive mixed-volume depth bound.
pk-intake-eight-base-original-exact-uppe.statement: Let $p_0,\ldots,p_7$ in order be $(-1,-2),(-1,-1),(-1,0),(0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,2),(2,3)$, and put $Q=\operatorname{conv}\lbrace p_0,p_2,p_5,p_7\rbrace$. Then $Q\cap\mathbb Z^2$ consists exactly of the eight displayed bases, with heights $(8,11,14,16,12,8,10,8)$. The upper facets of the lifted hull have sampled index sets $\lbrace0,1,2,3\rbrace$, $\lbrace2,3,4,5,6,7\rbrace$, and $\lbrace0,3,7\rbrace$. The projections of these facets contain exactly their indicated sampled bases as lattice points. The maximum-height roots in parities $(1,0),(1,1),(0,0),(0,1)$ are $2,1,3,4$, respectively. pk-intake-eight-base-revised-independent.relation_to_goal: An obstruction to independent root-face Helly guarantees with full overlap counted on both faces. It does not assert a shallow actual centroid or a failure of the locked conjecture.
pk-intake-eight-base-revised-independent.statement:

C=\lbrace(z,x): z\in Q,\ 0\le x\le r(z)\rbrace.

Then $C$ is a full-dimensional compact convex body with exactly these eight positive integer fibers, whose lengths are $(50,75,100,68,68,68,36,4)/100$. pk-intake-eight-base-zero-forest-grouped.relation_to_goal: Weighted depth at actual centroid marks for the specified eight-node midpoint pattern, uniformly over its allowable dimensions, translations and radii. There is no general forest aggregation claim.
pk-intake-eight-base-zero-forest-grouped.statement:
Let $p_0,\ldots,p_7$ in order be $(-1,-2),(-1,-1),(-1,0),(0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,2),(2,3)$. Let an actual compact convex source in $\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb R^d$ for an integer $d\ge1$ have these eight positive integer fibers and no others, all translates of positive homothetic copies of a common convex body with nonempty interior. Let $w_i$ denote the volume of fiber $i$ and $T=\sum_iw_i$. Give the graph of actual fiber centroids the atomic weights $w_i$. Write
$$
A=w_3,\qquad G=w_2,\qquad L=w_0+w_1,\qquad B=w_4+w_5,\qquad C=w_6+w_7.
$$
One of the marks at indices $3,2,1,4$ has raw atomic depth at least $D=\max\lbrace A,G,L,B+\min(G,C)\rbrace\ge T/4$. The same mark has raw mixed depth at least $\gamma_d D\ge\gamma_d T/4$, where $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Here depth is the infimum of the respective mass over closed ambient halfspaces containing the mark.

pk-intake-ellipsoidal-stationary-reflect.relation_to_goal: Ordinary volume in the ellipsoidal homothetic model with each central section centered. The original normals need not have rank at most two.
pk-intake-ellipsoidal-stationary-reflect.statement:
Let $d=m+1\ge2$, let $D\subset\mathbb R^m$ be a centered full-dimensional ellipsoid, and let $r$ be positive and concave on $[a,b]$ with $a<0<b$. Put $K=\{(X,z):a\le z\le b,\ X\in r(z)D\}$. For a finite menu of unit normals $u_i$, let $S_i=\mathcal H^{d-1}(K\cap u_i^\perp)$ and $p_i=|K\cap\{Y:u_i\cdot Y\ge0\}|/|K|$. Suppose each section has centroid $0$, and $\theta_i\ge0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$, $\sum_i\theta_i S_i u_i=0$. Then
$$
\sum_i\theta_i p_i\ge c_d,\qquad
c_2=\frac49,\qquad
c_d=\frac1{1+\max\{4/3,\sqrt{2(d-1)/d}\}}\quad(d\ge3).
$$
In particular, $c_d=3/7$ for $3\le d\le9$, $c_d>2/5$ for $d\ge10$, and $c_d\ge(d/(d+1))^d$.

pk-intake-endpoint-trimming-means-of-log.relation_to_goal: A scalar estimate for one-coordinate section centroids with supporting endpoints.
pk-intake-endpoint-trimming-means-of-log.statement:
Let $w_0,\ldots,w_L$ be positive and log-concave, $L\ge2$. Keep all interior weights and independently allow the endpoint weights at $0,L$ to vary between zero and $w_0,w_L$, respectively. The set of weighted means is the interval with endpoints
$$
m_-=\frac{\sum_{i=0}^{L-1}i w_i}{\sum_{i=0}^{L-1}w_i},\qquad
m_+=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{L}i w_i}{\sum_{i=1}^{L}w_i}.
$$
Its length $m_+-m_-$ is at most one, and the bound is attained for constant weights.

pk-intake-energy-only-compact-class-atta.relation_to_goal: Unrestricted minimization within the positive compatible class on one fixed base, conditional on original-depth compact representatives. The normalized energy-only buffer omits the local volume factor of the body-tied profile. The sharp payment inequality is a separate question.
pk-intake-energy-only-compact-class-atta.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in an affine lattice, equal to the lattice points of $\operatorname{conv}P$, and let $d\ge1$. At each $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, with $\sum_z\lambda_zK_z\subseteq K_p$ whenever $\sum_z\lambda_z z=p\in P$ is a convex representation. Write $C$ for the canonical convex hull of the lifted fibers, $C_z$ for its fiber over $z$, and $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathbf1_{K_z}\,dX)$ for the measured fibers. Put $M=\sum_z|K_z|$, let $g_z$ be the centroid of $K_z$, and define
$$
N=d+1,\qquad
\Sigma=\frac1M\sum_z\int_{K_z}(X-g_z)(X-g_z)^{\mathsf T}\,dX,\qquad
\Gamma(u)=\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma u},\qquad
f(z,x)=\left(\frac{E_{C_z}(x)}{M}\right)^{1/N}.
$$
Here $E_K(y)$ is the minimum of $\int_K[1+a\cdot(X-y)]^{-N}\,dX$ over parameters with positive denominator on $K$ when $y\in\operatorname{int}K$, and is zero on the own boundary. At a sampled mark $(p,y)$, the raw buffered depth $b_\varepsilon(p,y)$ is the infimum of $\mu$-masses of the closed caps
$$
a\cdot(Z-p)+u\cdot(X-y)\ge-\varepsilon f(p,y)\Gamma(u),\qquad u\ne0,
$$
and of the closed pure-base caps containing $p$ (with value $M$ in base rank zero). Write $\beta_\varepsilon(K)=\max_{p\in P,\ y\in K_p}b_\varepsilon(p,y)/M$. The case $\varepsilon=0$ gives ordinary normalized closed-halfspace depth.

Fix $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ and let $k(P)$ be the number of occupied parity classes in the inherited affine lattice. Suppose $\beta_0(K^{\rm ref})<b<\gamma_d/k(P)$ for a positive compatible family on $P$. Assume there is a compact set $\mathcal A$ of positive compatible families for the simultaneous Hausdorff metric with $M=1$, $K_z\subseteq R B_d$ and $\beta_0\le b$, such that every positive compatible family with $\beta_0\le b$ can be taken into $\mathcal A$ by an invertible map $(z,X)\mapsto(z,AX+Bz+c)$. Here $R>0$, $B_d$ is the Euclidean unit ball, and $L=|P||B_{d-1}|R^{d-1}$ with $|B_0|=1$.

For every $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that $\varepsilon_0LR<b-\beta_0(K^{\rm ref})$, and every $0\le\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$, the infimum $\beta_\varepsilon^*=\inf_K\beta_\varepsilon(K)$ over all positive compatible families on the fixed $P$ is attained, with a representative in $\mathcal A$. Moreover
$$
\beta_0^*\le\beta_\varepsilon^*\le\beta_0^*+\varepsilon LR .
$$
For $\varepsilon_j\to0$ in that interval, any sequence of minimizers can be represented in $\mathcal A$ and has subsequences converging there to ordinary minimizers. If also $\varepsilon_0 LR<\gamma_d/(4|P|)$, every buffered maximizing mark of every family in $\mathcal A$ has a proper own shifted trace in every nonvertical direction.

pk-intake-energy-only-exact-fixed-cover.relation_to_goal: An exact bound on actual buffered depth on a fixed finite support, using the old energy-only groups and recomputed covariance. Paths may be nonnested and need only converge in Hausdorff distance at the initial family.
pk-intake-energy-only-exact-fixed-cover.statement:
Take a positive compatible family and fixed energy-only buffered cap groups as in the preceding parity-face theorem. In particular, $\varepsilon>0$ is fixed, $Q$ is the old raw maximum, $I$ is the set of old deepest bases, $J_i$ cover $I$, and the selected caps have fixed normals $N_{ij}=(a_{ij},u_{ij})$ and actual mass $Q$ at thresholds $c_{ij}$. Use the same $P_i,h_i,\rho_{ij}$ as in that theorem. Let $K_z(t)$ be positive compatible bodies on the same bases with $K_z(t)\to K_z$ in Hausdorff distance as $t\downarrow0$. Write $\mu_t,M_t,\Gamma_t,f_t,b_{\varepsilon,t}$ for their actual measure, mass, covariance norm, energy-only profile and raw buffered depth. Put
$$
A_i(t)=\sum_j\rho_{ij}\Gamma_t(u_{ij}),\qquad
\alpha_i(t)=\min_{z\in J_i,\ x\in K_z(t)}
[P_i(z,x)-h_i-\varepsilon A_i(t)f_t(z,x)].
$$
Then $A_i(t)\to1$, $\alpha_i(t)\to0$, and the minimizing marks approach the finite old contact set $\{(z,y_z):z\in J_i\}$. For each $i,j$ let $c_{ij}(t,q)$ be the right upper $q$-quantile of $\mu_t$ in the fixed normal $N_{ij}$. For small $t$ there is a unique solution $q_i(t)$ near $Q$ to
$$
\sum_j\rho_{ij}c_{ij}(t,q_i(t))=h_i+\alpha_i(t).
$$
It tends to $Q$, and for all small $t$ one has
$$
b_{\varepsilon,t}(z,x)\le q_i(t)\quad (z\in J_i,\ x\in K_z(t)),\qquad
M_t\beta_\varepsilon(K(t))\le\max_i q_i(t).
$$

pk-intake-energy-only-finite-contact-der.relation_to_goal: First variation of the scalar whole-fiber contact budget for fixed normals on one actual path. The covariance and mass normalizations both enter the invariant energy-only coefficient.
pk-intake-energy-only-finite-contact-der.statement:
In the exact fixed-cover continuation for the energy-only covariance buffer, assume the compatible path also satisfies the bounded signed radial hypotheses of the uniform marked-energy and covariance lemma. Use its $D,J,C_z(y)$, and for group $i$ write $E_i=E_{K_z}(y_z)$ and $f_i=(E_i/M)^{1/N}$ for the old common energy and profile at its contacts. Put
$$
J_i^{\rm cov}=\sum_j\rho_{ij}u_{ij}^{\mathsf T}J u_{ij}.
$$
Then $A_i(t)=1+t(D-J_i^{\rm cov})/(2M)+o(t)$, and
$$
\alpha_i(t)=t\,\dot\alpha_i+o(t),\qquad
\dot\alpha_i=\varepsilon f_i
\left[\min_{z\in J_i}\frac{C_z(y_z)}{NE_i}
+\frac{J_i^{\rm cov}}{2M}-\frac{(N+2)D}{2NM}\right].
$$
In the variant with the old norm held fixed and the unnormalized profile $E^{1/N}$, use the corresponding old cap groups (equivalently rescale the old buffer parameter by $M^{-1/N}$). For its fixed parameter $\varepsilon$ the formula becomes $\dot\alpha_i=\varepsilon E_i^{1/N}\min_{z\in J_i}C_z(y_z)/(NE_i)$.

pk-intake-energy-only-parity-face-groups.relation_to_goal: Fixed positive old family and energy-only covariance buffer. The group count uses the inherited lattice of the fixed base, and the whole-fiber rigidity is facewise.
pk-intake-energy-only-parity-face-groups.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in an affine lattice, equal to the lattice points of $\operatorname{conv}P$, and let $d\ge1$. At each $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, with $\sum_z\lambda_zK_z\subseteq K_p$ whenever $\sum_z\lambda_z z=p\in P$ is a convex representation. Write $C$ for the canonical convex hull of the lifted fibers, $C_z$ for its fiber over $z$, and $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathbf1_{K_z}\,dX)$ for the measured fibers. Put $M=\sum_z|K_z|$, let $g_z$ be the centroid of $K_z$, and define
$$
N=d+1,\qquad
\Sigma=\frac1M\sum_z\int_{K_z}(X-g_z)(X-g_z)^{\mathsf T}\,dX,\qquad
\Gamma(u)=\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma u},\qquad
f(z,x)=\left(\frac{E_{C_z}(x)}{M}\right)^{1/N}.
$$
Here $E_K(y)$ is the minimum of $\int_K[1+a\cdot(X-y)]^{-N}\,dX$ over parameters with positive denominator on $K$ when $y\in\operatorname{int}K$, and is zero on the own boundary. At a sampled mark $(p,y)$, the raw buffered depth $b_\varepsilon(p,y)$ is the infimum of $\mu$-masses of the closed caps
$$
a\cdot(Z-p)+u\cdot(X-y)\ge-\varepsilon f(p,y)\Gamma(u),\qquad u\ne0,
$$
and of the closed pure-base caps containing $p$ (with value $M$ in base rank zero). Write $\beta_\varepsilon(K)=\max_{p\in P,\ y\in K_p}b_\varepsilon(p,y)/M$. The case $\varepsilon=0$ gives ordinary normalized closed-halfspace depth.

Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and suppose every old buffered maximizing mark has a proper shifted own section in every nonvertical direction, meaning the shifted plane cuts its own fiber interior. Let $Q=M\beta_\varepsilon$ and $I$ be the sampled bases at which $Q$ is attained. Then $I$ is the full lattice trace of $\operatorname{conv}I$. There are at most $k(I)\le k(P)$ cap groups, with parity counted in the inherited affine lattice of $P$. Each group $i$ is associated with a face $F_i$ of $\operatorname{conv}I$ and an old maximizing source over a sampled base in $\operatorname{relint}F_i$. The sets $J_i=I\cap F_i$ cover $I$. Each group consists of at most $d+1$ nonvertical caps $\{N_{ij}\cdot(Z,X)\ge c_{ij}\}$ of actual mass $Q$, with $N_{ij}=(a_{ij},u_{ij})$, $\Gamma(u_{ij})=1$, and weights $\rho_{ij}>0$ summing to one. They are proper on the group source's own fiber and their thresholds are right upper $Q$-quantiles. Define $P_i(z,x)=\sum_j\rho_{ij}N_{ij}\cdot(z,x)$ and $h_i=\sum_j\rho_{ij}c_{ij}$. Then
$$
P_i(z,x)-h_i-\varepsilon f(z,x)\ge0\qquad(z\in F_i,\ x\in C_z).
$$
For every real $z\in F_i$ the zero is a unique own-interior mark $y_z$, every selected buffered quantile constraint is an equality there, and the marks are affine on $F_i$. The bodies $C_z-y_z$ and the positive energy $E_{C_z}(y_z)=E_i$ are constant on that face, so $f(z,y_z)=(E_i/M)^{1/N}$.

pk-intake-energy-only-regular-cover-resp.relation_to_goal: First derivative of the finite covering upper bound, with regular selected cap expansions, for one actual compatible fixed-base path. Existence of a path satisfying every strict sign test at an attained minimum is a separate problem.
pk-intake-energy-only-regular-cover-resp.statement:
Use the exact fixed-cover continuation and its finite-contact derivative on one actual compatible signed radial path for the energy-only buffer. Put $\beta=Q/M$ and $\dot M=-D$. Suppose for each selected old cap its actual tail has the regular joint expansion
$$
\mu_t\{N_{ij}\cdot(Z,X)\ge c_{ij}+t s\}
=Q-t(L_{ij}+S_{ij}s)+o(t),\qquad S_{ij}>0,
$$
uniformly on bounded $s$ intervals. Here $L_{ij}$ is the first loss of mass at the fixed threshold. A sufficient trace condition is that each selected plane on each old fiber be a proper section, a strict full or empty cut, or a supporting section of zero $(d-1)$-dimensional measure. Under this condition $S_{ij}$ is the sum of proper section measures divided by $\lVert u_{ij}\rVert$, and $L_{ij}$ integrates the signed inward speed on the captured old boundary.

Let $B_i=\sum_j\rho_{ij}/S_{ij}$ and $\theta_{ij}=(\rho_{ij}/S_{ij})/B_i$. Then the right derivatives of the continued budgets satisfy
$$
\dot q_i=-\sum_j\theta_{ij}L_{ij}-\frac{\dot\alpha_i}{B_i},
\qquad
\left.\frac{d}{dt^+}\right|_{0}\frac{q_i(t)}{M_t}
=-\frac{\sum_j\theta_{ij}L_{ij}+\dot\alpha_i/B_i-\beta D}{M}.
$$
If $\sum_j\theta_{ij}L_{ij}+\dot\alpha_i/B_i>\beta D$ for every old group on this one path, then $\beta_\varepsilon(K(t))<\beta$ for all sufficiently small $t>0$.

pk-intake-entropy-balanced-mass-equality.relation_to_goal: Compares scalar finite-base capacities. Dominated escort mass is given by the separate factor c.
pk-intake-entropy-balanced-mass-equality.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in an affine Euclidean space, with masses $m_z>0$ for $z\in P$, and put $Q=\operatorname{conv} P$ and $M=\sum_{z\in P}m_z$. Fix $N>0$ and $p\in Q$. Let $F_p$ be the unique face of $Q$ with $p\in\operatorname{relint} F_p$, and write $P_p=P\cap F_p$ and $V_p=\operatorname{span}(F_p-p)$. Set
$$
L_z(\alpha)=1+\alpha\cdot(z-p),\qquad
E_p=\inf_{\substack{\alpha\in V_p\\L_z(\alpha)>0\ (z\in P_p)}}\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z L_z(\alpha)^{-N}.
$$

Let $\alpha_p$ be the unique relative minimizer and $M_p=\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z$. For $p\in Q$ define
$$
T_p=\max_{\substack{0\le q_z\le m_z\\\sum_{z\in P}q_z(z-p)=0}}\sum_{z\in P}q_z,\qquad
D_p=\min_{H\ni p}\sum_{z\in P\cap H}m_z,
$$
where $H$ ranges over closed affine halfspaces in $\operatorname{aff} Q$, with the whole-space trace allowed, including rank zero. The capacity and the halfspace depth are unchanged on restriction to $P_p$ in $\operatorname{aff}F_p$. With $a$ ranging over $\operatorname{span}(Q-p)$,
$$
T_p=\inf_a\sum_{z\in P}m_z(1+a\cdot(z-p))_+,\qquad
E_p\ge T_p\ge D_p .
$$
Writing $b_N(L)=L^{-N}-(1-N(L-1))_+$ for $L>0$, one has
$$
E_p-T_p\ge\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z b_N(L_z(\alpha_p)),\qquad
E_p=T_p\ \Longleftrightarrow\ p=M_p^{-1}\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z z .
$$
At equality $E_p=T_p=M_p$.

The escort masses $e_z=m_z L_z(\alpha_p)^{-N-1}$ on $P_p$ and zero off $P_p$ are dominated by the $m_z$ exactly when $\alpha_p=0$. The largest scalar $c\ge0$ with $c e_z\le m_z$ for all $z$ is $c=\min_{z\in P_p}L_z(\alpha_p)^{N+1}$. The resulting dominated row has total mass $cE_p$ and mean $p$. On the whole of $Q$, $E_p\le M$ with equality exactly at the original weighted base mean. If this mean is occupied and the compatible-fiber assumptions of the face-attainment result hold with $m_z=|K_z|$, its escort-selected continuous coordinate equals the original volume-weighted fiber centroid.

pk-intake-entropy-face-attainment-dual.relation_to_goal: Finite weighted bases and real N>0. Fiber compatibility gives membership of the centroid combination in its fiber.
pk-intake-entropy-face-attainment-dual.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in an affine Euclidean space, with masses $m_z>0$ for $z\in P$, and put $Q=\operatorname{conv} P$ and $M=\sum_{z\in P}m_z$. Fix $N>0$ and $p\in Q$. Let $F_p$ be the unique face of $Q$ with $p\in\operatorname{relint} F_p$, and write $P_p=P\cap F_p$ and $V_p=\operatorname{span}(F_p-p)$. Set
$$
L_z(\alpha)=1+\alpha\cdot(z-p),\qquad
E_p=\inf_{\substack{\alpha\in V_p\\L_z(\alpha)>0\ (z\in P_p)}}\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z L_z(\alpha)^{-N}.
$$

The infimum is attained at a unique $\alpha_p$. Its value is also the infimum of the analogous sum over $P$ with $\alpha\in\operatorname{span}(Q-p)$ and all denominators positive. This latter infimum is attained exactly when $F_p=Q$. In particular a singleton face $F_p=\{p\}$ gives $E_p=m_p$.

Let $e_z=m_zL_z(\alpha_p)^{-N-1}$ on $P_p$, and $e_z=0$ off $P_p$. Then $\sum_{z\in P}e_z=E_p$ and $\sum_{z\in P}e_z z=E_p p$. With $s=N/(N+1)$,
$$
E_p=\max_{\substack{\lambda_z\ge0,\ \sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z=1\\\sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z z=p}}
\left(\sum_{z\in P}m_z^{1/(N+1)}\lambda_z^s\right)^{N+1},
$$
and the unique maximizer is $\lambda_z=e_z/E_p$. In particular $E_p^{1/(N+1)}$ is concave on $Q$. If $\pi_z=m_z/M$ and $D_s(\lambda\Vert\pi)=(s-1)^{-1}\log\sum_z\lambda_z^s\pi_z^{1-s}$, then $E_p/M=\exp(-\min_\lambda D_s(\lambda\Vert\pi))$, over the same constraint set.

If $p\in P$ and $m_z$ are volumes of positive-volume compact convex $d$-fibers $K_z$ with centroids $g_z$, assume $\sum_z\lambda_z K_z\subseteq K_p$ for the displayed maximizing row (as for fibers of a convex body). Then $\sum_z\lambda_z g_z\in\operatorname{int}K_p$.

pk-intake-entropy-lattice-maximum-equali.relation_to_goal: Lattice-complete finite weighted supports. The conclusion is about the maximum of a scalar base energy.
pk-intake-entropy-lattice-maximum-equali.statement:
Let $\Lambda=c+L$ be an affine lattice, and let $P$ be a nonempty finite set with $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\Lambda$. Give every $z\in P$ mass $m_z>0$, put $M=\sum_{z\in P}m_z$, and let $k$ be the number of occupied cosets modulo $2L$. For $N>0$ let $E_p$ be the power-entropy energy defined in the face-attainment result, using the minimal face of $\operatorname{conv}(P)$ at each $p\in P$. Then
$$
\max_{p\in P}E_p\ge M/k,\qquad
\max_{p\in P}E_p=M/k
\ \Longleftrightarrow\
P\text{ consists of exactly }k\text{ vertices, all with mass }M/k.
$$
If $\operatorname{rank}L\le n$, the maximum is at least $M/2^n$, with equality exactly when $k=2^n$ and the same equal-vertex condition holds. Equal masses on $\{0,1\}^n$ attain this bound.

pk-intake-equal-canonical-fractions-alig.relation_to_goal: Exact oriented canonical fractions in each full-dimensional fiber; arbitrary equal noncanonical fractions and a physical escape are separate assertions.
pk-intake-equal-canonical-fractions-alig.statement: Let $d\ge2$ and let $K$ be a centroid-zero $d$-simplex with barycentric functions $1/(d+1)+l_i(x)$, $1\le i\le d+1$. Let $(K_z)$ be a finite compatible family of positive full-dimensional compact convex fibers with an affine interior section $q(z)$. If for every $z,i$ the cap $l_i(x-q(z))\ge0$ captures exactly the fraction $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ of $K_z$, then $K_z=q(z)+r_zK$ for some $r_z>0$ at every $z$. In particular $q$ is the centroid section.

pk-intake-equal-endpoint-actual-mixed-ce.relation_to_goal: Strict normalized depth above the sharp three-fiber threshold at the actual mixed centroid with one integer coordinate and equal endpoint masses.
pk-intake-equal-endpoint-actual-mixed-ce.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, and let $A,K,B\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies of volumes $v,k,v>0$ with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Let $\mu$ be the sum of the $d$-volumes on the integer fibers $A,K,B$ at bases $-1,0,1$ of their lifted convex hull. The actual mixed centroid is

$$
Y=\left(0,\frac{v g_A+k g_K+v g_B}{k+2v}\right),
$$

where $g_A,g_K,g_B$ are the uniform-volume centroids. It lies in $\lbrace 0\rbrace\times\operatorname{int}K$. Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, $A_d=1/\Gamma_d$, and let the positive constant $\varepsilon_d$ be

$$
\varepsilon_d=\frac{d}{d+1}\left[2+(1+1/d)(1+A_d/3)
-2(1+1/(2d))^{d+1}-2(1-(4A_d/3-1)/(2d))_+^{d+1}\right],
$$

with $t_+=\max(t,0)$. The raw depth at $Y$, the infimum of $\mu(H)$ over closed ambient halfspaces containing $Y$, is at least

$$
\frac{3\Gamma_d}{4}(k+v)+
\min\left(\frac{3\Gamma_d^2\varepsilon_d k}{4\cdot3^d},
               (1-3\Gamma_d/4)(k+v)\right).
$$

In particular it is strictly greater than $(3\Gamma_d/4)(k+v)\ge(\Gamma_d/2)(k+2v)$. The same conclusion holds in any convex body whose only positive $d$-volume integer fibers are those three fibers; any other integer fibers of zero $d$-volume do not affect $\mu$.

pk-intake-equal-endpoint-centroid-direct.relation_to_goal: Paired continuous cap volumes centered at the true Minkowski midpoint centroid. An arbitrary superbody centroid cannot be substituted in the argument.
pk-intake-equal-endpoint-centroid-direct.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $A,B$ be $d$-dimensional convex bodies of the same volume $a>0$. Let $M=(A+B)/2$ and let $g_M$ be its ordinary centroid. For $u\ne0$, put $w_D=h_D(u)+h_D(-u)$ for each body $D$, with $h_D$ its support function. For $t\in\mathbb R$ let $P$ denote the sum of the ordinary volumes captured on $A,B$ by $u\cdot x\ge u\cdot g_M+t$ and $u\cdot x\ge u\cdot g_M-t$, respectively. Then
$$
 h_M(u)-u\cdot g_M\ge\frac{w_A+w_B}{2(d+1)},
 \qquad P/a\ge\frac1{(d+1)^d}.
$$
If $d\ge2$, then for $R=w_A/w_B$,
$$
 P/a\ge W_d(R):=\frac{(R+1)^d}{(d+1)^d(R^{d/(d-1)}+1)^{d-1}} .
$$
The bounds hold for every such $u,t$, including supporting, full and empty endpoint traces.

pk-intake-equal-endpoint-minkowski-volum.relation_to_goal: Equal endpoint volumes and a restricted volume of their true Minkowski midpoint. The actual middle fiber may be larger, and it remains in the mixed denominator.
pk-intake-equal-endpoint-minkowski-volum.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $A,K,B$ be $d$-dimensional convex bodies with $|A|=|B|=a>0$ and $M=(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Write $m=|M|$, $k=|K|$, $r=m/a$, $\Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d$ and let $g_M,g_K$ denote their ordinary centroids. Suppose $1\le r\le11/8$. Set
$$
 \delta_d=\frac{-57+202\Gamma-121\Gamma^2}{64}\ge\frac{55}{7744}>0,
 \qquad c_d=2\Gamma+\delta_d.
$$
For every $u\ne0$ and real $t$, let $P$ be the sum of the $A$ and $B$ cap volumes for the inequalities $u\cdot x\ge u\cdot g_M+t$ and $u\cdot x\ge u\cdot g_M-t$, respectively. Then
$$
 P/a\ge 1-(1-\Gamma)^2r^2\ge\Gamma(2-r)+\delta_d.
$$

Place $A,K,B$ at bases $-1,0,1$ in their lifted convex hull, and measure the resulting three integer fibers by the sum of their ordinary volumes. At $(0,g_M)$ and $(0,g_K)$ the raw depths are at least $c_da$ and $\Gamma k$, respectively. Choose $(0,g_M)$ if $k/a\le c_d/\Gamma$, and $(0,g_K)$ otherwise. The selected point has normalized depth at least $\Gamma c_d/(c_d+2\Gamma)>\Gamma/2$ over all closed ambient halfspaces containing it.

pk-intake-equal-endpoint-sectional-minko.relation_to_goal: Ordinary midpoint volume and actual widths in a fixed continuous direction. No projected cap mass or independent choice of section profile is used.
pk-intake-equal-endpoint-sectional-minko.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $A,B\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies of equal $d$-volume $a>0$. Set $M=(A+B)/2$, $r=|M|/a$, and for any nonzero $u$ put $w_A=h_A(u)+h_A(-u)$, $w_B=h_B(u)+h_B(-u)$ and $R=w_A/w_B$. Then
$$
 |A+B|\ge(w_A+w_B)(a/w_A+a/w_B),
 \qquad R+R^{-1}\le 2^d r-2 .
$$
In all $d\ge1$ one consequently has both $1+R\le 2^d r$ and $1+R^{-1}\le 2^d r$.

pk-intake-equal-endpoint-width-residual-.relation_to_goal: An exact limitation of the uniform residual and support-width estimates for a realized equal-volume pair. The actual three-fiber body satisfies the depth target.
pk-intake-equal-endpoint-width-residual-.statement:
For every $d\ge3$ take centered coordinate boxes $A,B\subset\mathbb R^d$ with side lengths $(1,9/4,4/9,1,\ldots,1)$ and $(1,4/9,9/4,1,\ldots,1)$ respectively. Their volumes are one and their true midpoint $M=(A+B)/2$ has volume $r=9409/5184<2$. Write $\Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d$. For opposite endpoint thresholds in the first coordinate centered at $g_M=0$, the uniform centroid-residual bound $[1-(2[(1-\Gamma)r]^{1/d}-1)^d]_+$ and the exact-width estimate $W_d(1)=2/(d+1)^d$ are both strictly below $\Gamma(2-r)$. In $d=3$ their maximum falls short by $575/12288$. Hence the two lower estimates and the ordinary guarantee $\Gamma |M|$ for the own cap fail to certify the required raw mass $2\Gamma$ on those scalar data.

The actual midpoint-compatible choice $K=(2/r)^{1/d}M$ gives a middle fiber of volume two. The paired endpoint mass in the tested direction equals one for every opposite shift, and the actual mark $(0,0)$ has raw depth at least one in the lifted three-fiber body.

pk-intake-equalized-actual-smoothed-cap-.relation_to_goal: Requires actual $C^2$ cap integrals and contact minimum. It neither supplies them at an arbitrary extremizer nor asserts a sign for the coupled objective.
pk-intake-equalized-actual-smoothed-cap-.statement:
Along an actual scalar body path, let $F_j(t,b)$ be the raw mass of its $j$-th fixed-normal smoothed cap at threshold $b$. Assume $F_j$ is $C^2$ near $(0,b_j)$, $F_j(0,b_j)=Q$, and $S_j=-F_{j,b}(0,b_j)>0$. Fix $\rho_j>0$ with $\sum_j\rho_j=1$. Let $\tau_j(t,Y)$ denote the actual through-mark threshold for mark $Y$ in the deformed source fiber, with any prescribed mark-dependent buffer included, and assume the contact minimum $\alpha(t)=\min_Y\sum_j\rho_j[\tau_j(t,Y)-b_j]$ is $C^2$ and $\alpha(0)=0$. Then the system $F_j(t,b_j(t))=q(t)$ and $\sum_j\rho_j(b_j(t)-b_j)=\alpha(t)$ has a unique nearby $C^2$ branch and supplies a cap depth upper bound $q(t)$ at every mark on that source fiber. Writing $r_j=b_j'(0)$, $B=\sum_j\rho_j/S_j$ and $K_j=F_{j,tt}+2r_jF_{j,tb}+r_j^2F_{j,bb}$ at $(0,b_j)$,
$$
q''(0)=\frac{\sum_j\rho_j K_j/S_j-\alpha''(0)}{B}.
$$

pk-intake-euclidean-sharp-simplex-produc.relation_to_goal: Regularity criterion for normal Fritz–John multipliers at the sharp cap count and cap budget on simplex products.
pk-intake-euclidean-sharp-simplex-produc.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a $d$-simplex of volume $v$, and put $S=\{0,1\}^n\times K$ with summed fiber volume $\mu$ and mass $M=2^n v$. Write $H_j$ for the altitude from vertex $v_j$, $\lambda_j$ for its barycentric coordinate, $g$ for the centroid, $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, and $N_0=2^n(d+1)$. Suppose $d\ge2$ and fix any full cover at count $N_0$ by continuously unit-normal caps with each cap of mass at most $\gamma_d v$. The actual-fiber joint Fritz–John stress system has a solution with objective multiplier $\alpha_0>0$ if and only if $K$ is regular. If $K$ is regular, one may choose $\alpha_0=1$ and all cap-budget multipliers zero.

In the system, $(c_i,P_i,m_i)$ are the cap mass and base and continuous first moments, $(S_i,P_i^s,m_i^s)$ are the corresponding effective section moments with one common density per section and density one on proper sections, $\Psi_i=\int_S(L_i)_+\,d\mu$, and $\lambda_p$ are optimal probability minimax weights at base $p$. The multipliers $\alpha_0,r_i,\eta_p$ are nonnegative with complementarity for budget and cover. At each $\eta_p>0$ the system has a genuine contact $x_p\in K$ with every margin nonpositive and equality on positively weighted caps. Its moment balances are
$$
\begin{aligned}
\alpha_0c_i+r_i S_i&=\sum_p\eta_p\lambda_{pi},\\
\alpha_0P_i+r_i P_i^s&=\sum_p\eta_p\lambda_{pi}p,\\
\alpha_0m_i+r_i m_i^s&=\sum_p\eta_p\lambda_{pi}x_p+\alpha_0\Psi_i u_i .
\end{aligned}
$$

pk-intake-even-unimodal-truncation-energ.relation_to_goal: Supplies an exact ordinary scalar estimate for a truncated symmetric marginal.
pk-intake-even-unimodal-truncation-energ.statement:
Let $\phi$ be a nonnegative bounded compactly supported integrable function on $\mathbb R$, even and nonincreasing on $[0,\infty)$, with mass $M>0$. For $T>0$ put $v=M^{-1}\int_{s\le T}\phi(s)\,ds$. Then $1/2<v\le1$. For each real $p\ge2$, set $c_p=-2(1-v)/(pT)$. The denominator $1+c_p s$ is positive for $s\le T$, and
$$
\frac1M\int_{s\le T}(1+c_p s)^{-p}\phi(s)\,ds
\le\frac{2v-1}{v}.
$$

pk-intake-exact-actual-simplex-support-e.relation_to_goal: An exact geometric bound using the actual endpoint support values and midpoint inclusion. Alignment is required for attainment by the erosion.
pk-intake-exact-actual-simplex-support-e.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $v_1,\ldots,v_{d+1}$ span $\mathbb R^d$ and sum to zero. Set $T=\{x:v_i\cdot x\le1\ \forall i\}$ and $V=|T|$. Let $A,K$ be full-dimensional convex bodies. For every full-dimensional convex $B\subseteq T$ with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$, set $\alpha_i=h_A(-v_i)$, $t_i=h_K(-v_i)$ and $c_i=(1+2t_i-\alpha_i)/(d+1)$. Then
$
B\subseteq E=T\cap\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge\alpha_i-2t_i\ \forall i\}.
$
If some $c_i\le0$, $E$ has zero $d$-volume. Otherwise its exact relative volume is
$
\frac{|E|}{V}=\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d+1\}}(-1)^{|J|}\Bigl(1-\sum_{j\in J}c_j\Bigr)_+^d.
$
If $K=\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge-t_i\ \forall i\}$, then $E=T\cap\{x:x+A\subseteq2K\}$. Whenever this $E$ has positive volume it attains the maximum possible $|B|$ with those $A,K$ and $B\subseteq T$.

pk-intake-exact-balanced-three-fiber-pee.relation_to_goal: An exact directional balance interval and cap estimate for a single tested cap through the true mixed centroid with equal outer masses.
pk-intake-exact-balanced-three-fiber-pee.statement: Suppose the only positive-volume integer fibers of a convex source in $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ are $A,K,B$ at $-1,0,1$, of volumes $a,b,a>0$. Let $H=\{\ell\ge0\}$ be a closed non-pure-base cap through the actual mixed centroid, with affine restrictions $\ell_-,\ell_0,\ell_+$. Define $s=\min\{B(A,\ell_-),B(B,\ell_+)\}$, where $B(D,f)$ is the largest mass of a submeasure of the volume of $D$ with $f$-moment zero. Let $M=2a+b$ and $J(t)=[(2(a-t)^{1+1/d}+b^{1+1/d})/(M-2t)]^d$. The exact feasible common endpoint mass for a decomposition with balanced components at $-1,0,1$ is $t\in[0,s]$, with the residual output at $0$. For each such $t$ one has $\mu(H)\ge\gamma_d[2t+J(t)]$. If both endpoint centroids lie strictly outside $H$, then $\mu(H)\ge\gamma_d[2t+\max\{b,J(t)\}]$.

pk-intake-exact-circuit-quantile-cover-h.relation_to_goal: Second derivatives of a supplied local comparison on an open chart of actual positive fibers. The regularity of the cap masses is a hypothesis.
pk-intake-exact-circuit-quantile-cover-h.statement:
Let $K_w(p)\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a finite actual family of positive compact convex fibers at fixed bases $w\in P$, parametrized on an open neighborhood of $p_0$ (which can be an open coordinate chart of a feasible equality family). Write $\mu_p$ for the sum of their fiber Lebesgue measures and $M(p)>0$ for its total mass. Fix a positive circuit of actual closed caps $H_j(b)=\{(w,x):v_j\cdot w+u_j\cdot x\ge b\}$ through an old interior mark at base $z$, each with the same old raw mass $\tau_0$. The fixed weights satisfy $\sum_j\rho_j=1$, $\sum_j\rho_ju_j=0$, and $A=\sum_j\rho_jv_j$. Assume $F_j(p,b)=\mu_p(H_j(b))$ and $M(p)$ are $C^2$ near the old data and $S_j=-\partial_bF_j(p_0,b_j)>0$.

The actual common-mass thresholds $b_j(p)$ and mass $\tau_c(p)$ solving $F_j(p,b_j(p))=\tau_c(p)$ and $\sum_j\rho_jb_j(p)=A\cdot z$ are locally unique and $C^2$. The caps cover every continuous plane over $A\cdot w\ge A\cdot z$. At the old parameter in direction $\delta$, put $B_j=\partial_pF_j[\delta]$, $\theta_j=(\rho_j/S_j)/\sum_k(\rho_k/S_k)$, $a=\sum_j\theta_jB_j$ and $v'_j=(B_j-a)/S_j$. Then
$$
D\tau_c[\delta]=a,\qquad Db_j[\delta]=v'_j,\qquad
D^2\tau_c[\delta,\delta]=\sum_j\theta_j\bigl(\partial_{pp}F_j[\delta,\delta]+2\partial_{pb}F_j[\delta]v'_j+\partial_{bb}F_j(v'_j)^2\bigr).
$$
For $f_c=\tau_c/M$ with $f_c(p_0)=\beta$, on $\ker Df_c(p_0)$ one has $D^2 f_c[\delta,\delta]=(D^2\tau_c[\delta,\delta]-\beta D^2M[\delta,\delta])/M(p_0)$.

pk-intake-exact-contained-ambient-thicke.relation_to_goal: Exact realization inside the original ambient body, including mixed fibers of zero intrinsic mass.
pk-intake-exact-contained-ambient-thicke.statement: Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be an ambient convex body, $\Lambda=\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, and $q=\dim_H(C\cap\Lambda)>0$. Its intrinsic mixed mass is $R$, its full mixed centroid is $y$, and its normalized local closed-halfspace depth there is $1/2$.

pk-intake-exact-depth-localized-simplex-.relation_to_goal: Ordinary $d$-volume depth for convex subsets of a simplex with missing parts supported in small vertex neighborhoods, with arbitrary shape of the removed parts.
pk-intake-exact-depth-localized-simplex-.statement:
Let $T$ be a full-dimensional $d$-simplex, $d\ge2$, of volume $V$, with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i$, $0\le i\le d$. Set $m=d+1$, $\Gamma=(d/m)^d$. For a dimension-only $\eta_d\in(0,1/2)$, let $U_i=\{x\in T:\lambda_i(x)>1-\eta_d\}$, and let $K$ be any convex body with $T\setminus\bigcup_i U_i\subset K\subset T$. Write $t_i=|U_i\setminus K|/V$ and $t=\sum_i t_i$.

In a fixed neighborhood of the centroid, the minimum ordinary closed cap volume of $K$ at $y$, divided by $V$, is
$$
\min_i \bigl\{d^d\prod_{j\ne i}\lambda_j(y)-t_i\bigr\}.
$$
The global raw maximum is $DV$, where $D$ is the unique root near $\Gamma$ of
$$
\prod_i(D+t_i)\left(\sum_i(D+t_i)^{-1}\right)^d=d^d.
$$
The unique deepest point has barycentrics $\lambda_i^*=(D+t_i)^{-1}/\sum_j(D+t_j)^{-1}$. The normalized maximum is $D/(1-t)$.

pk-intake-exact-depth-small-simplex-corn.relation_to_goal: Ordinary full-dimensional simplex volume, with uniformly small parallel vertex truncations. The unique maximizer and the normalized expansion use remaining volume.
pk-intake-exact-depth-small-simplex-corn.statement:
Let $T$ be a full-dimensional $d$-simplex of volume $V$, with $d\ge1$, barycentrics $\lambda_i$ indexed by $0\le i\le d$, $m=d+1$, and $\Gamma=(d/m)^d$. There is a dimension-only $\varepsilon_*>0$ such that for any $0\le\varepsilon_i\le\varepsilon_*$ the body $K=T\cap\{\lambda_i\le1-\varepsilon_i\ \text{for all }i\}$ has volume $V(1-t)$, where $t_i=\varepsilon_i^d$ and $t=\sum_i t_i$. On a fixed neighborhood of the centroid of $T$, the least $K$-volume in a closed halfspace containing $y$, divided by $V$, is
$$
\min_i\left\{d^d\prod_{j\ne i}\lambda_j(y)-t_i\right\}.
$$
There is a unique root $D$ in a fixed neighborhood of $\Gamma$ of
$$
\prod_i(D+t_i)\left(\sum_i(D+t_i)^{-1}\right)^d=d^d.
$$
The unique global maximizing point is interior to $K$ and has coordinates $\lambda_i^*=c/(D+t_i)$, where $c=(\sum_i(D+t_i)^{-1})^{-1}$. Its raw depth is $DV$ and its normalized depth is $D/(1-t)$. In dimension one the global root and midpoint formula holds throughout $\varepsilon_0+\varepsilon_1<1$, with $D=(1-t)/2$.

For one nonzero corner $t_0=t$ the other barycentrics are equal to $b$, the root near $1/m$ of $d^d b^{d-1}(mb-1)=t$, and $D=d^d(1-db)b^{d-1}$. For $d=2$ these specialize to $b=(1+\sqrt{1+3t})/6$ and $D=2(1+\sqrt{1+3t})/9-2t/3$. For a fixed nonnegative vector $(\tau_i)$ and $t_i=s\tau_i$, put $T_1=\sum_i\tau_i$, $\bar\tau=T_1/m$, and $B_2=\sum_i(\tau_i-\bar\tau)^2$. As $s\downarrow0$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
D&=\Gamma-sT_1/m-s^2(d-1)B_2/(2m\Gamma)+O(s^3),\\
\lambda_i^*&=1/m+s(\bar\tau-\tau_i)/(m\Gamma)+O(s^2),\\
D/(1-sT_1)&=\Gamma+s(\Gamma-1/m)T_1
+s^2\left((\Gamma-1/m)T_1^2-(d-1)B_2/(2m\Gamma)\right)+O(s^3).
\end{aligned}
$$
The normalized linear coefficient is positive for $d\ge2$ and $T_1>0$. If all $t_i$ coincide, the maximizer is the centroid and $D=\Gamma-t/m$ exactly in the same regime.

pk-intake-exact-fiberwise-critical-cap-c.relation_to_goal: Exact local circuits on finite compatible families, with one whole-plane cover at each base and a bound depending on the number of bases.
pk-intake-exact-fiberwise-critical-cap-c.statement:
Fix $n,d\ge 1$, a finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb R^n$, and nonempty compact convex sets $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ for $z\in P$. Write $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$, $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_z})$, and $M=\mu(S)$. Let $h_\mu(z,x)$ be the infimum of $\mu(H)$ over closed ambient halfspaces $H$ containing $(z,x)$.

The family is compatible if the fiber of $C=\operatorname{conv}(S)$ at every $z\in P$ is exactly $K_z$. Equivalently, whenever a convex combination of bases in $P$ equals a base $z\in P$, the same Minkowski combination of the corresponding fibers lies in $K_z$. For a lattice application require $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$, so $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$.

Assume compatibility and $M>0$. Put $q_z=\max_{x\in K_z}h_\mu(z,x)$ and $Q=\max_{z\in P}q_z$. At any maximizing mark $x_z$ of a positive-volume fiber $K_z$, the active unit continuous normals
$$
U_z=\{u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}:c_z(u,u\cdot x_z)=q_z\}
$$
have zero in their convex hull, where $c_z(u,t)=\inf_a\mu\{(w,y):a\cdot(w-z)+u\cdot y\ge t\}$. There are $2\le k\le d+1$ actual nonvertical closed caps of mass exactly $q_z$ through $(z,x_z)$ whose unit continuous normals form a minimal positive dependence. The caps cover the whole plane $\{z\}\times\mathbb R^d$. At a null site two actual nonvertical zero-mass caps cover its whole plane. In particular at most $|P|(d+1)$ such caps cover $P\times\mathbb R^d$, each of mass at most $Q$. Caps selected at a site with $q_z<Q$ have strict slack at the common budget $Q$.

pk-intake-exact-fixed-fan-reverse-suppor.relation_to_goal: The test concerns reversal of a prescribed compatible family at fixed sampled bases.
pk-intake-exact-fixed-fan-reverse-suppor.statement:
Let $K_z,D_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be two compatible families of nonempty polytopes on a finite lattice-complete base, with $D_z\subseteq K_z$. Let $h,d$ be their actual support arrays on any common complete simplicial refinement of their normal fans, and let $A$ be the finite support and compatibility matrix from the fixed-fan lemma. The reverse array $(1+s)h-sd$ is feasible for a positive interval starting at $s=0$ if and only if $A_ad=0$ for every row $a$ active at $h$, equivalently if $d$ belongs to the minimal face containing $h$. Its exact feasible set for $s\ge0$ is $[0,s_*]$ if $s_*<\infty$, and $[0,\infty)$ otherwise, where
$$
s_*=\min_{a:A_ad>A_ah}\frac{A_ah}{A_ad-A_ah},
$$
with an empty minimum equal to $+\infty$. Each realized reverse fiber contains $K_z$.

Equivalently, the positive-step criterion is that $h_{D_z}$ is linear on every normal cone of $K_z$ for each $z$, and that each tight anchored support inequality of $h$ is tight for $d$ in the same direction with the same weights.

pk-intake-exact-fixed-mass-interval-sour.relation_to_goal: An exact one-dimensional calculation at the weighted centroid for each fixed input mass and multiplicity, including the fixed-dimension obstruction scale.
pk-intake-exact-fixed-mass-interval-sour.statement:
Let $B$ be a positive-length interval, $k\ge1$ an integer, $0\le\eta\le\mathbf1_B\,dx$, and $\eta(B)=\alpha|B|$ with $\alpha\in[0,1]$. Let $g$ be the centroid of $\mathbf1_B\,dx+k\eta$. Denote by $\Psi_k(\alpha)$ the infimum of $(|B\cap H|+\eta(H))/|B|$ over all such $B,\eta$ and all closed line halfspaces $H\ni g$. Then $\Psi_1(\alpha)=(1+\alpha^2)/2$. For $k\ge2$ set $L_k=(\sqrt{(k+1)/3}-1)/k$ and $U_k=(\sqrt{k(k+1)}-1)/k$. Then
$$
\Psi_k(\alpha)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \alpha+\frac{1+k\alpha^2}{2(1+k\alpha)},&0\le\alpha\le L_k,\\
\displaystyle \frac{2\sqrt{(1+k\alpha)^2+k+1}-3-k\alpha}{k},&L_k\le\alpha\le U_k,\\
\displaystyle \frac{k\alpha^2-(k-1)\alpha+k}{k+1},&U_k\le\alpha\le1.
\end{cases}
$$
The branches agree at the junctions and indicator bands attain the values. The endpoint values are $\Psi_k(0)=1/2$ and $\Psi_k(1)=1$. The minimum over $\alpha$ is $1/2$ uniquely at $\alpha=0$ for $k=1$, and $(\sqrt{3(k+1)}-2)/k$ uniquely at $\alpha=L_k$ for $k\ge2$. For $k\ge2$ an upper-end band of relative mass $L_k$ attains this minimum.

pk-intake-exact-local-hull-additions.relation_to_goal: Ordinary one-body geometry under pointwise support assumptions, including continuous dimension one.
pk-intake-exact-local-hull-additions.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, be a compact convex body with nonempty interior. Let $v\in\partial K$ have a unique outward unit supporting normal $u$, with $K\cap\{x:u\cdot x=h_K(u)\}=\{v\}$. Fix $h$ with $u\cdot h>0$. Then $K(t)=\operatorname{conv}(K\cup\{v+th\})$ has added volume $\Delta(t)=|K(t)|-|K|>0$ for $t>0$. The function $\Delta$ is continuous and strictly increasing, with $\Delta(0)=0$, and $\sup_{x\in K(t)\setminus K}\lVert x-v\rVert\to0$ as $t\downarrow0$. In particular each sufficiently small prescribed positive added volume has a unique small positive parameter.

For a finite list of distinct points $v_i$ with these hypotheses and corresponding directions $h_i$, write $a_i=v_i+t_i h_i$. For all sufficiently small positive $t_i$ one has the exact disjoint union
$$
\operatorname{conv}(K\cup\{a_i:i\})\setminus K
=\bigsqcup_i\bigl(\operatorname{conv}(K\cup\{a_i\})\setminus K\bigr).
$$

pk-intake-exact-local-inverse-arm-curvat.relation_to_goal: Local exact preservation of three continuous weighted arm integrals and the join conditions. The terminal value can increase at the completed top.
pk-intake-exact-local-inverse-arm-curvat.statement:
Let $I=[a,b]$, $a<b$, and let $w$ be continuous and nonnegative on $I$ and positive on its interior. Let $A$ be continuous, nonnegative, nonincreasing and concave on $I$, with finite $s_L=A'_+(a)$. There is a continuous nonnegative nonincreasing concave piecewise affine replacement $\widehat A$ preserving $A(a)$ and the three records
$$
\int_I wA,\qquad \int_I vwA,\qquad \int_I wA^2 ,
$$
with $\widehat A'_+(a)\le s_L$. If the cell is internal and $s_R=A'_-(b)$ is finite, one can preserve $A(b)$ and obtain $\widehat A'_-(b)\ge s_R$ using at most eight atoms in the closed-cell curvature representation, including any join atoms at the endpoints. On a terminal cell, with no restriction on the terminal slope, one can use at most seven atoms in the weighted curvature representation and require $\widehat A(b)\ge A(b)$. An atom at the terminal right endpoint represents slack in its completed value.

pk-intake-exact-mixed-helly-closed-cap-c.relation_to_goal: Conditional exact closed cover for arbitrary finite real bases, with a mixed Helly cardinality on the actual lattice fiber union.
pk-intake-exact-mixed-helly-closed-cap-c.statement:
Fix $n,d\ge 1$, a finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb R^n$, and nonempty compact convex sets $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ for $z\in P$. Write $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$, $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_z})$, and $M=\mu(S)$. Let $h_\mu(z,x)$ be the infimum of $\mu(H)$ over closed ambient halfspaces $H$ containing $(z,x)$. Assume $M>0$ and put $Q=\max_{(z,x)\in S}h_\mu(z,x)$. Suppose for every $\varepsilon>0$ the interiors of at most $N$ nonvertical closed ambient halfspaces cover $S$, each of mass less than $Q+\varepsilon M$. Then $S$ is covered by at most $N$ nonvertical closed ambient halfspaces of mass at most $Q$, with at least one of mass $Q$.

If $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$ for a compact convex set $C\subset\mathbb R^{n+d}$, the hypothesis holds with $N=2^n(d+1)$. The conclusion at this cardinality covers $S$.

pk-intake-exact-planar-corner-loss-commo.relation_to_goal: The exact loss and common-center reserve concern ordinary planar halfspace incidence with arbitrary weights. The numerical corollary uses the special actual mixed chord weights.
pk-intake-exact-planar-corner-loss-commo.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a convex body, let $H_i=\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge b_i\}$ for $1\le i\le3$ cover $A$, and assume the normals are pairwise linearly independent and all cuts are proper. Write $a=|A|$, $U_i=|A\cap H_i|$, $a_i=\mathcal H^1(A\cap\{v_i\cdot x=b_i\})/\lVert v_i\rVert$, and $L_i(p)=2U_i+(b_i-v_i\cdot p)a_i$. For arbitrary positive weights $\lambda_i$ put $\Lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i$, $\tau_2=\Lambda-\max_i\lambda_i$, and $c_i=(\tau_2-\lambda_i)_+$. The region $R_i=A\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{v_j\cdot x<b_j\}$ is the region captured only by $H_i$. For each $i$ with $r_i=|R_i|>0$, set $C_i=\overline{R_i}$ and, for $j\ne i$, let $\ell$ be the third index and put
$$
\tau_{ij}=\frac{\mathcal H^1(A\cap\{v_j\cdot x=b_j,\ v_\ell\cdot x\le b_\ell\})}{\lVert v_j\rVert}.
$$
Then $C_i=A\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{v_j\cdot x\le b_j\}$. For every $p\in A$ and $A_t=p+(1-t)(A-p)$ the exact right loss is
$$
D_i(p)=\lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{|R_i\setminus A_t|}{t}
=2r_i-\sum_{j\ne i}(b_j-v_j\cdot p)\tau_{ij}\ge0.
$$
It satisfies $D_i(p)\le2r_i$ on $C_i$ and its minimum there is attained and equals
$$
2r_i-\sum_{j\ne i}b_j\tau_{ij}
-h_{C_i}\Bigl(-\sum_{j\ne i}\tau_{ij}v_j\Bigr),
$$
where $h_C$ is the support function of $C$.

With null corners omitted, for every $p\in A$,
$$
\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)\ge 2a\tau_2-\sum_i c_iD_i(p).
$$
The right side attains its maximum at one common $p\in A$, with value
$$
2a\tau_2-2\sum_i c_ir_i+\sum_i c_i\sum_{j\ne i}b_j\tau_{ij}
+h_A\Bigl(-\sum_i c_i\sum_{j\ne i}\tau_{ij}v_j\Bigr).
$$
If just one positive-area corner $R_j$ has $c_j>0$, every $p\in C_j$ satisfies $\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)\ge 2a\tau_2-2(\tau_2-\lambda_j)r_j$. If all deficient corners are null, $\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)\ge2a\tau_2$ for every $p\in A$.

In the actual mixed setting of the critical chord-weight theorem, these one-corner and all-deficient-null estimates imply a normalized loss of at least $(a-r_j)/2$ and $a/2$, respectively, after dividing by $\Lambda$. In particular $r_j\le a/9$ gives a normalized loss of at least $4a/9$ at every $p\in C_j$.

pk-intake-exact-planar-six-piece-section.relation_to_goal: Exact replacement of two ordinary planar symmetric section bodies for one fixed axial tilt, preserving actual moments. The claim is a reduction of the functional.
pk-intake-exact-planar-six-piece-section.statement:
Let $f,g$ be nonnegative concave upper semicontinuous functions on respective compact intervals $I,J$ of positive lengths, each with integral one and first moment zero. Form the symmetric planar section bodies $E_f=\{(s,y):s\in I,\ |y|\le f(s)/2\}$ and $E_g$ analogously. Fix $\alpha\in\mathbb R$ and put
$$
J_\alpha(f,g)
=\left|\left(\tfrac12(E_f+E_g)\right)\cap\{s\ge0\}\right|
 +\int_\alpha^\infty f(s)\,ds+\int_{-\alpha}^\infty g(s)\,ds,
$$
where bars denote ordinary planar area, and extend each profile by zero only for the tail integrals.

If the profiles are piecewise affine on prescribed finite knots including the support endpoints and the feasible height set is nonempty, then $J_\alpha$ attains a minimum over those heights. A minimizer can be chosen with at most $2+z\le6$ affine pieces in each profile, where $z$ is its total number of zero endpoint heights. If all four endpoint heights are prescribed, a minimizer can be chosen with at most six pieces in each profile whenever this prescribed problem is feasible.

For arbitrary profiles as above, there exist profiles with the same respective support intervals, masses and first moments, each with at most six nonvertical affine graph pieces, whose $J_\alpha$ is no larger. The resulting closed profile endpoint values may differ from those of the input.

pk-intake-exact-polytopal-projective-two.relation_to_goal: A sufficient descent test and necessary local orbit condition with fixed continuous cap normals. It supplies no descent jet from a numerical depth failure alone.
pk-intake-exact-polytopal-projective-two.statement:
Let $P$ be a finite real base and $K_p$ positive compatible $d$-polytopes. Write $V_p=|K_p|$, $M=\sum_pV_p$, and $\beta$ for their maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth. Translate the origin into the relative interior of the base hull. At each deepest base $p_i$ take a positive critical circuit of closed caps
$$
a_{ij}\cdot p+u_{ij}\cdot X\ge b_{ij},\qquad
\|u_{ij}\|=1,\qquad b_{ij}=a_{ij}\cdot p_i+u_{ij}\cdot x_i
$$
of old mass $\beta M$, with weights $\rho_{ij}>0$ summing to one and $\sum_j\rho_{ij}u_{ij}=0$. Use fixed strictly cheaper whole-plane covers at the other bases. For affine $A,B$ set $L_t=1+tA+t^2B/2$. In each critical cap vary the base covector and threshold by
$$
a_{ij}(t)=a_{ij}+tc_{ij}+t^2e_{ij}/2,\qquad
b_{ij}(t)=b_{ij}+t(c_{ij}\cdot p_i+s_{ij})+t^2(e_{ij}\cdot p_i+r_{ij})/2 .
$$
Put $q_{ijp}=s_{ij}-c_{ij}\cdot(p-p_i)$ and $R_{ijp}=r_{ij}-e_{ij}\cdot(p-p_i)$. Let $F^0_{ijp}$ denote the old cap volume in $K_p$ and $D_{ijp},E_{ijp}$ its one-sided parallel cap coefficient functions at the old threshold. Define
$$
\begin{aligned}
b_{ij,1}&=\sum_p\left[D_{ijp}(q_{ijp})-dA(p)(F^0_{ijp}-\beta V_p)\right],\\
b_{ij,2}&=\sum_p\left[E_{ijp}(q_{ijp},R_{ijp})-2dA(p)D_{ijp}(q_{ijp})+
(d(d+1)A(p)^2-dB(p))(F^0_{ijp}-\beta V_p)\right].
\end{aligned}
$$
Suppose $\sum_j\rho_{ij}s_{ij}\le0$ for every group, with $\sum_j\rho_{ij}r_{ij}\le0$ whenever the first sum is zero. Suppose also $b_{ij,1}\le0$ for every critical cap, with $b_{ij,2}<0$ whenever $b_{ij,1}=0$. Then for every sufficiently small positive $t$, the actual projective image under $(p,X)\mapsto(p/L_t(p),X/L_t(p))$ has maximum normalized depth strictly less than $\beta$. At a local positive affine projective minimum these jets are therefore infeasible for every choice of old circuits. For each fixed first jet the second-order feasibility is a finite union of linear systems with weak and strict inequalities, branched on the signs of $R_{ijp}$ where $q_{ijp}=0$.

pk-intake-exact-retained-fiber-lattice-r.relation_to_goal: The exact fiber census and depth transfer are unconditional. A numerical sharp depth bound for a positive remaining integer rank is a stated hypothesis.
pk-intake-exact-retained-fiber-lattice-r.statement:
Let $Q\subset\mathbb R^r\times\mathbb R^s$ be compact and convex, with $s\ge1$, and let $a+L$ be a full-rank lattice coset in $\mathbb R^r$. Let $F\subseteq\mathbb R^r$ be an affine subspace. Take $P$ to consist of either all the lattice bases in $F$ with nonempty $Q$-fibers or all the lattice bases in $F$ with positive $s$-volume $Q$-fibers. Assume the sum $T_P$ of the retained fiber volumes is positive. Put $A=\operatorname{aff}P$, $t=\dim A$, and
$$
Q_P=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{p\in P}(\{p\}\times Q_p).
$$
For every $p\in(a+L)\cap A$ the fiber $(Q_P)_p$ equals $Q_p$ if $p\in P$ and is empty otherwise. The hull is a full-dimensional compact convex body in $A\times\mathbb R^s$. For any $p_0\in P$, the lattice there is $p_0+(L\cap(A-p_0))$, whose difference lattice is saturated in $L$ and has rank $t$. A lattice basis gives an affine identification with $\mathbb R^t\times\mathbb R^s$ and sample lattice $\mathbb Z^t\times\mathbb R^s$, preserving every fiber volume and the raw halfspace depth within the retained source. For every retained candidate, its raw depth in the original source is at least its retained raw depth. The same comparison holds if $Q$ is a fixed coarse slice of a larger original source.

For $t>0$, assume the sharp mixed-integer bound in dimensions $(t,s)$, namely that every full-dimensional compact convex body of positive sampled mass in those dimensions has a sampled point of normalized depth at least $2^{-t}\Gamma_s$, where $\Gamma_s=(s/(s+1))^s$. Then some retained point has raw depth at least $2^{-t}\Gamma_s T_P$ in the original source. At $t=0$ the same conclusion holds unconditionally.

pk-intake-exact-same-separator-buffer-fo.relation_to_goal: The force is the same-coefficient volume force. The result controls its scale and volume entropy.
pk-intake-exact-same-separator-buffer-fo.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $N=d+1$, and use original sampled mixed $d$-volume $dm$ of mass $M>0$ on a compact set of positive compatible fibers. Let $L$ be positive continuous and log-normalized by $\int\log L\,dm/M=0$. At finitely many own-interior marks $Y_a=(p_a,y_a)$ set $L_a=L(Y_a)$, $E_a=E_{K_{p_a}}(y_a)$, and for $\varepsilon>0$ take $\delta_a=\varepsilon(L_aE_a/M)^{1/N}$. Given positive coefficients $\kappa_a$, put $K=\sum_a\kappa_a$, $\Delta=\sum_a\kappa_a\delta_a$, $w_a=\kappa_a/K$ and $\sigma_a=\kappa_a\delta_a/\Delta$. Assume the same-coefficient probability rows $\rho_a$ satisfy $\int L\,d\rho_a=L_a$ and $\sum_a(\sigma_a/L_a)\rho_a=dm/(ML)$. Define $\bar\rho_a=(L/L_a)\rho_a$ and $K_V=\sum_a\sigma_a D(\bar\rho_a\|\rho_a)$. Then
$$
I:=\log(\varepsilon K/\Delta)=D(\sigma\|w)+\frac{K_V+\sum_a\sigma_a\log(M/E_a)}{N}\ge0.
$$
In particular $0<\Delta\le\varepsilon K$, $\Delta I\le\varepsilon K/e$, $\Delta D(\sigma\|w)\le\varepsilon K/e$, and $\Delta K_V\le N\varepsilon K/e$.

For a joint separator with effective coareas bounded above by $S_{\max}$, these upper bounds hold with $K$ replaced by $S_{\max}$ if its own coefficients supply the stated probability rows and $\Delta>0$. If the separator has total proper weight one and its coareas are also at least $S_{\min}>0$, then $K\ge S_{\min}$.

pk-intake-exact-single-unique-corner-com.relation_to_goal: Ordinary planar data preservation for a body already between the six-ray hull and the triangle and containing two triangle vertices.
pk-intake-exact-single-unique-corner-com.statement: Let $T$ be a nondegenerate planar triangle with an interior mark and three balanced spanning cap normals whose cuts through that mark strictly capture distinct vertices and strictly exclude the other two. Let $C$ be the hull of the six cut-line endpoints. If $C\subseteq K\subseteq T$ is a convex body containing two vertices of $T$, let $U$ be the corner triangle at the third vertex cut off by the line through its two neighboring cut-line endpoints. Set $E=|T|-|K|$ and $L=|U|$. Then $0\le E\le L$. Removing the corner homothetic to $U$ about that vertex with ratio $\sqrt{E/L}$ gives a quadrilateral if $E>0$ and $T$ if $E=0$. It has exactly the same six ray endpoints, full cutting chords, six sector areas, three cap areas, and normalized Lorentz rows as $K$.

pk-intake-exact-three-cut-triangle-clipp.relation_to_goal: Exact ordinary area for one fixed triangle and mark under three simultaneous cuts with strict distinct-vertex incidence.
pk-intake-exact-three-cut-triangle-clipp.statement:
Let $K$ be a nondegenerate triangle inside an outer triangle with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i$ satisfying $\min_K\lambda_i=0$. Let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$, $u_i=\lambda_i(y)$, and suppose each cap $C_i=K\cap\{\lambda_i\ge u_i\}$ strictly captures vertex $P_i$ and strictly excludes the other two, with the $P_i$ distinct. Put $S_{ij}=\lambda_i(P_j)$, $R=S^{-1}$, $a=Ru$, $q_i=|C_i|/|K|$, and $p_i=|C_j\cap C_l|/|K|$ for $\{i,j,l\}=\{1,2,3\}$. Set $\alpha_i=2u_i/S_{ii}$ and $\beta_i=2-2a_i/R_{ii}$. Then $R_{ii}>0$ and $0<\alpha_i,\beta_i<2$. For $0\le\rho\le2$ let $E_\rho=\{\xi\ge0:\sum_i\xi_i=\rho,\ S\xi\le2u\}$. Define its area by the vertex map $\xi\mapsto\sum_i\xi_iP_i$, so the full $\rho$-simplex has area $\rho^2|K|$. Then
$$
\frac{|E_\rho|}{|K|}
=\rho^2-4\sum_i q_i\left(\frac{(\rho-\alpha_i)_+}{2-\alpha_i}\right)^2
+4\sum_i p_i\left(\frac{(\rho-\beta_i)_+}{2-\beta_i}\right)^2.
$$
For fixed $K,y$ its maximum over $\rho\in[0,2]$ is among the endpoints, breakpoints, and interior stationary points of nonconstant quadratic pieces.

pk-intake-exclusive-lattice-facet-witnes.relation_to_goal: The result is about chosen relative-interior facet witnesses, including the case of exclusion on a convex projected domain.
pk-intake-exclusive-lattice-facet-witnes.statement: Let $L\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge1$, be a full-dimensional polyhedron with at least one irredundant facet, and let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a convex set. Suppose $\operatorname{int}L\cap A\cap\mathbb Z^n=\varnothing$ and each facet $F_i$ has a chosen witness $p_i\in\operatorname{relint}(F_i)\cap A\cap\mathbb Z^n$. Then each $p_i$ is a vertex of $W=\operatorname{conv}\{p_i\}$, and $W\cap\mathbb Z^n=\{p_i\}$. The witnesses have distinct coordinate parities, so there are at most $2^n$ of them, and equality gives one in every class. This applies to a lattice-free $L$ by taking $A=\mathbb R^n$, and requires no boundedness of $L$.

pk-intake-explicit-covering-radius-round.relation_to_goal: A sufficient finite-mesh regime for the full-dimensional sharp mixed depth bound, with an actual prescribed point and a positive full-fiber mass. The nonempty sampled interval case $(n,d)=(1,0)$ follows directly by a median.
pk-intake-explicit-covering-radius-round.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, $d\ge0$, $(n,d)\ne(1,0)$, $N=n+d$, and $R=N(N+2)$. Let $F(z,x)=(Az+t,Bz+Tx+c)$ be an invertible block affine normalization of a compact convex body $C$ with $B_2^N\subseteq K=F(C)\subseteq R B_2^N$. Let $\delta$ be the Euclidean covering radius of $A\mathbb Z^n$. Set $\Gamma_0=1$, $\Gamma_j=(j/(j+1))^j$ for $j\ge1$, $\kappa_j=|B_2^j|_j$ with $\kappa_0=1$, $\alpha=2^{-n}\Gamma_d$, $S_N=\kappa_{N-1}R^{N-1}$, and $E=2n(2R+2)^{N-1}$. Put
$$
\delta_*=\min\left\{\frac1{2R^N},
\frac{(\Gamma_N-\alpha)\kappa_N}{S_N+(1+\alpha)E}\right\}.
$$
If $\delta\le\delta_*$, let $g=(g_z,g_x)$ be the ordinary volume centroid of $K$, and choose any nearest $\lambda\in A\mathbb Z^n+t$ to $g_z$. Then $F^{-1}(\lambda,g_x)$ is an interior sampled point, the original sampled total is positive, and the point has normalized closed-halfspace depth at least $\alpha$. The following more restrictive condition also suffices:
$$
\delta\le\min\left\{\frac1{2R^N},
\frac{(\Gamma_N-\alpha)(2/\sqrt N)^N}{(1+3n)(2R+2)^{N-1}}\right\}.
$$
When $n=1,d\ge1$, if $W$ is the projection length of $C$ in its original integer coordinate, $W\ge R/\delta_*$ suffices for this prescribed point. For $n=d=1$, the resulting sufficient length is $1024$.

pk-intake-explicit-diagonal-small-slope-.relation_to_goal: A fixed-dimension explicit slope range of strictly negative scalar diagonal-envelope deficit, uniform over the allowed tilt interval.
pk-intake-explicit-diagonal-small-slope-.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$ and put $t=1/(d+1)$ and $\Gamma=(dt)^d$. For $a>0$, $0\le\beta\le at$ and $h\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$, set $r_h=(1-ah)_+$, $q_h=t-\beta h$ and $p_h=t+\beta(h+1)$, where $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$. The diagonal-envelope deficit is
$$
D(a,\beta)=\Gamma\sum_{h\ge0}r_h^d
-d^d\sum_{\substack{h\ge0\\r_h>0}}
  \left[q_h^{d-1}(r_h-dq_h)_++p_h^{d-1}(r_h-dp_h)_+\right].
$$
Both sums have only finitely many nonzero terms. Whenever $r_h>0$, one has $q_h\ge tr_h>0$ and $p_h\ge t>0$.

With the constants $C_d$ and $K_d$ of the uniform deficit expansion, define
$$
\varepsilon_d=\min\left\{\frac1{2d},\frac1{4[C_d+(d+1)K_d^2]}\right\}.
$$
For every $0<a\le1/(2d)$ and $0\le\beta\le at$,
$$
\frac{D(a,\beta)}{\Gamma}\le -\frac12+[C_d+(d+1)K_d^2]a.
$$
In particular $D(a,\beta)\le-\Gamma/4$ for all $0<a\le\varepsilon_d$ and $0\le\beta\le at$.

u_i=\mathbb E(Y_i\mid C)$. For every index $j$,
$$
\prod_{i
e j}
u_i\ge P.
$$
When $c_j>0$, equality holds exactly when all nonzero $c_i$ with $i
e j$ have the same sign, including the case in which all are zero. In a uniform $d$-simplex, a halfspace cap of positive volume fraction $P$ with centroid barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i$ consequently satisfies $(d+1)^d\prod_{i

pk-intake-exponential-hinge-positive-rat.relation_to_goal: Conditional on the exact common separator and jointly retained compact log measures. Positive-rate endpoints are included; the actual directional kernel and positive capture are separate.
pk-intake-exponential-hinge-positive-rat.statement:
Let $\eta_j$ be finite positive measures on a common compact normal-position space $\mathcal N\times C$ with $C$ contained in a Euclidean physical space. Let $L_j$ be a finite minimum of ambient affine functions, positive on the physical support of $\eta_j$, and let $0\le W_j\le1$. Take $\lambda_j>0$ with $\lambda_j\to0$, $\beta_j\to\beta$, and set $s_j=(-\log L_j)_+$, $r_j=\lambda_j s_j$, $\Xi_j=W_j-\beta_j+r_j+R_j$, with $|R_j|\le C_0\lambda_j$. Suppose
$$
\int\Xi_j\Phi\,d\eta_j\le0
$$
for every nonnegative continuous field $\Phi(n,w)$ globally finite and convex in the physical coordinate for each normal. The measures $B_j=s_j\eta_j\,\delta_{r_j}$ and $A_j=W_jB_j$ are assumed to have bounded masses, a common compact rate range, and joint weak limits with positive-rate parts $\widehat b,\widehat a$ supported in rates at most $\beta$. For every $R>0$, nonnegative continuous normal weight $\psi$, and globally finite nonnegative convex physical $f$, for either $T=\{r>R\}$ or $T=\{r\ge R\}$ one has
$$
\int_T\psi f/r\,d\widehat a+\int_T\psi f\,d\widehat b
\ \le\ \beta\int_T\psi f/r\,d\widehat b.
$$
If $\beta>0$, then $\widehat a(\{r=\beta\})=0$.

Each of these inequalities, and any inequality of the same type valid for all such $f$ with finite physical measures and bounded weights on its rate region, remains true with all measures restricted to the whole exposed zero face of an affine function nonnegative on their common compact convex physical support. This restriction can be repeated on successive exposed zero faces. It also applies to finite moment tests without reciprocal factors whenever their measures are finite after weighting.

pk-intake-exterior-contact-dimension-dro.relation_to_goal: Finite closed covers with a common exterior or boundary contact for one continuous body. The mixed statement tests one actual fiber at a time.
pk-intake-exterior-contact-dimension-dro.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body, and let $y\notin\operatorname{int}K$. Suppose finitely many proper closed halfspaces $H_i$ cover $\mathbb R^d$ and all their boundary hyperplanes contain $y$. Then
$$
\max_i |K\cap H_i|\ge\gamma_{d-1}|K|,
\qquad \gamma_j=\left(\frac{j}{j+1}\right)^j\ (j\ge1),\quad \gamma_0=1.
$$
For each $d$ the constant is attained both for some $y\notin K$ and for some $y\in\partial K$. For $d\ge2$ the constant also remains the infimum for each contact type when the normals span $\mathbb R^d$, equivalently when $y$ is the unique common point of their boundaries.

pk-intake-exterior-origin-radial-gauge.relation_to_goal: Convexity of a radial gauge for a compactly supported inverse-power density, including exterior origins.
pk-intake-exterior-origin-radial-gauge.statement:
Let $p\ge1$, and let $f$ be a bounded nonnegative upper-semicontinuous function of compact support on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space. Assume $\{f>0\}$ has nonempty interior and the extended function $f^{-1/(p+1)}$, with value $+\infty$ where $f=0$, is convex. For $x\ne0$ put $I_p(x)=\int_0^\infty t^{p-1}f(tx)\,dt$. Then
$$
U_p=\{0\}\cup\{x\ne0:I_p(x)\ge1\}
$$
is compact and convex. Its gauge is $I_p(x)^{-1/p}$ for $x\ne0$, interpreted as $+\infty$ if $I_p(x)=0$, and is zero at the origin. If $f$ is positive on a neighborhood of the origin, $U_p$ is a convex body with the origin in its interior.

Let $v_j=S_ju_j\in\mathbb R^d$, $u_j
e0$ and $S_j>0$, be a finite list for which the polytope of probabilities $
u$ with $\sum_j
u_jv_j=0$ is nonempty. An extreme such probability has at most $d+1$ positive entries, and on its positive support the $v_j$ form a minimal positive linear circuit. Rescaling to $u_j$ preserves the circuit. At rank one there are two opposite continuous directions, with one response weight at least $1/2\ge\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. At rank at least two no directions on the support repeat or are antipodal. Consequently if these are continuous normals of ambient caps, at most one cap of that menu can support a given positive-area facet of a sampled fiber. pk-intake-few-ordinary-caps-profile-equa.relation_to_goal: Extends the known ordinary D+1-cap equality criterion to the lower-rank case of fewer caps.
pk-intake-few-ordinary-caps-profile-equa.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^D$ be a convex body of volume $V$ covered by $m$ proper closed halfspaces $H_i$, where $3\le m\le D+1$. Put $r=m-1$, $A_i=|K\cap H_i|$, and $\gamma_r=(r/(r+1))^r$. For $\alpha>0$,
$$
\sum_i(A_i-\alpha)_++\frac{\alpha}{\gamma_r}=V
$$
holds exactly when the normals span a space of dimension $r$, the orthogonal pushforward of ordinary volume on $K$ to that span is a log-concave nonincreasing gauge profile of a centroid-centered $r$-simplex translated to a point $y$, and the projected halfspaces are its distinct canonical vertex halfspaces through $y$. In this case every $A_i=\alpha=\gamma_r V$. At $m=3$, taking $\alpha=\min_i A_i>0$ gives the same equality classification for the overlap bound with coefficient $3/4$.

pk-intake-fiberwise-constant-fractional-.relation_to_goal: The bound is for positive incidence constant almost everywhere within each positive intrinsic fiber. The constants may vary across fibers.
pk-intake-fiberwise-constant-fractional-.statement: Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex, $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\ne\varnothing$, and $q=\dim_H S\ge1$. Let $\mu=\mathcal H_q|_S$, $M=\mu(S)$, and $k$ be the number of coordinate parity classes occupied by the positive $\mathcal H_q$ fibers $C_z$. Suppose finitely many original closed ambient halfspaces $H_i$ have coefficients $\lambda_i>0$ such that $\sum_i\lambda_i\mathbf1_{H_i}(z,x)=b_z>0$ for $\mathcal H_q$-almost every $x\in C_z$ on each positive fiber, where $b_z$ is constant on that fiber. Then at most $2k$ original caps cover every positive fiber pointwise. In particular $\max_i\mu(H_i)\ge M/(2k)\ge\gamma_d M/2^n$, where $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. A finite partition up to $\mu$-null sets and overlaps consequently has at most $2k$ positive-mass original caps, allowing caps that contain entire positive fibers. The subcover size $2k$ and the mass bound $M/(2k)$ are both attained for $C=[0,1]^n\times K$ with any full-dimensional centrally symmetric $d$-body $K$ centered at zero.

pk-intake-fiberwise-projective-face-cone.statement: Let $F$ be a compact convex $(d-1)$-dimensional face in a continuous $d$-space, with apex $y$ at perpendicular distance $H>0$ below it in direction $-u$, where $u$ is the unit face normal. Under $v\mapsto v'=v/L$, the image face is in $N\cdot v'=H$ with $N=su+Ha_T$, and its tangential Jacobian is $\lVert N\rVert L^{-d}$. The measure $H L^{-d}\,d\mathcal H_{d-1}$ pushes forward to $(H/\lVert N\rVert)\,d\mathcal H_{d-1}$ there. For every measurable face patch its weighted mass is $d$ times the $d$-volume of the radial cone from the image apex to the image patch. For the full face this is $d$ times the volume of the bounded convex image pyramid.

pk-intake-fine-hyperplane-nonconcentrati.relation_to_goal: Sufficient antecedent for transformed-component recovery. The statement starts from fine hyperplane mass fractions and derives the positive coarse shapes, mesh and discarded fine mass conditions.
pk-intake-fine-hyperplane-nonconcentrati.statement:
Let $k\ge0$, $r\ge1$, $s\ge0$, $m=r+s$. Let $C_\ell\subset\mathbb R^k_z\times\mathbb R^r_u\times\mathbb R^s_x$ be compact convex sets whose nonempty coarse integer fibers have indices in a fixed finite $P\subset\mathbb Z^k$. Sample $u$ in a full-rank lattice coset $a_\ell+L_\ell$ of covolume $v_\ell$. At each coarse site $z$ let $\mu_{\ell,z}$ sum $v_\ell$ times the $s$-volume of its fine sections, using counting for $s=0$. Put $\mu_\ell=\sum_z\mu_{\ell,z}$ and $T_\ell=\mu_\ell(\mathrm{total})>0$. Assume that the largest fraction $\eta_\ell$ of $\mu_\ell$ on an affine hyperplane in the $u$ coordinates tends to zero.

Along any subsequence on which $\mu_{\ell,z}(\mathrm{total})/T_\ell\to\alpha_z$ at every $z$, let $E=\{z:\alpha_z>0\}$ and $M_{\ell,z}=|(C_\ell)_z|_m$. For each $z\in E$, the coarse fiber is eventually a full $m$-body,
$$
\frac{\mu_{\ell,z}(\mathrm{total})}{M_{\ell,z}}\to1,\qquad
\frac{M_{\ell,z}}{T_\ell}\to\alpha_z.
$$
The set $E$ is lattice-complete. For every integer combination point $j=\sum_i\lambda_i z_i$ with $z_i\in E$, $\lambda_i>0$ and $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$, it satisfies
$$
\alpha_j\ge\lambda_i^m\alpha_{z_i}>0\quad\text{for each }i,\qquad
\alpha_j^{1/m}\ge\sum_i\lambda_i\alpha_{z_i}^{1/m}.
$$
In particular $M_{\ell,E}=\sum_{z\in E}M_{\ell,z}\sim T_\ell$ and the fine mass off $E$ is $o(M_{\ell,E})$. Each retained fiber admits a uniformly round volume-one block normalization with transformed fine covering radius tending to zero. On each dependence component of $E$ one can choose a common block map of absolute determinant $1/M_{\ell,E}$ with transformed fine covering radius tending to zero and uniformly bounded diameters of all images in the component.

pk-intake-finite-active-base-normalized-.relation_to_goal: A sufficient first-order criterion for depth descent once a feasible motion and the active restricted-depth bounds have already been supplied.
pk-intake-finite-active-base-normalized-.statement:
For a one-sided family whose actual mixed candidate bases are drawn from one fixed finite set, suppose the total mass is $M(t)=M_0+t m+o(t)$, $M_0>0$, and the restricted raw maximum $Q_p(t)$ at each indexed base is defined and continuous at zero. Put $Q_0=\max_p Q_p(0)$, $D_0=Q_0/M_0$, and $I=\{p:Q_p(0)=Q_0\}$. If for each $p\in I$ one has $Q_p(t)\le Q_0+t a_p+o(t)$ as $t\downarrow0$, then for $D(t)=\max_p Q_p(t)/M(t)$,
$$
\limsup_{t\downarrow0}\frac{D(t)-D_0}{t}\le
\frac{\max_{p\in I}a_p-D_0m}{M_0}.
$$
In particular a strict negative numerator implies $D(t)<D_0$ for all sufficiently small positive $t$.

pk-intake-finite-affine-threshold-compac.relation_to_goal: A finite-real-base cap compactification for summed full d-dimensional fiber volume.
pk-intake-finite-affine-threshold-compac.statement: Fix $n,d\ge1$, finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb R^n$, and a ball $R B_d$ centered at zero with $R>0$. Let $H_j=\{(z,x):u_j\cdot x\ge t_j(z)\}$, where $\|u_j\|=1$ and $t_j$ is real affine. Some subsequence has $u_j\to u$ with $\|u\|=1$ and $t_j(z)\to t(z)\in[-\infty,\infty]$ for every $z\in P$. On $P\times R B_d$, the limiting traces $\{x:u\cdot x\ge t(z)\}$ at finite thresholds, the full traces at $t(z)=-\infty$ and the empty traces at $t(z)=+\infty$ are realized by one actual closed halfspace with unit continuous normal $u$ and a finite affine threshold. For summed $d$-volume $\mu$ on any fixed family of measurable fibers inside that ball, $\mu(H_j)$ along the subsequence tends to the mass of that halfspace. Every fixed point of $P\times R B_d$ contained in infinitely many caps of the subsequence belongs to the realizing halfspace.

pk-intake-finite-base-ball-strictificati.relation_to_goal: Uniform support gaps for general finite Euclidean bases, with a mass-preserving cap-flat specialization to centrally symmetric actual lattice fibers.
pk-intake-finite-base-ball-strictificati.statement:
For finite distinct Euclidean bases P with positive compact convex K_z satisfying all anchored Minkowski inclusions, set K_z(ε)=K_z+ε(R−|z|²)B_d, R>max|z|² and ε≥0. For each unit u and representation z=∑_w p_ww with p_z=0, its support gap grows exactly by ε∑_w p_w|w−z|²≥ε min_{w≠z}|w−z|² whenever such a representation exists. The family remains compatible. A common continuous-coordinate contraction with matching halfspaces multiplies each finite cap mass by the same factor s^d<1 and preserves its original cover property at that stage. A subsequent sufficiently small ball addition retains strict decreases in every originally positive cap budget and yields strict anchored compatibility.

Let P be a finite lattice-complete centrally symmetric spanning subset of ℤ^n, n≥1, and let the full-dimensional compact convex d-fibers K_z be compatible with K_{−z}=−K_z. For R>max_{z∈P}|z|² and ε>0 replace K_z by K_z+ε(R−|z|²)B_d, then scale all fibers by α_ε=(M/Σ_z|K_z+ε(R−|z|²)B_d|)^(1/d). The new families tend to the original, preserve central symmetry and total mass M and assign M/2 to every nonvertical origin-through cap. Every excluded-self anchored inclusion has ball slack at least α_ε ε min_{z≠w}|z−w|², and independent fiber Hausdorff changes smaller than one quarter of this slack still give actual compatible fibers on P.

pk-intake-finite-base-canonical-lift-and.relation_to_goal: Finite sampled bases. No integer arithmetic or quantitative lower bound on mixed depth is needed for the lift or the restriction.
pk-intake-finite-base-canonical-lift-and.statement:
For a nonempty finite set $P$ in a real affine space, call $T\subseteq P$ closed if $T=P\cap\operatorname{conv}(T)$. An anchored representation of $q\in P$ is $q=\sum_{p\in P}\lambda_pp$ with $\lambda_p\ge0$ and $\sum_p\lambda_p=1$. Let $L(P)\subseteq\mathbb R^P$ be the space of scalar functions preserving every such equality. For a basis $1,g_1,\ldots,g_{\ell-1}$ of $L(P)$, the map $\Phi_P(p)=(g_1(p),\ldots,g_{\ell-1}(p))$ is injective, with an affine projection back to $P$. Its image has affine dimension $\ell-1$, preserves exactly the anchored representations and the closed traces, and all representation-preserving functions on $\Phi_P(P)$ are affine restrictions. In particular its relative Helly number equals $h(P)$, the least number of ambient convex sets needed to certify an empty common trace on $P$ from any finite such system.

Fix $d\ge1$. A family of nonempty compact convex sets $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$ is compatible if $\sum_p\lambda_p K_p\subseteq K_q$ for every anchored representation of $q$. This is equivalent to being the exact sections of the convex hull of their placed fibers at all sites of $P$. For families of positive $d$-volume let $D_P(K)$ be the maximum, over placed fiber points, of the infimum of normalized mass of containing closed halfspaces, using the sum of fiber $d$-volumes. Let $M_T=\sum_{p\in T}|K_p|_d$ for nonempty $T\subseteq P$. Then, with the same retained fibers,
$$
D_P(K)\ \ge\ \frac{M_T}{M_P}\,D_T(K|_T)
\ \ge\ \frac{M_T}{M_P}\,D_{\Phi_T(T)}(K|_T).
$$
Here $T$ has its inherited placement and the last depth uses its own canonical lift. The closed-minor operation followed by canonical lifting, iterated on an initial $P$, produces only lifts of its nonempty closed subsets up to affine equivalence. For a closed $T$, $h(T)\le h(P)$.
