pk-intake-finite-base-critical-face-frac.relation_to_goal: The finite-base alternative has no midpoint label assumption. The mixed consequence uses an affine centroid graph and a relative Helly bound. The fractional partition is a necessary equality condition under these hypotheses.
pk-intake-finite-base-critical-face-frac.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in a Euclidean space, with weights $w_z>0$ of total $M$, and write $B=\operatorname{conv}P$. Fix an integer $h\ge1$ and set $\alpha=M/h$. Let $\mathcal F$ be the proper faces of $B$ of weight $w(F)=\sum_{z\in P\cap F}w_z=\alpha$. Exactly one of the following holds.

1. Some $v\in\mathbb R^P$ has $\sum_{z\in P}v_z=0$ and $\sum_{z\in P\cap F}v_z<0$ for every $F\in\mathcal F$. This holds vacuously for an empty face list.
2. There are numbers $\theta_F\ge0$ for $F\in\mathcal F$ such that $\sum_{F\in\mathcal F}\theta_F\mathbf1_{P\cap F}=\mathbf1_P$ and $\sum_{F\in\mathcal F}\theta_F=h$.

Suppose further that $h>1$ bounds the relative Helly number of $P$, and that the weights are the volumes of compact convex fibers $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ with positive $d$-volume, $d\ge1$, whose centroids are given by one affine function on the base. In case 1 there is an actual centroid mark of raw mixed halfspace depth strictly greater than $\gamma_d M/h$, where $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Thus if the maximum raw depth equals $\gamma_d M/h$, the critical proper faces have the fractional partition in case 2. The strict conclusion holds in particular if some site of $P$ lies outside every proper face of weight at most $\alpha$, including when $P$ meets $\operatorname{relint}B$.

pk-intake-finite-base-upward-max-support.relation_to_goal: Exact simultaneous compatibility on finite complete bases, with an algorithm-specific calibration and a conditional fixed-cover implication.
pk-intake-finite-base-upward-max-support.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty. Let positive compact convex $d$-bodies $K_z$ satisfy every anchored Minkowski inclusion on $P$. Give each base a nonnegative jointly continuous field $F_z(u,x)$ on $\mathbb S^{d-1}\times\mathbb R^d$, convex in $x$. Choose a linear height distinct on $P$. For each nonself extreme anchored probability vector $\lambda$ at $q$, choose a positive input $z$ of greater height than $q$, and define
$$
(T_eV)(u,x)=\lambda_z^{-1}\sup_{x_j\in K_j,\ j\ne z,\ \lambda_j>0} V(u,\lambda_z x+\sum_{j\ne z}\lambda_jx_j).
$$
Process targets in increasing height, with $V_z$ the maximum of $F_z$ and all incoming transfers. The resulting fields are pointwise least among arrays dominating the seeds and satisfying $V_z\ge T_eV_q$ for these chosen edges. Each field is the maximum of all composed directed seed transfers to its base. For all sufficiently small $\varepsilon\ge0$, the bodies
$$
K_z(\varepsilon)=\{x:u\cdot x+\varepsilon V_z(u,x)\le h_{K_z}(u)\text{ for every unit }u\}
$$
are positive and nested and satisfy all anchored inclusions exactly. Their lifted hull has precisely those integer fibers and full dimension relative to $\operatorname{aff}(P)\times\mathbb R^d$.

Let $M,Q$ be the old total mixed mass and maximum raw depth. Let $D,D(H)$ be the first total and fixed-cap losses on this path. If a finite list of fixed ambient closed halfspaces covers the old mixed set, has every mass at most $Q$, and satisfies $D(H)-(Q/M)D>0$ for every row of mass $Q$, the new maximum normalized depth is strictly below $Q/M$ for all sufficiently small positive $\varepsilon$. The critical normalized row expansion is $Q/M-\varepsilon[D(H)-(Q/M)D]/M+o(\varepsilon)$.

For $P=\{-m,\ldots,m\}$, $m\ge1$, identical centered fibers $L$, sole seed $h_L$ at $0$, and increasing height with each bracket charged to its right input, the final fields are $g_qh_L$ where $g_q=0$ for $q<0$ and $g_q=2^q$ for $q\ge0$. Total first loss divided by prescribed source loss is $2^{m+1}-1$. The constant continuation $h_L$ is also compatible and costs only $2m+1$ times the prescribed source loss.

pk-intake-finite-buffered-active-cap-bal.relation_to_goal: An actual finite cap group under strict own-trace properness. Its continuous resultant is the specified buffer gradient term and the cover is on the sampled source fiber.
pk-intake-finite-buffered-active-cap-bal.statement:
Use the finite mixed family, continuous concave buffer and closed buffered depth $b_\varepsilon$ from the closed quantile-region theorem. Suppose $\varepsilon>0$, $p\in P$ and $y$ is a local maximizer of $b_\varepsilon(p,\cdot)$ with $y\in\operatorname{int}K_p$ and $\varepsilon f(p,y)<\operatorname{dist}(y,\partial K_p)$. Put $q=b_\varepsilon(p,y)$. Then $0<q<b_{\rm base}(p)$. There are at most $d+1$ closed caps
$$
H_j=\{(Z,X):a_j\cdot(Z-p)+u_j\cdot(X-y)+\varepsilon f(p,y)\ge0\},
\qquad \|u_j\|=1,
$$
each of actual mass $q$ and with threshold the right $q$-quantile for its normal. There are positive weights $\rho_j$ summing to one and an own-fiber supergradient $g$ of $f(p,\cdot)$ at $y$ with $\sum_j\rho_j u_j=\varepsilon g$. The caps cover $\{p\}\times K_p$.

pk-intake-finite-capacity-allocation-ext.relation_to_goal: An extreme-point and dual certificate for fractional sites in a finite base allocation.
pk-intake-finite-capacity-allocation-ext.statement:
Let $P\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be finite, with capacities $a_z>0$ for $z\in P$. Fix a mass $m\ge0$ and a vector $g\in\mathbb R^n$, and assume
$$
Q=\{b:0\le b_z\le a_z,\ \sum_{z\in P}b_z=m,\ \sum_{z\in P}z b_z=mg\}
$$
is nonempty. A point of $Q$ is extreme exactly when the columns $(1,z)$ at its partially filled sites $0<b_z<a_z$ are linearly independent. Every linear cost $\sum_z c_zb_z$ has an extreme minimizer, and this minimizer has at most $\operatorname{rank}((1,z)_{z\in P})\le n+1$ partially filled sites.

There are a scalar $\lambda$ and vector $v\in\mathbb R^n$ such that the minimum value is
$$
\lambda m+v\cdot(mg)+\sum_{z\in P}a_z\min(0,c_z-\lambda-v\cdot z).
$$
For this pair a feasible $b$ is optimal exactly when $b_z=a_z$ at each strict negative reduced cost $c_z-\lambda-v\cdot z$ and $b_z=0$ at each strict positive one. If $c_z=\|z-g\|_2^2$ and $m>0$, the reduced cost is the squared distance from $g+v/2$ minus a nonnegative squared radius. Every optimizer thus fills the strict interior sites of the corresponding closed ball, leaves its exterior sites empty, and can be fractional only on its sphere.

pk-intake-finite-capped-signed-exponenti.relation_to_goal: Proves the exact restricted capped-normal ingredient for symmetric simplex chains.
pk-intake-finite-capped-signed-exponenti.statement:
Let $3\le d\le9$, and let $E_0,\ldots,E_d$ be independent unit exponentials. Over all $a\in[-1,1]^{d+1}$ with $a_0=-1$ and $\sum_i a_i=0$, the minimum of $\Pr(\sum_i a_iE_i\ge0)$ for each $d$ is given by
$$
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrr}
d&3&4&5&6&7&8&9\\ \hline
\text{minimum}&1/2&13/27&243/512&1472/3125&21875/46656&384912/823543&15647317/33554432 .
\end{array}
$$
In every listed dimension the minimum is realized by two positive unit coefficients, the fixed negative unit coefficient, and $d-2$ negative coefficients of magnitude $1/(d-2)$. Each minimum is strictly greater than $\tfrac76(d/(d+1))^d$.

pk-intake-finite-concave-sequence-power-.relation_to_goal: Finite scalar concave sequences, including zero endpoints. The result concerns adjacent power moments and their sharp homogeneous ratio.
pk-intake-finite-concave-sequence-power-.statement:
Let $f_0,\ldots,f_{N-1}$ be a nonnegative, nonzero concave sequence on consecutive indices, with $N\ge1$ and $m=\max_i f_i$. For every real $p\ge1$,
$$
(p+2)\sum_i f_i^{p+1}-(p+1)m\sum_i f_i^p\ge\frac{m^{p+1}}{N}.
$$
Consequently $\sum_i f_i^{p+1}/(m\sum_i f_i^p)>(p+1)/(p+2)$ for every finite sequence. At each fixed $p$, the latter constant is the infimum over all finite lengths and all such sequences.

pk-intake-finite-cover-asymmetry-localiz.relation_to_goal: Ordinary normalized volume and an actual reflected-copy containment at the contact of a finite whole-space cover.
pk-intake-finite-cover-asymmetry-localiz.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body of positive volume and let $y\in K$. Suppose finitely many proper closed halfspaces with boundaries through $y$ cover $\mathbb R^d$. Let $B$ be their largest cap fraction and let $\rho=\max\{r\ge0:y-r(K-y)\subseteq K\}$. For $\gamma_j=(j/(j+1))^j$,
$$
B\ge\frac{\gamma_{d-1}}{(1+\rho)^d}.
$$
In particular, if $\gamma_d\le\tau<\gamma_{d-1}$ and $B\le\tau$, then $y-r_0(K-y)\subseteq K$ for $r_0=(\gamma_{d-1}/\tau)^{1/d}-1$.

pk-intake-finite-depth-region-projected-.relation_to_goal: This is geometry for a nonempty lattice-excluded depth region of a probability measure. The contacts are on the auxiliary outer polytope, and the cap estimate uses the factor d+1.
pk-intake-finite-depth-region-projected-.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, $d\ge0$, let $C\subset\mathbb R^{n+d}$ be a convex body, and let $\mu$ be a Borel probability supported on $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. Fix $0<\alpha<1$. Suppose the ambient depth region $D_\alpha=\{y:\mu(H)\ge\alpha\text{ for every closed halfspace }H\ni y\}$ is nonempty and disjoint from $\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$. There is a compact full-dimensional ambient polytope $Q\supseteq D_\alpha$ disjoint from $\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, described by inequalities $a_i\cdot z+\beta_i\cdot x\le c_i$ with $\mu\{a_i\cdot z+\beta_i\cdot x>c_i\}<\alpha$.

Each facet $\ell_j\cdot z\le\delta_j$ of the base projection of $Q$ has a nonempty index set $I_j$ with $|I_j|\le d+1$ and positive multipliers $\lambda_{ji}$ such that
$$
\sum_{i\in I_j}\lambda_{ji}\beta_i=0,\qquad
\sum_{i\in I_j}\lambda_{ji}a_i=\ell_j\ne0,\qquad
\sum_{i\in I_j}\lambda_{ji}c_i=\delta_j.
$$
Every lifted point of $Q$ above that facet is tight in all inequalities indexed by $I_j$. At most $2^n$ of the facet halfspaces already have intersection disjoint from $\mathbb Z^n$. Their strict exteriors cover $S$, each exterior for facet $j$ having mass less than $|I_j|\alpha\le(d+1)\alpha$.

pk-intake-finite-fiber-anchored-capacity.relation_to_goal: Applies to arbitrary finite real base sets, including null fibers. Gives attainment of a cap and of the deepest point of a fixed family.
pk-intake-finite-fiber-anchored-capacity.statement:
Fix $n,d\ge 1$, a finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb R^n$, and nonempty compact convex sets $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ for $z\in P$. Write $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$, $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_z})$, and $M=\mu(S)$. Let $h_\mu(z,x)$ be the infimum of $\mu(H)$ over closed ambient halfspaces $H$ containing $(z,x)$. For each $z\in P$ and $(u,t)\in\mathbb S^{d-1}\times\mathbb R$ define
$$
c_z(u,t)=\inf_{a\in\mathbb R^n}\mu\{(w,y):a\cdot(w-z)+u\cdot y\ge t\}.
$$
The infimum is attained by a finite $a$, and $c_z$ is continuous on its entire parameter space. For every $x\in K_z$,
$$
h_\mu(z,x)=\min_{\|u\|=1}c_z(u,u\cdot x).
$$
In particular, the depth is continuous on each fiber, is attained by a nonvertical closed halfspace through the point, and attains its maximum over $S$.

pk-intake-finite-fiber-surface-parity-mi.relation_to_goal: Physical surface-measure transport on actual normal contact in finite compatible families. The theorem concerns conditional ceilings and convex order.
pk-intake-finite-fiber-surface-parity-mi.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $n\ge0$, and let $P=\operatorname{conv}P\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be nonempty and finite. For each $z\in P$ let $K_z$ be a convex body in $\mathbb R^d$. Assume compatibility in the sense that $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_z(\{z\}\times K_z)$ has exact sampled fibers $K_z$. Let $\eta$ be the sum of the ordinary boundary surface measures of $K_z$ on the marked bundle $(u,z,X)$, where $u$ is the almost everywhere unique outward normal (endpoint counting measure for $d=1$). Suppose $\gamma_-,\gamma_+\le\eta$ have an old coupling that preserves the common endpoint normal and whose midpoint $(p,Y)$ has $p\in P$, $Y\in F_{K_p}(u)$ almost everywhere. Then there is one same-normal coupling of the same marginals with the same actual-support midpoint property and $\rho\le2^n\eta$ for its marked midpoint law. Relative to a common finite normal reference, for almost every normal and each original endpoint parity class it has the original two conditional endpoint marginals, and its conditional physical midpoint law dominates the old one in full physical convex order. These orders can be integrated against any bounded nonnegative Borel normal weight.

More locally, its density ceiling over a given $(u,p)$ is the number of classes having positive conditional endpoint bases $z,w$ in that class with $z+w=2p$ and $h_{K_z}(u)+h_{K_w}(u)=2h_{K_p}(u)$. The uniform factor $2^n$ is sharp.

pk-intake-finite-gaussian-parity-concent.relation_to_goal: Posterior probabilities on actual unchanged fibers. No transfer of the selected centroid's depth to the prior.
pk-intake-finite-gaussian-parity-concent.statement:
Let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite nonempty, with positive compact convex $d$-fibers $K_z$, $d\ge1$, satisfying $\sum_j\lambda_jK_{z_j}\subseteq K_w$ whenever $w=\sum_j\lambda_jz_j\in P$ with convex weights. Put $V_z=|K_z|$ and $p_z\propto V_z\exp(a\cdot z-t|z|^2/2)$ for $t\ge0$. Each such anchored relation satisfies
$$
\frac{p_w}{\prod_jp_{z_j}^{\lambda_j}}
=\frac{V_w}{\prod_j V_{z_j}^{\lambda_j}}
 \exp\!\left(\frac t2\sum_j\lambda_j|z_j-w|^2\right)
\ge\exp\!\left(\frac t2\sum_j\lambda_j|z_j-w|^2\right).
$$
For distinct same-parity $z,z'$ with midpoint $w$, one has $p_w^2/(p_zp_{z'})\ge e^{t|z-z'|^2/4}$, hence $p_zp_{z'}\le e^{-t}$. If $k$ parities are occupied, one largest posterior weight per parity retains mass at least $1-(|P|-k)e^{-t/2}$ uniformly in $a$. A largest fiber's centroid therefore has posterior depth at least $(\Gamma_d/k)[1-(|P|-k)e^{-t/2}]_+$, where $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$.

If $a_t/t\to c$, the posterior mass outside the nearest bases to $c$ tends to zero. These bases have distinct parities. If $a_t=tc+b$ with fixed $b$, their limiting weights are proportional to $V_z e^{b\cdot z}$. In the observation process with prior proportional to $V_z$, the posterior tends almost surely to the single hidden base.

pk-intake-finite-global-cut-radial-loss.relation_to_goal: First losses under actual relative convex-body erosions on a fixed compatible finite lattice base, including fixed supporting traces.
pk-intake-finite-global-cut-radial-loss.statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge1$, and let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty. For each $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior. Assume $\sum_z\lambda_z K_z\subseteq K_p$ whenever $\lambda_z\ge0$, $\sum_z\lambda_z=1$, and $\sum_z\lambda_z z=p\in P$. Put $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$ and $h_z=h_{K_z}$.

A finite global-cut action on $C$ uses a nonempty finite index set $I$. For each $i\in I$, its function $\ell_i(u,z)$ is continuous in $u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}$ and affine in $z\in\operatorname{aff}(P)$, with $\ell_i(u,z)\ge h_z(u)$ on $P$. Its field $V_i(u,z,x)$ is jointly continuous and nonnegative on $\mathbb S^{d-1}\times C$ and convex in $(z,x)$ on $C$ for each fixed $u$. Fields satisfying these assumptions on a larger common convex domain can be restricted to $C$. For $\varepsilon\ge0$ define
$$
C_\varepsilon=C\cap
\bigcap_{i\in I,\;u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}}
\{(z,x):u\cdot x+\varepsilon V_i(u,z,x)\le\ell_i(u,z)\}.
$$
Then $C_0=C$, and for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon\ge0$, $C_\varepsilon$ is a nested compact convex body in $\operatorname{aff}(P)\times\mathbb R^d$. Its projection is $\operatorname{conv}(P)$, its integer fibers $K_z(\varepsilon)=(C_\varepsilon)_z$ have nonempty interior exactly for $z\in P$, and it has no other integer fibers. The deformed fibers satisfy all the same anchored Minkowski inclusions.

At a regular $x\in\partial K_z$, with unique outward unit normal $\nu_z(x)$, define
$$
v_z(x)=\max\Bigl(\{V_i(\nu_z(x),z,x):i\in I,\ \ell_i(\nu_z(x),z)=h_z(\nu_z(x))\}\cup\{0\}\Bigr).
$$
About each fixed $o_z\in\operatorname{int}K_z$, let $s_\varepsilon(x)$ be the fractional radial loss, so the new endpoint on the ray through $x$ is $o_z+(1-s_\varepsilon(x))(x-o_z)$. The ratios $s_\varepsilon(x)/\varepsilon$ are uniformly bounded in $x\in\partial K_z$ and, at each regular $x$, tend to $v_z(x)/[\nu_z(x)\cdot(x-o_z)]$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. Thus
$$
|K_z|-|K_z(\varepsilon)|=\varepsilon\int_{\partial K_z}v_z\,dS+o(\varepsilon),
\qquad dS=d\mathcal H^{d-1}.
$$

Let $\mu_\varepsilon(H)=\sum_{z\in P}|K_z(\varepsilon)\cap H_z|$, where $H_z=\{x:(z,x)\in H\}$ for a fixed closed ambient halfspace $H$. On $\partial K_z$, let $\kappa_{z,H}$ be $1$ if $K_z\subseteq H_z$, $0$ if $\operatorname{int}K_z\cap H_z=\varnothing$, and $\mathbf1_{\operatorname{int}H_z}$ otherwise. The first case includes an inside supporting cut and a pure-base cut whose boundary contains the whole fiber. The second includes an outside supporting trace, even when that trace has positive surface measure. Then
$$
\mu_0(H)-\mu_\varepsilon(H)=\varepsilon L(H)+o(\varepsilon),
\qquad L(H)=\sum_{z\in P}\int_{\partial K_z}\kappa_{z,H}v_z\,dS.
$$
The first total loss is $D=\sum_{z\in P}\int_{\partial K_z}v_z\,dS$. The remainders can be taken uniformly on each fixed finite cap list. For $d=1$, $dS$ is counting measure on the two endpoints.

pk-intake-finite-global-cut-speed-additi.relation_to_goal: Finite nonnegative addition of actual global-cut speeds on one common family, with their fixed linear responses.
pk-intake-finite-global-cut-speed-additi.statement:
On one common family $P,(K_z)_{z\in P},C$ as in the finite global-cut radial loss lemma, let $a=1,\ldots,N$, $N\ge1$, index finite global-cut actions with fields $V_{ai}$ and baselines $\ell_{ai}$. For any fixed coefficients $\alpha_a\ge0$, one finite global-cut action on $C$ has inward speeds
$$
v_{\alpha,z}(x)=\sum_{a=1}^N\alpha_a v_{a,z}(x)
$$
at every regular point $x$ of every original measured boundary $\partial K_z$. It has first total loss $D_\alpha=\sum_a\alpha_a D_a$ and, for every fixed closed ambient halfspace $H$, first cap loss $L_\alpha(H)=\sum_a\alpha_a L_a(H)$, with uniform little-o remainders on each fixed finite cap list. In particular it gives exactly the same combination of the first response rows $L_a(H)-\beta D_a$ for any fixed level $\beta$, and of the integrals of the speeds against any fixed bounded Borel boundary weights. If every $\alpha_a=0$, the constructed action is identically $C$ for all $\varepsilon\ge0$. All actions, including the constructed one, have zero-parameter body exactly $C$. The speeds and their finite linear response vectors therefore form algebraic cones under finite nonnegative combinations.

pk-intake-finite-knot-preservation-for-s.relation_to_goal: Extends exact finite physical cap, coarea and moment preservation to interior sources away from the maximum profile level.
pk-intake-finite-knot-preservation-for-s.statement:
Let $m\ge1$ be an integer and let $r:[a,b]\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous and concave with $a<0<b$ and $r(0)>0$. Put $R=\max r$ and write $\{z:r(z)\ge v\}=[-B(v),A(v)]$ for $0\le v\le R$. For any finite menu of $q$ positive slopes, with zero optionally included, there is a continuous concave piecewise affine profile on $[a,b]$ with the same $R$ and $r(0)$ and with the same $V$ and all selected $P(s),C(s),M(s)$ in its own physical density law. The replacement has at most $9(2q+2)$ curvature locations per inverse arm, including joins.

pk-intake-finite-marked-capacity-and-fac.relation_to_goal: The threshold is for a fixed actual profile on marked facet measures. The face quotas constrain a single transport and give no favorable-menu selection or parity estimate.
pk-intake-finite-marked-capacity-and-fac.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and nonempty and let $d\ge1$. Let $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$ be the affine barycentric coordinates of a nondegenerate $d$-simplex. For each $z\in P$, let $K_z=\{x:\lambda_i(x)\ge b_i(z)\ \forall i\}$, where $1-\sum_i b_i(z)>0$. Assume that these placed fibers are the actual sampled sections of their convex hull. Let $F_i(z)=K_z\cap\{\lambda_i=b_i(z)\}$, let $n_i$ be its outer unit normal, and put $\eta_i=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes\mathcal H^{d-1}|_{F_i(z)}$ in the physical variables $(z,x)$. For $d=1$ use counting measure on the endpoints. Let $\eta$ be the sum of these measures with their respective normal marks. For any bounded nonnegative Borel profile $W$ on this bundle, define
$$
\mathcal E(W)=\sup_\Phi \frac{\int \Phi W\,d\eta}{\int\Phi\,d\eta},
$$
over continuous nonnegative fields whose restriction at each fixed normal is a finite convex function of $(z,x)$ and whose denominator is positive.

For every $c\ge0$, $\mathcal E(W)\le c$ if and only if, for each $i$, there is a physical martingale with source $\mu_i=(W-c)_+\eta_i$ and second marginal at most $\nu_i=(c-W)_+\eta_i$, with $W$ restricted to mark $n_i$. The transport uses the actual measures, including any closed-cap boundary values in $W$.

Write $G_i=\operatorname{conv}\{(z,b_i(z)):z\in P\}$. For almost every source row on $F_i(p)$, all its target lifted bases lie in the minimal face of $G_i$ containing $(p,b_i(p))$. If $F$ is any nonempty face of $G_i$ and $E_F$ is the union of the actual $i$-facets whose lifted bases lie in $F$, then $\mathcal E(W)\le c$ implies
$$
\mu_i(E_F)\le\nu_i(E_F),\qquad \int_{E_F}W\,d\eta_i\le c\eta_i(E_F).
$$
The used target mass is subject to one global $\nu_i$ ceiling, including where source faces share subfaces. If every lifted base is a vertex of $G_i$, transport at mark $n_i$ preserves the base. If an affine $a$ satisfies $b_i(z)\ge a(z)$ with equality precisely on the bases in $F$, then for some $\delta>0$ an admissible potential equals $\delta$ on $E_F$ and zero on the rest of the marked bundle.

pk-intake-finite-planar-ear-cap-and-coar.relation_to_goal: Finite ordinary cap and section geometry; the ear may meet unique sectors, so its area is not treated as a pure double gain.
pk-intake-finite-planar-ear-cap-and-coar.statement:
Let $T$ be a triangle containing $0$ in its interior, with distinct vertices $P_i$ lying strictly in the unique sectors of caps $v_i\cdot x\ge0$ for $(v_1,v_2,v_3)=((1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1))$. Add a point $Q$ in the open double sector captured by caps $2,3$ beyond edge $P_2P_3$, with convex quadrilateral in cyclic order $P_1,P_2,Q,P_3$ and ear area $E>0$. For cap $2$, put $p=v_2\cdot P_2>0$, $w=-v_2\cdot P_3>0$, $v=v_2\cdot Q>0$. If $Q_2$ is raw cap area and $\sigma_2$ its chord length divided by $\lVert v_2\rVert$, then
$$
\Delta Q_2=E\left(1-\frac{w^2}{(w+p)(w+v)}\right),\qquad
\Delta\sigma_2=\frac{2Ew}{(w+p)(w+v)},\qquad
\frac{2Q_2^{\rm new}}{\sigma_2^{\rm new}}
=p+\frac{\Delta\sigma_2}{\sigma_2^{\rm old}+\Delta\sigma_2}\,v(1+p/w).
$$
The analogous formulas hold for cap $3$ with the roles of $P_2,P_3$ exchanged. Cap $1$ and its chord are unchanged.

pk-intake-finite-planar-lorentz-sector-t.relation_to_goal: Finite preservation for positive planar raw data under both endpoint cap ceilings. The geometric statement requires actual fixed chords and the stated signed sector changes.
pk-intake-finite-planar-lorentz-sector-t.statement:
For positive data $k,Q_i,\sigma_i$, $i=1,2,3$, set $q_i=Q_i/k$, $M=\sum_i Q_i/\sigma_i$, $f_i=2\sqrt{kQ_i}/(\sigma_i M)$, and $\Phi_i=f_i+(f_j+f_l)^2/4$ for $\{i,j,l\}=\{1,2,3\}$. For $E_i,G_i\ge0$, put $E=\sum_i E_i$ and $G=\sum_i G_i$. Keep the sections fixed and set $k(t)=k(0)+t(G-E)$ and $Q_i(t)=Q_i(0)+t(G-G_i-E_i)$ for $0\le t\le1$. Suppose both endpoints have positive data and all their cap ratios satisfy $q_i\le128/279$. If the initial rows are all at most two, the final rows are all at most two, strictly below two if any transfer is nonzero. At a tight row on the common feasible boundary in this cap band every unit unique loss has strictly negative derivative, and every unit double gain has derivative less than $-1/(4k)$.

For actual planar bodies with common interior mark, balanced spanning cap normals and identical full cutting chords, the transfer hypotheses hold if each final unique-sector area is no greater and each final double-sector area is no smaller. In particular, if $T$ is a strict distinct-vertex triangle, $C_T$ is the hull of its six cutting-ray endpoints, and $C_T\subseteq K\subseteq T$, the result applies when both $T$ and $K$ have the stated cap ceiling. The rows are strict for $K\ne T$.

pk-intake-finite-plane-section-log-zero-.relation_to_goal: The classification concerns each actual fiber separately and allows a nonzero logarithmic defect on a supporting limit even from proper prelimit cuts.

In the moving-section setup of the positive-anchor lemma suppose $d\ge2$, $\sup_j\int_{K_j}1/L_j<\infty$, and $L_j=\min_{1\le r\le R}A_{rj}$ on $K_j$, where the finite affine components converge coefficientwise to $A_r(X)=b_r+c_r\cdot X$. If the allocated section-log defect is nonzero, then $\Pi=\{A_r=0\}$ for at least one $r$ with $c_r\ne0$. In particular $u$ is parallel to $c_r$, the entire exposed face $K\cap\Pi$ lies in $\{L=0\}$ and has dimension at most $d-2$, and the limit incidence is inside supporting if $u$ is a positive multiple of $c_r$, outside supporting if it is a negative multiple.

Both orientations are possible even for sections proper at every sufficiently late index. For $a=1/m$, $\eta=2^{-m}$, $K_m=\{x,y\ge0:a\le x+y\le1\}$ and $L_m=x+y-a+\eta$, the section $x+y=a+\eta^2$ has ordinary coarea $a+\eta^2\to0$ for raw normal $(1,1)$, and its negative-log weighted coarea tends to $\log 2$. Reversing the normal or multiplying $L_m$ by positive constants whose logarithms are bounded preserves that limit.

pk-intake-finite-prefix-two-list-countin.relation_to_goal: A finite arithmetic-list inequality for all positive powers, used separately as an input to the large-maximum simplex cap theorem.
pk-intake-finite-prefix-two-list-countin.statement:
Let $1/2\le\theta<1$, $0\le b\le1-\theta$, $a\ge0$, and let $m\ge0$ be an integer with $am\le1$. For $0\le h\le m$ put
$$
\rho_h=1-ah,\qquad L_h=1-\frac{a(1-b)h}{\theta},\qquad B_h=1-\frac{ab}{\theta}-\frac{a(1+b)h}{\theta}.
$$
For every $x\in(0,1]$ the combined lists $(L_h)$ and $(B_h)$ have at least as many entries at least $x$ as $(\rho_h)$, counting multiplicities. Hence for every real $p>0$,
$$
\sum_{h=0}^m\big[(L_h)_+^p+(B_h)_+^p\big]\ \ge\ \sum_{h=0}^m\rho_h^p ,
\qquad v_+=\max(v,0).
$$
For $m=0$, equality in the power sum holds exactly when $ab\ge\theta$. For $m\ge1$, equality holds exactly when $m=1$, $a=1$ and $b=\theta=1/2$.

pk-intake-five-vertex-uniform-interval-t.relation_to_goal: Counterexample to factor-two domination by a uniform interval law on any one actual integer fiber.
pk-intake-five-vertex-uniform-interval-t.statement: Let $C=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(3,0),(3,2),(2,4),(0,2)\}\subset\mathbb R_z\times\mathbb R_x$ and let $\mu$ be its normalized summed integer-fiber length. There is no nondegenerate uniform interval law supported on any of its integer fibers with $\nu(H)\le2\mu(H)$ for every closed ambient halfspace $H$.

pk-intake-fixed-anchor-exponential-capac.relation_to_goal: Comparison of exponential capacity at a prescribed base with true unweighted mixed-centroid cap retention at the same base. The examples hold at fixed integer dimension while the continuous dimension varies.
pk-intake-fixed-anchor-exponential-capac.statement:
For the actual integer fibers of a convex body in $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$, let $w_z$ be their $d$-volumes in units of the volume of the standard simplex $T_d$. At an integer anchor $j$ define $E_j=\inf_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}\sum_z w_z e^{\alpha(z-j)}$. Let $T_j$ denote the maximum actual mass, in the same units, of a convex subbody whose positive unweighted mixed volume has centroid base $j$. In each of the following examples one ambient closed cap attains $T_j$.

1. For the five integer fibers $zT_4$, $z=1,\ldots,5$, at anchor $j=3$, $T_3=116$ and $E_3^{16}\ge 2^{90}3^{18}5^4>232^{16}$.
2. For the three integer fibers $(1+z/10)T_{40}$, $z=-1,0,1$, at anchor $j=0$, $T_0=1+2(9/10)^{40}$ and $E_0=1+2(99/100)^{20}\ge13/5>5/2>2T_0$.
3. For integers $N\ge1$ and $L\ge2S_2$, where $S_2=\sum_{k=1}^N k^2$, set $d=L^3$ and take the integer fibers $(1+z/L^2)T_d$, $z=-N,\ldots,N$, at anchor $j=0$. With $K=2N+1$,
$$
K(1-S_2/L)^{1/K}\le E_0\le K,\qquad
1\le T_0\le 1+\frac{N(N+3)}2\,2^{-L}.
$$
For each fixed $N$, the ratio $E_0/T_0$ tends to $K$ as $L$ tends to infinity through integers. In particular the ratio is unbounded over actual affine-root homothetic simplex frusta at fixed integer dimension one.

pk-intake-fixed-base-hausdorff-stability.relation_to_goal: Continuity for a tracked mark at a fixed base under fiberwise perturbations. The base set and positive limit total mass are fixed in the assertion.
pk-intake-fixed-base-hausdorff-stability.statement: Let $P$ be a nonempty finite subset of a Euclidean space $E$, and suppose $K_z^{(j)}$ and $K_z$ are compact convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$ of positive $d$-volume, $d\ge1$, with $K_z^{(j)}\to K_z$ in Hausdorff distance for every $z\in P$. Let $\mu_j$ and $\mu$ be the corresponding mixed measures given by summing $d$-volume on the fibers over $P$. Fix $p\in P$ and $x\in K_p$. For any $x_j\in K_p^{(j)}$ with $x_j\to x$, the raw closed-halfspace depths satisfy $h_{\mu_j}((p,x_j))\to h_\mu((p,x))$, and $\mu_j(E\times\mathbb R^d)\to\mu(E\times\mathbb R^d)>0$. Therefore any strict normalized depth bound at a specified mark persists for sufficiently small fixed-base Hausdorff perturbations at feasible nearby marks, including a strict bound at a centroid of an original affine centroid graph.

pk-intake-fixed-binary-core-sharp-shell-.relation_to_goal: Exact integer geometry and a volume barrier for a common binary core with arbitrary convex continuous fibers.
pk-intake-fixed-binary-core-sharp-shell-.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$, let $Q=\{0,1\}^n$, and let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body of volume $V>0$. Every nonempty integer fiber of a compact convex body whose fibers at $Q$ all equal $K$ is contained in $K$. In particular, adding a nonempty compact convex fiber $A$ at $p\in\mathbb Z^n\setminus Q$ to $[0,1]^n\times K$ and taking the convex hull preserves the core fibers if and only if $A\subseteq K$. The new projection has just one outside integer base $p$ if and only if $p\in[-1,2]^n$. At each such $p$ one can realize arbitrarily small positive added volume.

For any body with this fixed core, let $E$ be the sum of the $d$-volumes of its outside integer fibers. If $E<2^{-d}V$, every nonempty integer fiber, including any of zero volume, has base in $[-1,2]^n$. The constant $2^{-d}$ is the sharp infimum of $E/V$ in the presence of a farther nonempty base. For $0\in K$, adding $tK$ at $-2e_1$ for $0<t<1$ gives just the two extra fibers $tK$ and $((1+t)/2)K$ and has $E/V=t^d+((1+t)/2)^d$.

For an outside shell base $p$, let $q(p)$ be its coordinatewise clamp to $[0,1]$. Its opposite partner $2q(p)-p$ is in $Q$ and differs from $q(p)$. Define a group for each anchor $q\in Q$ by collecting the outside shell bases with $q(p)=q$, allowing empty groups. Within each group the partners are distinct. Under $E<2^{-d}V$, some group has total mass at least $E/2^n$.

pk-intake-fixed-body-projective-orbit-ca.relation_to_goal: A necessary condition at a local projective orbit minimum of a fixed positive compatible finite-real-base fiber family. All quantities use full d-dimensional fiber volume and the original sampled coordinates.
pk-intake-fixed-body-projective-orbit-ca.statement:
Let $d\ge1$. Let $P\subset\mathbb R^r$ be finite and affinely spanning, with the origin in the relative interior of $\operatorname{conv}(P)$. For each $p\in P$, let $K_p$ be a compact convex set of positive $d$-volume. Suppose the family is compatible, meaning that the convex hull of $S=\bigcup_{p\in P}(\{p\}\times K_p)$ has exactly $K_p$ as its fiber at $p$. Write $\mu=\sum_p\delta_p\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_p})$ and $M=\mu(S)$. For an affine $L$ positive on $P$, take the unweighted fiber-volume measure of the family obtained from $S$ by $(p,x)\mapsto(p/L(p),x/L(p))$. Assume its maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth is locally minimized at $L=1$ among positive affine denominators. Write $\beta$ for this maximum at $L=1$ and $Q=\beta M$.

Index the deepest bases by $p_i$. At each one choose any exact positive circuit of nonvertical closed caps
$$
H_{ij}=\{(p,x):a_{ij}\cdot p+u_{ij}\cdot x\ge b_{ij}\},\qquad
\|u_{ij}\|=1,\qquad \mu(H_{ij})=Q,
$$
whose boundaries pass through a common deepest mark $(p_i,x_i)$ and whose weights satisfy $\rho_{ij}>0$, $\sum_j\rho_{ij}=1$, and $\sum_j\rho_{ij}u_{ij}=0$. At every other base use a fixed circuit covering the full fiber plane with each cap of mass strictly below $Q$. Such choices exist.

For each selected critical cap, let $\theta^{\rm pr}_{ij}$, $\theta^{\rm in}_{ij}$ and $\theta^{\rm out}_{ij}$ be the sums of $(d-1)$-dimensional section area on its proper sections, inside supporting sections (the fiber is contained in the closed cap), and outside supporting sections (the cap meets the fiber in a supporting face of zero $d$-volume), respectively. These are measures on the lifted sections in the original coordinates, with zero-area sections contributing zero. For $d=1$ the section measure is counting measure.

For every such choice of circuits and every Borel system $\sigma^{\rm in}_{ij}\in[0,1]$ on the inside supporting sections, there exist outside densities $\sigma^{\rm out}_{ij}\in[0,1]$ and nonnegative multipliers $\lambda_{ij}$. Put
$$
\zeta_{ij}=\theta^{\rm pr}_{ij}+\sigma^{\rm in}_{ij}\theta^{\rm in}_{ij}
                     +\sigma^{\rm out}_{ij}\theta^{\rm out}_{ij},
\qquad S_{ij}=\zeta_{ij}(\mathbb R^{r+d})>0.
$$
One such choice satisfies the linear identity
$$
-d\int A(p)\,d\mu
=\sum_{i,j}\lambda_{ij}\left[-d\int_{H_{ij}} A(p)\,d\mu
                             +\int \ell_{ij}(p,x)\,d\zeta_{ij}\right]
\tag{1}
$$
simultaneously for every signed affine $A$ and every signed cap velocity $\ell_{ij}(p,x)=\delta a_{ij}\cdot p+\delta u_{ij}\cdot x-\delta b_{ij}$ satisfying, for every $i$,
$$
\sum_j\rho_{ij}\delta u_{ij}=0,\qquad
\sum_j\rho_{ij}(\delta a_{ij}\cdot p_i-\delta b_{ij})=0.
\tag{2}
$$
In particular, the same certificate gives
$$
\sum_{i,j}\lambda_{ij}=\frac1\beta,\qquad
\int A(p)\,d\mu=\sum_{i,j}\lambda_{ij}\int_{H_{ij}} A(p)\,d\mu
\quad\text{for every affine }A,\qquad
\lambda_{ij} S_{ij}=c_i\rho_{ij}\quad(c_i\ge0).
\tag{3}
$$
Consequently each group has either all multipliers positive or all zero. Equivalently, $\lambda_{ij}=\pi_i\kappa_{ij}/\beta$, where $\pi_i=\beta\sum_j\lambda_{ij}$ are nonnegative and sum to one, and $\kappa_{ij}=(\rho_{ij}/S_{ij})/\sum_l(\rho_{il}/S_{il})$. The same choice of outside allocations and multipliers works for all tests in (1)–(3) for the prescribed inside system.

pk-intake-fixed-body-retained-mass-stric.relation_to_goal: The function is the fixed-body ordinary retained mass. Strict quasiconcavity suffices for uniqueness on convex constraints.
pk-intake-fixed-body-retained-mass-stric.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K$ be a convex body in $\mathbb R^d$, and let $T_K(y)$ be the maximal mass of a measurable Lebesgue density $0\le f\le1$ on $K$ with $\int_K(x-y)f(x)\,dx=0$. If $y_1,y_2\in\operatorname{int}K$ are distinct and $0<\lambda<1$, then
$$
T_K((1-\lambda)y_1+\lambda y_2)>\min\{T_K(y_1),T_K(y_2)\}.
$$
Consequently $T_K$ attains its maximum uniquely on every nonempty compact convex subset of $\operatorname{int}K$.

pk-intake-fixed-cap-volume-from-fixed-pr.relation_to_goal: A variational consequence conditional on an attained minimum in one fixed lattice projection class.
pk-intake-fixed-cap-volume-from-fixed-pr.statement:
Fix $n,d\ge1$ and a finite nonempty lattice-convex projection $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$. Consider compatible families of nonempty compact convex fibers over exactly $P$, with positive total mixed $d$-volume. Compatibility means that the convex hull of the lifted fibers has the specified fiber at every site of $P$. For a family $S$, write $\mu_S$ for summed $d$-volume on its fibers, $M(S)=\mu_S(S)$, and $h_{\mu_S}$ for raw closed-halfspace depth. Suppose $S_*$ attains the minimum of $\max_{y\in S}h_{\mu_S}(y)/M(S)$ in this fixed-$P$ class, with value $\beta$ and total mass $M_*>0$.

There are two fixed-cap volume formulations of this attained minimum.

1. For any finite nonvertical closed cap cover $(H_j)$ of $S_*$ with $\mu_{S_*}(H_j)\le\beta M_*$, at each $z\in P$ whose plane is not entirely covered there is one closed supporting halfspace $E_z$ containing $K_{*,z}$, entirely covered by the cap traces at $z$. Then $S_*$ globally maximizes $M(S')$ over compatible families $S'$ on $P$ with $K'_z\subset E_z$ where imposed and $\mu_{S'}(H_j)\le\beta M_*$ for each $j$. In particular such a cover can be chosen with at most $2^n(d+1)$ caps.
2. There is a fixed cover by at most $|P|(d+1)$ nonvertical closed caps such that $S_*$ globally maximizes $M(S')$ subject solely to the budgets $\mu_{S'}(H_j)\le\beta M_*$ in the same class. In each formulation, the tight budget inequalities at $S_*$ are exactly those with cap mass $\beta M_*$.

pk-intake-fixed-coupling-one-sided-conve.relation_to_goal: An abstract estimate for fixed endpoint couplings. It does not construct an actual discounted repair, establish endpoint capacities, or control the physical crossing cost.
pk-intake-fixed-coupling-one-sided-conve.statement:
Let $C$ be a compact convex set, let $L=\min_i A_i>0$ there for finitely many affine $A_i$, and let $q\ge0$ on $C$ be the restriction of a finite global convex function. For $d\ge1$ define
$$
F(q,L)=\sup_{t\ge0}\{tq-(e^t-1)L\},\quad F_q(w)=F(q(w),L(w)),\quad w_q=(q-L)_+.
$$
The scalar $F$ is zero for $q\le L$ and equals $q\log(q/L)-q+L$ for $q>L$. It is convex in the pair, nondecreasing in $q$, and nonincreasing in positive $L$. The two physical functions $F_q,w_q$ have finite global convex extensions. For any endpoints $w_-,w_+\in C$, midpoint $b$, $a=(L(w_-)+L(w_+))/(2L(b))$, and $\delta_F=(F_q(w_-)+F_q(w_+))/2-F_q(b)$, one has
$$
w_q(b)(1-a^d)\ \le\ w_q(b)[1-e^{-d\delta_F/w_q(b)}]\ \le\ d\delta_F
$$
with the middle expression zero for $w_q(b)=0$.

Suppose finite nonnegative endpoint couplings $\pi,\pi_{\rm old}$ have the same respective marginals $\gamma_-,\gamma_+$ and midpoint laws $\rho,\rho_{\rm old}$, with $\rho_{\rm old}\preceq_{\rm cx}\rho$. Put $E=b_\#((1-a^d)\pi)$, $\eta=(\gamma_-+\gamma_+)/2$, $\Delta_{\rm old}=\int F_q\,d(\eta-\rho_{\rm old})$, and $T_{\rm end}=\int w_q\,d\eta$. Then
$$
\int w_q\,dE\ \le\ T_{\rm end}[1-e^{-d\Delta_{\rm old}/T_{\rm end}}]\ \le\ d\Delta_{\rm old},
$$
with zero middle expression for $T_{\rm end}=0$. The same $\pi$ works for every admissible $q$. If a prescribed source $\nu\preceq_{\rm cx}\rho_{\rm old}$ is given, the bound also holds with $\Delta_{\rm old}$ replaced by $\int F_q\,d(\eta-\nu)$. Over already supplied measurable components with finite summed budgets, the total is bounded by the same formula with the summed or integrated $T_{\rm end}$ and $\Delta_{\rm old}$. In particular this summation introduces no parity multiplier in the error bound.

pk-intake-fixed-deepest-base-face-buffer.relation_to_goal: A cover and contact identity on one old minimal deepest-base face, including a nested-family upper comparison with frozen thresholds.
pk-intake-fixed-deepest-base-face-buffer.statement:
Use the finite mixed family and buffer of the closed quantile-region theorem. Assume additionally that $f(z,X)=\mathcal F(C_z,X)$, where the nonnegative marked functional $\mathcal F$ is inclusion-monotone and is multiplied by $s^\kappa$ under any common homothety of the body and its mark with ratio $s>0$, for some $\kappa>0$. Then every own-fiber supergradient $g$ at $(p,y)$ has a finite full extension $(\alpha,g)$ satisfying
$$
f(z,X)\le f(p,y)+\alpha\cdot(z-p)+g\cdot(X-y)\qquad((z,X)\in C).
$$

Let $(p,y)\in S$ be a global buffered maximizer at $\varepsilon>0$ satisfying $y\in\operatorname{int}K_p$ and $\varepsilon f(p,y)<\operatorname{dist}(y,\partial K_p)$. Put $q=Q_\varepsilon$ and take any positive-weight group of right-quantile mass-$q$ caps with the balance $\sum_j\rho_j u_j=\varepsilon g$ of the finite active-cap balance theorem. Write $I$ for the bases of the sampled global maximizers and $F_p$ for the minimal face of $\operatorname{conv}I$ containing $p$. For any such full extension $(\alpha,g)$, the corrected vector $\ell=\sum_j\rho_j a_j-\varepsilon\alpha$ satisfies $\ell\cdot(z-p)\le0$ on $\operatorname{conv}I$ and vanishes in displacement from $p$ on $F_p$. For every $z\in F_p$ and $X\in C_z$, the weighted margin of the same fixed actual caps is at least $\varepsilon f(z,X)$. Thus these closed caps cover the whole fiber. At any $(z,X)\in D_{q,\varepsilon}$ over $F_p$, all their buffered quantile constraints are equalities, as is the displayed full tangent.

For a nested compatible smaller family on the same positive sampled bases, with updated buffer $f_t\le f$ on its canonical hull $C_t$, the old fixed cap thresholds give the upper bound $b_{\varepsilon,t}\le q$ on the part of $C_t$ over $F_p$.

pk-intake-fixed-epsilon-concave-array-at.relation_to_goal: An actual fixed-base, fixed-positive-scale variational result for a multiplier constant on each sampled fiber. The canonical minimal-bad-base application is conditional on a strict bad input. The estimate bounds infimal values as the scale vanishes.
pk-intake-fixed-epsilon-concave-array-at.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $N=d+1$, $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, and let $P$ be a finite complete affine-lattice base with $k$ occupied parities. Range over all actual positive compatible $d$-fibers on $P$. Denote the total sampled volume by $M$, the fiber volumes and centroids by $V_z$ and $g_z$, and the original normalized maximum closed-halfspace depth by $\beta_0(K)$. Let $\beta_0^*=\inf_K\beta_0(K)$. Fix $b$ with $\beta_0^*<b<\gamma_d/k$. Assume the entire original sublevel $\{\beta_0\le b\}$ admits a compact representative frame under invertible maps $(z,x)\mapsto(z,Ax+s(z))$, where $s$ is affine in the base. Its representatives have $M=1$, $V_z\ge v>0$, $K_z\subset R B_d$, and $V(T)\le b k(T)/\gamma_d$ for each nonempty proper closed minor $T=P\cap\operatorname{conv}(T)$.

A positive sampled-concave array $\ell$ satisfies $\ell_q\ge\sum_z\lambda_z\ell_z$ for every anchored convex representation $q=\sum_z\lambda_z z$ in $P$, and is normalized by $\sum_z(V_z/M)\log\ell_z=0$. At a mark $(p,y)$ use the displacement
$$
\varepsilon(\ell_p E_{K_p}(y)/M)^{1/N}G_K(u),\qquad
G_K(u)=\left(\frac{1}{M}\sum_z\int_{K_z}(u\cdot(X-g_z))^2\,dX\right)^{1/2},
$$
added to the margin $a\cdot(z-p)+u\cdot(X-y)$ of each through-mark cap with $u\ne0$. Here $E_{K_p}$ is the projective energy of d90ba05577427854, with boundary value zero. Include unchanged pure-base caps, with the harmless formal whole-base trace of mass $M$ in rank zero. Write $\beta_\varepsilon(K,\ell)$ for the normalized maximum buffered depth.

For each fixed $\varepsilon>0$ the sublevel $\{\beta_\varepsilon\le b\}$ is compact in the stated frame. If an admissible reference pair has $\beta_\varepsilon<b$, the unrestricted joint infimum is attained by a positive compatible family and positive array. Such a reference exists for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ the infimal value lies between $\beta_0^*$ and $\beta_0^*+\varepsilon |P|\kappa_{d-1}R^d$, where $\kappa_j$ is the volume of the Euclidean unit $j$-ball and $\kappa_0=1$.

pk-intake-fixed-face-marked-projective-e.relation_to_goal: Rigidity on a single fixed minimal face of the buffered maximizing base hull. The marked equality and actual cap cover give no joint deformation load inequality.
pk-intake-fixed-face-marked-projective-e.statement:
Use the finite canonical mixed family and Euclidean buffered depth of the closed quantile-region theorem with $f(z,X)=E_{C_z}(X)^{1/(d+1)}$ extended by zero to own-fiber boundaries. Let $\varepsilon>0$, let $(p,y)$ be a sampled global buffered maximizer with $y\in\operatorname{int}K_p$ and $\varepsilon f(p,y)<\operatorname{dist}(y,\partial K_p)$, and put $q=Q_\varepsilon$. Let $I$ be the set of sampled maximizing bases and $F_p$ the minimal face of $\operatorname{conv}I$ containing $p$. Choose a positive-weight balanced mass-$q$ cap group at $(p,y)$ and a full supergradient extension $(\alpha,g)$ from the fixed-face cover theorem.

The part of $D_{q,\varepsilon}$ over $F_p$ is the graph of a unique affine mark $x(z)\in\operatorname{int}C_z$ at every real base $z\in F_p$. It is also exactly the full-tangent equality locus over that face. Every mark is an equality point of every selected buffered right-quantile constraint. The whole centered fibers $C_z-x(z)$, their volumes, and the values $E_{C_z}(x(z))$ are constant on the face. For any convex combination of bases $z=\sum_i\lambda_i z_i$ there, $C_z=\sum_i\lambda_i C_{z_i}$ and $x(z)=\sum_i\lambda_i x(z_i)$. The assertions include caps with nonregular supporting traces.

pk-intake-fixed-facet-moving-equal-budge.relation_to_goal: The moving-cover and gap test are for a fixed three-planar-fiber configuration. The numerical implication with a strict below-2/9 original global budget has no instances on this domain by accepted 2a8c2bc6d7992c5e.
pk-intake-fixed-facet-moving-equal-budge.statement:
Let $A,K,B\subset\mathbb R^2$ be convex bodies at the only integer bases $-1,0,1$, with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Fix $y\in\operatorname{int}K$, and nonzero spanning normals $v_i$ for $1\le i\le3$ with $\sum_i v_i=0$. Put $h_i=h_B(v_i)$ and $b_i=2v_i\cdot y-h_i$. Suppose the caps $v_i\cdot(x-y)+(v_i\cdot y-h_i)z\ge0$ have common raw mass $Q$ and proper $A,K$ cuts. Write $a=|A|$, $M=|A|+|K|+|B|$, $U_i=|A\cap\{v_i\cdot x\ge b_i\}|$, and $a_i,k_i$ for the $A,K$ chord lengths divided by $\lVert v_i\rVert$. Put $s_i=2a_i+k_i$, $\lambda_i=1/s_i$, $\Lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i$, and
$$
L_i(p)=2U_i+(b_i-v_i\cdot p)a_i,\qquad
\overline L(p)=\frac{\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)}{\Lambda}.
$$

For every $p\in A$, contract $A$ to $A_t=p+(1-t)(A-p)$ and keep $K,B$ fixed. For all sufficiently small $t\ge0$ there is a $C^1$ meeting point $y(t)$ with $y(0)=y$ and a common cap budget $q(t)$ with $q(0)=Q$, obtained by substituting $y(t)$ for $y$ in the same three ambient caps. They cover the full middle plane, and $q'(0)=-\overline L(p)$. If $Q$ is the original global raw maximum and the two ordinary endpoint maxima are strictly below $Q$, the new global raw maximum is at most $q(t)$ for all sufficiently small $t\ge0$. Writing $M(t)=|A_t|+|K|+|B|$,
$$
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\frac{q(t)}{M(t)}\right|_{t=0}
=\frac{-M\overline L(p)+2aQ}{M^2}.
$$
In particular the optimized normalized depth strictly decreases if $\overline L(p)>2aQ/M$.

If the three original caps attain the true depth at $(0,y)$ and every singleton-capture region of the $A$ traces is null, then $\overline L(p)\ge a/2$ for every $p\in A$. The derivative above is then at most $(-Ma/2+2aQ)/M^2$. At a budget ratio $Q/M<2/9$ this last expression is less than $-a/(18M)$.

pk-intake-fixed-facet-roof-depth-deficit.relation_to_goal: First-order ordinary maximum depth for one fixed continuous roof and its displayed enclosing simplex. The error terms are pointwise in the fixed roof and majorant.
pk-intake-fixed-facet-roof-depth-deficit.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $m=d+1$, $\Gamma=(d/m)^d$, $c=(1-d^{1-d})/[(d-1)^2(d+1)]$, and $V=1/d!$. Let $B=\{z\in\mathbb R^{d-1}:z_j\ge0,\ \sum_j z_j\le1\}$, with normalized volume $\mu$ and barycentric coordinates $s=(z_1,\ldots,z_{d-1},1-\sum_j z_j)$. For a fixed continuous concave $\psi\ge0$ on $B$ and $\varepsilon>0$ put
$$
K_\varepsilon=\{(z,r):z\in B,\ \sum_jz_j-1\le r\le\varepsilon\psi(z)\}.
$$
This is a full-dimensional convex body, with $|K_\varepsilon|=V+\varepsilon dV\int_B\psi\,d\mu$. Let $\ell(z)=A+\sum_j B_jz_j$ be a fixed supporting affine majorant at the centroid of $B$. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, the simplex $S_\varepsilon$ given by
$$
q\ge0,\qquad z_j\ge0,\qquad q+\sum_j(1-\varepsilon B_j)z_j\le1+\varepsilon A,\qquad q=r-\sum_jz_j+1
$$
encloses $K_\varepsilon$. It satisfies
$$
|S_\varepsilon|=\frac{V(1+\varepsilon A)^d}{\prod_j(1-\varepsilon B_j)},\qquad
1-\frac{|K_\varepsilon|}{|S_\varepsilon|}
=\varepsilon d\int_B(\ell-\psi)\,d\mu+O(\varepsilon^2).
$$
For a full-dimensional body $K$, write $D(K)$ for maximum ordinary halfspace depth with respect to normalized volume. With $E_d(\psi)=\int_B[\#\{i:s_i\ge1/m\}-m\Gamma]\psi\,d\mu$,
$$
D(K_\varepsilon)=\Gamma+\varepsilon\frac{d}{m}E_d(\psi)+o(\varepsilon).
$$
For each fixed nonaffine roof the denominator in the following limit has positive linear coefficient, and
$$
\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}
\frac{D(K_\varepsilon)-\Gamma}{1-|K_\varepsilon|/|S_\varepsilon|}
=\frac{E_d(\psi)}{m\int_B(\ell-\psi)\,d\mu}
\ge\Gamma c.
$$
Equality in this limit is attained by $\psi=\min_i s_i$. If $\psi$ is affine, both linear terms vanish and the enclosing simplex formula still holds. The total variation distance of the two normalized uniform laws equals the displayed missing fraction, which therefore bounds their discrepancy over closed halfspaces. All error estimates are for the fixed roof and, where applicable, the fixed majorant.

pk-intake-fixed-fan-compatible-support-c.relation_to_goal: All direction and turnover claims are for a common fixed normal fan.
pk-intake-fixed-fan-compatible-support-c.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite, nonempty and lattice-complete, and fix a complete simplicial fan in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, with ray generators $u_r$. For each $z\in P$ and maximal cone $\sigma$, the proposed ray values $h_{zr}$ specify a unique linear piece $u\mapsto u\cdot v_{z,\sigma}$ on $\sigma$. These pieces give the actual support functions of the prescribed sampled fibers of a compact convex hull if and only if
$$
h_{zr}-u_r\cdot v_{z,\sigma}\ge0,\qquad
h_{qr}-\sum_z\lambda_z h_{zr}\ge0
$$
for every relevant $z,\sigma,r$ in the first inequality and every $q,r$ and vertex $\lambda$ of its anchored representation polytope in the second. The supports may be those of lower-dimensional fibers. Denote the resulting linear row matrix by $A$ and the active rows at a feasible array $h$ by $I$.

The radial tangent cone and the velocities at zero of differentiable two-sided feasible paths are respectively $\{v:A_Iv\ge0\}$ and $\{v:A_Iv=0\}$. Every velocity in the latter set is realized by $h+tv$ for both signs of sufficiently small $t$. For such $v$, the path $h+tv+t^2w/2$ is feasible for both signs near zero exactly when $A_Iw\ge0$. If the original fibers have positive $d$-volume, they remain positive in all sufficiently small feasible perturbations. A new facet can appear along a two-sided differentiable path with zero first velocity.

pk-intake-fixed-incidence-diagonal-spect.relation_to_goal: The construction varies actual sector areas in a planar ordinary body. The tested caps exceed the small-cap ceiling and satisfy the cubic inequality.
pk-intake-fixed-incidence-diagonal-spect.statement:
Let $K_t=\operatorname{conv}\{(7-17t,-6+15t),(1,-5),(7,-6),(2,4)\}$ for $9/10\le t\le11/10$. The listed order remains strictly convex and counterclockwise, the origin remains interior, and the three lines through zero with normals $v_1=(1,0),v_2=(0,1),v_3=(-1,-1)$ retain fixed strict vertex incidence. Write $k=|K_t|$, $Q_i=|K_t\cap\{v_i\cdot x\ge0\}|$ and $\sigma_i=\mathcal H^1(K_t\cap\{v_i\cdot x=0\})/\lVert v_i\rVert$. Put $M=\sum_iQ_i/\sigma_i$ and $f_i=2\sqrt{kQ_i}/(\sigma_iM)$. Let $B(f)$ be the symmetric three-by-three matrix with zero diagonal and cyclic off-diagonal entries $f_i/2$, and put $J(K_t)=\lambda_{\max}(B(f))$. For $r=9353/10000$ one has
$$
J(K_{9/10})<r<J(K_1),\qquad J(K_{11/10})<r<J(K_1).
$$
Consequently $J$ is not quasiconvex on this diagonal path and all its maximizers on the displayed compact interval are interior. The three tested bodies each satisfy $\sum_i f_i^2+f_1f_2f_3<4$.

pk-intake-fixed-interval-widths-actual-c.relation_to_goal: Fixed positive concave widths and their true integer-base mixed centroid. An exact optimization representation, with no universal numerical lower bound claimed.
pk-intake-fixed-interval-widths-actual-c.statement:
Let $w_i>0$ be concave on consecutive integer indices $P=\{-L,\ldots,R\}$ containing zero, with $\sum_i iw_i=0$, and let $M=\sum_iw_i$, $Q=\sum_iw_i^2$. Consider all actual compatible interval families $K_i=[r_i-w_i,r_i]$ of these widths with mixed centroid $(0,0)$, using summed length on the sampled fibers. The smallest mixed length in the cap $x\ge0$ is the minimum of finitely many attained linear programs.

For each consecutive block $[p,q]\cap P$ containing zero and each choice of the two outer tails as wholly captured or excluded, impose
$$
\Delta^2 w_i\le\Delta^2 r_i\le0\quad(i\text{ interior}),\qquad
\sum_iw_ir_i=Q/2,
$$
and impose $r_i\le0$ on an excluded tail, $0\le r_i\le w_i$ on the block, and $r_i\ge w_i$ on a captured tail. The objective is $\sum_{p\le i\le q}r_i+\sum_{\text{captured }i}w_i$. Each nonempty program attains its minimum. In every actual family $r_0\ge Q/(2M)$ and $r_0-w_0\le-Q/(2M)$.

pk-intake-fixed-interval-widths-symmetri.relation_to_goal: Symmetric proper block at the true integer-base interval centroid. The signed curvature term is retained outside the convex-order subcase.
pk-intake-fixed-interval-widths-symmetri.statement:
Let actual compatible intervals $[r_i-w_i,r_i]$ have positive widths on consecutive integer indices containing zero, and satisfy $\sum_i iw_i=0$ and $\sum_iw_ir_i=Q/2$, where $M=\sum_iw_i$ and $Q=\sum_iw_i^2$. Suppose the proper block of $x\ge0$ is $I=\{-h,\ldots,h\}$ of size $k=2h+1$, and the wholly captured exterior fibers have total width $T$. For each interior index $j$ put
$$
c_j=-\Delta^2r_j,\quad d_j=-\Delta^2w_j,\quad
\kappa_j=\sum_iw_i(i-j)_+-M(-j)_+,\quad
\tau_j=\sum_{i\in I}(i-j)_+-k(-j)_+.
$$
Then $0\le c_j\le d_j$, both deficits are nonnegative, and the mixed cap length is
$$
F=T+\frac{kQ}{2M}+\sum_j c_j\left[\frac{k}{M}\kappa_j-\tau_j\right]
\ \ge\ T+\frac{kQ}{2M}+\sum_j d_j\min\left\{0,\frac{k}{M}\kappa_j-\tau_j\right\}.
$$
If the width probability law $(w_i/M)_i$ dominates the uniform probability on $I$ in convex order, then $F\ge T+kQ/(2M)$. It suffices that $w_i/M\le1/k$ for each $i\in I$.

pk-intake-fixed-mass-one-copy-source-cos.relation_to_goal: Exact auxiliary continuous cap optimization at a prescribed weighted centroid. The charge includes one copy of the added measure; no mixed-integer allocation or center selection is asserted.
pk-intake-fixed-mass-one-copy-source-cos.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, $B\subset\mathbb R^d$ a compact convex body of positive $d$-volume, $0\le\eta\le\mathbf 1_B\,dx$, and $\alpha=\eta(B)/|B|$. Let $g$ be the centroid of $\mathbf 1_B\,dx+k\eta$. For a closed halfspace $H$ containing $g$, write $v=(|B\cap H|+\eta(H))/|B|$, $q=1+1/d$, and $\gamma_d=q^{-d}$. For real $k\ge1$ and fixed $\alpha\in[0,1]$, the sharp infimum of $v$ over $B,\eta,H$ is the attained minimum of $s+r$ under
$$
0\le s\le1,\quad 0\le r\le\min(\alpha,s),\quad s+\alpha-r\le1,\qquad
q(1+k\alpha)s^{q-1}\ge1+k r^q+k(s+\alpha-r)^q-k s^q.
$$
Every minimizing pair has $0<s<1$ and equality in the last constraint. A simplex with $\eta$ the volume restricted to its upper-tail quantile bands $[0,r]\cup[s,s+\alpha-r]$ attains every such pair. The endpoint optima at $\alpha=0,1$ are $\gamma_d,2\gamma_d$. Equivalently, for $r\in[0,\alpha]$ let $t(r)$ be the unique positive root in $s$ of the last constraint taken at equality, ignoring the other constraints. Minimize $r+\max\{r,t(r)\}$ over those $r$ with $\max\{r,t(r)\}\le1-\alpha+r$.

pk-intake-fixed-normal-mixed-volume-unbo.relation_to_goal: Raw mixed mass and a fixed cap under a feasible support deformation. The calculation does not determine the normalized actual critical circuit Hessian with source relaxation.
pk-intake-fixed-normal-mixed-volume-unbo.statement: For every $d\ge2$ and $N\ge1$ there is an open family of genuine fixed-facet-normal polytopes in $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ with complete positive integer base $\{0,\ldots,N\}$ whose mixed mass has positive-definite Hessian of size $N+1$ in the specified support-offset coordinates. In particular neither one nor the number of base parities bounds its positive index. In the same family, a fixed nonvertical cap's raw Hessian can have this same index even while its normalized cap fraction is constant.

pk-intake-fixed-normal-planar-cap-sectio.relation_to_goal: Ordinary planar Lebesgue area, fixed normals, and the original source at zero.
pk-intake-fixed-normal-planar-cap-sectio.statement: Among the area-one bodies with the fixed normals and cap bounds of the quantitative planar source-ball lemma, impose any further closed condition on the finite vector $(q_i)_i$. The resulting class is Hausdorff compact. If it is nonempty, all functions $\lambda_i=(1/\sigma_i)/\sum_j(1/\sigma_j)$ with $\sigma_i=\mathcal H_1(K\cap u_i^\perp)/\|u_i\|$, and the function $\min_i\lambda_i$, attain their minima. For $u_1=(1,0),u_2=(0,1),u_3=(-1,-1)$ and $c=128/279$, the class with $q_{(1)}+q_{(2)}+q_{(3)}/4\le1$ (increasing rearrangement) is nonempty.

pk-intake-fixed-normal-planar-cap-source.relation_to_goal: Planar Lebesgue area and the original source at zero.
pk-intake-fixed-normal-planar-cap-source.statement:
Let $u_1,\ldots,u_N\in\mathbb R^2\setminus\{0\}$ positively span the plane, let $0<c<1/2$, and let $K$ be a compact convex body of area $k>0$ with $q_i(K)=|K\cap\{u_i\cdot x\ge0\}|\le ck$ for every $i$. Set
$$
\epsilon=1-2c,\qquad
\kappa=\min_{\|e\|=1}\min\{\max_i u_i\cdot e,\max_i(-u_i\cdot e)\},\qquad
T=\max_i\|u_i\|/\kappa.
$$
Then $0\in\operatorname{int}K$, and for $R=\max_{x\in K}\|x\|$ and the origin-centered inradius $\rho$,
$$R^2\le 8Tk/\epsilon,\qquad \rho\ge\epsilon k/(2R),\qquad \rho^2\ge\epsilon^3k/(32T).$$

pk-intake-fixed-normal-tilt-first-and-se.relation_to_goal: Finite convex fibers and one fixed unit continuous normal. The section-area balance uses positive base rank.
pk-intake-fixed-normal-tilt-first-and-se.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty, with a full-dimensional compact convex fiber $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ at each $z\in P$, $d\ge1$. Fix $p\in P$, $y\in\operatorname{int}K_p$, and a unit vector $u\in\mathbb R^d$. Let $L=\operatorname{span}(P-p)$, $v_z=z-p$, $c_z=u\cdot y-a\cdot v_z$ for $a\in L$, and let $F(a)$ be the sum of the volumes of the closed traces $K_z\cap\{u\cdot x\ge c_z\}$. Write $l_z,r_z$ for the support endpoints in direction $u$ and $w_z(s)=\mathcal H^{d-1}(K_z\cap\{u\cdot x=s\})$ on $[l_z,r_z]$.

At tilt $a$, let $I$ be the indices of proper cuts, $E$ those with $c_z=r_z$, and $B$ those with $c_z=l_z$. Put $g=\sum_{z\in I}w_z(c_z)v_z$, $U=\sum_{z\in E}[0,w_z(r_z)v_z]$ and $V=\sum_{z\in B}[0,w_z(l_z)v_z]$, where segment sums are Minkowski sums. For $b_z=h\cdot v_z$, the right derivative is
$$
D^+F(a;h)=g\cdot h+\sum_{z\in E}w_z(r_z)(b_z)_++\sum_{z\in B}w_z(l_z)\min(b_z,0)
=h_{g+U}(h)-h_{-V}(h).
$$
It is nonnegative in every direction exactly when $-V\subseteq g+U$. In positive rank, strict positivity on the unit sphere of $L$ implies a strict local minimum.

A global minimizing tilt can be chosen with a supporting threshold or with $\{v_z:z\in I\}$ spanning $L$. At every support-free local minimum $g=0$. In the spanning alternative with $\dim L>0$, the weights $w_z(c_z)$ on non-own proper fibers normalize to positive coefficients representing $p$ as a convex combination of their bases. Those bases affinely span $p+L$, $p$ is in their relative interior, and the union of supports of the extreme representations on those bases still spans $p+L$.

At a support-free tilt in $d\ge2$, for $t\downarrow0$ the expansion is $F(a+th)=F(a)+t g\cdot h+t^2Q_a(h)/2+o(t^2)$, where
$$
Q_a(h)=-\sum_{\substack{z\in I\\b_z>0}} b_z^2 w'_{z,-}(c_z)
        -\sum_{\substack{z\in I\\b_z<0}} b_z^2 w'_{z,+}(c_z).
$$
A local minimum requires $Q_a(h)\ge0$ for every $h$. If all proper densities are differentiable at their cuts, this is the positive-semidefiniteness on $L$ of $-\sum_{z\in I}w'_z(c_z)v_zv_z^{\mathsf T}$. In $d=1$, $F$ is affine on each support-free trace cell and in positive rank a support-free global minimum can move to a supporting threshold at the same mass.

pk-intake-fixed-positive-family-projecti.relation_to_goal: A conditional attainment for one fixed positive family of arbitrary compact convex fibers. It neither imposes fixed-base shape minimality nor preserves lattice completeness under general projective maps.
pk-intake-fixed-positive-family-projecti.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $P\subset\mathbb R^r$ be finite and affinely spanning, and let $(K_p)_{p\in P}$ be a fixed actual compatible family of positive compact convex $d$-fibers. Translate the base so that $0$ lies in the relative interior of its hull. For affine $L>0$ on $P$, let $D(L)$ be maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth of the unweighted projective image $(p,x)\mapsto(p/L(p),x/L(p))$. Let $h(P)$ denote the Helly number of convex-set traces on $P$ and $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Suppose that for every finite base $Q$ with fewer sites than $P$, every actual positive compatible $d$-fiber family on $Q$ has maximum normalized depth at least $\gamma_d/h(Q)$. Normalize $\sum_{p\in P}L(p)=|P|$. If a sequence $L_j$ tends to a nonnegative boundary array with zero set $F\subset P$, then
$$
\liminf_j D(L_j)\ \ge\ \gamma_d/h(F)\ \ge\ \gamma_d/h(P).
$$
If $D(1)<\gamma_d/h(P)$, the infimum of $D(L)$ over positive affine denominators is attained at a positive denominator and remains strictly below the target. The minimizing image is locally minimal under further positive affine projective changes.

If an actual convex fiber family over $P$ has positive mixed $d$-volume and normalized maximum halfspace depth below $\alpha$, then for some integer $N\ge1$ the class of actual families over $P$ with $|K_{z_0}|=1$ in which every positive-volume fiber is a polytope with at most $N$ facets attains a minimum normalized maximum depth $\beta_N<\alpha$. Its zero-volume fibers may be arbitrary nonempty compact convex sets.

pk-intake-fixed-projection-interior-fibe.statement: Every simultaneous Hausdorff limit of the normalized actual families from the fixed-projection bounded-normalization lemma has central volume one, exact projection onto the same lattice set $P$, and the actual-fiber property. pk-intake-fixed-projection-interior-fibe.statement: Let $d\ge1$, $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty, and $z_0\in P\cap\operatorname{relint}\operatorname{conv}(P)$. Let $(K_z)_{z\in P}$ be nonempty compact convex sets that are the actual fibers of the convex hull of their lifts. If the central volume is already one, the maps can have determinant one. No bounds on other fiber volumes are required.

pk-intake-fixed-residue-low-degree-sampl.relation_to_goal: A continuous polynomial interpolation statement for each fixed residue and only the three specified exponents.
pk-intake-fixed-residue-low-degree-sampl.statement:
Fix $d\in\{1,2,3\}$ and $0\le\rho<1$, and write $x=q+1/2$. Define
$$
\begin{aligned}
P_1(q)&=\tfrac12\bigl(x^2-(\rho-\tfrac12)^2\bigr),\\
P_2(q)&=\tfrac13\bigl(x^3-x/4-c\bigr),\qquad c=\rho^3-\tfrac32\rho^2+\tfrac12\rho,\\
P_3(q)&=\tfrac14\bigl(x^4-x^2/2+1/16-\rho^2(1-\rho)^2\bigr).
\end{aligned}
$$
For every integer $m\ge0$, $P_d(\rho+m)=\sum_{j\ge0}(\rho+m-j)_+^d$. For each fixed $\rho$, the real-variable interpolant $P_d(q)^{1/(d+1)}$ is concave on $q\ge\rho$, including the continuous value zero at $q=0$ for $\rho=0$.

pk-intake-fixed-sector-lorentz-row-quadr.relation_to_goal: An ordinary single-body reduction at fixed cuts and sector areas for one selected row. The row inequality on the resulting polygons and containment of any prescribed neighboring-fiber midpoint set require separate arguments.
pk-intake-fixed-sector-lorentz-row-quadr.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a convex body, $y$ an interior point, and $n_1,n_2,n_3$ fixed spanning normals with $\sum_j n_j=0$. For their three caps $n_j\cdot(x-y)\ge0$ let $q_j$ be the areas, let $k=|K|$, and let $\ell_j$ be the length of the central chord $n_j\cdot(x-y)=0$ divided by $\lVert n_j\rVert$. Write $M=\sum_j q_j/\ell_j$, $f_j=2\sqrt{kq_j}/(\ell_j M)$ and $\Phi_i=f_i+(f_j+f_l)^2/4$ for $\{i,j,l\}=\{1,2,3\}$.

For each selected index $i$, there is a triangle or quadrilateral containing $y$ in its interior, with the same areas in all six sectors of the three fixed lines, whose $\Phi_i$ is at least that of $K$. The polygon can realize an attained global maximum among bodies with these fixed sector areas, preserving all six ray endpoints of the maximizing datum. Different selected rows may use different polygons.

pk-intake-fixed-sector-lorentz-row-singu.relation_to_goal: Attainment and structure for an ordinary planar optimization at six fixed positive sector areas. It leaves the selected-row inequality and mixed-integer depth open.
pk-intake-fixed-sector-lorentz-row-singu.statement:
Use the six cyclic rays with endpoints
$$
(P_0,\ldots,P_5)=((A,0),(0,B),(-t,t),(-a,0),(0,-b),(r,-r)),
\qquad (R_0,\ldots,R_5)=(A,B,t,a,b,r)>0.
$$
Indices on rays and sectors are modulo six. Sector $s$ is the cone between $P_s$ and $P_{s+1}$. A feasible datum $(R,W)$ is realized by an ordinary planar convex body with $0$ in its interior, these boundary ray endpoints and sector areas $W_s$.

Fix six positive sector areas $W_s$ for which at least one feasible radius vector exists.

Put $k=\sum_s W_s$ and let $q_1=W_0+W_4+W_5$, $q_2=W_0+W_1+W_2$, $q_3=W_2+W_3+W_4$ be the areas of the caps $x\ge0$, $y\ge0$, $x+y\le0$, respectively. The corresponding coarea chord lengths are $\ell_1=B+b$, $\ell_2=A+a$, $\ell_3=t+r$. Write
$$
M=\sum_{j=1}^3 q_j/\ell_j,\qquad f_j=\frac{2\sqrt{kq_j}}{\ell_jM},
\qquad \Phi_i=f_i+\frac{(f_j+f_l)^2}{4},\quad \{i,j,l\}=\{1,2,3\}.
$$

Set $c_s=1/(2W_s)$ and $h_s=1/(R_sR_{s+1})-c_s$. A core sector has $h_s=0$. Define the symmetric matrix $L$ by $L_{ss}=c_{s-1}+c_s-R_s^{-2}$, $L_{s,s+1}=L_{s+1,s}=-h_s$ and all other off-diagonal entries zero. Its connected blocks are on the components of the graph with edges $s,s+1$ when $h_s>0$.

The feasible radius set is compact, with $(c_{s-1}+c_s)^{-1/2}\le R_s\le 2W_s\sqrt{c_s+c_{s+1}}$, and each selected row $\Phi_i$ attains a maximum. At any local maximum with $W$ fixed, the following hold.

- There are at least two cores. Both endpoints of every chord with positive derivative $\partial_{\ell_j}\Phi_i$ are incident to a core. If all three chord derivatives vanish, every endpoint is incident to a core and there are at least three cores.
- Every positive-definite connected block has at most two nodes. At least two connected blocks are singular, so $\dim\ker L\ge2$.
- If there are exactly two cores, the datum has a unique realizing body. It is a quadrilateral with one vertex strictly inside each of the four positive-excess sectors.

pk-intake-fixed-sector-spectral-cubic-qu.relation_to_goal: An ordinary fixed-sector reduction for the spectral objective and an exact conditional quadrilateral witness under the cap ceiling.
pk-intake-fixed-sector-spectral-cubic-qu.statement: Let $K$ be a planar convex body with interior mark $y$ and spanning normals $v_1,v_2,v_3$ with $v_1+v_2+v_3=0$. Let $q_i$ be the areas of the caps $v_i\cdot(x-y)\ge0$, let $\ell_i$ be their chord lengths divided by $\lVert v_i\rVert$, and let $k=|K|$. Put $M=\sum_i q_i/\ell_i$ and $f_i=2\sqrt{kq_i}/(\ell_iM)$. Let $B(f)$ be the symmetric three-by-three matrix with zero diagonal and cyclic off-diagonal entries $f_i/2$, and write $J=\lambda_{\max}(B(f))$. Over ordinary convex bodies with these same lines, mark and six positive sector areas, $J$ attains its maximum. Every maximizing ray datum has at least two core sectors and at least two singular connected blocks in the prescribed-sector matrix. Thus some triangle or quadrilateral with these same sector areas attains the maximum. If $J>1$ and $q_i/k\le128/279$ for all $i$ on the original body, there is a quadrilateral with the same areas and $J>1$.

pk-intake-fixed-simplex-cap-threshold-va.relation_to_goal: Fixed proper barycentric caps on a physical simplex. The groups need not be concurrent, and no sign is asserted for signed multipliers or moving thresholds.
pk-intake-fixed-simplex-cap-threshold-va.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $m=d+1$, and let the reference labeled simplex of volume $V>0$ have vertex matrix $I$ in barycentric coordinates. In each direction $i$, take finitely many fixed proper caps $\xi_i\ge a_{gi}$, $0<a_{gi}<1$, with multipliers $\ell_{gi}\ge0$. For column-sum-one $W$ near $I$, let $F_{gi}(W)$ be the actual cap volumes and $L(W)=V\det W-\sum_{gi}\ell_{gi}F_{gi}(W)$. Define
$$
X_{gi}=\frac1{1-a_{gi}},\quad \eta_{gi}=\ell_{gi}(1-a_{gi})^d,\quad
e_i=\sum_g\eta_{gi},\quad \chi_i=d\sum_g\eta_{gi}(X_{gi}-1).
$$
The Lagrangian is stationary over all physical vertex velocities if and only if $e_i=e>0$ and $\chi_i=1-de$ at every $i$. In this case $0<e<1/d$ and the distributions with weights $\eta_{gi}/e$ have common mean $\mu=1/(de)$ in $X$. The single-threshold model with threshold $a_*=1-1/\mu=1-de$ at every vertex and multiplier $e/(1-a_*)^d$ has the same first derivative as the multigroup Lagrangian. Let $Q_*(B)$ be its normalized Hessian, and let $\sigma_i^2=\operatorname{Var}_i(X)$ under the vertex $i$ weights. For each zero-column-sum $B$,
$$Q_{\mathrm{multi}}(B):=\frac{D^2 L(I)[B,B]}{V}
=Q_*(B)-d(d-1)e\sum_i\sigma_i^2 B_{ii}^2.$$
The correction is zero exactly when $B_{ii}=0$ for every $i$ with $\sigma_i^2>0$. With $b_i=B_{ii}$, $A$ the off-diagonal part of $B$, $s_i=\sum_{j\ne i}A_{ij}$, and $T=\operatorname{tr}B$, the effective Hessian is
$$
Q_*(B)=T^2-\operatorname{tr}(B^2)-e\sum_i
\left([T+s_i+d(\mu-1)b_i]^2-\operatorname{tr}(B^2)-d\mu^2 b_i^2+\sum_{j\ne i}(b_i-A_{ij})^2\right).
$$

pk-intake-fixed-simplex-core-uniform-nea.relation_to_goal: An explicit fixed-core small-mass bound and a uniform directional pair estimate for all opposite shifts.
pk-intake-fixed-simplex-core-uniform-nea.statement:
Let $n\ge1$ and $d\ge2$. A compact convex body has the same full-dimensional simplex $T$ of volume $V$ at every binary base, and outside integer fibers of total $d$-volume $E$. In standard simplex coordinates put $b=1/(d+1)$, $\Gamma=(1-b)^d$, $\tau=1-2b$, and $\eta=\tau/(16\sqrt d)$. Let $g$ be the centroid, $\theta_i$ the unit normals in the directions of the barycentric gradients, and $F(u)=|T\cap\{u\cdot(x-g)\ge0\}|/V$ on the unit sphere. Define $G_d=\min_{\min_i\lVert u-\theta_i\rVert\ge\eta}(F(u)-\Gamma)>0$ on that sphere.

If $(E/V)^{1/d}\le\tau/4$, then for every outside positive fiber $A\subseteq T$, every unit $u$ within $\eta$ of a canonical $\theta_i$, and every pair of thresholds with sum $2u\cdot g$, the two upper caps in $A$ and $T$ have combined mass at least $|A|$. If moreover
$$
E/V\le\min\{2^{-d-1},(\tau/4)^d,G_d/\Gamma\},
$$
then some binary core centroid has raw closed ambient halfspace depth at least $\Gamma(2^nV+E)/2^n$. The mass threshold is independent of $n$. For an affine image of the standard simplex the normal neighborhood is interpreted after mapping the continuous coordinates to the standard simplex.

For every $0\le\sigma\le\mathbf 1_C dx$ of mass $aV$, put

The continuous allocations can be nonunique. Geometrically normalizing $\ell$ rescales both tilted marginals by the same factor and preserves the fractions and original-volume weights.

x\ge y+t(z-p)-\delta_p(y),\qquad x\le y+t(z-p)+\delta_p(y)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R)

and the unshifted closed pure-base caps containing $p$. pk-intake-fractional-signed-exponential-.relation_to_goal: Two sign limits for an explicit balanced scalar family.
pk-intake-fractional-signed-exponential-.statement:
For integers $k,m\ge1$, let $X_k\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(k,1)$ and $Y_m\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(m,1)$. Let $E_+,E_-$ be unit-mean exponentials, with all four variables independent. For $p\in[0,1]$ and $b=(k+p-1)/m\in[0,1]$, set
$$
V_{k,m,p}=X_k+pE_+-E_--bY_m,\qquad
G_{k,p}=\Pr(X_k+pE_+\ge E_-+k+p-1).
$$
The variance of $V_{k,m,p}$ is $\sigma^2=k+p^2+1+mb^2$ and lies in $[k+1,2(k+1)]$. As $k\to\infty$, the probability $\Pr(V_{k,m,p}\ge0)$ tends to $1/2$ uniformly over the admissible $m,p$. For fixed $k$, if $m_j\to\infty$ and $p_j\to p\in[0,1]$ along admissible parameters, then $\Pr(V_{k,m_j,p_j}\ge0)\to G_{k,p}$.

pk-intake-fractional-two-negative-expone.relation_to_goal: A balanced signed exponential law with at most two strictly negative phases, a fixed unit negative coefficient, and every positive coefficient at most one.

$$
\Pr\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^k p_iE_i\ge E_0+cE_*\right)\ge\frac12 .
$$
The bound is attained by the nonzero positive list $(1,c)$, with $c$ omitted if it is zero.

pk-intake-framed-whole-space-cover-norma.relation_to_goal: Fixed polytopal source and fixed cap count. Every frame cap is included in the optimization, with free tilts and offsets, and whole-space contacts may lie outside the source.
pk-intake-framed-whole-space-cover-norma.statement:
Take the framed whole-space cover problem above with $m=N+2d$ caps, the $N$ variable normals constrained to the unit sphere and the $2d$ frame normals fixed at $+e_l,-e_l$. All offsets and base tilts are free, and the full-dimensional source fibers are polytopes. Let $w(\tau)$ be the attained minimum total hinge at budget $c_i\le\tau M$. Its feasible domain is upward closed. On the interior of its feasible domain the value is $C^1$ except at finitely many budgets. At every budget in the remaining interior and for every minimizer, there is normal stationarity with objective multiplier one and nonnegative multipliers $r_i,\eta_z$ satisfying
$$
r_i(c_i-\tau M)=0,\qquad \eta_zF_z=0,\qquad M\sum_i r_i=-w'(\tau).
$$
For each cap, write $Z_i,X_i$ for the first moments of its source mass in $z,x$. Write $S_i,Z_i^s,X_i^s$ for consistent mass and first moments on its source sections $K_z\cap\{L_i(z,\cdot)=0\}$, with $\mathcal H_{d-1}$ density in $[0,1]$, equal to one almost everywhere on proper sections, and such that $(Z_i^s,X_i^s,-S_i)$ is a consistent Clarke cap-mass gradient in full affine cap parameters. For each active fiber margin with positive $\eta_z$ use a finitely supported probability measure $\nu_z$ on optimal whole-space LP saddle pairs $(x,\lambda)$, with $p_{zi}=\int\lambda_i\,d\nu_z$ and $q_{zi}=\int\lambda_i x\,d\nu_z$. Each pair satisfies $\sum_i\lambda_i u_i=0$, $L_i(z,x)\le0$, $\lambda_i L_i(z,x)=0$; the point $x$ is in $\mathbb R^d$. With terms of zero multiplier omitted, for every cap
$$
W_i:=c_i+r_i S_i=\sum_z\eta_z p_{zi},\qquad
Z_i+r_i Z_i^s=\sum_z\eta_z z p_{zi},
$$
and for each variable-normal cap
$$
X_i+r_i X_i^s-\sum_z\eta_z q_{zi}=\Psi_i u_i.
$$
In particular, with all sums running over both types of cap,
$$
\sum_i W_i u_i=0,\qquad
\sum_i u_i(Z_i+r_i Z_i^s)^T=0,\qquad
\sum_i W_i=\sum_z\eta_z,\qquad

pk-intake-full-log-parameter-contact-cov.relation_to_goal: A finite actual cover and moving-cover prerequisite for the independently chosen positive logarithmic parameter. It supplies no depth constant.
pk-intake-full-log-parameter-contact-cov.statement:

Compatibility means $\sum_z\lambda_zK_z\subset K_p$ whenever $\sum_z\lambda_zz=p\in P$ is a convex combination. Write $C_z$ for the fiber of $C$ at any real base $z$ and $\Gamma(u)=\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma u}$ for the pooled within-fiber covariance norm. Let $L>0$ be a finite minimum of affine functions on a neighborhood of $C$, with $\int\log L\,dm=0$. Put $N=d+1$ and $f(z,x)=(L(z,x) E_{C_z}(x)/M)^{1/N}$, using zero own-boundary projective energy. The profile is continuous and jointly concave on $C$, strictly concave on own interiors and positive precisely there. For an own-interior sampled mark $Y=(p,y)$, let $F=E_{C_z}(x)^{1/d}$ and $a_E$ be the minimizing projective parameter at $Y$. Every own supergradient of $f$ at $Y$ is $g=f(Y)a_E+f(Y)c/(NL(Y))$ for an own slope $c$ of a convex combination of the active affine $L$-planes. If $\alpha_L$ is the base slope of that combination and $(\alpha_F,\nabla_x F(Y))$ a full supergradient of $F$, then $(\alpha,g)$ is a full supergradient of $f$, with $\alpha=f(Y)\alpha_L/(NL(Y))+d f(Y)\alpha_F/(NF(Y))$.

Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and define buffered cap depth using threshold $a\cdot p+u\cdot y-\varepsilon\Gamma(u)f(p,y)$ for nonzero $u$ and unchanged closed pure-base caps. Let $Q$ be the maximum raw depth on sampled fibers and $I$ its deepest bases. Assume every deepest mark has own-interior distance $>\varepsilon f(Y)\sqrt{\lambda_{\max}(\Sigma)}$. Then $I$ is lattice-complete and admits a covering by at most $k(I)\le k(P)$ groups, with $k$ counting inherited parities. For each group $i$ there is an inclusion-maximal face $F_i$ of $\operatorname{conv}I$ among those with a sampled point in their relative interior. Assign it the finite set $J_i=I\cap F_i$, allowing overlaps. There are at most $d+1$ actual mass-$Q$ caps $N_{ij}\cdot w\ge c_{ij}$ in each group, with $\Gamma(u_{ij})=1$, right $Q$-quantile thresholds and positive weights $\rho_{ij}$ summing to one. Put $h_i=\sum_j\rho_{ij}c_{ij}$. The margin $\sum_j\rho_{ij}N_{ij}\cdot w-h_i-\varepsilon f(w)$ is nonnegative throughout every whole real fiber over $F_i$. On each sampled assigned fiber it has exactly one zero, at the own-interior deepest mark, where all selected quantiles are active.

Now move the compatible positive fibers on the same bases by $K_z(t)\to K_z$ in Hausdorff distance. Let $L_t$ be positive on the new hull, continuous there, and converge to $L$ on matched sampled marks uniformly. Let $N_{ij}(t)\to N_{ij}$ and $\varepsilon(t)\to\varepsilon$ be the current normals and scale, use the actual updated mass and covariance, and put $f_t=(L_t E_t/M_t)^{1/N}$ and $A_i(t)=\sum_j\rho_{ij}\Gamma_t(u_{ij}(t))$. Define
$$
\alpha_i(t)=\min_{z\in J_i,\ x\in K_z(t)}\left[\sum_j\rho_{ij}N_{ij}(t)\cdot(z,x)-h_i-\varepsilon(t)A_i(t)f_t(z,x)\right].
$$
All minimizers approach the finite old zeros. If the current objective is the one along the signed paths in 5fa497a06b11cbcb with $\varepsilon(t)=\varepsilon e^{st}$, its first coefficient is the minimum of their $A_{ia}-s\varepsilon f(Y_{ia})$. $$
\sum_j\lambda_{sj}\ell_{sj}(z,x)=a_s\cdot z-h_s,\qquad h_s<\beta_s.

If all $\mu(H_{sj})<T$ for $T>0$, then $\bigcup_jH_{sj}$ contains the whole continuous plane over every base in the basin of $p_s$, including the root. If $B_s$ is the set of basin bases in $P$, then
