pk-intake-intrinsic-mixed-half-depth-rig.relation_to_goal: Positive-dimensional intrinsic mixed traces with actual integer-base centers. The counting example establishes the limit of the characterization.
pk-intake-intrinsic-mixed-half-depth-rig.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact and convex, let $\Lambda=\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, and suppose $S=C\cap\Lambda$ has Hausdorff dimension $q>0$. Write $\mu=\mathcal H_q|_S$ and $M=\mu(S)>0$. For any actual $y=(j,c)\in S$, the following are equivalent.

1. Every closed ambient halfspace containing $y$ has $\mu$-mass at least $M/2$.
2. The angular pushforward of $\mu$ about $y$ is antipodally invariant.
3. Reflection about $y$ preserves $\mu$.
4. $\mathcal H_q(S\cap(2y-S))=M$.

When these hold, every positive $q$-dimensional fiber has its exact reflected partner, the fiber at $j$ is itself positive and centrally symmetric about $c$, $y$ is the full ambient centroid, and its normalized depth is $1/2$. The conclusions refer to the measured fibers and allow unmatched $\mathcal H_q$-null fibers. For counting measure the implication from half depth to symmetry can fail.

pk-intake-intrinsic-parity-fiber-directi.relation_to_goal: Intrinsic geometry within a single input parity. It does not impose parallelism across all sampled fibers.
pk-intake-intrinsic-parity-fiber-directi.statement: Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body with nonempty mixed trace $S$ and $q=\dim_H S>0$. In one base parity class let two finite nonnegative measures have positive mass and be absolutely continuous with respect to $\mathcal H^q|_S$. All input fibers of positive mass on either side have one common $q$-dimensional direction $L$. For any product pair of these input bases $z,w$, the midpoint base $p=(z+w)/2$ is sampled and the actual fiber $C_p$ has dimension $q$ and direction $L$. Writing each input affine hull as $b_z+L$ with $b_z\in L^\perp$, the perpendicular offset of $C_p$ is $(b_z+b_w)/2$ and depends only on $p$ within that class.

pk-intake-intrinsic-parity-reflection-co.relation_to_goal: Exact ordered, independent same-parity product law for compact convex mixed traces, including counting and varying intrinsic directions across parities.
pk-intake-intrinsic-parity-reflection-co.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact and convex with nonempty $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$, $q=\dim_H S$, $\mu=\mathcal H_q|_S$ and $M=\mu(S)>0$. For each represented positive-mass base parity $r$, let $S_r$ be the trace in that parity and let $\mu_r=\mu|_{S_r}$, $M_r=\mu_r(S)$, $m_r=\int y\,d\mu_r$, $g_r=m_r/M_r$, and $Q_r=\int yy^{\mathsf T}\,d\mu_r$. All coordinates are full ambient coordinates. Let $T(a,b)=(a+b)/2$, $R(y)=\mathcal H_q(S\cap(2y-S))$ and $R_r(y)=\mathcal H_q(S_r\cap(2y-S_r))$ for actual $y\in S$. Then
$$
R_r\mu=2^{-q}T_\#(\mu_r\otimes\mu_r),\qquad
R\mu=2^{-q}\sum_r T_\#(\mu_r\otimes\mu_r).
$$
These are finite Borel measure identities, including counting measure at $q=0$. For any two $q$-dimensional integer fibers of the same base parity, their directions coincide with that of the actual midpoint fiber, and its affine hull is the midpoint of their affine hulls. At an actual center with base $j$, $R$ is the sum of the overlaps over ordered $q$-dimensional fiber pairs with bases adding to $2j$. In particular $R$ vanishes at centers on smaller-dimensional fibers.

Write $A=\sum_r M_r^2$. The full moments satisfy
$$
\begin{aligned}
\int R\,d\mu&=2^{-q}A,\\
\int yR(y)\,d\mu(y)&=2^{-q}\sum_r M_r m_r,\\
\int yy^{\mathsf T}R(y)\,d\mu(y)
&=2^{-q-1}\sum_r(M_r Q_r+m_r m_r^{\mathsf T}).
\end{aligned}
$$
The probability law $\eta=(2^q/A)R\mu$ selects parity $r$ with probability $M_r^2/A$ and takes the midpoint of two independent draws from $\mu_r/M_r$. It has centroid $\sum_r M_r^2g_r/A$, which can differ from the centroid of $\mu/M$. It has the same centroid as $\nu=A^{-1}\sum_r M_r\mu_r$, and $\int\varphi\,d\eta\le\int\varphi\,d\nu$ for convex Borel $\varphi$ on $\operatorname{conv}(S)$ with both integrals defined. With $V_r=\int(y-g_r)(y-g_r)^{\mathsf T}\,d\mu_r(y)$, the covariance difference is $\operatorname{Cov}(\nu)-\operatorname{Cov}(\eta)=(2A)^{-1}\sum_r M_rV_r\succeq0$.

pk-intake-intrinsic-parity-variable-midp.relation_to_goal: Intrinsic Hausdorff-measure transport capacities on a mixed trace, including degenerate traces. These are not halfspace-depth constants.
pk-intake-intrinsic-parity-variable-midp.statement:
Let $n,d\ge0$, let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, and let $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\ne\varnothing$, $q=\dim_H S$ and $\mu=\mathcal H^q|_S$ (counting measure for $q=0$). Let $\gamma_-,\gamma_+$ be finite nonnegative measures of equal mass supported on $S$, and let $\Xi_{\rm old}$ be a coupling whose midpoints belong to $S$ almost everywhere. Assume $\gamma_i\le a_i\mu$ for bounded nonnegative upper semicontinuous $a_i$ on the compact supports $E_i=\operatorname{supp}\gamma_i$. Let $E_{i,r}$ and $\gamma_{i,r}$ denote the restrictions to original base parity $r$. For $q\ge1$ put $H_q(t,s)=((t^{-1/q}+s^{-1/q})/2)^{-q}$ on positive arguments and zero if either vanishes. Put $H_0(t,s)=\min(t,s)$. Define on the physical space
$$
c_r(w)=\max_{\substack{u\in E_{-,r},\,v\in E_{+,r}\\(u+v)/2=w}} H_q(a_-(u),a_+(v)),
$$
with the empty maximum zero. Then each $c_r$ is bounded and upper semicontinuous. There is one coupling of the original marginals whose classwise midpoint laws satisfy $\rho_{{\rm old},r}\preceq_{\rm cx}\rho_r\le c_r\mu$ in full physical coordinates, and whose classwise endpoint marginals are $\gamma_{-,r},\gamma_{+,r}$. Its total midpoint law satisfies $\rho\le(\sum_r c_r)\mu$. For fiberwise constant ceilings $c_r(p,x)$ is bounded by the maximum of $H_q$ over positive class-$r$ input base pairs summing to $2p$.

In particular, for unit ceilings let $D_r=(E_{-,r}+E_{+,r})/2$. Then $\rho_r\le\mathbf1_{D_r}\mu$ and $\rho\le\kappa\mu$ with $\kappa(w)=\#\{r:w\in D_r\}\le2^n$. At a boundary base $p$ of the projection of $C$, any supporting affine hyperplane $A$ gives $\kappa(p,x)\le 2^{\operatorname{rank}(\mathbb Z^n\cap\operatorname{dir}A)}$. If $q<d$ then $n\ge1$ and $\kappa\le2^{n-1}$ on $S$. The uniform constants $2^n$ for $q=d$ and $2^{n-1}$ for $q<d$ are sharp.

pk-intake-intrinsic-real-moment-cap.relation_to_goal: Realizes every feasible prescribed mass and real base moment of the positive intrinsic mixed measure by one actual cap, including a prescribed integer base centroid when feasible. The locked conjecture additionally requires an integer mark with a uniform lower bound against every closed halfspace.
pk-intake-intrinsic-real-moment-cap.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$ be integers, let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body, and put $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. For $z\in\mathbb Z^n$ set $K_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$. Assume that the maximum affine dimension $q$ of the nonempty integer fibers satisfies $1\le q\le d$. Set $\mu=\mathcal H_q|_S$, and for
$$
P=\{z:\dim K_z=q\},\qquad w_z=\mathcal H_q(K_z),\qquad v_z=(1,z),
$$
write $Z=\sum_{z\in P}[0,w_z]v_z$. The set $Z$ is exactly the set of pairs $(\eta(S),\int_S z\,d\eta)$ for positive measures $0\le\eta\le\mu$.

Fix any $u\in\mathbb R^d$ such that $x\mapsto u\cdot x$ is nonconstant on $\operatorname{aff}K_z$ for every $z\in P$. Such $u$ exist, and if $q=d$ every nonzero $u$ qualifies. For every $r\in Z$ there are finite $b\in\mathbb R$ and $a\in\mathbb R^n$ such that the single closed halfspace
$$
H=\{(z,x)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d:b+a\cdot z+u\cdot x\ge0\}
$$
satisfies $\mu(\partial H)=0$ and $(\mu(H),\int_H z\,d\mu)=r$. This includes the zero and full-mass targets and arbitrary real first moments.

If the mass $t$ of $r$ is positive, $D=C\cap H$ is a convex body with maximum integer-fiber dimension $q$ and $\mathcal H_q|_{D\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)}=\mu|_H$. If $r=(t,tj)$ with $j\in\mathbb Z^n$, the barycenter of this unweighted intrinsic measure belongs to $D\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$ and $D_j=\{x:(j,x)\in D\}$ has positive $\mathcal H_q$ measure. In particular, for an integer $j$, if
$$
T_j=\max\left\{\sum_{z\in P}s_z:0\le s_z\le w_z,\quad \sum_{z\in P}(z-j)s_z=0\right\}>0 ,
$$
then $T_j$ is the maximum mass of a dominated submeasure with base barycenter $j$ and also the maximum retained mass of a convex subbody of $C$ with that base barycenter, measured using the original exponent $q$. A single cap with the prescribed direction $u$ attains both maxima.

pk-intake-intrinsic-reflection-retention.relation_to_goal: A depth certificate at reflection centers and a weak intrinsic retention bound.
pk-intake-intrinsic-reflection-retention.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact and convex with nonempty $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$, $q=\dim_H S$, $\mu=\mathcal H_q|_S$ and $M=\mu(S)>0$. Write $M_r$ for the masses in the $p$ represented positive-mass base parities. The function $R(y)=\mathcal H_q(S\cap(2y-S))$ is upper semicontinuous on $S$ and attains its maximum $R_{\max}$ there. Every maximizer lies in a $q$-dimensional integer fiber and
$$
R_{\max}\ge \frac{\sum_r M_r^2}{2^q M}\ge\frac{M}{2^q p}\ge\frac{M}{2^{n+q}}.
$$
At every actual $y\in S$, each closed ambient halfspace containing $y$ has $\mu$-mass at least $R(y)/2$. In particular the normalized depth at a reflection maximizer is at least $\sum_r M_r^2/(2^{q+1}M^2)\ge2^{-(n+q+1)}$.

pk-intake-intrinsic-relative-residual-af.relation_to_goal: An explicit sufficient subcover certificate from relative errors at every positive intrinsic fiber.
pk-intake-intrinsic-relative-residual-af.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body with nonempty mixed set $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$, and write $C_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$. Put $q=\dim_H S\ge1$, $V_z=\mathcal H_q(C_z)$, $P=\{z\in\mathbb Z^n:V_z>0\}$, $M=\mathcal H_q(S)=\sum_{z\in P}V_z$, and let $k$ count the occupied coordinate parity classes of $P$. Fix finitely many original closed ambient halfspaces $H_i$ and an integer $t\ge1$. The mass of a cap is $\mathcal H_q(S\cap H_i)$.

Among affine functions $L$ on $\operatorname{aff}(P)$ with $L(z)\ge V_z^{1/q}$ on $P$, define the normalized minimum
$$
A_q(P,V)=\frac{1}{M}\min_L\sum_{z\in P}L(z)^q.
$$
It is attained, its sampled value vector is unique when $q>1$, and $1\le A_q(P,V)\le |P|\max_{z\in P}V_z/M$. One has $A_q(P,V)=1$ exactly when the volume roots are affine on $P$. If each $z\in P$ admits at most $t$ original caps with residual measure at most $\tau V_z$ for $\tau\ge0$, then at most $kt$ original caps leave total residual at most $\tau A_q(P,V)M$. Any nonnegative common cap mass bound $B$ satisfies $B\ge(1-\tau A_q(P,V))M/(kt)$. For $t=2$, $q=d$, the condition $\tau A_d(P,V)\le1-2\gamma_d$ gives $B\ge\gamma_dM/k$, where $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. In particular, the condition for equal-volume planar fibers is $\tau\le1/9$.

pk-intake-intrinsic-variable-shape-extra.relation_to_goal: Maximization of retained intrinsic mass for a fixed original body and true integer centroid base, with a prescribed local-depth threshold.
pk-intake-intrinsic-variable-shape-extra.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be an ambient convex body, with $q=\dim_H(C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d))>0$. Use the measure $\mu_D=\mathcal H^q|_{D\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)}$ for each ambient convex body $D\subseteq C$, with mass $m_D$ and true ambient centroid $g_D$ when $m_D>0$. Write $P=\{z:\mathcal H^q(C_z)>0\}$. Fix a depth threshold $\beta$. Among positive-mass bodies $D$ with integer centroid base $j$ and $\mu_D(H)\ge\beta m_D$ for every closed ambient halfspace $H\ni g_D$, the maximum of $m_D$ is attained if the feasible class is nonempty. This holds separately at each fixed feasible $j$.

Every such $j$ belongs to $P$, the positive $q$-volume fibers of any feasible $D$ have a common $q$-dimensional direction space, and at base $j$ their total mass is bounded above by
$
\max\left\{\sum_{z\in P}t_z:0\le t_z\le\mathcal H^q(C_z),\ \sum_{z\in P}(z-j)t_z=0\right\}.
$
For $\beta=\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, each $j\in P$ is feasible with retained mass $\mathcal H^q(C_j)$.

pk-intake-inverse-arm-two-contact-lemma.relation_to_goal: A conditional one-dimensional support lemma for a prescribed dual potential and prescribed complementarity. No global profile multiplier or attainment hypothesis is supplied by it.
pk-intake-inverse-arm-two-contact-lemma.statement:
Let $J$ be an open bounded interval in $(0,\infty)$, let $A$ be a finite concave function on $J$, and let $w:J\to(0,\infty)$ be continuous. Suppose $H\in C^2(J)$ has one fixed sign and
$$
H''(v)=w(v)[av+b+cA(v)],\qquad \operatorname{supp}(-A'')\subseteq\{H=0\}.
$$
If $c\ne0$, or if $c=0$ and $av+b$ is a nonzero affine function, then the curvature measure $-A''$ is supported on at most two points in $J$.

pk-intake-inverse-power-contact-marginal.relation_to_goal: All marginals are ordinary continuous integrals. The surviving negative-power and quasiconcavity inequalities concern the real projection of the contact set.
pk-intake-inverse-power-contact-marginal.statement:
Let $f$ be bounded, positive and continuous on a bounded open convex set $D$ and zero off $D$, and suppose $f^{-1/\beta}$ is convex on $D$ for $\beta\ge1$. Integrating out one coordinate yields a bounded, positive and continuous function $F$ on the open projected set, extended by zero off it. If $\beta>1$, $F^{-1/(\beta-1)}$ is convex there. If $\beta=1$, $F$ is quasiconcave there.

Let a compact convex flattened contact set have tangent dimension $m=d-1\ge1$, with at least one positive $m$-volume tangent fiber and positive affine $H=H(z)$ and $L=L(z,\xi)$ on the whole set. The weight $f=HL^{-m-1}$ has jointly convex inverse power $f^{-1/m}=H(L/H)^{(m+1)/m}$. Integrating out $r<m$ orthonormal tangent coordinates gives a marginal with convex inverse power $-1/(m-r)$ in the interior of its projection, taken relative to the base affine span and the remaining tangent coordinates. The full tangent marginal is quasiconcave on the real base, including boundary bases with positive fiber mass. If $H$ is constant, the initial exponent improves to $-1/(m+1)$ and the full tangent marginal has convex reciprocal on the set where it is positive.

pk-intake-inverse-power-convex-decreasin.relation_to_goal: Ordinary continuous rearrangement lemma for bounded compactly supported inverse-power minorants.
pk-intake-inverse-power-convex-decreasin.statement: Let $d\ge1$, $p>0$, and let $g$ be a bounded nonnegative measurable density of compact support in $\mathbb R^d$ with positive integral. Suppose $h=g^{-1/p}$, with value $+\infty$ where $g=0$, is convex. Then the symmetric decreasing rearrangement $g^*$ admits an equimeasurable representative with convex extended inverse $p$th root that is radial and nondecreasing in radius. In particular $\int g^*=\int g$. If $g\le f$ almost everywhere for a radially nonincreasing nonnegative $f$, then $g^*\le f$ almost everywhere.

pk-intake-inverse-power-density-centerpo.relation_to_goal: Continuous Lebesgue densities with a specified convex inverse power. The statement concerns the maximum depth in one continuous space.
pk-intake-inverse-power-density-centerpo.statement: Let $r\ge1$ be an integer. Let $f$ be a bounded nonnegative upper-semicontinuous density of compact support in $\mathbb R^r$. Assume $\{f>0\}$ has nonempty interior and the function $f^{-1/(r+1)}$, extended by $+\infty$ where $f=0$, is convex. Then there is a point $y$ in the interior of the support of $f$ such that every closed halfspace containing $y$ has $f$-mass at least $\gamma_r\int f$, where $\gamma_r=(r/(r+1))^r$. The constant is sharp.

pk-intake-inverse-power-density-global-e.relation_to_goal: Ordinary Lebesgue densities. Supplies the global envelope and radial finiteness used at the critical exponent.
pk-intake-inverse-power-density-global-e.statement:
Let $r\ge1$, $\beta\ge r+1$, and let $f:\mathbb R^r\to[0,\infty]$ be a measurable density of mass $M\in(0,\infty)$ with full-dimensional positive support. Assume $g=f^{-1/\beta}$ with value $+\infty$ where $f=0$ is convex, interpreting $g=0$ where $f=+\infty$. For every $y\in\operatorname{int}\{f>0\}$ there exist $C,c,\delta>0$ such that
$$
f(x)\le C(1+\|x-y\|)^{-\beta}\quad(x\in\mathbb R^r),\qquad
f(x)\ge c\quad(\|x-y\|<\delta).
$$
In particular $f$ has no infinite point values, and the integrals $\int_0^\infty t^{r-1}f(y+tu)\,dt$ have a positive lower bound and a finite upper bound uniform over unit directions $u$.

pk-intake-inverse-power-tangent-remainde.statement: For every real $r>0$ define $D_r(x)=x^{-r}-1+r(x-1)$ for $x>0$. The ratio $D_{r+1}(x)/D_r(x)$, continuously extended at $x=1$, is strictly decreasing on $(0,\infty)$, with value $(r+2)/r$ at $1$ and limit $(r+1)/r$ at infinity.

pk-intake-irreducible-circuit-sole-secti.relation_to_goal: No internal cancellation in one limiting full-rank irreducible group, under a stated normal restriction. It does not assert that a selected limit retains full rank or that the reserve holds after splitting a cap law.
pk-intake-irreducible-circuit-sole-secti.statement:
Let one finite limiting actual cap law have weights $\theta_H>0$ summing to one and allocated section-log defects $s_H$ on the physical sampled set. Suppose its nonzero continuous normals $u_H$ form an irreducible positive dependence of full rank $d\ge2$, and fix $c\ne0$ such that $s_H\ne0$ implies $u_H\parallel c$. Then at most one index $E$ has $u_E\parallel c$. The total vector section correction is $\theta_Eu_Es_E$ if that index exists and is zero otherwise. When $E$ exists it vanishes as a vector measure only if $s_E=0$.

The normal hypothesis holds in the finite-plane section classification when the actual limiting contact rows have one surviving continuous slope $c$ and every retained limiting affine component touches at an own-fiber interior mark. In that case each affected fiber has a zero supporting face on the cap plane, and the signs of the proportionality to $c$ distinguish inside from outside support.

pk-intake-isolated-facet-signed-realizat.relation_to_goal: A sufficient two-direction isolation condition at one facet normal. Other normals and contact-constrained facets need no freedom assumption.
pk-intake-isolated-facet-signed-realizat.statement: Use the compatible sampled family of the complete signed global-cut theorem. At a unit normal $u$, say that $z$ is forced for $q$ if an anchored convex representation $\sum_w\lambda_w w=q$ has $\lambda_z>0$ and $\sum_w\lambda_w h_{K_w}(u)=h_{K_q}(u)$. Suppose $K_p$ is a polytope, $F$ is its facet of outward unit normal $u_0$, and at $u_0$ no $z\ne p$ is forced for $p$ and $p$ is forced for no $q\ne p$. Then for each finite continuous convex $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ an actual complete signed-cut path has signed inward speed $\phi(X)$ on $\operatorname{relint}F$ and zero surface-almost everywhere on all remaining sampled boundary. In particular the two parallel speeds $1,-1$ are realized. When $d\ge2$, so is the outward centroid-pyramid speed $-T$. Their finite nonnegative combinations are also realized.

pk-intake-isolated-interior-point-planar.relation_to_goal: A classification for actual full planar lattice traces and the distinct-endpoint midpoint relation.
pk-intake-isolated-interior-point-planar.statement: Let $R$ be a two-dimensional lattice polygon, $T=R\cap\mathbb Z^2$, and give $T$ the hyperedges $\{p,q,(p+q)/2\}$ for distinct same-parity endpoints $p,q\in T$. If an interior lattice point of $R$ is isolated in this hypergraph, an affine unimodular change of coordinates sends it to zero and sends $T$ to $\{0,e_1,e_2,-e_1-e_2\}$. Conversely these four points form the full lattice trace of their hull, and all are isolated.

pk-intake-isotropic-gaussian-base-poster.relation_to_goal: Finite posterior reweighting of unchanged continuous fibers. Fixed-mark depth is a supermartingale; the same assertion does not hold for the maximization over marks.
pk-intake-isotropic-gaussian-base-poster.statement:
Take a finite nonempty base $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ with positive prior $\pi_z$ and fixed uniform laws on positive compact convex fibers $K_z$. Let
$$
Z(a,t)=\sum_z\pi_z e^{a\cdot z-t|z|^2/2},\qquad p_z(a,t)=\pi_z e^{a\cdot z-t|z|^2/2}/Z(a,t).
$$
For a bounded fixed statistic with fiber means $g_z$, put $G=\sum_z p_zg_z$ and $m=\sum_zp_zz$. Then
$$
\begin{aligned}
\nabla_a\log Z&=m,&D_a^2\log Z&=\operatorname{Cov}_p(z),&
\partial_t\log Z&=-\tfrac12\mathbb E_p|z|^2,\\
\nabla_aG&=\operatorname{Cov}_p(g,z),&
D_a^2G&=\mathbb E_p[(g-G)(z-m)(z-m)^{\mathsf T}],&
\partial_tG&=-\tfrac12\operatorname{Cov}_p(g,|z|^2).
\end{aligned}
$$
In particular $(\partial_t+m\cdot\nabla_a+\Delta_a/2)G=0$. Sample $Z_0\sim\pi$ and independent standard Brownian motion $B_t$; observe $A_t=tZ_0+B_t$. In the observation filtration the conditional base probabilities are $p_z(A_t,t)$, and the innovation $W_t=A_t-\int_0^t m_s\,ds$ is Brownian. The processes $p_z,G$ are bounded martingales with $dp_z=p_z(z-m)\cdot dW$ and $dG=\operatorname{Cov}_p(g,z)\cdot dW$. For fixed actual mark $Y$, its normalized depth $D_Y(p)$ for this measure is a concave $1$-Lipschitz function of $p$ in $\ell^1$ and is a supermartingale. The attained maximum $D_*(p)$ over actual marks is also $1$-Lipschitz.

pk-intake-jensen-graph-kernel-character-.relation_to_goal: A finite arithmetic criterion for a specified witness under an integrality filter. The simultaneous character test is on the actual deletion kernel.
pk-intake-jensen-graph-kernel-character-.statement:
Let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^k$ be finite and nonempty. A Jensen function on $P$ preserves every convex representation whose target is in $P$. For a rational Jensen function $g$ set $P_g=\{p\in P:g(p)\in\mathbb Z\}$ and $T_g=\{(p,g(p)):p\in P_g\}$. For nonempty $W\subseteq P$ put $K(W)=\bigcap_{w\in W}\operatorname{conv}(W\setminus\{w\})$, with $\operatorname{conv}(\varnothing)=\varnothing$.

Choose integer feature rows $A_p\in\mathbb Z^\ell$ for a basis of the rational Jensen space so that every rational Jensen function is $g(p)=\alpha\cdot A_p$ for $\alpha\in\mathbb Q^\ell$. For a fixed nonempty $W\subseteq P$, set $\Lambda=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Z}\{A_p:p\in P\}$, $\Lambda_W=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Z}\{A_w:w\in W\}$, and $G_W=\Lambda/\Lambda_W$. Some rational Jensen function integral on $W$ makes the lifted $W$ a Helly witness in its integral graph if and only if a finite-order character $G_W\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$ is nonzero on every class $[A_p]$ with $p\in P\cap K(W)$. All these classes are torsion. In particular, one such class being zero rules out $W$ for all rational Jensen functions. Testing the simultaneous condition on the finite torsion subgroup is sufficient and necessary.

pk-intake-joint-cap-record-and-allocatio.relation_to_goal: Ordinary measures for actual allocated caps on fixed positive fibers. The result carries the original cap-law weights and allocations. It gives no weighted logarithmic or inverse-rate limit and no bound for the locked depth target.
pk-intake-joint-cap-record-and-allocatio.statement:
Fix finitely many bases $P$ and positive compact convex $d$-fibers $K_z^j\subset RB_d$, $d\ge1$, converging in Hausdorff distance to positive $K_z$. At each $j$ let a probability law of actual nonvertical caps $H=\{a\cdot z+u\cdot X\ge c\}$ have common mixed $d$-volume $Q_j\to Q$, with $0<u_{\min}\le |u|\le u_{\max}$. Finitely many fixed group labels may be included. Retain the original boundary selector $s_H$ and the section coarea $\lambda_{H,z}$. The selector is the strict-side bit away from a supporting facet. The section coarea is full $\mathcal H^{d-1}/|u|$ on a proper section, $(1-s_H)dS/|u|$ at inside support, $s_HdS/|u|$ at outside support, and zero for strict full or empty traces. Use endpoint counting for $d=1$.

Fix $B>u_{\max}R$. There are uniformly bounded Borel cap records preserving every threshold $c-a\cdot z$ in $[-B,B]$ and moving the others only within their respective exterior rays. They preserve all the given fiber traces and allocations. Along one subsequence the law of these records, its joint selected boundary measure recording the outward unit normal, and its joint allocated section measure converge weakly. The disintegrated limits use the same allocation rules for almost every record, and every support record has mixed $d$-volume $Q$. For each fiber, almost every record satisfies, for every $C^1$ spatial test $\psi$,
$$
\int_{\partial K_z}s_H\psi n\,dS
=\int_{K_z\cap H}\nabla_X\psi\,dX+u\int\psi\,d\lambda_{H,z}.
$$
In particular the allocated coarea masses and first moments converge jointly as measures of the record. There is no extra singular section measure at a supporting edge.

pk-intake-joint-fiber-cap-volume-quantil.relation_to_goal: Fiberwise cap inverse and exact original uniform mixed moments. The whole-mass centroid and section-weighted stationarity use different weights.
pk-intake-joint-fiber-cap-volume-quantil.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, compact and convex, $d\ge1$, $P=\operatorname{proj}_z C$, $K_z=C_z$, $r(z)=|K_z|^{1/d}$, and $L(z,x)=a\cdot z+u\cdot x-b$ with $u\ne0$. All volumes in a fiber are Lebesgue $d$-volumes. On the domain $z\in P,\ 0\le t\le r(z)$, set $U(z,0)=\max_{K_z}L(z,\cdot)$ and, for $t>0$, set
$$
U(z,t)=\sup\{s:|K_z\cap\{L(z,\cdot)\ge s\}|\ge t^d\}.
$$
The domain is convex and $U$ is finite, bounded, upper semicontinuous and jointly concave. For the cap $H=\{L\ge0\}$, its root $c_z=|K_z\cap\{x:L(z,x)\ge0\}|^{1/d}$ is concave on the projection of $C\cap H$ if that set is nonempty. On a positive fiber a proper cap has the unique root $U(z,c_z)=0$ and the zero and full cases are decided by the fiber support extrema. Its actual mixed cap mass is $\sum_z c_z^d$, summed over the integer bases in $P$.

For each positive fiber,
$$
\int_{K_z} L(z,x)\,dx=d\int_0^{r(z)}t^{d-1}U(z,t)\,dt.
$$
At a mixed centroid $(j,y)$ with integer $j$, $L(j,y)=0$ and positive total mixed mass, the exact moment equations are $\sum_z(z-j)r(z)^d=0$ and $\sum_z d\int_0^{r(z)}t^{d-1}U(z,t)\,dt=0$. Null fibers contribute zero.

For $H_v=\{L(z,x)+v\cdot(z-j)\ge0\}$, the inverse is $U_v(z,t)=U(z,t)+v\cdot(z-j)$. At a parameter with no endpoint contacts on positive fibers, let $c_z$ now be the cap roots for $H_v$ and $\beta_z=-\partial_t U_v(z,c_z)$ at proper roots. These derivatives exist and are strictly positive. The mixed cap tilt gradient is
$$
\sum_{\mathrm{proper}\ z}(z-j)\frac{dc_z^{d-1}}{\beta_z}
=\sum_{\mathrm{proper}\ z}(z-j)\frac{\mathcal H^{d-1}(K_z\cap\partial H_v)}{\|u\|}.
$$
It vanishes at a tilt minimum. In dimension one, when the oriented continuous coefficient is normalized to one, each proper section has weight one.

pk-intake-joint-logarithmic-defects-with.relation_to_goal: A joint compactness and exact marginal statement for actual selected logarithmic concentrations. It retains more than the projected ordinary defects and quadratic reserve.
pk-intake-joint-logarithmic-defects-with.statement:
Use the exponential-floor separator setting and put $r_j=\lambda_j(\ell_j)_+$. Suppose the normal and physical support ranges are compact, $\lambda_j\to0$, $\beta_j\to\beta\ge0$, $L_j\to L$ uniformly on the physical range with $L\ge0$, $\eta_j\rightharpoonup\eta$, $W_j\eta_j\rightharpoonup W\eta$, $\eta(Z)=0$ for $Z=\{(n,w):L(w)=0\}$, and $\sup_j\int(\ell_j)_+\,d\eta_j<\infty$. Record the rate in the measures
$$
\widehat B_j=(\ell_j)_+\eta_j\delta_{r_j},\qquad
\widehat A_j=W_j(\ell_j)_+\eta_j\delta_{r_j}.
$$
Along any joint weakly converging subsequence their limits are $\ell_+\eta\delta_0+\widehat b$ and $W\ell_+\eta\delta_0+\widehat a$, respectively, with $\ell=-\log L$ off $Z$ and $0\le\widehat a\le\widehat b$ supported on $Z\times[0,\beta]$. Let $\pi$ forget the rate, and let $b,a$ be the residuals after removing the ordinary parts of the unlifted body and cap-load log limits. Then $b=\pi_*\widehat b$, $a=\pi_*\widehat a$, and $\lambda_j(\ell_j)_+^2\eta_j\rightharpoonup q=\pi_*(r\widehat b)$ on this subsequence.

pk-intake-joint-measure-homothetic-domin.relation_to_goal: Exact domination and support geometry of a positive finite family satisfying the entire joint inequality. The assertion includes atomic and full-dimensional incidences and does not require rank drop.
pk-intake-joint-measure-homothetic-domin.statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $N\ge1$, and let $\mu_z$ be nonzero finite positive Borel measures of compact support $S_z\subset\mathbb R^D$ indexed by a finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$. Suppose every positive-weight combination $z=\sum_i\theta_i z_i\in\mathbb Z^n$, with $z_i\in P$ and $\sum_i\theta_i=1$, has $z\in P$ and satisfies
$$
\mu_z\!\left(\sum_i\theta_i E_i\right)^{1/N}
\ \ge\ \sum_i\theta_i\mu_{z_i}(E_i)^{1/N}
$$
for all compact $E_i$ with $\mu_{z_i}(E_i)>0$. For any such incidence, any input index $i$, and any choices $x_l\in S_{z_l}$ for $l\ne i$, put $F_i(x)=\theta_i x+\sum_{l\ne i}\theta_l x_l$. Then the finite measures satisfy $\mu_z\ge\theta_i^N(F_i)_\#\mu_{z_i}$.

Each $S_z$ is convex, and each $\mu_z$ is absolutely continuous in its own affine hull, with counting measure at a point. For positive support dimension $q$, writing $|\cdot|_q$ for Lebesgue measure in the support affine hull, its density is at most $2^N\mu_z(S_z)/|S_z|_q$ almost everywhere. At an incidence every input and the output have the same support affine dimension and tangent space. Partition $P$ into strata $P_c$ by the pair of these invariants. Every $P_c$ is lattice-complete, different strata use disjoint original parity classes, and hence $\sum_c k(P_c)=k(P)\le2^n$, where $k$ counts occupied classes modulo $2\mathbb Z^n$. The convex hull of the placed supports in any stratum has exactly those supports as its integer fibers. The same exact fiber assertion holds for the hull of all the placed supports.

pk-intake-joint-projective-energy-marked.relation_to_goal: Ordinary marked convex bodies and actual compact convex fibers with full-dimensional interior marks. The result is an energy interpolation statement without a mixed halfspace-depth estimate.
pk-intake-joint-projective-energy-marked.statement:
Let $d,m\ge1$, let $K_i\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies, and choose $y_i\in\operatorname{int}K_i$ and weights $\lambda_i\ge0$ with $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$. Use the energy $E_K(y)=\min_{a:\,1+a\cdot(x-y)>0\ (x\in K)}\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx$. Put $M=\sum_i\lambda_i K_i$ and $y=\sum_i\lambda_i y_i$. Then $y\in\operatorname{int}M$ and
$$
E_M(y)^{1/d}\ \ge\ \sum_i\lambda_i E_{K_i}(y_i)^{1/d}.
$$
Equality holds exactly when the centered bodies $K_i-y_i$ with $\lambda_i>0$ are positive scalar multiples of one another. In particular $y\mapsto E_K(y)^{1/d}$ is strictly concave on $\operatorname{int}K$.

If $H$ is a convex body containing $M$, the same lower bound holds for $E_H(y)^{1/d}$. Equality then requires both $H=M$ and the same marked homothety condition. Consequently, for a compact convex set $C\subset\mathbb R^{n+d}$ with fibers $C_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$, the function $(z,y)\mapsto E_{C_z}(y)^{1/d}$ is jointly concave on the convex domain $\{(z,y): y\in\operatorname{int}_{\mathbb R^d}C_z\}$.

pk-intake-joint-retained-cap-equality.relation_to_goal: Ordinary Lebesgue retained caps in positive continuous dimension; the equality classification concerns retained caps.
pk-intake-joint-retained-cap-equality.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K_i\subset\mathbb R^d$ be finitely many convex bodies with interior marks $y_i$, and let $\lambda_i>0$ sum to one. Let the convex body $K$ contain $\sum_i\lambda_iK_i$ and set $y=\sum_i\lambda_i y_i$. For any such marked body $(H,b)$, let $T_H(b)$ be the maximum Lebesgue mass of a measurable density $0\le f\le1$ on $H$ with $\int_H(x-b)f(x)\,dx=0$, and let $D_H(b)$ be its unique optimizing convex cap. Write $D_i=D_{K_i}(y_i)$ and $s_i=|D_i|^{1/d}$. Then
$$
T_K(y)^{1/d}\ge\sum_i\lambda_i s_i.
$$
Equality holds exactly when there is a convex body $D_0$ of volume one and centroid zero such that $D_i=y_i+s_iD_0$ for every $i$ and
$$
D_K(y)=\sum_i\lambda_iD_i=y+\Big(\sum_i\lambda_i s_i\Big)D_0.
$$

pk-intake-large-maximum-normal-simplex-c.relation_to_goal: Exact mixed mass of the fixed halfspace with nonnegative normalized continuous normal, maximum at least 2/(d+1), and base coefficient −β for β≥0 on finite concave paired simplex chains.
pk-intake-large-maximum-normal-simplex-c.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and $m\ge0$ be integers. Put $T_d=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)$, $V_d=1/d!$, $\tau=1/(d+1)$ and $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Take radii $R=r_0\ge r_1\ge\cdots\ge r_m\ge0$ with $R>0$ and nondecreasing drops $r_{h-1}-r_h$. The actual integer fibers at $-h$ and $h+1$ are $r_hT_d$, for $0\le h\le m$, with no other integer fibers. Let $\mu$ be the sum of their $d$-dimensional volumes, so the total mass is $2V_d\sum_{h=0}^m r_h^d$.

Fix $u\in[0,\infty)^d$ with $\sum_i u_i=1$ and $M=\max_i u_i\ge2\tau$. For every $\beta\ge0$, the closed halfspace
$$
H=\{(z,x):-\beta z+u\cdot x\ge R\tau\}
$$
through the actual centroid $(0,R\tau,\ldots,R\tau)$ at base zero captures at least $\Gamma_d V_d\sum_{h=0}^m r_h^d$, a fraction $\Gamma_d/2$ of the total mass. Equality holds exactly when every outer radius $r_h$, $h\ge1$, is zero, $u=e_i$ for some $i$, and $\beta\ge R(1-\tau)$. The condition on outer radii is vacuous when $m=0$.

pk-intake-large-negative-phase-section-v.relation_to_goal: A scaled limit for coarea moments of signed exponentials; the limiting product uses actual old-cap conditional moments.
pk-intake-large-negative-phase-section-v.statement:
Let $W=pY_p+qY_q-\sum_j r_jY_j$, where $p>q>0$, the list of $r_j\ge0$ is finite and may be empty, and all variables are independent unit-rate exponentials. Add an independent unit-rate exponential $Y_*$ and set $V_a=W-aY_*$ for $a>0$. Write $F_a=\Pr(V_a\ge0)$ and $\mu_i(a)$ for the coarea conditional mean of $Y_i$ at $V_a=0$. Set $P=\Pr(W>0)$, $M=\mathbb E(W\mid W>0)$ and $\nu_i=\mathbb E(Y_i\mid W>0)$ for every old index $i$. If $I$ is all old indices or all old indices except one, then
$$
\lim_{a\to\infty} a\left[\mu_*(a)\prod_{i\in I}\mu_i(a)-F_a(1-F_a)\right]
=M\left[\prod_{i\in I}\nu_i-P\right]\ge0.
$$

pk-intake-larger-hull-selector-obstructi.relation_to_goal: PK's fixed three-fiber example rules out the prescribed middle hull at the sharp threshold. This cap certificate does not bound points outside that hull and makes no claim against the locked weak conjecture.
pk-intake-larger-hull-selector-obstructi.statement:
Let $B=\{x\in\mathbb R^5:x_i\ge0,\ \sum_i x_i\le1\}$, $V=|B|=1/120$, and $g=(1/6,\ldots,1/6)$. Set $R=9/2$, $r=497/3000$, $\ell=11/12-Rr$, and $T=1-r-\ell=3979/6000$. Let $D$ be the simplex with vertices $p=(0,11/12,0,0,0)$, $b_0=(r,\ell,0,0,0)$, and $b_0+T e_i$ for $i=2,3,4,5$. Put

$$
m=|D|/V=rT^4=\frac{124581095445185057}{3888000000000000000},
\qquad q=m^{-1/5},\qquad A=(2-q)D,\qquad C=qD,
\qquad a=(2m^{1/5}-1)^5.
$$

The convex body $L=\operatorname{conv}((\{-1\}\times A)\cup(\{0\}\times B)\cup(\{1\}\times C))$ has exactly the three integer fibers $A,B,C$ at $-1,0,1$, with volumes $aV,V,V$ and $0<a<10^{-5}$. Each fiber has strictly less than half the total mixed volume. Write $\mu(H)$ for the summed five-dimensional volumes of the integer fibers of $L$ in an ambient halfspace $H$, and $\Gamma_5=(5/6)^5$.

Set $h_1=1/6-(2/25)a$ and $h_2=1/6+(17/50)a$. The two proper closed ambient halfspaces

$$
H_1=\{(z,x):x_1+(1-q)rz\ge h_1\},\qquad
H_2=\{(z,x):x_2-2z\ge h_2\}
$$

cover $\{0\}\times\operatorname{conv}(\{g\}\cup D)$. Their respective mixed masses in units of $V$ are

$$
\frac{\mu(H_1)}{V}=\Gamma_5[1+(12/125)a]^5,\qquad
\frac{\mu(H_2)}{V}=\Gamma_5[1-(51/125)a]^5+a.
$$

Both are strictly below $\Gamma_5(1+a/2)$. Consequently the maximum original mixed depth normalized by $(2+a)V$ on $\{0\}\times\operatorname{conv}(\{g\}\cup D)$ is strictly below $\Gamma_5/2$.

pk-intake-lattice-simplex-full-potential.relation_to_goal: Exact attained upper bound over the whole normal-dependent nonnegative convex cone, on this lattice-complete family. It does not satisfy strict proper-minor quotas.
pk-intake-lattice-simplex-full-potential.statement:
For each $d\ge2$, use the lattice product $C=D\times K$ and the $d+1$ actual critical caps $H_j$ just described in lattice-simplex-product-exact-critical-depth: $D=\operatorname{conv}\{(-1,\ldots,-1),e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$ and $K$ is a $d$-simplex with barycentric functions $\lambda_j$. On the sum $\eta$ of the $\mathcal H^{d-1}$ surface measures of all actual integer fibers, mark each point by the outward unit continuous normal $u$, defined off a null set. Let $W=(d+1)^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^d\mathbf1_{H_j}$. Over all finite nonnegative potentials $\Phi(u,z,x)$ measurable on this marked bundle and convex in $(z,x)$ for each fixed $u$, with finite positive denominator, one has
$
\sup_\Phi\frac{\int\Phi W\,d\eta}{\int\Phi\,d\eta}
=\frac{1+\gamma_d}{d+2}<\gamma_d,\qquad \gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d .
$
The constant potential attains the supremum. The $d+2$ positive measured fibers have distinct parities and equal masses, so each attains equality in the singleton quota at mass fraction $1/(d+2)$.

pk-intake-lattice-simplex-product-exact-.relation_to_goal: Lattice-complete product with (n=d), ordinary mixed (d)-volume, and an exact globally critical menu.
pk-intake-lattice-simplex-product-exact-.statement:
For each $d\ge2$, put $v_0=(-1,\ldots,-1)$, $v_i=e_i$ for $1\le i\le d$, and $D=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_d\}\subset\mathbb R^d$. Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be any simplex of volume $V>0$, with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$ and centroid $g$. Set $C=D\times K$ with integer coordinates in $D$. Let $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ and set $\ell_0(z)=-\sum_i z_i$, $\ell_i(z)=(d+1)z_i-\sum_j z_j$ for $i\ge1$. The $d+1$ closed ambient caps
$
H_j=\{(z,x):\lambda_j(x)-1/(d+1)+\ell_j(z)\ge0\}
$
cover all of ambient space and all have mass $Q=(1+\gamma_d)V$. The unique global deepest point on the actual lattice sample of $C$ is $(0,g)$, with normalized depth $(1+\gamma_d)/(d+2)$.

At that point the caps are a positive critical circuit. Their only nonempty cut sections among the integer fibers are proper on the middle fiber; the section centroids are $(0,g)$ and their coarea masses for the displayed continuous normals are all $d(d/(d+1))^{d-1}V$. In particular the normalized inverse-coarea response weights are all $1/(d+1)$.

pk-intake-least-active-stochastic-joint-.relation_to_goal: A joint curvature restriction for a homogeneous column-stochastic maximum, with no assumed curvature at unperturbed rows.
pk-intake-least-active-stochastic-joint-.statement:
Let $X$ maximize $\sum_i f_i(X_i)$ on nonnegative $N\times m$ matrices with each column sum one, with each $f_i$ finite and positively homogeneous of degree one. Choose $X$ with the fewest nonzero rows and let $k$ be that count. For each $i$ in a selected set $S$ of strictly positive rows, assume $f_i$ is $C^2$ near $X_i$ and let $E_i$ be a subspace on which the Hessian $\nabla^2 f_i(X_i)$ is positive definite. Then
$$
k+\sum_{i\in S}\dim E_i\le m.
$$
In particular, this applies to $f_i=\omega_i\phi$ with positive weights on the selected rows and positive-definite subspaces of the Hessian of $\phi$ there.

pk-intake-limiting-normal-transition-fac.relation_to_goal: Cap-wise vanishing-width covariance, with tests centered at one specified cut-plane point. No arbitrary constant tests or comparison of total masses are inferred.
pk-intake-limiting-normal-transition-fac.statement:
For the uniform outward cap model in the finite-width Hessian theorem, take a sequence of locally minimizing nonvertical normals on the same finite base set, with compact positive convex fibers $K_{z,l}\to K_z$ in Hausdorff distance and all limiting fibers positive. Suppose $h_l\downarrow0$, $b_l\to b\ge0$, $Y_l\to Y$, $\Sigma_l\to\Sigma$ positive definite, and $N_l=(a_l,u_l)\to N=(a,u)$ with $\Gamma_l(u_l)=1$. Set $c_l=N_l\cdot Y_l-b_l$, $c=N\cdot Y-b$ and $\bar Y=Y-b(0,\Sigma u)$. Use actual balanced endpoint coareas at $c_l-h_l,c_l$. On a common subsequence they converge weakly. Their lower-minus-upper difference vanishes on each proper or null/empty limiting cut and is $\chi_z d\mathcal H^{d-1}/\|u\|$ on each positive-area outside-supporting facet $F_z$, and $-\chi_z d\mathcal H^{d-1}/\|u\|$ on each inside-supporting facet, with $0\le\chi_z\le1$. For every full normal direction $D$,
$$
\sum_{\mathrm{out}}\int_{F_z}\chi_z[D\cdot(w-\bar Y)]^2\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}
\ \ge\
\sum_{\mathrm{in}}\int_{F_z}\chi_z[D\cdot(w-\bar Y)]^2\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}.
$$
For pure-base $D=(a',0)$ the incidence is $a'\cdot(z-p)$. If the finite-width strip coareas satisfy $S_l>0$, their actual centroid tends to $\bar Y$.

On the same subsequence, the actual outside boundary capture and inside boundary omission selectors at the moving facet-side roofs converge strongly in $L^1$ on each compact inner facet patch to $\tau_z$, and $\mathbf 1_{0<\tau_z<1}\le\chi_z\le1$ almost everywhere. For the joint weak graph record $\nu_w$ of actual scaled roof arguments $q_l^F$ on the compactified real line, the conditional transition value equals one on $-1<q<0$, zero outside $[-1,0]$, and may take values in $[0,1]$ at $-1,0$. Consequently $\chi_z(w)\le\nu_w([-1,0])\le\nu_w(\mathbb R)$ a.e. The record is taken on the same facets and subsequence as the balanced endpoint limits.

pk-intake-linear-cap-distance-localized-.relation_to_goal: A quantitative ordinary-depth estimate for arbitrary localized removals, with a two-parameter planar illustration and a fixed-reference first-order coefficient.
pk-intake-linear-cap-distance-localized-.statement:
Let $T$ be a full-dimensional $d$-simplex, $d\ge2$, of volume $V$, with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i$, $0\le i\le d$. Set $m=d+1$, $\Gamma=(d/m)^d$. For a dimension-only $\eta_d\in(0,1/2)$, let $U_i=\{x\in T:\lambda_i(x)>1-\eta_d\}$, and let $K$ be any convex body with $T\setminus\bigcup_i U_i\subset K\subset T$. Write $t_i=|U_i\setminus K|/V$ and $t=\sum_i t_i$.

Write $a_d=\Gamma-1/m>0$, $D(K)$ for normalized ordinary maximum depth, and $d_{\rm cap}(\mu,\nu)=\sup_H|\mu(H)-\nu(H)|$ over closed halfspaces. All uniform measures are probability measures. After choosing $\eta_d$ sufficiently small,
$$
D(K)-\Gamma\ge\frac{a_d t-4t^2/\Gamma}{1-t}.
$$
In particular, if $t\le\Gamma a_d/8$, then $D(K)-\Gamma\ge(a_d/2)t\ge(a_d/2)d_{\rm cap}(\mu_K,\mu_T)\ge(a_d/2)\inf_S d_{\rm cap}(\mu_K,\mu_S)$, where $S$ ranges over full-dimensional simplices. Uniformly in the ratios of the corner losses, $D(K)-\Gamma=a_d t+O_d(t^2)$. A flat single-corner deletion attains $d_{\rm cap}(\mu_K,\mu_T)=t$, so $a_d$ is sharp to first order for missing volume and cap distance from this fixed reference.

For positive $h,k$ sufficiently small, put $Q=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2,(1+h-k,k))$ and $S=\operatorname{conv}(0,[1+h/(1-k)]e_1,e_2)$. Then $Q\subset S$ and the relative missing area and fixed-reference cap distance are $\tau=hk/(1+h-k)$. The exact normalized ordinary maximum of $Q$ is
$$
\frac{2(1+\sqrt{1+3\tau})/9-2\tau/3}{1-\tau}
=\frac49+\frac{\tau}{9}-\frac{5\tau^2}{36}+O(\tau^3).
$$
Consequently its ordinary depth excess and cap distance from $S$ have order $hk$.

In particular the maximum normalized ordinary halfspace depth satisfies $D(Q)-4/9\ge\tau/45$.

pk-intake-linear-one-copy-source-cap-bud.relation_to_goal: A quantitative cap-budget consequence for a supplied coupling and supplied dominated output, with no assertion that the necessary source groups or coupling can be chosen.
pk-intake-linear-one-copy-source-cap-bud.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, $B\subset\mathbb R^d$ a compact convex body of positive $d$-volume, $0\le\eta\le\mathbf 1_B\,dx$, and $\alpha=\eta(B)/|B|$. $$
v\ge\gamma_d(1/k+\alpha),\qquad
v\ge\max\{L,2L+\alpha-1\},\qquad
L=\gamma_d\left(\frac{1+k\alpha^q}{1+k\alpha}\right)^d.
$$
In the ambient mixed-integer application let $k\ge2$ be an integer and embed $B$ at one fixed integer base $j$. Suppose $k$ source submeasures of common mass $a$ are coupled by a measure of mass $a$ whose average map has image measure $\eta$ on that copy of $B$. Assume the sum of the $k$ source submeasures and the $B$-volume measure is dominated by the original ambient measure. Every closed ambient halfspace containing $(j,g)$ then has original mass at least $\gamma_d(|B|+ka)/k$.

pk-intake-linear-value-gap-for-free-log-.relation_to_goal: The scale is an optimized normalized value estimate for the freely chosen positive log-normalized concave parameter.
pk-intake-linear-value-gap-for-free-log-.statement:
On a fixed finite nonempty real base $P$, let $d\ge1$, use the summed $d$-volume $dm$ of actual positive compatible fibers, and let $M$ denote its total mass. Let $L>0$ be finite concave on the canonical hull with $\int_S\log L\,dm/M=0$. For the ordinary through-mark halfspace caps add the displacement $\varepsilon(L(p,y)E_{K_p}(y)/M)^{1/(d+1)}\Gamma(u)$ to the margin when the continuous normal $u$ is nonzero. Here $E_K(y)$ is marked projective energy, zero on the own boundary, and $\Gamma(u)=\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma u}$ for the pooled within-fiber covariance. Keep pure-base caps unchanged and use the supremum of the raw depths divided by $M$ for $\beta_\varepsilon(K,L)$, or equivalently the maximum when attained. Write $\beta_0$ for the ordinary normalized maximum.

At a fixed actual positive compatible family on a finite real base that is a local minimum of the ordinary normalized maximum over all actual fixed-base positive compatible Hausdorff perturbations, the infimum over the positive concave log-normalized parameters of the covariance-buffered normalized maximum lies between $\beta_0+c\varepsilon$ and $\beta_0+C\varepsilon$ for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, with the lower bound holding for every such parameter.

For the joint infimum, let $\beta_*$ be the unrestricted ordinary fixed-base infimum. Suppose $\beta_*<b$ and every family with $\beta_0\le b$ has a representative under an invertible common continuous affine change and affine base shear with $M=1$, $K_z\subset RB_d$, $|K_z|\ge v>0$, an own inball of radius $r_b>0$ in every fiber, and $\lambda_- I\le\Sigma\le\lambda_+ I$ with $\lambda_->0$, all bounds common to the class. Then $\beta_*+c\varepsilon\le\inf_{K,L}\beta_\varepsilon(K,L)\le\beta_*+C\varepsilon$ for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$.

pk-intake-local-planar-convex-body-loren.relation_to_goal: Ordinary planar Hausdorff neighborhood at one strict triangle for one fixed interior source and normal circuit.
pk-intake-local-planar-convex-body-loren.statement:
For a planar convex body $K$ containing $0$ in its interior and three nonzero spanning normals $v_1+v_2+v_3=0$, write
$$
k=|K|,\qquad Q_i=|K\cap\{v_i\cdot x\ge0\}|,\qquad
\sigma_i=\mathcal H^1(K\cap v_i^\perp)/\lVert v_i\rVert .
$$
Set $M=\sum_iQ_i/\sigma_i$, $f_i=2\sqrt{kQ_i}/(\sigma_i M)$ and $\Phi_i=f_i+(f_j+f_l)^2/4$ where $\{i,j,l\}=\{1,2,3\}$. A triangle has strict distinct-vertex incidence if cap $i$ contains its vertex $P_i$ in its open halfplane and excludes both other vertices strictly.


Fix a strict distinct-vertex triangle $T$ containing $0$ in its interior, and keep the mark and three normals fixed. There is a Hausdorff neighborhood of $T$ in which every convex body $K$ contains the mark in its interior and satisfies $\Phi_i(K)\le2$ for all three rows. Every nontriangular $K$ there satisfies all three inequalities strictly.

For a row tight at $T$, apply the support-preserving six-sector replacement to $K$, and let $P$ be its polygon and $T_0$ the triangle of the three auxiliaries in the unique-cap sectors. For sufficiently close $K$, one has
$$
\Phi_i(P)\le\Phi_i(T_0)-c_i|P\setminus T_0|\le2-c_i|P\setminus T_0|
$$
with $c_i>0$ depending on the fixed configuration.

pk-intake-log-buffer-row-tail.relation_to_goal: This is a uniform bound conditional on same-force contact rows and their likelihood and force estimates.
pk-intake-log-buffer-row-tail.statement:
Let $S$ be a finite union of sampled convex $d$-fibers with $d$-dimensional volume at least $v>0$ in each fiber, summed measure $dm$ and $M\le M_{\max}$. Let $L>0$ on sampled interiors be nonnegative, upper semicontinuous and concave on each fiber. For finitely many source values $L_i>0$ assume probabilities $\rho_i,\bar\rho_i$ and weights $\sigma_i$ satisfy
$$
\frac{dm}{M}=\sum_i\sigma_i\bar\rho_i,\quad
d\bar\rho_i=(L/L_i)\,d\rho_i,\quad L/L_i\le A\ \rho_i\text{-a.e.},\qquad
\sum_i\sigma_i\log L_i\le0.
$$
Assume $N>0$, $0\le E_i\le M$, $\kappa_i\ge0$, $\sum_i\kappa_i\le K_*$, and
$$
\sigma_i=\frac{\kappa_i (L_i E_i/M)^{1/N}}{\Delta/\varepsilon},
\qquad \Delta/\varepsilon\ge a_*>0.
$$
Put $B_*=K_*N/(e a_*)$. Then for $T>1$,
$$
m\{L>AT\}/M\le B_*/\log T,\qquad
\sup_S L\le 2A\exp(2^dM_{\max}B_*/v)=:L_*.
$$

pk-intake-log-buffer-source-cores.relation_to_goal: This is a conditional estimate on sampled interiors and source occurrences.
pk-intake-log-buffer-source-cores.statement:
Assume the hypotheses and the bound $L_*$ of the same-force row-tail lemma, and $\int_S\log L\,dm=0$. Suppose all sampled fibers lie in $RB_d$. For any point $(p,y)$ with $B(y,r)\subset K_p$, $r>0$, one has
$$
L(p,y)\ge\frac{r}{r+2R}\sup_{K_p}L(p,\cdot)
\ge \frac{r}{r+2R}L_*^{-M_{\max}/v}.
$$
In particular this holds uniformly at source marks $(p_i,y_i)$ with a common own inball radius and with $L_i=L(p_i,y_i)$. If their $E_i$ are the marked projective energies, and $a_*\le\Delta/\varepsilon\le a^*<\infty$, then $\sigma_i$ and $\kappa_i$ are comparable at every source by positive constants depending only on these uniform bounds, $N$, and $d$.

pk-intake-log-concave-cap-profile-equali.relation_to_goal: Classifies equality at a positive trimming parameter for r+1 caps in the full-dimensional log-concave density class.
pk-intake-log-concave-cap-profile-equali.statement:
Let $r\ge2$, and let $f$ be an integrable log-concave density of mass $V>0$ on $\mathbb R^r$ with full-dimensional positive support. Suppose $r+1$ proper closed halfspaces $H_i$ cover the interior of that support, and put $A_i=\int_{H_i}f$, $\gamma_r=(r/(r+1))^r$, and $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$. For $\alpha>0$, equality
$$
\sum_i(A_i-\alpha)_++\frac{\alpha}{\gamma_r}=V
$$
holds exactly under the following conditions. There are a point $y$ and an $r$-simplex $T$ with centroid zero such that $f(y+x)=\exp[-h(p_T(x))]$ almost everywhere on $p_T(x)<R$, and $f=0$ almost everywhere outside this radial support. Here $p_T$ is the gauge of $T$, $0<R\le\infty$, and $h$ is convex and nondecreasing with positive finite profile mass. The halfspaces are the $r+1$ distinct vertex halfspaces of $y+T$ through $y$ and parallel to the opposite facets, on the side retaining the corresponding vertex. Every $A_i$ equals $\alpha=\gamma_r V$.

pk-intake-log-concave-reciprocal-laplace.relation_to_goal: An analytic statement on positive log-concave functions on a half-line, independently usable for signed exponential laws.
pk-intake-log-concave-reciprocal-laplace.statement:
For a positive log-concave probability density on $[0,\infty)$, the associated variable $X$ satisfies $\mathbb E X^2\le 2(\mathbb E X)^2$, with equality exactly for an exponential law. Let $h:[0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be continuous, integrable and log-concave with $h(0)=1$. For $a>0$ put
$$
M_r(a)=\int_0^\infty t^r e^{-t/a}h(t)\,dt,\qquad \psi(a)=a/M_0(a).
$$
Then $\psi(0+)=1$ and $\psi''(a)=[2M_1(a)^2-M_0(a)M_2(a)]/[a^3M_0(a)^3]\ge0$. Moreover $\psi(a)\ge1$ implies $\psi'(a)>0$.

pk-intake-log-contact-original-row-centr.relation_to_goal: Original-volume mean identity conditional on supplied mixed contact rows.
pk-intake-log-contact-original-row-centr.statement:
Let $dm$ be finite positive mixed volume of mass $M$ supported on a compact sampled set $S$, and let $L>0$ be continuous on $C=\operatorname{conv}S$. Assume positive weights $\sigma_i$ summing to one and probability laws $\rho_i$ on $S$ satisfy $\int w\,d\rho_i=Y_i$, $\int L\,d\rho_i=L_i=L(Y_i)$ and $\sum_i(\sigma_i/L_i)\rho_i=dm/(ML)$. Suppose for each row there is an affine majorant $A_i\ge L$ on $C$ touching $L$ at $Y_i$ and agreeing with $L$ $\rho_i$-almost everywhere. Let $a_i$ be its full linear part, $C_i=\operatorname{Cov}_{\rho_i}(w)$, and $d\bar\rho_i=(L/L_i)d\rho_i$. Then $\bar\rho_i$ are probabilities with $dm/M=\sum_i\sigma_i\bar\rho_i$, and their means $\bar Y_i$ obey
$$
\bar Y_i-Y_i=C_i a_i/L_i,\qquad
a_i\cdot(\bar Y_i-Y_i)=\operatorname{Var}_{\rho_i}(L)/L_i.
$$
The vector $C_i a_i$ is independent of the choice of touching contact plane. The mean displacement is zero exactly when $L=L_i$ $\rho_i$-almost everywhere, equivalently when $\bar\rho_i=\rho_i$. Writing $a_i=(b_i,c_i)$ in base and continuous coordinates, the continuous displacement is $(C_i^{Xz}b_i+C_i^{XX}c_i)/L_i$. The original mixed centroid is $\sum_i\sigma_i[Y_i+C_i a_i/L_i]$.

pk-intake-log-contact-original-row-entro.relation_to_goal: Exact bulk entropy and strictness for supplied volume rows. No cap-loss bound.
pk-intake-log-contact-original-row-entro.statement:
Let $dm$ be finite positive mixed volume of mass $M$ on a compact sampled set $S$. Let $L$ be continuous and strictly positive on its compact convex hull with $\int\log L\,dm/M=0$. Let $\rho_i$ be finitely many probability rows on $S$ with $L_i=\int L\,d\rho_i$, and assume $\sigma_i>0$ with $\sum_i\sigma_i=1$ and $\sum_i(\sigma_i/L_i)\rho_i=dm/(ML)$. Set $d\bar\rho_i=(L/L_i)d\rho_i$, $\ell_i=\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_{\rho_i}L$, $u_i=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{\rho_i}L$, and $D_i=D(\bar\rho_i\|\rho_i)$. Then
$$
D_i=\int\log(L/L_i)\,d\bar\rho_i,\qquad
\frac{\operatorname{Var}_{\rho_i}(L)}{2L_i u_i}\le D_i\le
\frac{\operatorname{Var}_{\rho_i}(L)}{2L_i\ell_i},\qquad
\sum_i\sigma_i D_i=-\sum_i\sigma_i\log L_i\ge0.
$$
The last inequality is equality exactly when each row has $L=L_i$ almost everywhere. If in a positive row $L$ agrees almost everywhere with an affine function whose continuous gradient is nonzero, and $dm$ sums Lebesgue $d$-volume on finitely many positive fibers with $d\ge1$, then that row has $D_i>0$ and the total reserve is strictly positive.

$$
\frac1{M_j}\sum_{z\in P}\int_{K_{j,z}}\log L_j(z,X)\,dX=0,\qquad
M_j=\sum_{z\in P}|K_{j,z}|.
$$
Then the sampled zero set $Z$ is nonempty.

pk-intake-log-parameter-boundary-layer-s.relation_to_goal: This is a counterexample to replacing a moving integrand by its limit in a shell derivative based solely on the stated topology.
pk-intake-log-parameter-boundary-layer-s.statement: Interior-uniform and logarithmic $L^1$ convergence of positive continuous concave log-normalized parameters, even with a common positive lower bound, need not allow replacement by their limit in a first-order shell integral. On $K=[0,1]$ let $L=1$, $c=1-\log2$, and $U_t(x)=e^{ct}\min(1,1/2+x/(2t))$, $0<t<1/2$. For the actual removed shell $R_t=[0,t]$ of $K_t=[t,1]$, the integral $\int_{R_t}\log U_t=-ct+ct^2$ has normalized limit $-c$ after division by $t$, whereas $\int_{R_t}\log L=0$. The current log renormalization of $U_t$ on $K_t$ is identically one.

pk-intake-log-scale-selection.relation_to_goal: This is a scalar selection rule conditional on a linear value gap.
pk-intake-log-scale-selection.statement:
Let $b:(0,\bar\varepsilon]\to\mathbb R$ be lower semicontinuous and satisfy $b_*+c\varepsilon\le b(\varepsilon)\le b_*+C\varepsilon$ with $0<c\le C<\infty$. For all sufficiently small $\tau>0$, $b(\varepsilon)-\tau\log\varepsilon$ attains its minimum, and every minimizer is interior and satisfies
$$
\frac{\tau}{eC}\le\varepsilon_\tau\le\frac{2\tau}{c}\log(2C/c).
$$
The same bounds and interior conclusion hold for an attained minimum over joint choices with fixed-scale infima $b(\varepsilon)$, without a separate lower-semicontinuity assumption on $b$.

pk-intake-longest-half-mass-balanced-mom.statement:

For $t=M/2=59/40$, write $M_t(j)$ for the set of continuous barycenters of submeasures $\nu\le\mu$ of mass $t$ and base barycenter $j$. Then
$$
M_t(-1)=[-13/100,21/200],\qquad
M_t(0)=[-14791/118000,13831/118000],\qquad M_t(1)=\varnothing.

Their two feasible lengths are $47/200$ and $14311/59000$, respectively. Base zero uniquely maximizes length by $223/29500$. Its moment interval midpoint $y=-6/1475$ lies on the closed cap $x-z\le y$, of mass $2171/2950<M/4$, with raw gap $37/23600$. The base $-1$ is the unique weighted median, and the original marginal closed-halfspace depth at base zero is $31/25<t$.

pk-intake-marked-entropy-fixed-body-supe.relation_to_goal: Identifies the logarithmic concave-parameter value on fixed sampled fibers and fixed marked upper bounds, assuming an old contact certificate. The locked conjecture concerns the maximum mixed halfspace depth.
pk-intake-marked-entropy-fixed-body-supe.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be nonempty and finite, with $n\ge0$ and $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$. Let $d\ge1$ and let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex bodies with nonempty interior for $z\in P$. Put $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$ and $C=\operatorname{conv}S$, and assume $C\cap(\{z\}\times\mathbb R^d)=\{z\}\times K_z$ for each $z\in P$. All hulls and affine coefficients are relative to $\operatorname{aff}(P)\times\mathbb R^d$. Write $dm=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes dX|_{K_z}$ and $M=m(S)$. Let $L$ be positive, continuous, and concave on $C$, with $\int_S\log L\,dm/M=0$. Fix $k\ge1$ marks $Y_i=(p_i,y_i)$ with $p_i\in P$ and $y_i\in\operatorname{int}K_{p_i}$, and write $l_i=L(Y_i)$ and $l=(l_i)_{i=1}^k$.

Assume there is at least one contact certificate. This means weights $\sigma_i\ge0$ with $\sum_i\sigma_i=1$ and, for each $\sigma_i>0$, a probability measure $\rho_i$ on $S$ with
$$
\int_S w\,d\rho_i=Y_i,\qquad
\int_S L\,d\rho_i=l_i,\qquad
\sum_{i:\,\sigma_i>0}\frac{\sigma_i}{l_i}\rho_i=\frac{dm}{ML}.
\tag{1}
$$
Let $\mathcal W$ be the set of all weight vectors of such certificates. For $b\in(0,\infty)^k$, let $H_C(b)$ be the supremum of $M^{-1}\int_S\log U\,dm$ over positive continuous concave functions $U$ on $C$ with $U(Y_i)\le b_i$ for all $i$.

For every such $U$ and every $\sigma\in\mathcal W$ one has
$$
\frac1M\int_S\log(U/L)\,dm
\le\sum_{i=1}^k \sigma_i\log\frac{U(Y_i)}{l_i}.
\tag{2}
$$
This also holds for continuous nonnegative concave $U$ on $C$ that are positive in the interior of every sampled fiber and have integrable sampled $\log U$. If $U(Y_i)\le l_i$ for all $i$ and the left-hand side is zero, then $U=L$ on every closed sampled fiber.

The function $H_C$ is finite, concave, and coordinatewise nondecreasing on the positive orthant, with $H_C(cb)=H_C(b)+\log c$ for $c>0$. One has $H_C(l)=0$, attained by $L$, and
$$
\partial^+H_C(l)=\left\{\left(\frac{\sigma_i}{l_i}\right)_{i=1}^k:\ \sigma\in\mathcal W\right\},
\tag{3}
$$
where $\partial^+$ consists of the supergradients for the concave function. In particular $\mathcal W$ is compact and convex, and for every $h\in\mathbb R^k$ and $t\downarrow0$,
$$
H_C(l+th+o(t))=t\min_{\sigma\in\mathcal W}\sum_i \frac{\sigma_i h_i}{l_i}+o(t).
\tag{4}
$$

pk-intake-marked-entropy-local-attainmen.relation_to_goal: Establishes local attainment near positive contact-certified data and a first-order value for fixed marked constraints. Optimized buffered depth involves an additional inverse response for all halfspaces and the motion of the deepest constraints.
pk-intake-marked-entropy-local-attainmen.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be nonempty and finite, with $n\ge0$ and $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$. Let $d\ge1$ and let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex bodies with nonempty interior for $z\in P$. Put $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$ and $C=\operatorname{conv}S$, and assume $C\cap(\{z\}\times\mathbb R^d)=\{z\}\times K_z$ for each $z\in P$. All hulls and affine coefficients are relative to $\operatorname{aff}(P)\times\mathbb R^d$. Write $dm=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes dX|_{K_z}$ and $M=m(S)$. Let $L$ be positive, continuous, and concave on $C$, with $\int_S\log L\,dm/M=0$. Fix $k\ge1$ marks $Y_i=(p_i,y_i)$ with $p_i\in P$ and $y_i\in\operatorname{int}K_{p_i}$, and write $l_i=L(Y_i)$ and $l=(l_i)_{i=1}^k$.

Assume there is at least one contact certificate. This means weights $\sigma_i\ge0$ with $\sum_i\sigma_i=1$ and, for each $\sigma_i>0$, a probability measure $\rho_i$ on $S$ with
$$
\int_S w\,d\rho_i=Y_i,\qquad
\int_S L\,d\rho_i=l_i,\qquad
\sum_{i:\,\sigma_i>0}\frac{\sigma_i}{l_i}\rho_i=\frac{dm}{ML}.
\tag{1}
$$
Let $\mathcal W$ be the set of all weight vectors of such certificates. For $b\in(0,\infty)^k$, let $H_C(b)$ be the supremum of $M^{-1}\int_S\log U\,dm$ over positive continuous concave functions $U$ on $C$ with $U(Y_i)\le b_i$ for all $i$.

For another compatible family of compact convex bodies $K'_z$ over the same $P$, write $S'$, $C'$, and $dm'$ for the corresponding sampled set, hull, and measure. Retain the same marks and define $H_{C'}(b)$ by the same supremum with domain $C'$ and integral over $S'$ against $dm'/M$, with the fixed old denominator $M$.

There is a fixed function $\widetilde L$, a minimum of at most $k$ affine functions on the relative ambient space, positive on a neighborhood of $C$ and equal to $L$ on $S$. For all families sufficiently close to the old family in maximum fiber Hausdorff distance and all $b$ sufficiently close to $l$, the marks stay interior to their own fibers and $H_{C'}(b)$ is finite and attained. It has a representative that is the minimum of at most $k$ affine functions, whose coefficients are uniformly bounded and whose minimum has a uniform positive floor on $C'$, on $C$, and on a fixed neighborhood of $C$. The maximizing sampled restriction is unique. As $(K'_z,b)\to(K_z,l)$, the optimal value tends to zero, the maximizing restriction converges uniformly on $S'$ to $\widetilde L|_{S'}$, and the bounded finite-plane representatives in the proof converge uniformly to $L$ on $S$.

Let $t\downarrow0$ and let $K_z(t)$ be such compatible bodies with $\max_z d_H(K_z(t),K_z)=O(t)$, using subscript $t$ for the moving objects. For arbitrary $b(t)\to l$ in the positive orthant,
$$
H_t(b(t))
=H_C(b(t))+
\frac{1}{M}\left(\int_{S_t}\log\widetilde L\,dm_t-\int_S\log L\,dm\right)+o(t).
\tag{6}
$$
Suppose in addition that for each $z$ and some fixed $o_z\in\operatorname{int}K_z$, the endpoint on the ray through each $X\in\partial K_z$ changes to $o_z+(1-s_{z,t}(X))(X-o_z)$. Assume $|s_{z,t}|\le Ct$ uniformly and
$s_{z,t}(X)/t\to v_z(X)/(n_z(X)\cdot(X-o_z))$ for surface-almost every $X$, where $n_z$ is the outward unit normal and $v_z$ is a bounded measurable signed inward speed. Use counting measure on the two endpoints for $d=1$. For $b_i(t)=l_i+th_i+o(t)$, with arbitrary $h\in\mathbb R^k$,
$$
H_t(b(t))
=t\left[-\frac1M\sum_{z\in P}\int_{\partial K_z}\log L(z,X)v_z(X)\,dS(X)
+\min_{\sigma\in\mathcal W}\sum_i\frac{\sigma_i h_i}{l_i}\right]+o(t).
\tag{7}
$$
The minimum is attained. Using the current total volume $M_t=m_t(S_t)$ as the denominator gives the same first-order coefficient.

pk-intake-marked-fiber-graph-depth-trans.relation_to_goal: Finite marked fibers with certified individual depths. Strictness uses one common intrinsic direction space. The location is a fixed graph mark.
pk-intake-marked-fiber-graph-depth-trans.statement:
Let $z_i\in\mathbb R^n$ be finitely many distinct bases, with $n\ge0$. For each base let $K_i\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex of affine dimension $r\ge1$ with intrinsic volume $V_i=\mathcal H_r(K_i)$, and let $x_i\in\operatorname{relint}K_i$. Put a weight $0<c_i\le D_{K_i}(x_i)<V_i$ on each $v_i=(z_i,x_i)$, where $D_{K_i}$ is raw ordinary depth computed in $\operatorname{aff}K_i$. Let $T=\{v_i\}_i$, and let $\mu$ be the sum of intrinsic $r$-volume on the disjoint lifted fibers $\{z_i\}\times K_i$.

If every closed ambient halfspace containing $y=v_j$ has atomic weight at least $\alpha>0$, then the actual raw depth $h_\mu(y)=\inf_{H\ni y}\mu(H)$ is at least $\alpha$. If all fiber planes have a common direction space and the minimal face of $\operatorname{conv}T$ containing $y$ has atomic weight greater than $\alpha$, then $h_\mu(y)>\alpha$.

pk-intake-marked-projective-energy-posit.relation_to_goal: Joint continuity includes arbitrary marks approaching the boundary of positive limiting bodies.
pk-intake-marked-projective-energy-posit.statement:
Let \(d\ge1\) and let convex bodies \(K_j\subset\mathbb R^d\) converge in Hausdorff distance to a convex body \(K\). If \(y_j\in K_j\) converges to \(y\in K\), then \(E_{K_j}(y_j)\to E_K(y)\), where
$$
E_A(v)=\inf_{a:\,1+a\cdot(x-v)>0\ \forall x\in A}
\int_A [1+a\cdot(x-v)]^{-d-1}\,dx.
$$
This same infimum is zero at each boundary mark. In a common Euclidean ball, if \(u\) is a unit normal and \(\delta=h_A(u)-u\cdot v>0\), then \(E_A(v)\le 2^{d+1}L\delta/d\), where \(L\) bounds the \((d-1)\)-volumes of sections perpendicular to \(u\). For \(d=1\) the section bound can be taken as one.

pk-intake-marked-same-parity-support-pai.relation_to_goal: Actual marked finite-fiber surface laws and conditional accounting for a supplied repair. Existence of a useful common projective capacity and a distinct repairable separator branch is a separate obligation.
pk-intake-marked-same-parity-support-pai.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty. Let the compact convex fibers $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ of positive $d$-dimensional volume be the exact sampled fibers of their canonical convex hull $C$. The marked actual support graph consists of $(u,z,X)$ with $u$ a unit continuous normal, $z\in P$ and $X\in F_{K_z}(u)$. Suppose a finite law $\nu(ds,du)P_{s,u}(dt)$ has both $(u,s)$ and $(u,t)$ on the marked actual support graph, and its conditional target mean is $s$ with target marginal $\eta$. Here $s,t$ include the base and continuous coordinates. There is a marked pair law with source $\nu$, each endpoint marginal $\eta$, common normal and common endpoint parity, such that its midpoint $b$ is on the actual support graph and $\mathbb E[b\mid s,u]=s$. Its conditional midpoint mean after fixing the original parity need not equal $s$.

The same support conclusion holds for any prescribed marked pair law $\tau$ with common normal, equal parity within each pair, endpoints and source on the graph, and the same conditional midpoint mean. For its endpoint marginals $\gamma_\pm$, let $\eta=(\gamma_-+\gamma_+)/2$ and $\rho=b_\#\tau$, retaining the common normal in the marginals. For positive continuous concave $L$ on $C$,
$$
S=\int\log L\,d(\nu-\eta)
 =\int\log L\,d(\nu-\rho)+\Delta,\qquad
 \Delta=\int\log L\,d(\rho-\eta).
$$
Both terms on the right are nonnegative. The symmetric construction has identical endpoint laws within each normal and parity, and their diagonal coupling has midpoint law $\eta$, dominates the old midpoint in convex order on each such class, and has zero tuple-discount loss. Thus if $\eta\le\omega$ this diagonal uses one copy of $\omega$. If $\gamma_\pm\le\eta$ and their average is $\eta$, they are both equal to $\eta$.

For a proper same-normal and same-parity binary branch $\tau_b$ with endpoint marginals $\gamma_\pm$ of mass $m_b>0$ and midpoint law $\rho_b$ on the actual support graph, suppose $\gamma_-+\gamma_+\le\eta$ and $\nu=\eta-\gamma_--\gamma_++2\rho_b$. Then $\nu$ is the source of a physical normal-preserving martingale to $\eta$, and $S=2\Delta_b$ with $\Delta_b=\int\log L\,d(\rho_b-(\gamma_-+\gamma_+)/2)$. If a repaired branch with the same separate endpoint marginals on each normal/parity class and midpoint convex order above the old branch is supplied, and $L$ is finite piecewise affine, then its error $E_b=b_\#[(1-a^d)\tau_{b,\mathrm{new}}]$, with $a=(L(t_-)+L(t_+))/(2L(b))$, obeys
$$
E_b(\mathrm{total})\le m_b[1-\exp(-d S/(2m_b))].
$$
Replacing the branch in the rebuilt source gives error measure $2E_b$. If the repaired branch has discounted law $b_\#(a^d\tau_{b,\mathrm{new}})\le 2^n\omega$ for a common capacity $\omega$, the rebuilt branch has ceiling $2^{n+1}\omega$ on its discounted part, separate from the unchanged diagonal residual.

pk-intake-maximal-intrinsic-stratum-cent.relation_to_goal: Intrinsic lower-dimensional transfer and maximal-stratum mass bound; the ratio of maximal-stratum mass to total mass remains for unequal fibers.
pk-intake-maximal-intrinsic-stratum-cent.statement: Use the maximal intrinsic-volume centroid graph setup: $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ is compact and convex with nonempty mixed trace $S$, $n,d\ge0$, $n+d\ge1$, $q=\dim_H S$ is the maximum integer fiber dimension, and $a>0$ is the maximum fiber $\mathcal H_q$-volume. Put $M=\mathcal H_q(S)$ and $M_{\max}=a|P_{\max}|$, where $P_{\max}$ is the set of bases attaining $a$. Write $\gamma_0=1$ and $\gamma_j=(j/(j+1))^j$ for $j\ge1$. There is an actual centroid $y$ in a maximum-volume fiber such that every closed ambient halfspace $H$ containing $y$ satisfies $\mathcal H_q(S\cap H)\ge 2^{-n}\gamma_q M_{\max}$. Consequently the normalized depth is at least $2^{-n}\gamma_q M_{\max}/M\ge 2^{-n}\gamma_d M_{\max}/M$. If all positive intrinsic fiber volumes are equal this gives $2^{-n}\gamma_q$. In particular for $q=0$, including $d=0$, it gives normalized counting depth $2^{-n}$.

pk-intake-maximal-reflection-extraction-.relation_to_goal: Gives an actual sharp local half-depth extraction for one body and the exact first-order loss of local half-depth under a base-balanced positive enlargement.
pk-intake-maximal-reflection-extraction-.statement:
Let $C=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(3,0),(3,3),(2,10),(0,2)\}$. Its integer fibers are $[0,2],[0,6],[0,10],[0,3]$ and its total mixed length is $21$. The convex hull $D$ of the three fibers $[3,6],[0,6],[0,3]$ at bases $1,2,3$ attains the maximum mixed length among full-dimensional convex subbodies of $C$ with true integer-base centroid and local normalized depth at least $1/2$.

For $0<t\le1$, enlarge just the middle fiber to $[0,6+t]$ and take the corresponding hull $D_t$. Then $D_t\subseteq C$ has exactly these three integer fibers, mass $12+t$, and true centroid $(2,c_t)$ with $c_t=3+(3t+t^2/2)/(12+t)$. The closed cap $x+z-2\ge c_t$ through this centroid has mass $15+t-3c_t$, below half the mass of $D_t$ by $t(3+t)/(12+t)$. This deficit is $t/4+O(t^2)$ as $t\downarrow0$.

pk-intake-median-pair-finite-cap-dual-co.relation_to_goal: Finite dual over cap weights for a generally discontinuous step cost, with approximation at an optimizer of the original closed-cap objective.
pk-intake-median-pair-finite-cap-dual-co.statement:
In the median-pair depth problem in continuous dimension $d\ge1$, fix a median-fiber mark $y$. Let $v_y=\max_\sigma f_y(\sigma)$ over the prescribed probability couplings and let $v_F=\max_\sigma\min_i\int c_i\,d\sigma$ for a nonempty finite list of closed through-$y$ caps $H_i$, with $c_i=\mathbf1_{H_i}\circ T$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ some list satisfies $v_y\le v_F<v_y+\varepsilon$. For every finite list,
$$
v_F=\min_{\lambda_i\ge0,\,\sum_i\lambda_i=1}\ \max_\sigma\int c_\lambda\,d\sigma,
\qquad c_\lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i c_i.
$$
Both optima and a finite primal optimum are attained. For any minimizing $\lambda$, every finite primal optimizer maximizes the weighted cost and satisfies $\int c_i\,d\sigma_F=v_F$ whenever $\lambda_i>0$. At a joint optimizer $(\sigma_*,y_*)$ of value $V$, choose an approximating list at $y_*$. Its minimizing weights satisfy
$$
0\le\max_\sigma\int c_\lambda\,d\sigma-\int c_\lambda\,d\sigma_*<\varepsilon,
\qquad
0\le\sum_i\lambda_i\bigl(\nu_{\sigma_*}(H_i)-V\bigr)<\varepsilon.
$$

\qquad V=\sup_{\sigma\in\Pi(\alpha,\beta),\,y\in K} f_y(\sigma).
$$
Then $V$ is attained at one pair $(\sigma_*,y_*)$ and is the maximum closed-halfspace depth of a realizable median target when optimized jointly over coupling and mark. For $d=0$ the analogous value is attained and is $1$.

\sum_e\int_e(w-1)u_e\,d\mathcal H_1=2\eta\,u_{12}(m)

hold for the normal velocities $u_e$ of every affine variation, with one positive contact $\eta=\sigma\,\mathcal H_1(e_{12})/2$. pk-intake-middle-face-tent-green-signed-.relation_to_goal: An exact one-dimensional profile identity for conditional middle-face costs. It does not establish the separate geometric deformation theorem.
pk-intake-middle-face-tent-green-signed-.statement:
Let $F=[\alpha,\beta]$, $\alpha<\beta$, and $f$ be a bounded piecewise constant function on $F$. Put
$
U(t)=\int_\alpha^\beta
\frac{(\min(t,s)-\alpha)(\beta-\max(t,s))}{\beta-\alpha} f(s)\,ds.
$
Then $U\in C^1(F)$, $U(\alpha)=U(\beta)=0$, and $-U''=f$ almost everywhere. For the piecewise affine tent $T_t$ of height one at $t\in(\alpha,\beta)$ and zero at the endpoints,
$
\int_F T_t f=\frac{(\beta-\alpha)U(t)}{(t-\alpha)(\beta-t)}.
$
Consequently nonnegative costs for all interior peaks are equivalent to $U\ge0$, and then $U'(\alpha)\ge0\ge U'(\beta)$.

For $\alpha\le\alpha_0<c\le d<\beta_0\le\beta$, define $H(s)=\min\{1,(s-\alpha_0)/(c-\alpha_0),(\beta_0-s)/(\beta_0-d)\}$. Then
$
\int_F H f
=\frac{U(c)-(\alpha_0-\alpha)U'(\alpha)}{c-\alpha_0}
+\frac{U(d)+(\beta-\beta_0)U'(\beta)}{\beta_0-d}.
$
In particular $U\ge0$ implies nonnegative cost for a trapezoid based on the whole face, including a tent with $c=d$. With a positive outer trimming length, $U\ge0$ alone does not fix the sign of the signed cost. For an already justified face variation with signed normal speed $H/2$, the profile term is one half this integral.

pk-intake-midpoint-compression-packing-a.relation_to_goal: Finite fractional convex-hull packing with fixed geometric source sites. The comparison controls packing value; it does not assert mixed halfspace depth monotonicity.
pk-intake-midpoint-compression-packing-a.statement:
For a finite source set $S\subset\mathbb R^n$ with nonnegative capacities $w$, let $f_w(z)$ be the largest total weight of a fractional packing of nonempty groups $G\subseteq S$ with $z\in\operatorname{conv}G$, where the sum of the weights of groups using a site $p$ is at most $w_p$. Let $u,v\in S$ be distinct with $m=(u+v)/2\in S$, and let $0\le\delta\le\min(w_u,w_v)$. For every target $z$,
$$
 f_{w-\delta e_u-\delta e_v+2\delta e_m}(z)\le f_w(z)+\delta,\qquad
 f_{w-\delta e_u-\delta e_v+\delta e_m}(z)\le f_w(z),
$$
where $e_p$ is the coordinate unit capacity at $p$. The latter compression loses total capacity $\delta$.

pk-intake-midpoint-correction-own-depth-.relation_to_goal: The bound concerns every midpoint-closed assignment of one mark per fiber and its sum of ordinary own-depth charges. The source meets the sharper mixed-depth target via an actual point.
pk-intake-midpoint-correction-own-depth-.statement:
Let $I_{-1}=I_1=[-1/2,1/2]$, $I_0=[-11/20,19/20]$, and $J=[-1/2,1/2]$. Take the convex hull of the lifted rectangles $I_j\times J$ at integer bases $j=-1,0,1$, then pad the base by $[0,1]^{n-1}$ for any $n\ge1$. The actual integer fibers are the stated rectangles in every binary copy, with total area $M=2^{n-1}(7/2)$ and $k=2^n$ occupied parities. Every fiber has area strictly less than $M/k$.

For any choice of marks in these fibers whose graph contains the midpoint of every pair of marks on congruent bases modulo two, the sum of their raw ordinary own depths is at most $2^{n-1}(31/20)<(4/9)M$. The midpoint-closed interval construction obtained by omitting $J$ at $n=1$ has exact maximum total own depth $31/20<7/4$. In contrast, the rectangle source has an actual point of raw mixed depth at least $33/40>7/9=(4/9)M/k$ in each binary copy. The corresponding point in the interval source has raw mixed depth exactly $33/20$.

pk-intake-midpoint-label-balanced-face-a.relation_to_goal: Finite atomic face-incidence rigidity for positive weights with actual same-label midpoint membership.
pk-intake-midpoint-label-balanced-face-a.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite subset of a real affine space, with $k$ occupied labels. Assume the geometric midpoint of every pair of distinct points of the same label belongs to $P$. Give each $p\in P$ a weight $w_p>0$, put $M=\sum_{p\in P}w_p$, $Q=\operatorname{conv}(P)$ and $\alpha=M/k$, and set $w(F)=\sum_{p\in P\cap F}w_p$ for each face $F$ of $Q$, allowing $Q$ itself. Let $\mathcal F$ be the faces of weight $\alpha$, and write $\chi_F$ for their incidence vectors on $P$.

Exactly one of the following holds.

1. There is $v\in\mathbb R^P$ with $\sum_{p\in P}v_p=0$ and $v\cdot\chi_F<0$ for every $F\in\mathcal F$. When $\mathcal F$ is empty, $v=0$ works.
2. The set $P$ consists of exactly $k$ vertices of $Q$, all of weight $\alpha$.

Moreover, a nonnegative combination $\sum_{F\in\mathcal F}\lambda_F\chi_F=\mathbf 1_P$ exists precisely in case 2. In that case its coefficients are $\lambda_{\{p\}}=1$ for all $p\in P$.

pk-intake-midpoint-label-strict-minimal-.relation_to_goal: A finite weighted centerpoint with a strict original minimal-face mass alternative for midpoint-closed labels.
pk-intake-midpoint-label-strict-minimal-.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in a real affine space with $k$ occupied labels. For every pair of distinct points of the same label, assume their geometric midpoint belongs to $P$. Give the points positive weights $w_p$, with total $M=\sum_{p\in P}w_p$. Let $Q=\operatorname{conv}(P)$ and let $F_p$ be the unique face of $Q$ whose relative interior contains $p$, allowing $Q$ itself. Write $w(F)=\sum_{p\in P\cap F}w_p$ and let $\delta_w(p)$ be the minimum weight in any closed affine halfspace containing $p$. The whole-space trace is allowed and is the sole trace containing $p$ in rank zero.

There exists $p\in P$ with $\delta_w(p)\ge M/k$. Such a point can be chosen with $w(F_p)>M/k$ except exactly when $P$ consists of $k$ vertices of $Q$ of weight $M/k$ each. In the exception every point has $\delta_w(p)=w(F_p)=M/k$. In particular, strict minimal-face mass holds for some center whenever $|P|>k$.

For a finite nonempty complete subset $P=Q\cap(c+L)$ of an affine lattice, the labels can be the occupied cosets modulo $2L$. Then $k\le 2^{\operatorname{rank} L}$, including rank zero. E(Y)=\inf_{L>0\text{ on }C}\int_S L(W)^{-p}\,d\mu(W),\qquad L(W)=1+a\cdot(W-Y),

with the parameter in the actual relative linear span. Let $F$ be the minimal face of $\operatorname{conv}P$ containing $b$, $S_F$ the union of fibers over $P\cap F$, $C_F=\operatorname{conv}S_F$, and $\mu_F=\mu|_{S_F}$. \int_{S_F}(W-Y)L^{-p-1}\,d\mu_F=0,\qquad

pk-intake-monotone-line-shell-superlevel.statement:
Let $w_0\ge\cdots\ge w_N\ge0$, extend by zero off $\{0,\dots,N\}$, and put $S_j=\sum_{i=0}^j w_i$ for $0\le j\le N$, with $S_{-1}=0$. $$
R_j=S_{\min(2j,N)}-S_j,\quad
F_j=\min\{S_{\min(2j,N)},S_N-S_{j-1}+S_{\min(2j,N)}-S_j\}.
$$
Every superlevel of $F$ is an integer interval, possibly empty. The interval assertion also holds for nondecreasing weights. For a nonempty finite family of such monotone profiles on the same base, if their chosen superlevel intervals are nonempty and pairwise intersect, they have a common integer anchor.

$$
\tau_{p,0}=t,\qquad \tau_{p,i}=t+w_i[r_p-(d+1)t]\quad(1\le i\le d).
$$
Then $G_j(t\mathbf1)=\min_{i\in\{0,1\}}\min_{a,w}F_i(t;a,w)$. The tilt can be restricted to one compact set uniformly in $i,t,w$. $$
\|\xi\|_\infty\le \left(\max_{p\in P}\max\{r_p,r_j\}\right)\max_I\|V_I^{-1}\|_\infty,

where the rows of $V_I$ are any $m$ independent rows $v_p^{\mathsf T}$ and the matrix norm is the maximum absolute row sum. When $m=0$ take $a=0$. The depth is continuous in $t$.

If $n=1$ and $r_p=r_j+s_-(p-j)$ on $p\le j$ and $r_p=r_j+s_+(p-j)$ on $p\ge j$, with $s_-\ge s_+$, the roof branch $i\ge1$ can instead use threshold $t+w_i[r_j-(d+1)t]$ and left and right tilts $a_\pm=a-w_i s_\pm$.
