$$
P_j(y)=\inf_{a\in\mathbb R^n,\ w\in\mathcal W_d}\sum_{p\in P}
\left|r_pT_d\cap\{X:a\cdot\Delta_p+w\cdot X\ge w\cdot y\}\right|.

$$
\Sigma_j=M_j^{-1}\sum_z\int_{K_{j,z}}(X-g_{j,z})(X-g_{j,z})^{\mathsf T}\,dX,

a\cdot(z-p)+u\cdot(X-y)+\varepsilon\bigl(U(p,y)E_{K_{j,p}}(y)/M_j\bigr)^{1/N}
\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_j u}\ge0,\qquad u\ne0 .

$$

On the critical tangent, writing a vertex velocity as $B=b\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}+E$ with $b$ its diagonal, the group threshold velocities are all $b$, the matrix $E$ has zero diagonal, row and column sums, and the constrained Lagrangian Hessian is $-V\|E\|_F^2/m$.

This applies to the $m$ cyclic groups with $a_{gg}=1-d/(3m)$ and $a_{gi}=1/(3m)$ for $i\ne g$, and to the three planar cyclic permutations of $(4/5,1/10,1/10)$.

pk-intake-moving-section-positive-anchor.relation_to_goal: Fiberwise moving-section estimates for an auxiliary concave parameter. They do not exclude logarithmic defects on collapsing sections away from the assigned contact fibers.
pk-intake-moving-section-positive-anchor.statement:
If $D$ is an $m$-dimensional compact convex set, $m\ge1$, and $F:D\to[0,\infty)$ is concave with $F(x_0)\ge c>0$ at some $x_0\in D$, then
$$
|\{F<t\}|_m\le [1-(1-t/c)^m]|D|_m\le (m|D|_m/c)t\quad(0<t<c).
$$
In particular, for $B\ge0$ with $e^{-B}<c$, the integral of $(-\log F)_+$ over $\{(-\log F)_+>B\}$ is at most $(m|D|_m/c)(B+1)e^{-B}$.

Let full-dimensional compact convex $K_j\subset\mathbb R^d$ in a common ball converge in Hausdorff distance to full-dimensional $K$. Let $L_j$ be positive concave on $K_j$, with uniform convergence on the common compact range to a continuous $L$ that is nonnegative on $K$ and positive on its interior. Put $\Pi_j=\{u_j\cdot X=t_j\}$, with $(u_j,t_j)\to(u,t)$ and $|u_j|\ge b_*>0$, $D_j=K_j\cap\Pi_j$, and $0\le\lambda_j\le |u_j|^{-1}\mathcal H^{d-1}|_{D_j}$. Take a subsequence with $\lambda_j\rightharpoonup\lambda$ and $(-\log L_j)_+\lambda_j\rightharpoonup\mu$ finite. The section-log defect is $s=\mu|_{\{L=0\}}$. Uniformly positive section anchors imply $s=0$ and $\mu=(-\log L)_+\lambda$, as does a limiting plane $\Pi=\{u\cdot X=t\}$ meeting the interior of $K$. If $s\ne0$, every retained Hausdorff limit of the nonempty $D_j$ is contained in $\{L=0\}\cap K$.

If additionally $L$ on $K$ is a finite minimum of affine functions and $\sup_j\int_{K_j}1/L_j<\infty$, then each exposed affine zero face has dimension at most $d-2$ for $d\ge2$. A nonzero $s$ then forces $\mathcal H^{d-1}(D_j)\to0$ and $\lambda_j(D_j)\to0$ along its retained subsequence. For $d=1$ the section measure uses counting measure, a uniformly positive anchor suffices directly, and the finite-affine and inverse-integral hypotheses imply that $L$ has no zero in $K$.

pk-intake-moving-simplex-cap-group-affin.relation_to_goal: Fixed continuous normals and prescribed affine group sums. Free physical vertex stationarity requires an open feasible chart, and cap stationarity gives no global depth conclusion.
pk-intake-moving-simplex-cap-group-affin.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $m=d+1$, and $L_i$, $1\le i\le m$, be barycentric affine coordinates of a simplex $T$, with $\sum_i L_i=1$. At a finite set of sampled bases take reference fibers $K_z=c_z+r_zT$, $r_z>0$, of volumes $V_z$. Their labeled vertex evaluations are $b_{zi}+r_z\delta_{ij}$ in row $i$ and column $j$. For each group $g$, the caps $\{L_i(x)\ge a_{gi}(z)\}$ have affine thresholds in $z$ and fixed continuous normals. The allowed threshold motions $h_{gi}(z)$ are affine with $\sum_i h_{gi}=0$ identically. Each group's whole-plane cover region $\{\sum_i a_{gi}(z)\le1\}$ is preserved. Work in the open chamber with proper or strictly saturated traces and write, for a proper trace,
$$
t_{giz}=(a_{gi}(z)-b_{zi})/r_z,\qquad
D_{giz}=dV_z(1-t_{giz})^{d-1}/r_z,
$$
and $D_{giz}=0$ for saturated traces. Its global cap derivative in a threshold direction is $-\sum_z D_{giz}h_{gi}(z)$. With multipliers $\ell_{gi}\ge0$, threshold stationarity of total volume minus weighted cap masses is equivalent to
$$
\ell_{gi}\sum_z D_{giz}(1,z)=\nu_g\qquad\text{for every }i
$$
for a common vector $\nu_g$ per group.

When all physical vertex velocities are independently available on an open actual chart, set
$$
e_{zi}=\sum_{g:\,\mathrm{proper}}\ell_{gi}(1-t_{giz})^d,\qquad
\chi_{zi}=\sum_{g:\,\mathrm{proper}}d\ell_{gi}(1-t_{giz})^d[(1-t_{giz})^{-1}-1],
$$
and $w_z=1-\sum_{g,i:\,\mathrm{strictly\ full\ at}\ z}\ell_{gi}$. If $d\ge2$, the additional physical stationarity conditions are $e_{zi}=e_z$ independent of $i$ and $\chi_{zi}=w_z-de_z$ for all $i$. If $d=1$, these conditions are instead $e_{zi}+\chi_{zi}=w_z$ for each $i$.

For a single reference simplex with proper concurrent groups of normalized thresholds $a_{gi}$, the joint stationarity conditions for $d\ge2$ are that $\kappa_g=\ell_{gi}(1-a_{gi})^{d-1}$ be independent of $i$, $\sum_g\kappa_g=1/d$, and $\sum_g\kappa_g a_{gi}=1/(dm)$ for every $i$. When $d=1$ only the independence of $\kappa_g=\ell_{gi}$ from $i$ and $\sum_g\kappa_g=1$ are required.

pk-intake-multiple-small-shell-fibers-an.relation_to_goal: The credit is for one clamped vertex in the stated shell. Exactness for arbitrary extra shapes requires a common anchor.
pk-intake-multiple-small-shell-fibers-an.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, $d\ge2$, and let $T\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a $d$-simplex of volume $V$ and centroid $g$. Use $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ and the reflected simplex profile minimum $\rho_d$ from fact 53fe12b742a7608d. Let an actual compact convex source have fibers $T$ at all bases of $Q=\lbrace0,1\rbrace^n$. Suppose the positive-volume fibers outside $Q$ have bases $p\in[-1,2]^n\cap\mathbb Z^n\setminus Q$ and are bodies $A_p\subseteq T$. Define $q(p)$ by clipping the coordinates of $p$ to $[0,1]$, and put $E_q=\sum_{q(p)=q}|A_p|$. If $E_q\le\rho_d V$, the raw mixed closed-halfspace depth of $(q,g)$ is at least $\Gamma_d V+E_q$.

Conversely choose a nonempty subset of the shell bases having the same $q(p)=q$ and place any positive convex bodies $A_p\subseteq T$ there. The convex hull of these and the binary simplex fibers has exactly the assigned integer fibers. If their extra mass $E$ is at most $\rho_d V$, its unique maximizing mixed-integer point is $(q,g)$, with raw depth $\Gamma_d V+E$ and normalized depth $(\Gamma_d+E/V)/(2^n+E/V)$. In particular along $E=tW+o(t)$ the normalized right derivative at $t=0$ is $W(2^n-\Gamma_d)/(4^n V)$.

pk-intake-near-centroid-planar-low-cap-l.relation_to_goal: Explicit ordinary planar cap geometry; no deletion or other-body hypothesis.
pk-intake-near-centroid-planar-low-cap-l.statement: Let $S$ be a nondegenerate triangle with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\lambda_1,\lambda_2$. If $|\lambda_i(y)-1/3|\le1/10000$ for all $i$, every closed halfspace through $y$ capturing at most $(4/9+1/10000)|S|$ strictly isolates one vertex $i$ and has the equation $A_j\lambda_j+A_k\lambda_k\le1$ for the other indices $j,k$, with equality at $y$ and $29/20<A_j,A_k<31/20$. In particular a direction through a vertex of $S$ cannot satisfy the area threshold.

pk-intake-near-grunbaum-common-contact-l.relation_to_goal: Controls a single actual ordinary convex body under a common-contact whole-space cap cover.
pk-intake-near-grunbaum-common-contact-l.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, $d\ge2$, with centroid $g$. Put $D=K-K$, let $\|\cdot\|_D$ be its gauge, and write $\gamma_j=(j/(j+1))^j$ for $j\ge1$. Suppose finitely many closed halfspaces $H_i=\{x:\ell_i(x-y)\ge0\}$ cover $\mathbb R^d$, where each $\ell_i$ has width one on $K$. Assume $|K\cap H_i|\le\tau|K|$ for every $i$, with $\gamma_d\le\tau<\gamma_{d-1}$. Then $y\in\operatorname{int}K$, and for every $v\in\partial D$,
$$
\max_i\ell_i(v)\ge\frac{\gamma_{d-1}-\tau}{d}.
$$
Equivalently, the convex hull of the $\ell_i$ contains $(\gamma_{d-1}-\tau)D^\circ/d$, where $D^\circ$ is the polar. Moreover,
$$
\|y-g\|_D
\le\min\left\{1,\frac{d^2(\tau-\gamma_d)}{\gamma_{d-1}-\tau}\right\}.
$$
In particular $\tau=\gamma_d$ forces $y=g$. If $0\le\epsilon=\tau-\gamma_d\le(\gamma_{d-1}-\gamma_d)/2$, the bound is at most $2d^2\epsilon/(\gamma_{d-1}-\gamma_d)$.

pk-intake-near-triangle-planar-convex-un.relation_to_goal: Ordinary planar uniform area, arbitrary convex boundaries and explicit local affine radius. Controls the total missing area of the constructed triangle, with cap distance bounded above by that area fraction.
pk-intake-near-triangle-planar-convex-un.statement:
Let $Q$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body in $\mathbb R^2$ and suppose that some invertible affine map $A$ makes $\delta=d_{H,\infty}(AQ,\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2))\le10^{-6}$. There is a triangle $S\supseteq Q$ constructed from three supporting lines, with $\tau=1-|Q|/|S|\le81\delta$, such that its normalized maximal ordinary halfspace depth satisfies
$$
D(Q)-4/9\ge\frac{\tau/90-9\tau^2/4}{1-\tau}\ge\tau/180.
$$
The uniform probability measures obey $d_{\rm cap}(\mu_Q,\mu_S)\le\operatorname{TV}(\mu_Q,\mu_S)=\tau$, where cap distance is the supremum of the absolute probability difference over closed halfspaces and total variation is the supremum over measurable sets. In particular $\inf_{S'}d_{\rm cap}(\mu_Q,\mu_{S'})\le180[D(Q)-4/9]$ over full-dimensional triangles.

pk-intake-near-triangle-quadrilateral-en.relation_to_goal: Ordinary planar quadrilaterals in the explicit affine Hausdorff neighborhood; exact cap-distance equality for the constructed enclosing triangle.
pk-intake-near-triangle-quadrilateral-en.statement:
Let $Q$ be a full-dimensional convex quadrilateral and suppose that some invertible affine map $A$ makes $d_{H,\infty}(AQ,\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2))\le1/240000$. Then there is an enclosing triangle $S\supseteq Q$ with
$$
\tau=1-|Q|/|S|\le45\bigl[D(Q)-4/9\bigr],\qquad
d_{\rm cap}(\mu_Q,\mu_S)=\tau .
$$
Here $D(Q)$ is maximal normalized ordinary halfspace depth, $\mu_Q,\mu_S$ are uniform probability measures, and $d_{\rm cap}$ is the supremum of their absolute mass difference over closed halfspaces. Consequently $D(Q)-4/9\ge(1/45)\inf_{S'}d_{\rm cap}(\mu_Q,\mu_{S'})$ over all full-dimensional triangles $S'$.

pk-intake-negative-minimum-dispersion-cr.relation_to_goal: The universal form of the sufficient sign condition in candidate e239a5fb0d0efe4d §6 (11), namely nonnegative credit for a selected actual rank-two three-cap group on planar mixed-integer fibers. The normalized maximum depth is above the sharp target, and the separate conditional regimes of a subthreshold budget or a locally minimizing body are outside the claim.
pk-intake-negative-minimum-dispersion-cr.statement:
In the planar three-cap aggregation, let the positive integer fibers be partitioned into ownership groups $P_i$. Each group has three actual closed ambient caps $H_{i,j}$ of mixed mass at most $B$, with restrictions on each owned fiber that cover its whole plane and whose normals span that plane with a strictly positive dependence. For each group let $L_i$ be the sum over owned fibers of the minimum of the three local cap areas, and let $X_i$ be the sum of the three cap masses outside the owned fibers, counted with multiplicity. The unconditional inequality $\sum_i X_i\ge (3/4)\sum_i(B-L_i)$ fails even for a single group whose caps are all active at the same globally deepest point of a full-dimensional mixed-integer convex body.

Specifically, take $C=\{(z,x,y):-1\le z\le1,\ |x-z/2|\le1,\ |y|\le1\}$ in $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2$. The actual integer fibers are $K_z=[z/2-1,z/2+1]\times[-1,1]$ at $z=-1,0,1$. Their total mixed area is $M=12$, and the origin attains the global maximum raw depth $6$, or normalized depth $1/2$. The one group owns every fiber and uses $H_1=\{x\ge0\}$, $H_2=\{y\ge0\}$ and $H_3=\{x+y\le0\}$. Each has mixed mass $B=6$, and all three traces are positive proper cuts on every owned fiber. In this group $X=0$, $L=33/8$, and $X-(3/4)(B-L)=-45/32$. The actual local overlap surpluses above the coefficient $3/4$ sum to $93/32$.

pk-intake-negative-power-affine-buffer-p.relation_to_goal: This is a two-sided affine parameter derivative for a fixed mixed body. It supplies the exact factor for a cap continuation when that continuation is available.
pk-intake-negative-power-affine-buffer-p.statement:
Fix a compact canonical hull $C$ with positive mixed fiber mass, and write $\langle\cdot\rangle$ for its mixed probability integral over the sampled fibers. Let $d\ge1$, $N=d+1$, $r\ge d$ and let $L$ be affine and positive on $C$ with $\langle L^{-r}\rangle=1$. For every affine $\phi$, both signs of sufficiently small $t$ are allowed in the normalized perturbation
$$
L_t=(L+t\phi)\,\langle(L+t\phi)^{-r}\rangle^{1/r}.
$$
Then $\dot L=\phi-L\langle L^{-r-1}\phi\rangle$ at $t=0$. At every fixed mark with positive projective energy, for $f_L=(LE/M)^{1/N}$ with the energy $E$ and mass $M$ fixed, the derivative is
$$
\frac{\dot f_L}{f_L}=\frac1N\left(\frac{\phi}{L}-\langle L^{-r-1}\phi\rangle\right).
$$

pk-intake-negative-power-affine-paramete.relation_to_goal: This classifies parameter limits and the actual centroid multipliers under joint variation of the positive fibers. Buffered bad-attainment additionally needs a base-depth choice in the complement of a limiting zero face.
pk-intake-negative-power-affine-paramete.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, let $P$ be a fixed nonempty finite base, and let $\mathcal A$ be a compact family in the simultaneous Hausdorff metric of tuples of positive convex $d$-fibers $K_z$, $z\in P$, of total volume one, with every fiber volume at least $v>0$ and all fibers contained in a fixed ball. Use mixed measure $\mu_K=\sum_z\delta_z\otimes(\mathbf 1_{K_z}\,dX)$, its centroid $m_K$, and $C_K=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_z(\{z\}\times K_z)$. There is $\rho>0$ such that every $C_K$ contains the relative $\rho$-ball about $m_K$. Hence the affine functions $h\ge0$ on $C_K$ with $\int h\,d\mu_K=1$ have relative linear coefficient norm at most $1/\rho$ and uniformly bounded constant coefficients in fixed relative affine coordinates.

Fix $r\ge d$. For every sequence $K_j\in\mathcal A$ and affine $L_j>0$ on $C_{K_j}$ with $\int L_j^{-r}\,d\mu_{K_j}=1$, there is a subsequence with $K_j\to K\in\mathcal A$ and $h_j=L_j/\int L_j\,d\mu_{K_j}$ converging coefficientwise to an affine $h\ge0$ on $C_K$ of mixed mean one. If $h>0$ on $C_K$, then $L_j$ converges coefficientwise to a finite positive normalized affine parameter on $C_K$. Otherwise $\int L_j\,d\mu_{K_j}\to+\infty$. In this second case, write $g_{j,z}$ for the actual centroid of $K_{j,z}$. If $h$ has nonzero continuous coefficient then $L_j(z,g_{j,z})\to+\infty$ for every $z\in P$. If its continuous coefficient vanishes, its base zero set is a nonempty proper exposed face $F$ of $\operatorname{conv}P$ and the same divergence holds for each $z\in P\setminus F$.

pk-intake-negative-power-full-affine-buf.relation_to_goal: This proves covariance of the normalized parameter and the actual covariance-buffered caps under the common continuous affine maps and base-dependent continuous shears.
pk-intake-negative-power-full-affine-buf.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $N=d+1$ and $r\ge d$. Let $P$ be a finite complete canonical lattice base with positive compatible convex $d$-fibers $K_z$. Put $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$, $C=\operatorname{conv}S$, $M=\sum_z|K_z|$ and let $\langle\cdot\rangle$ be integration against the mixed probability measure on $S$ with density $1/M$ on each fiber. Take $L$ affine on $\operatorname{aff}P\times\mathbb R^d$, positive on $C$, and normalized by $\langle L^{-r}\rangle=1$. Write $g_z$ for the centroid of $K_z$, $E_{K_z}(y)$ for marked projective energy extended by zero to the boundary, and put
$$
f_L(z,y)=\left(\frac{L(z,y)E_{K_z}(y)}{M}\right)^{1/N},\qquad
G_K(u)^2=\frac1M\sum_z\int_{K_z}[u\cdot(X-g_z)]^2\,dX.
$$
Under any map $(z,X)\mapsto(z,AX+Bz+c)$ with invertible $A$, transport $L$ by composition with the inverse map. Then positivity and inverse-power normalization are preserved, $f_L$ agrees at corresponding marks and $G_K$ agrees at corresponding continuous covectors $u'=A^{-\mathsf T}u$. The shifted caps using displacement $\varepsilon f_LG_K$ correspond exactly and have the same normalized mass, as do pure-base caps.

pk-intake-nested-fiberwise-minkowski-ext.relation_to_goal: Nested sampled-fiber enlargement for q=d inside a fixed ambient body, with explicit centroid drift even when the endpoint bases agree.
pk-intake-nested-fiberwise-minkowski-ext.statement:
Let $D\subseteq C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be ambient convex bodies with positive mixed $d$-mass for $D$, and let $P_D=\{z:|D_z|_d>0\}$. For $0\le t\le1$ the fibers $E_z(t)=(1-t)D_z+t C_z$, $z\in P_D$, are nested in $t$ and have an ambient convex realization in $C$ with exactly these integer fibers. If $w_z(t)=|E_z(t)|_d$, $m(t)=\sum_z w_z(t)$, and $j(t)$ is the base centroid, then
$
j(t)=\frac{\sum_z z\,w_z(t)}{m(t)},\qquad
j'(0)=\frac{\sum_z(z-j(0))w'_z(0)}{m(0)},\qquad
w'_z(0)=d[V(D_z[d-1],C_z)-|D_z|_d]\ge0 .
$
Even if $j(0)=j(1)\in\mathbb Z^n$, the intermediate base centroid can leave that integer. In $n=1,d=2$, take bases $-1,0,1$, unit square endpoint fibers for $D$, a common middle fiber $[0,3]\times[0,3/2]$, and endpoint fibers $[0,4]\times[0,1]$, $[0,2]\times[0,2]$ for $C$, respectively. Then $j(0)=j(1)=0$ and $j(t)=(t^2-t)/(13/2+5t+t^2)<0$ for $0<t<1$.

pk-intake-nested-three-fiber-depth.relation_to_goal: The common-core center and the $\gamma_d/2$ lower bound for inclusion-ordered compatible triples, with $n=1$ and arbitrary $d\ge1$.
pk-intake-nested-three-fiber-depth.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, and let $A,B,C\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies with $(A+C)/2\subseteq B$. Set $S=(\{-1\}\times A)\cup(\{0\}\times B)\cup(\{1\}\times C)$, measured by summing $d$-dimensional volumes on its three fibers. If a convex body $K$ satisfies $A\subseteq K\subseteq B\cap C$, let $a=|A|$, $V=|K|$, $E=|B|+|C|-2V$ and let $g_K$ be the volume centroid of $K$. Then the actual point $(0,g_K)$ has normalized mixed halfspace depth at least
$$
\frac{\gamma_d V+a/2}{2V+E+a}.
$$
This is at least $\gamma_d/2$ if $E\le(1/\gamma_d-1)a$. In particular, for $B=C=K$ the displayed bound holds with $E=0$, and the same conclusion holds at the actual middle centroid when $B$ and $C$ are translates of one another, taking $V=|B|$.

If $A,B,C$ are totally ordered by inclusion, some actual mixed point has normalized depth at least $\gamma_d/2$. The same holds if such an order is obtained by an affine change preserving $\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R^d$, including a shear affine in the integer base.

pk-intake-nested-triangle-unequal-positi.relation_to_goal: Obstruction to a specified positive-normal menu at one prescribed centroid. No unrestricted infimum is asserted.
pk-intake-nested-triangle-unequal-positi.statement:
Put $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2)$ and $V=|T|=1/2$. Take the convex hull of the three fibers $r_zT$ at $z=-1,0,1$ with radii $(1/2,3/2,3/4)$. For the actual middle centroid $y=(0,1/2,1/2)$, let $\mu$ sum the areas of the integer fibers, and write
$$
H_{a,\beta}=\{(z,x):a x_1+(1-a)x_2+\beta z\ge1/2\},\qquad 1/2\le a\le1,\quad\beta\in\mathbb R.
$$
Then the infima of $\mu(H_{a,\beta})/V$ over $\beta$ for $a=1$ and $a=1/2$ are $33/32$ and $5/4$, respectively. They are attained at $\beta=-1/8$ and at every $\beta\in[-1/4,1/8]$, respectively. Interchanging the coordinates gives the same minimum for the other coordinate normal. At $(a,\beta)=(6/7,-3/28)$ the mass in units of $V$ is $81/80$, with strict gap $3/160$ below the coordinate minimum. Thus restricting normalized nonnegative continuous normals to the two coordinate normals and the equal-coefficient normal can increase the infimum even with arbitrary shared tilt.

pk-intake-neutral-cover-does-not-preserv.relation_to_goal: Refutes continuation of a prescribed deepest path from exact cover neutrality and zero normalized retained derivative. It does not refute the locked weak Oertel conjecture.
pk-intake-neutral-cover-does-not-preserv.statement: Even with an actual nested convex-cut erosion, exact neutrality of an old critical cover and zero first derivative of the normalized retained mass on a prescribed path through the old deepest point do not imply that the path remains deepest. For any $n\ge0$, take $[-1/4,1/4]^n\times[-1,1]$ with only measured base $0$ and continuous dimension $1$, and impose the cuts $x+\varepsilon\le1$ and $-x+\varepsilon\le1$. For $0<\varepsilon<1/2$ the old covering halfspaces $x\ge0$ and $x\le0$ each still have half the mixed mass. The mark $(0,\varepsilon^2)$ has zero first derivative of normalized retained mass at zero, but its raw depth is $1-\varepsilon-\varepsilon^2$, strictly smaller than the new deepest depth $1-\varepsilon$.

pk-intake-nine-base-actual-zero-slack-ce.relation_to_goal: Atomic depth at the original volume-weighted centroid graph points. The original continuous mixed depth has a separate lower bound at graph point 1 by the accepted paired-tail theorem.
pk-intake-nine-base-actual-zero-slack-ce.statement:
Let $Q=\operatorname{conv}\{(1,1),(3,-2),(4,3)\}$, let $K=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:x\ge0,\ \sum_i x_i\le1\}$ for $d\ge1$, and for $R\ge0$ let $C$ be the compact convex body with fibers $K_z=(R+t(z))K$ over $z\in Q$, where $t(z)=\min\{14,17-z_1-2z_2\}$. In index order from zero its nine positive integer bases are
$$
(1,1),(2,0),(2,1),(3,-2),(3,-1),(3,0),(3,1),(3,2),(4,3),
$$
with values $(14,14,13,14,14,14,12,10,7)$ of $t$. The volume-maximal parity roots, with ties broken by minimum base Euclidean norm, are $0,1,2,5$. Every edge of the corresponding root-midpoint forest is an exact Minkowski midpoint of the original child fiber and its designated parity root.

Give each actual centroid graph point its original fiber volume as atomic weight and divide by the total. The maximum of closed-halfspace depth over graph points is exactly
$$
\frac{2(R+14)^d}{5(R+14)^d+(R+13)^d+(R+12)^d+(R+10)^d+(R+7)^d}.
$$
For $d=1$ this equals $2(R+14)/(9R+112)$, equals $1/4$ at $R=0$ and is strictly below $1/4$ for $R>0$. At $R=21$ it is $70/301=10/43$, with gap $3/172$ from $1/4$. For each $d$ it tends to $2/9$ as $R\to\infty$, and the choice $R=63d-7$ already gives strict failure of $1/4$.

pk-intake-non-even-subunit-radial-gauge.relation_to_goal: The subunit positive exponents for an integrable log-concave density with an interior positive anchor complement the accepted p≥1 result.
pk-intake-non-even-subunit-radial-gauge.statement:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to[0,\infty)\) be integrable and log-concave, where \(n\ge1\) and \(0\) is interior to \(\{f>0\}\). For every \(0<p<1\), the function
$$
q_p(x)=\left(\int_0^\infty t^{p-1} f(tx)\,dt\right)^{-1/p}\quad (x\ne0),\qquad q_p(0)=0
$$
is finite, continuous, convex and positively homogeneous. Its unit sublevel set is a compact convex body containing \(0\) in its interior.

pk-intake-nonatomic-rank-one-local-polyg.relation_to_goal: Local planar repair with proportional residuals or at most three compatible fibers under the stated domination. The cap guards are fixed before approximation.
pk-intake-nonatomic-rank-one-local-polyg.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and nonempty, with planar convex bodies of nonempty interior and support functions $h_z$ satisfying every Jensen support inequality
$$
h_z\ge\sum_{w\in P}p_wh_w,\qquad p_w\ge0,\quad\sum_wp_w=1,\quad\sum_wp_ww=z.
$$
Let $I=[a,b]$ be a closed normal interval with $0<b-a<\pi$. Fix a finite list of prescribed caps for each fiber. For each such cap, given by a fixed halfplane, suppose the entire exposed boundary arc over $I$ is on one strict side of its cap line, at a uniformly positive distance. Let $B_z$ be the homogeneous solution of $B_z''+B_z=0$ matching $h_z$ at $a,b$, and put $f_z=h_z-B_z$.

Suppose the curvature measures $R_z=h_z''+h_z$ are nonatomic on $I$ and $f_z=c_z f$ with $c_z>0$ for one $f\in H_0^1(I)$ with finite, nonzero, positive curvature source $\nu=f''+f$ on $\operatorname{int} I$. Then there are arbitrarily close simultaneous replacements by actual convex bodies, piecewise homogeneous on a common finite mesh on $I$, with supports unchanged outside $\operatorname{int} I$. All Jensen inequalities, individual areas and prescribed cap areas are preserved exactly. Endpoint facets are allowed.

In particular, the same conclusion holds for at most three distinct base points if instead $c\nu\le R_z\le C\nu$ on $I$ for a nonzero finite nonatomic positive measure $\nu$ and $0<c\le C<\infty$, and both endpoints are inward accumulation points of $\operatorname{supp}\nu$. This includes $C^2$ supports on a neighborhood of $I$ with strictly positive curvature on $I$.

pk-intake-nonatomic-tensor-affine-local-.relation_to_goal: Exact planar arc replacement under common nonatomic curvature domination and tensor independence, for finite compatible fibers with prescribed cap guards.
pk-intake-nonatomic-tensor-affine-local-.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and nonempty. Let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^2$, $z\in P$, be convex bodies with interior, with support functions $h_z$ satisfying every Jensen support inequality
$$
h_z\ge\sum_{w\in P}p_wh_w,\qquad p_w\ge0,\quad \sum_w p_w=1,\quad \sum_w p_ww=z.
$$
Fix a closed normal interval $I=[a,b]$ with $0<b-a<\pi$. Suppose on $I$ the curvature measures $R_z=h_z''+h_z$ satisfy $c\nu\le R_z\le C\nu$ for some finite nonzero nonatomic positive measure $\nu$ and constants $0<c\le C<\infty$. Both endpoints of $I$ are inward accumulation points of $\operatorname{supp}\nu$. Fix a finite list of prescribed caps for each fiber. For each such cap, given by a fixed halfplane, suppose the entire exposed boundary arc over $I$ lies on one strict side of its cap line, at a uniformly positive distance. Let $B_z$ be the homogeneous solution of $B_z''+B_z=0$ with the same two endpoint values as $h_z$, and let $f_z=h_z-B_z\in H_0^1(I)$. Assume the tensors $(1,z)\otimes f_z$ are linearly independent.

There are arbitrarily close simultaneous replacements by actual convex bodies whose supports are piecewise homogeneous on a common finite mesh on $I$ and equal the old supports outside $\operatorname{int} I$. They preserve every Jensen support inequality, every individual area and every prescribed cap area. Endpoint facets are allowed. Zero-curvature endpoint portions may first be trimmed. If $\nu=0$ all the original supports are already homogeneous on $I$.

pk-intake-nonconvex-arithmetic-angular-v.relation_to_goal: Auxiliary angular-area convexification of the positive chart, with a separate interpolation requirement. The original mixed source and its central fiber have their usual measure.
pk-intake-nonconvex-arithmetic-angular-v.statement:
Let $C=[-3,3]\times[-1,1]$ have mixed measure equal to the sum of lengths on its seven integer fibers. In the positive projective chart $(z,x)=r(1,s)$, let $R(s)=\min(3,1/|s|)$, interpreted as $3$ at $s=0$, and $f_+(s)=\sum_{1\le k\le R(s)}k$. There is no compact planar convex set containing the origin whose ordinary angular area density in this chart is $f_+(s)$ almost everywhere.

Separately, no convex gauge on the positive chart can interpolate the reciprocal angular radii $1/\sqrt2,1/\sqrt6,1/\sqrt{12}$ at $s=1,1/2,1/3$, respectively. For the polynomial interpolation $F_1(R)=R(R+1)/2$ of the arithmetic sum, the candidate reciprocal radius on $1/3<s<1$ is $s/\sqrt{1+s}$ and is strictly concave there.

pk-intake-nonfacet-polytopal-truncation-.relation_to_goal: A geometric first-order perturbation bound for polytopes and ordinary fiber volume.
pk-intake-nonfacet-polytopal-truncation-.statement:
Let $K$ be a full-dimensional $d$-polytope, $d\ge2$. Let $n\ne0$ expose a face of dimension $k\le d-2$, and set $K(t)=K\cap\{n\cdot x\le h_K(n)-t\}$. For small $t\ge0$,
$$
h_{K(t)}(n)=h_K(n)-t,\qquad |K\setminus K(t)|=O(t^{d-k})=o(t).
$$
Uniformly for $m$ near $n$ and $t$ small, $h_K(m)-h_{K(t)}(m)\ge t(1-C\lVert m-n\rVert)$ for some $C$. Under nearby affine body motions and matched nearby directions this bound is $t-O(t|p|)$, where $p$ denotes the nearby parameters. Finitely many simultaneous cuts of this kind, with nonnegative depths $\sigma$, change volume and every halfspace cap volume by $o(|\sigma|)$, uniformly for nearby affine body motions and all caps.

pk-intake-nonhollow-joint-slice-affine-s.relation_to_goal: Support geometry for a non-hollow joint slice law on its original base. The affine offsets are support-plane offsets.
pk-intake-nonhollow-joint-slice-affine-s.statement: Let $n\ge0$, $N\ge1$, and let $\mu_z$ be nonzero finite positive Borel measures of compact support $S_z\subset\mathbb R^D$ indexed by a finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$. Suppose every combination $z=\sum_i\theta_i z_i\in\mathbb Z^n$, with $z_i\in P$, $\theta_i>0$, and $\sum_i\theta_i=1$, has $z\in P$ and satisfies $\mu_z(\sum_i\theta_i E_i)^{1/N}\ge\sum_i\theta_i\mu_{z_i}(E_i)^{1/N}$ for compact positive-mass $E_i$. If $\operatorname{relint}\operatorname{conv}(P)$ contains an integer point, then all supports have a common tangent space $V$. There is an affine map $b:\operatorname{aff}(P)\to V^\perp$ such that $S_z\subseteq b(z)+V$ for every $z\in P$. The hull of the placed supports has exactly those integer fibers. The affine shear $(z,x)\mapsto(z,x-b(z))$ fixes bases, preserves intrinsic fiber measure, and carries affine halfspaces to affine halfspaces in the space over $\operatorname{aff}(P)$.

pk-intake-normal-conditional-surface-bal.relation_to_goal: A comparison of actual conditional surface capacities at one tight midpoint of two bodies. It supplies no joint capacity sum over different triples.
pk-intake-normal-conditional-surface-bal.statement:
Let $A,B,K\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, be convex bodies with $(A+B)/2\subset K$, and let $Z=\{u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}:h_K(u)=(h_A(u)+h_B(u))/2\}$. For $L=A,B,K$, let $\eta_L$ be ordinary surface measure marked by its almost everywhere unique outer unit normal and let $S_L$ be the normal marginal. Put $\lambda=S_A+S_B+S_K$ and disintegrate $\eta_L(du,dx)=\lambda(du)\mu_{L,u}(dx)$ using finite kernels, with total mass $dS_L/d\lambda$. On one Borel $\lambda$-full normal set, for every $u\in Z$ there and every pair of open balls $B(c_-,a_-),B(c_+,a_+)$ with both endpoint conditional masses positive,
$$
 \mu_{K,u}\bigl(B((c_-+c_+)/2,(a_-+a_+)/2)\bigr)
 \ \ge\
 \left[\frac{\mu_{A,u}(B(c_-,a_-))^{1/(d-1)}
             +\mu_{B,u}(B(c_+,a_+))^{1/(d-1)}}{2}\right]^{d-1}.
$$

pk-intake-normal-localized-logarithmic-c.relation_to_goal: Conditional normal-localized inequality with possible mass deficit on the zero set. The full test cone, pointwise remainder and selector convergence remain hypotheses of an application. The result allows a nonzero defect and yields no numerical depth bound.
pk-intake-normal-localized-logarithmic-c.statement:
Let $U$ and $X$ be compact, with $U$ a metric space of recorded normals and $X$ in a finite-dimensional affine physical space. Let finite positive measures $\eta_j$ on $U\times X$ converge weakly to $\eta$. For each $j$ the physical projection of $\operatorname{supp}\eta_j$ lies in a compact convex body range on which the finite minimum of affine functions $L_j$ is positive. Assume the $L_j$ converge uniformly on $X$ to a nonnegative $L$, $\eta(Z)=0$ for $Z=\{(u,w):L(w)=0\}$, and $\sup_j\int \ell_{j,+}\,d\eta_j<\infty$, where $\ell_j=-\log L_j$ on the support of $\eta_j$. Suppose $0\le W_j\le1$, $W_j\eta_j\rightharpoonup W\eta$, $\beta_j\to\beta$, and $\lambda_j>0$ tends to zero. Assume $|R_j|\le C\lambda_j$ $\eta_j$-almost everywhere and that the common inequality
$$
\int \psi(u)\Phi(w)(W_j-\beta_j+\lambda_j\ell_j+R_j)\,d\eta_j\le0
$$
holds for every continuous $\psi\ge0$ and every globally finite convex $\Phi$ on the physical space.

The measures $\lambda_j\ell_{j,+}^2\eta_j$ have bounded masses. Along any joint weakly converging subsequence write the limits of $\ell_{j,+}\eta_j$, $W_j\ell_{j,+}\eta_j$, and $\lambda_j\ell_{j,+}^2\eta_j$ as $\ell_+\eta+b$, $W\ell_+\eta+a$, and $q$, respectively, with $\ell=-\log L$ off $Z$. Then $0\le a\le b$ and $q\ge0$, all three supported on $Z$. For every such $\psi$ and every nonnegative globally finite convex $f$,
$$
\int\psi(u)f(w)\,d(a+q)\le\beta\int\psi(u)f(w)\,db .
$$
In particular $a(U\times X)+q(U\times X)\le\beta b(U\times X)$.

pk-intake-normalized-physical-retained-r.relation_to_goal: A prescribed-mark mixed retained-mass response and a finite envelope conditional on actual deepest paths. No exact stationarity, tertiary selection or locked bound follows.
pk-intake-normalized-physical-retained-r.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty, $n\ge0$, and let the positive-volume $d$-dimensional fibers $K_{z,\varepsilon}$, $z\in P$, be those of an actual nested convex deformation with fixed measured sites $P$. Assume each fiber satisfies the homothet and almost-everywhere radial speed hypotheses of the physical retained-mass derivative theorem, with old fiber $K_z$ and inward speed $v_z$. Let
$$
M_\varepsilon=\sum_{z\in P}|K_{z,\varepsilon}|,\qquad
M=M_0,\qquad D_{\rm mix}=\sum_{z\in P}\int_{\partial K_z}v_z\,dS .
$$
Fix $p\in P$ and $y\in\operatorname{int}K_p$ and prescribe $y_\varepsilon=y+\varepsilon w+o(\varepsilon)$ in that fiber. Let $U_p$ be the old optimizing hinge set for $T=T_{K_p}(y)$ and put $\tau=T/M$. The right derivative is
$$
\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\right|_{0+}
\frac{T_{K_{p,\varepsilon}}(y_\varepsilon)}{M_\varepsilon}
=\frac1M\min_{u\in U_p}\left\{
\tau D_{\rm mix}
-\int_{\partial K_p}[1+u\cdot(x-y)]_+v_p(x)\,dS(x)-T\,u\cdot w
\right\}. \tag{6}
$$
It is nonnegative exactly when every row in braces is nonnegative. Off the centroid there is a single row. At $y=g_{K_p}$ the criterion is exactly
$$
\tau D_{\rm mix}-D_p-p_{K_p-y}(-B_p-|K_p|w)\ge0,\qquad
D_p=\int_{\partial K_p}v_p\,dS,\quad
B_p=\int_{\partial K_p}(x-y)v_p\,dS .
\tag{7}
$$
When $K_p$ is a polytope and $y=g_{K_p}$, the minimum can be taken at the finitely many vertices of $U_p=\{u:1+u\cdot(a-y)\ge0\text{ for every vertex }a\text{ of }K_p\}$. These are linear response rows when the actual physical speeds and prescribed velocity depend linearly on deformation parameters.

One actual setting for such averaging is the single-baseline case of accepted fact 84cd8a85417b0d7a. Use one fixed continuous-in-normal, affine-in-base support baseline satisfying its majorization hypotheses; average the nonnegative convex cut fields on that baseline before constructing the body. For a Borel probability average, assume a nonempty compact metric field parameter space and joint continuity of the fields, and average prescribed velocities integrable in that parameter. The response in (6) is then the average of individual responses off the centroid; at the centroid it is the minimum of the averaged rows.

For a conditional use of (6), define depth as the infimum of the physical mixed masses of closed ambient halfspaces containing the mark, and deepest points as the maximum-depth points on $\bigcup_{p\in P}\{p\}\times K_{p,\varepsilon}$. For this maximum, define $T_L(q)$ at boundary marks by the same mass and moment constraints; it is zero there since a supporting hyperplane through $q$ is Lebesgue-null and every feasible density with barycenter $q$ must be concentrated on that hyperplane. Suppose the secondary maximum $S(\varepsilon)$ of $T_{K_{p,\varepsilon}}(y)/M_\varepsilon$ among deepest points exists for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon\ge0$. Assume a fixed nonempty finite list of paths $(p_j,y_j(\varepsilon))$, each deepest for all such $\varepsilon$, with $p_j\in P$, $y_j(0)\in\operatorname{int}K_{p_j}$ and $y_j(\varepsilon)=y_j(0)+\varepsilon w_j+o(\varepsilon)$. Assume every secondary maximizer for small $\varepsilon>0$ lies on a listed path. Let $\tau_j=T_{K_{p_j}}(y_j(0))/M$ and $b_j$ be the derivative (6) on path $j$. Then
$$
S(\varepsilon)=\tau_*+\varepsilon\max_{j:\tau_j=\tau_*}b_j+o(\varepsilon),
\qquad \tau_*=\max_j\tau_j .
\tag{8}
$$
This gives the finite right derivative at zero if and only if $\tau_*=S(0)$, equivalently if at least one listed path begins at an old secondary maximizer. Without this equality, (8) is the right-hand expansion about the branch limit.

pk-intake-null-supporting-sections-stric.relation_to_goal: Geometry and cardinality of deepest marks in the null-supporting-section subclass, including strictly convex positive fibers in dimension at least two.
pk-intake-null-supporting-sections-stric.statement:
Let $n\ge1,d\ge2$ and $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$ for compact convex $C\subset\mathbb R^{n+d}$. Let $\mu$ sum the $d$-volume of its fibers, with $\mu(S)>0$, and let $D$ be raw closed ambient halfspace depth. Suppose every supporting hyperplane of every positive-volume fiber meets that fiber in a set of zero $\mathcal H^{d-1}$ measure.

For distinct $y_0,y_1\in S$ of positive depth and every $y=(1-t)y_0+ty_1\in S$ with $0<t<1$, one has $D(y)>\min(D(y_0),D(y_1))$. This includes endpoints in the same fiber.

Every attaining cap through a global maximizing point strictly excludes all other maximizing points. There is at most one maximizing point per parity class of the integer base, hence at most $2^n$ in total, with distinct bases. Their base set $I$ satisfies $I=\operatorname{conv}(I)\cap\mathbb Z^n$, and every $p\in I$ is an exposed vertex of $\operatorname{conv}(I)$. In particular, at a maximizing point $(p,x)$ take any positive circuit of attaining nonvertical through-caps with margins $a_j\cdot(z-p)+u_j\cdot(X-x)$ and coefficients $\lambda_j>0$ with $\sum_j\lambda_j u_j=0$. Then $\sum_j\lambda_j a_j$ strictly exposes $p$ among the maximizing bases when $I$ contains more than one point.

pk-intake-oblique-centroidal-projective-.statement:
Let $D\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a full-dimensional rational convex polygon with centroid zero. Let $k\in\mathbb Q^2$ satisfy $-1/2<k\cdot x<1$ for $x\in D$, put $B=\{x/(1-k\cdot x):x\in D\}$ and $K=\operatorname{conv}(B\times\{-1\},(0,0,2))$. Then $|K|=|B|$, $g_K=((3/4)g_B,-1/4)$, and $z=3k\cdot x$ cuts the graph over $(2/3)D$ with centroid zero. For the apex-facing cap, with inward unit normal $u$ and section area $S$,
$$
p=(8/27)|D|/|B|,\qquad s=S(u\cdot g_K)/|K|=-|D|(1+9k\cdot g_B)/(9|B|).
$$
A vertical plane over a centered chord of $B$ has centroidal section, the same cap fraction as for $B$, and scalar $s$ equal to $9/8$ times the planar scalar. The oblique nonsimplex case occurs when $k\ne0$ and $D$ has at least four vertices.

pk-intake-oblique-centroidal-rational-pr.statement:
For rational $1<h<2$ set $a=2(h^2-h+1)/(3(h-1))$, $W=\{(x,y):x\le1,\ |y|\le a+x\}$ and $D=W\cap\{x\ge-h\}$. For a rational convex polygon $B$ with $D\subseteq B\subseteq W$ and any additional vertices at $x<-h$, let $K=B\times[-1,1]$. Its planes $z=\pm x/h$ cut sections with centroid zero. Let $p$ be the inward cap fraction and $s=S(u\cdot g_K)/|K|$ for inward unit normal $u$ and section area $S$. In both orientations $\pm z\ge x/h$,
$$
p=1-|D|/(2|B|),\qquad s=-|D|(g_B)_x/(2h|B|),\qquad |D|=(a+1)^2-(a-h)^2 .
$$
Complements have data $(1-p,-s)$. A vertical plane over a centered chord $[-q,q]$ has centroidal section and the corresponding planar $p,s$ for $B$, with normalized coarea vector $(2Rq/|B|,0)$ for a right-angle planar rotation $R$. Transverse intersections of edges of $B$ and $-B$ give rational endpoints of centered chords.

pk-intake-occupied-parity-mass-of-buffer.relation_to_goal: A lower bound on original depth using the mass of a fixed positive-buffer stratum and its occupied parities.
pk-intake-occupied-parity-mass-of-buffer.statement:

pk-intake-odd-hemisphere-transform-and-a.relation_to_goal: Finite ambient Borel measures with no atom at the marked point for the depth characterization.

pk-intake-one-apex-ordinary-centroid-dep.relation_to_goal: Computes ordinary raw depth over all continuous directions. For the specific compatible pentagon, the ordinary value lower-bounds the ambient mixed depth at the lifted ordinary centroid.

pk-intake-one-buffered-dual-with-allocat.relation_to_goal: A conditional common conservative selector for a physically realizable finite buffered cover. The lower branch retains inside body loss and drops its positive hinge, and the centroid identity averages contact occurrences.
pk-intake-one-buffered-dual-with-allocat.statement:

Each such test permits all independent signed cap-normal velocities shared over the contacts in each group. Let $\ell_i^0$ be the proper conservative loss and use the actual loss for each atomic cap. Suppose simultaneous strict improvement of all normalized responses (loss minus $\beta D$) would yield strict actual descent by this cover.

There is one separator for all tests. It has atomic weights $\eta_A\ge0$, cap weights $\omega_{ij}\ge0$, and nonnegative contact weights $\kappa_{ia}$, with $\sum_{ij}\omega_{ij}+\sum_A\eta_A=1$. At each proper group of positive total weight $\eta_i=\sum_j\omega_{ij}$, every cap weight is positive. Its effective outside selector $\theta_{ij}$ satisfies $0\le\theta_{ij}\le1$ and is used both in the body weight and in the section coarea, which on the outside face is $\theta_{ij}\,dS/\|u_{ij}\|$. The inside-support body and section selectors are respectively $1$ and $0$. If $T_{ij}$ is the total allocated coarea and $\bar w_{ij}$ its full physical mean, put $\kappa_i=\sum_a\kappa_{ia}$, $e_{ia}=\varepsilon f_a\kappa_{ia}$, $e_i=\sum_a e_{ia}$. Then
$$
\omega_{ij}T_{ij}=\kappa_i\rho_{ij},\qquad
\bar w_{ij}=\frac{\sum_a\kappa_{ia}Y_{ia}}{\kappa_i}
-\frac{e_i}{\kappa_i}(0,\Sigma u_{ij}).
$$
In the separator's linear inequality the body terms have the allocated cap weights and the proper contact terms have budget coefficients $\kappa_{ia}$. More explicitly, with $B_{ij}^{\theta}(v)=B_{ij}(v)+\int_{\rm out}\theta_{ij}v\,dS$ and $m_{ij}^{\theta}=T_{ij}\bar w_{ij}$, the proper terms before the common $-\beta D$ are
$$
\sum_{ij}\omega_{ij}\bigl(B_{ij}^{\theta}(v)-m_{ij}^{\theta}\cdot\nu_{ij}\bigr)+\sum_{ia}\kappa_{ia} A_{ia}.
$$

pk-intake-one-coordinate-facet-roof-affi.relation_to_goal: Ordinary volume on a fixed one-coordinate facet roof. The threshold in the comparison may depend on that roof. The affine case has zero first-order deficit.
pk-intake-one-coordinate-facet-roof-affi.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $m=d+1$, $b=1/m$, $h=d/m$, and $\Gamma=h^d$. On a $(d-1)$-simplex with barycentrics $s_1,\ldots,s_d$, let $P$ be uniform probability, $N(s)=\#\{i:s_i\ge b\}$ and $E_d(\psi)=\int(N-m\Gamma)\psi\,dP$. For $0<c<1$ set $E(c)=E_d(\min(s_1,c))$. Write $I_L(c)=0$ for $c<0$ and otherwise
$$
I_L(c)=\frac{cL^{d-1}}{d-1}-\frac{L^d-(L-c)_+^d}{d(d-1)}.
$$
Then $E(c)>0$ and
$$
\begin{aligned}
E(c)&=m\Gamma(d-1)I_1(c)-(d-1)I_h(c-b)-(d-1)^2I_h(c),\\
E(c)&=\left(h^{d-1}-\frac1d\right)(1-c)^d-\frac{d-1}{d}(h-c)_+^d\qquad(c\ge b).
\end{aligned}
$$
For $0<c<b$ one has $E''(c)\ge(h^{d-2}/m)(d-1)(1-c)^{d-2}$, with $E(0)=E'(0)=0$.

Let
$$
k_d=\min\left\{\frac{h^{d-2}}m,\ d h^{d-1}-1-(d-1)((d-1)/d)^d\right\}>0.
$$
For each continuous nonnegative concave $\phi$ on $[0,1]$, write $\mu=-\phi''$ on $(0,1)$ in the distributional sense. Define the affine function
$$
\ell(x)=(1-x)\phi(0)+x\phi(1)
 +(1-x)\int_{(0,b]}c\,d\mu(c)+x\int_{(b,1)}(1-c)\,d\mu(c).
$$
Then $\ell\ge\phi$, $\int(\ell(s_1)-\phi(s_1))\,dP\le E_d(\phi(s_1))/k_d$, and the deficit is zero exactly when $\phi$ is affine.

In the standard facet coordinates $\mathcal B=\{z\in\mathbb R^{d-1}:z_j\ge0,\ \sum_jz_j\le1\}$, let $K_\varepsilon$ be the body with $\sum_jz_j-1\le r\le\varepsilon\phi(z_1)$ over $\mathcal B$. For $\ell(x)=A+Bx$, let $S_\varepsilon$ have the same lower bound and upper bound $\varepsilon\ell(z_1)$ over all $z_j\ge0$. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, $S_\varepsilon$ is an enclosing simplex of volume $(1+\varepsilon A)^d/[d!(1-\varepsilon B)]$, and
$$
1-\frac{|K_\varepsilon|}{|S_\varepsilon|}
=\varepsilon d\int(\ell(s_1)-\phi(s_1))\,dP+O_\phi(\varepsilon^2)
\le\frac{\varepsilon d}{k_d}E_d(\phi(s_1))+O_\phi(\varepsilon^2).
$$
If $\phi$ is fixed and nonaffine, the lower limit of the ratio of the normalized maximum ordinary halfspace depth excess $D(K_\varepsilon)-\Gamma$ to this missing fraction is at least $k_d/m$. For each $0<a<k_d/m$ and all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, this excess is at least $a$ times the missing fraction, and hence at least $a$ times the infimum of the closed-halfspace discrepancies to uniform probability laws on full-dimensional simplices.

$$
\frac{LW}{s+1}\le A\le LW,\qquad
\sup_H\frac{|A_h(H)-A(H)|}{A}\le\eta:=\frac{hW}{A}\le\frac{(s+1)h}{L},
$$
where the supremum is over closed halfspaces and the whole space. The lower peak-to-total bound is sharp. If $\eta<1$, then $A_h>0$ and
$$
\sup_H\left|\frac{A_h(H)}{A_h}-\frac{A(H)}A\right|\le\frac{2\eta}{1-\eta}.
$$
For fixed $s$, $L/h\to\infty$ gives uniform normalized cap convergence. Under $u'=au+c$, $x'=Tx+bu+d$, with $a\ne0$ and $T$ invertible, use the actual grid $aG+c$. Both $\eta$ and $h/L$ are invariant.

pk-intake-one-integer-polytope-reflected.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact and convex, $d\ge1$. Suppose $D=K_{-1}\subset K=K_0$ are positive-volume fibers, $K$ is a polytope, and $D$ meets every facet hyperplane of $K$. Then every nonempty real fiber $K_t$ with $t\ge0$ is contained in $K$.

If even one $b(u)<[h_K(u)+\min_{x\in K}u\cdot x]/2$, no nonempty fiber at an integer base $\ge2$ exists, so base $1$ is strictly exposed among the nonempty sampled bases. The complete miss on $K_1$ follows if the strip $-w<a+u\cdot(x-y)<0$ has zero volume there and the margin is strictly negative at one mark there. pk-intake-one-row-planar-chord-center-an.relation_to_goal: A single planar row, including any local fixed-mark cap minimum with the proper/zero statuses. Scalar sharpness does not assert realizability by a globally critical three-fiber configuration.
pk-intake-one-row-planar-chord-center-an.statement:

$$
J:=2y-E_A-(s/t)(c_K-y)\subseteq F.
$$
If these equivalent conditions hold, writing $b=|F|$ and $c_B$ for its length and center,
$$
b\ge t,\qquad s\ge(t+b)/2,\qquad
\big\|(c_A+c_B)/2-c_K\big\|\le \frac{s-(t+b)/2}{2}.
$$

$$
\frac{\|y-c_K\|}{s}\le\frac{(t/s)(1-t/s)}{1+2t/s}\le\frac{2-\sqrt3}{2}.
$$
The smaller-to-larger distance ratio from $y$ to the ends of $E_K$ is at least $1/\sqrt3$. The last scalar maximum is attained at $t/s=(\sqrt3-1)/2$.

pk-intake-one-sided-buffered-cap-source-.relation_to_goal: An integer-width necessity for a single common minimum with one-sided positive supporting coarea. No affine outer envelope, menu construction or mixed-depth payment is used.
pk-intake-one-sided-buffered-cap-source-.statement:

Suppose all positive outside-supporting coarea strictly beyond $[a,b]$ lies to its left. Then there is a unique outside-supporting positive fiber on the left, at an integer $L<a$ with positive coarea. Put $m=b-a$ and $h=b-L$. If $d\ge2$, then
$$
m\sum_{j=1}^{h-1}(j/h)^{d-1}\le h-m,\qquad m\le d-1.
$$
If $d=1$, these hypotheses are impossible. Reversing the base gives the same width conclusion when all positive outside coarea beyond the source interval lies to its right.

Independently of minimality, if a cap is proper at both $a$ and $b$, each side of $[a,b]$ has at most one positive fiber with an outside-supporting trace and at most one with an inside-supporting trace. Each such base is an endpoint of the projection of the appropriate closed cut body.

pk-intake-one-unit-fractional-exponentia.relation_to_goal: The k=1 scalar family of balanced capped signed-exponential laws with one fixed negative unit and equal residual negative magnitudes. The conclusion concerns its finite-m sign probability.
pk-intake-one-unit-fractional-exponentia.statement:
Let $m\ge1$ be an integer and $p\in[0,1]$. Let $E_0,E_1,E_2$ be mean-one exponentials and $Y\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(m,1)$ have shape $m$ and scale one, all independent. Put $P_m(p)=\Pr(E_1+pE_2\ge E_0+(p/m)Y)$. Then
$$
P_m(p)\ge P_m(1)=\left(\frac{m}{m+1}\right)^m\frac{5m+3}{4(m+1)}.
$$
Also $P_m(0)=1/2$. Equality in the endpoint bound holds exactly when $p=1$ or $m=1$. For $m=1$ the probability is $1/2$ on the entire interval.

pk-intake-open-cover-strict-cap-profile.relation_to_goal: Gives strictness for a fixed ordinary density cover when every point of positive support is in the interior of some cap.
pk-intake-open-cover-strict-cap-profile.statement:
Let $r\ge1$ and $\beta\ge r+1$. Let $f$ be a Lebesgue density of mass $M\in(0,\infty)$, positive on a nonempty open convex set $U\subset\mathbb R^r$ and zero outside $U$. Assume $f^{-1/\beta}$ is finite, positive and convex on $U$. Let finitely many proper closed halfspaces $H_i$ satisfy $U\subset\bigcup_i\operatorname{int}H_i$, and write $A_i=\int_{H_i}f$ and $\gamma_r=(r/(r+1))^r$. For every $\alpha>0$,
$$
\sum_i(A_i-\alpha)_+ + \frac{\alpha}{\gamma_r}>M,
\qquad x_+=\max\{x,0\}.
$$

pk-intake-opposite-pair-section-centroid.relation_to_goal: A section-centroid inequality for the opposite-paired simplex class, including zero vertex coefficients.
pk-intake-opposite-pair-section-centroid.statement:
Let $k\ge1$, let $p_i>0$ for $1\le i\le k$, and let $Y_i,Y_i'$ be independent mean-one exponentials, with any finite number of additional independent mean-one exponentials of coefficient zero. Set $V=\sum_{i=1}^k p_i(Y_i-Y_i')$, and let $\mu_j$ denote each coordinate mean under the coarea conditional law at $V=0$. Then $\Pr(V\ge0)=1/2$, and
$$
\prod_j\mu_j\ge\frac14,\qquad \prod_{j\ne r}\mu_j\ge\frac14\quad\text{for every coordinate }r.
$$
Both inequalities are strict for $k\ge2$. For $k=1$, the active means are $1/2$ and the zero-coefficient means are one. Thus the full product and each omission of a zero-coefficient coordinate are $1/4$, and each omission of an active coordinate is $1/2$.

On a uniform $d$-simplex with these coefficients as the values of an affine functional on its $d+1$ vertices, let $b_j$ be the barycentric coordinates of the uniform section centroid at functional value zero. Then $\mu_j=d b_j$.

$$
\begin{array}{ll}
br>Bt & X\le \dfrac{Bt(bt+Br+2br)}{2(br-Bt)},\\[5pt]
br<Bt & Y\le \dfrac{br(bt+Br+2Bt)}{2(Bt-br)}.

$$
For $br=Bt$ there is no additional bound. All indicated equalities are allowed. pk-intake-optimized-buffer-value-scalar-.relation_to_goal: This gives an exact comparison and a conditional first-order lower bound for the optimized normalized value at a fixed buffer scale.
pk-intake-optimized-buffer-value-scalar-.statement:
Assume the actual compatible fixed-base bodies and old positive continuous log-normalized parameter $L$ satisfy the finite volume certificate hypotheses of 569a05581be52e0e at a fixed $\varepsilon>0$. In particular the contact probabilities $\rho_i$ have weights $\sigma_i>0$ summing to one, full means $Y_i=(p_i,y_i)$ and $L$-means $L_i=L(Y_i)$, and $\sum_i(\sigma_i/L_i)\rho_i=dm/(ML)$. Each $Y_i$ is an old maximizing mark with raw depth $Q$, strictly below its closed pure-base depth. Let $K_z(t)\to K_z$ be positive compatible bodies in the fixed-base fiber Hausdorff topology as $t\downarrow0$, with mixed volume $dm_t$ and total $M_t$. Define $v(t)=\inf_U Q_t(U)/M_t$ over current positive continuous concave, log-normalized parameters. Choose $U_t$ with $Q_t(U_t)/M_t\le v(t)+t^2$.

Choose a common inward fractional contraction $a_t\to0$, $0\le a_t<1$, of the old fibers about their old centroids $g_z$ so that its image $I_{t,z}$ is contained in $K_z(t)$. Let $T_t(z,X)=(z,g_z+(1-a_t)(X-g_z))$ and $j_t=(1-a_t)^d$. Let $Y_i^t$ be the mean of $(T_t)_\#\rho_i$, and $B_i(t,s)$ its actual raw buffered depth with scalar parameter value $s$. On a common interval of raw depths about $Q$, for all sufficiently small $t$ there is a unique positive inverse $s_i(t,q)$ of this scalar depth. Define $H_t(q)=\sum_i\sigma_i\log(s_i(t,q)/L_i)$ and let $\chi_t$ denote its local inverse. If
$$
\xi_t=-\frac1{Mj_t}\sum_z\int_{K_z(t)\setminus I_{t,z}}\log U_t\,dX,
$$
then $H_t(Q_t(U_t))\ge\xi_t$ and $Q_t(U_t)\ge\chi_t(\xi_t)$.

Let $h_t=\sum_z|K_z(t)\setminus I_{t,z}|$ and let $B\ge1$ be a common sampled upper bound for $U_t$. Then $\xi_t\ge-h_t\log B/(Mj_t)$ and $v(t)\ge\chi_t(-h_t\log B/(Mj_t))/M_t-t^2$. More precisely, for positive continuous reference values $L_{\rm ref,t}$ on the sampled moving fibers that converge to $L$ along all convergent sampled marks, we have $\sup_{S_t}(U_t-L_{\rm ref,t})_+\to0$ and
$$
\xi_t\ge-\frac1{Mj_t}\sum_z\int_{K_z(t)\setminus I_{t,z}}\log L_{\rm ref,t}\,dX+o(h_t).
$$
If the moving endpoint on the ray through a regular old boundary point $X$ from $g_z$ is $g_z+(1-b_{z,t}(X))(X-g_z)$, assume $|b_{z,t}(X)|=O(t)$ uniformly and $b_{z,t}(X)/t\to v_z(X)/[n_z(X)\cdot(X-g_z)]$ surface-almost everywhere, where $v_z$ is a bounded measurable signed inward speed. With $a_t=ct+o(t)$ and $H_z(X)=n_z(X)\cdot(X-g_z)$, containment gives $cH_z-v_z\ge0$ and
$$
\liminf_{t\downarrow0}\frac{\xi_t}{t}\ge
c_{\rm col}:=\frac1M\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}\log L(z,X)[v_z(X)-cH_z(X)]\,dS.
$$

If, independently, $H_t(Q+tr)=t(A_0 r+B_0)+o(t)$ uniformly for bounded $r$, with $A_0>0$, and $\liminf\xi_t/t\ge c_0$, then $\liminf (Q_t(U_t)-Q)/t\ge(c_0-B_0)/A_0$. If also $M_t=M-tD+o(t)$, then
$$
\liminf_{t\downarrow0}\frac{v(t)-Q/M}{t}
\ge\frac{(c_0-B_0)/A_0+(Q/M)D}{M}.
$$

pk-intake-optimized-one-mark-fiber-graph.relation_to_goal: Refutes certification of the sharp Oertel target by optimized exact depth of an atomic graph with one own-depth-weighted mark per fiber.
pk-intake-optimized-one-mark-fiber-graph.statement:

=\frac12
<\frac{\gamma_1}{4}\mu(S)=\frac9{16},\qquad \gamma_1=\frac12 .

pk-intake-ordinary-and-paired-simplex-co.relation_to_goal: Obstruction to a volume bound for replacing fibers by simplex containers and convexifying at their existing lattice bases.
pk-intake-ordinary-and-paired-simplex-co.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$ and a real $0<\varepsilon\le1/16$. Let $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)$, $V=1/d!$, $\Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d$, and set $a=1+\varepsilon^2$ and
$$
A=\{x:x_i\ge0,\ \varepsilon\le\textstyle\sum_i x_i\le1\},\qquad
B=\varepsilon^2T,\qquad P=\{x:x_i\le a,\ \textstyle\sum_i x_i\ge\varepsilon\}.
$$
The hull of the lifts of $A,P/2,B$ at bases $0,1,2$ has exactly those three positive integer fibers $K_j$. For a continuous convex body $K$, write $D(K)$ for the maximum normalized ordinary depth. Write $D_{\rm pair}(K)$ for the maximum over $y\in K$ of the infimum over nonzero $u$ and $s\ge0$ of
$$
\frac{|K\cap\{u\cdot(x-y)\ge s\}|+|K\cap\{u\cdot(x-y)\ge-s\}|}{2|K|}.
$$
Define $\delta_{\rm ord}(K)=|K|(D(K)-\Gamma)$ and $\delta_{\rm pair}(K)=|K|(D_{\rm pair}(K)-\Gamma)$. Then
$$
0\le \sum_j\delta_{\rm pair}(K_j)\le\sum_j\delta_{\rm ord}(K_j)\le\Gamma\varepsilon^d V.
$$
Every choice of enclosing $d$-simplex for each actual integer fiber, convexified at the same bases, adds at least $\varepsilon V/(16d^2)$ of actual mixed $d$-volume. For either positive deficit sum the ratio of added mass to that sum is at least $\varepsilon^{1-d}/(16d^2\Gamma)$. Consequently no finite constant bounds the added mass by either deficit sum, even at fixed $d$.

pk-intake-ordinary-central-radius-satura.relation_to_goal: Ordinary planar convex-body feasibility and optimization for a fixed central line arrangement. The local topology is the finite endpoint and sector data. A mixed-integer realization would require a separate midpoint constraint.
pk-intake-ordinary-central-radius-satura.statement:
Let $K$ be a planar convex body with $0$ in its interior. Choose $N\ge2$ distinct lines through $0$. Let $e_i$ be nonzero vectors on the $2N$ rays in counterclockwise order with $e_{i+N}=-e_i$, and write the boundary endpoints as $R_ie_i$, $R_i>0$. All indices are cyclic modulo $2N$. Let $d_i=\det(e_i,e_{i+1})>0$ and let $W_i$ be the area of $K$ in the sector between these consecutive rays.

With all $W_i$ and all other radii fixed, the feasible values of the $i$th radius that are at least $R_i$ are exactly the closed interval
$$
R_i\le R_i'\le \min\left\{\frac{2W_{i-1}}{d_{i-1}R_{i-1}},\frac{2W_i}{d_iR_{i+1}}\right\}.
$$
Each value has a convex polygonal realization containing $0$ in its interior with at most $4N$ vertices. At the upper endpoint at least one adjacent sector has area equal to its core triangle. Opposite radii can be increased to their upper endpoints independently. All fixed-line cap areas and all other central chord lengths are preserved. For any fixed positive length scaling on each line, the normalized inverse weight of the changed chord strictly decreases if either of its radii increases.

In the canonical three-line coordinates, let $R=(A,B,t,a,b,r)$ on ray vectors $(1,0),(0,1),(-1,1),(-1,0),(0,-1),(1,-1)$. For the caps $x\ge0$, $y\ge0$, $x+y\le0$, write $W=(Y_3,X_2,Y_1,X_3,Y_2,X_1)$, where $X_j$ is area in cap $j$ alone and $Y_j$ is area in the other two caps. The coarea chord lengths are $B+b$, $A+a$, and $r+t$. Every realized datum admits a replacement with target coarea chord $B+b$ no shorter and with one of the core-sector pairs $(Y_3,X_3),(Y_3,Y_2),(X_2,X_3),(X_2,Y_2)$. Every local minimum of the target inverse weight in the finite radius and area data, and every attained global minimum, already lies in this union under any constraints depending only on $W$. The pairs allow additional core equalities.

pk-intake-ordinary-clipped-unique-sector.relation_to_goal: Necessary inequalities for actual ordinary planar data under the stated ascending sorted profile. Equivalence concerns the relaxed area system.
pk-intake-ordinary-clipped-unique-sector.statement:
Let $K$ be a planar convex body containing $0$ in its interior. Use the caps $x\ge0$, $y\ge0$, $x+y\le0$, with areas $q_i$ and total area $k=|K|$. Write $X_i$ for the area in cap $i$ alone and $Y_i$ for the area in precisely the two other caps. Suppose $4/9\le c<1/2$, each $q_i\le ck$, and $q_{\min}+q_{\mathrm{mid}}+q_{\max}/4\le k$. Then each $G_i>0$ and
$$
\max_i G_i/C\ge\tfrac13,\qquad
\sum_i\min(G_i/C,\tfrac13)\ge \frac{4}{3c}-2.
$$
At $c=128/279$ the right side is $29/32$. With $G_i>0$, the two inequalities are equivalent to feasibility of the relaxed system $0<d_i\le G_i$, $m=\max_i d_i\ge C/3$, $C+m\le c(2C+\sum_i d_i)$ for finite real $d_i$.

$$

pk-intake-ordinary-cubic-tight-edge-gree.relation_to_goal: First-order ordinary planar edge variation under strict corner incidence. The point masses retain actual chord variation.
pk-intake-ordinary-cubic-tight-edge-gree.statement:
Let $T$ be a nondegenerate triangle, $y$ an interior source, and $v_i$ nonzero spanning normals summing to zero whose through-source caps strictly isolate three distinct vertices $P_i$. Write $k=|T|$, $Q_i$ for cap areas, $\sigma_i$ for chord lengths divided by $\lVert v_i\rVert$, $M=\sum_iQ_i/\sigma_i$, $f_i=2\sqrt{kQ_i}/(\sigma_iM)$, and $\Psi=\sum_i f_i^2+\prod_i f_i$. Assume $\Psi=4$. Fix the edge $P(t)=(1-t)P_i+tP_j$ opposite $P_s$, and let $a$ be the entry into cap $j$ and $b$ the exit from cap $i$. Then $0<a<b<1$.

Take an outward vector $w$ with $|\det(P_j-P_i,w)|=1$. In the coordinates $P(t)+rw$, the first variation under an outward piecewise-affine roof $r=\varepsilon h(t)$ with $h(0)=h(1)=0$ is $D\Psi[h]=\int h\,d\nu$. The density of $\nu$ is $\alpha_i,\beta_s,\alpha_j$ on $(0,a),(a,b),(b,1)$, respectively. With $C=8+\prod_i f_i$, $E_\ell=2f_\ell^2+\prod_i f_i$ and $T_\ell=\sqrt{k/Q_\ell}$,
$$
2k\alpha_\ell=C+E_\ell T_\ell^2-Cf_\ell T_\ell,\qquad
\beta_s=\alpha_i+\alpha_j-\frac C{2k}.
$$
At either crossing $t_0$ of cap $\ell$, there is an atom of weight $(\partial_{\sigma_\ell}\Psi)/|v_\ell\cdot(P_j-P_i)|$, where $\partial_{\sigma_\ell}\Psi=-E_\ell/\sigma_\ell+C Q_\ell/(\sigma_\ell^2 M)$. The moments $\int(1-t)d\nu$ and $\int t\,d\nu$ both vanish.

Put $U(\theta)=\int[\min(t,\theta)-t\theta]\,d\nu(t)$. The unit-height triangular roof with peak $\theta\in(0,1)$ has derivative $U(\theta)/[\theta(1-\theta)]$, where
$$
U(\theta)=-\alpha_i\theta^2/2\quad(0\le\theta\le a),\qquad
U(\theta)=-\alpha_j(1-\theta)^2/2\quad(b\le\theta\le1).
$$
For $\theta=a+z(b-a)$ with $0\le z\le1$,
$$
2U(\theta)=-(1-z)\alpha_i a^2-z\alpha_j(1-b)^2+\beta_s(b-a)^2z(1-z).
$$
Both $\alpha_i$ and $\alpha_j$ are positive. The derivative is nonpositive at every peak exactly when
$$
\beta_s(b-a)^2\le \bigl(a\sqrt{\alpha_i}+(1-b)\sqrt{\alpha_j}\bigr)^2.
$$
Strict inequality gives a negative derivative at every peak. Equality in this criterion gives exactly one zero peak.

pk-intake-ordinary-deepest-face-exhausti.relation_to_goal: Original normalized depth and unrestricted actual fixed-base perturbations. The result is independent of parity, quotas and buffered objectives.
pk-intake-ordinary-deepest-face-exhausti.statement:
Fix a finite nonempty real base $P$ and $d\ge1$. Suppose the compact convex bodies $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ have positive volume and are the exact sampled fibers of $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$. Let $F_p$ be the smallest face of $\operatorname{conv}(P)$ containing $p$ and let $I=\{p:q_p=Q\}$. If $u\in P\setminus\bigcup_{p\in I}F_p$, replace just the input at $u$ by $K_u+t B_d$ for $t>0$, where $B_d$ is the Euclidean unit ball, and form the hull $C_t$ of these inputs. Its actual fibers satisfy $K_z\subseteq K_z(t)\subseteq K_z+tB_d$ for all $z\in P$, and their total mass $M_t$ is strictly greater than $M$. For all sufficiently small $t>0$, $Q(C_t)=Q$ and $\beta_0(C_t)=Q/M_t<\beta_0(C)$.

Consequently the faces $F_p$ for $p\in I$ cover $P$ at every local minimum of $\beta_0$ among all actual positive compatible families on the fixed base, in the product Hausdorff topology. If $P$ contains a site in $\operatorname{relint}(\operatorname{conv}(P))$, then at least one deepest base at such a minimum belongs to this relative interior.

pk-intake-ordinary-depth-descent-by-supp.relation_to_goal: A local upper-cover argument for ordinary uniform maximal depth under an actual full critical circuit. It yields a derivative of the cover bound and uses equality at the starting body. It supplies no bound for the locked mixed-integer problem.
pk-intake-ordinary-depth-descent-by-supp.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$. Suppose the $d+1$ unit vectors $u_i$ span $\mathbb R^d$ and form a minimal positive circuit, and that $\theta_i>0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$ satisfy $\sum_i\theta_i S_i u_i=0$, where $S_i=\mathcal H^{d-1}(K\cap u_i^\perp)$. As in the stationary setting, suppose the sections have centroid $0$. Assume the central cap masses $|K\cap\{x:u_i\cdot x\ge0\}|$ all equal $Q$, where $Q$ is the maximum over $y\in K$ of $\inf_{H\ni y}|K\cap H|$ for closed halfspaces $H$. Then the selected caps attain the depth at the deepest point $0$.

Take a bump $K_t$ as in the section-preserving support-bump lemma with signature weight $W\ne Q/|K|$. Such a bump exists if $h$ is $C^2$ with everywhere positive-definite $A_h$. For small signed $t$ there are a point $y(t)$ near $0$ and $d+1$ parallel translates of the respective original caps through $y(t)$, all with the same mass $q(t)$. They cover $\mathbb R^d$ and bound the new maximum raw depth by $q(t)$. The normalized cover bound has derivative
$$
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\frac{q(t)}{|K_t|}\right|_{t=0}
=\left(W-\frac Q{|K|}\right)\frac{V'_0}{|K|}.
$$
For all sufficiently small nonzero $t$ of the appropriate sign, the maximal normalized ordinary depth of $K_t$ is strictly below that of $K$.

pk-intake-ordinary-maximal-depth-minkows.relation_to_goal: Equality for ordinary volume at one tested Minkowski interpolation with positive coefficients. The midpoint identity applies to that actual compatible midpoint.
pk-intake-ordinary-maximal-depth-minkows.statement:
Let $K,L,N\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, be compact convex bodies with nonempty interiors, and suppose $N\supseteq sK+tL$ for $s,t>0$. Write $A(B)$ for the maximum raw ordinary closed-halfspace depth in $B$. Then
$$
A(N)^{1/d}\ge sA(K)^{1/d}+tA(L)^{1/d}.
$$
Equality holds exactly when $N=sK+tL$ and $K,L$ are positively homothetic. If equality holds, let $g_K,g_L,g_N$ be their unique deepest points. Then $g_N=sg_K+tg_L$ and
$L=r(K-g_K)+g_L$ for $r=(A(L)/A(K))^{1/d}$.
For every active direction at $g_N$, the entire captured cap of $N$ is the weighted Minkowski sum of the caps of $K,L$ through $g_K,g_L$ in the same direction.

Equivalently, under this containment, equality in the maximal-depth-root inequality is the same as $|N|^{1/d}=s|K|^{1/d}+t|L|^{1/d}$. The statement applies in parallel $d$-dimensional affine planes, with intrinsic volumes and the same Minkowski containment. In particular, $s=t=1/2$ gives rigidity at an actual compatible midpoint.

pk-intake-ordinary-own-depth-layer-cake-.relation_to_goal: Own-depth-weighted volume and its ordinary comparison. A positive mixture is a different candidate for uniform volume and its exact obstruction is explicit.
pk-intake-ordinary-own-depth-layer-cake-.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body, $d\ge1$, with volume $V$, raw ordinary halfspace depth $f$, peak $A=\max_Kf>0$ and levels $W_s=\{x\in K:f(x)\ge s\}$. For every measurable $H$, $\int_0^A|W_s\cap H|\,ds=\int_{K\cap H} f(x)\,dx$. For every $0\le s\le A$ and any maximizer $g_*$,
$$
g_*+[1-(s/A)^{1/d}](K-g_*)\subseteq W_s,\qquad
V[1-(s/A)^{1/d}]^d\le |W_s|\le V-2s .
$$
Thus $VA/\binom{2d}{d}\le\int_K f\le V^2/4$. Both bounds are exact for intervals. The lower factor is also attained for the larger class of potentials with nonnegative concave $d$th root and zero boundary values. Any probability mixture of the uniform laws on $W_s$ for $0\le s<A$ that equals uniform volume on $K$ is concentrated at $s=0$. The same holds if $s=A$ is allowed with its law defined as the Dirac mass at the unique deepest point. In particular, for triangle fibers the layer-cake total is $(7/54)\sum_z|K_z|^2$.

pk-intake-ordinary-projective-energy-sha.relation_to_goal: One full-dimensional compact ordinary convex body and a prescribed interior mark. The least upper comparison constant is dimensionwise d+1; it is approached at an interior mark moving toward a vertex of a fixed simplex and is never attained. No base-energy conversion, sampled-mixture claim, or mixed halfspace guarantee follows.
pk-intake-ordinary-projective-energy-sha.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior, and let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. Define
$$
E_K(y)=\min_{\substack{a\in\mathbb R^d\\1+a\cdot(x-y)>0\ (x\in K)}}
\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx,\qquad
T_K(y)=\max_{\substack{0\le f\le1\\\int_K(x-y)f(x)\,dx=0}}\int_Kf(x)\,dx,
$$
where $f$ is Lebesgue measurable. Both extrema are attained, and the energy minimizer is unique. The maximizing density for $T_K(y)$ is the indicator, up to null sets, of a unique convex cap of centroid $y$. The cap is all of $K$ at its centroid. In particular $T_K(y)$ is the greatest volume of a convex subbody of $K$ with centroid $y$.

For every such $(K,y)$,
$$
0<T_K(y)\le E_K(y)<(d+1)T_K(y).
$$
Equality $T_K(y)=E_K(y)$ holds exactly when $y$ is the centroid of $K$. For each fixed $d\ge1$, the supremum of $E_K(y)/T_K(y)$ over these pairs is $d+1$, and no pair attains it. More precisely, if $K=\operatorname{conv}\{0,e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$ and $y=(\varepsilon,\ldots,\varepsilon)$ with $0<\varepsilon\le1/(d+1)$, then
$$
\frac{E_K(y)}{T_K(y)}=(d+1)(1-d\varepsilon).
$$
For an arbitrary simplex of volume $V$ and an interior mark with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$, $E_K(y)=V(d+1)^{d+1}\prod_{i=0}^d\lambda_i$. In dimension one, for $K-y=[-\ell,r]$ with $\ell,r>0$, $T_K(y)=2\min(\ell,r)$ and $E_K(y)=4\ell r/(\ell+r)$.

pk-intake-ordinary-simplex-depth-atomic-.relation_to_goal: An exact one-dimensional obstruction for weak additions to an ordinary uniform interval measure.
pk-intake-ordinary-simplex-depth-atomic-.statement:

u_t=\delta_g$ and $\widetilde
u_t=\delta_{g+\sqrt t}$ have the same weak limit $\delta_g$. The exact maximum ordinary raw closed-halfspace depths of $1_T\,dx+t

u_t$ be probability measures with weak limit $
u$ as $t\downarrow0$, where $
u$ has compact support and $
u\{\lambda_i=1/m\}=0$ for every $i$. Put $p_i=
u\{\lambda_i\ge1/m\}$ and $ ar p=m^{-1}\sum_i p_i$. The ordinary closed-halfspace depth for $\mu_t=1_T\,dx+t
u_t$ attains its maximum for all sufficiently small $t$. Its maximal raw and normalized values are

pk-intake-ordinary-strict-triangle-cubic.relation_to_goal: Ordinary strict triangle cuts in the specified canonical normalization. The determinant retains the coarea scale in these coordinates.
pk-intake-ordinary-strict-triangle-cubic.statement:
Use the canonical balanced normals $(1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1)$ and a marked interior point in a nondegenerate triangle with strict distinct-vertex incidence. Let $k,Q_i,\sigma_i$ be respectively the area, cap areas and chord lengths divided by the respective normal lengths. Set $M=\sum_iQ_i/\sigma_i$, $H=2M$, $f_i=2\sqrt{kQ_i}/(\sigma_iM)$ and $u_i=v_i\cdot(P_i-P_{i+1})/H$ cyclically for the matched vertices $P_i$. Put $P=\prod_i u_i$, $R=\prod_i(1-u_i)$. Then
$$
2k/H^2=P+R,\qquad \prod_i f_i=8\sqrt{PR},\qquad
k/M^2-\tfrac12\prod_i f_i=2(\sqrt P-\sqrt R)^2.
$$
In particular $M\prod_i\sigma_i\ge4\sqrt{kQ_1Q_2Q_3}$, with equality exactly when $\sum_i f_i^2+\prod_i f_i=4$.

pk-intake-ordinary-triangle-all-incidenc.relation_to_goal: An ordinary uniform triangle, an interior mark and three balanced actual normals.
pk-intake-ordinary-triangle-all-incidenc.statement:

Put $k=|K|$, $M=\sum_iq_i/\sigma_i$, and $f_i=2\sqrt{kq_i}/(\sigma_i M)$. Then
$$
\sum_i f_i^2+f_1f_2f_3\le4,\qquad
f_i+(f_j+f_l)^2/4\le2\quad(\{i,j,l\}=\{1,2,3\}).
$$
The cubic is strict if one cap strictly captures two vertices. In general equality holds precisely when the caps each have one strictly captured vertex, those vertices are distinct, and the three off-diagonal column splits of the normalized edge fractions defined in the proof have equal forward and backward products. pk-intake-ordinary-triangle-cubic-circum.relation_to_goal: Ordinary planar triangles with a balanced three-cap circuit. This characterizes equality without a cap-fraction ceiling or a restriction to centroid cuts.
pk-intake-ordinary-triangle-cubic-circum.statement:
Let $T$ be a nondegenerate planar triangle with interior source $y$ and nonzero spanning normals $v_i$ summing to zero. Put $k=|T|$, $Q_i=|T\cap\{v_i\cdot(x-y)\ge0\}|$, $\sigma_i=\mathcal H^1(T\cap\{v_i\cdot(x-y)=0\})/\lVert v_i\rVert$, $M=\sum_iQ_i/\sigma_i$, and $f_i=2\sqrt{kQ_i}/(\sigma_iM)$. Then $\sum_i f_i^2+\prod_i f_i\le4$, strictly if any cap strictly captures two vertices. Equality holds precisely when the vertices can be labeled $P_i$ so that $v_i\cdot(P_i-y)>0$ and $v_i\cdot(P_j-y)\le0$ for $j\ne i$, and an ellipse through the three $P_i$ has outward normals at them that are positive multiples of $v_i$.

In this weak incidence regime put $L_{ij}=v_i\cdot(P_i-P_j)>0$ and $H=\sum_i v_i\cdot(P_i-y)$. Then $f_i^2=4L_{ij}L_{i\ell}/H^2$ for $\{i,j,\ell\}=\{1,2,3\}$ and the row vector is independent of $y$ within the same labeled incidence regime. The ellipse condition is equivalent to $L_{12}L_{23}L_{31}=L_{13}L_{32}L_{21}$ and to the existence of $\mu_i>0$ with $\mu_iL_{ij}=\mu_jL_{ji}$. These weights are unique up to scale. The ellipse center is $O=(\sum_iP_i/\mu_i)/(\sum_i1/\mu_i)$, strictly inside $T$, and its defining quadratic form is positive definite and determined up to positive scale.

pk-intake-ordinary-two-core-inverse-weig.relation_to_goal: Conditional ordinary planar result for an attained fixed-budget minimizer with exactly two core sectors. Uniqueness is for the specified endpoint and area data.
pk-intake-ordinary-two-core-inverse-weig.statement:

Suppose $R$ minimizes $p$ over the feasible radius vectors for $W$ and exactly two sectors are cores. The core pair is one of $(0,3),(0,4),(1,3),(1,4)$. The datum $(R,W)$ has a unique realizing body, a quadrilateral whose four vertices lie strictly in the four other sectors. pk-intake-orientation-resolved-common-cr.relation_to_goal: A necessary condition at a genuine plateau of global maximizers. The terms on different supporting sections remain separate.
pk-intake-orientation-resolved-common-cr.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$ and let $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$ for compact convex $C\subset\mathbb R^{n+d}$. Let $\mu$ be its summed fiber $d$-volume, $M=\mu(S)>0$, and $D$ its raw closed ambient halfspace depth. Suppose distinct global maximizers $y_0=(p_0,x_0)$ and $y_1=(p_1,x_1)$ have an intermediate segment point in $S$. Put $Q=\max_S D$.

There are $2\le s\le d+1$ nonvertical closed caps of mass $Q$, each with both endpoints on its boundary, whose unit continuous normals $u_i$ have a minimal positive dependence of rank $s-1$. Write $\lambda_i>0$ for the coefficients, normalized by $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$ and $\sum_i\lambda_i u_i=0$. For every ambient affine $h$ with $h(y_0)=0,h(y_1)=1$, put $\delta=\operatorname{dist}(h,[0,1])$. Use only the positive-volume fibers to label each cap's proper, empty-side and full-side supporting boundary sections as in the common-cap flux lemma, with measures $\sigma_i$, proper area $A_i$, and supporting labels $E_i,F_i$. Each cap satisfies the oriented inequality individually and
$$
\sum_i\lambda_i A_i+\sum_i\lambda_i\int_{F_i}(1+\delta)\,d\sigma_i
\le \sum_i\lambda_i\int_{E_i}\delta\,d\sigma_i .
$$
In particular every cap has an empty-side supporting section with positive weighted measure outside the slab $0\le h\le1$. For polytopal positive fibers this section is a facet.

If $p_0\ne p_1$, take any affine base functional $h$ with $h(p_0)=0,h(p_1)=1$. In the affine fiber translation $x'=x-x_0-h(z)(x_1-x_0)$, every resulting base coefficient $a'_i$ satisfies $a'_i\cdot(p_1-p_0)=0$.

pk-intake-oriented-supporting-facet-flux.relation_to_goal: A necessary inequality for an actual cap minimizing at two marks. The inequality gives an empty-side exterior incidence condition and a full-side cost.
pk-intake-oriented-supporting-facet-flux.statement:

Suppose the nonvertical closed cap $H=\{L\ge0\}$ minimizes $\mu(H)$ among all closed halfspaces containing $y_e$ for each of two distinct points $y_0,y_1$ in their own fiber interiors. Assume $L(y_0)=L(y_1)=0$, and normalize the continuous component of the affine margin $L$ to norm one. The bases may coincide.

On the boundary sections $K_z\cap\{L(z,\cdot)=0\}$ use the summed $\mathcal H^{d-1}$ measure $\sigma$, with counting measure for $d=1$. Label nonempty sections by $P$ if the plane cuts the fiber interior, by $E$ if the fiber lies in $\{L\le0\}$, and by $F$ if the fiber lies in $\{L\ge0\}$. For every ambient affine $h$ with $h(y_0)=0$ and $h(y_1)=1$, put $\delta=\operatorname{dist}(h,[0,1])$ and $A=\sigma(P)$. Then
$$
0<A,\qquad A+\int_F(1+\delta)\,d\sigma\le\int_E\delta\,d\sigma.
$$
If $h$ depends only on the base, each integral is a sum of its integrand at the base times the corresponding section measure.

pk-intake-original-depth-minimal-canonic.relation_to_goal: The attainment is conditional on a strict bad input and is on a smallest bad canonical minor of the given finite base. The Helly threshold on arbitrary finite bases and the parity threshold on complete bases are distinct numerical claims. The elementary lower bound is gamma_d divided by the number of sites.
pk-intake-original-depth-minimal-canonic.statement:
Fix $d\ge1$ and $\tau>0$. For a finite nonempty base $P$ let $D_P(K)$ be normalized maximum closed-halfspace depth on the full compatible positive $d$-volume fibers $K$, and let $b_d(P)=\inf_K D_P(K)$ over all such families. Write $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Use one of the following budgets consistently on closed subsets and their canonical lifts.

- For an arbitrary finite base $P$, use its relative Helly number $q(P)=h(P)$.
- For a complete finite affine-lattice base $P$, use the number $q(P)=k(P)$ of occupied parity classes. Each closed subset uses the inherited affine lattice, and each canonical lift uses its complete integer graph realization with the inherited graph lattice.

Suppose $D_P(K)<\tau/q(P)$ for some positive compatible family. Then among the canonical lifts of nonempty closed subsets of $P$ with $b_d(\Phi_U(U))<\tau/q(U)$, choose one with the fewest sites. Write $B=\Phi_U(U)$ for any such choice, using the integer realization in the parity case. It is dependence-connected, $q(B)=q(U)\le q(P)$, every representation-preserving function on $B$ is affine, and $\dim\operatorname{aff}(B)\le h(B)-1$. In the parity case $B$ is complete in its inherited affine lattice, even if its affine rank exceeds the original rank.

On this $B$ the unrestricted infimum $\beta=b_d(B)<\tau/q(B)$ is attained by a compatible family of total volume one with every fiber of positive $d$-volume, and $\beta\ge\gamma_d/|B|>0$. More precisely, for every $0<\delta<\tau/q(B)$, the mass-one sublevel $D_B(K)\le\delta$ has a uniform positive lower bound on all fiber volumes and is sequentially compact for simultaneous fiber Hausdorff convergence after common continuous affine normalizations and affine shears on $B$. For every nonempty proper closed $T\subset B$ every member of this sublevel satisfies
$$
M_T\ \le\ \frac{D_B(K)}{\tau}\,q(T)\ \le\ \frac{\delta}{\tau}\,q(T)\ <\ \frac{q(T)}{q(B)},
\qquad M_T=\sum_{p\in T}|K_p|_d.
$$
For $\tau=\gamma_d$, the Helly case is the auxiliary finite-base reduction. In the parity case an actual mixed-integer body on $\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$ with positive total mixed $d$-volume and normalized maximum depth below $\tau/2^n$ supplies a strict bad input on its complete positive-fiber base. This includes $\tau=\gamma_d$ and any fixed $c_0\in(0,1/e)$ by taking $\tau=c_0$.
