pk-intake-original-lattice-compact-full-.relation_to_goal: Compactification of full coarse fiber shapes over a fixed lattice projection; the lift has intrinsic m-volume in continuous ambient dimension D, and no fine lattice is transported.
pk-intake-original-lattice-compact-full-.statement:
Let $k\ge0$, $m\ge1$, and let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^k$ be finite and nonempty and span $\mathbb R^k$ affinely. For every $\ell$ let $(K_{\ell,z})_{z\in P}$ be a compatible family of convex $m$-bodies in $\mathbb R^m$: for every anchored representation $z=\sum_a\lambda_a z_a$ in $P$, with nonnegative coefficients summing to one, $\sum_a\lambda_a K_{\ell,z_a}\subseteq K_{\ell,z}$. Put $M_\ell=\sum_z |K_{\ell,z}|_m$ and assume $|K_{\ell,z}|_m/M_\ell\to p_z>0$ for each $z$. Let $P_1,\ldots,P_s$ be the dependence components generated by the nontrivial anchored representations, let $L(P)$ be the scalar space preserving all anchored representations, and write $t=\dim L(P)-k-1$ and $D=sm+t$.

There are full-dimensional convex bodies $B_\ell\subset\mathbb R^k\times\mathbb R^D$ with exactly the integer bases $P$, whose integer fibers lie in fixed affine $m$-planes and are uniformly bounded there. The lifted mixed trace has intrinsic $\mathcal H_m$-mass one, with masses $|K_{\ell,z}|_m/M_\ell$. A global affine map $F_\ell$ fixing the base maps it onto the original placed family and pushes its intrinsic measure to the original sum of fiber volumes divided by $M_\ell$. On the fixed plane of a lifted fiber over $P_i$, in isometric coordinates, its continuous map has the form $x\mapsto A_{\ell,i}x+b_{\ell,z}$ with $|\det A_{\ell,i}|=M_\ell$. At every lifted point the original normalized depth at its image is at least its lifted depth. At a point in component $i$ the lifted depth equals the component mass times its depth for the normalized component law, and is continuous within each fiber. Along a subsequence all lifted fibers converge in Hausdorff distance to positive $m$-bodies in their planes; their hull is a full-dimensional limit lift with exactly those integer fibers, and maximum normalized lifted depth converges to its maximum normalized depth. Finally $m\le D\le (m+1)2^k-k-1$. All depths use every containing closed ambient halfspace.

pk-intake-original-marginal-parity-cap-t.relation_to_goal: Intrinsic original mixed mass and actual closed cap covers. The label count concerns active cap indices and fractional integer-mean sources. It supplies no response-weight payment or bound on the number of distinct centroid bases.
pk-intake-original-marginal-parity-cap-t.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$, let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact and convex, and let $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$ be nonempty. Put $q=\dim_{\mathrm H}S$, $\mu=\mathcal H^q|_S$ and $M=\mu(S)>0$. Write $\mu_r$ for the restriction to base parity $r$ and use only $r$ with $M_r=\mu_r(S)>0$. The measure $\pi=\sum_r(\mu_r\otimes\mu_r)/M_r$ has mass $M$, both marginals $\mu$, swap symmetry, and actual integer-base midpoints. Its midpoint pushforward has density $2^q\sum_r\mathcal H^q(S_r\cap(2Y-S_r))/M_r$ relative to $\mu$, where $S_r$ is the parity-$r$ trace.

For any finite cover of $S$ by closed ambient halfspaces $H_i$, assign each ordered pair symmetrically and measurably to a cap containing its midpoint, and refine by the midpoint base $j$. Let $\pi_{ij}$ be the resulting pair submeasures, $\nu_{ij}$ their common marginal and $t_{ij}$ their mass. Then $\sum_{ij}\nu_{ij}=\mu$, each $\nu_{ij}\le\mu$, and $\int(z-j)\,d\nu_{ij}=0$. For $t_{ij}>0$ the centroid $Y_{ij}$ of $\nu_{ij}$ belongs to $S\cap H_i$. For any affine margin $L_i$ defining $H_i$,
$t_{ij}L_i(Y_{ij})=\int L_i((A+B)/2)\,d\pi_{ij}\ge0$. If $\max_i L_i\ge\varepsilon>0$ on $S$, assignment by a largest margin ensures the stronger bound $\varepsilon t_{ij}$.

For any subset $T$ of positive table labels, write $I$ for its cap indices, $U=\bigcup_{i\in I}H_i$, and $\pi_T,\nu_T,t_T$ for the corresponding sums. Put $\kappa_T=\pi_T(U\times U)$, $c_i=\mu(H_i)$, and $D_I=\sum_{i\in I}c_i-\mu(U)$. Then
$$
t_T+\kappa_T=2\nu_T(U)\le2\mu(U),\qquad
t_T+\kappa_T+2D_I\le2\sum_{i\in I}c_i.
$$
In particular the single-index aggregates satisfy $t_i+\kappa_i\le2c_i$. Under assignment prioritizing any common endpoint cap, $\sum_i\kappa_i>0$. If $c_i\le B$ for all $i$ and $K$ indices are active, then $M+\sum_i\kappa_i\le2KB$ and $K>M/(2B)$. With $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, $B<\gamma_d M/2^n$ implies $K>2^n/(2\gamma_d)\ge2^n$.

pk-intake-original-volume-affine-scale-c.relation_to_goal: Geometric envelope contact for one sampled integer coordinate under the pushforward of original fiber volumes. It assumes no actual deepest-source or critical-cap equations.
pk-intake-original-volume-affine-scale-c.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ be an integer and let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}D$. Define $\ell(z)=z+1$ for $0\le z\le3$ and $r(z)=\min\{z+1,3\}$ there. The compact convex set
$$
C=\{(z,x):0\le z\le3,\ x\in r(z)D\}
$$
is the canonical hull of its positive integer fibers at $0,1,2,3$. The affine envelope $\ell(z)D$ equals the actual fiber throughout $[0,2]$, which contains the interior integer $1$, and every integer fiber has strictly less than half the original total mixed volume. Under $(z,x)\mapsto x/\ell(z)$, the original mixed volume has density
$$
f=(1+2^d+3^d)\mathbf 1_D+4^d\mathbf 1_{(3/4)D}.
$$
There is no positive continuous $g$ on $\operatorname{int}D$ with $f/2\le g\le f$ almost everywhere there. In particular there is no such bounded positive log-concave $g$, or such positive $g$ with a finite convex inverse power on $\operatorname{int}D$.

pk-intake-outward-smoothed-balanced-fini.relation_to_goal: Whole-fiber upper covers and their exact first-order loss at positive width.
pk-intake-outward-smoothed-balanced-fini.statement:
Use the uniform outward positive-width problem of the clipping theorem with tied buffer $\varepsilon f$ for $\varepsilon\ge0$. Assume the compact response-preserving clipping, proper coarea and pure-base reserve hold at all deepest marks, which are singleton on their bases. For each deepest mark $Y_i=(p_i,y_i)$ of raw depth $Q$, there is an actual finite menu of $\Gamma$-unit active caps $(N_{ij},c_{ij})$ with positive weights $\rho_{ij}$ summing to one, at most $d+1$ caps, and $\sum_j\rho_{ij}u_{ij}=\varepsilon\nabla_x f(Y_i)$.

Take an actual compatible signed radial path with the uniform $O(t)$ radial bound and bounded almost-everywhere inward speed $v_z$. For $\varepsilon>0$ allow finite cap-normal velocities $\nu_j=(\dot a_j,\dot u_j)$ and a signed log-scale velocity $s$, with $\varepsilon(t)=\varepsilon e^{st}$. For $\varepsilon=0$ keep the cap normals fixed and $\varepsilon(t)=0$. In both cases keep $h>0$ fixed. Put
$$
\alpha_i(t)=\min_{x\in K_{p_i}(t)}\left[
\sum_j\rho_{ij}\{N_{ij}(t)\cdot(p_i,x)-c_{ij}\}
-\varepsilon(t) f_t(p_i,x)\sum_j\rho_{ij}\Gamma_t(u_{ij}(t))\right].
$$
Then $\alpha_i(0)=0$. $$
S(p,\ell)=\sum_{h\ge0}(p-\ell h)_+^2,\qquad
f_k(p,\ell)=(1-k)\left(\frac{p^3}{3\ell}+\frac{p^2}{2}\right)+kp^2,
$$
where the sum is over integers. For $1/3\le b\le1/2$ and $0\le z\le b$, put $P=1-b$. Then
$$
\frac{f_k(P,k(1-z))+f_k(P-kz,k(1+z))}{2-3b}
>\frac49\left(\frac1{3k}+\frac12+\frac{k}{5}\right).
$$

$$

f_-(h)=F_{1-kh}(t-\beta h),\qquad f_+(h)=F_{1-kh}(t+\beta(h+1)),

pk-intake-parity-preserving-signed-arith.relation_to_goal: Actual one-integer one-continuous-dimensional buffer. This shows changing nondeepest cap credit at fixed parity totals and fixed deepest status. The example has one positive deepest stratum and concerns a buffered objective.
pk-intake-parity-preserving-signed-arith.statement:
Let $n=d=1$, $1/16\le a\le1/8$ and $b=9/8-a$. Let $C(a,b)$ be the canonical hull of centered intervals of lengths $a,1,b$ at the integer bases $-1,0,1$. Write $\mu$ for the original mixed length, $M=17/8$, and $\Sigma=(a^3+1+b^3)/(12M)$ for the original volume-weighted within-fiber variance. For $0<\varepsilon\le10^{-4}$, let $L$ range over continuous nonnegative concave parameters on $C(a,b)$ with $\int L\,d\mu=M$. Use the ordinary interval projective energy $E_z(y)$, with value zero at the own endpoints, and the arithmetic buffer
$$
\varepsilon\sqrt{\Sigma}\,|u|\sqrt{L(z,y)E_z(y)/M}
$$
subtracted from the through-mark threshold for a cap with continuous coefficient $u$. Pure-base containing caps are unchanged. Equivalently, a unit continuous normal gives the displayed physical shift without the factor $|u|$. The unique parameter minimizing the maximum raw buffered depth is $L_*(z,y)=M(1+z)/(1+2b)$. Its unique deepest mark is $(0,0)$ and its exact maximum is $Q_\varepsilon=1/2+a+\varepsilon D$, where $D=\sqrt{\Sigma/(1+2b)}$ and $\beta_\varepsilon=Q_\varepsilon/M$.

On the actual path $(a_t,b_t)=(a-t,b+t)$ while $a_t$ stays in range, the sampled even and odd masses stay $1,9/8$, respectively, and the real length roof changes by $tz$. At the current parameters
$$
\frac{D'}D=\frac12\left[\frac{3(b^2-a^2)}{a^3+1+b^3}-\frac{2}{1+2b}\right],\qquad
Q_\varepsilon'<-1+\frac{3\varepsilon}{10}<0,\qquad
\beta_\varepsilon'=Q_\varepsilon'/M.
$$
The caps $\pm x-2z\ge-\varepsilon D$ attain the depth at $(0,0)$ and each has own coarea one in this scaling. Each fully captures the zero-$L$ left fiber and misses the positive-$L$ right fiber, so its odd-parity credit decreases at rate one with the fixed parity mass. The only deepest base is $0$, in the positive-$L$ class. All nonempty proper closed-minor quotas $\sum_{z\in B}V_z<M k(B)/2$ are strict for $a>1/16$, and at $a=1/16$ only the right singleton meets equality. Here $B$ ranges over sampled subsets closed under taking the sampled convex hull, and $k(B)$ counts their occupied base parities.

pk-intake-parity-witness-forest-affine-a.relation_to_goal: A deterministic point-incidence implication. It makes no claim about disjointness of images or how original mixed volume is apportioned among cap traces.
pk-intake-parity-witness-forest-affine-a.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^{n+d}$ be compact convex and let $J$ be its nonempty lattice projection, meaning the integer bases with nonempty fiber $K_z$. Choose $p_r\in J$ in each parity $r\bmod 2$, and suppose $\operatorname{conv}\{p_r\}\cap\mathbb Z^n=\{p_r\}$. For each root choose $g_r\in K_{p_r}$. Put $z_0=z\in J$, $z_{j+1}=(z_j+p_{[z_j]})/2$, where $[z_j]$ denotes the parity of $z_j$, and stop when $z_k=p_s$. This happens in finitely many steps. For every $x\in K_z$, the point
$$
T_z(x)=2^{-k}x+\sum_{j<k}2^{j-k}g_{[z_j]}
$$
belongs to $K_{p_s}$. For every closed ambient halfspace containing $(p_s,T_z(x))$, it contains $(z,x)$ or at least one of the anchors $(p_{[z_j]},g_{[z_j]})$ used on this path.

pk-intake-physical-martingale-affine-con.relation_to_goal: An identity for the actual physical marginals of a martingale. Its equality hypothesis is what a subsequent exact contact repair would need.
pk-intake-physical-martingale-affine-con.statement:
Let $\Pi(ds,dt)=\nu(ds)P_s(dt)$ be a finite physical martingale on a compact convex set $C$ with target $\eta$, and let $L=\min_{1\le i\le N}A_i$ be the minimum of finitely many affine functions on $C$. Choose the least active index $i(s)$ at each source. Then
$
\int L\,d\nu-\int L\,d\eta
=\int[A_{i(s)}(t)-L(t)]\,d\Pi(s,t)\ge0.
$
Equality holds exactly when for $\nu$-almost every source $s$, its row $P_s$ is concentrated in every closed contact cell $\{A_i=L\}$ active at $s$. If $\nu=(W/\beta)\eta$ with $\beta>0$, the dissipation equals $\beta^{-1}\int L(W-\beta)\,d\eta$. These assertions apply separately under any conditioning for which the conditional marginals and martingale row identity hold.

pk-intake-physical-retained-mass-right-d.relation_to_goal: Ordinary retained centroidal volume under actual radial erosions. No stationarity or mixed depth bound is asserted.
pk-intake-physical-retained-mass-right-d.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior, and let $y,o\in\operatorname{int}K$. Let $K_\varepsilon$ be nested compact convex bodies for $\varepsilon\ge0$ with $K_0=K$. Suppose that for some $C\ge0$ and all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$,
$$
o+(1-C\varepsilon)(K-o)\subseteq K_\varepsilon\subseteq K.
$$
For $x\in\partial K$, write the radial endpoint of $K_\varepsilon$ on the ray from $o$ through $x$ as $o+(1-t_\varepsilon(x))(x-o)$. At a regular boundary point $x$, let $n(x)$ be its unique outward unit normal and set $dS=d\mathcal H^{d-1}$ on $\partial K$. Assume that for a bounded measurable $v$,
$$
\frac{t_\varepsilon(x)}{\varepsilon}\longrightarrow
\frac{v(x)}{n(x)\cdot(x-o)}
\qquad\text{for $dS$ almost every }x.
$$
Then $v\ge0$ almost everywhere. Take $y_\varepsilon=y+\varepsilon w+o(\varepsilon)$ for a fixed $w\in\mathbb R^d$. For a body $L$ and $q\in\operatorname{int}L$, let
$$
T_L(q)=\max\left\{\int_L f(x)\,dx:\ 0\le f\le1,\ f\text{ measurable},\
                       \int_L(x-q)f(x)\,dx=0\right\}.
$$
Set $T=T_K(y)$ and let $U$ be the compact nonempty set of minimizers of $G_0(u)=\int_K[1+u\cdot(x-y)]_+\,dx$, where $[a]_+=\max(a,0)$. For all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, $y_\varepsilon\in\operatorname{int}K_\varepsilon$. The following right derivative exists, and the minimum is attained:
$$
\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\right|_{0+}T_{K_\varepsilon}(y_\varepsilon)
=\min_{u\in U}\left\{
-\int_{\partial K}[1+u\cdot(x-y)]_+v(x)\,dS(x)-T\,u\cdot w
\right\}. \tag{1}
$$
When $y$ differs from the centroid $g_K$, $U$ is a singleton. When $y=g_K$, put $V=|K|$, $D=\int_{\partial K}v\,dS$ and $B=\int_{\partial K}(x-y)v(x)\,dS(x)$. For the Minkowski gauge $p_{K-y}(z)=\inf\{t\ge0:z\in t(K-y)\}$, (1) becomes
$$
\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\right|_{0+}T_{K_\varepsilon}(y_\varepsilon)
=-D-p_{K-y}(-B-Vw).
\tag{2}
$$
The ordinary centroid satisfies $g_{K_\varepsilon}=y-\varepsilon B/V+o(\varepsilon)$. The derivative in (2) equals $-D$ exactly when $w=-B/V$, and is strictly smaller otherwise. In dimension $1$, $dS$ is counting measure on the two endpoints. The formula allows hinge hyperplanes incident with vertices, edges, and supporting facets; it does not require a differentiable cutting section.

pk-intake-physical-simplex-canonical-cap.relation_to_goal: Ordinary d-volume on a simplex whose labeled vertices may move freely near the reference position. The cap halfspaces are fixed; this is not an optimized threshold Hessian for a stochastic row.
pk-intake-physical-simplex-canonical-cap.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $m=d+1$, and $\gamma=(d/m)^d$. In the barycentric hyperplane $\sum_i \xi_i=1$ with a fixed Euclidean metric, the reference simplex has vertex matrix $I$ and volume $V>0$. Fix the $m$ cap halfspaces $\{\xi_i\ge1/m\}$. For a column-sum-one matrix $W$ near $I$, let $F_i(W)$ be its simplex volume in cap $i$. Then its total volume is $V\det W$, and
$$
F_i(W)=V\det W\frac{(W_{ii}-1/m)^d}{\prod_{j\ne i}(W_{ii}-W_{ij})}.
$$
The Lagrangian $L(W)=V\det W-(m\gamma)^{-1}\sum_iF_i(W)$ is stationary at $I$. For $W=I+tB$, where the column sums of $B$ are zero, set $A$ equal to the off-diagonal part of $B$, with column sums $c$ and row sums $s$. Then $F_i'(0)/(\gamma V)=\operatorname{tr}B+\sum_jB_{ij}$ and
$$
\frac{L''(0)}{V}=\frac{\lVert c\rVert^2}{d}-\frac{\lVert s\rVert^2+\lVert A\rVert_F^2}{m}.
$$
The Hessian of $L$ on the full physical vertex tangent space has inertia $(d,1,d^2-1)$ in the order positive, zero, negative.

pk-intake-planar-affine-frustum-common-c.relation_to_goal: Exact two-law bound for a fixed proper planar affine profile with a nontrivial bounded centered branch.
pk-intake-planar-affine-frustum-common-c.statement:
Let $H>0$ and $0<U<H$, and put $r(z)=(H-z)/(H+1)$ on $[-1,U]$. Use density $1/2$ on the planar region $|x|\le r(z)$. For finite $s\ge0$, let $P(s)$ be the mass of $z+sx\ge0$, and let $C(s),M(s)$ be the integrals of the density and of $z$ times the density over $z+sx=0$ inside the region, with respect to $d\mathcal H^1/\sqrt{1+s^2}$. Set $a=1/(H+1)$, $T=U/r(U)$, $t=r(U)^2$, $V_0=(H+1)/2$, $V=(1-t)V_0$, $C_0=1-a$ and $p=(1-a)^2$. Assume $0<a<1/2$ and $T\ge s_*=1/(1-2a)$. Set
$$
v_*=1-a,\quad e_*=\frac{1-2a}{1-a},\quad
\kappa=\frac{v_*+t}{1+e_*},\quad
\beta=\frac{\kappa-t}{1-t},\quad
c=\frac{V_0}{C_0}(p-\kappa).
$$
For every probability law on $[0,\infty]$ with averaged moment zero, where $\infty$ has record $(V/2,0,0)$, its averaged records obey $\beta V\le P-cC\le(1-\beta)V$, with $4/9\le\beta\le1/2$. For any two separately centered laws $\mu,\nu$ with $C_\mu+C_\nu>0$, the balanced mean
$$
\frac{C_\nu P_\mu+C_\mu(V-P_\nu)}{V(C_\mu+C_\nu)}
$$
is at least $\beta$. Its value is $1/2$ if one coarea is zero, and it extends continuously as $1/2$ at zero total coarea. The bound $\beta$ is attained by the pair $\delta_0,\delta_{s_*}$.

$$
|A\cap\{t\le2-2W\}|\le v,\qquad W\le\frac{2a}{h-\ell},\qquad |A\cap\{t\ge2\}|\ge a-v-2W^2.

If the cut $t=-1$ meets the interior of $A$, put $H=h+1$. Then $W<2a/H$ and $|A\cap\{t\ge2\}|\ge a-v-8a^2/H^2$. The same conclusions hold if any two distinct covectors from $(1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1)$ are used as $x,y$, with $t$ given by the remaining covector.

Let $A\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a convex body of area $a$. Write $u=|A\cap\{x\ge-1\}|$ and $v=|A\cap\{y\ge-1\}|$, with $u\le v$ and $0<v<a/2$. Put $t=-x-y$, $h=\max_A t>2$, $H=h+1$, $w=|A\cap\{t\ge-1\}|$, $e=a-w>0$, and $\Delta=\sqrt a-\sqrt e$. Then

\qquad
(v-e)H^2-6\sqrt e\,\Delta H+8a^2-9\Delta^2\ \ge\ 0.

pk-intake-planar-concave-roof-depth-and-.relation_to_goal: Ordinary planar depth for each fixed roof. The threshold in epsilon can depend on the roof.
pk-intake-planar-concave-roof-depth-and-.statement:
Let $\psi:[0,1]\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous, concave and not identically zero. Put $I=[1/3,2/3]$, $Z=\int_0^1\psi$ and $E=\int_I\psi-Z/3$. For $\varepsilon>0$, let $K_\varepsilon=\{(s,r):0\le s\le1,\ s-1\le r\le\varepsilon\psi(s)\}$ and $V=1/2$. Its maximum normalized ordinary closed-halfspace depth is $4/9+\varepsilon E/(3V)+o(\varepsilon)$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. If $E>0$, for every fixed $0<c<1/9$ and all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, the excess over $4/9$ is at least $c$ times the infimum of its closed-halfspace discrepancy to normalized uniform laws on full-dimensional triangles. Here the discrepancy is the supremum of the absolute mass difference over closed halfspaces.

For the secant $\ell(s)=a+bs$ through the ends of $I$, set $A=\int_I(\psi-\ell)$ and $B=\int_{[0,1]\setminus I}(\ell-\psi)$. Then $E=(2A+B)/3$ and $\int_0^1|\psi-\ell|=A+B\le3E$, with $E=0$ exactly for affine roofs. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, the explicit triangle $L_\varepsilon=\{(s,r):s\ge0,\ s-1\le r\le\varepsilon\ell(s)\}$ gives a comparison with total variation divided by $\varepsilon$ tending to $\max(A,B)/V$.

pk-intake-planar-critical-cap-root-covar.relation_to_goal: Finite affine arrays with a positive-root constraint. The formula gives a stationary mass when applied to actual planar caps and does not certify all-normal depth.
pk-intake-planar-critical-cap-root-covar.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite, $z_0\in P$, and $a_z>0$ affine on $P$ with $\sum_z(z-z_0)a_z=0$. Write $N=|P|$, $\bar z=N^{-1}\sum_z z$, $E=\operatorname{span}(P-\bar z)$, $\Sigma=N^{-1}\sum_z(z-\bar z)(z-\bar z)^{\mathsf T}$ on $E$, $w=z_0-\bar z$, and $\Delta=w^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}w$. For a singleton take $\Delta=0$ and omit the inverse term. With $\alpha=N^{-1}\sum_z a_z$ and $a_0=a_{z_0}$,
$$
a_z=\alpha[1+w^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}(z-\bar z)],\qquad
a_0=\alpha(1+\Delta),\qquad
\sum_z a_z^2=\frac{Na_0^2}{1+\Delta}.
$$
Conversely the displayed affine array for any $\alpha>0$ satisfies the balance and is admissible exactly when all brackets are positive. For $P=\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$, $N\ge2$, this is equivalent to $|z_0-\bar z|<(N+1)/6$. At $N=2m,z_0=m-1$, feasibility is equivalent to $m\ge2$, and $\sum_z a_z^2=2ma_0^2(4m^2-1)/(4m^2+2)$. For $a_0^2=4/9$ the latter mass is $4m(4m^2-1)/(9(2m^2+1))$, equal to $112/33$ when $m=4$.

pk-intake-planar-diagonal-envelope-own-c.relation_to_goal: Ordinary triangle area bounds for a specified nonnegative normal. The own-centroid estimate has the sharp angular coefficient in the stated range.
pk-intake-planar-diagonal-envelope-own-c.statement:
Let $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2)$ and $V=|T|=1/2$. For $a\in[1/2,1]$, $r\ge0$ and $q\in\mathbb R$ set $F_{a,r}(q)=|rT\cap\{ax_1+(1-a)x_2\ge q\}|/V$, using planar area. For all $q\ge0$,
$$
F_{a,r}(q)\ge 4q(r-2q)_+,\qquad s_+=\max\{s,0\}.
$$
For $1/2\le a\le2/3$, $F_{a,r}(r/3)\ge r^2/2=(4/9+1/18)r^2$. The coefficient $1/2$ is attained at $a=2/3$.

pk-intake-planar-endpoint-all-level-extr.relation_to_goal: Necessary inequalities for the actual planar all-zero-B critical regime under the stated bad-source bounds. The new information is levelwise and uses the actual section-length function.
pk-intake-planar-endpoint-all-level-extr.statement:
Let $A,K,B\subset\mathbb R^2$ be actual positive-area convex fibers at the only positive-area integer sites $-1,0,1$, respectively. Assume $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$ and $0\in\operatorname{int}K$. Set $v_1=(1,0),v_2=(0,1),v_3=(-1,-1)$ and $T=\{X:v_i\cdot X\le1,\ 1\le i\le3\}$, of area $9/2$. Assume $B\subseteq T$ and each closed cap $v_i\cdot X\ge z$ through $(0,0)$ attains its actual raw mixed area depth $Q$, with proper $A$ cut and zero $B$ area. Write $a,k,b$ for the three fiber areas and $u\le v\le w$ for the ordered $A$ cap areas, with $v_\ell$ the normal of a largest one. Assume $b\le a+k$ and $Q\le2(a+k+b)/9$. Set
$$
q=Q-w,\quad H=h_A(v_\ell)+1,\quad r=(a-u-v)/w,\quad s=\sqrt{1-r}.
$$
Then $H\ge3/s>3$ and $w\le2q$. For every $t\in[-2,1]$ put $x=H-1+t$, $\eta=(t+2)/3$, and $\ell(t)=\mathcal H^1(B\cap\{v_\ell\cdot X=t\})/\lVert v_\ell\rVert$, with value zero on empty sections. Then $b=\int_{-2}^1\ell(t)\,dt$, $0\le\ell(t)\le t+2$, and
$$
4q\ge x\ell(t)+w\max\{(x/H)^2,[\eta+(1-\eta)\sqrt r]^2\}.
$$
In particular, with $A_0=H-3$,
$$
b\le\int_{A_0}^H\min\{x-A_0,\ 4q/x-wx/H^2\}\,dx.
$$
This integral is $9/2$ when $4q\ge3H+w$. Otherwise it equals $2q-A_0(x_0-A_0)/2-w/2+4q\log(H/x_0)$, with
$$
x_0=\frac{A_0+\sqrt{A_0^2+16q(1+w/H^2)}}{2(1+w/H^2)}.
$$
The following further bounds hold:
$$
\begin{aligned}
b&\le 2q[1+\log((9+w)/(4q))]-w/2,\\
b&\le \frac{8s}{2-s}q-\frac{s(2-s)}2 w,\\
b&\le \frac{2s}{2-s}\left[4q-\frac w4(1+\sqrt r)^2\right].
\end{aligned}
$$
In particular $(41s-18)q\ge2(2-s)(s^2+2s+3)w$ and $r<1357/1681$. The preceding upper bounds and levelwise inequality remain valid when $r$ is replaced by $r_*=(a-v-u/4)/w$ and $s$ by $\sqrt{1-r_*}$; the final coupled lower bound on $(41s-18)q$ is stated for the original $r,s$.

pk-intake-planar-equal-area-exact-midpoi.relation_to_goal: Exact Minkowski midpoint and equal-area planar endpoints. The uniform constant is a certified lower bound at the specified ordinary midpoint centroid.
pk-intake-planar-equal-area-exact-midpoi.statement:

In the convex hull of the lifted endpoint bodies at bases $-1,1$, the only integer fibers are $A,M,B$ at $-1,0,1$. For every closed ambient halfspace containing $(0,g_M)$ the fraction of total mixed area it captures is at least
$$
 G(r)=\frac{4r/9+\max\{1/9,\;4\sqrt{5r}/3-20r/9\}}{r+2}.
$$
In particular the normalized depth at that mark is at least
$$
 \frac{4(22+12\sqrt 2)}{9(57+12\sqrt 2)}>\frac29 .
$$

pk-intake-planar-grid-hull-exact-trapezo.relation_to_goal: An exact area identity for planar hulls of original grid sections, including collapsed projections.
pk-intake-planar-grid-hull-exact-trapezo.statement: Let $G=t+h\mathbb Z$, $h>0$, and let $Q\subset\mathbb R_u\times\mathbb R_x$ be nonempty, compact and convex, with $Q=\operatorname{conv}(Q\cap(G\times\mathbb R))$. Its nonempty grid fibers have consecutive indices $j=a,\ldots,b$. Write $N=b-a+1$, their lengths $w_j\ge0$, $T=\sum_jw_j$, and $E=(w_a+w_b)/2$, counting the same endpoint twice if $N=1$. Then $|Q|_2=h(T-E)$. If $N\ge2$, then $T\ge NE$ and $(1-1/N)T\le|Q|_2/h\le T$, so $T\le2|Q|_2/h$. Affine widths attain the lower inequality and zero endpoint widths attain the upper one.

pk-intake-planar-interval-reflection-var.relation_to_goal: Exact finite planar mixed-length identity at an actual mark and an explicit fiber-count estimate. Half-depth rigidity and the extraction equivalence have separate accepted facts.
pk-intake-planar-interval-reflection-var.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R$ be a compact convex body with positive mixed length $M$. Write $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R)$, $\mu=\mathcal H^1|_S$, and let $K_z$ be its integer interval fibers. Fix any actual $y=(j,c)\in S$, including an endpoint or a point fiber. Define
$$
F(a)=\mu\{(z,x):x-c-a(z-j)\ge0\},\qquad R(y)=\mu(S\cap(2y-S)).
$$
For $k\ge1$ set $I_k^+=(K_{j+k}-c)/k$ and $I_k^-=(c-K_{j-k})/k$, with a missing fiber giving the empty interval. Then almost everywhere in $a$,
$$
F'(a)=\sum_{k\ge1}k\bigl(\mathbf1_{I_k^-}(a)-\mathbf1_{I_k^+}(a)\bigr),
$$
and
$$
M-R(y)=\operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb R}(F)+|F(+\infty)+F(-\infty)-M|.
$$
Here $F$ is continuous and piecewise affine with constant tails, and $\operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb R}(F)=\int_{\mathbb R}|F'(a)|\,da$. If the anchor lies on a positive-length fiber, $N$ is the number of positive-length fibers, $A_C(y)$ is the raw closed-halfspace depth, and $\delta=M/2-A_C(y)$, then $M-R(y)\le4(N-1)\delta$ for $N\ge2$, and $M-R(y)=2\delta$ for $N=1$.

pk-intake-planar-marked-depth-aligned-mi.relation_to_goal: A named source on three actual planar fibers, for three true minimizing cuts with zero area on the same endpoint.
pk-intake-planar-marked-depth-aligned-mi.statement:
Let the only nonempty integer fibers of a convex body in $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2$ be full planar convex bodies $A,K,B$ at $-1,0,1$. Use $v_1=(1,0)$, $v_2=(0,1)$, $v_3=(-1,-1)$, and put $T=\{x:v_i\cdot x\le1\ \forall i\}$. Assume $0\in\operatorname{int}K$, each $A$ cut $v_i\cdot x=-1$ is proper, and each ambient cap $v_i\cdot x\ge z$ captures zero area in $B$ and attains the genuine raw depth $Q$ at $(0,0)$, computed over all containing closed ambient halfspaces. Write $a=|A|$, $k=|K|$, $b=|B|$, $M=a+k+b$, and let $u\le v\le w$ be the three sorted $A$ cap areas. Then $B\subseteq T$, and
$$
a\le w+v+u/4,\qquad k\le9Q/4-u-v-w/4,\qquad
w\le2Q/3,\qquad Q\ge4k/9.
$$
Consequently $Q/M\ge4k/(11k+9b)$, so $k\ge9b/7$ suffices for $Q/M\ge2/9$. If $Q\le2M/9$, then $Q\le4b/7$ and $k\le9b/7$. If $K=\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge-t_i\ \forall i\}$ is the aligned triangle, then $Q/M>4/17>2/9$.

pk-intake-planar-nested-triangle-contain.relation_to_goal: Planar area estimate for arbitrary enclosing triangles and compact convex enlargements, used to measure the cost of convexifying separate fiber containers.

P=\{(x,y):x,y\le a,\ x+y\ge\varepsilon\}.

$$
(|R|-|A|)+\tfrac14(|L|-|P|)\ge\varepsilon/16.
$$

pk-intake-planar-paired-simplex-central-.relation_to_goal: Prescribes the actual centroid at base zero for half-integer-reflected chains of homothetic common-vertex triangles with concave radii. pk-intake-planar-paired-simplex-central-.statement: Let $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2)$, $V=|T|=1/2$, and $m\ge0$ be an integer. Let $S$ have the two fibers $r_hT$ at integer bases $-h$ and $h+1$ for each $0\le h\le m$, and no other fibers. Write $\mu=\mathcal H_2|_S$, $W=\sum_{h=0}^m r_h^2$, $t=R/3$, and $y=(0,t,t)$. The fraction $2/9$ is attained within this class when $m=0$. For every $a\in[1/2,2/3]$ and every real $b$, the through-$y$ halfspace $\{bz+ax_1+(1-a)x_2\ge t\}$ has mass at least $V((4/9)W+R^2/162)$.

pk-intake-planar-prescribed-sector-area-.relation_to_goal: Exact feasibility of ordinary planar ray-endpoint and sector-area data; does not certify feasibility of an ambient mixed-integer family or establish a depth bound.
pk-intake-planar-prescribed-sector-area-.statement:
Let $m\ge3$ and let $P_i\in\mathbb R^2\setminus\{0\}$ lie on distinct rays in counterclockwise cyclic order with consecutive angular gaps strictly less than $\pi$. Put $D_i=\det(P_i,P_{i+1})>0$, $E_i=\det(P_{i-1},P_{i+1})$, and $\kappa_i=D_{i-1}+D_i-E_i$. Prescribe finite areas $A_i\ge D_i/2$, set $h_i=1/D_i-1/(2A_i)$ and $b_i=\kappa_i/(D_{i-1}D_i)$, and define $L$ by
$$
x^\top Lx=\sum_i b_i x_i^2-\sum_i h_i(x_i+x_{i+1})^2.
$$
There is a convex body containing $0$ in its interior whose boundary intersects the $i$th ray at exactly $P_i$ and whose area in $\operatorname{cone}(P_i,P_{i+1})$ is exactly $A_i$ if and only if $L$ is positive semidefinite. If feasible, the body can be chosen to be a polygon with at most one vertex in each open sector and at most $2m$ vertices in total. If any prescribed area is below $D_i/2$, realization is impossible.

In the open sector between two consecutive rays, $Q$ has at most one vertex. Thus it has at most $2m$ vertices.

pk-intake-pointwise-own-depth-root-equal.statement: Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex, $d\ge1$, and let $F(Y)$ be the $d$th root of the ordinary raw depth in the fiber of $Y=(z,x)\in C$. pk-intake-polygon-adjacent-sector-cut-an.relation_to_goal: Ordinary planar feasible polygons, in the Hausdorff topology; no termination or unrestricted minimizing shape, Lorentz row or mixed-fiber conclusion.
pk-intake-polygon-adjacent-sector-cut-an.statement:
Use the three normals $v_1=(1,0)$, $v_2=(0,1)$, $v_3=(-1,-1)$ through the interior mark $0$. For a planar convex body $K$, let $q_i$ be the cap areas, $\sigma_i=\mathcal H^1(K\cap v_i^\perp)/\lVert v_i\rVert$, and $\lambda_i=(1/\sigma_i)/\sum_j(1/\sigma_j)$. Let $K$ be a convex polygon and $P=(0,h)$, $h>0$, its positive vertical ray endpoint. Suppose $P$ lies in the relative interior of an edge with consecutive vertices $R,S$, or is a vertex flanked by $R,S$ in counterclockwise order. Require $R=(r_x,r_y)$ with $r_x,r_y>0$, and $S=(s_x,s_y)$ with $s_x<0<s_y$ and $s_x+s_y>0$. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ there is an actual nearby polygon with the same area and changes
$$
\Delta(q_1,q_2,q_3)=(s_x\varepsilon/2,0,0),\qquad
\Delta(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)=(\varepsilon,0,0).
$$
The new polygon contains $0$ in its interior and converges to $K$ in Hausdorff distance. Thus $\lambda_1$ strictly decreases, the other weights increase, and an initially minimal $\lambda_1$ remains minimal. Any initially satisfied cap upper bounds of the form $q_i\le c_i|K|$ and the constraint $q_{\min}+q_{\mathrm{mid}}+q_{\max}/4\le |K|$ remain satisfied. Consequently this adjacent-sector endpoint geometry cannot occur at a local minimum of the selected inverse weight within the feasible polygon class. The corresponding statements hold after cyclically permuting the caps or interchanging the two coordinate axes.

pk-intake-polytopal-distal-quantile-vari.relation_to_goal: Piecewise fixed-normal variation with polytopal fibers, including right creation at the null core. The formulas do not give a sign or a C² extension across chamber changes.
pk-intake-polytopal-distal-quantile-vari.statement:
Use the distal quantile path of an actual mixed critical cover and suppose $C$ is a polytope. Write $G(T)=\mu(C\cap\bigcap_i\{\ell_i\le T_i\})$. Then $G$ is continuous and piecewise polynomial of degree at most $d$ on a finite polyhedral subdivision. Each original tail $F_i$ has the corresponding piecewise polynomial property in its threshold. Off finitely many levels, the selected inverse branches $t_i(a)$ are analytic and algebraic with
$$
S_i=-F_i'(t_i)>0,\qquad t_i'=1/S_i,\qquad t_i''=-S_i'/S_i^3,
$$
where $S_i'$ is the threshold derivative and $S_i$ sums original proper section areas. After finitely subdividing $0<a<B$, the path is on a single chamber or persistent face on each open piece, and a chamber polynomial $P$ evaluates $G$ along it. On that piece,
$$
M'=\sum_i P_i/S_i,\qquad
M''=\sum_{ij}P_{ij}/(S_iS_j)-\sum_i P_i S_i'/S_i^3 .
$$
On open chambers without moving-facet coincidences, $P_i$ is the sum of exposed clipped areas for that cut, between $0$ and $S_i$.

Let $q_0$ be the largest affine dimension of a nonempty core fiber $(C_0)_z$ over an originally positive fiber. Then $0\le q_0\le d-1$ and
$$
M(a)=c\,a^{d-q_0}+O(a^{d-q_0+1})\qquad(a\downarrow0)
$$
for some $c>0$. In particular $M(a)/a\to0$ if $q_0\le d-2$ and $M(a)/a\to c$ if $q_0=d-1$.

pk-intake-polytopal-parallel-cap-two-jet.relation_to_goal: A fiberwise cap calculus for polytopes, including positive-area supporting facets.
pk-intake-polytopal-parallel-cap-two-jet.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact polytope and $u$ a unit vector. Then $F(T)=|K\cap\{u\cdot X\ge T\}|$ is continuous and polynomial of degree at most $d$ between consecutive vertex heights in direction $u$, and constant outside their range. Write $f^\pm$ and $h^\pm$ for its one-sided first and second derivatives at a given $T$. For $t\downarrow0$,
$$
F(T+tq+t^2 r/2)=F(T)+tD(q)+t^2 E(q,r)/2+o(t^2),
$$
where $D(0)=0$, $D(q)=f^{\operatorname{sgn}(q)}q$ if $q\ne0$, $E(0,r)=D(r)$, and $E(q,r)=h^{\operatorname{sgn}(q)}q^2+f^{\operatorname{sgn}(q)}r$ if $q\ne0$. At an inside supporting facet of area $S$, $D(q)=-S\max(q,0)$. At an outside supporting facet of area $S$, $D(q)=S\max(-q,0)$. At a proper cut the two first derivatives agree and equal minus the section area.

pk-intake-positive-coarse-fiberwise-fine.relation_to_goal: Exact depth convergence in the fixed product splitting with a positive limiting full coarse mass and individual coarse-fiber limits.
pk-intake-positive-coarse-fiberwise-fine.statement:
Let $k\ge0$, $r\ge1$, $s\ge0$, and $m=r+s$. Let $C_\ell\subset\mathbb R^k\times\mathbb R^r\times\mathbb R^s$ be compact and convex, with the same finite set $P\subset\mathbb Z^k$ of all nonempty coarse integer fibers. Suppose these fibers $Q_{\ell,j}\subset[-R,R]^m$ converge individually in Hausdorff distance to nonempty $Q_j$, and $M_*=\sum_{j\in P}|Q_j|_m>0$. Sample the first $r$ fiber coordinates on any full-rank cosets $a_\ell+L_\ell$, with measurable fundamental cells of $L_\ell$ contained in $[-\delta_\ell,\delta_\ell]^r$ and $\delta_\ell\to0$. Let $\mu_\ell$ be the sum of $s$-volumes at the sampled pairs $(j,\lambda)$, multiplied by the covolume of $L_\ell$, using counting for $s=0$. Put $S_*=\bigcup_{j\in P}(\{j\}\times Q_j)$ and let $\nu_*$ sum the full $m$-volumes on these fibers. All depths are normalized and use closed ambient halfspaces.

The fine mass is eventually positive. The supremum of fine depth over the actual sampled trace of $C_\ell$ converges to the maximum $\nu_*$ depth over $S_*$. Each positive-depth limiting mark can be recovered to arbitrary depth accuracy by fine marks at the same coarse base. There is a full-dimensional compact convex body with exactly the lifted fibers $S_*$ at all integer coarse bases, including the nonempty fibers of zero $m$-volume.

In particular this gives the fixed-body limit for $C_\ell=C$ and positive coarse mass. In that fixed-body setting, write $\Gamma_j=(j/(j+1))^j$ for $j\ge1$ and $\Gamma_0=1$. If the coarse depth is at least $2^{-k}\Gamma_m$, then sufficiently late fine traces have a point of depth at least $2^{-k-r}\Gamma_s$ in the strict cases $(r,s)\ne(1,0)$. The coarse premise holds for $k=0$ by ordinary centroid depth.

pk-intake-positive-density-two-facet-inc.relation_to_goal: Counterexample to raw facet restriction under physical normal-preserving boundary transport, with positive source density and complete actual fibers. No critical-cap stress assumption is used.
pk-intake-positive-density-two-facet-inc.statement:
For every $d\ge1$ there is a full-dimensional compact polytope with all its nonempty integer fibers of positive $d$-volume, and a measure $\nu$ with strictly positive density relative to its marked fiber boundary target $\eta$, such that a physical normal-preserving martingale $\nu\to\eta$ exists but the raw restrictions to two nonvertical supporting facets cannot transport to their full unweighted targets. In fact, for
$$
C=\{0\le z\le4,\ -1\le x_1\le\min(z,4-z),\ x'\in[0,1]^{d-1}\}
$$
one can take the two upper facets $F_L=\{x_1=z\}\cap C$ and $F_R=\{x_1=4-z\}\cap C$. Both have continuous normal $e_1$, $\eta(F)=3$, $\nu(F)=11/4$, and incoming mass $1/4$ supported on their common unit-area own-fiber facet at $z=2$.

pk-intake-positive-normal-triangle-cap-e.relation_to_goal: Ordinary planar cap area with nonnegative normalized normals, used as an auxiliary scalar bound in mixed-integer applications.
pk-intake-positive-normal-triangle-cap-e.statement:
Let $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2)\subset\mathbb R^2$ and $V=|T|$, where $|\cdot|$ denotes planar area. For $r>0$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$, the minimum of $|rT\cap\lbrace x:w\cdot x\ge t\rbrace|/V$ over $w_1,w_2\ge0$ with $w_1+w_2=1$ is
$$
P_r(t)=
\begin{cases}
r^2,& t\le0,\\
(r-t)^2,& 0\le t\le r/3,\\
4t(r-2t),& r/3\le t\le r/2,\\
0,& t\ge r/2 .
\end{cases}
$$
In particular, $P_r(t)\ge(4/9)r^2$ for $t\le r/3$, with equality at $t=r/3$.

pk-intake-positive-ordinary-lorentz-cap-.relation_to_goal: Ordinary planar cap and section data. The band width is existential and no mixed coarea weight conclusion is asserted.
pk-intake-positive-ordinary-lorentz-cap-.statement: There exists a universal $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that the following holds. Let $K$ be a planar convex body, let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$, and take three nonzero spanning normals $v_1+v_2+v_3=0$. For their closed through-$y$ caps write $Q_i=|K\cap\{v_i\cdot(x-y)\ge0\}|$, $k=|K|$, $q_i=Q_i/k$, and $\sigma_i=\mathcal H^1(K\cap\{v_i\cdot(x-y)=0\})/\lVert v_i\rVert$. With $M=\sum_iQ_i/\sigma_i$, set $f_i=2\sqrt{kQ_i}/(\sigma_i M)$ and $\Phi_i=f_i+(f_j+f_l)^2/4$ for distinct indices. If every $q_i\le4/9+\varepsilon_0$, then every $\Phi_i\le2$. For every nontriangular $K$ in this band every row is strict.

pk-intake-positive-parallel-cap-exclusio.relation_to_goal: An exclusion for the original equal-mass cap law once all original selected bases have the stated reserve. It leaves geometric rate support and aggregate payment open.
pk-intake-positive-parallel-cap-exclusio.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let a finite family of compact positive $d$-volume fibers $K_z$ be placed over bases $z\in P$ with summed fiber-volume measure $m$. Write $b(p)$ for the closed-halfspace depth of a base $p$ with weights $|K_z|$; in base rank zero set $b(p)=m(S)$. Let $e$ be a unit continuous covector and let an affine function $A$ have continuous gradient $ce$, $c>0$, and be nonnegative on the entire sampled family. Let a closed cap $H$ have raw mass $Q=m(H)$ and margin $(t/c)A+\ell(z)$ with $t>0$ and affine $\ell$. Suppose $A_{\rm sec}>0$ bounds the sum of maximal areas of sections of the individual $K_z$ perpendicular to $e$, using counting measure on zero-dimensional sections for $d=1$. If $b(p)\ge Q+g_0$ for all $p\in P_+$ and $g_0>0$, then
$$
\ell(z)\le -t g_0/A_{\rm sec}\qquad (z\in\operatorname{conv}P_+).
$$
Consequently the same cap misses every point over that hull with $A/c<g_0/A_{\rm sec}$, including its $A=0$ face.

pk-intake-positive-projective-chart-glob.relation_to_goal: One source chart with freely chosen base coefficient on a finite anchored hull. The cut conclusion uses a lattice-complete finite base and concerns the actual nested bodies and local inward speeds.
pk-intake-positive-projective-chart-glob.statement:
Let $d\ge1$. Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and nonempty, let each $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ for $z\in P$ be a convex body, and assume the sampled anchored Minkowski inclusions. Put $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$. Fix $p\in P$ and $y\in\operatorname{int}K_p$, and let $a_y$ be the optimal parameter for $E_{K_p}(y)=\min_a\int_{K_p}[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx$ over positive denominators. There exists a fixed base vector $b$ for which
$$
L(z,x)=1+a_y\cdot(x-y)+b\cdot(z-p),\qquad
\min_C L=\min_{x\in K_p}[1+a_y\cdot(x-y)]\ge\frac1{d+1}.
$$
For every threshold $0<\delta<1/(d+1)$, a tangent continuation of $t^{-d}$ below $\delta$ is inactive on a neighborhood of $C$ when evaluated at $L$.

If $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$, choose any continuous anchored support majorant $\ell(u,z)=h_{K_p}(u)+A_p(u)\cdot(z-p)\ge h_{K_z}(u)$ on $P$ for each unit $u$. Then the pure inverse-power cuts
$$
C_\varepsilon=C\cap\bigcap_{u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}}
\{(z,x):u\cdot x+\varepsilon h_{K_p-y}(u)L(z,x)^{-d}\le \ell(u,z)\}
$$
give a nested compact convex deformation for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon\ge0$, in $\operatorname{aff}(P)\times\mathbb R^d$, with projection $\operatorname{conv}(P)$ and positive integer fibers exactly at $P$. On the source fiber the cuts are exactly the prescribed single-source cuts with denominator $1+a_y\cdot(x-y)$. At a regular old boundary point $x\in\partial K_z$ with normal $\nu$, the inward first speed is $h_{K_p-y}(\nu)L(z,x)^{-d}$ if $\ell(\nu,z)=h_{K_z}(\nu)$, and zero otherwise.

pk-intake-positive-projective-tilt-finit.relation_to_goal: Obstructions to exact positive tilted-volume representation by uniform convex volume, either as a continuous marginal or at fixed integer labels.
pk-intake-positive-projective-tilt-finit.statement:
The pushforward of $dX/(1+X)$ on $[0,1]$ under $X\mapsto Y=X/(1+X)$ is the measure $(1-Y)^{-1}\,dY$ on $[0,1/2]$. It cannot be the $Y$-marginal, up to a common positive factor, of uniform Lebesgue volume on a compact convex body in $\mathbb R^{1+r}$ for any integer $r\ge1$.

Even requiring only preservation of total tilted masses at original integer labels can fail. Use the same volume-one convex fiber at $z=-1,0,1$ and $L(z)=1+z/2$, giving tilted masses $(2,1,2/3)$. No compact convex fibers $A_{-1},A_0,A_1\subset\mathbb R^r$ with $(A_{-1}+A_1)/2\subset A_0$, $1\le r<\infty$, have these three volumes up to a common positive factor. More generally, set $L(-1)=e$, $L(0)=1$, $L(1)=2-e$ with $0<e<1$, extended affinely, and $\nu_z=1/L(z)$. If such compatible fibers have $r$-volumes $W_z$ with $s\nu_z/D\le W_z\le sD\nu_z$ for some $s>0$ and $D\ge1$, then
$$
D\ge\left(\frac{e^{-1/r}+(2-e)^{-1/r}}2\right)^{r/2}\ge[e(2-e)]^{-1/4}.
$$
In particular no uniform two-sided factor works even with the lift dimension freely chosen.

pk-intake-positive-rate-radial-tail-and-.relation_to_goal: A whole-fiber positive-rate relation and spatial compensation for finite geometric cells. It concerns neither a cap-selected section law nor the mass at rate zero.
pk-intake-positive-rate-radial-tail-and-.statement:
Use the compact-rate finite geometric cell hypotheses of the positive-rate inverse slice theorem, and fix $o\in\operatorname{int}K$. Let $\widehat b$ be the restriction to $R>0$ of any simultaneous joint weak limit of
$(-\log L_j)_+\,dS_j\,\delta_{r_j}$ on boundary normal, physical position and rate, where $dS_j$ records the actual outward unit normal $n$. Let $\widehat\zeta_i$ be the positive-rate part of the geometric cell inverse limit. Put $h(n,X)=n\cdot(X-o)$ and $b_i=A_i(o)>0$. Then on the positive-rate range
$$
M\sum_i b_i\widehat\zeta_i(dX,dr)
=\left[\int_{R\ge r}\frac{h(n,X)}{R}\,\widehat b(dn,dX,dR)\right]\,dr.
$$
Every cell has no atom at any fixed positive rate. Extend its post-threshold conditional $\gamma_i$ by zero below $R_i$. The weighted total $M\sum_i b_i\gamma_i(r)$ has a decreasing version in measure order, and at every $R>0$ its one-sided limits give
$$
\sum_{R_i=R}b_i\gamma_i(R+)
\le\sum_{R_i<R}b_i\bigl(\gamma_i(R-)-\gamma_i(R+)\bigr)
$$
as spatial measures. For a single affine plane, the surface tail in brackets is decreasing and is $1/(d-1)$-concave on positive-mass compact sets for almost every $r>0$.

pk-intake-positive-right-index-knot-defi.relation_to_goal: Pointwise scalar diagonal-envelope estimate on admissible positive-right-index knots. Global maximization and geometric halfspace-depth applications are separate.
pk-intake-positive-right-index-knot-defi.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and $H,J$ be integers with $1\le J\le H\le(2d+1)J+d$. Put $t=1/(d+1)$ and $\Gamma=(dt)^d$. Define the double knot
$$
a=\frac{t(H+J+1)}{H(2J+1)},\qquad
\beta=\frac{t(H-J)}{dH(2J+1)}.
$$
Write $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$. For $h\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ put $r_h=(1-ah)_+$, $q_h=t-\beta h$, and $p_h=t+\beta(h+1)$. Define the finite diagonal-envelope deficit by
$$
D=\Gamma\sum_{h\ge0}r_h^d
-d^d\sum_{\substack{h\ge0\\r_h>0}}\left[q_h^{d-1}(r_h-dq_h)_++p_h^{d-1}(r_h-dp_h)_+\right].
$$
The thresholds in the second sum are positive, and $D/\Gamma\le-1/1080$.

pk-intake-positive-set-parity-center.relation_to_goal: Weighted closed depth on a finite complete affine-lattice base, under quotas local to the zero set. A pure-base center by itself gives no continuous-fiber depth bound.
pk-intake-positive-set-parity-center.statement: Let $\Lambda=c+L$ be an affine lattice and $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\Lambda$ be finite and nonempty. Assign each $z\in P$ a positive weight $V_z$, let $V(T)=\sum_{z\in T}V_z$, and put $M=V(P)$. Write $k(T)$ for the number of classes of $T$ modulo $2L$ and $k=k(P)$. Let $h:P\to[0,\infty)$ be nonzero and assume $h((z+z')/2)\ge(h(z)+h(z'))/2$ whenever the midpoint belongs to $P$. Suppose $V(T)\le k(T)M/k$ for every nonempty proper closed minor $T=P\cap\operatorname{conv}(T)$ contained in $\{h=0\}$. Then there is $p\in P$ with $h(p)>0$ such that every closed base halfspace containing $p$ has weight at least $M/k$. Allow the whole-base trace, which is the only containing trace in rank zero.

pk-intake-positive-simplex-row-full-cut-.relation_to_goal: Exact full-cut classification for the uniform-simplex capacity.
pk-intake-positive-simplex-row-full-cut-.statement: For $d\ge2$, let $U$ be uniform on $\Delta_d$ and $\phi_d(x)=\inf_{t>0:\Pr(x\cdot U\le t)>0}t/\Pr(x\cdot U\le t)^{1/d}$. For a strictly positive row $x$, the full threshold $m=\max_jx_j$ minimizes the ratio exactly when $x=m\mathbf 1$ or $x$ is a permutation of $(a,m,\ldots,m)$ with $0<a<m$ and $d$ entries equal to $m$. In these cases the capacity is $m$ and the minimizing threshold is unique.

pk-intake-positive-simplex-row-unique-ca.relation_to_goal: Threshold attainment, uniqueness and envelope derivative for a uniform-simplex row.
pk-intake-positive-simplex-row-unique-ca.statement: Let $d\ge2$, let $U$ be uniform on $\Delta_d$, and put $F_x(t)=\Pr(x\cdot U\le t)$ and $\phi_d(x)=\inf_{t>0:F_x(t)>0}t/F_x(t)^{1/d}$. For every nonconstant $x\in(0,\infty)^{d+1}$ there is a unique minimizing threshold in $(\min_j x_j,\max_j x_j]$. If the minimizing threshold $t$ is proper, meaning $t<\max_j x_j$, it depends continuously on the row near $x$, the capacity is locally $C^1$, and $\nabla\phi_d(x)=F_x(t)^{-1/d}b$ for the actual barycentric centroid $b$ of the section $x\cdot u=t$.

pk-intake-positive-volume-recipients-in-.relation_to_goal: Transfers the surface integral on a fixed empty-side face to traces on that same face. For the oriented circuit it can use a separate covering family. There is no mixed-mass budget estimate.
pk-intake-positive-volume-recipients-in-.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior. Suppose finitely many closed halfspaces $H_1,\dots,H_N$ cover $K$ up to a Lebesgue-null set. Write $J_+=\{j:|K\cap H_j|_d>0\}$. Then $K\subset\bigcup_{j\in J_+}H_j$. The same holds if some $H_j$ are the whole space or the empty set.

In particular, if $|K\cap H_i|_d=0$ and $F_i=K\cap\partial H_i$ is a supporting face, then for every nonnegative $\mathcal H^{d-1}$-measurable $w$ on $F_i$,
$$
\int_{F_i}w\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}
\le\sum_{j\in J_+}\int_{F_i\cap H_j}w\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}.
$$
For $d=1$ use counting measure. This applies separately on every positive fiber of a finite closed ambient mixed cover.

pk-intake-positive-volume-to-intrinsic-m.relation_to_goal: Conditional transfer preserving the numerical constant with the original n,d. Substituting the sharper product constant is conditional on its full-volume premise.
pk-intake-positive-volume-to-intrinsic-m.statement: Fix $n,d\ge1$ and $c\in[0,1]$. Assume that every convex body $D\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ whose integer trace has positive mixed $d$-volume has a point of normalized closed-halfspace depth at least $c$ for that mixed volume. Let $C$ be any convex body with nonempty integer trace $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$ and let $q=\dim_{\mathrm H}S$. Then $S$ has a point of closed-halfspace depth at least $c$ for the normalized intrinsic measure $\mathcal H^q|_S/\mathcal H^q(S)$, including $q=0$. The case $n=0$ already has $q=d$ for a convex body, and when $d=0$ the measure is counting measure throughout.

pk-intake-prescribed-mixed-barycentric-c.relation_to_goal: Compact fixed-marginal convex-order repair with one physical output ceiling. Product base integrality and any actual face geometry are hypotheses for the corresponding applications.
pk-intake-prescribed-mixed-barycentric-c.statement:
Let $n,d\ge0$ be integers with $n+d\ge1$, and let $P_i\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite for $1\le i\le k$, $k\ge1$. For a finite base set $Q$ put $\sigma_Q=\sum_{q\in Q}\delta_q\otimes\mathcal L^d$, with $\mathcal L^0$ the unit measure on the single point $\mathbb R^0$. Let $\gamma_i$ be compactly supported finite nonnegative Borel measures on $P_i\times\mathbb R^d$, with common mass $M$ and $\gamma_i\le a_i\sigma_{P_i}$ for $0<a_i<\infty$. Let $\lambda_i>0$ sum to one, put $P=\sum_i\lambda_iP_i$, and use the full physical barycentric map $b(x_1,\ldots,x_k)=\sum_i\lambda_i x_i$. For every prescribed coupling $\pi_0$ of the $\gamma_i$ there is one coupling $\pi$ of exactly those marginals such that
$$
 b_\#\pi_0\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}} b_\#\pi,\qquad
 b_\#\pi\le A_d\,\sigma_P,\qquad
 A_d=\begin{cases}
  \bigl(\sum_i\lambda_i a_i^{-1/d}\bigr)^{-d},&d\ge1,\\
  \min_i a_i,&d=0.
 \end{cases}
$$
Here convex order requires equal mass and compares integrals of every finite convex function on $\mathbb R^{n+d}$. The barycentric first moment is fixed by the prescribed marginals. Moreover, every optimizer of $\int\phi(b(x))\,d\pi(x)$ over the same couplings satisfies the displayed ceiling if $\phi$ is smooth with $D^2\phi\ge\varepsilon I$ everywhere for some $\varepsilon>0$. When $n=0$, the optimizer ceiling already holds for $\phi\in C^2$ with the same Hessian lower bound. The constant is sharp uniformly over the indicated data of positive common mass and supports.

If all the input measures are supported in one compact convex set $C$, the new law is carried by $C\cap(P\times\mathbb R^d)$. Thus, when $P\subseteq\mathbb Z^n$, it is carried by the actual mixed-integer fibers and obeys the same ceiling there. Equal weights $1/k$ and $P_i\subseteq r+k\mathbb Z^n$ for all $i$, for some $r\in\mathbb Z^n$, suffice for this integrality assumption.

In the single-input-base-per-slot case there is also an intrinsic face version. Let $K_{z_i}$ and $K_p$ be compact convex fibers in a common Euclidean space, where $p=\sum_i\lambda_i z_i$ is a sampled integer base. Suppose $\sum_i\lambda_iK_{z_i}\subseteq K_p$ and $h_{K_p}(u)=\sum_i\lambda_i h_{K_{z_i}}(u)$ for a unit normal $u$. Suppose each endpoint exposed face spans an affine space of dimension $m\ge1$ and these spaces have a common tangent space. For equal-mass endpoint laws $\gamma_i$ on these faces bounded by $a_i$ times their Euclidean $m$-area, one can dominate any prescribed old barycentric law in full physical convex order while bounding the new law by $A_m$ times Euclidean $m$-area of the weighted affine plane, on which its support is contained in the actual exposed face of $K_p$. If the latter face has dimension $m$, this is a ceiling relative to its face area. If the prescribed physical branches are $\alpha_i$ of masses $\lambda_i M$ and unit $m$-area ceilings, applying this assertion to $\gamma_i=\alpha_i/\lambda_i$ gives $A_m=(\sum_i\lambda_i^{1+1/m})^{-m}$ for the mass-$M$ barycentric law.

pk-intake-prescribed-regular-product-int.relation_to_goal: Boundary response efficiency for a prescribed regular circuit in a common-fiber product interval with another deepest base, and the singleton case.
pk-intake-prescribed-regular-product-int.statement:
Let $P=\{m,m+1,\ldots,M\}\subset\mathbb Z$ be nonempty and let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body of volume $V>0$ and centroid $g$, with $d\ge1$. Assume $K$ has a finite volume-preserving affine symmetry group whose average orbit is $g$, as for a simplex. Use the sum of fiber volumes on $P\times K$ and let $Q$ be the maximum raw closed-halfspace depth on that set.

Fix an actual deepest point $(p,y)$ and a prescribed finite list of caps $H_j=\{a_j(z-p)+u_j\cdot(x-y)\ge0\}$ of mass $Q$, with $u_j\ne0$ and positive $\rho_j$ satisfying $\sum_j\rho_ju_j=0$. For each cap assume differentiability in the full hyperplane parameters with the usual mixed coarea derivative. If there is a deepest point at a different base, or if $P$ is a singleton, there is one exposed endpoint $e$ and one continuous nonnegative potential $\Phi(n,z,x)$, convex in $(z,x)$ for each fixed unit $n$, supported on the actual boundary bundle over $e$. With $\eta$ the sum of boundary $\mathcal H^{d-1}$ lifted by the outward continuous unit normal, its integral is $dV$ and
$\int\Phi\sum_j\theta_j\mathbf 1_{H_j}\,d\eta\ge dV(d/(d+1))^d$ for every $\theta_j\ge0$ with $\sum_j\theta_j=1$. In particular the conclusion holds if the deepest bases meet every parity class occupied by $P$.

More generally, in any finite base dimension with a common fiber, the same localization conclusion holds for any finite list of nonvertical caps through $(p,g)$ if an exposed base $e$ satisfies $a_j\cdot(e-p)\ge0$ for every row. In that implication the list need not be critical or balanced.

pk-intake-prescribed-sector-sparse-slack.relation_to_goal: Ordinary reconstruction of the same finite ray and sector data with at least one core. This does not impose any containment of fixed neighboring-fiber averages.
pk-intake-prescribed-sector-sparse-slack.statement:
Let $m\ge3$ and take nonzero ray endpoints $P_i$ on distinct counterclockwise rays whose consecutive gaps are less than $\pi$. Indices are cyclic. Put $D_i=\det(P_i,P_{i+1})$, $E_i=\det(P_{i-1},P_{i+1})$. Suppose the finite sector areas $W_i$ and these endpoints are realized by an ordinary convex body with $0$ interior. Define $h_i=1/D_i-1/(2W_i)$, $b_i=(D_{i-1}+D_i-E_i)/(D_{i-1}D_i)$ and
$$
x^\top Lx=\sum_i b_i x_i^2-\sum_i h_i(x_i+x_{i+1})^2.
$$
If some $h_i=0$, let $s$ count the singular connected components of the graph joining $i$ to $i+1$ when $h_i>0$, where singularity refers to the corresponding block of $L$. The same ray endpoints and all the same sector areas admit a convex polygonal realization with $0$ interior and exactly $\operatorname{rank} L=m-s$ vertices. There is one strict vertex in each sector with $h_i>0$ and one strict ray vertex in each positive-definite component. The ray vertex may be chosen arbitrarily in its component.

pk-intake-present-corner-shifted-tail-ch.relation_to_goal: A planar endpoint section inequality for one proper cut and an actually present corner.
pk-intake-present-corner-shifted-tail-ch.statement:
Let $A,B$ be planar convex bodies, let $v_1,v_2,v_3$ be nonzero spanning normals with $\sum_i v_i=0$, and fix $y\in\mathbb R^2$. Use planar area $|\cdot|$. Set $h_i=h_B(v_i)-v_i\cdot y$, where $h_B(v)=\max_{x\in B}v\cdot x$, and put $W=\sum_i h_i$, $H_i^A=\{x:v_i\cdot(x-y)\ge-h_i\}$, $U_i=|A\cap H_i^A|$, and $a=|A|$.

Fix an index $i$ whose $A$ cut is proper, meaning that its cutting line meets $\operatorname{int}A$. Suppose the residual corner $R_i=A\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{x:v_j\cdot(x-y)<-h_j\}$ is nonempty. Define $T_i=|A\cap\{x:v_i\cdot(x-y)\ge W-h_i\}|$ and $\delta_i=(a-U_j-U_k)_+$ for the other indices $j,k$, where $(s)_+=\max(0,s)$. Write $\sigma_{A,i}=\mathcal H^1(A\cap\{x:v_i\cdot(x-y)=-h_i\})/\lVert v_i\rVert$. Then $W>0$, $0<T_i<U_i$, $T_i\ge\delta_i$, and
$$
\sigma_{A,i}\le \frac{2}{W}\bigl(U_i-\sqrt{U_iT_i}\bigr)
\le \frac{2}{W}\bigl(U_i-\sqrt{U_i\delta_i}\bigr),\qquad
\sigma_{A,i}<\frac{2U_i}{W}.
$$

pk-intake-primitive-extrusion-exact-roof.relation_to_goal: An exact mixed-measure law for extrusion and its quotient coefficient, without a depth credit for an individual added term.
pk-intake-primitive-extrusion-exact-roof.statement:
Let $n\ge1,d\ge0$, let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex, and take primitive $v\in\mathbb Z^n$. Choose unimodular coordinates $(t,w,x)$ with $v=e_t$, and let $T=\pi_v C$ in the quotient lattice $\mathbb Z^n/\mathbb Zv$. Write $\nu$ for quotient mixed measure restricted to $T$. At $(w,x)\in T$ let $[a(w,x),b(w,x)]$ be the actual closed line section. For every integer $k\ge0$, the measure of $C_k=C+[0,k](v,0)$ is
$$
\mu|_{C_k}=\mu|_C+\sum_{r=1}^k(R_r)_\#\nu,\qquad R_r(w,x)=(\lfloor b(w,x)\rfloor+r,w,x).
$$
Thus $\mu(C_k)=\mu(C)+k\mu_{n-1,d}(T)$. For a closed halfspace with margin $\alpha t+\ell(w,x)-\beta$, its mass increment is the sum of $\int_T\mathbf1_{\{\alpha(\lfloor b\rfloor+r)+\ell\ge\beta\}}\,d\nu$ over $r$. For $\alpha=0$ this is $k$ times the corresponding quotient cap mass. An integer generator $cv$ with $c\ge1$ gives total mass increment $kc\mu_{n-1,d}(T)$, using either orientation of the primitive line.

For each integer quotient base $w$, let $Q_w=\{(t,x):(t,w,x)\in C\}$ and $T_w=\pi_xQ_w$. For every real $s\ge0$,
$$
|Q_w+[0,s]e_t|_{d+1}=|Q_w|_{d+1}+s|T_w|_d.
$$
The continuous extrusion coefficients sum to $\mu_{n-1,d}(T)$ when the $t$ length is lattice-normalized. The statements include initially unsampled or degenerate sections, empty sets and zero-dimensional quotient measures.

pk-intake-primitive-extrusion-full-level.relation_to_goal: The marked quotient point is fixed across all levels and cap normals. The tail budget uses actual raw depths.
pk-intake-primitive-extrusion-full-level.statement:
Let $C$ be nonempty compact convex in primitive unimodular coordinates $(t,w,x)$, let $T=\pi_t C$, and use the actual mixed measures in each ambient space. Suppose $T$ has positive quotient mass. Put $a_0=\min_C t$, $b_0=\max_C t$. For any integer $k\ge\lceil b_0\rceil-\lfloor a_0\rfloor$, set $l=\lceil b_0\rceil$, $r=k+\lfloor a_0\rfloor$, $N=r-l+1$. The integer levels of $C+[0,k]e_t$ consist of full copies of $T$ for $l\le t\le r$, left tails $T^-_s=\pi_t(C\cap\{t\le s\})$ at $t=s$ for $\lceil a_0\rceil\le s<l$, and right tails $T^+_s=\pi_t(C\cap\{t\ge s\})$ at $t=k+s$ for $\lfloor a_0\rfloor<s\le\lfloor b_0\rfloor$.

For an actual quotient mark $y$, let $Q=D_T(y)$, $L=\sum_sD_{T^-_s}(y)$, $R=\sum_sD_{T^+_s}(y)$, where $D$ is raw closed-halfspace depth, zero off the convex set and equal to mass in a zero-dimensional quotient. For every integer $l\le j\le r$,
$$
D_{C+[0,k]e_t}(j,y)\ge \min\{(j-l+1)Q+L,(r-j+1)Q+R\}.
$$
When $Q>0$, the maximum of the right-hand side over these levels is
$$
\frac{(N+1)Q+L+R}{2}-Q\operatorname{dist}\!\left(\frac{N-1}{2}+\frac{R-L}{2Q},\{0,\ldots,N-1\}\right).
$$
If $|R-L|\le(N-1)Q$ this is at least $(NQ+L+R)/2$. Positive tail mass alone need not give positive credit at the deepest quotient mark.

pk-intake-primitive-three-site-chain-bel.relation_to_goal: The assertion applies to any below-parity-threshold compatible family, before attainment. It gives the actual middle fiber inclusion without any bound on the mass in other fibers.
pk-intake-primitive-three-site-chain-bel.statement: Let $U$ be a nonempty finite complete subset of an affine lattice with direction lattice $L$, with $k(U)$ occupied classes modulo $2L$. Let positive compact convex $d$-fibers $K_u$, $d\ge1$, form a compatible family on $U$, with total mass $M>0$ and normalized maximum closed-halfspace depth strictly below $\gamma_d/k(U)$, where $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Then $|K_u|_d<M/k(U)$ for every $u$, so $|U|>k(U)$. In any Euclidean norm, a shortest distinct same-parity pair has the form $p,p+2v$ with $v$ primitive in $L$. Its midpoint $p+v$ belongs to $U$, has different parity, and has fiber containing $(K_p+K_{p+2v})/2$.

pk-intake-probability-complement-product.statement:

R_m(t)=\frac{\prod_i(1-t_i)}{2\sum_{i<j}t_it_j}

off the vertices of the probability simplex and $R_m=1/2$ at its vertices. Then $R_m$ is continuous and $((m-1)/m)^{m-1}\le R_m(t)\le1/2$. For $m=2$ it is identically $1/2$; for $m>2$ the lower equality holds only at the uniform vector.

pk-intake-probability-simplex-capacity-o.relation_to_goal: Counterexample to a probability-only replacement for the uniform-simplex capacity problem.
pk-intake-probability-simplex-capacity-o.statement:
For $d\ge1$ and $m=d+1$, let $D_d$ consist of all $v\in\mathbb R_+^m$ for which there exists a nonnegative zero-diagonal column-stochastic $m\times m$ matrix $Y$ satisfying $v_i\le \operatorname{GM}_d((Y_{ij})_{j\ne i})$ for every $i$, where $\operatorname{GM}_d$ is the geometric mean of $d$ entries. But $a\notin D_2$, with $\sum_i a_i^2+2a_1a_2a_3-1=33583/20346417>0$. The polynomial test at $p=(200/273,1,1)$ has value $-142/74529$.

pk-intake-projected-contact-normal-condi.relation_to_goal: Conditions projected cover normals at the exterior threshold in projection rank r.
pk-intake-projected-contact-normal-condi.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^D$ be a convex body, let $\mu$ be uniform probability on $K$, and let $\pi:\mathbb R^D\to\mathbb R^r$ be a surjective linear map with $1\le r\le D$. Put $\nu=\pi_\#\mu$ and $B=\pi K$. Write $\gamma_0=1$ and $\gamma_j=(j/(j+1))^j$ for $j\ge1$. Suppose finitely many closed halfspaces $H_i=\{x:\ell_i(x-c)\ge0\}$ cover $\mathbb R^r$, each $\ell_i$ has width one on $B$, and $\nu(H_i)\le\tau<\gamma_{r-1}$ for every $i$. Then $c\in\operatorname{int}B$ and
$$
\max_i\ell_i(v)\ge\frac{\gamma_{r-1}-\tau}{D}\qquad(v\in\partial(B-B)).
$$
Equivalently, the convex hull of the $\ell_i$ contains $(\gamma_{r-1}-\tau)(B-B)^\circ/D$, where $(B-B)^\circ$ is the polar in the dual space. In particular, the $\ell_i$ span the dual space.

pk-intake-projected-deepest-point-slab.relation_to_goal: Controls the scalar law at any deepest point of the exact projected marginal.
pk-intake-projected-deepest-point-slab.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^D$ be a convex body, let $\mu$ be uniform probability on $K$, and let $\pi:\mathbb R^D\to\mathbb R^r$ be a surjective linear map with $1\le r\le D$. Put $\nu=\pi_\#\mu$ and $B=\pi K$. Let $\alpha$ be the maximum closed-halfspace depth for $\nu$ and let $\mathcal A$ be its set of maximizers. The set $\mathcal A$ is nonempty and compact in $\operatorname{int}B$. Let $\ell$ have width one on $B$ and let $p$ be the scalar section-volume density of $\ell_\#\nu$, extended by zero off its support. Then $0\le p\le D$. For each $c_*\in\mathcal A$, put $t_*=\ell(c_*)$ and $L=t_*-\min_B\ell$. Then $p(t_*)\ge\alpha$ and
$$
\nu\{x:t_*-a\le\ell(x)\le t_*\}\ge\alpha a/D\qquad (0\le a\le L).
$$
In particular, if $c\in B$ and $\ell(c_*-c)\ge0$, the cap $\{x:\ell(x-c)\ge0\}$ has mass at least $\alpha+(\alpha/D)\ell(c_*-c)$.

pk-intake-projected-deepest-set-localiza.relation_to_goal: Controls localization to every deepest point of the exact projected marginal in the difference-body gauge.
pk-intake-projected-deepest-set-localiza.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^D$ be a convex body, let $\mu$ be uniform probability on $K$, and let $\pi:\mathbb R^D\to\mathbb R^r$ be a surjective linear map with $1\le r\le D$. Put $\nu=\pi_\#\mu$ and $B=\pi K$. Let $\alpha$ be the maximum closed-halfspace depth for $\nu$ and let $\mathcal A$ be its set of maximizers. Write $\gamma_0=1$ and $\gamma_j=(j/(j+1))^j$ for $j\ge1$. Suppose finitely many closed halfspaces $H_i=\{x:\ell_i(x-c)\ge0\}$ cover $\mathbb R^r$, each $\ell_i$ has width one on $B$, and $\nu(H_i)\le\tau<\gamma_{r-1}$ for every $i$. Then $c\in\operatorname{int}B$, $\gamma_r\le\alpha\le\tau$, and for every $c_*\in\mathcal A$ the gauge of the difference body satisfies
$$
\lVert c-c_*\rVert_{B-B}
\le\min\left\{1,\frac{D^2(\tau-\alpha)}{\alpha(\gamma_{r-1}-\tau)}\right\}
\le\min\left\{1,\frac{D^2(\tau-\gamma_r)}{\gamma_r(\gamma_{r-1}-\tau)}\right\}.
$$
If $\tau=\alpha$ then $\mathcal A=\{c\}$. If $\tau=\gamma_r$ then additionally $\alpha=\gamma_r$.

pk-intake-projected-stationary-sections-.relation_to_goal: Ordinary continuous inequality for actual central sections whose normals lie in one plane. The claim requires their projected centroids and the specified area-weighted balance.
pk-intake-projected-stationary-sections-.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with volume $V>0$, and let $E$ be a two-dimensional linear subspace. Suppose $0$ lies in the interior of the orthogonal projection of $K$ onto $E$. Let $u_i\in E$ be a finite list of unit normals and set
$$
S_i=\mathcal H^{d-1}(K\cap u_i^\perp),\qquad
p_i=\frac{|K\cap\{x:u_i\cdot x\ge0\}|}{V}.
$$
Suppose the centroid of each section $K\cap u_i^\perp$ has orthogonal projection $0$ onto $E$. If $\theta_i\ge0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$, and $\sum_i\theta_i S_i u_i=0$, then
$$
\sum_i\theta_i p_i\ge c_d,\qquad
c_2=\frac49,\qquad
c_d=\frac1{1+\max\{4/3,\sqrt{2(d-1)/d}\}}\quad(d\ge3).
$$
For $3\le d\le9$ this is $3/7$. For $d\ge10$ it is strictly greater than $2/5$. In particular $c_d>(d/(d+1))^d$ for $d\ge3$.

Consequently, in any dimension $d\ge1$, if $0\in\operatorname{int}K$, each central section has full centroid $0$, and the positive-weight normals span a space of dimension at most two, then the same weighted mean is at least $(d/(d+1))^d$. In rank one the mean is exactly $1/2$, even without section centering.

pk-intake-projection-coefficient-rounded.relation_to_goal: A sufficient sharp-depth regime in terms of actual projection coefficients. The proof uses ordinary full dimension and positive ambient-fiber mixed mass.
pk-intake-projection-coefficient-rounded.statement:
Let $n\ge1,d\ge0,D=n+d$ and let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body. Work in fixed unimodular integer-base coordinates and use the actual projected mixed volumes $A_I(C)=\mu_{n-|I|,d}(\pi_I C)$. Put $M=\mu_{n,d}(C)>0$, $V=\operatorname{vol}_D(C)$, $E=\sum_{I\ne\varnothing} A_I(C)$, $V_i=\operatorname{vol}_{D-1}(\pi_{\{i\}}C)$, and $\Gamma_j=(j/(j+1))^j$ for $j\ge1$, $\Gamma_0=1$.

For the ordinary centroid $c$ and any real displacement $y=c+(\delta,0)$, every containing closed halfspace $H$ has ordinary cap volume at least $\Gamma_DV-\sum_i|\delta_i|V_i$, and $V_i\le\sum_{I\ni i}A_I(C)$. In particular, round the integer coordinates of $c$ independently to nearest integers with deterministic ties, leaving the other coordinates fixed. At the resulting $y$ every containing closed halfspace has raw mixed mass at least
$$
\Gamma_DV-E-\sum_i|\delta_i|V_i\ \ge\
B_\delta:=\Gamma_D M-\sum_{I\ne\varnothing}
(\Gamma_D+1+\sum_{i\in I}|\delta_i|)A_I(C).
$$
If $B_\delta>0$, this $y$ belongs to the actual mixed set $S$ and to its convex hull. Let $B$ be the same expression with $\sum_{i\in I}|\delta_i|$ replaced by $|I|/2$. If $B\ge2^{-n}\Gamma_d M$, the rounded point attains at least $2^{-n}\Gamma_d$ normalized depth. In all cases the maximum normalized depth on $S$ is at least
$$
\max\{\Gamma_d W/M,\ \max(0,B)/M\},
\qquad W=\max_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z).
$$

pk-intake-projection-extreme-nonfacet-st.statement: Consider a finite compatible family of positive-volume $d$-polytopes, $d\ge2$, at fixed bases. pk-intake-projective-all-active-optimize.relation_to_goal: A local necessary condition in the free projective chart orbit of a fixed sampled family. Cap circuits and smooth fixed-normal profiles are explicit. The image generally has different real labels and the theorem does not claim preservation of the integer lattice.
pk-intake-projective-all-active-optimize.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and let $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, be compact convex bodies of positive volume. Write $\mu$ for the sum of their labeled fiber volumes, $M=\int d\mu$, and $\beta$ for the maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth on the sampled fibers. Assume this maximum is locally minimized at $L=1$ when the measure on the same sampled family is reweighted by $L(p)^{-d}$ for positive affine $L$ near $1$. Equivalently one can use ordinary fiber volumes of the image family $(p,x)\mapsto(p/L(p),x/L(p))$.

Select finitely many circuits indexed by $i$, at least one at each deepest base. In each circuit the caps
$$
H_{ij}=\{a_{ij}\cdot p+u_{ij}\cdot x\ge b_{ij}\},\qquad \|u_{ij}\|_2=1,
$$
have mass $\beta M$, pass through the same interior deepest mark $(p_i,x_i)$, and have weights $\rho_{ij}>0$ with $\sum_j\rho_{ij}=1$, $\sum_j\rho_{ij}u_{ij}=0$. At every other base assume there is a fixed finite cover of the entire fiber plane by caps of mass strictly below $\beta M$. Define $\delta_{ip}=p-p_i$, $T_{ijp}=b_{ij}-a_{ij}\cdot p$, and $F_{ijp}(s)=|K_p\cap\{u_{ij}\cdot x\ge s\}|$. Assume $F_{ijp}$ is $C^2$ near $T_{ijp}$ for all $i,j,p$. At that threshold set
$$
S_{ijp}=-F'_{ijp},\quad R_{ijp}=-F''_{ijp},\quad S_{ij}=\sum_p S_{ijp}>0,\qquad
\kappa_{ij}=\frac{\rho_{ij}/S_{ij}}{\sum_l \rho_{il}/S_{il}}.
$$
Put $H^*_{ij}=-\sum_p R_{ijp}\delta_{ip}\delta_{ip}^{\mathsf T}$, $V_{ij}=\sum_p S_{ijp}\delta_{ip}\delta_{ip}^{\mathsf T}$, $h_{ij}=\sum_p R_{ijp}\delta_{ip}$, and $k_{ij}=-\sum_p R_{ijp}$. Use matrices on $\operatorname{span}(P-P)$. Then $H^*_{ij}\succeq0$. For an affine direction $A$ with linear part $b$, define
$$
B_{ij}(A)=-d\int_{H_{ij}}A\,d\mu,\quad t_i(A)=\sum_j\kappa_{ij}B_{ij}(A),\quad
g_i(A)=t_i(A)+d\beta\int A\,d\mu,
$$
and put $v_{ij}=(B_{ij}(A)-t_i(A))/S_{ij}$, $w_{ij}=dV_{ij}b-v_{ij}h_{ij}$. The first-order condition is $\max_i g_i(A)\ge0$ for every affine $A$.

Fix any $A$ with $\max_i g_i(A)=0$. Let $I_0(A)=\{i:g_i(A)=0\}$ and $J(A)=\{i\in I_0(A): w_{ij}\in\operatorname{ran}H^*_{ij}\text{ for all }j\}$. For $i\in J(A)$ set
$$
n_i(A)=d(d+1)\left[\sum_j\kappa_{ij}\int_{H_{ij}}A^2\,d\mu-\beta\int A^2\,d\mu\right]
 +\sum_j\kappa_{ij}\left[k_{ij}v_{ij}^2-w_{ij}^{\mathsf T}(H^*_{ij})^\dagger w_{ij}\right].
$$
Here the dagger denotes the inverse on the range and zero on the kernel. Then $J(A)$ is nonempty and there are weights $\pi_i\ge0$ on $J(A)$ with
$$
\sum_i\pi_i=1,\qquad \sum_i\pi_i g_i=0\text{ as an affine-direction functional},\qquad
\sum_i\pi_i n_i(A)\ge0.
$$
Moreover, if $W$ is a linear space of affine directions on which every $g_i$ vanishes, let $E(W)$ be the groups $i$ for which $A\mapsto w_{ij}(A)$ belongs to $\operatorname{ran}H^*_{ij}$ for every $A\in W$ and every $j$. Then $0\in\operatorname{conv}\{g_i:i\in E(W)\}$.

pk-intake-projective-contact-weight-same.relation_to_goal: The obstruction concerns exact uniform volume representation at the same labels for the specified projectively weighted contact measures. The original product and the ordinary projective image are actual convex sets, and the example gives no assertion about their deepest marks.
pk-intake-projective-contact-weight-same.statement: There is a compact convex product with original lattice bases $-1,0,1$, a single common exposed contact plane, and a positive affine projective denominator $L$, whose weighted contact masses $\int_{F_z}H(z)L(z,\xi)^{-2}\,d\xi$ cannot be the uniform volumes of any compact convex family in any finite positive continuous dimension at the same labels, even after a common positive rescaling. Explicitly, take $C=[-1,1]_z\times[0,1]_s\times[-2,0]_t$, contact plane $t=0$, the affine apex graph $y_z=(1/2,-1)$, so $H=1$, and $L=1+z/2$. The masses are $4,1,4/9$ at the three labels. Its ordinary projective image has bases $-2,0,2/3$, face lengths $2,1,2/3$ and perpendicular apex heights $2,1,2/3$.

pk-intake-projective-energy-attainment-e.relation_to_goal: Ordinary full-dimensional compact convex bodies at interior marks. The escort is an ordinary Lebesgue density and the projective volume is computed in the continuous coordinates.
pk-intake-projective-energy-attainment-e.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior, and let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. For $a\in\mathbb R^d$ put $L_a(x)=1+a\cdot(x-y)$ and define
$$
E_K(y)=\inf_{\{a:L_a>0\ \text{on }K\}}\int_K L_a(x)^{-d-1}\,dx.
$$
The infimum is positive and attained at a unique admissible $a_*$, and $E_K(y)$ is the minimum $d$-volume of the images of $K-y$ under $w\mapsto w/(1+a\cdot w)$ over these $a$. For $L=L_{a_*}$ and $E=E_K(y)$,
$$
\int_K (x-y)L(x)^{-d-2}\,dx=0,\qquad
\int_K L(x)^{-d-2}\,dx=\int_K L(x)^{-d-1}\,dx=E.
$$
Thus $\rho=L^{-d-2}/E$ on $K$ is a probability density with barycenter $y$ and $\int_K L\rho\,dx=1$. Its restriction to $K$ extends to a smooth positive function on a neighborhood of $K$.

For every invertible linear $Q$ and every $b\in\mathbb R^d$, $E_{QK+b}(Qy+b)=|\det Q|E_K(y)$. If $K\subset H$ for another convex body $H$, then $E_K(y)\le E_H(y)$ with equality exactly when $K=H$. Writing $g_K=|K|^{-1}\int_K x\,dx$ for the ordinary centroid, $E_K(y)\le |K|$ with equality exactly when $y=g_K$.

pk-intake-projective-energy-envelope-den.relation_to_goal: A single full-dimensional ordinary body and a fiber-interior mark. The floor holds for the optimizing affine denominator.
pk-intake-projective-energy-envelope-den.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, and let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. Define $E_K(y)=\min_a\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx$ over $a$ for which the denominator is positive on $K$, and let $a_y$ be its unique minimizer. The maps $y\mapsto a_y$ and $y\mapsto E_K(y)$ are smooth on $\operatorname{int}K$ and
$$
\nabla_y E_K(y)=(d+1)E_K(y)a_y,\qquad
\nabla_y E_K(y)^{1/d}=\frac{d+1}{d}E_K(y)^{1/d}a_y.
$$
The optimal denominator $1+a_y\cdot(x-y)$ is at least $1/(d+1)$ on $K$ and strictly greater than $1/(d+1)$ on $\operatorname{int}K$.

pk-intake-projective-energy-ordinary-ent.relation_to_goal: Ordinary Lebesgue densities on a convex body with a fixed interior barycenter. The feasible class has no pointwise density cap.
pk-intake-projective-energy-ordinary-ent.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, and let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. Put $p=(d+1)/(d+2)$ and let $E_K(y)$ be the minimum of $\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx$ over affine denominators strictly positive on $K$. Then
$$
E_K(y)=\max_{\substack{\rho\ge0,\ \int_K\rho\,dx=1\\\int_K x\rho(x)\,dx=y}}
\left(\int_K\rho(x)^p\,dx\right)^{d+2}.
$$
The maximum is over ordinary Lebesgue densities on $K$ with the displayed mass and mean. Its unique maximizer up to Lebesgue null sets is $\rho=L^{-d-2}/E_K(y)$, where $L(x)=1+a_*\cdot(x-y)$ is the attained optimal denominator.

pk-intake-projective-whole-row-chart-cov.relation_to_goal: An exact calculation for conditional volume rows. It supplies neither boundary response weights nor a depth payment.
pk-intake-projective-whole-row-chart-cov.statement:
Let $C$ be a compact convex subset of a finite-dimensional Euclidean affine space, and let $L:C\to(0,\infty)$ be continuous. Let $\nu_i$ be finitely many positive measures on $C$ of masses $m_i>0$ and barycenters $Y_i$. In one group of these rows, suppose $B$ is affine, $B(Y_i)=L(Y_i)$ and $B=L$ almost everywhere for each grouped $\nu_i$. Let $W$ be positive affine on $C$ with $W(Y_i)=L(Y_i)$ at all grouped marks. Define $\eta=L\sum_i\nu_i$, $\widehat\eta=W\sum_i\nu_i$, $g=W/L$ and $s=\sum_i m_iL(Y_i)$, where all sums run over the group. With $\operatorname{Cov}_i$ the covariance of the probability $\nu_i/m_i$ about $Y_i$ in the full affine space and $b=\nabla(W-B)$, one has
$$
\eta(C)=\widehat\eta(C)=s,\qquad
\int w\,d(\widehat\eta-\eta)(w)=\sum_i m_i\operatorname{Cov}_i b.
$$
If $s>0$, the finite equal-mass entropies are
$$
D(\eta\|\widehat\eta)=-\int\log g\,d\eta\ge0,\qquad
D(\widehat\eta\|\eta)=\int g\log g\,d\eta\ge0.
$$
Each equality holds exactly when $W=L$ almost everywhere for $\eta$. For an empty group all measures and integrals are zero.

pk-intake-propagated-erosion-prescribed-.relation_to_goal: Prescribed boundary credits of an actual compatible erosion; the relative credit against propagated cost and the resulting depth payment are separate questions.
pk-intake-propagated-erosion-prescribed-.statement:
Under the hypotheses of finite-base-upward-max-support-erosion, fix finitely many marks $(p_i,y_i)$ with $y_i\in\operatorname{int}K_{p_i}$. Let $T_{a_i}(w)=w/(1+a_i\cdot w)$ be the centered positive projective normalization of $K_{p_i}-y_i$, and let $f_i$ equal $s^{-d}$ above the minimum denominator on this body, with its tangent extension below. Seed the upward construction with the maximum over the marked seeds at each base (or zero if none), where
$$
P_i(u,x)=h_{K_{p_i}-y_i}(u)f_i(1+a_i\cdot(x-y_i)),\qquad d_i=d|T_{a_i}(K_{p_i}-y_i)|.
$$
Every fixed ambient closed cap containing $(p_i,y_i)$ loses at least $\Gamma_d d_i$ to first order on the actual $p_i$ fiber, where $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. These lower bounds add across distinct bases. On a shared base their maximum is guaranteed by the individual inequalities.

pk-intake-proper-cap-partition-midpoint-.relation_to_goal: Counts the original caps of a partition up to null overlap, with every trace on every positive fiber proper in measure. Arbitrary overlapping covers and partitions permitting whole-fiber ownership are outside this component bound.
pk-intake-proper-cap-partition-midpoint-.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex, $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\ne\varnothing$, $q=\dim_H S\ge1$, and $\mu=\mathcal H_q|_S$, with $M=\mu(S)$. Let $P$ be the bases of the $q$-dimensional integer fibers, and $k$ their number of occupied coordinate parities. Join each distinct same-parity pair of bases in $P$ to its integer midpoint in one hyperedge; the midpoint also belongs to $P$. Write $c(P)$ for the number of connected components.

Suppose $r$ original closed ambient halfspaces of positive $\mu$-mass cover $S$ up to $\mu$-null sets and have pairwise $\mu$-null intersections. Suppose also that no one of them has full $\mathcal H_q$-measure on any fiber over $P$. On each positive fiber exactly two traces have positive measure; they are complementary cuts and their unordered pair of original cap indices is constant on each component. In particular $r\le2c(P)\le2k$. If $|P|>k$, then $r\le2(k-1)$. For equal actual cap mass $D$, one has $M=rD$ and $D\ge M/(2c(P))\ge M/(2k)\ge \Gamma_qM/k$, where $\Gamma_q=(q/(q+1))^q$.

pk-intake-proper-empty-endpoint-local-ca.relation_to_goal: Necessary fixed-body, fixed-mark condition for one proper/zero endpoint row. It controls section areas, with no general captured-volume comparison or all-endpoint status assumption.
pk-intake-proper-empty-endpoint-local-ca.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $A,K,B$ be compact convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$ with nonempty interiors at the only sampled bases $-1,0,1$, with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Use summed $d$-volume. Suppose $y\in\operatorname{int}K$ and the cap $u\cdot(x-y)+\alpha z\ge0$, $u\ne0$, locally minimizes capture under all small normal changes through $(0,y)$. Suppose its $A$ capture is proper and its $B$ capture has volume zero. Write $E_A,E_K$ for the proper sections, $t,s>0$ for their $\mathcal H^{d-1}$ areas, $c_A,c_K$ for their centroids, and $F$ for the possibly empty section on $B$. For every $w\in\mathbb R^d,\beta\in\mathbb R$,
$$
t[w\cdot(c_A-y)-\beta]+s\,w\cdot(c_K-y)+\int_F[w\cdot(x-y)+\beta]_+\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}(x)\ge0.
$$
Consequently $F$ is a positive-area supporting facet, $M=\mathcal H^{d-1}(F)\ge t$, and
$$
s^{1/(d-1)}\ge\frac{t^{1/(d-1)}+M^{1/(d-1)}}2\ge t^{1/(d-1)}.
$$
