pk-intake-proper-simplex-cut-first-varia.relation_to_goal: First variation for the uniform law on a single simplex.
pk-intake-proper-simplex-cut-first-varia.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $U$ be uniform on $\Delta_d=\{u\ge0:\sum_{j=0}^d u_j=1\}$, and set $F_x(t)=\Pr(x\cdot U\le t)$ for $x\in\mathbb R^{d+1}$. For every $\min_j x_j<t<\max_j x_j$, the function $(x,t)\mapsto F_x(t)$ is jointly $C^1$ near $(x,t)$. Let $b$ be the barycentric centroid of the section $S=\Delta_d\cap\{x\cdot u=t\}$ for uniform $(d-1)$-dimensional volume on $S$, and let $n$ be the projection of $x$ onto $\{\sum_j u_j=0\}$. Then
$$
\partial_t F_x(t)=\frac{\operatorname{vol}_{d-1}(S)}
{\operatorname{vol}_{d}(\Delta_d)\lVert n\rVert}>0,
\qquad \partial_{x_j}F_x(t)=-b_j\partial_t F_x(t).
$$
The formula includes a plane through any simplex vertex or lower-dimensional face consistent with properness.

pk-intake-pure-smooth-parity-menu-cover.relation_to_goal: Pure uniform outward smoothing, full occupied parity at the deepest bases, and every finite raw balanced menu. The reserve is a margin inequality.
pk-intake-pure-smooth-parity-menu-cover.statement:
Let $C$ be a compact convex body in $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$, $n,d\ge1$, with finitely many nonempty sampled fibers $K_z$, all of positive volume, and base set $P$. Use pure uniform outward smoothing of width $h\Gamma(u)$, $h>0$, where $\Gamma(u)=\sqrt{u^\top\Sigma u}$ for the pooled within-fiber covariance $\Sigma$. Assume that every deepest mark is attained with a nonvertical active cap of positive own strip coarea. Write the deepest marks as $Y_i=(p_i,y_i)$ and assume their bases $I=\{p_i\}$ occupy every parity represented in $P$. Assign a source $p(z)$ of the same parity to each $z$ once and iterate $z\mapsto (z+p(z))/2$ until reaching a root $p_i$. If $z\notin I$, this occurs after finitely many steps $t\ge1$ and yields
$$
p_i=\lambda z+\sum_{j\ne i}\lambda_jp_j,\qquad
0<\lambda\le\frac1{1+2^{t-1}},\qquad
\lambda_j\ge0,\qquad \lambda+\sum_{j\ne i}\lambda_j=1.
$$
For every finite menu of actual nonvertical active caps at the root, each attaining the common deepest raw mass and having positive own strip coarea and positive raw weights $\rho_\ell$ satisfying $\sum_\ell\rho_\ell u_\ell=0$, the sum of weighted margins at $(z,x)$ is strictly positive for every $x\in\mathbb R^d$. If all selected caps have zero strip coarea on $K_z$, one of the caps captures that whole fiber.

Suppose additionally that the selected caps have zero strip coarea on the other deepest fibers, that the other deepest marks are interior to their own fibers, and that $\Gamma(u_\ell)=1$, $\sum_\ell\rho_\ell=1$. Then the same weighted margin is at least $h+\min_{\lambda_j>0}\sum_\ell\rho_\ell h_{K_{p_j}-y_j}(u_\ell)>0$, where $h_K$ is the support function of $K$.

pk-intake-pyramid-centroidal-section-ene.relation_to_goal: Identifies the ordinary projective energy with an actual centroidal section of a symmetric-base pyramid.
pk-intake-pyramid-centroidal-section-ene.statement:
Let $D\subset\mathbb R^m$ be a convex body centrally symmetric about zero, $m\ge1$, and let $H>0$, $d=m+1$, and $B=H+1$. Put $K=\operatorname{conv}(D\times\{-1\},\{(0,H)\})$, with $d$-volume $V=B|D|/d$. For $a\in\mathbb R^m$, let $A=D\cap\{b:a\cdot b\le1\}$ and $N=(a,1)$. The section $K\cap\{(X,z):z+a\cdot X=0\}$ has parameterization
$$
X=\frac{Hb}{B-a\cdot b},\qquad z=-a\cdot X,\qquad b\in A.
$$
Its measure $d\mathcal H^m/\lVert N\rVert_2$ pulls back to $H^m B(B-a\cdot b)^{-d}\,db$. Write $C_a$ for this section measure divided by $V$, $p_a$ for the fraction of $K$ in the cap $z+a\cdot X\ge0$, and $C_0=dH^m/B^d$. Then
$$
C_a=\frac{dH^m}{|D|}\int_A(B-a\cdot b)^{-d}\,db,\qquad
p_a=\frac Hd C_a+1-\frac{|A|}{|D|}.
$$
The section has centroid zero if and only if $\int_A b(B-a\cdot b)^{-d-1}\,db=0$. In that case $\ell=-a/B$ minimizes the projective-energy integral on $A$ at zero, and $C_a/C_0=E_A(0)/|D|$.

pk-intake-quadratic-midpoint-repair-inve.relation_to_goal: An obstruction to a regularity requirement on convex-order improvements of a prescribed old midpoint law in an actual three-fiber model.
pk-intake-quadratic-midpoint-repair-inve.statement:
In the plane, let
$$
K=\{(x,t):\sqrt{1+\sqrt{1+x^2}}\le t\le3,\ |x|\le t/4\},\qquad
L=\{(a,b):|a|\le1/4,\ 1\le b\le 9/2-a^2/2\}.
$$
Use their unnormalized area measures as marginals. For their unique coupling maximizing the Euclidean second moment of the midpoint, the midpoint density $h$ satisfies $h(0,s)=4t/(1+t)^2$ on an interior segment with $s=t/2+t^2/4$ near $t=2$. More generally, for any positive smooth density with this restriction, its log has $s$-derivatives $-1/9$ and $1/81$ at $s=2$, and
$$
\frac{(h^{-1/\beta})''}{h^{-1/\beta}}(0,2)=\frac{1-\beta}{81\beta^2}.
$$
Thus the extended inverse $\beta$th root fails convexity for every $\beta>1$, also after constant density normalization. Any feasible midpoint law dominating this optimal law in convex order equals it. These are endpoint and midpoint laws on the three actual integer fibers of $\operatorname{conv}((\{0\}\times K)\cup(\{2\}\times L))$.

pk-intake-quadratic-source-contraction-f.relation_to_goal: A new parameter certificate may use different positive source weights and rows. No statement about retention of a physical separator is part of this contraction.
pk-intake-quadratic-source-contraction-f.statement:
Let $C$ be a compact convex hull with sampled set $S$ and normalized reciprocal target $\nu=dm/(ML)$ for summed positive fiber volume $dm$ of mass $M$ and positive continuous concave $L$ on $C$. Let $J$ be a finite set of integer bases with one mark $Y_p\in S$ over each $p\in J$. Assume that every positive-weight combination of bases in $J$ with integer average $r$ has $r\in J$, with mark and $L$-value equal to the combinations of the input marks and $L$-values. Set
$$
T_L=\{h\in C(C):h+cL\text{ is concave on }C\text{ for some }c\ge0\}.
$$
If some nonnegative masses $m_p$ satisfy $\sum_p m_p h(Y_p)\ge\int h\,d\nu$ for all $h\in T_L$, then there are such masses with positive support $J_0$ satisfying $\operatorname{conv}J_0\cap\mathbb Z^n=J_0$ and with every point of $J_0$ a vertex of its hull. In particular its bases have distinct parities. The new masses satisfy $\sum_p m_pL(Y_p)=1$ and admit rows with target $\nu$, mass $m_p$, barycenter $Y_p$, and $L$-moment $m_pL(Y_p)$.

pk-intake-quantitative-log-contact-certi.relation_to_goal: Quantitative control of a fixed positive logarithmic parameter from its supplied full-space marks and actual original volume.
pk-intake-quantitative-log-contact-certi.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite base with compatible compact convex bodies $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$. Write $S=\bigcup_z\{z\}\times K_z$, $C=\operatorname{conv}S$, and $dm=\sum_z\delta_z\otimes dX|_{K_z}$, with $M=m(S)$ and $dP_0=dm/M$. Let $L,U>0$ be continuous concave on $C$, with $\int\log L\,dP_0=\int\log U\,dP_0=0$. Suppose finitely many marks $Y_i\in C$, weights $\sigma_i>0$ with $\sum_i\sigma_i=1$, and probability laws $\rho_i$ on $S$ satisfy
$$
\int w\,d\rho_i=Y_i,\qquad \int L\,d\rho_i=L_i=L(Y_i),\qquad
\sum_i\frac{\sigma_i}{L_i}\rho_i=\frac{dm}{ML}.
$$
If $U(Y_i)/L_i\le e^\delta$ for every $i$, where $\delta\ge0$, then $b=\int(U/L)\,dP_0$ lies in $[1,e^\delta]$,
$$
D\bigl(P_0\,\big\|\,(U/(bL))P_0\bigr)=\log b,\qquad

\le M\max_S L\bigl(e^\delta\sqrt{2\delta}+e^\delta-1\bigr).

\max_{K_z}U\le\frac{(d+1)M\max_S L}{|K_z|}e^\delta .
$$
The first estimate on the core applies to any two nonnegative continuous concave functions on a full-dimensional compact convex body, with the zero case $B_z=0$ understood directly. pk-intake-quantitative-near-deepest-face.relation_to_goal: Ordinary fixed-base normalized depth and actual compatible competitors. The statement gives stability of the face cover near its ordinary infimum.
pk-intake-quantitative-near-deepest-face.statement:
Fix a finite nonempty real base $P$ and $d\ge1$. Let the convex bodies $K_z$ be the actual sampled fibers of their canonical hull, and use their summed $d$-volume as mixed measure. Suppose the total mass is one, each $K_z\subset R B_d$ contains a ball of radius $r_b>0$, and $|K_z|\ge v>0$. Let $q_z$ be the maximum raw ordinary closed-halfspace depth on fiber $z$, $Q=\max_z q_z$, $F_p$ the smallest face of $\operatorname{conv}P$ containing $p$, and $\beta_*$ the infimum of normalized ordinary maximum depth over all positive compatible families on $P$. Set $g=Q-\beta_*$, $\omega_j=|B_j|$ with $\omega_0=1$, and
$$
\begin{aligned}
A&=|P|\omega_{d-1}R^{d-1},& q_*&=\omega_d r_b^d/2,\\
C_V&=(d/r_b)(1+1/r_b)^{d-1},& c_m&=dv/(2R),\\
C_D&=C_V+A,& c_F&=q_*c_m/[2C_D(1+C_V)].
\end{aligned}
$$
For $0<\eta\le2C_D$, if the faces of the bases with $q_p\ge Q-\eta$ miss a sampled base, then $g\ge c_F\eta$. In particular, for $0\le g\le(c_F/2)\min(2C_D,q_*/2)$, the minimal faces of the bases with $q_p\ge Q-2g/c_F$ cover $P$, and each maximizing mark on these fibers contains an own inball centered there of radius $q_*/(4A)$.

pk-intake-quartic-continuous-kernel-gain.relation_to_goal: Scalar continuous kernels for affine simplex-chain envelopes. Discrete sampling and the mixed halfspace-depth conclusion require separate arguments.
pk-intake-quartic-continuous-kernel-gain.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ be an integer, $\theta=d/(d+1)$, and $f(z)=(1+z)^{d+1}/(1+\theta z)^d$ for $z\ge-1$. For every $v\in[0,1]$,
$$
f(v)+f(-v)\ge 2+\theta v^2+\frac{\theta}{4}v^4,
$$
with equality exactly at $v=0$.

For $z\in[-1,1]$, let $K_z(x)=(1+zx)^{d-1}[1-(d+1+dz)x]$ for $0\le x\le 1/(d+1+dz)$ and let $K_z(x)=0$ for larger $x$. Put $A_d(v)=\int_0^\infty (K_v(x)+K_{-v}(x))\,dx$. Then $A_d(v)=[f(v)+f(-v)-2]/(dv^2)$ for $v>0$, and $A_d(0)=1/(d+1)$ is its continuous extension. In particular,
$$
A_d(v)\ge\frac{1+v^2/4}{d+1}\qquad(0\le v\le 1),
$$
with equality exactly at $v=0$.

pk-intake-radial-log-parameter-contact-c.relation_to_goal: Parameter-only stationarity with its explicit no-strict-direction premise. No body-minimum, atomic cleanup or cap-variation assertion.
pk-intake-radial-log-parameter-contact-c.statement:
Let $C$ be a compact convex set in a finite-dimensional affine space and let $dm$ be a finite positive measure supported on a compact $S\subset C$, with mass $M>0$. Let $L>0$ be continuous and concave on $C$, with $\int_S\log L\,dm/M=0$. Let $Y_1,\ldots,Y_s\in C$ with $s\ge1$, and put $L_i=L(Y_i)$. Define
$$
\mathcal T_L=\{h\in C(C): h+cL\text{ is concave for some }c\ge0\},\qquad
B_i(h)=h(Y_i)/L_i-\int_S h/L\,dm/M.
$$
Assume no $h\in\mathcal T_L$ has $B_i(h)<0$ for all $i$. Then there are $\sigma_i\ge0$ summing to one, with $\mu=\sum_i(\sigma_i/L_i)\delta_{Y_i}$ and $d\nu=dm/(ML)$ of equal mass and full first moment. For every continuous convex $\phi$ on $C$, $\int\phi\,d\mu\le\int\phi\,d\nu$, and $\int L\,d\mu=\int L\,d\nu=1$. For positive indices there are measurable allocations $q_i\ge0$ on $S$, with $\sum_iq_i=1$ $\nu$-almost everywhere, satisfying
$$
\int q_i\,d\nu=\sigma_i/L_i,\qquad
\int wq_i\,d\nu=(\sigma_i/L_i)Y_i,\qquad \int Lq_i\,d\nu=\sigma_i.
$$
For every affine majorant $A\ge L$ on $C$ touching $L$ at $Y_i$, $A=L$ $q_i\nu$-almost everywhere.

Let $r^0:B\to(0,\infty)$ be continuous and concave with $r^0(z)=r^0(-z)$ at the sampled bases. For positive continuous concave $r$ on $B$ write $r_z=r(z)$ and take $C_r=\{(z,x):z\in B,\ x\in r(z)T_d\}$ with actual mixed set $S_r=C_r\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. Put $R_0=\sum_z(r_z^0)^d$ and $Q_0=c_dR_0$. Then
$$
\tau(r)=c_d\min_{a\in L}\sum_z |r_z+a\cdot z|^d.
$$
The minimum is attained uniquely. This is $c_d$ times the $d$th power of the $\ell_d$ distance of the sampled array from the subspace of functions $z\mapsto a\cdot z$, with no fitted constant. For $a\in L$ such that both compatible arrays lie in the validated neighborhood, replacing $r(z)$ by $r(z)+a\cdot z$ gives $\beta(r+a\cdot z)=\beta(r)-da$ and preserves $\tau(r)$ exactly. Both signs of sufficiently small $a$ are compatible on all of $B$. For nonzero such $a$, at least one sign gives strictly greater total mass at the same actual global raw depth, so if $\dim L>0$ no member of this local class is a local fixed-depth mass maximum. At the even baseline, every sufficiently small affine perturbation with $a\in L\setminus\{0\}$ has depth $Q_0$ and strictly increases mass above $V_dR_0$. $$
\int\psi f g(r)\,d\widehat a+\int\psi f r g(r)\,d\widehat b
\le\beta\int\psi f g(r)\,d\widehat b .
$$
In particular this holds for $g(r)=r^m$, $m\ge1$ integer, and $g=1$ recovers the projected reserve. For $0\le t\le\beta$, put $a_t=\pi_*((r-t)_+\widehat a)$ and $b_t=\pi_*((r-t)_+\widehat b)$. Then
$$
\int\psi f\,da_t+\int\psi f(r-t)_+^2\,d\widehat b
\le(\beta-t)\int\psi f\,db_t .
$$

pk-intake-rational-dilation-residue-push.relation_to_goal: An exact intrinsic pushforward for rational weights and actual integral target bases. Directions may vary across different pairs and residue classes.
pk-intake-rational-dilation-residue-push.statement:
Let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}$ be compact and convex, let $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$ be nonempty, and put $q=\dim_H S$, $\mu=\mathcal H_q|_S$. Fix an actual $Y\in S$ and $0<t<1$. Define $L_t=t(S-Y)\cap[-(1-t)(S-Y)]$, $G_t(Y)=\mathcal H_q(L_t)$. Suppose $t=r/m$ with $m=r+s$ and positive coprime integers $r,s$. Write $K_z=\{x:(z,x)\in S\}$. At $Y=(p,x)$, $G_t(p,x)$ is the sum of $\mathcal H_q(tK_z\cap(x-(1-t)K_w))$ over ordered occupied pairs with $rz+sw=mp$. This equation is equivalent to $z=p+s\ell,\ w=p-r\ell$ for $\ell\in\mathbb Z^n$. An ordered pair has integral weighted base precisely if $z\equiv w\pmod m$. For each residue class $c\bmod m$ let $\mu_c$ be the original intrinsic measure restricted to its fibers, $M_c=\mu_c(S)$ and $m_c=\int A\,d\mu_c(A)$. For every nonnegative Borel or bounded signed Borel test $\varphi$,
$$
\int_S \varphi(Y)G_t(Y)\,d\mu(Y)
=[t(1-t)]^q\sum_c\iint\varphi(tA+(1-t)B)\,d\mu_c(A)d\mu_c(B).
$$
In particular the total and vector first moment are $[t(1-t)]^q\sum_c M_c^2$ and $[t(1-t)]^q\sum_c M_cm_c$. If the summand uses the unscaled intersection $K_z\cap((x-(1-t)K_w)/t)$, its pushforward factor is instead $(1-t)^q$.

pk-intake-raw-moment-john-free-mass-stat.relation_to_goal: Stationarity of the raw-moment ellipsoid program, for source caps with balanced base and common mass. The caps need not be depth-attaining through the selected centroid.
pk-intake-raw-moment-john-free-mass-stat.statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge1$, and let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty. For each $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body of positive $d$-volume, and set $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_z})$. Call $b=(t,v)$ feasible if $\int f\,d\mu=t$ and $\int zf\,d\mu=v$ for some measurable $0\le f\le1$. For a feasible $b$ let $Q(b)$ be the set of $\int xf\,d\mu$ over those densities. For a compact convex nonempty set $Q\subset\mathbb R^d$ write $J(Q)=\max\{(\det A)^{1/d}:c+AB_d\subset Q,\ A\succeq0\}$, with $B_d$ the closed Euclidean unit ball and $A$ symmetric.

For $j\in\operatorname{conv}P$ write $Q_t(j)=Q(t,tj)$ and $T_j=\max\{t:(t,tj)\text{ is feasible}\}$.

Fix $j\in\operatorname{conv}P$ and an interior maximizing mass $0<t_0<T_j$ for $J(Q_t(j))$. Let $c+AB_d$ be a maximum-volume ellipsoid of $Q_{t_0}(j)$, with $A$ symmetric positive definite. There are $m\le 1+d+d(d+1)/2$ unit vectors $v_i$, positive weights $\lambda_i$, and real slopes $b_i$ with
$$
\sum_i\lambda_i v_i=0,\qquad
\sum_i\lambda_i v_i v_i^{\mathsf T}=I_d,\qquad
\sum_i\lambda_i b_i=0 .
$$
With $u_i=A^{-1}v_i$ there are finite $a_i$ and caps $H_i=\{L_i\ge0\}$, $L_i(z,x)=u_i\cdot x+a_i\cdot(z-j)-b_i$, of mass $t_0$, base mean $j$, and raw continuous moments $c+Av_i$. Put $\Psi_i=\int(L_i)_+\,d\mu$. Then $\sum_i\lambda_i\Psi_i=d$. The dominated measure $d^{-1}\sum_i\lambda_i\mu|_{H_i}$ has mass $t_0$ and centroid $(j,c/t_0)$, and the constituent continuous centroids under weights $\lambda_i/d$ have covariance $A^2/(dt_0^2)$. On the plane $z=j$, the caps $H_i$ cover the plane and so do their opposite closed halfspaces. Also
$$
\int\left[\sum_i\lambda_i a_i\cdot(z-j)\right]_+\,d\mu\le d.
$$

pk-intake-raw-moment-john-integer-maxima.relation_to_goal: The maximizing bases are for a raw-moment ellipsoid objective. The actual closed-halfspace depth hull, width-two witness constructions, and the locked depth bound are different statements.
pk-intake-raw-moment-john-integer-maxima.statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge1$, and let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty. For each $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body of positive $d$-volume, and set $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_z})$. Call $b=(t,v)$ feasible if $\int f\,d\mu=t$ and $\int zf\,d\mu=v$ for some measurable $0\le f\le1$. For a feasible $b$ let $Q(b)$ be the set of $\int xf\,d\mu$ over those densities. For a compact convex nonempty set $Q\subset\mathbb R^d$ write $J(Q)=\max\{(\det A)^{1/d}:c+AB_d\subset Q,\ A\succeq0\}$, with $B_d$ the closed Euclidean unit ball and $A$ symmetric.

For $j\in\operatorname{conv}P$ write $Q_t(j)=Q(t,tj)$ and $T_j=\max\{t:(t,tj)\text{ is feasible}\}$.

The positive-mass feasible integer bases are exactly $\operatorname{conv}P\cap\mathbb Z^n$. For each of them the maximum of $J(Q_t(j))$ over $[0,T_j]$ is positive and attained at a unique $t>0$. The set $E$ of bases reaching the joint maximum satisfies
$$
E=\operatorname{vert}(\operatorname{conv}E)=\operatorname{conv}E\cap\mathbb Z^n,\qquad |E|\le2^n.
$$
The cardinality bound is attained by $[0,1]^n\times K$ with $K$ a positive-volume convex body.

For $j\in P$, every feasible density of mass $T_j$ and mean base $j$ fills $K_j$ almost everywhere. If $0<\varepsilon<|K_j|$ and $Z_\varepsilon=\{\int_{K_j}xg(x)\,dx:0\le g\le1,\ \int_{K_j}g\,dx=\varepsilon\}$, then $Q_{T_j-\varepsilon}(j)\supseteq Q_{T_j}(j)-Z_\varepsilon$, where subtraction means addition of the reflected set. In particular the maximizing mass is less than $T_j$ at these bases. When the $K_z$ are all positive integer fibers of one compact convex body, every positive-mass feasible integer base belongs to $P$ and hence has interior maximizing mass.

Writing $M=\mu(\mathbb R^{n+d})$ and $(g_z,g_x)=M^{-1}\int(z,x)\,d\mu$, one has $Q(M-t,Mg_z-v)=Mg_x-Q(t,v)$. The unique maximum over all feasible real constraint pairs is at $(M/2,Mg_z/2)$. If $g_z$ is integral, the integer program has the unique optimal base and mass $(g_z,M/2)$, with the center of every optimal ellipsoid equal to $(M/2)g_x$.

pk-intake-raw-moment-prescribed-slope-ca.relation_to_goal: A free-mass balanced linear source objective with a fixed prescribed slope, including arbitrary finite source families.
pk-intake-raw-moment-prescribed-slope-ca.statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge1$, and let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty. For each $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body of positive $d$-volume, and set $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_z})$. Call $b=(t,v)$ feasible if $\int f\,d\mu=t$ and $\int zf\,d\mu=v$ for some measurable $0\le f\le1$. For a feasible $b$ let $Q(b)$ be the set of $\int xf\,d\mu$ over those densities.

For $j\in\operatorname{conv}P$ write $Q_t(j)=Q(t,tj)$ and $T_j=\max\{t:(t,tj)\text{ is feasible}\}$.

Fix $j\in\operatorname{conv}P$ and $0<t_0<T_j$. If
$$
u\cdot q\le u\cdot q_0+b(t-t_0),\qquad u\ne0,
$$
is a supporting plane at $(t_0,q_0)$ of $\{(t,q):0\le t\le T_j,\ q\in Q_t(j)\}$, there is a finite $a\in\mathbb R^n$ such that $H=\{u\cdot x+a\cdot(z-j)-b\ge0\}$ satisfies
$$
\mu(H)=t_0,\qquad \int_H(z-j)\,d\mu=0,\qquad \int_H x\,d\mu=q_0.
$$
The scalar $b$ is the prescribed slope of the supporting plane.

pk-intake-raw-moment-support-and-strict-.relation_to_goal: An auxiliary source-body theorem for dominated densities on arbitrary finite positive fibers, with raw moments and no depth assertion.
pk-intake-raw-moment-support-and-strict-.statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge1$, and let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty. For each $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body of positive $d$-volume, and set $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_z})$. Call $b=(t,v)$ feasible if $\int f\,d\mu=t$ and $\int zf\,d\mu=v$ for some measurable $0\le f\le1$. For a feasible $b$ let $Q(b)$ be the set of $\int xf\,d\mu$ over those densities. For a compact convex nonempty set $Q\subset\mathbb R^d$ write $J(Q)=\max\{(\det A)^{1/d}:c+AB_d\subset Q,\ A\succeq0\}$, with $B_d$ the closed Euclidean unit ball and $A$ symmetric.

The feasible domain and the joint graph $\{(b,q):q\in Q(b)\}$ are compact convex. For every feasible $b$ and $u\ne0$ there is exactly one density, up to $\mu$-null sets, maximizing $u\cdot\int xf\,d\mu$. On each fiber this density is the indicator of an upper $u$-cap of its assigned mass, including empty and full traces up to null sets.

For every finite feasible mixture $b=\sum_i\alpha_i b_i$ with $\alpha_i>0$, $\sum_i\alpha_i=1$ and at least two distinct $b_i$, there is $\varepsilon>0$ such that $\sum_i\alpha_i Q(b_i)+\varepsilon B_d\subseteq Q(b)$. In particular $J(Q(b))>\sum_i\alpha_i J(Q(b_i))$, with $J=0$ on lower-dimensional sets.

pk-intake-real-degree-centered-slab-tail.relation_to_goal: A real-degree scalar tail estimate and its application to outer vertical regions with one integer coordinate.
pk-intake-real-degree-centered-slab-tail.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be real, and let $(w_i)$ be a nonzero nonnegative sequence on a finite consecutive integer interval, with $(w_i^{1/d})$ concave there and $\sum_i i w_i=0$. Put $M=\sum_i w_i$, $m=\max_i w_i$, $r_d=(2/(d+2))^{(d+1)/d}$ and $\kappa_d=1/(3+d r_d)$. For every integer $h\ge0$,
$$
\min\left\{\sum_{i>h}w_i,\ \sum_{i<-h}w_i\right\}
\ge\kappa_d\bigl[M-(2h+1)m\bigr].
$$
The constants satisfy $1/5<\kappa_d\le9/31<3/10$, with $\kappa_1=9/31$ and $\lim_{d\to\infty}\kappa_d=1/5$.

Let $d$ be a positive integer and $C\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ a convex body of positive mixed $d$-volume $M$ whose mixed-volume centroid has integer base coordinate $j$. Write $w_i=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_i)$ and $m=\max_{i\in\mathbb Z} w_i$. With $\kappa_d$ as above, each of $z>j+h$ and $z<j-h$ has mixed $d$-volume in $C\cap(\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R^d)$ at least $\kappa_d[M-(2h+1)m]$ for every integer $h\ge0$.

pk-intake-real-width-hinge-degeneration-.relation_to_goal: Sharp interval-fiber obstruction to a positive lower calibration in the all-real-base width.
pk-intake-real-width-hinge-degeneration-.statement:
For $L\ge0$, let $C_L$ be the convex hull of four unit intervals at binary bases $00,10,01,11$, with fibers $[0,1]$ except the fiber $[L,L+1]$ at $11$. Its mixed mass is $M=4$ and its maximum normalized ambient closed-halfspace depth is $1/8$. The real fiber over $(s,t)\in[0,1]^2$ is
$$
[L\max(0,s+t-1),\,1+L\min(s,t)].
$$
Thus $D_{\rm int}=[-1,1]$ and $D_{\rm all}=[-W,W]$ with $W=1+L/2$. At cap count eight and cap budget $1/2$ the exact width-normalized hinge minima divided by $M$ are $1/4$ for $D_{\rm int}$ and $1/(4W)$ for $D_{\rm all}$. In particular there is no positive dimension-only lower bound for the latter normalized minimum at the sharp depth budget, even at $n=2,d=1$.

pk-intake-recipient-section-length-obstr.relation_to_goal: Refutes a consequence of local cover and positive balance alone. The configuration is unrestricted by actual common contact, minimizing caps or a prescribed mixed-mass budget.
pk-intake-recipient-section-length-obstr.statement: There is no universal constant bounding the total length of positive-area recipient traces on an empty supporting face of a planar triangle by the sum of the recipients' own section lengths, even when the family covers the triangle, both recipients cut it properly, and the three inward unit normals have a strictly positive dependence. More precisely, for $0<\varepsilon<1$ take $K=\operatorname{conv}\{(-1,0),(1,0),(0,-1)\}$, $H_0=\{y\ge0\}$, $H_+=\{y\ge-1+\varepsilon\}$ and $H_-=\{y\le-1+\varepsilon\}$. The face $F_0=K\cap\partial H_0$ has length $2$ and the two traces on it have lengths $2,0$. The recipient cap areas are $1-\varepsilon^2,\varepsilon^2$, and their own section lengths sum to $4\varepsilon$.

pk-intake-reciprocal-rectangles-absolute.relation_to_goal: Refutes the auxiliary absolute raw $4/3$ target with equal unit-area endpoints and its fixed-direction concave-profile version. The upper bound controls all centers, while the computed minimum is over axial tilts.
pk-intake-reciprocal-rectangles-absolute.statement:
Let $R\ge1$, $A=[-1/2,1/2]^2$, $B_R=[-R/2,R/2]\times[-1/(2R),1/(2R)]$, and $C_R=\operatorname{conv}((\{-1\}\times A)\cup(\{1\}\times B_R))$ in coordinates $(z,s,t)$. Its exact integer fibers at $-1,0,1$ are $A,M_R=(A+B_R)/2,B_R$. The middle area is $m_R=(R+2+1/R)/4$. In raw summed fiber area, the minimum over all $\alpha\in\mathbb R$ of the closed cap $s+\alpha z\ge0$ is
$$J_R=\frac R8+\frac34+\frac5{8R}
=\frac{3m_R}{2}-\sqrt{m_R(m_R-1)}>\frac{m_R+1}{3}.$$
It is attained at $\alpha=1/2$, minimized as a function of $R$ at $\sqrt5$ with value $(3+\sqrt5)/4$, and is less than $4/3$ exactly when $5/3<R<3$. The origin maximizes depth on the middle fiber and all extreme-fiber points have depth at most $1/2$. Hence every mixed point has raw depth at most $J_R$. At $R=2$, the total mixed area is $25/8$ and the cap at $\alpha=1/2$ has raw area $21/16$, including a nonempty null supporting edge at $z=-1$. This cap also realizes $J_{1/2}(f,g)=21/16$ for the centered, unit-mass, single-piece concave profiles $f=1$ on $[-1/2,1/2]$ and $g=1/2$ on $[-1,1]$, where $J_\alpha$ adds the positive axial midpoint area to the two upper endpoint tails at $\alpha,-\alpha$.

pk-intake-reciprocal-sector-change-psd-a.relation_to_goal: Exact ordinary planar feasibility with the six ray endpoints of a strict distinct-vertex triangle fixed.
pk-intake-reciprocal-sector-change-psd-a.statement:
Let $T$ be a planar triangle with three balanced spanning cuts through an interior mark, with distinct strict captured vertices. Fix its six actual ray endpoints. Prescribe positive finite unique areas $X_i$ between their ray-core values and $X_i^T$, and double areas $Y_j\ge Y_j^T$. Write $\ell_i=1/(2X_i)-1/(2X_i^T)$ and $g_j=1/(2Y_j^T)-1/(2Y_j)$. The baseline matrix consists of three rank-one two-node blocks $L_{T,i}=\lambda_i\begin{pmatrix}\beta_i^2&-\alpha_i\beta_i\\-\alpha_i\beta_i&\alpha_i^2\end{pmatrix}$, with $\lambda_i>0$ and positive normalized kernel $(\alpha_i,\beta_i)$, $\alpha_i+\beta_i=1$. Feasibility of the changed data is equivalent to
$$
L=\operatorname{diag}_{i=1}^3(L_{T,i}+\ell_i\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T})-\sum_j g_j a_j a_j^{\mathsf T}\succeq0,
$$
where $a_j$ indicates the two nodes of double edge $j$. In particular, if $\ell_i=0$, both double gains adjacent to that corner vanish. At most one positive unique loss implies no positive double gains.

pk-intake-reflected-roof-exact-transvers.relation_to_goal: A full-normal minimizing-cap formula at prescribed marks and a two-sided directional-transfer example. For long extrusions the prescribed mark is strictly shallower than an explicit actual competitor.
pk-intake-reflected-roof-exact-transvers.statement:
Let $D\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R$ be a compact convex body centrally symmetric about $0$, with mixed length measure $\nu$ of mass $W>0$. Let $g$ be continuous, positive and concave on $D$, and let $L\ge\max_Dg$. Set $Q=\int_Dg\,d\nu$ and $C=\{(X,t):X\in D,\ -L\le t\le g(X)\}$. The total mixed area is $LW+Q$. Whenever $(\max_Dg-L)/2\le h\le\min_Dg$, the raw depth at the actual point $(0,h)$ is $Q-hW$, attained by $\{t\ge h\}$. The section $t=0$ is $D$ and has normalized maximum depth $1/2$. At $h=0$ the original cap cuts every positive fiber properly and the original normalized depth tends to zero as $L\to\infty$ with $D,g$ fixed.

For $D=[-1,1]\times[-1,1]$ in coordinates $(z,s)$, with $z$ integer, take $g=5/4-s$ and $L=3$. Then $W=6$, $Q=15/2$ and the total mixed area is $51/2$. On $-3/8\le h\le1/4$ the raw depth is $15/2-6h$, and the original normalized depth at $h=0$ is $5/17$. The direction $\{s\ge0\}$ captures half the section and half the lower area at $t=0$, but only $3/10$ of the upper cap's area.

pk-intake-reflection-retention-through-s.relation_to_goal: Actual mixed length and integer-base reflection centers for planar interval-fiber bodies with at most six positive fibers. The implication to original halfspace depth uses reflection symmetry directly.
pk-intake-reflection-retention-through-s.statement: Let $C\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R$ be a compact convex body. Let $\mu=\mathcal H^1|_{C\cap(\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R)}$ have mass $M>0$ and suppose exactly $N\le6$ integer fibers have positive length. Over actual integer-base centers $Y$, set $R_*=\max_Y\mu(C\cap(2Y-C))$. Then $R_*\ge M/2$. For exactly four positive fibers the inequality is strict if every fiber has mass strictly below $M/2$, and $R_*/M=1/2$ is attained with four positive fibers. For exactly five positive fibers, $R_*\ge4M/7$ and $\inf R_*/M=4/7$. In particular some actual point has original raw closed-halfspace depth at least $M/4$, or at least $2M/7$ for five positive fibers.

pk-intake-reflexive-triangle-product-exp.statement: For $r\in\{3,4\}$ let $D_r=\operatorname{conv}\{(-r,-r),(r,0),(0,r)\}$, with actual base $D_r\cap\mathbb Z^2$, and let $K$ be any nondegenerate planar triangle with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_j$. In the $D_4\times K$ product, restrict to any one of the three exposed base edges and sum arclength on $\partial K$ over its five integer sites, with the outer continuous edge normal $n$ attached. The supremum of $\int\Phi W/\int\Phi$ for finite nonnegative $\Phi(n,z,x)$ convex in $(z,x)$ for each fixed $n$, with finite positive denominator and both integrals using this edge measure, is $2/5$. pk-intake-regular-affine-simplex-cover-r.relation_to_goal: Regular one-circuit response at common-normal simplices and finite labeled stress on the chosen velocity space.
pk-intake-regular-affine-simplex-cover-r.statement:
Under affine-simplex-first-jets-by-actual-hull-repair, the added fiber volumes between the actual repaired fibers and their candidate affine images are $O(t^2)$. The change in total volume and in the mass of any fixed or moving ambient closed cap is consequently $O(t^2)$ uniformly in the cap.

Let a fixed regular critical circuit of old mass $Q=\beta M$ per cap have nonzero continuous normals $u_j$, positive balancing coefficients $\rho_j$ with $\sum_j\rho_j u_j=0$, and nonnegative weighted margin on all assigned base planes. Suppose it controls the deepest base planes and finite covers with strict slack cover the others. Assume no positive-area supporting coincidence and that each row has positive total proper coarea $S_j$ (the sum of its proper section areas divided by $\|u_j\|$). Put $\theta_j=(\rho_j/S_j)/\sum_h(\rho_h/S_h)$ and $W_z(x)=\sum_j\theta_j\mathbf 1_{H_j}(z,x)$. The normalized common first cover response times $M$ is
$$
R(V)=\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}(W_z-\beta)n\cdot V_z\,dS .
$$
The total first derivative is $\sum_z |K_z|\operatorname{tr}A_z$. A local minimum under these actual paths forces $R\ge0$ on the labeled first-jet cone.

For any linear $R$ on the chosen velocity space, nonnegativity whenever $L_\ell\ge0$ is equivalent to $R=\sum_\ell\gamma_\ell L_\ell$ on that space for some $\gamma_\ell\ge0$. If the velocity space permits all independent affine fields and $R$ has the above boundary profile, put $f_z=\int_{\partial K_z}(W_z-\beta)n\,dS$ and $B_z=\int_{\partial K_z}(W_z-\beta)nx^{\mathsf T}\,dS$. Each contact label with target $q$, weights $a_z$, normal $n_i$, tuple $x_z$ and mean $\xi$ contributes $\gamma_\ell n_i$ and $\gamma_\ell n_i\xi^{\mathsf T}$ at its target, minus the terms $\gamma_\ell a_z n_i$ and $\gamma_\ell a_z n_i x_z^{\mathsf T}$ at its inputs. In particular $\sum_z f_z=0$, $\sum_z B_z=0$, and $\sum_z f_z z^{\mathsf T}=0$.

pk-intake-regular-buffered-cap-contact-a.relation_to_goal: A conditional regular cap statement and a strict-convexity sufficient condition in d at least two, for a fixed family.
pk-intake-regular-buffered-cap-contact-a.statement:
Use the Euclidean buffered quantile regions and the fixed-face cover of the preceding theorems. For any active nonvertical cap at a sampled mark $(p,y)$ of depth $q>0$, suppose its own trace is proper and all its nonproper fiber sections have zero $\mathcal H^{d-1}$ measure. Let $(\bar z,\bar X)$ denote the barycenter of the actual sections weighted by $\mathcal H^{d-1}/\|u\|$. Then the right quantile is differentiable at its normal and $(\bar z,\bar X)=(p,y-\varepsilon f(p,y)u)$ for the unit continuous normal $u$.

In the fixed-face cover, if a selected positive-weight cap has a right quantile differentiable in the base tilts at its fixed normal, then $F_p=\{p\}$. If this holds at each sampled maximizing base and $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$, then every maximizing base is extreme in $\operatorname{conv}I$, $I=P\cap\operatorname{conv}I$, and $|I|=k(I)\le k(P)\le2^n$, where $k(A)$ is the largest size of a subset of $A$ in convex position whose hull contains no other points of $A$. For $d\ge2$, strict convexity of every sampled fiber ensures the asserted nonproper-section condition and $C^1$ cap mass throughout the nonvertical parameters. In particular every proper shifted own trace in such a family gives a $C^1$ right quantile locally.

pk-intake-regular-buffered-row-strict-co.relation_to_goal: A conditional statement about the exposed face of a chosen corrected resultant at a fixed buffered maximizer.
pk-intake-regular-buffered-row-strict-co.statement:
Fix a finite positive compatible mixed family and a fixed buffered depth with continuous covectors normalized in a fixed norm independent of the base tilt $a$. Let $(p,y)$ be a global sampled buffered maximizer, with value $Q$ and maximizing base set $I$. Suppose a chosen group of actual mass-$Q$ caps is
$$
H_j=\{(z,x):a_j\cdot(z-p)+u_j\cdot(x-y)\ge-\varepsilon f(p,y)\},
$$
with thresholds equal to the right upper $Q$-quantiles of their fixed normals. Let $\varepsilon>0$ and suppose $\rho_j>0$, $\sum_j\rho_j=1$, $\sum_j\rho_j u_j=\varepsilon g$, with a full supporting bound
$$
f(z,x)\le f(p,y)+\alpha\cdot(z-p)+g\cdot(x-y).
$$
The corrected resultant is $\ell=\sum_j\rho_j a_j-\varepsilon\alpha$. If at least one selected cap has $C^1$ actual mass as a function of its full hyperplane parameters $(a,u,c)$ near that cap and its total section coarea is positive, then
$$
\ell\cdot(r-p)<0\qquad(r\in I,\ r\ne p).
$$
Thus the face exposed by this particular resultant on $\operatorname{conv}I$ is $\{p\}$. If the fibers are polytopes and a selected row has a proper own section, failure of its full $C^1$ regularity requires a supporting section of positive $(d-1)$-measure in another fiber.

pk-intake-regular-cap-second-variation.relation_to_goal: Local second variation for ordinary volume under smooth transverse cut regularity.
pk-intake-regular-cap-second-variation.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^k\times\mathbb R$ be a convex body, $k\ge1$, with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$, and write $(z,t)$ for its coordinates. Suppose $\partial K$ is $C^2$ near $t=0$ and the horizontal component $N_z$ of its outer unit normal $(N_z,N_t)$ is nonzero along $\partial K\cap\{t=0\}$. Let $V=|K|$, $Q_t=\{z:(z,t)\in K\}$, and let $S(t),M_1(t),M_2(t)$ be the integrals of $1,z,zz^\mathsf T$ on $Q_t$. For $F(h,b)=|K\cap\{t+h\cdot z\ge b\}|/V$, the gradient and Hessian at $(h,b)=(0,0)$ are
$$
\nabla F(0,0)=\frac1V\binom{M_1(0)}{-S(0)},\qquad
\nabla^2F(0,0)=\frac1V
\begin{pmatrix}
-M_2'(0)&M_1'(0)\\
M_1'(0)^\mathsf T&-S'(0)
\end{pmatrix}.
$$
The direction $(0,1)$ is stationary for the spherical through-origin cap fraction $p$ exactly when $Q_0$ has centroid $0$. At such a direction, the spherical Hessian in horizontal tangent coordinates is
$$
-\frac1V M_2'(0)
=\frac1V\int_{\partial Q_0}zz^\mathsf T\,\frac{N_t}{\lVert N_z\rVert}\,d\mathcal H^{k-1}(z).
$$

pk-intake-regular-critical-circuit-shell.relation_to_goal: Fixed normals and a regular compatible shell contraction. Establishes an upper cover response under a strict circuit-by-circuit test.
pk-intake-regular-critical-circuit-shell.statement:
Assume the compatible homothetic deformation and boundary-null cone gluing of the shared-source shell-credit lemma, with $M$ the old total mass and $Q=\beta M$ the old global maximum raw mixed depth. Take a finite collection of selected circuits of critical closed caps of mass $Q$, each through a deepest mark and with unit continuous normals $u_j$, weights $\rho_j>0$ satisfying $\sum_j\rho_j u_j=0$, and weighted old margin nonnegative on its assigned base planes. Treat copies of a cap in different circuits separately. Every old fiber trace of each selected cap is proper or strictly full or empty, and $S_j>0$ is the sum of its proper section areas. Let $L_j$ denote its fixed-cap loss derivative and $B_j\le L_j$ the shared-source bound from the lemma.

For a circuit, there are nearby equal-mass caps with the same normals and unchanged weighted threshold budget. Their common raw mass is $Q+\varepsilon q_c+o(\varepsilon)$, where
$$
q_c=-\sum_j\theta_jL_j,\qquad \theta_j=\frac{\rho_j/S_j}{\sum_h\rho_h/S_h}.
$$
If $\sum_j\theta_jB_j>\beta dV_I$ in each selected circuit for the same compatible deformation, and finite covers with strict old cap-mass slack cover every remaining measured base plane, the new global maximum normalized depth is strictly less than $\beta$ for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$.

pk-intake-regular-mixed-near-quantile-ti.relation_to_goal: A local statement under C² regularity of actual critical cap maps. The bound on displaced source depth is one-sided.
pk-intake-regular-mixed-near-quantile-ti.statement:
Use raw summed volume of a finite family of compact convex fibers with positive $d$-dimensional volume, and let $Y$ be interior to its own fiber with raw depth $Q$. Let finitely many nonvertical critical closed caps through $Y$ have mass $Q$ and continuous normals $u_j$ positively balanced by weights $\rho_j$ with $\sum_j\rho_j=1$. Linearly perturb their full normals to $N_j+sN'_j$ with continuous parts $u_j+s w_j$. Define $m_j(W)=N_j\cdot(W-Y)$, $\ell_j(W)=N'_j\cdot(W-Y)$ and $F_j(s,c)=\mu\{m_j+s\ell_j\ge c\}$. Assume $F_j$ is $C^2$ near $(0,0)$ and $S_j=-\partial_cF_j(0,0)>0$. Put $A_j=\partial_{ss}F_j(0,0)$. Then $\partial_sF_j(0,0)=0$, $A_j\ge0$, and the actual raw $Q$-quantile threshold is
$$
c_j(s)=\frac{A_j}{2S_j}s^2+o(s^2).
$$
For $s>0$ the coefficients $\rho_j/s$ combine the continuous normals exactly to $\sum_j\rho_jw_j$ and the thresholds to $(s/2)\sum_j\rho_j A_j/S_j+o(s)$. If the missing components of unit representatives have magnitude $O(s)$, recovering a nonzero component there requires total positive coefficient $\Omega(1/s)$. With a $C^1$ cap map the scalar inversion still gives $c_j(s)=o(s)$ and the same normal identity with threshold sum $o(1)$.

Under local coarea moment regularity, writing $d\sigma$ for the sum of fiber-section areas divided by $|u_j|$, the first normal derivative is $\int_{m_j=0}\ell_j\,d\sigma$, and $A_j=-\partial_c\int_{m_j=c}\ell_j^2\,d\sigma|_{c=0}$. In particular the identities hold for stable proper, strictly full or strictly empty cuts of finite polytopal fibers whose varying planes avoid the vertices. If a continuous direction $e$ satisfies $u_j\cdot e=0$, $w_j\cdot e\ne0$ and $A_j>0$ for some $j$, then
$$
h_\mu(Y+he)\le Q-\frac{S_j^2(w_j\cdot e)^2}{2A_j}h^2+o(h^2).
$$

pk-intake-regular-support-face-surface-j.relation_to_goal: Exact local conditional surface densities and pointwise compatibility on regular common charts. The area-Jacobian and dimension hypotheses are explicit.
pk-intake-regular-support-face-surface-j.statement:
Let $K_-,K_0,K_+\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies with $(K_-+K_+)/2\subset K_0$. Let $n:U\subset\mathbb R^k\to\mathbb S^{d-1}$ be a $C^2$ injective immersion of rank $k$ on an open set, let $m=d-1-k$, and assume $h_i(t)=h_{K_i}(n(t))$ is $C^2$ for each body. Suppose the actual support faces at $n(t)$ have affine dimension $m$, and their relative interiors give regular boundary patches with the indicated unique normal and ordinary surface measure given by the area Jacobian of the one-to-one affine-face parametrizations below. Use common orthonormal frames $N(t)$ of $\operatorname{im}Dn(t)$ and $E(t)$ of $L(t)=\ker n(t)^{\mathsf T}\cap\ker Dn(t)^{\mathsf T}$ locally. For the canonical perpendicular origins $a_i(t)$ of the affine face hulls and points $X_i(t,s)=a_i(t)+E(t)s$ on those faces, put $R=N^{\mathsf T}Dn$ and $Q_i(t,s)=D^2h_i(t)-\sum_j X_{i,j}(t,s)D^2 n_j(t)$. For $k>0$, the $Q_i$ are positive semidefinite and the actual marked surface densities relative to the common $dt\,ds$ are $J_i=\det Q_i/|\det R|$.

Write $Z=\{t:h_0(t)=(h_-(t)+h_+(t))/2\}$. At Lebesgue-almost every $t\in Z$, and at every point of an open tight chart, $a_0=(a_-+a_+)/2$. For every endpoint face pair at such a parameter, its physical midpoint is $X_0(t,s_0)$ with $s_0=(s_-+s_+)/2$, and $Q_0(t,s_0)=(Q_-(t,s_-)+Q_+(t,s_+))/2$. For $k>0$ this gives
$$
J_0(t,s_0)^{1/k}\ge \frac{J_-(t,s_-)^{1/k}+J_+(t,s_+)^{1/k}}2.
$$
If $m>0$, in particular $J_0(t,s_0)\ge ((J_-(t,s_-)^{-1/m}+J_+(t,s_+)^{-1/m})/2)^{-m}$, with zero on the right if either input is zero. For $m=0$ the conditional densities are singleton masses and $J_0\ge\min(J_-,J_+)$. For $k=0$ the fixed normal has unit Euclidean facet density, including unit endpoint counting mass when $d=1$.

pk-intake-relative-fine-coarse-closed-ha.relation_to_goal: A uniform closed-halfspace discrepancy estimate under relative mesh control; no total-variation or unconditional sharp depth claim.
pk-intake-relative-fine-coarse-closed-ha.statement:
Let $r\ge1$, $s\ge0$, $m=r+s$, and let $(K_z)_{z\in P}$ be a finite family of compact convex sets in $RB_2^m$ placed at a fixed finite set $P\subset\mathbb R^k$ with $J=|P|$ and $R>0$. The sets may have zero $m$-volume. Write the continuous coordinates as $(u,x)\in\mathbb R^r	imes\mathbb R^s$. Let $a+L$ be a full-rank lattice coset in $\mathbb R^r$ with covolume $v$ and a measurable fundamental cell $F$ for $L$, with translates tiling up to null sets and $F\subseteq[-\delta,\delta]^r$. Define $
u$ as the summed coarse $m$-volume and $\mu$ as $v$ times the sum of $s$-volumes at fine bases in $a+L$ within each coarse fiber, with $\operatorname{vol}_0$ counting on $\mathbb R^0$. Set $M=
u(\mathrm{total})>0$ and $E=2r\delta(2R+2\delta)^{m-1}$. Then $|\mu(H)-
u(H)|\le JE$ for every closed ambient halfspace $H$, and $|\mu(\mathrm{total})-M|\le JE$. If $M>JE$, the two normalized measures differ by at most $2JE/(M-JE)$ on all closed halfspaces, and their normalized depths at every same ambient point differ by at most that quantity. For a sequence with common $J,R$ and $\delta_\ell/M_\ell	o0$, the fine mass is eventually positive and this normalized error tends to zero.

pk-intake-relative-mesh-fine-depth-recov.relation_to_goal: Conditional relative-mesh sharp recovery; the hypothesis uses smaller integer ranks than k+r but requires intrinsic measures in larger continuous ambient dimensions. No claim for the regime without delta/M tending to zero.
pk-intake-relative-mesh-fine-depth-recov.statement:
Let $k\ge0$, $r\ge1$, $s\ge0$, $m=r+s$, and let $C_\ell\subset\mathbb R^k\times\mathbb R^r\times\mathbb R^s$ be compact and convex. Suppose all nonempty integer-$z$ fibers $K_{\ell,z}$ are indexed by one fixed finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb Z^k$ and lie in $RB_2^m$ for a fixed $R>0$. Let $M_\ell=\sum_z|K_{\ell,z}|_m>0$. In the first $r$ continuous coordinates sample full-rank lattice cosets $a_\ell+L_\ell$ of covolume $v_\ell$, with measurable fundamental cells in $[-\delta_\ell,\delta_\ell]^r$. Give the fine mixed trace the sum of the sampled $s$-volumes multiplied by $v_\ell$, with $\operatorname{vol}_0$ counting. Assume $\delta_\ell/M_\ell\to0$ and write $D_\ell$ for its maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth, defined once the fine mass is positive. Put $B(k,m)=(m+1)2^k-k-1$, $\gamma_0=1$ and $\gamma_j=(j/(j+1))^j$ for $j\ge1$.

Assume the following lower-rank sharp bounds: for every integer rank $0\le j\le k$ and continuous ambient dimension $1\le D\le B(k,m)$, each full-dimensional compact convex body with nonempty mixed trace has a point in its mixed trace of normalized depth at least $2^{-j}\gamma_D$ for the intrinsic Hausdorff measure in the dimension of that trace. Then the fine mass is eventually positive and $\liminf_\ell D_\ell\ge 2^{-k}\gamma_{B(k,m)}$. For $k=0$ the only input needed is ordinary continuous centroid depth. If $s\ge1$, or if $s=0$ and $r\ge2$, the displayed limit lower bound is strictly larger than $2^{-k-r}\gamma_s$, giving a single feasible fine mixed point satisfying that sharp target for every sufficiently late $\ell$. The limit comparison alone need not give the sharp finite threshold for $s=0,r=1$.

In the recovery step, an original coarse fiber in $RB_2^m$ containing $w_\ell+\rho A_\ell B_2^m$, where $\rho>0$ and $|\det A_\ell|=M_{\ell,+}$, contains the ball of radius $(\rho^m/R^{m-1})M_{\ell,+}$ at $w_\ell$. If $M_{\ell,+}/M_\ell\to1$, moving only the first $r$ continuous coordinates of $w_\ell$ to a sample point within $\sqrt r\,\delta_\ell$ is feasible for all sufficiently late $\ell$ and loses at most $|P|\kappa_{m-1}R^{m-1}\sqrt r\,\delta_\ell/M_\ell$ in normalized coarse depth. Here $\kappa_{m-1}$ is the unit $(m-1)$-ball volume and $\kappa_0=1$.

pk-intake-relative-ordinary-simplex-dept.relation_to_goal: Ordinary normalized halfspace depth for a convex body with a specified enclosing simplex and exact facet-centroid contacts. The locked problem uses mixed-integer volume and centers.
pk-intake-relative-ordinary-simplex-dept.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $m=d+1$, $b=1/m$, $\Gamma=(d/m)^d$ and $c=(1-d^{1-d})/[(d-1)^2m]$. There is a constant $\delta_d>0$ depending only on $d$ with the following property. Suppose $S$ is a full-dimensional simplex in $\mathbb R^d$ with centroid $g$, $K$ is a compact convex body, and
$$
g+(1-\delta)(S-g)\subseteq K\subseteq S,\qquad 0\le\delta\le\delta_d.
$$
Assume the centroid of every facet of $S$ belongs to $K$. With $\tau=1-|K|/|S|$, there is one $y\in\operatorname{int}K$ such that for every closed halfspace $H$ containing $y$,
$$
\frac{|K\cap H|}{|K|}\ge\Gamma+\frac{\Gamma c}{4}\tau .
$$
In particular, if $D(K)$ is the maximum normalized ordinary halfspace depth and $\mu_K,\mu_S$ are the normalized uniform laws, then
$$
\sup_{H\ \mathrm{closed\ halfspace}}|\mu_K(H)-\mu_S(H)|
\le \operatorname{TV}(\mu_K,\mu_S)=\tau
\le \frac{4}{\Gamma c}\bigl(D(K)-\Gamma\bigr).
$$

The loss estimates below use the same nested inclusion and facet-centroid contacts before imposing the depth radius $\delta_d$. Let $\lambda_i$ be the barycentric functions of $S$ and $R_i=|(S\setminus K)\cap\{\lambda_i\ge b\}|/|S|$. For $0\le\delta<1$ one has $\sum_i R_i\le m\Gamma(1-c)(1-\delta)^{-d}\tau$. Put
$$
\eta=\min\left\{\frac{1}{8m},\frac{\Gamma c}{4\cdot8m\cdot2^{d+1}}\right\},
\qquad E=8m\eta\,2^{d+1},\qquad
L_i=\min\{\tau,R_i+E\tau\},\qquad
\bar L=\frac1m\sum_i L_i .
$$
For $\delta\le1/2$, each $L_i$ bounds the deleted fraction relative to $|S|$ for every affine margin within $\eta$ of $\lambda_i-b$ on $S$. For $\delta\le\min\{1/2,c/(4d)\}$, $\bar L\le\Gamma(1-c/2)\tau$. The point in the depth conclusion can be taken with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i(y)=b+(\bar L-L_i)/(m\Gamma)$.

pk-intake-relative-paired-simplex-depth-.relation_to_goal: Full-dimensional ordinary volume in dimensions d≥3. The theorem uses an actual real center and the two shifted caps with a common normal. The Hausdorff estimate is local in an ordinary affine frame.
pk-intake-relative-paired-simplex-depth-.statement:
For a full-dimensional convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, write $\Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d$. For $y\in K$, a unit vector $u$ and $s\ge0$, put $H_\pm(y,u,s)=\{x:u\cdot(x-y)\ge\pm s\}$ and
$$
p_K(y)=\min_{\lVert u\rVert_2=1,\ s\ge0}\frac{|K\cap H_+(y,u,s)|+|K\cap H_-(y,u,s)|}{2|K|},\qquad
P(K)=\max_{y\in K}p_K(y).
$$
Here $|\cdot|$ is ordinary $d$-dimensional volume.

Let $d\ge3$, $m=d+1$, and $c=(1-d^{1-d})/[(d-1)^2m]$. There exists $\delta_d>0$ depending only on $d$ such that for every full-dimensional simplex $S$ with centroid $g$, and every convex body $K$ with
$$
g+(1-\delta)(S-g)\subseteq K\subseteq S,\qquad 0\le\delta\le\delta_d,
$$
whose intersection with each facet of $S$ contains that facet's centroid, there is one $y\in\operatorname{int}K$ such that
$$
p_K(y)-\Gamma\ \ge\ \frac{\Gamma c}{4}\left(1-\frac{|K|}{|S|}\right).
$$
With $\tau=1-|K|/|S|$ and barycentric functions $\lambda_i$ of $S$, one may take $\lambda_i(y)=1/m+(\bar L-L_i)/(m\Gamma)$, where
$$
\eta=\min\left\{\frac1{8m},\frac{\Gamma c}{4\cdot 8m\cdot 2^{d+1}}\right\},\quad
R_i=\frac{|(S\setminus K)\cap\{\lambda_i\ge1/m\}|}{|S|},\quad
L_i=\min\{\tau,R_i+8m\eta\,2^{d+1}\tau\},\quad \bar L=\frac1m\sum_i L_i.
$$

In the ordinary affine frame of a reference simplex, let $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)$, $L=8(d+1)^3$, and
$$
\varepsilon_d=\min\left\{\frac1{64(d+1)^3},\ \frac{\delta_d}{d(d+1)(L+1)}\right\}.
$$
If the Hausdorff distance in the infinity norm satisfies $d_{H,\infty}(K,T)\le\varepsilon_d$, a minimum-volume enclosing simplex exists, and every such simplex $S$ satisfies $P(K)-\Gamma\ge(\Gamma c/4)(1-|K|/|S|)$. The claim applies in any ordinary affine image of this frame.

pk-intake-residual-covariance-fixed-sour.relation_to_goal: This is a fixed-source coordinate change and moment balance for a cap-cover optimization. The covariance is held fixed during cap motions.
pk-intake-residual-covariance-fixed-sour.statement:
Let $(Z,X)$ have the probability law of normalized summed volume on finitely many compact, positive full-dimensional fibers in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$. Put $V=\operatorname{Cov}(Z)$ and choose $B$ satisfying $BV=\operatorname{Cov}(X,Z)$. The regression residual $R=X-\mathbb E X-B(Z-\mathbb E Z)$ exists, is independent of the choice of $B$ almost surely, and has positive definite covariance $\Sigma$. Under $z'=Uz+h$, $x'=Ax+Dz+e$ with $U$ integral unimodular, $h$ integral and $A$ invertible, $\Sigma'=A\Sigma A^\top$. An unchanged affine cap margin $L=a\cdot z+u\cdot x-b$ then has
$$
u'=A^{-\top}u,\qquad a'=U^{-\top}(a-D^\top u'),\qquad
b'=b+a'\cdot h+u'\cdot e .
$$
Thus $u^\top\Sigma u$ is invariant. The raw cap masses and hinges scale by $\Delta=|\det A|$ and normalized cap budgets are invariant.

For a fixed source, use the actual hinge cover and Fritz–John conditions of c343c9f3dc96957e with the constraint $u_i^\top\Sigma u_i=1$ in place of the Euclidean sphere. Write $(c_i,P_i,m_i)$ for the cap mass and base and continuous moments, $(S_i,P_i^s,m_i^s)$ for the effective section moments, and $q_{zi}=\lambda_{zi}x_z$ for the weighted contact moment on a positive coverage multiplier $\eta_z$. The two mass and base balances are unchanged, and the continuous balance becomes
$$
\alpha_0m_i+r_im_i^s-\sum_z\eta_z q_{zi}
=\alpha_0\Psi_i\Sigma u_i,\qquad
\Psi_i=\int(L_i)_+\,d\mu .
$$

pk-intake-residual-projection-first-exit.relation_to_goal: Auxiliary correction on one row with real boundary contacts and classical Brunn–Minkowski.
pk-intake-residual-projection-first-exit.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex, $d\ge1$, and write $C_z$ for its fiber over $z$. Let $H=\lbrace(z,x):\ell(z,x)\ge0\rbrace$ be a closed affine halfspace whose continuous normal is nonzero, and set $f(z)=|C_z\cap\lbrace\ell(z,x)<0\rbrace|^{1/d}$. Suppose $p=\sum_j\theta_jz_j$ with finitely many $\theta_j>0$, $\sum_j\theta_j=1$, positive $d$-volume fibers at $p,z_j$, and $f(p)>0$. If $f(z_j)>0$, set $t_j=1$ and $b_j=z_j$. Otherwise let $b_j=p+t_j(z_j-p)$ be the first exit from the positive residual projection on the segment to $z_j$. For each index with $f(z_j)=0$, one has $0<t_j\le1$ and $C_{b_j}\cap\lbrace\ell(b_j,x)\le0\rbrace$ is nonempty with volume zero. With $c=\sum_j\theta_j/t_j$, the weights $\widehat\theta_j=\theta_j/(ct_j)$ form a probability row of mean $p$ on the $b_j$. Moreover
$$
\sum_{j:f(z_j)>0}\theta_jf(z_j)
\le c f(p)
= f(p)+ f(p)\sum_{j:f(z_j)=0}\theta_j(1/t_j-1).
$$

pk-intake-residual-projection-stopped-fl.relation_to_goal: Finite stopped process conditional on the specified transition and stopping matrices. Its inequality uses the modified terminal law.
pk-intake-residual-projection-stopped-fl.statement:
Let $C$ and $H$ satisfy the hypotheses of the first-exit correction lemma. At finitely many bases $p_i$ with positive-volume $d$-fibers, write $f_i=|C_{p_i}\cap H^c|^{1/d}$ and $I=\lbrace i:f_i>0\rbrace$. Assume a nonnegative transition matrix $T$ and a nonnegative diagonal stopping matrix $D$ with $T\mathbf 1+D\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1$, $\sum_jT_{ij}p_j+D_{ii}p_i=p_i$, and $D_{ii}>0$ for $i\in I$. For each $i\in I$, $j\notin I$ with $T_{ij}>0$, let $t_{ij}$ be the first exit fraction along $p_i$ to $p_j$, with exit point $b_{ij}$. Set $c_i=1+\sum_{j\notin I:T_{ij}>0}T_{ij}(1/t_{ij}-1)$ and $C_0=\operatorname{diag}(c_i:i\in I)$.

At $i\in I$ let a modified process continue to $j\in I$ with probability $T_{ij}/c_i$, stop at $p_i$ with probability $D_{ii}/c_i$, and stop at $b_{ij}$ with probability $T_{ij}/(c_it_{ij})$ on each exiting edge. Each modified row has mean $p_i$. With $R=C_0^{-1}T_{I,I}$, the probabilities of stopping by the $D$ rule at the original states in $I$ are $W=(\mathrm{Id}-R)^{-1}C_0^{-1}D_{I,I}$, and $W(f_i)_{i\in I}\le(f_i)_{i\in I}$ entrywise. The omitted row mass stops on contacts with zero residual volume.

pk-intake-residue-level-cap-expansion.relation_to_goal: Full d-dimensional raw volume of a single chosen actual cap or compact convex set. Different residue outputs can overlap. No simultaneous center follows.
pk-intake-residue-level-cap-expansion.statement:
Let $E\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex with $d\ge1$, let $r\in\mathbb Z^n$ and let $m\ge2$ be an integer. Write $w_p=\operatorname{vol}_d(E_p)$, $\mu(E)=\sum_{p\in\mathbb Z^n}w_p$, $A_t=\{p\in r+m\mathbb Z^n:w_p>t\}$, and $a_r=\max_{p\in r+m\mathbb Z^n}w_p$ with empty maximum zero. For $0<t<a_r$ put $N_t=|A_t|$, $s_t=\dim\operatorname{aff}A_t$ and $Q_t=\operatorname{conv}((A_t-r)/m)$. Then
$$
|Q_t\cap\mathbb Z^n|=N_t,\qquad
\big|\{p\in\mathbb Z^n:w_p>t\}\big|\ge |mQ_t\cap\mathbb Z^n|\ge B_m(s_t,N_t),
$$
where $B_m(s,N)=\binom{m+s}{s}+(N-s-1)\binom{m+s-1}{s}$. Consequently
$$
\mu(E)\ge\int_0^{a_r}|mQ_t\cap\mathbb Z^n|\,dt\ge\int_0^{a_r} B_m(s_t,N_t)\,dt.
$$
The integrals are zero when $a_r=0$. At $m=2$, the integrand $B_2(s,N)=(s+1)N-s(s+1)/2$ is at least $2N-1$, giving $\mu(E)\ge 2\sum_{p\in r+2\mathbb Z^n}w_p-a_r$. With $r=0$, both integral inequalities are equalities for $E=[0,m(N-1)]\times K$ with $N\ge2$ and for $E=(m\Delta_s)\times K$, where $K$ is a $d$-dimensional convex body and $\Delta_s$ the standard unimodular simplex in its integer coordinates. The inequalities apply to $E=C\cap H$ for any compact convex $C$ and closed ambient halfspace $H$.

$$

pk-intake-saturated-exact-gamma-infimum.relation_to_goal: An exact scalar infimum under unit positive phases, a fixed negative unit, and residual negative coefficients capped at one.
pk-intake-saturated-exact-gamma-infimum.statement:
Let $k\ge1$ be an integer. Consider the laws
$$
P_k(b)=\Pr\!\left(X\ge E_0+\sum_{i=1}^q b_iE_i\right),
\qquad 0\le b_i\le1,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^q b_i=k-1,
$$
where $X$ has the $\operatorname{Gamma}(k,1)$ law and $E_0,\ldots,E_q$ are unit-mean exponentials, with all variables independent. Here $q$ ranges over the finite nonnegative integers for which the coefficient constraints are feasible. For $k\ge2$, the fixed-$q$ minimum is
$$
A_{k,q}=\Pr\!\left(X\ge E_0+\frac{k-1}{q}\,G\right),
\qquad G\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(q,1)
$$
with $G$ independent. These minima strictly decrease as $q$ increases and converge to
$$
G_k=\Pr(X\ge E_0+k-1)
=e^{-(k-1)}\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{(k-1)^j}{j!}\left(1-2^{-(k-j)}\right).
$$
Thus the infimum over all finite $q$ and all feasible $b$ is $G_k$, and $P_k(b)>G_k$ for every such $b$ when $k\ge2$. In particular $G_2=5/(4e)$ and $G_3=27/(8e^2)$. When $k=1$ every residual coefficient is zero, and $P_1(b)=G_1=1/2$, including the empty list.

pk-intake-saturated-negative-equalizatio.relation_to_goal: A fixed-count comparison for balanced scalar exponential laws with unit positive phases, capped negative phases, and a fixed negative unit.
pk-intake-saturated-negative-equalizatio.statement:
Let $k\ge2$ and $q\ge k-1$ be integers. For $b=(b_1,\ldots,b_q)\in[0,1]^q$ with $\sum_i b_i=k-1$, let
$$
P_k(b)=\Pr\!\left(X\ge E_0+\sum_{i=1}^q b_iE_i\right),
$$
where $X$ has the $\operatorname{Gamma}(k,1)$ law and $E_0,\ldots,E_q$ are unit-mean exponentials, with all variables independent. Set $\bar b=(k-1)/q$. Transferring a positive amount from an above-average coefficient to a below-average one, up to the first point at which either reaches $\bar b$, strictly decreases $P_k$. Consequently
$$
P_k(b)\ge \Pr(X\ge E_0+\bar b\,G),
$$
where $G$ is an independent $\operatorname{Gamma}(q,1)$ variable. Equality holds exactly when every $b_i=\bar b$.

pk-intake-saturated-strip-chord-moments-.relation_to_goal: A conditional raw area comparison for one planar three-fiber strip family with two first-order critical caps. No global deepest-point, equal-cap-mass, or third-cap assumption is used.

The chords of $K$ on $x=0$ and $y=0$, with endpoint coordinates $-q_i,p_i$ respectively in the varying coordinate, satisfy $p_i^2-q_i^2=9$ and $p_i>3$ for $i=1,2$. If also $(A_L+B)/2\subset K$, then $|K|>|A_L|+|B|=6L+9/2$.

pk-intake-scalar-envelope-fixed-product-.relation_to_goal: A compact finite-dimensional minimizer description and a conditional reduction of a scalar inequality.
pk-intake-scalar-envelope-fixed-product-.statement:
For an integer $m\ge1$ and $0\le x_j\le h<1$ with some $x_j>0$, put $\rho=\prod_j(1-x_j)$, $E=\rho^{-1}-1$, and
$$
L=\left(1-\frac{\sum_j x_j}{E}\right)\prod_j(1+x_j/E),\qquad
R=\rho(E+h)\left[1-\frac{(E+h)\prod_j(h-x_j)}{h^{m+1}}\right].
$$

Fix $m$, $h\in(0,1)$ and $E>0$ such that $\Omega=\{x\in[0,h]^m:\prod_j(1-x_j)=1/(1+E)\}$ is nonempty. The gap $L-R$ attains its minimum on $\Omega$. Every minimizer has $r$ coordinates equal to $h$, $\ell$ coordinates all equal to one $t\in(0,h)$, and $m-r-\ell$ coordinates equal to zero. If $\ell>0$ then $t=1-[(1+E)^{-1}(1-h)^{-r}]^{1/\ell}$, and if $\ell=0$ then $(1-h)^r=(1+E)^{-1}$.

Consequently, if the gap is nonnegative at every nonzero upper face with some $x_j=h$ in all dimensions, its nonnegativity for all interior vectors is equivalent to its nonnegativity on all equal interior vectors. A counterexample would then have an equal-vector witness of at least two coordinates.

 f_i+\frac{(f_j+f_k)^2}{4}\le2\quad(\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}).

Then $(f_i/\sqrt{q_i})/\sum_\ell(f_\ell/\sqrt{q_\ell})>223/1000=2/9+7/9000$ for every $i$.

pk-intake-section-preserving-support-bum.relation_to_goal: A deformation and weighted-cap statement for ordinary uniform volume. The feasibility argument is local in normal space and gives no admissible deformation for a general singular patch or a compatible mixed-fiber family.
pk-intake-section-preserving-support-bum.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$, and let $u_1,\ldots,u_m$ be unit vectors. Write $H_i=\{x:u_i\cdot x\ge0\}$, $V=|K|$, and $\Phi(K)=\sum_i\theta_i|K\cap H_i|/V$ for weights $\theta_i>0$ with $\sum_i\theta_i=1$. Let $h$ be the support function of $K$ on the unit sphere. Take a nonzero $C^2$ function $\psi\ge0$ on the sphere such that on an open neighborhood of $\operatorname{supp}\psi$, $h$ is $C^2$ and $A_h=\nabla_S^2 h+hI$ is positive definite on each spherical tangent space. Suppose the support points $X(n)=h(n)n+\nabla_S h(n)$ for $n\in\operatorname{supp}\psi$ satisfy $s_i u_i\cdot X(n)>0$ for fixed signs $s_i\in\{-1,1\}$ and every $i$.

For all sufficiently small signed $t$, $h_t=h+t\psi$ is the support function of a convex body $K_t$ with $0\in\operatorname{int}K_t$. The changed radial intervals are in $\{x:s_i u_i\cdot x>0\text{ for all }i\}$ and stay uniformly away from the cutting planes. In particular $K_t\cap u_i^\perp=K\cap u_i^\perp$ for all $i$. Set $V_t=|K_t|$, $\Delta V(t)=V_t-V$, $e_i=\mathbf1_{\{s_i=1\}}$, and $W=\sum_i\theta_i e_i$. Then
$$
|K_t\cap H_i|-|K\cap H_i|=e_i\Delta V(t),\qquad
\Phi(K_t)-\Phi(K)=(W-\Phi(K))\,\frac{\Delta V(t)}{V_t}.
$$
The volume $V_t$ is $C^1$ near $0$, $\Delta V(t)$ has the sign of $t$ for $t\ne0$, and
$$
V'_0=\int_{\partial K}\psi(n(x))\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}(x)>0
$$
where $n(x)$ is the outward unit normal wherever it is unique.

At a Hausdorff local minimum of $\Phi$ subject to the same section traces, every such patch has $W=\Phi(K)$. Group the $u_i$ by their unoriented planes. A positive-curvature patch crossing exactly one such plane at a point on no other distinct plane excludes a local minimum if the two orientations in that class have unequal total weights. If $h$ is $C^2$ and $A_h>0$ on the entire sphere, an imbalanced class always gives such a patch. If all classes balance, $\Phi(K)=1/2$ for every $K$.

pk-intake-selected-circuit-second-order-.relation_to_goal: A necessary condition on every touching finite comparison in an open feasible chart; it gives no regularization of an arbitrary depth minimizer.
pk-intake-selected-circuit-second-order-.statement:
Use the finite-fiber touching deepest-circuit comparison of fact 1fa8cb387c27b040 on an open feasible chart. Suppose $p_0$ is a local minimum of actual maximal normalized depth with value $\beta$. At each old globally deepest site select any one available exact comparison whose ratio $f_i=\tau_{c_i}/M$ is $C^2$ near $p_0$. Put $g_i=Df_i(p_0)$. For every direction $\delta\in\bigcap_i\ker g_i$, there exist probabilities $\pi_i$ (possibly depending on $\delta$) such that
$$
\sum_i\pi_i g_i=0,\qquad \sum_i\pi_i D^2f_i(p_0)[\delta,\delta]\ge0.
$$
With one site $g_1=0$ and the selected Hessian is positive semidefinite. With two nonzero gradients one has $g_2=-c g_1$ for $c>0$, and $(cD^2f_1+D^2f_2)/(1+c)$ is nonnegative on $\ker g_1$. If both gradients vanish, the pointwise maximum of the two Hessian quadratic forms is nonnegative. If exactly one vanishes, its Hessian is nonnegative on the common kernel. These conclusions hold for every selection. The same necessary conditions apply if the touching comparison is supplied directly by actual nearby covers, with a persistent strict gap at the remaining sites.

pk-intake-selected-circuit-signed-dual.relation_to_goal: A necessary variational condition for the chosen regular circuits at a local minimum in a class containing the exact signed perturbations.
pk-intake-selected-circuit-signed-dual.statement:
In the setting of the exact signed local mass theorem, write $D(C)$ for the maximum over the measured set of the infimum of normalized $\mu_C$-mass of closed ambient halfspaces containing the point. Put $\beta=D(C)$, $Q=\beta M$, and let $I$ be the bases attaining this deepest value. At each $p\in I$ choose a finite positive circuit of actual caps
$$
H_{pj}=\{(z,x):a_{pj}\cdot z+u_{pj}\cdot x\ge b_{pj}\},\qquad
\lVert u_{pj}\rVert=1,\qquad \sum_j\rho_{pj}u_{pj}=0,\quad \rho_{pj}>0,
$$
through one maximizing mark in that fiber. Assume every selected cap has old mass $Q$, its boundary avoids every selected $w_i$, and its old threshold function satisfies $F_{pj}(b_{pj}+s)=Q-S_{pj}s+o(|s|)$ with $S_{pj}>0$. In particular this expansion is two-sided and uses the full mixed measure. Define $\kappa_{pj}=(\rho_{pj}/S_{pj})/\sum_\ell(\rho_{p\ell}/S_{p\ell})$ and $A_{pi}=\sum_j\kappa_{pj}\mathbf1_{H_{pj}}(w_i)$. For every fixed real vector $\xi$, the exact signed mass competitors satisfy
$$
\limsup_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\frac{D(C_\varepsilon)-\beta}{\varepsilon}
\le \frac1M\max_{p\in I}\sum_i\xi_i(A_{pi}-\beta).
$$
If $C$ is a local minimum among all actual positive fiber families over $P$, with the fiberwise Hausdorff topology, there is a probability vector $\pi$ on the selected deepest-base circuits such that $\sum_{p\in I}\pi_p A_{pi}=\beta$ for every selected $i$. This holds for every permitted finite selection of points and one circuit per deepest base. The probability vector is attached to that selection. When $I$ has one base, the corresponding score itself equals $\beta$ at each selected point.

pk-intake-separate-surface-logarithmic-j.relation_to_goal: Conditional estimate for an actual physical surface inequality. It does not identify its surface coupling with a tilted-volume coupling or give a numerical depth bound.
pk-intake-separate-surface-logarithmic-j.statement:
Let $dS$ be the finite sum of sampled fiber boundary area measures on the compact physical hull $C$, with endpoint counting measure for one-dimensional fibers. Let $\Xi$ be an integrable actual signed boundary density. Assume the physical inequality $\int\Xi\Phi\,dS\le0$ holds for every globally finite convex physical $\Phi$, as when each such function is an actual common inward speed for this separator. Let $L>0$ on $C$ be the minimum of finitely many affine functions, $L_{\max}=\max_C L$, $k\ge0$, $B=-k\log L$, and $\Xi_0=\Xi-B$. Set $\mu_S=\Xi_+dS$ and $\nu_S=\Xi_-dS$.

There is a compactly supported physical martingale $\pi_S$ from $\mu_S$ to $\nu_S$. For every such coupling and $d_L(w)=L(w)-\mathbb E_{\pi_S}[L(w')\mid w]$, one has $d_L\ge0$ $\mu_S$-almost everywhere and
$$
\begin{aligned}
R&=-\int\Xi_0 B\,dS-\int B^2\,dS
 =k\int[\log L(w)-\log L(w')]\,d\pi_S\\
&\ge k\int\frac{d_L(w)}{L(w)}\,d\mu_S(w)
 +\frac{k}{2L_{\max}^2}\int[L(w')-L(w)]^2\,d\pi_S\ge0 .
\end{aligned}
$$
All terms involving the coupling are zero when the common surface mass is zero.

pk-intake-separated-exact-pair-depth-obs.relation_to_goal: Obstruction to an optimized separated lower bound for actual three-fiber sources. The obstruction concerns the split infima over cap directions.
pk-intake-separated-exact-pair-depth-obs.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $0<\varepsilon\le1/10$, and $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)$ have volume $V$. Put $A=\varepsilon T$, $a=\varepsilon^d$ and $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. The lifted hull with fibers $A,T,T$ at $-1,0,1$ has exactly these integer fibers and mixed volume $M=(2+a)V$, with each fiber of mass strictly below $M/2$.

For $y\in T$ let $f(y)$ be its ordinary raw halfspace depth in $T$, and $P(y)$ the raw depth of $(0,y)$ in the endpoint-only measure, using all closed ambient halfspaces. The raw mixed depth of $(0,y)$ is at least $f(y)+P(y)$, but
$$
\max_{y\in T}(f(y)+P(y))=\Gamma_d V<\frac{\Gamma_d}{2}M.
$$
The mixed raw depth maxima restricted to the bases $-1,1$ are $\Gamma_d aV$ and $\Gamma_d V$, respectively. For $d=2,\varepsilon=1/10$ the separated maximum is $2/9$, the target is $67/300$, and the difference is $1/900$.

\int\psi(n)\Phi(w)(W_j-\beta_j+\lambda_j\ell_j+R_j)\,d\eta_j\le0
$$
holds for every nonnegative continuous normal weight $\psi$ and every globally finite nonnegative convex $\Phi$. Then throughout the canonical hull

pk-intake-seven-base-atomless-and-tangen.relation_to_goal: First variation for the specified seven-base hull, with two separate sufficient hypotheses for convergence of the optimized opposite-shift cap costs. The formula in the tangent regime requires d≥2.
pk-intake-seven-base-atomless-and-tangen.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $T\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full simplex of volume $V$ and centroid $g$. Let $\lambda_i$ be its barycentric coordinates and $\ell_i$ their linear parts for $0\le i\le d$. Set $b=1/(d+1)$, $\Gamma=(1-b)^d$ and $\kappa=dV(1-b)^{d-1}$. At each of the four bases in $\{0,1\}^2$ place $T$. At $r=(-1,0)$, $p=(-1,1)$ and $p'=(1,-1)$ place convex bodies $R_t,A_t,C_t\subseteq T$ of respective volumes $t w_t,t a_t,t c_t$, where $(w_t,a_t,c_t)\to(w,a,c)\in(0,\infty)^3$ as $t\downarrow0$. Take their lifted convex hull and use the sum of $d$-volumes on the actual integer fibers and all closed ambient halfspaces. The auxiliary six-base hull deletes the generator at $r$. Let $q=(0,0)$, let $D_{6,t}^0$ and $D_{7,t}^0$ be the maximum raw depths on the $q$ fibers, and let $D_{7,t}$ be the global maximum raw depth in the seven-base hull.

Assume either of these two regimes.

- The normalized uniform laws of $A_t,C_t$ converge weakly to $\nu,\omega$, respectively, and both limits give zero mass to every level of every $\lambda_i$. Set
  $J_i=\min_{s\in\mathbb R}[a\,\nu\{\lambda_i\ge b+s\}+c\,\omega\{\lambda_i\ge b-s\}]$.
- With $\epsilon_t=t^{1/d}$, write $A_t=g+\epsilon_t B_t$ and $C_t=g+\epsilon_t E_t$ where $B_t,E_t$ converge in Hausdorff distance to full-dimensional convex bodies $B,E$. Then $a=|B|,c=|E|$. Set
  $J_i=\min_{\sigma\in\mathbb R}[|B\cap\{\ell_i\ge\sigma\}|+|E\cap\{\ell_i\ge-\sigma\}|]$.

The displayed minima are attained and can be restricted to compact shift intervals. Write $\bar J=(d+1)^{-1}\sum_iJ_i$ and $L=\max\{a,c,w+\bar J\}$. Then $D_{6,t}^0=\Gamma V+t\bar J+o(t)$, and
$$
D_{7,t}=\Gamma V+tL+o(t),\qquad
D_{7,t}/M_t=\Gamma/4+t[4L-\Gamma(w+a+c)]/(16V)+o(t).
$$
Every maximizing mark on the seven-base $q$ fiber satisfies $y_t=g+t v_*+o(t)$, where the unique $v_*$ is given by $\ell_i(v_*)=(J_i-\bar J)/\kappa$ for every $i$. If $w+\bar J>\max(a,c)$, every global maximizer lies at $q$ for sufficiently small $t$. If $a>\max(c,w+\bar J)$ the unique global maximizer is $((0,1),g)$, and if $c>\max(a,w+\bar J)$ it is $((1,0),g)$.

pk-intake-seven-base-exact-owned-fiber-l.relation_to_goal: A prelimit geometric reduction for identical small contained additions to the planar seven-base construction, with no limiting-shape hypothesis.
pk-intake-seven-base-exact-owned-fiber-l.statement:
Let $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2)$, $V=|T|=1/2$, $g=(1/3,1/3)$, and $\Gamma=4/9$. For $a>0$ and small $t>0$, place $T$ at the four binary bases in two integer dimensions and the same convex body $E_t\subset T$ of area $ta$ at $r_0=(-1,0)$, $p=(-1,1)$ and $p'=(1,-1)$. Their hull has exactly these seven integer fibers and total area $4V+3ta$. Write $q=(0,0)$ and let $A_{7,t}(y)$ be the raw mixed closed-halfspace depth at $(q,y)$. Let $A_{6,t}(y)$ be the corresponding depth after deleting $r_0$ and taking the remaining hull. For unit $u$, let $F_T(y,u)=|T\cap\{u\cdot x\ge u\cdot y\}|$ and let $J_t(u,y)$ be $a$ times the minimum over $s\in\mathbb R$ of the two tail probabilities of the uniform law on $E_t$ at opposite shifts $u\cdot y+s$ and $u\cdot y-s$. Then
$$
A_{6,t}(y)=\min_{\lVert u\rVert=1}\,[F_T(y,u)+tJ_t(u,y)].
$$
For some fixed neighborhood of $g$ in $T$ and all sufficiently small $t$, $A_{7,t}(y)=ta+A_{6,t}(y)$ there. Both local maximizing sets on $q$ are attained, lie within $O(t)$ of $g$ uniformly, and coincide for small $t$. The raw maxima at the other three core bases $(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)$ are $\Gamma V+ta,\Gamma V+ta,\Gamma V$, respectively. Every mark on an added fiber has raw depth at most $ta$.

In particular the result applies to $E_t=\{g+s(1,-1)+tr(-1/2,-1/2):|s|\le L,\ |r+H/2|\le H\}$ with $0<L<1/3$, $H>0$, and $a=4LH$. It has area $ta$ and lies in $\operatorname{int}T$ when $tH/4<1/3-L$ and $3tH/2<1/3$.

pk-intake-seven-base-general-exact-depth.relation_to_goal: Exact seven-base reduction for independently varying contained additions in dimension d≥2 and fixed core simplex. The expansion is conditional on the six-base local coefficient.
pk-intake-seven-base-general-exact-depth.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $T\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full simplex of volume $V$ and centroid $g$. Let $\lambda_i$ be its barycentric coordinates and $\ell_i$ their linear parts for $0\le i\le d$. Set $b=1/(d+1)$, $\Gamma=(1-b)^d$ and $\kappa=dV(1-b)^{d-1}$. At each of the four bases in $\{0,1\}^2$ place $T$. At $r=(-1,0)$, $p=(-1,1)$ and $p'=(1,-1)$ place convex bodies $R_t,A_t,C_t\subseteq T$ of respective volumes $t w_t,t a_t,t c_t$, where $(w_t,a_t,c_t)\to(w,a,c)\in(0,\infty)^3$ as $t\downarrow0$. Take their lifted convex hull and use the sum of $d$-volumes on the actual integer fibers and all closed ambient halfspaces. The auxiliary six-base hull deletes the generator at $r$. Let $q=(0,0)$, let $D_{6,t}^0$ and $D_{7,t}^0$ be the maximum raw depths on the $q$ fibers, and let $D_{7,t}$ be the global maximum raw depth in the seven-base hull.

The seven listed sites are precisely the actual integer fibers, with their placed bodies unchanged, and the total mixed volume is $M_t=4V+t(w_t+a_t+c_t)$. There is a fixed neighborhood $U\subseteq T$ of $g$ such that for every sufficiently small $t$ and every $y\in U$ the raw depth at $(q,y)$ in the seven-base hull is its six-base raw depth plus $tw_t$. All local maxima are attained. The full sets of $q$-fiber maximizers coincide for sufficiently small $t$ and all their marks are $O(t)$ from $g$, so $D_{7,t}^0=tw_t+D_{6,t}^0$.

At bases $(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)$ the raw local maxima are respectively $\Gamma V+ta_t$, $\Gamma V+tc_t$ and $\Gamma V$ for sufficiently small $t$. The first two occur only at $g$ in their fibers. Every added-fiber mark has depth at most the mass of its fiber. Thus
$$
D_{7,t}=\Gamma V+\max\{ta_t,tc_t,tw_t+D_{6,t}^0-\Gamma V\}.
$$
In particular, if $D_{6,t}^0=\Gamma V+t\bar J+o(t)$ and $L=\max\{a,c,w+\bar J\}$, then
$$
D_{7,t}=\Gamma V+tL+o(t),\qquad
\frac{D_{7,t}}{M_t}=\frac{\Gamma}{4}
+t\frac{4L-\Gamma(w+a+c)}{16V}+o(t).
$$
A strictly largest term among $a,c,w+\bar J$ forces every global maximizer into its corresponding base $(0,1),(1,0),q$. In the first two cases the centroid there is the unique global maximizer.

pk-intake-seven-fiber-scalar-allocation-.relation_to_goal: Failure of the scalar guarantee based only on own volume, total midpoint mass and total density ceiling at the prescribed weighted centroid. The rank-two witnesses are valid for the universal scalar infimum and need not be actual midpoint couplings.
pk-intake-seven-fiber-scalar-allocation-.statement:
For $L\ge0$, $0\le\alpha\le L$, define $\beta_d(L,\alpha)=\inf_{F,\eta}D_{\mathbf1_Fdx+\eta}(g_{\mathbf1_Fdx+2\eta})$, where $F$ is a convex $d$-body of volume one, $0\le\eta\le L\mathbf1_Fdx$, $\eta(F)=\alpha$, $D$ is raw depth for closed containing halfspaces and $g$ is the ordinary centroid. Then $\beta_d(L,\alpha)\le\gamma_d(1+\alpha)$ and $\beta_d(0,0)=\gamma_d$, where $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. For $d=2$, $\alpha\in[0,7/8]$, and $L\ge\ell(\alpha)$ one has $\beta_2(L,\alpha)\le136/225$, where $\ell(\alpha)$ equals $16\alpha/9$ on $[0,9/16]$, $4\alpha-5/4$ on $[9/16,13/16]$, and $16\alpha-11$ on $[13/16,7/8]$.

For every $n\ge1$ there is an actual convex body $C_n$ with $2^{n-1}$ binary blocks of seven positive triangle fibers, of original mixed area $M_n=2^{n-1}11/4$, with the following property. At any positive integer anchor of own area $k$, consider all distinct unordered reflected pairs of positive endpoint fibers with areas $a_j,b_j$. Choose any $t_j\in[0,\min(a_j,b_j)]$ and set $\alpha=\sum_jt_j/k$ and $L=\sum_jt_j/((\sqrt{a_j}+\sqrt{b_j})/2)^2$. The supremum of $k\beta_2(L,\alpha)$ over every such allocation and anchor, including the option $\gamma_2 k$, is at most $136/225$. At a noncentral chain base the bound is $7/18$. The scalar guarantee is at least $1/150$ below $\gamma_2 M_n/2^n=11/18$.

pk-intake-shared-inequality-attainment-o.relation_to_goal: The threshold, fixed base and positive limit come from the smallest bad canonical minor theorem. The objective is original closed-halfspace depth and the complexity bound concerns one shared list of inequalities.
pk-intake-shared-inequality-attainment-o.statement:
Use the assumptions and either budget of the smallest bad canonical minor theorem, and let $B$ be one of its selected bases. For a positive integer $N$ let $\mathcal R_N(B)$ consist of positive fiber families with a representation by $N$ shared affine inequalities
$$
K_b=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:n_f\cdot x\le t_f(b),\ 1\le f\le N\}\qquad(b\in B),
$$
where $n_f\ne0$ and $t_f$ is an affine function on the affine hull of $B$. Redundant and repeated inequalities are allowed. There is some finite $N$ for which $\beta_N=\inf_{K\in\mathcal R_N(B)}D_B(K)$ is attained with total mass one, positive volume in every fiber, and $\beta_N<\tau/q(B)$.

For any fixed finite base and fixed $N$, this class is closed under simultaneous Hausdorff limits whose fibers all have positive volume. A sufficiently small perturbation of all shared inequality coefficients of an $\mathcal R_N(B)$ family keeps each fiber positive and bounded and preserves compatibility. The minimum $\beta_N$ is a separate extremal value and satisfies $b_d(B)\le\beta_N$.

pk-intake-shared-plane-closure.relation_to_goal: Fixed-projection finite-complexity geometry with mixed d-volume and null fibers allowed.
pk-intake-shared-plane-closure.statement: Fix $n,d,N\ge1$, finite nonempty lattice-convex $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ and $z_0\in P\cap\operatorname{relint}\operatorname{conv}P$. A family is compatible if its nonempty compact convex fibers are the actual sections of the convex hull of their lifts over $P$. In the compatible class with $|K_{z_0}|_d=1$, impose the requirement that a common list of at most $N$ inequalities $n_f\cdot x+a_f\cdot z\le b_f$, with $n_f\ne0$, represent every positive-volume fiber as their full intersection in $\mathbb R^d$. The class is closed under simultaneous Hausdorff convergence, with no representation condition on null fibers. If every fiber is positive, sufficiently small changes in all the coefficients give positive bounded actual fibers over $P$ with the same list size. The coefficient assertion allows the central volume to change before common rescaling restores it.

pk-intake-shared-plane-corner-fill-stric.relation_to_goal: An actual local shared-plane motion in one explicit three-fiber planar family, evaluated against all actual mixed marks.
pk-intake-shared-plane-corner-fill-stric.statement:
Let $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2)$, $0<\varepsilon\le1/16$, $b=\varepsilon^2$, $a=1+b$, and $\varepsilon/2\le s\le\varepsilon$. Consider the body on $0\le z\le2$ given by
$$
\begin{gathered}
x,y\le 1-(1-b)z/2,\qquad
x,y\ge\max\{-(a-s)z/2,-(a-s)(2-z)/2\},\\
s(1-z/2)\le x+y\le\min\{1+bz,2+b-z\}.
\end{gathered}
$$
It is bounded and full dimensional. Its actual fibers at $0,1,2$ are $A_s=\{x,y\ge0:s\le x+y\le1\}$, $P_s/2$ for $P_s=\{x,y\le a:x+y\ge s\}$, and $B=bT$. The nine shared plane inequalities have fixed nonzero continuous normals. Decreasing $s$ relaxes the five lower inequalities and preserves the other four.

If additionally $\varepsilon$ is smaller than the dimension-two radius in d2f95e21650e61cb, base 0 is the unique base attaining the global raw maximum. That maximum is $f(s)=(1+\sqrt{1+3s^2})/9-s^2/3$, at the unique mark with continuous coordinates both $(1+\sqrt{1+3s^2})/6$. For $M(s)=(1-s^2)/2+(2a-s)^2/8+b^2/2$, the global normalized maximum $f(s)/M(s)$ decreases along the shared-plane fill $ds/dt=-1$, with derivative at most $-1/[60M(s)^2]<-1/240$ throughout the interval.
