pk-intake-shared-plane-depth-attainment.relation_to_goal: The projection is fixed and has a relative-interior lattice site. Null removal does not assert that the smaller projection retains that property.
pk-intake-shared-plane-depth-attainment.statement: Fix $n,d\ge1$, finite nonempty lattice-convex $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ and $z_0\in P\cap\operatorname{relint}\operatorname{conv}P$. Let depth mean the maximum, over actual lifted fiber points, of the infimum of summed $d$-volume of containing closed ambient halfspaces, divided by total summed $d$-volume. If a compatible family over exactly $P$ of positive total volume has depth less than $\alpha$, then for some finite $N$ this depth attains its minimum $\beta_N<\alpha$ in the central-unit-volume shared-plane class of the preceding lemma. At a minimizing family with null fibers their removal preserves the measure and maximum depth and gives a proper lattice-convex subprojection. Otherwise all fibers are positive and arbitrary small shared coefficient changes are actual competitors after restoring central unit volume.

pk-intake-shared-plane-owner-derivatives.relation_to_goal: The moving body consists of a common finite ambient plane list. The calculus allows coincident owner and cap restrictions.
pk-intake-shared-plane-owner-derivatives.statement:
Let finitely many positive compact polytopal fibers $K_z$ be represented by the same nonvertical ambient inequality list $n_f\cdot x+a_f\cdot z\le b_f$, with each $n_f$ initially unit. Also fix a nonvertical ambient cap with margin $v_j\cdot z+u_j\cdot x-b_j$ and initially unit $u_j$. In a joint coefficient direction write $r_f=\delta b_f-\delta a_f\cdot z-\delta n_f\cdot x$ and $\tau_j=\delta v_j\cdot z+\delta u_j\cdot x-\delta b_j$. For a fiber facet $F$, let $O(z,F)$ be its owners, the rows whose equality supports $F$. The one-sided total volume derivative is
$$
M'(\delta)=\min_{g\in G_0}g(\delta),\qquad
G_0=\left\{\delta\mapsto\sum_{z,F}\int_F\sum_{f\in O(z,F)}\omega_f r_f\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}:\ \omega_f\ge0,\ \sum_f\omega_f=1\right\}.
$$
All allocations are measurable. For each cap the one-sided derivative is at most $\max_{g\in G_j}g(\delta)$, where the compact convex set $G_j$ consists of
$$
\delta\mapsto \sum_{z,F}\int_F\sum_{f\in O(z,F)}\alpha_{jf}r_f\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}
 +\sum_z\int \tau_j\,d\nu_{jz}.
$$
On a facet portion strictly inside the cap, $\alpha_{jf}\ge0$ sum to one, and strictly outside they vanish. A proper cap section contributes ordinary $(d-1)$-area to $\nu_{jz}$, and strict full, strict empty and lower-dimensional contact sections contribute zero. On a coincident facet $F$, the section measure is $\sigma_j\mathcal H^{d-1}|_F$ from the same allocation as the body term. If the body lies inside the cap, $\alpha_{jf},\sigma_j\ge0$ and $\sum_f\alpha_{jf}+\sigma_j=1$. If it lies outside, $\alpha_{jf}\ge0$ and $\sum_f\alpha_{jf}=\sigma_j\in[0,1]$. Use counting measure on endpoints and proper sections when $d=1$.

pk-intake-shared-plane-rotating-cap-stre.relation_to_goal: Necessary stationarity in the all-positive attained shared-plane class, with cap coefficients varying in the assigned linear cover. The full-rank centroid can have a noninteger base.
pk-intake-shared-plane-rotating-cap-stre.statement:
Fix $n,d,N\ge1$ and a nonempty finite lattice-convex $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ with $z_0\in\operatorname{relint}\operatorname{conv}P\cap P$. Let a compatible family attain minimum normalized maximal closed-halfspace depth $\beta$ in the shared-plane class with $|K_{z_0}|_d=1$, and assume all its fibers are positive. Denote its total summed $d$-volume by $M$. Select whole critical groups from fiberwise maximizing marks and assign each $p\in P$ to one selected group covering the whole plane over $p$. At most $2^n$ deepest-origin groups suffice on the deepest bases. Assign each nondeep base to its own additional slack group. No group of mass below $\beta M$ covers a deepest base. Each group $i$ has positive fixed circuit weights $\rho_{ij}$, unit initial continuous normals $u_{ij}$, and projected margins $C_{ip}=\sum_j\rho_{ij}(v_{ij}\cdot p-b_{ij})\ge0$ for its assigned bases.

There are nonnegative cap multipliers $\lambda_{ij}$, zero for slack caps, nonnegative multipliers $\eta_{ip}$ of the assigned coverage inequalities, zero for strict inequalities, and one objective allocation $\omega$ and cap allocations $(\alpha_{ij},\nu_{ijz})$ of the owner-derivative lemma. For every shared body plane $f$ the measure $dW_f=(\omega_f-\sum_{ij}\lambda_{ij}\alpha_{ijf})\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}$ summed over its facet traces at their integer bases satisfies $\int dW_f=\int z\,dW_f=\int x\,dW_f=0$. Write $S_{ij},Z_{ij},X_{ij}$ for the mass, base first moment, and continuous first moment of $\sum_z\delta_z\otimes\nu_{ijz}$. For some $q_i\in\mathbb R^d$ and $t_i=\sum_p\eta_{ip}$ the same choices satisfy
$$
\lambda_{ij} S_{ij}=\rho_{ij}t_i,\qquad
\lambda_{ij} Z_{ij}=\rho_{ij}\sum_p\eta_{ip}p,\qquad
\lambda_{ij} X_{ij}=\rho_{ij}q_i,\qquad
\sum_{ij}\lambda_{ij}=\frac1\beta.
$$
For each stressed group $t_i>0$, all its caps carry stress and have a common effective-section centroid on their cap planes. Its base is $\sum_p\eta_{ip}p/t_i$, and its continuous coordinate differs from the $\eta$-weighted average of deepest marks at these bases by a vector in $\bigcap_j\ker u_{ij}$. In rank $d$ the two points coincide and their ambient depth, normalized by $M$, is $\beta$.

pk-intake-shared-plane-signed-moment-ten.relation_to_goal: A factorization of signed trace certificates with an explicit extra signed volume hypothesis for the new facets.
pk-intake-shared-plane-signed-moment-ten.statement: Let finitely many full-dimensional polytopes $K_z\subset\mathbb R^m$ be fibers given by one shared plane list, with a unique owner at each facet, and let caps $H_j$ have no coincidence with any fiber facet. For coefficients $\lambda_j\ge0$, let $W_f$ be the objective boundary measure on the facets owned by $f$ minus $\sum_j\lambda_j$ times its restrictions to the caps. Keep the integer base label $z$ in this measure. Let $V$ be the summed fiber volume measure minus $\sum_j\lambda_j$ times its restrictions to the same caps. Suppose each $W_f$ and $V$ integrates every affine function of $(z,x)$ to zero. Replace each fiber by $K_z\times B$ for any full-dimensional compact polytope $B\subset\mathbb R^k$, $k\ge1$, and keep the caps independent of the new coordinate $w$. On every product shared plane the resulting signed boundary measure integrates every function $a(z,x)\psi(w)$ to zero for affine $a$ and bounded measurable $\psi$. In particular all its signed masses and full $(z,x,w)$ first moments vanish.

pk-intake-sharp-all-facet-self-coupling-.relation_to_goal: Sharp loss under domination by actual marked surface area, for an unrestricted self-coupling with a prescribed common marginal. This is a boundary-measure result and imposes no claims about original fiber volume or stationary depth.
pk-intake-sharp-all-facet-self-coupling-.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $D$ be a centered $d$-simplex with vertices $v_0,\ldots,v_d$ and barycentric coordinates $\lambda_\ell$. Take $0<\delta<t=1/(d+1)$ and distinct $i,j$. Set
$$
K_A=(1-\delta)v_i+\delta D,\qquad K_B=(1-\delta)v_j+\delta D,
\qquad K_M=(K_A+K_B)/2.
$$
Use integer bases $A=(0,0)$, $M=(1,0)$, $B=(2,0)$, and let $C$ be the convex hull of $\{A\}\times K_A$, $\{B\}\times K_B$, and $([0,2]\times[1,3])\times D$. The three named bottom fibers are actual, all sampled fibers have positive $d$-volume and lie in $D$, and the plateau $([0,2]\times[1,3])\times D$ has relative-interior integer base $(1,2)$.

Write $\eta$ for the sum of the actual fiber surface measures, with physical coordinates $(z,x)$ and optional marks given by the outer unit normal at regular boundary points. Let $\mu_A,\mu_M,\mu_B$ be its three bottom-fiber restrictions, of common total mass $s$, and put $\gamma=\mu_A+\mu_B$. The normal-preserving translated swap self-coupling of $\gamma$ has midpoint law $\rho_0=2\mu_M$. For arbitrary weights $\omega_\ell>0$ with $\sum_{\ell=0}^d\omega_\ell=1$, put $W(x)=\sum_{\ell=0}^d\omega_\ell\mathbf1_{\{\lambda_\ell(x)\ge t\}}$.

Every self-coupling of $\gamma$ whose physical midpoint law $\rho$ is dominated by the physical surface measure $\eta$ satisfies
$$
\int W\,d\rho\le\tfrac34\int W\,d\rho_0
=\tfrac32 s(\omega_i+\omega_j).
$$
Equality is attained by the equally weighted mixture of the diagonal and translated swap. This mixture preserves normals, has midpoint domination also with the normal marks, and satisfies $\rho_0\preceq_{\rm cx}\rho$ on the physical coordinates.

pk-intake-sharp-centered-line-radial-cho.relation_to_goal: One-dimensional comparison for a centered section of a planar radial body, including the sharp m=d−2 power-concave lower bound.
pk-intake-sharp-centered-line-radial-cho.statement:
Let \(f:\mathbb R\to[0,\infty)\) be integrable and log-concave, with \(0\) in the interior of its positive interval and \(\int_{\mathbb R}x f(x)\,dx=0\). Put \(c=f(0)>0\), \(S=\int_{\mathbb R} f\), \(I=\int_0^\infty x f(x)\,dx>0\), and \(L=2\sqrt{2I}\). Then
$$
\sqrt{c/2}\ \le\ S/L\ \le\ \sqrt c.
$$
If \(f^{1/m}\) is concave on the positive interval for an integer \(m\ge1\), the lower bound improves to \(\sqrt{c(m+2)/(2(m+1))}\). The upper bound is attained by a uniform interval centered at \(0\), the general lower bound by \(f(x)=c e^{-|x|/a}\), and the power-concave lower bound by \(f(x)=c(1-|x|/a)_+^m\), with \(a>0\). A constant density on an interval with centroid \(0\) has \(S/L=\sqrt c\).

pk-intake-sharp-centroid-cap-crossing-ev.relation_to_goal: A sharp fixed-cap bound under the every-positive-fiber crossing condition. It concerns the actual centroid and leaves caps missing that condition outside its scope.
pk-intake-sharp-centroid-cap-crossing-ev.statement: Let $K\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R$ be a compact convex body with positive mixed length $\mu(K)$ on $N$ positive integer interval fibers. Let $g$ be its true mixed-length centroid, allowing a noninteger base. Suppose a nonvertical closed halfspace $H$ has boundary through $g$ that meets every positive-length integer fiber, with tangency allowed. Both $H$ and its opposite closed halfspace have normalized mixed length at least $1/(1+\kappa_N)$, with $\kappa_1=1$, $\kappa_2=\sqrt2$, and $\kappa_N^2=2N(2N-3)/(3(N-1)(N-2))$ for $N\ge3$. In particular the universal bound is $(\sqrt3-1)/2$. It is attained by the actual lifted hull with fibers $[-1,0],[-1,\sqrt3],[-1,0]$ at $-1,0,1$ and is approached even if all crossings must be strict.

pk-intake-sharp-coupled-fine-hyperplane-.relation_to_goal: Invariance and sharp factor for finite-level hyperplane fractions of a pushed-forward measure, allowing level-dependent lattice offsets after a shear.
pk-intake-sharp-coupled-fine-hyperplane-.statement:
Let a positive finite Borel measure on $(z,u,x)$ be supported on at most $J$ coarse levels $z$, with $u\in\mathbb R^r$, $r\ge1$. Let $\eta_u$ be the largest mass fraction on $b\cdot u=c$ with $b\ne0$, and let $\eta_c$ be the largest on $a\cdot z+b\cdot u=c$ with $b\ne0$. Then
$$
\eta_u\le\eta_c\le\min(1,J\eta_u).
$$
For the pushed-forward normalized measure, $\eta_c$ is invariant under invertible affine changes with $z'=Uz+z_0$ and $u'=Au+Bz+u_0$, where $U,A$ are invertible. With uniformly bounded $J$, either fraction tends to zero exactly when the other does. The factor $J$ is attained by a full-dimensional mixed body for each integer $J\ge2$.

pk-intake-sharp-fine-lattice-hyperplane-.relation_to_goal: An unconditional sampled-volume concentration estimate on one fine level or one cut. The hyperplane may depend on the cut.
pk-intake-sharp-fine-lattice-hyperplane-.statement:
Let $L\subset\mathbb R^r$, $r\ge1$, be a full-rank lattice of covolume $v$. Let $f\colon\mathbb R^r\to[0,\infty)$ be bounded and measurable with compact support and convex strict superlevels $\{f>t\}$ for all $t>0$. Put $T=\sum_{p\in a+L}f(p)>0$ and $M=\int_{\mathbb R^r}f$. There is an affine hyperplane $E$ spanned by $r$ affinely independent coset points such that
$$
\sum_{p\in(a+L)\setminus E}f(p)\le r!M/v,\qquad
\sum_{p\in(a+L)\cap E}f(p)\ge (T-r!M/v)_+,
$$
where $x_+=\max(x,0)$. If the positive sample set has full affine rank, take $E$ from the greedy rule which repeatedly chooses a highest-valued sample outside the previously selected affine span, starting with a highest-valued sample and stopping at $r$ points. For $b=\max_{p\in(a+L)\setminus E}f(p)>0$ the same $E$ satisfies
$$
M\ge \frac{v}{r!}\left[\sum_{p\in a+L}\min(f(p),b)-rb\right].
$$
If the positive sample set has smaller rank, one can choose $E$ containing all positive samples.

For a compact convex $Q\subset\mathbb R^r\times\mathbb R^s$, $s\ge1$, these conclusions apply to $f(u)=\operatorname{vol}_s(Q_u)$ with $M=\operatorname{vol}_{r+s}(Q)$, provided $T>0$. They apply separately to each closed halfspace intersection of $Q$ with positive sampled mass. In the counting case $s=0$, take $f=\mathbf 1_Q$ for compact convex $Q\subset\mathbb R^r$. The coefficient $r!$ in the outside-mass bound is sharp for every $r\ge1$ and $s\ge0$, including full-dimensional bodies whose nonempty sampled fibers all have positive mass.

pk-intake-sharp-finite-concave-sequence-.relation_to_goal: An auxiliary discrete norm inequality for one nonnegative concave sequence, with a sharp constant for each number of entries.
pk-intake-sharp-finite-concave-sequence-.statement:
For every nonnegative nonzero concave sequence $c_0,\ldots,c_{N-1}$ on consecutive indices,
$$
N\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}c_i^2\le\kappa_N^2\left(\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}c_i\right)^2,\qquad
\kappa_1=1,\quad \kappa_2=\sqrt2,\quad
\kappa_N^2=\frac{2N(2N-3)}{3(N-1)(N-2)}\quad(N\ge3).
$$
These are the sharp constants for each $N$. For $N\ge3$, a tent with zero endpoints and peak at index $1$ or $N-2$ attains equality. Over all $N$, $\kappa_N$ has maximum $\sqrt3$, attained only at $N=3$.

pk-intake-sharp-fixed-mass-density-sandw.relation_to_goal: Sharp normalized centroid-tail constant for the specified Lebesgue density sandwich with fixed extra mass.
pk-intake-sharp-fixed-mass-density-sandw.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$, $\alpha\in[0,1]$, and $q=1+1/d$. Consider all convex bodies $B\subset\mathbb R^d$, measures $0\le\eta\le\mathbf1_B\,dx$ with $\eta(B)=\alpha|B|$, and closed halfspaces $H$ containing the centroid of $\rho=\mathbf1_B\,dx+2\eta$. The minimum of $\rho(H)/\rho(B)$ equals the minimum of $(s+2r)/(1+2\alpha)$ over the scalar domain
$$
0\le s\le1,\qquad 0\le r\le\min(\alpha,s),\qquad s+\alpha-r\le1,\qquad
q(1+2\alpha)s^{q-1}\ge1+2r^q+2(s+\alpha-r)^q-2s^q.
$$
Every minimizing pair has $0<s<1$ and equality in the final constraint. It is attained by taking $B$ to be a volume-one simplex and $\eta$ to be its volume restricted to the upper-tail rank bands $[0,r]$ and $[s,s+\alpha-r]$ of a vertex barycentric coordinate. At $\alpha=0$ or $1$ the minimum equals $(d/(d+1))^d$.

pk-intake-sharp-full-sampled-rank-coarse.relation_to_goal: An unconditional ordinary volume and sampled affine rank estimate. It classifies mass by the ranks of whole nonempty sampled projections.
pk-intake-sharp-full-sampled-rank-coarse.statement:
Let $r,s\ge1$ be integers, $Q\subset\mathbb R^r\times\mathbb R^s$ compact and convex, and $a+L$ a full-rank lattice coset in $\mathbb R^r$ of covolume $v$. Let $P=\{p\in a+L:Q_p\ne\varnothing\}$ include all nonempty fibers, including those of zero $s$-volume. If $P$ affinely spans $\mathbb R^r$, then
$$
M\ge \frac{v\,s!}{(r+s)!}\,T,\qquad
M=\operatorname{vol}_{r+s}(Q),\qquad T=\sum_{p\in P}\operatorname{vol}_s(Q_p).
$$
The coefficient $s!/(r+s)!$ is sharp, and remains the sharp infimum if all nonempty sampled fibers are required to have positive $s$-volume.

For any finite family of such sets with the same fine covolume $v$, let $T>0$ and $M$ now denote the sums of their sampled masses and ordinary volumes. The total sampled mass of levels whose nonempty sampled bases affinely span $\mathbb R^r$ is at most $(r+s)!M/(s!\,v)$. The remaining levels carry at least $(T-(r+s)!M/(s!\,v))_+$.

pk-intake-sharp-homothetic-centroid-disp.relation_to_goal: Sharpness for the coefficient in a specific paired endpoint certificate at the own centroid of an actual three-fiber body.
pk-intake-sharp-homothetic-centroid-disp.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, $g=(1,\ldots,1)/(d+1)$, $K=T-g$, $v=-g$ and $V=|K|$. For $\rho>0,\delta\ge0$ the convex hull of the lifted copies $\rho K$ at bases $-1,1$ and $-\delta v+(\rho+\delta)K$ at base $0$ has precisely those three actual integer fibers. Its middle centroid is $(0,-\delta v)$, with $\gamma_K(-\delta v)=d\delta$, where $\gamma_K$ is the Minkowski gauge.

At $\delta=\rho/d$ a closed halfspace through this centroid captures zero endpoint volume. Hence no constant $D<d$ can replace $d$ in a universal endpoint-volume lower bound of the form $(1-D\delta/\rho)_+^d$ times a positive equal-pair budget, with $(t)_+=\max\{t,0\}$. More generally, for $0\le\delta\le\rho/d$ there is a through-point cap of total endpoint volume $\rho^dV[1-(1-2a)^d]$, where $a=(1-d\delta/\rho)/(d+1)$.

pk-intake-sharp-integer-centroid-partiti.relation_to_goal: Bounds the number of positive convex cells, not the number of source fibers within a cell. It gives no lower bound on mixed centroid depth or assertion of a recursive single-cut partition.
pk-intake-sharp-integer-centroid-partiti.statement:
Let $n,d$ be positive integers and let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body. Write $\Lambda=\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, $S=C\cap\Lambda$, and assume $q=\dim_{\mathrm H}S\ge1$. Then $C$ is the union of $k\le2^n$ closed affine-score winner cells that are ambient convex bodies, each cut from $C$ by at most $k-1$ closed halfspaces. Every mixed piece $D_i\cap\Lambda$ has dimension $q$ and positive $\mathcal H_q$ measure. Distinct mixed pieces overlap in $\mathcal H_q$-null sets. The actual centroid of $\mathcal H_q|_{D_i\cap\Lambda}$ belongs to $D_i\cap\Lambda$, and the distinct centroid bases are exactly the vertices and all the lattice points of their convex hull. In particular $\sum_i\mathcal H_q(D_i\cap\Lambda)=\mathcal H_q(S)$.

The universal count $2^n$ is sharp already for $q=d$, even if fractional splitting of the mixed measure is allowed instead of convex cells.

pk-intake-sharp-integer-mean-powered-fib.relation_to_goal: A single marked fiber weight, for one integer coordinate in the geometric specialization, conditional on an exactly integer weighted mean.
pk-intake-sharp-integer-mean-powered-fib.statement:
Let $f_0,\ldots,f_{N-1}$ be a nonnegative, nonzero concave sequence with $N\ge1$ and $m=\max_i f_i$. Fix a real $d\ge1$, put $w_i=f_i^d$ and $W=\sum_i w_i$, and assume that $j=\sum_i iw_i/W$ is an integer. Then
$$
f_j\ge\frac{d+1}{d+2}m+\frac{m^{d+1}}{(d+2)NW},
\qquad
w_j>\left(\frac{d+1}{d+2}\right)^d\max_i w_i.
$$
The last coefficient is the infimum of $w_j/\max_i w_i$ for each fixed $d$ among these sequences with integer mean.

For positive integer $d$, let $C\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body of positive mixed $d$-volume. If its true mixed-volume centroid has integer base $j$, these bounds apply with $w_i$ the positive integer-fiber volumes, $f_i=w_i^{1/d}$, $W$ the total mixed volume, and $N$ the number of positive-volume integer fibers. The same homogeneous coefficient is sharp for actual convex bodies.

pk-intake-sharp-midpoint-capacity-centro.relation_to_goal: Failure of a specified density-centroid selector, even though its reference measure has the full target mass.
pk-intake-sharp-midpoint-capacity-centro.statement: For each integer $d\ge1$, let $T=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:x_i\ge0,\ \sum_i x_i\le1\}$, $V=1/d!$, $g=(1,\ldots,1)/(d+1)$, $a=10^{-d}$, $r=11/20$ and $\Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d$. The hull of the lifts of $A=T/10$, $B=T$ and $C=T$ at bases $-1,0,1$ has exactly these three positive integer fibers, none as large as half of their total mixed volume $M=(2+a)V$. Its mass-$aV$ midpoint measure $\eta=(a/r^d)\mathbf1_{rT}\,dx$ attains the sharp density bound $|A|/|(A+C)/2|$ for uniform endpoint marginals and is the unique midpoint measure satisfying that bound. The centroid of $\mathbf1_B\,dx+[(1+a)/a]\eta$, placed at base zero, is the actual point $(0,hg)$ with $h=(31+11a)/(40+20a)$, independent of the endpoint coupling. The closed halfspace $H=\{(z,x):\sum_i x_i+z\le dh/(d+1)\}$ through this point has mixed mass $V(\Gamma h^d+a)\le(39/40)\Gamma V<\Gamma M/2$. For its base-zero trace $H_0$, the auxiliary cost $|B\cap H_0|+\eta(H_0)$ is at most this same mixed mass.

pk-intake-sharp-one-copy-source-cost-asy.relation_to_goal: Fixed-continuous-dimension asymptotics for two different denominators in the prescribed-centroid model; the normalized optimum is not identified at finite k.
pk-intake-sharp-one-copy-source-cost-asy.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, $B\subset\mathbb R^d$ a compact convex body of positive $d$-volume, $0\le\eta\le\mathbf 1_B\,dx$, and $\alpha=\eta(B)/|B|$. Let $g$ be the centroid of $\mathbf 1_B\,dx+k\eta$. For a closed halfspace $H$ containing $g$, write $v=(|B\cap H|+\eta(H))/|B|$, $q=1+1/d$, and $\gamma_d=q^{-d}$. Let $k\ge2$ be real. Write $\Xi_{d,k}=\inf v$ and $\Xi^{\rm norm}_{d,k}=\inf v/(1+\alpha)$ over all $B,\eta,H$, including all masses $\alpha$. Let $u_*\in(0,1)$ solve $u_*^d+du_*=d$ and set $E_*=u_*^d$, $A_d=(qE_*-E_*^q)/(1+E_*)^q$, $C_d=A_d^{-1/q}$. Let $R,R_+$ be the unique positive roots of
$$
qR^{1/d}+kA_dR^q=1,\qquad
q[R_+/(1+E_*)]^{1/d}+kA_dR_+^q=1.
$$
Then
$$
R\le\Xi_{d,k}\le R_+,\qquad
\Xi^{\rm norm}_{d,k}\ge
\frac{\Xi_{d,k}}{1-1/k+\Xi_{d,k}/\gamma_d}
\ge \frac{R}{1-1/k+R/\gamma_d}.
$$
For each fixed $d$ both infima are asymptotic to $C_d k^{-d/(d+1)}$ as $k\to\infty$, with $C_1=\sqrt3$.

pk-intake-sharp-planar-cyclic-support-ar.relation_to_goal: Ordinary planar convex bodies inside a prescribed triangle, with continuous-coordinate cyclic symmetrization.
pk-intake-sharp-planar-cyclic-support-ar.statement:
Let $v_1=(1,0)$, $v_2=(0,1)$, $v_3=(-1,-1)$ and $T=\{x:v_i\cdot x\le1\text{ for all }i\}$. For a planar convex body $B\subseteq T$ set $b=|B|$, $S=\sum_i h_B(-v_i)$ and $m=S/3$, where $h$ denotes the support function and $|\cdot|$ ordinary area. Then $0<m\le2$ and $b/|T|\le f(m)$, where $|T|=9/2$ and
$$
 f(m)=\begin{cases}
 m^2&0<m\le1/2,\\
 1-(2-m)^2/3&1/2\le m\le2,\\
 1&m\ge2 .
 \end{cases}
$$
For each feasible $m$ the bound is attained by $T\cap(-mT)$. Moreover $6\sqrt{b/|T|}-S\le3\sqrt7-6<3$, with equality in the first inequality attained at $m=2-3/\sqrt7$.

pk-intake-sharp-positive-circuit-triangl.relation_to_goal: Ordinary area and vertex incidence for three specified through-source caps on an actual triangle. Mixed compatibility, criticality, and middle-body shape are separate assumptions.
pk-intake-sharp-positive-circuit-triangl.statement: Let $P$ be a nondegenerate triangle in $\mathbb R^2$ with an interior point $p$. Let $n_1,n_2,n_3$ span $\mathbb R^2$ and satisfy $\sum_{i=1}^3\omega_i n_i=0$ for some $\omega_i>0$. Define $H_i=\{w:n_i\cdot(w-p)\ge0\}$ and let $q_i=|P\cap H_i|/|P|$, using ordinary planar area. If $q_i\le c<2\sqrt3-3$ for all $i$, each $H_i$ strictly captures one vertex and strictly excludes the other two, and the three captured vertices are distinct. In particular this holds when $q_i\le128/279$ for all $i$.

pk-intake-sharp-quantitative-simplex-ver.relation_to_goal: Ordinary simplex probability and facet integration. The facet estimate can be used as an input to separate body-stability arguments.
pk-intake-sharp-quantitative-simplex-ver.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $\mu$ be uniform probability on $F=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:x_i\ge0,\ \sum_i x_i=1\}$, and let $g=(1/d,\ldots,1/d)$. Independently take $Z\sim\mu$ and a uniform vertex index $I$. For $0\le b\le1/d$ put $Y_b=(1-b)Z+be_I$ and $a=1-db$. The largest constant for which
$$
\mathbb E\psi(Y_b)-\mathbb E\psi(Z)
\ge c_d(b)\bigl(\psi(g)-\mathbb E\psi(Z)\bigr)
$$
holds for every continuous concave $\psi$ on $F$ is
$$
c_d(b)=\frac{a-a^d/(1-b)^{d-1}}{(d-1)^2}.
$$
It is positive for $0<b<1/d$ and vanishes at both endpoints. The test $\psi(x)=\min_i x_i$ attains equality with a positive Jensen gap throughout the parameter interval. In particular,
$$
c_d\bigl(1/(d+1)\bigr)=\frac{1-d^{1-d}}{(d-1)^2(d+1)}.
$$

**Facet consequence.** On any facet of a $d$-simplex, $d\ge2$, let $\mu$ be normalized facet volume, $s_1,\ldots,s_d$ its barycentric coordinates, and $g_F$ its centroid. Set $m=d+1$, $\Gamma=(d/m)^d$, $c=c_d(1/m)$, $N(s)=\#\{i:s_i\ge1/m\}$, and $E_d(\psi)=\int_F(N-m\Gamma)\psi\,d\mu$. The uniform point $Z$ and averaged point $Y_{1/m}$ on the facet obey
$$
E_d(\psi)=m\Gamma\bigl(\mathbb E\psi(Y_{1/m})-\mathbb E\psi(Z)\bigr).
$$
For every continuous concave $\psi$ and every supporting affine majorant $\ell$ at $g_F$,
$$
\int_F(\ell-\psi)\,d\mu=\psi(g_F)-\int_F\psi\,d\mu\le\frac{E_d(\psi)}{m\Gamma c}.
$$
The coefficient is sharp, and $E_d(\psi)=0$ exactly for affine $\psi$. In convex form, every continuous convex $f\ge0$ with $f(g_F)=0$ satisfies $\int_F Nf\,d\mu\le m\Gamma(1-c)\int_F f\,d\mu$.

pk-intake-sharp-scalar-trimming.relation_to_goal: A scalar estimate for the volume of the retained endpoint copy.

$$
(r-2\varepsilon)^d\ge\frac{r^d+s^d-(s+\varepsilon)^d}{2}.
$$
The uniform coefficient $1/2$ is optimal, with equality and a positive bracket at $d=2$, $s=r$, $\varepsilon=r/3$.

pk-intake-sharp-simplex-fibers-internal-.relation_to_goal: The equal-weight construction refutes a strict improvement based only on a supporting-hyperplane deficit. The unequal-weight construction gives an exact sharpness comparison for a vanishing unrestricted deficit.
pk-intake-sharp-simplex-fibers-internal-.statement:
There is a full-dimensional empty lattice polytope $Q$ in $\mathbb R^4$ with sixteen vertices, lattice width two, and precisely one affine hyperplane containing eight vertices. This hyperplane is internal, and a supporting hyperplane contains at most seven vertices, with seven attained.

For each $d\ge1$, the product of $Q$ with any positive $d$-simplex has exact maximum normalized mixed depth $\gamma_d/16$, where $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Its only half-mass base hyperplane is internal, and every supporting base hyperplane has mass at most $7/16$.

For each $0<\varepsilon\le1/30$ there is also a full-dimensional convex body with the same base hull and precisely these sixteen integer bases, such that the maximum mass on any real affine base hyperplane is exactly $1/2-\varepsilon$ and the maximum normalized mixed depth is exactly $(1+2\varepsilon)\gamma_d/16$. All bodies equal the convex hulls of their actual mixed traces. Thus the coefficient $2$ in an improvement factor $1+2\varepsilon$ under the all-affine-hyperplane mass deficit is sharp, already at integer dimension four and each fixed $d\ge1$.

pk-intake-sharp-simplex-joint-row-fronti.relation_to_goal: An all-dimensional simplex row restriction on the specified source fiber. It requires strict distinct-vertex incidence and makes no assertion about cap volumes in other fibers.
pk-intake-sharp-simplex-joint-row-fronti.statement:
Let $d\ge2$. On $d+1$ indices take positive $a_i,b_{ij}$ for $i\ne j$, with $\sum_i a_i=1$ and $\sum_{i\ne j}b_{ij}=a_j$. Set $f_i=d[\prod_{j\ne i}(a_i+b_{ij})]^{1/d}$. For every $i$,
$$
f_i+(d-1)\left(\frac{\sum_{j\ne i}f_j}{d}\right)^{d/(d-1)}\le d.
$$
Write $\bar f_j$ for the values after simultaneously averaging the rows and columns over permutations fixing $i$, and put $g=\sum_{j\ne i}f_j$, $\bar g=\sum_{j\ne i}\bar f_j$, $p=d/(d-1)$. The deficit is exactly
$$
d-f_i-(d-1)(g/d)^p
=(\bar f_i-f_i)+(d-1)\big[(\bar g/d)^p-(g/d)^p\big],
$$
with two nonnegative terms. Equality holds exactly when there are $A,B>0$ with $a_i=A$, $b_{ij}=B$ for $j\ne i$, and
$$
a_j+b_{ji}=1/d\quad(j\ne i),\qquad
a_j+b_{jk}=(1-A-B)/(d-1)>0\quad(k\ne i,j,\ j\ne i).
$$
For every prescribed $f_i\in(0,d)$ equality occurs for the normalized vertex evaluations of actual strict distinct-vertex simplex caps with interior common mark and nonzero spanning normals summing to zero.

pk-intake-sharp-simplex-product-hinge-ri.relation_to_goal: Exact sharp-budget hinge geometry for simplex products and continuously unit-normal caps.
pk-intake-sharp-simplex-product-hinge-ri.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a $d$-simplex of volume $v$, and put $S=\{0,1\}^n\times K$ with summed fiber volume $\mu$ and mass $M=2^n v$. Write $H_j$ for the altitude from vertex $v_j$, $\lambda_j$ for its barycentric coordinate, $g$ for the centroid, $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, and $N_0=2^n(d+1)$. Consider finite full covers of $S$ by $N$ closed ambient caps with margins $L_i(z,x)=a_i\cdot z+u_i\cdot x-b_i$, $\lVert u_i\rVert_2=1$, each of mass at most $\gamma_d v$. Each feasible cover contains, for every binary $p$ and each $j$, a distinct cap with own-fiber margin $H_j(\lambda_j(x)-1/(d+1))$ and zero cap volume on all other fibers. Thus $N\ge N_0$, and at $N=N_0$ these are exactly all the caps. For every $N\ge N_0$ the exact attained minimum is
$$
\min\sum_i\int_S(L_i)_+\,d\mu
=\frac{M d\gamma_d}{(d+1)^2}\sum_{j=0}^d H_j.
$$
Every feasible cover at $N=N_0$ has this value. For a regular simplex of inradius $r$ it is $M d r\gamma_d$.

pk-intake-sharp-simplex-product-residual.relation_to_goal: The result gives an explicit normal stress in a fixed-source product model and characterizes the local continuous balance under a common metric.
pk-intake-sharp-simplex-product-residual.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a positive $d$-simplex, $d\ge1$, with volume $v$, centroid $g$ and uniform covariance $\Sigma_K$. Put $S=\{0,1\}^n\times K$ for $n\ge0$, with summed mass $M=2^nv$. Among covers by $2^n(d+1)$ closed caps with continuous normals normalized by the residual covariance, the minimum feasible normalized cap-mass budget is $\gamma_d/2^n$, where $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Isolated canonical centroid caps give a normal hinge stress at that budget with objective multiplier one and all budget multipliers zero. The total hinge at that cover is $M\gamma_d\sqrt{d(d+2)}$.

More generally consider any canonical centroid vertex cap of a simplex fiber, with barycentric gradient $\beta_i$ and centered vertex $w_i$. Suppose its positively weighted contacts lie at the own centroid and the cap has zero actual mass on all other fibers, with zero multiplied section moments from those fibers. Under any fixed positive definite normalization $\Sigma$, the remaining continuous cap balance for a positive objective multiplier requires
$$
\frac{w_i}{d+1}
=\frac{d\,\Sigma\beta_i}{(d+1)^2\,\beta_i^\top\Sigma\beta_i}.
$$
The displayed compatibility holds for all $d+1$ types exactly when $\Sigma$ is a positive scalar multiple of $\Sigma_K$.

pk-intake-sharp-simplex-vertex-averaging.relation_to_goal: Continuous test functions on an ordinary simplex. The statement concerns the simplex probability laws, without a mixed-integer center assertion.
pk-intake-sharp-simplex-vertex-averaging.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $Z$ be uniform on the simplex $\Delta_d=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:x_j\ge0,\ \sum_jx_j=1\}$, and let $I$ be independent and uniform on its vertex indices. For $0\le b\le1$ set $Y_b=(1-b)Z+be_I$. Then $Y_b\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}} Z$ if and only if $b\le1/d$, where the order means $\mathbb E\phi(Y_b)\le\mathbb E\phi(Z)$ for every continuous convex $\phi$ on $\Delta_d$. Equivalently the inequality reverses for every continuous concave test.

At $b=1/d$, there is a coupling $(Y,X)$ of $Y_{1/d}$ and $Z$ with $\mathbb E[X\mid Y]=Y$ in which the minimum coordinate value and its unique index agree almost surely. The common minimum has survival function $(1-ds)_+^{d-1}$ for $s\ge0$. In fact for every $b\ge1/d$, $\mathbb E\min_j(Y_b)_j=(1-b)/(d(d-1))$, whereas $\mathbb E\min_j Z_j=1/d^2$.

At $b=0$ every test gives equality. For $0<b<1/d$ equality holds precisely for affine tests. At $b=1/d$ equality holds precisely when the test is affine on every slice $\{x\in\Delta_d:x_i=t/d,\ x_j\ge t/d\text{ for all }j\ne i\}$, for every $i$ and $0\le t\le1$. In particular the minimum is a nonaffine concave equality test at the critical step. When $d=2$ and $b=1/2$ the whole laws agree. For $d\ge3$ the critical comparison is strict for every strictly convex test.

pk-intake-sharp-weighted-bisected-planar.relation_to_goal: Uniform planar area and finitely many proper chords individually bisected at a common point, with a balance of their oriented endpoints. No construction of such chords in an arbitrary mixed-integer cover and no higher-dimensional stationary-section estimate.
pk-intake-sharp-weighted-bisected-planar.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a compact convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$. Let $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ be nonzero vectors with $p_i,-p_i\in\partial K$ for every $i$. Write $R(x_1,x_2)=(-x_2,x_1)$ and $H_i=\{x:(Rp_i)\cdot x\ge0\}$. If $\theta_i\ge0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$, and $\sum_i\theta_i p_i=0$, then
$$
\sum_i\theta_i|K\cap H_i|\ge \frac49|K|,
$$
where $|\cdot|$ denotes planar area. The constant is sharp. Equality holds exactly when $K$ is a triangle with centroid $0$ and, after dropping zero weights and merging repeated oriented chords, the three $H_i$ are the vertex halfplanes through $0$ parallel to the opposite sides, with total weight $1/3$ on each. A balanced opposite pair, or a positive noncollinear triple with one weight $1/2$, has weighted cap area $|K|/2$.

pk-intake-shell-fiber-directional-exposu.relation_to_goal: The finite binary full-or-zero exposure costs give certified upper bounds. The theorem does not identify the exact optimum of a partly captured trace.
pk-intake-shell-fiber-directional-exposu.statement:
Use the binary simplex and positive shell fiber setting of the aggregate credit theorem. Put $b=1/(d+1)$, $h=1-b$, $a_p=|A_p|$, and $E=\sum_p a_p$. For each fixed core vertex $q$, flip coordinates to make it zero and use $p$ for the transformed outside bases. For a barycentric coordinate $\lambda_i$, write $U_{p,i}=\max_{x\in A_p}\lambda_i(x)$. Define
$$
\Omega_{q,i}=\min_Z \sum_{p\notin Z}a_p,
\qquad
\eta_j\ge h\ (1\le j\le n),\quad \eta\cdot p\ge U_{p,i}-b\ (p\in Z),
$$
where the minimum is over subsets of the positive outside bases for which the displayed system has a solution $\eta\in\mathbb R^n$. That system is feasible exactly when every $\gamma_j,\mu_p\ge0$ with $\sum_j\gamma_j e_j+\sum_{p\in Z}\mu_pp=0$ satisfies $h\sum_j\gamma_j+\sum_{p\in Z}\mu_p(U_{p,i}-b)\le0$. The raw depth at $(q,g)$ is at most $\Gamma_d V+\min_i\Omega_{q,i}$.

Let $\chi_q(a)$ be the minimum weight $\sum_{p\in F}a_p$ over discarded outside subsets $F$ such that $\eta_j\ge1$ for all $j$ and $\eta\cdot p\ge1$ for each $p\notin F$ are feasible. This is equivalent to strict exposure of $q$ after discarding $F$, and feasibility is equivalent to absence of a nonzero nonnegative dependence of the row vectors. Then $E_q\le\chi_q(a)\le E$, and $\chi_q$ is homogeneous, continuous and piecewise linear in the nonnegative masses. Every point of the core fiber at $q$ has raw depth at most $\Gamma_d V+\chi_q(a)$. If $E\le\rho_d V$, the maximum over all actual mixed-integer points lies between $\Gamma_d V+\max_q E_q$ and $\Gamma_d V+\max_q\chi_q(a)$. Along a fixed finite support with $a_p(t)=t\omega_p+o(t)$, the same bracket bounds the lower and upper right difference quotients of the raw maximum by $\max_q E_q(\omega)$ from below and $\max_q\chi_q(\omega)$ from above, respectively.

pk-intake-signed-exponential-arbitrary-m.relation_to_goal: An obstruction to removing the largest-receiver condition from a scalar coefficient-transfer assertion.
pk-intake-signed-exponential-arbitrary-m.statement:
Let $E_1,E_2,E_3,F_1,F_2$ be independent exponential random variables of mean one. Define $X=(E_1+E_2+18E_3)/20$, $X'=(2E_1+18E_3)/20$, and $Y=(F_1+F_2)/2$. Both positive coefficient totals and the negative coefficient total are one. The two smallest positive coefficients of $X$ are merged in $X'$, and
$$
\Pr(X'\ge Y)-\Pr(X\ge Y)=\frac{25}{1173942}>0.
$$
This refutes the claim that merging any two positive coefficients of a balanced signed-exponential sum can only decrease its nonnegative sign probability.

pk-intake-signed-exponential-cap-derivat.relation_to_goal: Exact derivatives of a signed exponential probability on the stated sign stratum, with first derivatives through zero margins and second derivatives in strictly positive coefficients.
pk-intake-signed-exponential-cap-derivat.statement:
Let $E_0,\ldots,E_d$ be independent unit exponentials, $d\ge2$, and set $V=\sum_{i=0}^d c_iE_i$, $P(c)=\Pr(V\ge0)$. Suppose at least two $c_i$ are positive and at least one is negative. The density $f$ of $V$ is bounded, strictly positive, continuously differentiable and log-concave on $\mathbb R$. The map $P$ is continuously differentiable in a neighborhood of $c$ even in coordinates with $c_i=0$. Its derivative is $P_i(c)=f_{V+c_iE'}(0)>0$ for an independent unit exponential $E'$, with $P_i(c)=f(0)$ when $c_i=0$.

With $f$ held fixed, put $\phi(a)=f_{V+aE'}(0)/f(0)$ for $a>0$. Varying only the strictly positive coefficients, $P$ has continuous second derivatives, and for positive $c_i,c_j$ with $i\ne j$,
$$
P_{ii}(c)=2f(0)\phi'(c_i),\qquad
P_{ij}(c)=f(0)\frac{\phi(c_i)-\phi(c_j)}{c_i-c_j},
$$
where the divided difference is $\phi'(c_i)$ when $c_i=c_j$.

pk-intake-signed-exponential-cap-joint-s.relation_to_goal: Joint cap-law regularity in all row coordinates. It includes mixed derivatives in the signed and zero coefficients.
pk-intake-signed-exponential-cap-joint-s.statement: For $d\ge2$, let $E_0,\ldots,E_d$ be independent unit exponentials, $V=\sum_{j=0}^d c_jE_j$, and $P(c)=\Pr(V\ge0)$. If $c$ has at least two strictly positive coefficients and at least one strictly negative coefficient, $P$ is jointly $C^2$ near $c$, allowing repeated or zero entries. Set $g=\nabla P(c)$ and $H=\nabla^2P(c)$. Then $g\cdot c=0$, $Hc=-g$, and $g_j=d f_V(0)b_j$, where $b$ is the actual barycentric centroid of the section $c\cdot u=0$ of the uniform simplex and $f_V$ is the density of $V$.

pk-intake-signed-exponential-largest-mer.relation_to_goal: A scalar sign probability with equal positive and negative totals. It applies before any geometric or mixed-integer reduction.
pk-intake-signed-exponential-largest-mer.statement:
Let $E_1,\ldots,E_p,F_1,\ldots,F_q$ be independent exponential random variables of mean one. Let $a_i,b_j$ be positive with $\sum_i a_i=\sum_j b_j>0$ and put
$$
P(a,b)=\Pr\left(\sum_i a_iE_i\ge\sum_j b_jF_j\right).
$$
Lists of nonnegative coefficients are allowed after zero entries are discarded. If $p\ge2$, $a_i=\max_k a_k$, and $j\ne i$ is another positive index, then replacing $(a_i,a_j)$ by $(a_i+t,a_j-t)$ strictly decreases $P(a,b)$ for every $0<t\le a_j$. At $t=0$ it leaves $P(a,b)$ unchanged. Any tied largest index can be chosen. A zero donor allows only the unchanged transfer.

For all $p,q\ge1$,
$$
P(a,b)\ge\prod_{j=1}^q\left(1+\frac{b_j}{\sum_i a_i}\right)^{-1}
\ge\Gamma_q,\qquad \Gamma_q=\left(\frac{q}{q+1}\right)^q.
$$
Equality in the first bound holds exactly when $p=1$. Equality at $\Gamma_q$ holds exactly when $p=1$ and the $b_j$ are equal. For each fixed positive phase count $p$ and negative phase count $q$, $\Gamma_q$ is the infimum.

pk-intake-signed-inverse-arms-physical-c.relation_to_goal: Physical interval-layer identities for concave profiles and an interior source, including sources below the maximum.
pk-intake-signed-inverse-arms-physical-c.statement:
Let $m\ge1$ be an integer and let $r$ be a continuous nonnegative concave function on $[a,b]$ with $a<0<b$ and $r(0)>0$. Write $R=\max r$ and $\{z:r(z)\ge v\}=[-B(v),A(v)]$ for $v\in[0,R]$. Both arms are continuous, concave and nonincreasing, with $A(0),B(0)>0$ and $A+B\ge0$. Equip $\{(x,z):a\le z\le b,\ |x|\le r(z)\}$ with the planar density $f(x,z)=r(z)^{m-1}/2$. Define $V$ as its total mass, $P(s)$ as the mass of $z+sx\ge0$, and $C(s),M(s)$ as the line integrals of $f,zf$ on $z+sx=0$ with line measure divided by $\sqrt{1+s^2}$. Then
$$
V=m\int_0^R v^{m-1}(A+B)\,dv .
$$
For $s>0$ define the even function
$$
j_s(t,v)=
\begin{cases}
m v^{m-1}|t|/2,& |t|\ge sv,\\
s(m+1)v^m/4+(m-1)v^{m-2}t^2/(4s),& |t|\le sv.
\end{cases}
$$
For $v>0$ off the branch boundaries put $c_s=\partial_t j_s$ and $k_s=-s\partial_s j_s$. Then
$$
\begin{aligned}
P(s)&=V/2+\int_0^R[j_s(A(v),v)-j_s(B(v),v)]\,dv,\\
C(s)&=\int_0^R[c_s(A(v),v)+c_s(B(v),v)]\,dv,\\
M(s)&=\int_0^R[k_s(A(v),v)-k_s(B(v),v)]\,dv.
\end{aligned}
$$
At $s=0$ one has $P(0)=V/2+(m/2)\int_0^R v^{m-1}(|A|-|B|)\,dv$, $C(0)=r(0)^m$, and $M(0)=0$. Terms with coefficient $m-1$ are omitted for $m=1$.

pk-intake-signed-physical-cone.relation_to_goal: Signed paths of actual compatible bodies, with simultaneous addition in the declared convex-field class.
pk-intake-signed-physical-cone.statement:
Let $P$ be finite and lattice-complete and let the positive convex bodies $K_z$ satisfy the sampled anchored Minkowski inclusions. Let $\Phi(u,z,X)$ be jointly continuous for $u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}$ and all physical coordinates $(z,X)$, finite and convex in $(z,X)$ for each $u$. For $t\ge0$ define
$$
K_z(t)=\{X:u\cdot X+t\Phi(u,z,X)\le h_{K_z}(u)\text{ for every unit }u\}.
$$
For small $t$ these are positive compact convex bodies $O(t)$ Hausdorff-close to the old ones, satisfying the same sampled compatibility, hence they are their canonical hull's actual sampled fibers. At a regular old boundary point $X$ with unique outer unit normal $n$, let the endpoint on its ray from an old inball center $o$ be $X_t=o+(1-s_t(X))(X-o)$. Then $|s_t(X)|=O(t)$ uniformly and
$$
\frac{s_t(X)}t\longrightarrow\frac{\Phi(n,z,X)}{n\cdot(X-o)}.
$$
This gives a bounded measurable signed inward speed almost everywhere for surface area, with counting measure on the endpoints if $d=1$. Finite nonnegative combinations of the fields realize the corresponding sums of speeds. Both signs of normal-dependent affine physical fields are allowed. Independent finite cap-normal velocities and, when the scale is interior, either sign of $s=\dot{\log\varepsilon}$ can be appended.

pk-intake-signed-radial-energy-and-covar.relation_to_goal: An interior uniform energy envelope and actual body-dependent covariance derivative on signed radial paths. It does not require cap regularity or a path of maximizing marks.
pk-intake-signed-radial-energy-and-covar.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $N=d+1$, and let finitely many convex bodies $K_z(t)\subset\mathbb R^d$ move through $K_z=K_z(0)$ as $t\downarrow0$. In each old body choose an interior origin $o_z$, and let $R_z,R_{z,t}$ be the old and moving radial functions about it. Suppose $|R_{z,t}-R_z|\le Ct$ and $(R_{z,t}-R_z)/t\to r_z$ almost everywhere on the sphere. At a regular old boundary point $X=o_z+R_z(\omega)\omega$ set $v_z(X)=-r_z(\omega)n_z(X)\cdot\omega$, with $n_z$ the outward unit normal. This is the signed inward speed. Use endpoint counting measure in dimension one. Let
$$
M=\sum_z|K_z|,\quad D=\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}v_z\,dS,\quad
J=\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}(X-g_z)(X-g_z)^{\mathsf T}v_z(X)\,dS
$$
with $g_z$ the old centroids, and define $M_t,\Sigma_t,\Gamma_t$ using actual moving masses and within-fiber centroids as in the invariant energy-only buffer. For a compact $U\subset\operatorname{int}K_z$, write $a_y$ for the unique old parameter minimizing the projective energy at $y$, and set
$$
C_z(y)=\int_{\partial K_z}[1+a_y\cdot(X-y)]^{-N}v_z(X)\,dS.
$$
Then, uniformly for $y\in U$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
E_{K_z(t)}(y)&=E_{K_z}(y)-tC_z(y)+o(t),\\
f_t(z,y)&=f(z,y)+t\,\frac{f(z,y)}N
 \left[-\frac{C_z(y)}{E_{K_z}(y)}+\frac DM\right]+o(t),
\end{aligned}
$$
where $f_t(z,y)=(E_{K_z(t)}(y)/M_t)^{1/N}$. The right derivatives at zero satisfy
$$
\dot M=-D,\qquad \dot\Sigma=(D\Sigma-J)/M,\qquad
\dot\Gamma(u)=\frac{u^{\mathsf T}\dot\Sigma u}{2\Gamma(u)}\quad(u\ne0).
$$

pk-intake-signed-uniform-strip-partial-c.relation_to_goal: An exact cap-wise strip cost with both supporting orientations and no inferred sign from the covariance comparison.
pk-intake-signed-uniform-strip-partial-c.statement:
For the common uniform outward cap sequence and facet selectors $\tau_z$ of the transition-facet covariance theorem, write $S_l=\int\psi(q_l)d\mu_l/h_l$ and $A_l=\int q_l\psi(q_l)d\mu_l$, with $\psi=\mathbf1_{(-1,0)}$. Let $S_{\rm prop}$ be the summed proper limiting coarea and use $dS=d\mathcal H^{d-1}$ on the limiting supporting facets. Then
$$
\begin{aligned}
S_l&\longrightarrow S_{\rm prop}+\frac1{\|u\|}\sum_{\rm supp}\int_{F_z}\tau_z\,dS,\\
A_l/h_l&\longrightarrow-\frac{S_{\rm prop}}2
+\frac1{\|u\|}\sum_{\rm out}\int_{F_z}(-\tau_z+\tau_z^2/2)\,dS
-\frac1{2\|u\|}\sum_{\rm in}\int_{F_z}\tau_z^2\,dS,\\
A_l/h_l+S_l/2&\longrightarrow
\frac{\sum_{\rm in}\int_{F_z}\tau_z(1-\tau_z)\,dS-\sum_{\rm out}\int_{F_z}\tau_z(1-\tau_z)\,dS}{2\|u\|}.
\end{aligned}
$$
The nonnegative unsigned facet density satisfies $\tau_z(1-\tau_z)\le\chi_z/4$ for the actual transition density from that theorem.

pk-intake-simplex-balanced-vertex-sectio.relation_to_goal: Sharp stationary weighted-cap bound restricted to vertex-isolating simplex sections and their complements. Multi-vertex cuts and mixed-integer volumes are not covered.
pk-intake-simplex-balanced-vertex-sectio.statement: Let $T$ be a $d$-simplex, $d\ge2$, and $y$ an interior point with barycentrics $\lambda$. When all $\lambda_i\le1/d$, the pure vertex-side balanced mean $F_d$ lies in $[\gamma_d,1/2]$ with lower equality exactly at uniform $\lambda$; its reversal has mean $1-F_d$. If exactly one $\lambda_k>1/d$, only the section at $k$ is available and the balanced mean is $1/2$. If at least two coordinates exceed $1/d$, no such section exists. In $d=1$ any balanced combination of the two interval caps through any point of the interval has mean $1/2=\gamma_1$.

pk-intake-simplex-capacity-coordinate-de.relation_to_goal: One-sided uniform-simplex row derivatives, including the fixed-support boundary rows needed for column transfers.
pk-intake-simplex-capacity-coordinate-de.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $U$ be uniform on $\Delta_d$, and $\phi_d(x)=\inf_{t>0:\Pr(x\cdot U\le t)>0}t/\Pr(x\cdot U\le t)^{1/d}$. Let $x=(a,m,\ldots,m)$ with $0<a<m$, and write $\beta=(m-a)/m$. In a direction with zero low-coordinate component and high-coordinate components $w$, the directional derivative from positive steps is
$$
\min_{s\in\mathbb R}\left[s+\frac{\mathbb E(W-s)_+}{\beta}\right],
$$
where $W$ is the linear form with coefficients $w$ on a uniform $\Delta_{d-1}$ point. In particular, for the scalar parameter increasing one high coordinate, the right and left derivatives are
$$
D_+=1-\frac{d-1}{d}\beta^{1/(d-1)},\qquad
D_-=1-\frac{d-1}{d\beta}\big[1-(1-\beta)^{d/(d-1)}\big].
$$
They satisfy $D_+>D_-$. At a constant strictly positive row the corresponding derivatives are $1$ and $0$. For every nonnegative row and each of its strictly positive coordinates the two coordinate derivatives exist and $D_+-D_-\ge0$.

$$
v=d b_j e_i-d b_i e_j,\qquad
w=v+\frac{\mathbf 1^\mathsf{T}Hv}{dP(c)}\mathbf 1.

Then $w^\mathsf{T}\nabla^2\phi_d(x)w=-P(c)^{-1/d}v^\mathsf{T}Hv/(dP(c))>0$. Other margins may be zero and the two captured heights may coincide.

pk-intake-simplex-capacity-threshold-sch.relation_to_goal: An optimized row Hessian for the uniform-simplex auxiliary model, including repeated heights and vertex contacts.
pk-intake-simplex-capacity-threshold-sch.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, and let a strictly positive row $x$ have a proper minimizing threshold for the uniform-simplex capacity $\phi_d(x)=\inf_{t>0:F_x(t)>0}t/F_x(t)^{1/d}$, where $F_x(t)=\Pr(x\cdot U\le t)$. Rescale the row and threshold so that this threshold equals $1$. Write $\mathbf 1=(1,\ldots,1)$, $c=\mathbf 1-x$, $V=\sum_jc_jE_j$ for independent unit exponentials, $P=P(c)=\Pr(V\ge0)$, $g=\nabla P(c)$, and $H=\nabla^2P(c)$. Set $\eta=H\mathbf 1$, $B=d(d-1)P-\mathbf 1^\mathsf{T}H\mathbf 1$, and $K=P^{-1/d}/(dP)$. Then the minimizing section strictly captures at least two vertices, $\mathbf 1^\mathsf{T}g=dP$, and
$$
B=d(d-1)[P+f_V'(0)]>0 .
$$
The capacity is locally $C^2$ and
$$
\nabla^2\phi_d(x)
=K\left[\frac{d+1}{dP}gg^\mathsf{T}-H-\frac{(\eta-dg)(\eta-dg)^\mathsf{T}}{B}\right].
$$
In particular, for $g\cdot v=0$ and any real $s$,
$$
(v+s\mathbf 1)^\mathsf{T}\nabla^2\phi_d(x)(v+s\mathbf 1)
=-K\left[v^\mathsf{T}Hv+\frac{(\eta\cdot v-sdP)^2}{B}\right].
$$

pk-intake-simplex-corner-cap-coareas-and.relation_to_goal: Actual ordinary simplex caps with strict distinct-vertex incidence, retaining the coarea scale and dimension.
pk-intake-simplex-corner-cap-coareas-and.statement:
Let $K$ be a $d$-simplex, $d\ge1$, with vertices $P_i$, $1\le i\le d+1$, and $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. Suppose nonzero spanning normals $v_i$ sum to zero and satisfy $v_i\cdot(P_i-y)>0>v_i\cdot(P_j-y)$ for every $j\ne i$. Set
$$
H=\sum_i v_i\cdot(P_i-y),\qquad
a_i=\frac{v_i\cdot(P_i-y)}H,\qquad b_{ij}=-\frac{v_i\cdot(P_j-y)}H\quad(j\ne i).
$$
Then all these entries are positive, $\sum_i a_i=1$ and $\sum_{i\ne j}b_{ij}=a_j$. If $q_i$ is the volume fraction of the cap with margin $v_i\cdot(x-y)\ge0$ and $\sigma_i$ is the section's $(d-1)$-measure divided by $\|v_i\|$, then
$$
q_i=\frac{a_i^d}{\prod_{j\ne i}(a_i+b_{ij})},\qquad
\sigma_i=\frac{d|K|q_i}{Ha_i}.
$$
With $f_i=d a_i/q_i^{1/d}$ and $g_i=d a_i+\sum_{j\ne i}b_{ij}$, the inverse coareas are proportional to $f_i/q_i^{(d-1)/d}$, $f_i\le g_i$, $\sum_i g_i=d+1$, and
$$
d+1-\sum_i f_i\ge\frac1d\sum_i\ \sum_{\substack{j<k\\j,k\ne i}}\!
  \left(\sqrt{a_i+b_{ij}}-\sqrt{a_i+b_{ik}}\right)^2 .
$$
For $d=1$ the two row values are $f_1=f_2=1$.

pk-intake-simplex-exposed-finite-respons.relation_to_goal: A sufficient certificate for a prescribed regular finite menu. Nonemptiness, regularity, and any claimed target value must be checked in that menu.
pk-intake-simplex-exposed-finite-respons.statement:
Take the compatible simplex fibers and marked potential class of the exposed-vertex hinge lemma. At one deepest source take a finite menu of regular nonvertical depth-attaining closed caps $H_l$ through that source, with nonzero continuous normals $u_l$ and positive total coareas
$$
S_l=\sum_{z\in P}\frac{\mathcal H^{d-1}(K_z\cap\{x:(z,x)\in\partial H_l\})}{\lVert u_l\rVert}.
$$
Let $g_l=S_l u_l$ and suppose $T=\{\theta\ge0:\sum_l\theta_l=1,\ \sum_l\theta_l g_l=0\}$ is nonempty. For each actual lifted simplex vertex $X$ exposed in some incident facet bundle put $h_{X,l}=\mathbf1_{\{X\in\operatorname{int}H_l\}}$. If the set of such vertices is nonempty, an achievable efficiency using an actual single positive circuit of at most $d+1$ menu caps is at least

$\max_X\ \max_{\theta\in T}\ \sum_l\theta_l h_{X,l}.$

For each $X$ the inner maximum is attained with support at most $d+1$ and equals $\inf_{v\in\mathbb R^d}\max_l(h_{X,l}-v\cdot g_l)$. In particular an inner value at least $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ certifies a paying circuit.

pk-intake-simplex-exposed-profile-hinge.relation_to_goal: The profile is prescribed and need not be selected or critical. Exposure is at the lifted vertex, not merely on an exposed facet.
pk-intake-simplex-exposed-profile-hinge.statement:
Take the compatible simplex fibers and notation of the simultaneous facet-contact lemma. Let $n_i$ be the outward unit normal of $F_i(z)$, independent of $z$, and let $\eta$ be the sum of the facet $\mathcal H^{d-1}$ measures on the actual placed fibers with their normal marks $n_i$. For $d=1$ this counts the corresponding endpoints. Let $H_l$ be a finite list of closed ambient halfspaces, $\theta_l\ge0$, $\sum_l\theta_l=1$, and
$$
W=\sum_l\theta_l\mathbf1_{H_l},\qquad
W_{\rm strict}(X)=\sum_{\{l:X\in\operatorname{int}H_l\}}\theta_l.
$$
An admissible potential is a continuous nonnegative function $\Phi(n,z,x)$ convex in $(z,x)$ for each fixed $n$, with $\int\Phi\,d\eta>0$. If a lifted vertex $X=(p,v_j(p))$ has no simultaneous representation by other bases as in the contact lemma, there is an admissible potential with efficiency $\int\Phi W\,d\eta/\int\Phi\,d\eta\ge W_{\rm strict}(X)$; the constructed efficiency equals $W(X)$ when no cap boundary contains $X$. Hence if the supremum of efficiencies is at most $c$, every such vertex with $W_{\rm strict}(X)>c$ has the simultaneous anchored representation for all its active offsets.

pk-intake-simplex-facet-contact-volume-a.relation_to_goal: Facet measure forces volume in a simplex, with sharp area for the planar problem. The actual application requires local minimizing caps and common zero capture at B.
pk-intake-simplex-facet-contact-volume-a.statement:
Let $B$ be a convex body in a full-dimensional $d$-simplex $T$, $d\ge2$. For its facets $G_i=\{\lambda_i=0\}\cap T$ put $f_i=\mathcal H_{d-1}(B\cap G_i)/\mathcal H_{d-1}(G_i)$, where $\lambda_i$ are the barycentric coordinates. For every $p\in B$,
$$
|B|/|T|\ge\sum_i f_i\lambda_i(p)\ge\min_i f_i.
$$
For $d=2$, given $a_i\in(0,1]$ with $f_i\ge a_i$ on all three edges, the least possible area fraction is $a_{(1)}+a_{(2)}-a_{(1)}a_{(2)}$, where $a_{(1)},a_{(2)}$ are the two smallest. A single corner cut attains the minimum, with $B=T$ when that fraction is one.

In the compatible three-fiber setting at $-1,0,1$, suppose $d+1$ through-source locally minimizing caps at an interior middle mark have continuous normals forming a full-rank positive circuit and all have zero $B$ volume. Normalize to $v_i\cdot x\ge z$, $\sum_i v_i=0$, so $B\subset T=\{v_i\cdot x\le1\}$. For each proper $A$ cut define $a_i=\mathcal H_{d-1}(A\cap\{v_i\cdot x=-1\})/\mathcal H_{d-1}(G_i)$, and otherwise put $a_i=0$. The first bound holds with $a_i$ in place of $f_i$. If $d=2$ and all three $A$ cuts are proper, the displayed sharp triangular lower bound with these $a_i$ applies.

pk-intake-simplex-fixed-normal-uniform-t.relation_to_goal: An exact gap and localization of fixed-normal minima for arbitrary volume-close replacements on three bases.
pk-intake-simplex-fixed-normal-uniform-t.statement:
For an integer $d\ge2$, let $T_d=\{x:x_i\ge-1,\ \sum_i x_i\le1\}$, $V_d=(d+1)^d/d!$, and $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Put the same fiber $T_d$ at each of the three bases $-1,0,1$, and let $F(a)$ be the closed cap mass at normal $(a,e_1)$ through $(0,0)$. For $0<\eta\le1$ and every $|a|\ge\eta$,
$$
F(a)-F(0)\ge g_\eta
=\min\left\{\frac{d^{d-2}}{(d-2)!}\eta^2,\ (1-2\Gamma_d)V_d\right\}>0.
$$
Replace these fibers by positive convex bodies $L_z$ on the same bases and keep the same anchor and continuous normal. If $\Delta=\sum_z|L_z\mathbin{\triangle}T_d|$ and $2\Delta<g_\eta$, all global minimizing tilts for the new fixed-normal objective belong to $(-\eta,\eta)$. When $\eta<1$, the corresponding three sections are proper whenever the $L_z$ are sufficiently close to $T_d$ in Hausdorff distance.

pk-intake-simplex-fixed-section-corner-l.relation_to_goal: Ordinary fixed-section simplex corner losses with explicit unique-cap localization, including the planar six-ray geometric class.
pk-intake-simplex-fixed-section-corner-l.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, fix an interior mark $y$ and $d+1$ nonzero spanning normals $v_i$ with $\sum_i v_i=0$. For a convex body $K$ with $y$ interior, let $k$ be its volume, $Q_j$ its cap volumes in $v_j\cdot(x-y)\ge0$ and $\sigma_j$ the corresponding $(d-1)$-dimensional section measure divided by $\lVert v_j\rVert$. With $M=\sum_jQ_j/\sigma_j$ and $p=d/(d-1)$, put
$$
f_j=\frac{d k^{1/d}Q_j^{(d-1)/d}}{\sigma_j M},\qquad
\Phi_i=f_i+(d-1)\left(\frac{\sum_{j\ne i}f_j}{d}\right)^p .
$$
A simplex has strict distinct-vertex incidence if the open positive halfplane of each cap contains one vertex and its open negative halfplane contains every other vertex, with a different positive vertex for each cap.

Fix a strict distinct-vertex simplex $T$ with at least one tight row $\Phi_i(T)=d$. For every sufficiently nearby simplex $T'$ (in its ordered vertices) and convex body $K\subseteq T'$ with all actual section measures unchanged and with all lost volume confined, up to null sets, to the $d+1$ regions belonging to exactly one cap, put $E=|T'\setminus K|$. There is a fixed positive threshold for $E$ such that for every row tight at $T$,
$$
\Phi_i(K)\le\Phi_i(T')-\frac{a_{T,i}}2 E\le d-\frac{a_{T,i}}2 E,
\qquad a_{T,i}=\min_j \alpha_{ij}(T)>0 .
$$
Here $\alpha_{ij}(T)$ is the negative partial derivative at the data of $T$ obtained by subtracting the same loss from $k,Q_j$ with all sections fixed. The rows strict at $T$ remain strict, so all rows are strict when $E>0$.

In the plane the geometric premises on $K$ are guaranteed by $C_{T'}\subseteq K\subseteq T'$, where $C_{T'}$ is the convex hull of the six cutting-chord endpoints. Within the inner-body class, retaining the full cutting chords is equivalent to containing $C_{T'}$. For planar row $1$, writing $e_1=f_1$, $e_j=(f_2+f_3)f_j/2$ for $j\ne1$ and $C=\sum_j e_j$, one has $\alpha_{1j}=C/(2k)+e_j/(2Q_j)-C/(M\sigma_j)$ at $T$.

pk-intake-simplex-independent-step-densi.relation_to_goal: Ordinary simplex stationarity for independent absolutely continuous step laws in at least three coordinates. The atom examples record stationary laws outside the uniqueness class.
pk-intake-simplex-independent-step-densi.statement: For an integer $m\ge3$, let $W$ be uniform on the simplex $\Delta_m=\{x\in\mathbb R^m:x_j\ge0,\ \sum_jx_j=1\}$, let $J$ be uniform on its vertex indices, and let $B$ have an absolutely continuous probability density $w$ on $[0,1]$. Assume the three variables are independent. Then $(1-B)W+Be_J$ is uniform on $\Delta_m$ if and only if $w(b)=m(1-b)^{m-1}$ almost everywhere. If an atom at zero is allowed, any mixture of this beta law and the unit mass at zero is stationary. For $m=2$ the constant step $B=1/2$ is also stationary.

pk-intake-simplex-negative-vertex-cap-ga.relation_to_goal: Intrinsic uniform volume on a simplex at its ordinary centroid, with a quantitative refinement of the ordinary Γ_d bound when fewer vertices are strictly excluded.
pk-intake-simplex-negative-vertex-cap-ga.statement:
Let $T=\operatorname{conv}(v_0,\ldots,v_d)$ be a $d$-simplex with $d\ge1$ and centroid $g$. Let $h$ be a nonconstant affine function on $\operatorname{aff}(T)$ with $h(g)=0$. Let $p=\#\{i:h(v_i)>0\}$ and $q=\#\{i:h(v_i)<0\}$. Then $p,q\ge1$ and the closed centroid cap $C=T\cap\{h\ge0\}$ satisfies
$$
\frac{|C|_d}{|T|_d}\ge \Gamma_q=\left(\frac{q}{q+1}\right)^q.
$$
Equality holds exactly when $p=1$ and all $q$ strictly negative margins are equal. For each $d$ and $1\le q\le d$ the bound is attained. If $p>1$ is fixed as well with $p+q\le d+1$, the bound is the infimum and is never attained.

For $d\ge2$, a proper closed centroid cap containing at least two vertices has fraction at least $\Gamma_{d-1}>\Gamma_d$. This bound is attained exactly when one vertex has positive margin, one has zero margin, and the remaining $d-1$ have equal negative margins. In dimension one, each proper closed centroid cap is a half-interval of relative length $1/2$ and contains exactly one vertex.

pk-intake-simplex-own-depth-inner-level-.relation_to_goal: Ordinary own-depth level geometry in all simplex dimensions.
pk-intake-simplex-own-depth-inner-level-.statement:
Let $T$ be a full-dimensional $d$-simplex, $d\ge1$, of volume $V$, centroid $g$ and barycentrics $\lambda_i$, and set $\Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d$. Write $L_\tau=\{x\in T:f_T(x)\ge\tau V\}$ for its ordinary raw depth region. The unique maximum is $\Gamma V$ at $g$. On each vertex-to-centroid ray $f_T(v_i+t(g-v_i))=\Gamma Vt^d$ for $0\le t\le1$. For $\tau\le\Gamma$ sufficiently close to $\Gamma$ the exact level region is given by the simultaneous inequalities $d^d\prod_{j\ne i}\lambda_j(x)\ge\tau$ on $T$. As $\varepsilon\downarrow0$,
$$
(\Gamma/\varepsilon)(L_{\Gamma-\varepsilon}-g)\longrightarrow -(T-g)
\quad\text{in Hausdorff distance},\qquad
|L_{\Gamma-\varepsilon}|/V=(\varepsilon/\Gamma)^d(1+O_d(\varepsilon)).
$$

pk-intake-simplex-product-hinge-inradius.relation_to_goal: Counterexample to a dimension-only Euclidean hinge upper bound at the exact sharp cap budget.
pk-intake-simplex-product-hinge-inradius.statement:
For $n\ge1$ and $d=2$, take $S=\{0,1\}^n\times K_L$ where $K_L=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(L,0),(0,1)\}$ and $L\ge1$. Let $v=|K_L|_2$ and $M=2^n v$. At each binary anchor $p$, the largest mass of a submeasure of the mixed volume with base mean $p$ is $v$. Its continuous centroid body at mass $v/2$ is the ordinary half-mass metronoid of $K_L$, with inradius $r_L$ satisfying
$$
\frac{1-1/\sqrt2}{2+\sqrt2}\le r_L\le\frac12.
$$
For $N\ge 3\cdot 2^n$ and the sharp cap budget $\gamma_2 v$, the continuously unit-normal hinge minimum satisfies
$$
\frac{\Psi_{\min}}{M r_L}
=\frac{8}{81r_L}\left(L+1+\frac{L}{\sqrt{L^2+1}}\right)
\ge \frac{16L}{81}.
$$
Thus even after uniform continuous scaling to $r_L=1$ there is no dimension-only upper bound for $\Psi_{\min}/(M r_L)$.

pk-intake-simplex-section-noncentral-coo.relation_to_goal: An incidence constraint for the actual centroid of a simplex section.
pk-intake-simplex-section-noncentral-coo.statement: Let $d\ge2$ and let $c\cdot U=0$ be a proper section of the uniform barycentric simplex, with centroid $b$. Suppose the signed exponential sum $V=\sum_jc_jE_j$ for independent unit exponentials has a positive $C^1$ log-concave density. Then all indices with $b_j>1/d$ have the same strict sign of $c_j$. If $c_j=0$ then $b_j=1/d$. The hypotheses hold in particular for every proper minimizing section of a strictly positive uniform-simplex capacity row.

pk-intake-simplex-simultaneous-facet-con.relation_to_goal: An exact contact test for compatible common-normal simplex fibers; no depth or selected-circuit lower bound.
pk-intake-simplex-simultaneous-facet-con.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty finite set, and let the full-dimensional fibers $K_z$ at $z\in P$ be the actual sampled fibers of a convex set $C$. Fix the affine barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$ of a nondegenerate simplex in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, and assume

$K_z=\{x:\lambda_i(x)\ge b_i(z)\ \forall i\},\qquad 1-\sum_i b_i(z)>0.$

Write $v_j(z)$ for the vertex opposite facet $F_j(z)$, and let $B_i=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times F_i(z))$. For $p\in P$, the following are equivalent:
1. $(p,v_j(p))$ is not a vertex of some $B_i$ with $i\ne j$.
2. It is not a vertex of any $B_i$ with $i\ne j$.
3. There are other bases $z_r\ne p$ and positive weights $t_r$ summing to one such that

$p=\sum_r t_r z_r,\qquad b_l(p)=\sum_r t_r b_l(z_r)\quad\text{for every }l\ne j.$

In particular, the same representation works for all $d$ active offsets. For each $l\ne j$, the continuous-projection offset $\inf_{x\in C_z}\lambda_l(x)$ is affine on the convex hull of these $z_r$.

pk-intake-simplex-stochastic-common-cent.relation_to_goal: A structural row selection at a simplex-capacity maximum, with a nonunit capacity vector and no row-rank assumption.
pk-intake-simplex-stochastic-common-cent.statement: Let $d\ge2$ and $m=d+1$. For uniform barycentric $U$ on $\Delta_d=\{u\ge0:\sum_j u_j=1\}$ define the row capacity $\phi_d(x)=\inf_{t>0:\Pr(x\cdot U\le t)>0}t/\Pr(x\cdot U\le t)^{1/d}$. Fix positive weights $c_i$ on the $m$ rows of nonnegative $m$-square column-stochastic matrices and let $H(X)=\sum_i c_i\phi_d(X_i)$. Suppose a local maximizer $X$ has a strictly positive row and its capacity vector is not a standard unit vector. Every strictly positive row has a proper minimizing threshold and all such rows share an actual normalized-section-volume centroid $b$. Each nonzero nonfull row has a unique zero at some column $h$ and $b_j\le1/d$ for all $j\ne h$. At least one strictly positive row has a minimizing cap strictly capturing two vertices with $b_j\le1/d$.

pk-intake-simplex-stochastic-full-row-ex.relation_to_goal: All d≥2 for least-active positive-weight square stochastic maxima with a nonunit capacity vector. No exclusion of every lower-rank case.
pk-intake-simplex-stochastic-full-row-ex.statement: Let $d\ge2$ and $m=d+1$. For uniform barycentric $U$ on $\Delta_d=\{u\ge0:\sum_j u_j=1\}$ define the row capacity $\phi_d(x)=\inf_{t>0:\Pr(x\cdot U\le t)>0}t/\Pr(x\cdot U\le t)^{1/d}$. Let $X$ be a global maximizer of $H$ with the fewest nonzero rows, and suppose its capacity vector is not a standard unit vector. If $X$ has a strictly positive row, then its number $k$ of nonzero rows is at most $d$. If the full rows' common actual centroid satisfies $b_j\le1/d$ for every $j$, and there are $f$ strictly positive rows, then $k+f\le d+1$.

pk-intake-simplex-strict-support-radial-.relation_to_goal: A local sufficient condition requiring strict lower contact in every facet mark and a through-source profile; no assertion that such a base or an appropriate source always exists.
pk-intake-simplex-strict-support-radial-.statement:
Let $K_z$, $F_i(z)$, $n_i$, $\eta$ and the admissible potentials be as in the finite marked face-quota theorem. Fix $p\in P$ and suppose that for every $i$ there exists $a_i\in\mathbb R^n$ such that

$b_i(z)>b_i(p)+a_i\cdot(z-p)\quad(z\ne p).$

For every $y\in\operatorname{int}K_p$ there is an admissible potential equal to $n\cdot(x-y)$ on the actual marked boundary of $K_p$ and zero on every other sampled boundary. Its denominator equals $d|K_p|$. For any normalized finite profile $W=\sum_l\theta_l\mathbf1_{H_l}$ of closed ambient halfspaces with boundary through $(p,y)$, its efficiency is exactly

$\sum_l\theta_l\frac{|\{x\in K_p:(p,x)\in H_l\}|}{|K_p|}.$

This is at least the ordinary normalized depth of $y$ in $K_p$. In particular, it is at least $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ for the own-fiber centroid or any mark with ordinary depth at least $\Gamma_d$.

pk-intake-simplex-vertex-section-balance.relation_to_goal: Ordinary Euclidean simplex volume and actual vertex-isolating sections. The strict tetrahedral specialization is already covered; this result includes all dimensions d≥2, noncentral points with an available cap, and endpoint sections.
pk-intake-simplex-vertex-section-balance.statement:
Let $T$ be a $d$-simplex, $d\ge2$, and let $y$ have interior barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i>0$ for $0\le i\le d$. A plane with actual section centroid $y$ and only vertex $i$ strictly on its cap side exists exactly when $\lambda_j\le1/d$ for every $j\ne i$, and is unique in that orientation. It meets the edge from $i$ to $j$ at parameter $d\lambda_j$, allowing an endpoint. Its cap fraction is $f_i=d^d\prod_{j\ne i}\lambda_j$. For varying barycentrics $\xi$, put $u_i=\nabla(d-\sum_{j\ne i}\xi_j/\lambda_j)$, with gradient taken in the affine hull. The inward unit normal multiplied by section area and divided by $|T|$ is $f_i u_i$.

If all $\lambda_i\le1/d$, set $t_i=1-d\lambda_i$ and $D=\sum_i\lambda_i t_i=1-d\sum_i\lambda_i^2>0$. The effective section vectors have rank $d$. The unique nonnegative probability weights on the vertex-side caps with $\sum_i\theta_i f_i u_i=0$ are $\theta_i=\lambda_i t_i/D$. Their mean cap fraction is
$$
F_d=\frac{d^d\prod_i\lambda_i}{D}
=\frac{\prod_i(1-t_i)}{2\sum_{i<j}t_i t_j}.
$$

pk-intake-simultaneous-cap-profile-and-c.relation_to_goal: Uses the same actual baseline for each increasing Boolean profile. The planar specialization uses exact common raw ambient cap masses and all the corresponding middle traces. No center selection is required.
pk-intake-simultaneous-cap-profile-and-c.statement:
Let $A,B,K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be full-dimensional convex bodies with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$, let $P\subseteq A$ be nonempty compact with $\dim\operatorname{aff}P<d$, and let $v_i\cdot b\le1$ for every $b\in B$ and $i=1,\dots,s$. Write $\sigma_i(x)=\mathbf1_{\{v_i\cdot x<0\}}$ and $\rho_i(a)=\mathbf1_{\{v_i\cdot a<-1\}}$. For every coordinatewise nondecreasing $\Psi:\{0,1\}^s\to[0,\infty)$, the same baseline $P+B$ gives
$$
2^d\int_K\Psi(\sigma)\,dx
\ge \int_{P+B}\Psi(\sigma)\,dx+\int_A\Psi(\rho)\,da.
$$
This includes unions, intersections, and positive excess above a threshold for the number of missed caps. For compact mixed-lattice source sets on one common integer parity class and finite source measure $\mathcal H_q(A)$, with Borel $K$ containing all actual midpoints, the factor is $2^q$, the integrals use $\mathcal H_q$, and the final integral is over $A\setminus\operatorname{aff}P$.

In the planar case with three nonzero spanning normals $v_0+v_1+v_2=0$, suppose the three caps $v_i\cdot x-z\ge0$ each have raw mixed area $Q$ in the actual fibers $A,K,B$ at $-1,0,1$. Put $k=|K|$, $U_i=|A\cap\{v_i\cdot x\ge-1\}|$, and $R_i(A)=A\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{v_j\cdot x<-1\}$. For every such $P$ of affine dimension at most one,
$$
4(2k-3Q+\sum_i U_i)
\ge \sum_i |(P+B)\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{v_j\cdot x<0\}|+\sum_i|R_i(A)|.
$$

pk-intake-single-parity-depth-retention.relation_to_goal: Compares two sampling rules and two admissible sets for the same full-dimensional body, allowing a codimension-one fine hull. The fine depth is at least $\gamma_s/2^m$, since $2m\le2^m$, and hence exceeds even the sharp ambient fine target $\gamma_s/2^{m+1}$. The locked conjecture concerns one sampling law and a lower bound in terms of its own mass.
pk-intake-single-parity-depth-retention.statement:
Let $m,s\ge1$ be integers, let $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, and let $K\subset\mathbb R^s$ be a full-dimensional simplex of volume $V$ and centroid $c$. Put $\gamma_s=(s/(s+1))^s$, $Q_m=\{p\in\mathbb R^m:\sum_i |p_i|\le1\}$, $g(p)=(1+\sum_i p_i)/2$, and
$$
C=\{(p,u,x)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^s:
p\in Q_m,\ |u-g(p)|\le\varepsilon,\ x\in K\}.
$$
The body $C$ is full-dimensional. The coarse rule requires $p\in\mathbb Z^m$, with admissible set $S_{\mathrm c}=C\cap(\mathbb Z^m\times\mathbb R^{1+s})$ and measure $\mathcal H_{s+1}|_{S_{\mathrm c}}$. The fine rule additionally requires $u\in\mathbb Z$, with admissible set $S_{\mathrm f}=C\cap(\mathbb Z^{m+1}\times\mathbb R^s)$ and measure $\mathcal H_s|_{S_{\mathrm f}}$. For each rule normalize its measure by its own total mass. Define its maximum depth as the maximum over its admissible set of the infimum of normalized mass of all closed ambient halfspaces containing the point.

The coarse rule has $2m+1$ fibers of mass $2\varepsilon V$ and maximum depth $D_{\mathrm c}=\gamma_s$, attained at $(0,1/2,c)$. The fine rule has exactly $2m$ fibers of mass $V$, at $(e_i,1)$ and $(-e_i,0)$ for $1\le i\le m$, and maximum depth $D_{\mathrm f}=\gamma_s/(2m)$, attained at the centroid of each fiber. The ambient normalized laws are mutually singular. After projection to $(p,x)$, their total variation distance, defined by the supremum over measurable sets, is exactly $1/(2m+1)$, the coarse probability of the omitted base $p=0$.

The affine span of the fine bases has dimension $m$. Its integer points project bijectively to the odd-sum coset of the index-two even-sum sublattice of $\mathbb Z^m$. The fine mixed hull is $\operatorname{conv}(S_{\mathrm f})=\{(p,g(p),x):p\in Q_m,\ x\in K\}$ and has codimension one in $C$. Replacing $C$ by this hull preserves the fine set and fine measure and reduces the original coarse $\mathcal H_{s+1}$ mass to zero.

Thus for fixed $s$ and $\varepsilon$, a single added integer condition of projected index two gives $D_{\mathrm f}/D_{\mathrm c}=1/(2m)\to0$ with projected total variation tending to zero. In particular there is no positive dimension-independent retention factor for this comparison, even when the omitted coarse base marginal mass is arbitrarily small.

pk-intake-six-base-identical-weak-point-.relation_to_goal: An exact local weak-limit obstruction on the six specified bases. The accepted seven-base global obstruction concerns a different source.
pk-intake-six-base-identical-weak-point-.statement: Let $T$ be a full-dimensional $d$-simplex, $d\ge2$, of volume $V$ and centroid $g$, and put $\Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d$. If the added body is $g+r_t(T-g)$ with $r_t^dV=ta$, the exact local raw mixed closed-halfspace depth maximum at base $q=(0,0)$ is $\Gamma V+2\Gamma ta$. If instead the added body is a homothet of a fixed full-dimensional centrally symmetric body about $g$ with the same volume, the exact local maximum is $\Gamma V+ta$ whenever that homothet is contained in $T$. Both constructions are possible for all sufficiently small $t>0$, have the same masses, and the normalized laws of both additions converge to $\delta_g$. pk-intake-six-base-opposite-trace-finite.relation_to_goal: An exact all-shift and all-normal reduction at one actual core fiber, with a uniform finite bound on the realizing base coefficients.
pk-intake-six-base-opposite-trace-finite.statement:
Let $T$ be a full $d$-simplex, $d\ge2$, and place $T$ at each binary base in two integer dimensions. Place convex bodies $A_t,C_t\subseteq T$ of volumes $ta,tc$, with $t,a,c>0$, at $p=(-1,1)$ and $p'=(1,-1)$, and form the convex hull. It has exactly the six designated integer fibers. Use the sum of the $d$-volumes on these fibers and let $\nu_t,\omega_t$ be the normalized uniform laws of $A_t,C_t$. For $q=(0,0)$, $y\in T$, and a unit vector $u$, set $F_T(y,u)=|T\cap\{u\cdot x\ge u\cdot y\}|$ and
$$
J_t(u,y)=\min_{s\in\mathbb R}
\bigl[a\nu_t\{u\cdot x\ge u\cdot y+s\}
+c\omega_t\{u\cdot x\ge u\cdot y-s\}\bigr].
$$
The raw mixed closed-halfspace depth of $(q,y)$ equals $\min_{\lVert u\rVert=1}[F_T(y,u)+tJ_t(u,y)]$. With $D=\operatorname{diam}T$, $L=D+1$, and $K=D+L/2+1$, the shifts can be restricted to $|s|\le L$. For each such shift the base coefficient $(-K+s/2,-K-s/2)$ realizes the two endpoint shifts and excludes the three unwanted core fibers with margin at least one. The direction and shift minima and the maximum over $y\in T$ are attained.

pk-intake-six-base-partial-tail-first-va.relation_to_goal: First variation of the local absolute depth maximum at the designated actual core fiber, retaining optimized proper tail allocations and every maximizing selection.
pk-intake-six-base-partial-tail-first-va.statement:
Let $T\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional simplex, $d\ge2$, of volume $V$ and centroid $g$. Put $m=d+1$, $b=1/m$, $h=d/m$, $\Gamma=h^d$, and $\kappa=dVh^{d-1}$. Write $\lambda_i$ and $\ell_i$ for the barycentric coordinates and their linear parts. Form the six-base hull by placing $T$ at the four binary bases and convex bodies $A_t,C_t\subseteq T$ of volumes $ta,tc$ at $(-1,1),(1,-1)$ respectively, with $a,c>0$ fixed and $t\downarrow0$. Suppose the respective normalized uniform laws $\nu_t,\omega_t$ converge weakly to $\nu,\omega$, and both limits give zero mass to every level set of every $\lambda_i$. Define
$$
J_i=\min_{|s|\le2}\bigl[a\nu\{\lambda_i\ge b+s\}+c\omega\{\lambda_i\ge b-s\}\bigr],
\qquad \bar J=\frac1m\sum_i J_i.
$$
The attained maximum raw mixed closed-halfspace depth on the fiber at $q=(0,0)$ is $D_t^q=\Gamma V+t\bar J+o(t)$. Every maximizing point on that fiber satisfies $y_t=g+tv_*+o(t)$, where the unique $v_*$ solves $\ell_i(v_*)=(J_i-\bar J)/\kappa$ for all $i$. Equivalently $\max_v\min_i[J_i-\kappa\ell_i(v)]=\bar J$, with unique maximizer $v_*$.

pk-intake-slab-simplex-large-subbody-dep.statement:

m=\frac{|L|}{V}=\left(\frac{83}{100}\right)^4-\left(\frac{800001}{1000000}\right)^4.

Set $Q=m^{-1/4}$, $r=2-Q$, $A=rL$, $C_+=QL$, and $a=(2m^{1/4}-1)^4$. Let $K$ be the convex hull of the lifts of $A,B,C_+$ at levels $-1,0,1$, respectively. Its integer fibers are precisely $A,B,C_+$ with masses $aV,V,V$ and $0<a<10^{-8}$.

e=\frac{(83/400-h/5)a}{1+a},\qquad \frac a5\le e\le\frac{83a}{400}.

Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Every closed ambient halfspace containing $(0,c)$ has $\mu_{K'}$-mass at least $\Gamma_4(1+a)V$. The normalized depth of $(0,c)$ in $K'$ is at least $\Gamma_4$, and its normalized depth in $K$ is at least $\Gamma_4(1+a)/(2+a)>\Gamma_4/2$.

For an open parameter domain with linear derivatives, every selection of these response functionals, one for each old deepest base, has zero in its convex hull. The same holds if each base's available rows are replaced by their closed convex hull. When there is just one deepest base, each of its available response functionals vanishes identically in this open linear setting.

pk-intake-smooth-five-fiber-nonhomotheti.relation_to_goal: Counterexample to a finite stable-contact subdivision and to homothetic classification of minimal longer tensor dependencies.
pk-intake-smooth-five-fiber-nonhomotheti.statement: There is a full-dimensional compact convex body in $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2$ with exactly five integer fibers indexed by $P=\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}$, all with smooth support functions $h_z$ and strictly positive curvature radii, with the following properties. On a closed normal arc $I$ of length in $(0,\pi)$ let $B_z$ be the solution of $B_z''+B_z=0$ with the same endpoint values as $h_z$. The residuals $f_z=h_z-B_z$ span dimension two. The five tensors $(1,z)\otimes f_z$ have rank four, every proper subset is independent, and their unique dependence up to scale has coefficients $(1,-4,6,-4,1)$ in base order. The lift $(1,z)$ spans all scalar coordinates preserving all anchored barycentric representations on $P$. In addition, no finite subdivision of $I$ into intervals on which each nontrivial Jensen gap vanishes identically or is strictly positive throughout the interior is possible.

pk-intake-smooth-triangle-product-menu-e.relation_to_goal: The result concerns a specified actual menu of a fixed body with normalized smooth depth tending to 13/36. The target constant 1/9 here is lower, and menus with different tilts need not have this efficiency.
pk-intake-smooth-triangle-product-menu-e.statement:
Use the triangle product, actual unique deepest mark and three-cap balanced menu of the positive-width triangle-product singleton theorem. Attach the outward normal to each fiber edge and let $\eta$ be the sum of the four edge arclength measures on this marked bundle. The boundary profile $W_{\epsilon,h}$ is the average of the three cap kernels. Let $W^0$ be the own-fiber average of the three ordinary canonical vertex caps at the centroid, and let $\eta_{\epsilon,h}$ be the maximum over own edges of the fraction of edge length on which the own restriction of $W_{\epsilon,h}$ differs from $W^0$. Then $\eta_{\epsilon,h}\to0$. For every finite nonnegative normal-dependent field $\Phi(n,z,x)$ convex in $(z,x)$ at fixed normal and with positive denominator,
$$
\frac{\int\Phi W_{\epsilon,h}\,d\eta}{\int\Phi\,d\eta}
\le\frac{13}{36}+\frac{\eta_{\epsilon,h}}2
<\frac49
$$
for all sufficiently small positive $\epsilon,h$. The supremum tends to $13/36$, as does the normalized smooth depth. This applies in particular to the actual tied projective-energy buffer of 32418f8d50e792af on the same product.
