pk-intake-smoothed-cap-normal-hessian-an.relation_to_goal: A second-order necessary condition for the actual normal of a smoothed fixed-body fixed-source cap, including positive-area supporting strip endpoints.
pk-intake-smoothed-cap-normal-hessian-an.statement:
Let $\mu$ sum $d$-volume on finitely many compact positive $d$-dimensional convex fibers, $d\ge1$, and fix $Y=(p,y)$, positive definite $\Sigma$, normalized buffer $b\ge0$ and width $h>0$. Let $N=(a,u)$, with $\Gamma(u)=\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma u}=1$, locally minimize the cap integral in all normal parameters through $Y$. For $D=(a',v)$ write
$$
m=N\cdot(w-Y),\qquad q=(m+b)/h,\qquad
\gamma=u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma v,\qquad k=D\cdot(w-Y)-\gamma m,\qquad
\eta=v^{\mathsf T}\Sigma v-\gamma^2,
$$
and set $S=\int\psi(q)d\mu/h,\ A=\int q\psi(q)d\mu$, where $\psi=\Psi'$. Vary the normal by $N+tD$ using
$$
Q(t)=\int\Psi\left(\frac{(N+tD)\cdot(w-Y)/\Gamma(u+tv)+b}{h}\right)d\mu(w).
$$
The first and second derivatives of the normalized margin are $k$ and $-2\gamma k-\eta m$. For a $C^2$ CDF $\Psi$,
$$
Q''(0)=\int\psi'(q)k^2\,d\mu/h^2+(bS-A)\eta\ge0.
$$
The polarized form uses $k_Dk_E$ and $v_D^{\mathsf T}\Sigma v_E-\gamma_D\gamma_E$ in place of $k^2,\eta$. The normalization term vanishes for radial variations $D=N$ and pure-base variations. For an outward kernel with $\psi$ supported on $[-1,0]$, $-hS\le A\le0$.

For the uniform outward ramp $\Psi(q)=(q+1)_+-q_+$, set $c=N\cdot Y-b$. Let $\bar\sigma_\ell$ sum the coarea $d\mathcal H^{d-1}/\|u\|$ on all proper sections at level $N\cdot w=\ell$, with half that coarea on positive-area supporting facets and zero on null or empty sections. Then
$$
\lim_{t\to0}\frac{Q(t)+Q(-t)-2Q(0)}{t^2}
=\frac{\int k^2\,d\bar\sigma_{c-h}-\int k^2\,d\bar\sigma_c}{h}+(bS-A)\eta\ge0.
$$
In the right second derivative $\lim_{t\downarrow0}2(Q(t)-Q(0))/t^2$, replace each half-facet $k^2/2$ by $[k]_-^2$ when the fiber is on the positive side of that endpoint plane, and $[k]_+^2$ when it is on the negative side, retaining the lower plus and upper minus signs. This derivative is also nonnegative. If neither endpoint supports a positive-area facet, the expression is the ordinary Hessian. On the hyperplane $\gamma=0$ the PSD matrix is the lower balanced second-moment matrix of $w-Y$ minus the upper one, plus $h(bS-A)\operatorname{diag}(0,\Sigma)$.

pk-intake-smoothed-supporting-planar-sla.relation_to_goal: Exact actual planar patch contributions. A slab contribution does not determine the Hessian of a changing convex body, cap menu, or contact minimum.
pk-intake-smoothed-supporting-planar-sla.statement:
Let $A>0,h>0$, and let $\Psi$ be a nondecreasing CDF equal to zero below $-1$ and one above $0$. Set $J(q)=\int_{-\infty}^q\Psi(s)\,ds$, $\kappa=\eta/h$, and $W=\Psi(\kappa)$. For sufficiently large $H$ so that the remote endpoints remain saturated near $t=0$, define the actual slab masses
$$
F_{\rm in}(t)=A\int_{tv}^{H}\Psi((x+\eta-tc)/h)\,dx,\qquad
F_{\rm out}(t)=A\int_{-H}^{-tv}\Psi((x+\eta-tc)/h)\,dx.
$$
At continuity of $\Psi$ at $\kappa$ their first losses are $-F_{\rm in}'(0)=A[vW+c(1-W)]$ and $-F_{\rm out}'(0)=A(v+c)W$. The relevant first formula also holds when its primitive argument is stationary ($v=c$ or $v=-c$, respectively), regardless of continuity. At differentiability of $\Psi$ at $\kappa$, the signed second-order loss coefficients (with denominator $t^2/2$ after removing the linear term) are respectively $+(A/h)\Psi'(\kappa)(v-c)^2$ and $-(A/h)\Psi'(\kappa)(v+c)^2$. These are classical second derivatives of the losses if $\Psi$ is also continuous near $\kappa$.

Without any regularity assumption, write $D_J(k,s)=J(k+s)+J(k-s)-2J(k)\ge0$. The exact centered losses $2F(0)-F(t)-F(-t)$ are respectively $Ah D_J(\kappa,t(v-c)/h)$ and $-Ah D_J(\kappa,t(v+c)/h)$. For bounded $\kappa$ and fixed sufficiently small $t$ as $h\downarrow0$, these tend to $A|t||v-c|$ and $-A|t||v+c|$. For the uniform outward ramp the signed second coefficients above use $\Psi'(\kappa)=1$ for $-1<\kappa<0$ and zero strictly outside; at $\kappa=-1,0$ the finite-difference identity remains exact, with the two one-sided responses given by the primitive.

pk-intake-specified-monotone-endpoint-ma.relation_to_goal: The specified transport assumption is conditional; two individually dominated outputs do not establish simultaneous collective allocation over different pairs.
pk-intake-specified-monotone-endpoint-ma.statement: Let $k\ge1$ and let $A,D$ be equal-positive-volume convex bodies in the actual endpoint fibers at $-k,k+1$ of a convex source whose two middle fibers at $0,1$ are the same body $B$. Suppose a specified injective monotone map $T:A\to D$ differentiable on $\operatorname{int}A$, with symmetric positive semidefinite derivative there, pushes Lebesgue volume on $A$ onto Lebesgue volume on $D$. For $\theta=k/(2k+1),(k+1)/(2k+1)$, the map $(1-\theta)\operatorname{Id}+\theta T$ sends volume on $A$ to a measure with density at most $\mathbf1_B$. Arbitrary volume-preserving maps can fail: for $A=D=B=-B$ and $T(x)=-x$, both output densities are $(2k+1)^d$ on their images.

pk-intake-square-root-tail-defect-and-eq.relation_to_goal: Scalar equality and rigidity for finite positive concave sequences on consecutive indices.
pk-intake-square-root-tail-defect-and-eq.statement:
For $\rho>0$, put $A_m=\sum_{j=0}^m(\rho+j)$ for integers $m\ge0$. At every actual interior index $m\ge1$, $A_m^{1/2}$ is strictly midpoint concave unless $\rho=1/2$. At $\rho=1/2$ it equals $(m+1)/\sqrt2$ at every index.

Let $a_\ell,\ldots,a_r>0$ be a concave sequence on consecutive integers and set $F_i=\sum_{j=i}^r a_j$. For each $\ell<i<r$,
$$
2\sqrt{F_i}\ge\sqrt{F_{i-1}}+\sqrt{F_{i+1}}.
$$
Equality holds exactly when $a_j=(2(r-j)+1)a_r$ for every $j=i-1,\ldots,r$. The equality indices form an empty set or a terminal block of the actual interior indices. When there are at least three entries, the last interior equality holds exactly for a last-three ratio $5:3:1$, and equality at all interior indices holds exactly for the full odd profile. For example, $(15/2,7,5,3,1)$ has equality at precisely its last two interior indices.

At an interior node with $A=a_{i-1}>b=a_i$, put $F=F_i$, $\delta=A-b$, and $q=b/\delta>1$. Write $q=m+\rho$ with integer $m\ge1$ and $0<\rho\le1$, taking $\rho=1$ if $q$ is an integer. Set
$$
F_{\max}=\delta\sum_{k\ge0}(q-k)_+,qquad
F_*=(A+b)^2/(8\delta).
$$
The exact defect identities are
$$
\begin{aligned}
F_*-F&=\tfrac\delta2(\rho-\tfrac12)^2+F_{\max}-F,\\
2\sqrt F-\sqrt{F+A}-\sqrt{F-b}
&=\frac{8\delta(F_*-F)}
   {(2\sqrt F+\sqrt{F+A}+\sqrt{F-b})(2F-\delta+2\sqrt{(F+A)(F-b)})}.
\end{aligned}
$$
The two terms in the first identity are nonnegative. If the $a_i$ sum to one, the support is nonsingleton, and the mean $\mu=\sum_i i a_i$ is integral, then the Jensen comparison $\sqrt{F_\mu}>\sum_i a_i\sqrt{F_i}$ is strict.

pk-intake-stable-constraint-gram-local-p.relation_to_goal: Local planar repair with smooth positive curvature and stable linear constraints. This preserves the full Gram matrix, a stronger invariant than the separate area identities.
pk-intake-stable-constraint-gram-local-p.statement:
Let finitely many planar convex bodies with interior have support functions $h_z$ that are $C^2$ on a neighborhood of a closed normal interval $I=[a,b]$ with $0<b-a<\pi$. Assume $h_z''+h_z\ge c>0$ on $I$. Assume the original supports satisfy a finite list of homogeneous linear constraints $\sum_z A_z h_z\ge0$ in all directions, with each gap identically zero or uniformly strictly positive on $I$. Fix a finite list of prescribed caps for each fiber. For each such cap, suppose the whole exposed arc over $I$ lies on one strict side of the cap line with a uniformly positive distance. Let $B_z$ solve $B_z''+B_z=0$ with the same endpoint values as $h_z$, set $f_z=h_z-B_z$, and set $Q(f,g)=\int_I(f'g'-fg)\,d\theta$.

There are arbitrarily close simultaneous replacements by actual convex bodies, piecewise homogeneous on a common finite mesh on $I$, with all supports unchanged outside $\operatorname{int} I$. They preserve every listed support constraint, every individual area and every prescribed cap area, as well as every linear relation among the residuals and all pairwise values $Q(f_z,f_w)$. Endpoint facets are allowed. If the bodies are indexed by a finite base and the list includes every extreme Jensen constraint at that base, the replacements are exact fibers of the convex hull of their lifts.

pk-intake-stationary-cap-hessian-realiza.relation_to_goal: Realizes curvature at one individual centered section of an ordinary convex polytope, at an arbitrary fraction.
pk-intake-stationary-cap-hessian-realiza.statement: For every $k\ge1$, $\alpha\in(0,1)$, and symmetric real $k\times k$ matrix $A$, there are convex polytopes $K\subset\mathbb R^k\times\mathbb R$ with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$ and section $t=0$ centered at $0$, whose angular cap fraction $p$ is analytic near $(0,1)$ and satisfies $p(0,1)=\alpha$ and $\operatorname{Hess}_{\mathbb S^k}p(0,1)=2^k A/(3|K|)$ in horizontal tangent coordinates. The factor $2^k/(3|K|)$ can be arbitrarily large while $\alpha,A$ are fixed. In particular every Hessian signature occurs at each prescribed fraction.

pk-intake-stationary-common-simplex-enve.relation_to_goal: Exact ordinary planar counterexample to interpretations of shared-orientation stationarity.
pk-intake-stationary-common-simplex-enve.statement:
Let $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2)$ and take the two equal-weight triangles
$$
A=\operatorname{conv}((3/5,2/5),(0,3/5),(2/5,0)),\qquad
B=\operatorname{conv}((2/5,3/5),(0,2/5),(3/5,0)).
$$
At the orientation of $T$, all directional derivatives of their total envelope area vanish and none of their individual facet contact points is the facet centroid. The total envelope area there is $1$, and the orientation of $A$ gives total envelope area $109/175$. The orientation of $T$ is also not a local minimum.

pk-intake-stationary-fractional-exponent.relation_to_goal: A second-variation exclusion inside the explicit fractional coefficient family. It gives no endpoint comparison on the surviving range p>b.
pk-intake-stationary-fractional-exponent.statement:
Let $k,m$ be integers with $m\ge k\ge1$ and let $p,b\in(0,1)$ satisfy $mb=k+p-1$. In a signed sum of independent unit-mean exponentials, take positive coefficients given by $k$ units and one $p$, and negative coefficients given by a fixed $-1$ and $m$ copies of $-b$. Let $P(t)$ be its nonnegative-sign probability on the feasible path replacing $p$ by $p+t$ and every $b$ by $b+t/m$, with the units fixed.

If $P'(0)=0$, $k\ge2$, and $p\le b$, then $P''(0)<0$. If $k=1$ and $p\le b$, the balance forces $m=1$ and $p=b$, and the probability on the path is identically $1/2$. Consequently any local minimum in this fractional family with probability below $1/2$ must have $p>b$, equivalently $(m-1)p>k-1$, and in particular $m>k$. The conclusion applies to a local minimum in the full capped coefficient domain that has this fractional pattern.

pk-intake-stationary-simplex-cap-positiv.relation_to_goal: Stationarity and local cap volumes for ordinary uniform measure on a simplex. The pairwise threshold applies to the selected pair.
pk-intake-stationary-simplex-cap-positiv.statement:
Let $T=\operatorname{conv}(v_0,\ldots,v_d)$ be a $d$-simplex, $d\ge2$, in its affine hull, and let $y\in T$ have barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i$. Consider the relative volume of an oriented closed halfspace cap through $y$ as a function of its oriented normal. Call the cut proper when some vertex is strictly included and some vertex is strictly excluded. At a stationary proper cap, if two strictly included vertices $i,j$ have $\lambda_i,\lambda_j\le1/d$, there is a feasible variation with strictly negative second derivative. If two strictly excluded vertices satisfy the same coordinate bound, there is a feasible variation with strictly positive second derivative. The conclusions permit zero margins at other vertices. Under $\max_i\lambda_i\le1/d$, every proper local minimum strictly includes exactly one vertex, and any stationary proper cap with at least two strictly included and two strictly excluded vertices has both signs of second variation.

For a stationary proper cap with at least three nonzero vertex margins, all $\lambda_i$ are positive and every zero vertex margin satisfies $\lambda_i=1/d$.

pk-intake-stationary-tetrahedral-cap-mix.relation_to_goal: This is an ordinary tetrahedral law at positive stationary rows. It supplies no global maximizing property for the capacity objective and no mixed-integer depth bound.
pk-intake-stationary-tetrahedral-cap-mix.statement:
Let $\mu$ be uniform probability on $\Delta_3=\{\xi\in\mathbb R^4:\xi\ge0,\ \sum_j\xi_j=1\}$. Take
$$
c_1=(7,12,-28,-28),\qquad c_2=(12,7,-28,-28),\qquad c_3=(-19,-19,56,56).
$$
The proper quadrilateral sections $c_i\cdot\xi=0$ have the same section centroid $b=(56,56,19,19)/150$, and $\sum_i c_i=0$. Set $H_i=\{\xi:c_i\cdot\xi\ge0\}$, $P_i=\mu(H_i)$, and let $f_i$ be the density at zero of $\sum_j c_{ij}E_j$ for independent unit exponentials. Then
$$
(P_1,P_2,P_3)=\left(\frac4{25},\frac4{25},\frac{354368}{421875}\right),\quad
(f_1,f_2,f_3)=\left(\frac1{100},\frac1{100},\frac{2128}{421875}\right),\quad
T=\sum_iP_i/f_i=\frac{3772}{19}.
$$
The probability density $w=T^{-1}\sum_i \mathbf1_{H_i}/f_i$ relative to $\mu$ has the same centroid as $\mu$, but the measures $w\mu,\mu$ are incomparable in convex order. The integrals against $(w-1)\mu$ of $(\xi_0-\xi_1)^2$ and $(\xi_0+\xi_1-4/5)_+$ are respectively $-24871/106087500$ and $63/1178750$.

This law is realized by strictly positive column-stochastic rows $x_i=((P_i/f_i)\mathbf1-c_i)/T$ for $i=1,2,3$. For $F_x(t)=\Pr_\mu(x\cdot\xi\le t)$ and $\phi_3(x)=\inf_{t>0,\ F_x(t)>0} t/F_x(t)^{1/3}$, row $x_i$ has the unique proper minimizing threshold $P_i/(Tf_i)$ and $P_i^{1/3}\nabla\phi_3(x_i)=b$. Thus the weighted capacity sum $\sum_iP_i^{1/3}\phi_3(x_i)$ is stationary under column-sum-preserving row motions.

pk-intake-stochastic-all-rows-have-zeros.relation_to_goal: All-dimensional containment on the boundary stratum of the auxiliary stochastic capacity problem.
pk-intake-stochastic-all-rows-have-zeros.statement: For $d\ge1$, let $U$ be uniform on $\Delta_d=\{u\in\mathbb R_+^{d+1}:\sum_j u_j=1\}$, and for $x\ge0$ put $F_x(t)=\Pr(x\cdot U\le t)$ and $\phi_d(x)=\inf_{t>0:F_x(t)>0} t/F_x(t)^{1/d}$. For $d\ge1$ and $m=d+1$, let $D_d$ consist of all $v\in\mathbb R_+^m$ for which there exists a nonnegative zero-diagonal column-stochastic $m\times m$ matrix $Y$ satisfying $v_i\le \operatorname{GM}_d((Y_{ij})_{j\ne i})$ for every $i$, where $\operatorname{GM}_d$ is the geometric mean of $d$ entries. If $X$ is any nonnegative column-stochastic $(d+1)\times(d+1)$ matrix with at least one zero entry in every row, then $(\phi_d(X_i))_i\in D_d$.

pk-intake-stochastic-boundary-row-multip.relation_to_goal: Necessary multiplier identities for boundary rows of the auxiliary problem. The unrestricted transfer at a zero row is stronger than its tests on directions with a zero.
pk-intake-stochastic-boundary-row-multip.statement:
For $d\ge1$, let $U$ be uniform on $\Delta_d=\{u\in\mathbb R_+^{d+1}:\sum_j u_j=1\}$, and for $x\ge0$ put $F_x(t)=\Pr(x\cdot U\le t)$ and $\phi_d(x)=\inf_{t>0:F_x(t)>0} t/F_x(t)^{1/d}$. Assume $d\ge2$. Let $X$ be a local maximizer of $H(X)=\sum_i c_i\phi_d(X_i)$ over nonnegative column-stochastic $(d+1)\times(d+1)$ matrices, where $X_i$ is row $i$ and every $c_i>0$. Suppose at least one strictly positive row has a proper minimizing threshold. Let $\lambda>0$ be its weighted capacity gradient and put $S=\sum_j\lambda_j$. For a row $i$ whose only zero is in column $h$, put $g_i=\phi_d(X_i)$ and $\mu_i=c_i g_i/d$. Then
$$
X_{ij}=\frac{\mu_i}{\lambda_j}\quad(j\ne h),\qquad
c_i=d\,\operatorname{GM}_d((\lambda_j)_{j\ne h}),\qquad
d\max_{j\ne h}\lambda_j\le S.
$$
Two such rows with distinct zero columns imply $\lambda_j\le S/d$ for every $j$. For an identically zero row $i$ one has $c_i\le d\,\operatorname{GM}_d((\lambda_j)_{j\ne h})$ for every $h$.

pk-intake-stochastic-common-section-cent.relation_to_goal: First-order restrictions on positive rows of the auxiliary column-stochastic capacity problem.
pk-intake-stochastic-common-section-cent.statement:
For $d\ge1$, let $U$ be uniform on $\Delta_d=\{u\in\mathbb R_+^{d+1}:\sum_j u_j=1\}$, and for $x\ge0$ put $F_x(t)=\Pr(x\cdot U\le t)$ and $\phi_d(x)=\inf_{t>0:F_x(t)>0} t/F_x(t)^{1/d}$. Assume $d\ge2$. Let $X$ be a local maximizer of $H(X)=\sum_i c_i\phi_d(X_i)$ over nonnegative column-stochastic $(d+1)\times(d+1)$ matrices, where $X_i$ is row $i$ and every $c_i>0$. Suppose the capacity vector $(\phi_d(X_i))_i$ differs from every standard unit vector and at least one row is strictly positive. Then all strictly positive rows have a unique proper minimizing threshold $t_i$, with $\min_j X_{ij}<t_i<\max_j X_{ij}$. Let $F_i=F_{X_i}(t_i)$ and let $b_i$ be the barycentric centroid of the actual section $\{u\in\Delta_d:X_i\cdot u=t_i\}$ under normalized coarea measure. There is a common vector $\lambda>0$ such that, for each strictly positive row $i$ and $S=\sum_j\lambda_j$,
$$
\lambda=c_i\nabla\phi_d(X_i)=c_i F_i^{-1/d}b_i,\qquad
c_i F_i^{-1/d}=S,\qquad b_i=\frac{\lambda}{S},
\qquad t_i=X_i\cdot b_i,\qquad c_i\phi_d(X_i)=St_i .
$$
The same equations hold between any pair of strictly positive rows with proper minimizing thresholds at a local maximum, by comparing those rows directly.

pk-intake-stochastic-full-cut-row-exclus.relation_to_goal: Necessary condition for local or global maxima of a finite stochastic row objective. The saturated exception concerns its capacity vector.
pk-intake-stochastic-full-cut-row-exclus.statement: Let $d\ge2$ and maximize $\sum_i \omega_i\phi_d(X_i)$ locally over nonnegative $(d+1)\times(d+1)$ matrices with each column sum equal to one, where $X_i$ is row $i$, $\omega_i>0$, and $\phi_d$ is the uniform-simplex row capacity. If a strictly positive row $X_r$ has a full-cut minimum, it has maximum entry one and saturates at least $d$ columns. The capacity vector then equals $e_r$ and is realized also by a zero-diagonal column-stochastic matrix. If the capacity vector is no unit vector, every strictly positive row has a unique proper minimizing threshold and locally differentiable capacity.

pk-intake-stochastic-joint-threshold-sch.relation_to_goal: Joint compensation for corrected directions at actual proper cuts of uniform-simplex capacity rows.
pk-intake-stochastic-joint-threshold-sch.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $m=d+1$, and let $\phi_d$ be the uniform-simplex row capacity $\inf_{t>0:F_x(t)>0}t/F_x(t)^{1/d}$ for $F_x(t)=\Pr(x\cdot U\le t)$ and uniform $U$ on $\Delta_d=\{u\in\mathbb R_+^m:\sum_j u_j=1\}$. Let $X$ be nonnegative and column-stochastic with $m$ columns, and let $V$ be its active-row span. Select any collection $S$ of strictly positive rows $X_i$ with proper minimizing thresholds $t_i$, and for each set $c_i=\mathbf 1-X_i/t_i$. Put $P(c)=\Pr(\sum_j c_jE_j\ge0)$ for independent unit exponentials, $g_i=\nabla P(c_i)$ and $H_i=\nabla^2P(c_i)$. Define
$$
T_i(v)=v+\frac{\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}H_i v}{dP(c_i)}\mathbf 1
\qquad (g_i\cdot v=0).
$$
Each $T_i$ is injective on $g_i^\perp$ and satisfies
$$
T_i(v)^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2\phi_d(X_i)T_i(v)
=-\frac{P(c_i)^{-1/d}}{t_i dP(c_i)}v^{\mathsf T}H_i v .
$$
For each tangent tuple $(v_i)_{i\in S}$ one has $\sum_i T_i(v_i)\in V$ if and only if $\sum_i v_i\in V$. In particular, if $X$ is a least-active maximizer of a positively weighted sum of $\phi_d$ and $N_i\subseteq g_i^\perp$ are negative-definite subspaces for $H_i$, then $k+\sum_{i\in S}\dim N_i\le m$, where $k$ is the number of active rows.

pk-intake-stochastic-partial-zero-row-ex.statement: For $d\ge1$, let $U$ be uniform on $\Delta_d=\{u\in\mathbb R_+^{d+1}:\sum_j u_j=1\}$, and for $x\ge0$ put $F_x(t)=\Pr(x\cdot U\le t)$ and $\phi_d(x)=\inf_{t>0:F_x(t)>0} t/F_x(t)^{1/d}$. Let $X$ be a local maximizer of $H(X)=\sum_i c_i\phi_d(X_i)$ over nonnegative column-stochastic $(d+1)\times(d+1)$ matrices, where $X_i$ is row $i$ and every $c_i>0$. If one row is strictly positive, every other nonzero row has at most one zero entry.

pk-intake-stochastic-proportional-row-co.relation_to_goal: An exactly feasible variation of a finite stochastic matrix with homogeneous row objectives.
pk-intake-stochastic-proportional-row-co.statement:
Let $X$ be a local maximizer of $L(X)=\sum_i f_i(X_i)$ on the nonnegative $N\times m$ matrices with each column sum one, where each $f_i$ is finite and positively homogeneous of degree one on $\mathbb R_+^m$. Write $I=\{i:X_i\ne0\}$. Choose a set $S\subseteq I$ of strictly positive rows and vectors $v_i\in\mathbb R^m$ for $i\in S$, with $v_i=0$ for $i\in I\setminus S$. Suppose $\sum_{i\in S}v_i\in\operatorname{span}\{X_i:i\in I\}$, and choose $a_i$ with $\sum_{i\in I}(v_i+a_iX_i)=0$. Assume for $i\in S$ that the two-sided directional derivative $\ell_i=\frac{d}{ds}f_i(X_i+s v_i)|_{s=0}$ exists.

Then the matrix with rows $X_i(t)=(1+t a_i)X_i+t v_i$ for $i\in I$ and zero elsewhere is feasible for sufficiently small signed $t$, and, with $s_i=t/(1+t a_i)$,
$$
L(X(t))-L(X)
=\sum_{i\in S}(1+t a_i)
 \bigl[f_i(X_i+s_i v_i)-f_i(X_i)-s_i\ell_i\bigr].
$$
In particular, for $S=\{r\}$ and $f_r=\omega_r\phi$ with $\omega_r>0$, every such direction in the active span has nonpositive capacity remainder for all small $s_r$. If a second directional coefficient exists along that direction, it is nonpositive.

pk-intake-stochastic-row-capacity-attain.relation_to_goal: Attainment for a finite-dimensional stochastic objective for an arbitrary barycentric law.
pk-intake-stochastic-row-capacity-attain.statement:
Let $m\ge1$ be an integer, let $d\ge1$, and let $\Xi$ have any probability law on $\{u\in\mathbb R_+^m:\sum_j u_j=1\}$. For $x\in\mathbb R_+^m$ put $F_x(t)=\Pr(x\cdot\Xi\le t)$ and
$$
\phi(x)=\inf_{\substack{t>0\\F_x(t)>0}}\frac{t}{F_x(t)^{1/d}}.
$$
Then $\phi$ is coordinatewise nondecreasing, positively homogeneous of degree one, continuous on $\mathbb R_+^m$, and satisfies $0\le\phi(x)\le\max_j x_j$. For each fixed finite positive number of rows and fixed nonnegative weights $\omega_i$, the objective $\sum_i\omega_i\phi(X_i)$ attains a maximum over the nonnegative matrices with $m$ columns whose column sums all equal one. It has a maximizer with the fewest nonzero rows.

pk-intake-stochastic-single-full-row-cen.relation_to_goal: Necessary centroid restrictions in the one-positive-row stratum of the auxiliary objective.
pk-intake-stochastic-single-full-row-cen.statement:
For $d\ge1$, let $U$ be uniform on $\Delta_d=\{u\in\mathbb R_+^{d+1}:\sum_j u_j=1\}$, and for $x\ge0$ put $F_x(t)=\Pr(x\cdot U\le t)$ and $\phi_d(x)=\inf_{t>0:F_x(t)>0} t/F_x(t)^{1/d}$. Assume $d\ge2$. Let $X$ be a local maximizer of $H(X)=\sum_i c_i\phi_d(X_i)$ over nonnegative column-stochastic $(d+1)\times(d+1)$ matrices, where $X_i$ is row $i$ and every $c_i>0$. Suppose exactly one row $r$ is strictly positive, with a proper minimizing threshold $t$. Write $x=X_r$, $b$ for its actual section centroid, $\lambda=c_r\nabla\phi_d(x)$ and $S=\sum_j\lambda_j$. Group the nonzero rows other than $r$ by their unique zero column, and replace each group by its sum in one of its own row labels, setting the other rows in that group to zero. Permute columns to place each surviving such row's zero on its diagonal. After this relabeling, let $\mu_i=c_i\phi_d(X_i)/d$ for each surviving row other than $r$, and set $\mu_i=0$ at unmatched labels including $r$. Write $\mu=\sum_i\mu_i$. The merger preserves the objective and gives
$$
H(X)=S,\qquad b=\lambda/S,\qquad
0<t=x\cdot b<1,\qquad
\lambda_j(1-x_j)=\mu-\mu_j,\qquad
\mu=\frac{S(1-t)}d .
$$
The image of the actual section measure under $u_j\mapsto (1-x_j)u_j/(1-t)$ is a probability on $\Delta_d$ whose $j$th centroid coordinate is
$$
\frac{(1-x_j)b_j}{1-t}=\frac1d-\frac{\mu_j}{S(1-t)}\le\frac1d.
$$
Equality holds exactly at unmatched labels. The pushforward statement includes collapsed coordinates.

pk-intake-stratified-centers-for-joint-s.relation_to_goal: Existential depth in the original single-cell law. An application to a positive rate needs the actual simultaneous law and any claimed rank bound. No marked cap or multiple-cell payment is used.
pk-intake-stratified-centers-for-joint-s.statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $N\ge1$, and let $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes\mu_z$ for a nonempty finite $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ and nonzero finite positive compactly supported Borel measures $\mu_z$ on $\mathbb R^D$. Suppose every combination $z=\sum_i\theta_i z_i\in\mathbb Z^n$, with $z_i\in P$, $\theta_i>0$, and $\sum_i\theta_i=1$, has $z\in P$ and satisfies
$$
\mu_z\!\left(\sum_i\theta_i E_i\right)^{1/N}\ge\sum_i\theta_i\mu_{z_i}(E_i)^{1/N}
$$
for every compact positive-mass choice of $E_i$. Partition $P$ into strata of equal support affine dimension and equal support tangent space. For stratum $c$, let $W_c$ be its total mass, $q_c$ its support affine dimension, and $k_c$ the number of its occupied base parities modulo $2\mathbb Z^n$. Write $W=\sum_c W_c$ and $k(P)=\sum_c k_c$.

There is a point in the actual support of $\mu$ whose raw depth, the infimum of $\mu(H)$ over all containing closed ambient halfspaces $H$, is at least
$$
\max_c \frac{W_c}{(q_c+1)k_c}\ \ge\ \frac{W}{\sum_c(q_c+1)k_c}.
$$
In particular, if all $q_c\le1$, and $k_0,k_1$ are the sums of the occupied parity counts over dimensions $0,1$ respectively, then this depth is at least $W/(k_0+2k_1)\ge W/[2k(P)]\ge (N/(N+1))^N W/k(P)$. This includes all laws with $q_c<N$ when $N\in\{1,2\}$.

pk-intake-strict-atomic-gap-compact-buff.relation_to_goal: An own-section threshold inverse for buffered caps with strict atomic gap. Other fibers may have supporting facets.
pk-intake-strict-atomic-gap-compact-buff.statement:
Use the finite compatible positive-fiber setting, the $\Gamma$-unit normals and the buffered depth of the whole-fiber capture and atomic-gap lemma. At any interior mark $Y=(p,y)$ with $\delta>0$ and $b_\delta(Y)<b_{\rm base}(p)$, the buffered infimum is attained by a nonvertical cap. There is a bounded set of base tilts containing a representative of every $\Gamma$-unit nonvertical cap with its mass on each fiber preserved. Among the representatives in a common closed ball, the minimizing caps form a compact set. Their own-section coarea $\mathcal H^{d-1}(K_p\cap\{u\cdot(X-y)=-\delta\})/\lVert u\rVert$ is bounded below by a positive constant. This lower bound, after decreasing it, persists for nearby parameters and small parallel changes of threshold. In particular cap mass has a local strict inverse in the threshold, with inverse Lipschitz constant bounded uniformly near the compact minimizing set.

For a fixed family and $\Sigma$, allow $\delta$ to be continuous on each fiber, positive in its interior and zero on its boundary. If every global maximizing mark has a strict atomic gap, the compact representative and coarea conclusions hold uniformly over those marks.

pk-intake-strict-compatibility-ambient-e.relation_to_goal: A finite geometric support lemma. Its conclusion is an ambient exposing functional at one prescribed point.
pk-intake-strict-compatibility-ambient-e.statement: Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge1$, $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and nonempty, and $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies for $p\in P$. Fix $q\in P$. Assume the strict compatibility condition at $q$: for every extreme point of the polytope $E_q$ of convex representations of $q$ using $P\setminus\{q\}$, the associated Minkowski combination of the $K_p$ is compactly contained in $\operatorname{int}K_q$. This condition is vacuous if $E_q$ is empty. For any unit $u$ whose support face in $K_q$ is $\{v\}$, there exists $a\in\mathbb R^n$ such that $a\cdot(p-q)+h_{K_p}(u)-h_{K_q}(u)<0$ for every $p\ne q$. Thus $(q,v)$ is the unique maximizer of $(z,x)\mapsto a\cdot z+u\cdot x$ on $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{p\in P}(\{p\}\times K_p)$. In particular, if the own boundary is $C^1$ and strictly convex, each own boundary point has a unique unit supporting normal and is exposed in $C$.

pk-intake-strict-compatibility-open.relation_to_goal: An openness statement for the actual integer-fiber constraints on a fixed base set.
pk-intake-strict-compatibility-open.statement:
Let $n\ge0$ and $d\ge1$ be integers. Let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty, with $\operatorname{aff}(P)=\mathbb R^n$, and let $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$, $p\in P$, be compact convex bodies with nonempty interior. For each $q\in P$, let
$$
E_q=\left\{\lambda\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{P\setminus\{q\}}:\quad
\sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p=1,\quad \sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p p=q\right\}.
$$
Call the family strictly compatible if for each extreme point $\lambda$ of each nonempty $E_q$, the Minkowski combination $\sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p K_p$ is compactly contained in $\operatorname{int}K_q$. Under this condition there is a common $\kappa>0$ such that $\sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p K_p+\kappa B_d\subseteq K_q$ for every such extreme point, where $B_d$ is the closed unit ball. For any family of convex bodies $K'_p$ with $d_H(K'_p,K_p)<\eta<\kappa/2$ for all $p$, the convex hull of the lifted bodies $\{p\}\times K'_p$ has exactly the prescribed integer fibers $K'_p$ at $p\in P$. In particular the original family is actual.

pk-intake-strict-convex-cost-empty-targe.relation_to_goal: The full fractional allocation polytope and a selector-specific consequence for an actual body.
pk-intake-strict-convex-cost-empty-targe.statement:
Let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be nonempty and finite, let $w_z>0$ for $z\in P$, and let $\phi$ be strictly convex on $\operatorname{conv}(P)$. In the fractional allocation polytope
$$
c_{jz}\ge0,\qquad
\sum_{j\in P}c_{jz}=w_z,\qquad
\sum_{z\in P}(z-j)c_{jz}=0\quad(j\in P)
$$
write $m_j=\sum_{z\in P}c_{jz}$. For every minimizer of $\sum_{j\in P}m_j\phi(j)$, the set $V=\{j:m_j>0\}$ is both the vertex set and the set of all lattice points of $\operatorname{conv}(V)$.

In the rectangle of the minimum-variance partition obstruction, every exhaustive positive two-piece integer-centroid convex partition with such a target set, allowing null mixed overlap, has target bases $0,1$ and is one of the two shallow partitions established there.

pk-intake-strict-depth-contact-from-prop.relation_to_goal: Strict contact for one attained nonvertical cap with one proper sampled section and the stated through-source differentiability.
pk-intake-strict-depth-contact-from-prop.statement:
Let $\mu$ sum $d$-volume on finitely many positive compact convex fibers $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ at bases $z\in\mathbb R^n$, with $d\ge1$. Define the raw depth $D(Y)$ of an ambient point to be the infimum of $\mu(H)$ over closed halfspaces containing $Y$. Let $H=\{w:N\cdot(w-Y)\ge0\}$ attain $Q=D(Y)$, with nonzero continuous component of $N$. Assume its boundary cuts the interior of at least one sampled fiber. Assume also that for every ambient vector $v$ the function
$$
t\longmapsto\mu\{w:(N+t v)\cdot(w-Y)\ge0\}
$$
is differentiable at zero. Then $H\cap\{D\ge Q\}=\{Y\}$.

pk-intake-strict-depth-interpolation-acr.statement: Let $n,d\ge1$ and $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$ for compact convex $C\subset\mathbb R^{n+d}$. Let $\mu$ sum the $d$-volume of its fibers and assume $\mu(S)>0$. Write $D$ for its raw closed ambient halfspace depth. Let $y_e=(p_e,x_e)\in S$ have positive depth, with $p_0\ne p_1$. Suppose an affine base functional $h$ satisfies $h(p_0)=0$, $h(p_1)=1$ and $0\le h(z)\le1$ on every positive-volume base. Then every $y=(1-t)y_0+ty_1\in S$ with $0<t<1$ satisfies $D(y)>\min(D(y_0),D(y_1))$.

pk-intake-strict-depth-interpolation-one.relation_to_goal: Strict interpolation between distinct bases for ordinary depth when n=1.
pk-intake-strict-depth-interpolation-one.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact and convex, $d\ge1$, with positive mixed $d$-volume $M$. Let $D(Y)$ be its normalized depth over all closed ambient halfspaces. Let $Y_e=(z_e,x_e)$ be sampled points of positive depth, with $z_0<z_1$ integers. For every integer $p$ strictly between $z_0$ and $z_1$, let $t=(p-z_0)/(z_1-z_0)$. Then
$$
D((1-t)Y_0+tY_1)>\min\{D(Y_0),D(Y_1)\}.
$$
In particular the globally maximizing integer bases form a singleton or a pair of adjacent integers. Supporting sections of positive $\mathcal H^{d-1}$ measure are allowed, including supporting endpoints when $d=1$.

pk-intake-strict-equal-mass-mixed-helly-.relation_to_goal: A certificate under a prescribed strict upper bound on maximum depth, for the positive full d-volume fibers.
pk-intake-strict-equal-mass-mixed-helly-.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$, let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex and let $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$ have positive mixed $d$-volume $M$. $$
a_i\cdot p_i>b_i,qquad a_j\cdot p_i<b_j\quad(j\ne i).
$$
Its exclusive region thus contains a positive-volume ball in that witness fiber.

pk-intake-strict-finite-logconcave-survi.statement: Let $w_0,\ldots,w_N>0$ be log-concave, with zero extension, $S_i=\sum_{h\ge i}w_h$ for integer $i\ge0$, and $M=S_0$. Monotonicity of the original weights is unnecessary.

pk-intake-strict-five-triangle-chain-all.relation_to_goal: An explicit actual family with one integer and two continuous coordinates. Its baseline normalized depth is 4/9.
pk-intake-strict-five-triangle-chain-all.statement:
Let $T=\operatorname{conv}\{(-1,-1),(2,-1),(-1,2)\}$, $V=9/2$, and $P=\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}$. In the order of $P$, set $r=(4/5,19/20,1,19/20,4/5)$ and $e=(1,0,-8/5,0,1)$. Let $r_j(a,b)=r_j+aj+be_j$, and let $S(a,b)$ have fibers $r_j(a,b)T$ for $j\in P$. If $|a|+|b|<1/100$, the piecewise-affine radius interpolation realizes exactly these integer fibers in a compact convex body with interior and with negative discrete second differences at the interior integer knots. Write $R=817/200$, $E=114/25$, and $Q=2R$. The total mixed area is
$$
M(a,b)=V(R+10a^2+Eb^2).
$$
At $(0,0)$ each velocity in this parameter plane has zero first area derivative separately in each parity class.

For all sufficiently small $(a,b)$, the true maximum raw depth over $S(a,b)$ is attained at $(0,0,0)$ and equals $D_0(a,b)=Q+2Eb^2$. Every point at a nonzero base has strictly smaller depth. Put $u_1=(1,0)$, $u_2=(0,1)$, $u_3=(-1,-1)$, with indices read cyclically. At the baseline the only minimizing normal rays at the middle centroid have continuous part $u_i$ and zero integer tilt. Nearby the minimizing rays at that centroid have margins $u_i\cdot x-2az$. In the chart of margins $x_1+\theta x_2+\alpha z$, the exact cap area for nearby parameters and normals is
$$
\Phi(\alpha,\theta)=\frac{(2-\theta)^2 R(a,b)+2\alpha(2-\theta)J(a,b)+10\alpha^2}{2(1-\theta)},\qquad
R(a,b)=R+10a^2+Eb^2,\quad J(a,b)=10a,
$$
and the other two cyclic charts give the same formula.

At each inner centroid $(\pm1,0,0)$ there is a cyclic triple of depth-attaining through-centroid caps, all with mass strictly below $D_0(a,b)$. The three continuous normals span the plane and sum to zero. The common integer coefficient is positive on the right and negative on the left. The right triple covers every point at bases $1,2$ and the left triple covers every point at bases $-2,-1$. Each original slack triple may also be kept fixed with the same coverage and strict slack under sufficiently small changes of the radii.

pk-intake-strict-five-triangle-ownership.relation_to_goal: Exact ownership and fixed-budget comparison in one above-target family with baseline normalized depth 4/9.
pk-intake-strict-five-triangle-ownership.statement:
Use the strict five-triangle family with $T=\operatorname{conv}\{(-1,-1),(2,-1),(-1,2)\}$, bases $P=\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}$ and radii $r_j+aj+be_j$, where $r=(4/5,19/20,1,19/20,4/5)$ and $e=(1,0,-8/5,0,1)$. Write $R=817/200$, $E=114/25$, $Q=2R$, $D_0=Q+2Eb^2$, and $a_\pm=\max\{\pm a,0\}$. In the proper cyclic middle-cap chamber with equal positive cover weights, assigning the middle group to cover bases $\{-2,-1,0\}$ and the right slack group to cover $\{1,2\}$ gives smallest largest middle-cap mass $D_0+20a_-^2$. The assignment with middle bases $\{0,1,2\}$ and left slack bases $\{-2,-1\}$ gives $D_0+20a_+^2$. Choosing the better assignment attains $D_0$ and is optimal even among unrestricted through-middle-centroid cap choices.

Along $(a,b)=t(A,B)$ for $t\ge0$, the frozen middle-cap second derivative is $40A^2+(456/25)B^2$. With the stress $3/4$ on each middle cap, the second derivatives of total mass minus the stressed sum of optimized middle-cap masses are $90(A_+)^2$ for the right assignment, $90(A_-)^2$ for the left, and $90A^2$ after assignment optimization. The same quadratic terms hold with smoothly varying positive balance weights equal at the baseline.

Finally, the common continuous homothety of scale $k$ with $k^2=R/(R+Eb^2)$ fixes the actual global raw depth at $Q$ and gives total mixed area
$$
M(0,0)+\frac{45Ra^2}{R+Eb^2}.
$$
Thus it gives strict fixed-budget volume gain and strict decrease of normalized maximum depth exactly when $a\ne0$. The full $b$ axis is neutral after this normalization.

pk-intake-strict-gap-deepest-source-stra.relation_to_goal: Rigidity and parity separation for strict-gap deepest source bases in a physical-buffer limit.
pk-intake-strict-gap-deepest-source-stra.statement:
In the buffered limit setting of the sampled shift and depth limit theorem, take $P$ to be a complete affine-lattice base and suppose the $h_j$ are positive. Along a further subsequence let $J$ be the fixed set of all buffered maximizing bases whose closed pure-base depth exceeds $Q_j$ at each $j$. At each $p\in J$ there is exactly one maximizing mark $Y_{j,p}$. Pass to a subsequence along which all of them converge. Set $J_0=J\cap Z$ and $J_+=J\setminus Z$.

For any convex combination of bases in $J$ whose target $r$ belongs to $P$, the base $r$ belongs to $J$, its unique mark is the same combination of the input marks, and the positive input weights at finite $j$ satisfy
$$
\frac{h_j(Y_{j,p})}{h_j(Y_{j,q})}=
\left(\frac{|K_{j,p}|}{|K_{j,q}|}\right)^{1/d}
$$
for any two positive inputs $p,q$. Their centered fibers $K_{j,p}-y_{j,p}$ are positive homothets. No such combination uses positive weights in both $J_0$ and $J_+$. Each nonempty class is a closed minor and $k(J_0)+k(J_+)\le k(J)\le k(P)$ for inherited occupied parity counts.

pk-intake-strict-half-cap-planar-sector-.relation_to_goal: Ordinary planar area and coarea only. Global containment K ⊆ T is asserted only sectorwise on the unique sectors; the theorem does not transfer a cap ceiling or preserve mixed fibers.
pk-intake-strict-half-cap-planar-sector-.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a compact convex body with an interior mark and three spanning balanced normals whose through-mark caps each have area strictly below $|K|/2$. Translate the mark to $0$ and normalize the normals to $(1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1)$. The six cyclic ray endpoints are $(A,0),(0,B),(-t,t),(-a,0),(0,-b),(r,-r)$. The three bridge halfplanes
$$
x/A+y/B\le1,\qquad x+(1-a/t)y\ge-a,\qquad y+(1-b/r)x\ge-b
$$
intersect in a nondegenerate triangle $T$ with exactly these six ray endpoints and all three original cutting chords. In each unique sector (captured by just one cap), the piece of $K$ is contained in the piece of $T$. In each double sector, the piece of $T$ is exactly the core triangle spanned by $0$ and its two ray endpoints, hence is contained in the piece of $K$. The three vertices of $T$ lie one each in the three closed unique cones. The ordinary Lorentz rows of $T$ are all at most $2$: if $k=|T|$, $Q_i$ is its cap area, $\sigma_i$ its central chord length divided by the normal length, $M=\sum_i Q_i/\sigma_i$, and $f_i=2\sqrt{kQ_i}/(\sigma_iM)$, then $f_i+(f_j+f_l)^2/4\le2$ for every $\{i,j,l\}=\{1,2,3\}$.

pk-intake-strict-homothetic-compatibilit.relation_to_goal: Actual compatible simplex families with one common group of fixed canonical cap budgets. The inequality is about that cap group and does not assert all-normal depth improvement.
pk-intake-strict-homothetic-compatibilit.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and lattice-complete with at least two points. Let $K$ be a full-dimensional $d$-simplex with centroid zero and volume $V$, and let $r_zK$ be positive compatible fibers at $z\in P$. Use the $d+1$ fixed continuous canonical centroid caps on every fiber, with total mass $M=V\sum_zr_z^d$ and $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. For $R>\max_{z\in P}\|z\|^2$, set
$$
t_z=r_z+\varepsilon(R-\|z\|^2),\qquad
\lambda=\left(\frac{\sum_zr_z^d}{\sum_zt_z^d}\right)^{1/d},\qquad s_z=\lambda t_z.
$$
For every $\varepsilon\ge0$ the family $s_zK$ is compatible and preserves $M$ and each canonical budget $\gamma_dM$. If $\varepsilon>0$, every anchored radius gap for a representation of its target using only other sites is at least $\lambda\varepsilon\min_{p\ne q}\|p-q\|^2$. Consequently there is an open product neighborhood of independently variable convex fibers around this family, each realized with exactly the original integer bases. An affine shear for the centroid field or use of the induced relative lattice preserves these conclusions.

If $d\ge2$, there are arbitrarily close actual compatible simplex families whose total volume is strictly larger and whose mass in each fixed canonical cap is strictly smaller. At any strictly compatible family, let $V_p,V_q$ be the positive volumes of two distinct fibers, $m=d+1$, and let $c$ be a nonzero zero-sum column vector in $\mathbb R^m$. The opposing weighted vertex lifts used below have aggregate Lagrangian Hessian
$$
H=\frac{d^2-1}{d(dm-1)}\|c\|^2\left(V_p+V_p^2/V_q\right)>0.
$$
A vertex acceleration gives second derivative $-\gamma_dH/2$ in every aggregate cap and $H/2$ in the total volume. For $d=1$ both fixed canonical cap budgets cannot be lowered while increasing total volume.

pk-intake-strict-inverse-power-minimum-d.relation_to_goal: Ordinary continuous maximal halfspace depth, with equality for centroid-centered simplex gauge profiles. Includes the log-concave consequence in dimension at least two.
pk-intake-strict-inverse-power-minimum-d.statement:
Let $r\ge2$ be an integer and $\beta>r+1$. Let $f$ be a nonnegative Lebesgue density on $\mathbb R^r$ of mass $M\in(0,\infty)$ with full-dimensional convex positive set. Assume $f^{-1/\beta}$, extended by $+\infty$ where $f=0$, is convex. Write $U=\operatorname{int}\{f>0\}$ and set $f=0$ on its boundary when taking the density representative. Define $D(f)$ to be the supremum over $y\in\mathbb R^r$ of the infimum of $\int_H f/M$ over closed halfspaces $H$ containing $y$. Put $\gamma_r=(r/(r+1))^r$. The supremum is attained in $U$ and $D(f)\ge\gamma_r$. Equality holds if and only if there are a point $y\in U$, a full-dimensional simplex $T\subset\mathbb R^r$ with centroid $0$, and a profile $F$ positive and continuous on $[0,R)$ for some $R\in(0,\infty]$ and zero for $t>R$, with $0<\int_0^R t^{r-1}F(t)\,dt<\infty$ and $F^{-1/\beta}$ convex and nondecreasing on $[0,R)$, such that
$$
f(y+x)=F(p_T(x))\qquad\text{for almost every }x\in\mathbb R^r,
$$
where $p_T$ is the Minkowski gauge of $T$. The point $y$ is a deepest point, and $U=y+\{x:p_T(x)<R\}$. If $T$ is the radial body at $y$, then $r\int_0^R t^{r-1}F(t)\,dt=1$.

In particular for a positive finite-mass log-concave density with full-dimensional positive support in dimension $r\ge2$, equality $D(f)=\gamma_r$ holds precisely for these centroid-centered simplex profiles with $F(t)=\exp(-h(t))$ on $[0,R)$ for a finite convex nondecreasing $h$, and zero beyond $R$. Values at a finite endpoint $R$ are immaterial.

pk-intake-strict-inverse-power-polytope-.relation_to_goal: Ordinary Lebesgue density and an interior anchor in dimension at least two. The facet equality uses the strict exponent beta > r+1 and concerns the actual continuous radial body.
pk-intake-strict-inverse-power-polytope-.statement:
Let $r\ge2$ be an integer and $\beta>r+1$. Let $f$ be a nonnegative Lebesgue density on $\mathbb R^r$ of mass $M\in(0,\infty)$ with full-dimensional convex positive set. Assume $f^{-1/\beta}$, extended by $+\infty$ where $f=0$, is convex. Write $U=\operatorname{int}\{f>0\}$ and set $f=0$ on its boundary when taking the density representative. For $y\in U$ the radii
$$
\rho_{B_y}(u)^r=r\int_0^\infty t^{r-1}f(y+tu)\,dt,\qquad u\in\mathbb S^{r-1},
$$
define a compact convex body $B_y$ containing $0$ in its interior. For every Borel set $E\subseteq\mathbb S^{r-1}$, the $f$-mass of rays from $y$ with directions in $E$ equals the volume of $B_y$ in the corresponding rays from $0$. In particular $|B_y|=M$, and every closed through-$y$ halfspace has the same mass as the volume of its translate intersected with $B_y$.

If $B_y$ is a polytope, let $p_{B_y}$ denote its Minkowski gauge. There are $R\in(0,\infty]$ and a profile $F$ positive and continuous on $[0,R)$ and zero for $t>R$ such that $f(y+x)=F(p_{B_y}(x))$ almost everywhere. On $[0,R)$ the function $F^{-1/\beta}$ is convex and nondecreasing. The positive interior is $U=y+\{x:p_{B_y}(x)<R\}$, and $r\int_0^R t^{r-1}F(t)\,dt=1$. The value at a finite endpoint $R$ is immaterial.

pk-intake-strict-mixed-cap-finite-family.relation_to_goal: Conditional volume promotion for actual cap covers and chosen exclusive pieces. The estimate does not lower-bound exclusive volumes in terms of cap mass.
pk-intake-strict-mixed-cap-finite-family.statement:
Let a compact convex set $D\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, have positive raw mixed $d$-volume $M$. Suppose a finite collection of closed ambient halfspaces has common normalized mixed mass $\tau$, and their open interiors cover the mixed trace of $D$. Fix a nonempty set $I$ of indices, and choose compact convex positive-volume pieces $A_i$ in the continuous fibers at integer bases $z_i$ for $i\in I$. Each piece is strictly inside its own cap and strictly outside every other cap. Put $V_i=|A_i|$, $Q=\operatorname{conv}\{z_i:i\in I\}$ and
$$
f_I(z)=\max\left\{\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i V_i^{1/d}:\lambda_i\ge0,\ \sum_i\lambda_i=1,\ \sum_i\lambda_i z_i=z\right\}.
$$
Then
$$
|I|\tau M\ge\sum_{z\in Q\cap\mathbb Z^n}\max\left(f_I(z)^d,\ \sum_{i\in I:z_i=z}V_i\right).
$$
For two distinct same-parity bases $z_i,z_j$, this gives
$$
2\tau M\ge V_i+V_j+\left(\frac{V_i^{1/d}+V_j^{1/d}}2\right)^d .
$$
For $k$ distinct same-parity bases with equal exclusive volumes $V$, it gives $V\le k\tau M/(2k-1)$.

pk-intake-strict-mixed-cap-same-fiber-wi.relation_to_goal: The common integer base is essential. No bound for an entire parity class follows.
pk-intake-strict-mixed-cap-same-fiber-wi.statement: Consider the mixed trace of a compact convex set, with a finite family of closed ambient halfspaces whose open interiors cover all its positive $d$-volume integer fibers, $d\ge1$. For each halfspace suppose there is a witness in the interior of a positive fiber that lies strictly inside its halfspace and strictly outside all the others. Then at most $d+1$ witnesses share any one integer base. If two witnesses share a base, the two corresponding open caps intersect inside that fiber in positive $d$-volume.

pk-intake-strict-monotone-median-reflect.relation_to_goal: Strict arithmetic improvement for finite monotone weights, with sharpness across support lengths. It does not infer reflection of the spatial fibers.

pk-intake-strict-nonzero-shift-centroid-.relation_to_goal: Scalar probability theorem and its ordinary convex-body specialization in integer dimensions d≥3. The strict bound concerns each fixed nonzero shift at the volume centroid.
pk-intake-strict-nonzero-shift-centroid-.statement:
Let $d\ge3$ be an integer and $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. If $Z$ has a compactly supported, nonatomic, centered $1/d$-concave probability law on $\mathbb R$, then for every $s\ne0$,
$$
\mathbb P(Z\ge s)+\mathbb P(Z\ge -s)>2\Gamma_d.
$$
In particular, if $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ is a convex body with volume $V>0$ and centroid $g$, then for each $u\ne0$ and $s\ne0$ the two closed caps $K\cap\{x:u\cdot(x-g)\ge s\}$ and $K\cap\{x:u\cdot(x-g)\ge -s\}$ have total volume greater than $2\Gamma_d V$.

pk-intake-strict-one-third-mixed-depth-a.relation_to_goal: True integer-base centroid, one integer and one continuous coordinate, and raw original-fiber length. The claim is conditional on the true centroid's integer base.
pk-intake-strict-one-third-mixed-depth-a.statement: Let $C\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R$ be compact and convex. Equip $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R)$ with the sum of the original integer-fiber lengths and assume its total mass $M$ is positive. If its true mixed-length centroid has integer base coordinate, it belongs to $S$ and has raw mixed length strictly greater than $M/3$ in the infimum over all closed ambient halfspaces containing it. This allows any finite number of positive integer fibers and also allows zero-length fibers.

pk-intake-strict-order-on-actual-tied-so.relation_to_goal: Pointwise ordering and actual slab accounting along the integral trace of one tied segment.
pk-intake-strict-order-on-actual-tied-so.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body, $d\ge1$, with positive total summed $d$-volume $\mu$ on $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. Let $D(Y)=\inf_{H\ni Y}\mu(H)$ use closed ambient halfspaces, and let $F(Y)$ be the $d$th root of raw ordinary depth in the actual fiber at $Y$. Put $P_\lambda(Y)=D(Y)+\lambda F(Y)$ and $E(\lambda)=\max_{Y\in S}P_\lambda(Y)$ for $\lambda\ge0$. Fix $\lambda>0$ and two $P_\lambda$ maximizers $Y_0,Y_1$ with $F_1>F_0$, and put $A=D_0-D_1=\lambda(F_1-F_0)>0$. Set $Y_t=(1-t)Y_0+tY_1$ and retain $t\in[0,1]$ whose base is integral. For each retained $0<t<1$, put $\Delta_t=F(Y_t)-(1-t)F_0-tF_1$. For every nonvertical depth-attaining through-$Y_t$ cap $H_t=\{L_t\ge0\}$,
$$
L_t(Y_0)<0<L_t(Y_1),\qquad D_1<D(Y_t)<D_0,\qquad F_0<F(Y_t)<F_1 .
$$
Along all retained parameters the actual depth is strictly decreasing and the own-depth root strictly increasing. For $0<t<s\le1$ both retained, the original slab $T_{t,s}=\mu\{0\le L_t<L_t(Y_s)\}$ satisfies
$$
0<T_{t,s}\le D(Y_t)-D(Y_s),\qquad
T_{t,1}+\lambda\Delta_t\le (1-t)A .
$$
Any finite increasing list of retained parameters $0<t_0<\cdots<t_N\le1$ has total adjacent slab charge at most $D(Y_{t_0})-D(Y_{t_N})\le A$. If the endpoint bases agree, each real $t$ is retained and no interior point of the segment is a local maximum of actual depth in that fiber.

pk-intake-strict-own-interior-physical-b.relation_to_goal: Pointwise actual cap geometry at an interior mark, including pure-base competitors. The bound gives a strict gain for a positive fixed displacement at that mark.
pk-intake-strict-own-interior-physical-b.statement:
Let $P$ be a finite nonempty real base with positive-volume compact convex fibers $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$. Use their summed volume measure. For a mark $Y=(p,y)$ with $y\in K_p$, let $D_0(Y)$ be ordinary raw closed-halfspace depth and $b_{\rm base}(p)$ be closed atomic base depth for weights $V_z=|K_z|$. Include the whole-base trace, the sole trace in rank zero. Then $D_0(Y)\le b_{\rm base}(p)-V_p/2$.

If $B(y,r)\subseteq K_p$ with $r>0$ and $\Gamma$ is a norm on continuous covectors with $\|u\|\le C$ whenever $\Gamma(u)=1$, let $D_\delta(Y)$ use a displacement $\delta\Gamma(u)$ added to each nonvertical through-mark margin, leaving pure-base caps unchanged, where $\delta>0$. Then
$$
D_\delta(Y)\ \ge\ D_0(Y)+\min\!\left\{\frac{V_p}{2},
\kappa_{d-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt3r}{2}\right)^{d-1}
\min\!\left(\frac r2,\frac{\delta}{C}\right)\right\}>D_0(Y),
$$
where $\kappa_{d-1}$ denotes the unit $(d-1)$-ball volume and $\kappa_0=1$.

pk-intake-strict-quota-centroid-reversal.relation_to_goal: This defeats feasibility of a particular reverse centroid-hull deformation under strict parity quotas.
pk-intake-strict-quota-centroid-reversal.statement:
At bases $-1,0,1$ put $K_-=K_+=[-1,1]\times[-3,0]$ and
$K_0=\operatorname{conv}\{(-2,0),(2,0),(2,-1),(1,-3),(-1,-3),(-2,-1)\}$.
These are exactly the integer fibers of the convex hull of their lifts. They have areas $(6,10,6)$ and centroids $(0,-3/2),(0,-4/3),(0,-3/2)$. For every nonempty proper closed base minor $T=P\cap\operatorname{conv}(T)$, with $P=\{-1,0,1\}$ and $k(T)$ the number of its parities, $\sum_{z\in T}|K_z|<22k(T)/2$.

Let $D_z$ be the fiber at $z$ of the convex hull of the three placed centroids. For every $s\ge0$ each $(1+s)h_{K_z}-s h_{D_z}$ is a support function. For every $s>0$ the reverse family fails the upward anchored support inequality at base zero by exactly $-s/6$.

pk-intake-strict-reflected-simplex-profi.relation_to_goal: An ordinary simplex profile used in a special mixed-depth theorem; no bound for arbitrary mixed-integer sources.
pk-intake-strict-reflected-simplex-profi.statement:
Let $T\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional simplex of volume $V$, centroid $g$, and barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$. Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. For a unit vector $u$, set $b=u\cdot g$, $\ell=\min_T u\cdot x$ and
$$
f(u)=\frac{|T\cap\lbrace u\cdot x\ge b\rbrace|}{V},\qquad
R(u)=\frac{|T\cap\lbrace u\cdot x\ge 2b-\ell\rbrace|}{V},\qquad
\rho_d=\min_{\lVert u\rVert=1}[f(u)-\Gamma_d+R(u)].
$$
Then $f(u)\ge\Gamma_d$, with equality precisely for the $d+1$ unit normals in the directions of $\nabla\lambda_i$. The constant $\rho_d$ is affine invariant; $\rho_1=0$, and for $d\ge2$,
$$
0<\rho_d\le\left(\frac{d-1}{d+1}\right)^d<\Gamma_d.
$$
Equivalently, $\rho_d$ is the minimum of $\Phi_r(\bar r)+\Phi_r(2\bar r)-\Gamma_d$ over $r=(r_0,\ldots,r_d)\in[0,1]^{d+1}$ with $\min_i r_i=0$, $\max_i r_i=1$, where $\bar r=\sum_i r_i/(d+1)$ and $\Phi_r(s)=\Pr(\sum_i r_i\lambda_i(X)\ge s)$ for $X$ uniform on $T$. In dimension two this minimum equals $2(\sqrt{10}-3)/9$ and its normalized vertex levels are $(0,1-\sqrt{2/5},1)$ up to permutation.

pk-intake-strict-triangle-actual-signed-.relation_to_goal: An actual area identity for one ordinary triangle and its three strict vertex caps.
pk-intake-strict-triangle-actual-signed-.statement:
Let $K$ be a nondegenerate planar triangle of area $k$ with $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. Let $v_1,v_2,v_3$ be nonzero spanning normals with $\sum_i v_i=0$. Suppose the caps $v_i\cdot(x-y)\ge0$ strictly capture distinct vertices $P_i$ and strictly exclude the other two vertices. Let $q_i$ be their area fractions, and use cyclic indices. Put $H=\sum_i v_i\cdot(P_i-y)$, $D=|\det(v_1,v_2)|$, $a_i=v_i\cdot(P_i-y)/H$, $b_{ij}=-v_i\cdot(P_j-y)/H$ for $i\ne j$, $d_i=b_{i,i+1}-b_{i,i+2}$, and $f_i=2a_i/\sqrt{q_i}$. Then
$$
R:=1+\Bigl(\sum_i d_i\Bigr)^2-2\sum_i d_i^2=4-\sum_i f_i^2=\frac{8Dk}{H^2}>0.
$$
If all $q_i\le128/279$, then $F:=\sum_i f_i\ge2/\sqrt{128/279}>59/20$ and $R\ge F^2+4F-20>201/400$.

pk-intake-strict-triangle-cap-floor.relation_to_goal: Ordinary triangle cap and source-coordinate bounds. The strict incidence is an explicit premise.
pk-intake-strict-triangle-cap-floor.statement: Let $K$ be a nondegenerate planar triangle, with an interior point $y$ and three caps cut by lines through $y$ that each strictly capture a different vertex and strictly exclude the other two. Let $q_i$ be the ordinary area fractions of the caps, indexed by the captured vertices. If $q_i\le128/279$ for all $i$, then each barycentric coordinate of $y$ is less than $5/14$, and each $q_i>20/49$.

pk-intake-strict-triangle-cubic-deficit.relation_to_goal: Exact cubic slack for ordinary strict triangle data, with a separate equality description.
pk-intake-strict-triangle-cubic-deficit.statement:
Let $K$ be a nondegenerate planar triangle with interior source $y$ and nonzero spanning normals $v_1,v_2,v_3$ that sum to zero. Suppose the through-source caps strictly capture three distinct vertices and strictly exclude the other vertices in each cap. Write $k=|K|$, $Q_i$ for the cap areas, $\sigma_i$ for the chord lengths divided by the respective $\lVert v_i\rVert$, and $f_i=2\sqrt{kQ_i}/(\sigma_i\sum_\ell Q_\ell/\sigma_\ell)$. In the exact parameterization $f_i=2\sqrt{u_i(1-u_{i+1})}$ with $0<u_i<1$ and $1<\sum_i u_i<2$, the cubic deficit satisfies
$$
4-\sum_i f_i^2-f_1f_2f_3
=4\left(\sqrt{\prod_i u_i}-\sqrt{\prod_i(1-u_i)}\right)^2\ge0.
$$
Consequently each row satisfies $f_i+(f_j+f_k)^2/4\le2$. Equality in this row holds exactly when the cubic deficit is zero and $f_j=f_k$, for $\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}$.

pk-intake-strict-triangle-psd-downward-h.relation_to_goal: Downward hull of the strict triangle image. Positive data have single-triangle dominators and nonnegative boundary data are treated by closure.
pk-intake-strict-triangle-psd-downward-h.statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be the ordinary strict triangle row image, equivalently the set of $f$ with $f_i=2\sqrt{u_i(1-u_{i+1})}$ for cyclic indices, $0<u_i<1$, and $1<\sum_i u_i<2$. For $f\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^3$ define $B(f)$ to have zero diagonal and symmetric cyclic entries $B(f)_{i,i+1}=B(f)_{i+1,i}=f_i/2$. Then
$$
D:=\{f\ge0:I-B(f)\succeq0\}=\left\{f\ge0:\sum_i f_i^2+f_1f_2f_3\le4\right\}
$$
is both the closed coordinatewise downward hull and the closed downward convex hull of $\mathcal T$, taken in the nonnegative orthant. Every strictly positive $f\in D$ has an attained single strict triangle dominator $f'=f/\rho\in\mathcal T$, where $\rho=\lambda_{\max}(B(f))\in(0,1]$.

pk-intake-strict-triangle-row-image.relation_to_goal: Actual strict ordinary triangle data, with a separate closed image for their limits.
pk-intake-strict-triangle-row-image.statement:
Let $K$ range over nondegenerate planar triangles, $y$ over their interior points, and $v_1,v_2,v_3$ over nonzero spanning normals with $\sum_i v_i=0$. Require that the cap $v_i\cdot(x-y)\ge0$ strictly capture vertex $P_i$ and strictly exclude the other two vertices, with the $P_i$ distinct. Let $k=|K|$, let $Q_i$ be the cap areas, let $\sigma_i$ be the cutting chord lengths divided by $\lVert v_i\rVert$, and set
$$
 f_i=\frac{2\sqrt{kQ_i}}{\sigma_i\sum_\ell Q_\ell/\sigma_\ell}.
$$
With indices modulo three, the set of these $f$-vectors is exactly
$$
 f_i=\sqrt{g_i^2-d_i^2},\qquad g_i=1-d_{i+1}+d_{i+2},\qquad \sum_i|d_i|<1.
$$
Equivalently, the set is exactly
$$
f_i=2\sqrt{u_i(1-u_{i+1})},\qquad
0<u_i<1,\qquad 1<\sum_i u_i<2 .
$$
Its closure is the image given by replacing the strict inequalities in either domain with weak inequalities.

pk-intake-strict-triangle-signed-row-def.relation_to_goal: Ordinary area and actual chords of a single triangle, with strict distinct-vertex incidence.
pk-intake-strict-triangle-signed-row-def.statement:
Let $K$ be a nondegenerate planar triangle, let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$, and let the nonzero spanning normals $v_1,v_2,v_3$ satisfy $\sum_i v_i=0$. Suppose the cap $v_i\cdot(x-y)\ge0$ strictly captures $P_i$ and strictly excludes the other two vertices, with $P_1,P_2,P_3$ distinct. Use indices modulo three. Put $q_i=|K\cap\lbrace v_i\cdot(x-y)\ge0\rbrace|/|K|$, $\sigma_i=\mathcal H^1(K\cap\lbrace v_i\cdot(x-y)=0\rbrace)/\lVert v_i\rVert$, and $\lambda_i=(1/\sigma_i)/\sum_\ell(1/\sigma_\ell)$.

Set $H=\sum_\ell v_\ell\cdot(P_\ell-y)$, $a_i=v_i\cdot(P_i-y)/H$, and $b_{ij}=-v_i\cdot(P_j-y)/H$ for $j\ne i$. All $a_i,b_{ij}$ are positive. With $d_i=b_{i,i+1}-b_{i,i+2}$, $g_i=1-d_{i+1}+d_{i+2}$, and $f_i=2a_i/\sqrt{q_i}$, the identities are
$$
\sum_i a_i=1,\qquad a_j=\sum_{i\ne j} b_{ij},\qquad
q_i=\frac{a_i^2}{(a_i+b_{i,i+1})(a_i+b_{i,i+2})},\qquad f_i=\sqrt{g_i^2-d_i^2},
$$
and
$$
\sum_i f_i\sqrt{q_i}=2,\qquad
\lambda_i=\frac{f_i/\sqrt{q_i}}{\sum_\ell f_\ell/\sqrt{q_\ell}}.
$$
For each $i$, with $\{j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}\setminus\{i\}$, the deficit satisfies
$$
2-f_i-\frac{(f_j+f_k)^2}{4}
=\frac{d_i^2}{g_i+f_i}
 +\frac{(g_jd_k+g_kd_j)^2}{2(g_jg_k+d_jd_k+f_jf_k)}\ge0.
$$
Equality holds precisely when $d_i=0$ and $d_j+d_k=0$, in which case $f_j=f_k$. Equivalently, writing $Q=\sum_\ell\lambda_\ell q_\ell$, the row inequalities are
$$
2\lambda_i\sqrt{q_i}\,Q+
  (\lambda_j\sqrt{q_j}+\lambda_k\sqrt{q_k})^2\le2Q^2 .
$$

pk-intake-strict-winner-score-cap-circul.relation_to_goal: An incidence statement for already realized positive winner cells. It imposes no cap volume bound and makes no depth assertion.
pk-intake-strict-winner-score-cap-circul.statement:
Let $C$ be a compact mixed-integer convex body with intrinsic mixed measure $\mu$. Let $L_i(z,x)=\beta_i+b_i\cdot z+u_i\cdot x$ be finitely many affine scores, with $\mu$-null pairwise ties and positive-mass winner cells $D_i=C\cap\bigcap_{k\ne i}\{L_i\ge L_k\}$. In particular, null ties hold when the score differences are nonconstant on each positive intrinsic fiber. Write $t_i=\mu(D_i)$, $y_i=(j_i,c_i)$ for its mixed centroid and $\ell_i=L_i-L_i(y_i)$. Then
$$
\Delta_{ki}=L_k(y_k)-L_i(y_k)=t_k^{-1}\int_{D_k}(L_k-L_i)\,d\mu>0\quad(k\ne i).
$$
For every nonnegative off-diagonal circulation $\alpha$ (its row and column sums agree label by label),
$$
\sum_{i,k}\alpha_{ik}\ell_i(y_k)=-\sum_{i,k}\alpha_{ik}\Delta_{ki}.
$$
Consequently the relation $i\to k$ for $i\ne k$ and $\ell_i(y_k)\ge0$ is acyclic. For arbitrary centered margins $h_i(z,x)=a_i\cdot(z-j_i)+v_i\cdot(x-c_i)$ the corresponding identity is
$$
\sum_{i,k}\alpha_{ik}h_i(y_k)=
-\sum_{i,k}\alpha_{ik}\Delta_{ki}
+\sum_{i,k}\alpha_{ik}\big[(a_i-b_i)\cdot(j_k-j_i)+(v_i-u_i)\cdot(c_k-c_i)\big].
$$
In particular, if $v_i=u_i$, $\alpha\ne0$ and every positive-weight edge captures its destination, the base correction is at least $\sum_{i,k}\alpha_{ik}\Delta_{ki}>0$. For finite families $h_{ir}$ of such margins with weights $\rho_{ir}\ge0$, $\sum_r\rho_{ir}=1$ and $\sum_r\rho_{ir}v_{ir}=0$, the averaged circulation is exactly $\sum_{i,k}\alpha_{ik}(\sum_r\rho_{ir}a_{ir})\cdot(j_k-j_i)$.

pk-intake-strictly-convex-outer-approxim.relation_to_goal: Exact conditional depth transfer under explicit strict-convex outer approximation in fixed dimensions.
pk-intake-strictly-convex-outer-approxim.statement:
Let $n,d\ge0$ be integers with $m=n+d\ge1$, and let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body with positive mixed $d$-volume $M$, with counting measure when $d=0$. Choose $R\ge1$ with $C\subset R B_m$ and a finite $1/k$-net $U_k$ of the unit sphere containing the signed coordinate vectors. With $T_k=k(R^2+1)+R$ and $h_C(u)=\max_{x\in C}u\cdot x$, put
$$
C_k=\bigcap_{u\in U_k}B(-T_k u,T_k+h_C(u)+1/k),
$$
where the balls are closed. These bodies are strictly convex, contain $C$ in their interiors, and satisfy
$$
d_H(C_k,C)\le\frac{1+\sqrt m(R+1)+R}{k}.
$$
Eventually the nonempty integer bases are exactly those of $C$. Each original nonempty integer fiber is full-dimensional in $C_k$ and converges in Hausdorff distance to its original fiber.

Let $\mu_k,\mu$ be the ambient measures obtained by summing the $d$-volumes of their respective fibers, with totals $M_k,M$. Then
$$
\sup_{A\ \mathrm{Borel}}|\mu_k(A)-\mu(A)|=\delta_k=M_k-M\longrightarrow0.
$$
If $A_\nu(y)=\inf_{H\ni y}\nu(H)$ for closed ambient halfspaces, then
$$
\sup_y\left|\frac{A_{\mu_k}(y)}{M_k}-\frac{A_\mu(y)}{M}\right|\le\frac{\delta_k}{M_k}.
$$
Every subsequential limit of mixed points $y_k\in C_k$ of normalized depth at least $c$ is an original mixed point of normalized depth at least $c$. For $d\ge2$, all positive fibers of the approximants have zero $\mathcal H^{d-1}$ measure on each supporting hyperplane. For $d=1$, a supporting endpoint of a positive interval has $\mathcal H^0$ measure one. For $d=0$, the counting measures eventually coincide.

pk-intake-strictly-convex-planar-cut-and.relation_to_goal: Ordinary planar caps in the Hausdorff topology. Perturbations need not be strictly convex; no shape reduction for arbitrary bodies.
pk-intake-strictly-convex-planar-cut-and.statement: Use the three normals $v_1=(1,0)$, $v_2=(0,1)$, $v_3=(-1,-1)$ through the interior mark $0$. For a planar convex body $K$, let $q_i$ be the cap areas, $\sigma_i=\mathcal H^1(K\cap v_i^\perp)/\lVert v_i\rVert$, and $\lambda_i=(1/\sigma_i)/\sum_j(1/\sigma_j)$. Assume $K$ is compact and strictly convex. For every selected index $i$, there are convex bodies converging to $K$ in Hausdorff distance, containing $0$ in their interiors, preserving total area and the other two cap areas and coarea chord lengths, strictly decreasing $q_i$ and increasing $\sigma_i$. Thus $\lambda_i$ strictly decreases while any initially satisfied bounds $q_j\le c_j|K|$ and $q_{\min}+q_{\mathrm{mid}}+q_{\max}/4\le |K|$ remain satisfied. By choosing an initially minimal $\lambda_i$, the minimum of the three weights also strictly decreases. In particular $K$ is not a local minimum of either specified objective in the full feasible convex-body class.

pk-intake-strong-barycentric-surplus-inv.relation_to_goal: Fixed-marginal transport optimizer structure, including singular and mixed-fiber marginals.
pk-intake-strong-barycentric-surplus-inv.statement: Let $k,N\ge1$. Let $\gamma_i$ be compactly supported finite nonnegative Borel measures on $\mathbb R^N$ of common mass $M>0$, and let $\lambda_i>0$ with $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$. Set $b(x)=\sum_i\lambda_i x_i$. Let $\phi\in C^2(\mathbb R^N)$ with $D^2\phi\ge\varepsilon I_N$ everywhere for some $\varepsilon>0$. There are finite convex $C^1$ functions $V_i$ on $\mathbb R^N$ with globally Lipschitz gradients such that, for $F_i(z)=\nabla V_i(\lambda_i\nabla\phi(z))$, every coupling $\pi$ maximizing $\int \phi(b(x))\,d\pi(x)$ satisfies $x_i=F_i(b(x))$ for $\pi$-almost every tuple. In particular $F_i$ is locally Lipschitz, $(F_i)_\#(b_\#\pi)=\gamma_i$, and $\sum_i\lambda_i F_i(z)=z$ for $b_\#\pi$-almost every $z$.

pk-intake-supporting-facet-incoming-mass.relation_to_goal: Exact restriction and straightening for a supplied marked martingale on actual positive integer fibers. This identifies a reduced volume law and its correction, without asserting a lower-dimensional boundary-stress law.
pk-intake-supporting-facet-incoming-mass.statement:
Let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact polytope, $d\ge1$, whose nonempty integer fibers are all positive $d$-volume. Let $\eta$ be the sum of their boundary $\mathcal H^{d-1}$ measures, with the regular outward continuous unit normal marked, and let $\Pi$ be a physical martingale coupling from a finite $\nu\ll\eta$ to $\eta$ preserving that mark. Let $F=C\cap\{a\cdot z+u\cdot x=b\}$ be a nonvertical supporting facet with $|u|=1$ and $a\cdot z+u\cdot x\le b$ on $C$. Restrict the physical points to $F$ with their marks retained. The target of the rows starting in $F$ is $\eta|_F-\zeta_F$, where $\zeta_F$ is exactly the target law of the rows starting outside $F$ and ending in $F$. Its mass is
$$
L_F=\eta(F)-\nu(F)=\Pi\{w\notin F,\ w'\in F\}\ge0.
$$
The raw restriction of the coupling has target $\eta|_F$ exactly when $L_F=0$. In general it extends, by adding the diagonal coupling of $\zeta_F$, to a martingale from $\nu|_F+\zeta_F$ to $\eta|_F$. Without the correction, $\int_F\psi\,d\nu\le\int_F\psi\,d\eta$ for each finite nonnegative convex function on the affine plane of $F$.

Let $E:\mathbb R^{d-1}\to u^\perp$ be a linear isometry, $\Psi(z,t)=(z,Et+(b-a\cdot z)u)$, and $D=\Psi^{-1}(F)$. Then $D$ is full-dimensional in $\mathbb R^{n+d-1}$ with its entire integer trace, and
$$
(\Psi^{-1})_\#(\eta|_F)=\mu_F=\sum_{p\in\mathbb Z^n}\mathcal H^{d-1}|_{D_p}.
$$
The common mark $u$ is forgotten in this equality. If $\eta(F)>0$, $\mu_F$ is the intrinsic Hausdorff measure on the mixed trace of $D$. The ambient Jacobian of $\Psi$ is $\sqrt{1+|a|^2}$ and the corresponding base projection coarea Jacobian is its reciprocal. The displayed mixed fiber law has no slope factor. At $d=1$ the nonempty reduced fibers are singletons, with unit counting mass. The pullback laws satisfy $\widehat\nu_F+\widehat\zeta_F\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}}\mu_F$ in equal-mass convex order, with the correction of mass $L_F$.

If $d\nu=\sum_j\lambda_j\alpha_j\,d\eta$ for a finite cap menu with actual bounded Borel body allocations and $\lambda_j\ge0$, the reduced source density is $\sum_j\lambda_j(\alpha_j\circ\Psi)$ relative to $\mu_F$. An ambient cap $c_j\cdot z+v_j\cdot x\ge b_j$ pulls back to
$$
(c_j-(v_j\cdot u)a)\cdot z+(E^{\mathsf T}v_j)\cdot t
\ \ge\ b_j-(v_j\cdot u)b .
$$
A zero linear part gives the entire reduced space or the empty set. At strict traces the density selector is the literal indicator. At an equality locus of positive measure the original allocation is retained. If every affine cap-plane equality locus is $\mu_F$-null, the source is exactly the weighted sum of closed trace indicators almost everywhere.

If $\eta$-almost every measured point lies on exactly one nonvertical ambient facet, then $L_F=0$ for every such facet.

pk-intake-supporting-facet-section-minko.relation_to_goal: This is an ordinary sectional Brunn–Minkowski estimate with a mixed three-fiber cap application. It retains the geometric effect of the zero-d-volume endpoint support facet.
pk-intake-supporting-facet-section-minko.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $D$ be a convex body in $\mathbb R^d$, and let $F$ be a compact convex subset of a hyperplane normal to the unit vector $e$, with $f=\mathcal H^{d-1}(F)>0$. Translate $F$ to height zero in this direction, let $I$ be the open height interval of $D$, and write $h=|I|$, $m=d-1$, $U=|D|$ and $D_t$ for the height-$t$ section identified with $e^\perp$. Then $(D+F)_t=D_t+F$, and
$$
\begin{aligned}
|D+F|&\ge\int_I\bigl(|D_t|^{1/m}+f^{1/m}\bigr)^m\,dt\\
&=U+fh+\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}\binom mj f^{j/m}\int_I |D_t|^{(m-j)/m}\,dt .
\end{aligned}
$$
For $d=2$, $|D+F|=U+fh$.

In particular, suppose $A,K,B$ are convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$ with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$, $u\ne0$, $D=A\cap\{u\cdot x\ge a_0\}$ is a proper positive-volume cap, and $B\subseteq\{u\cdot x\le b_0\}$ has a support facet $F=B\cap\{u\cdot x=b_0\}$ with $f=\mathcal H^{d-1}(F)>0$. For $q=|K\cap\{u\cdot x\ge(a_0+b_0)/2\}|$, the first bound above applies to $2^dq$ with $e=u/\lVert u\rVert$ and $h=(h_A(u)-a_0)/\lVert u\rVert$, where $h_A$ is the support function of $A$. In particular $2^dq\ge U+fh$. If these bodies are the positive-volume fibers at $-1,0,1$ of a mixed body and the closed ambient cap with these three thresholds has raw mixed mass $Q$, then $2^d Q\ge (2^d+1)U+fh$.

For $d=2$, $B=T=\{x:v_i\cdot x\le1,\ i=1,2,3\}$ and $(v_1,v_2,v_3)=((1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1))$, the cap $v_i\cdot x\ge z$ has $2^d Q_i=4Q_i\ge5U_i+3(h_A(v_i)+1)$ for every proper positive $A$ trace of area $U_i$.

pk-intake-supporting-facets-strict-mixed.relation_to_goal: Actual local cap geometry at a fixed mixed point. The conclusion concerns a neighborhood of oriented through-point normals.
pk-intake-supporting-facets-strict-mixed.statement: Set $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2)$, $B=(1/3,1/6)+T/3$, and $C=\operatorname{conv}((\{-1\}\times B)\cup(\{0\}\times T)\cup(\{1\}\times B))$. The actual integer fibers are $B,T,B$, with total mixed area $11/18$. At $y_*=(0,1/3,1/3)$, the cap $x\le1/3$ is a strict local minimum of original raw cap mass over all nearby oriented through-point halfspaces, with mass $5/18$ and normalized fraction $5/11$. It strictly contains two vertices of $T$; the middle section has centroid with barycentric coordinates $(1/3,1/3,1/3)$ and the two endpoint sections are full supporting edges with centroid barycentric coordinates $(1/2,0,1/2)$ in their respective triangles. The cap mass in the full normal chart is locally Lipschitz and nondifferentiable at the cap, with zero in its Clarke subdifferential.

pk-intake-surface-area-ball-cut-localiza.relation_to_goal: Ordinary surface area under a geometric truncation. The strict support condition is needed to exclude cutting-sphere contributions.
pk-intake-surface-area-ball-cut-localiza.statement:
Let $L\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, be a convex body, let $B(c,a)$ be an open Euclidean ball of positive radius, and suppose $L'=L\cap\overline{B(c,a)}$ is full dimensional. Write $\eta_L$ for $\mathcal H^{d-1}$ on its regular boundary marked by its unique outer unit normal, $S_L$ for the normal marginal, and $G(v,x)=v$ for projection to the normal. On the open normal set $V=\{v\in\mathbb S^{d-1}:h_L(v)<v\cdot c+a\}$,
$$
 S_{L'}|_V=\bigl[G_\#(\mathbf 1_{\{x\in B(c,a)\}}\eta_L)\bigr]|_V.
$$
If the exposed face of $L$ at $v$ meets the open ball, then $v\in V$ and the cut body is full dimensional.

pk-intake-surface-area-domination-on-con.relation_to_goal: Ordinary area measures on the exact support equality set, including singular measures. The midpoint comparison applies to one compatible triple of mixed fibers.
pk-intake-surface-area-domination-on-con.statement:
Let $L\subseteq K$ be full-dimensional compact convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, and let $Z=\{u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}:h_L(u)=h_K(u)\}$. Then
$$
S_L|_Z\le S_K|_Z.
$$
For full-dimensional compact convex bodies $A,B,K$ with $M=(A+B)/2\subseteq K$, it follows with $Z=\{h_M=h_K\}$ that
$$
(S_A\wedge S_B)|_Z\le S_K|_Z.
$$
For $d=1$, the area measure is counting measure on the two endpoint normals.

pk-intake-surviving-cap-group-section-ce.relation_to_goal: A surviving group's conditional ordinary limit with all through-contact equations explicitly retained. The conclusion concerns its assigned bases and its coarea law.
pk-intake-surviving-cap-group-section-ce.statement:
Use the joint actual cap-record and allocation limit on fixed finite positive fibers. In a retained group at index $j$, write $H_{jk}$ for its caps, $\omega_{jk}$ for their actual law weights, $T_{jk}$ and $\bar w_{jk}$ for their allocated coareas and full physical section means, and $u_{jk}$ for their continuous normals. Let the group's finitely many labeled contact marks $Y_{ja}=(p_a,y_{ja})$ converge with fixed bases and a uniform own inball radius $r_s>0$. Suppose every cap has margin $\delta_{ja}\ge0$ at every group contact, with $\max_a\delta_{ja}\to0$. Let $\Sigma_j$ be the converging covariance matrices from the cap normalization and assume the actual same-coefficient identities
$$
\begin{gathered}
\kappa_j=\sum_a\kappa_{ja},\qquad
e_{ja}=\kappa_{ja}\delta_{ja},\qquad e_j=\sum_a e_{ja},\qquad
\bar Y_j=\kappa_j^{-1}\sum_a\kappa_{ja}Y_{ja},\\
\omega_{jk}T_{jk}=\kappa_j\rho_{jk},\qquad \sum_k\rho_{jk}=1,\qquad
\bar w_{jk}=\bar Y_j-(e_j/\kappa_j)(0,\Sigma_j u_{jk}),\\
\kappa_j\sum_k\rho_{jk}u_{jk}=\sum_a e_{ja}b_{ja},
\qquad |b_{ja}|\le(1+1/N)/r_s,\quad N=d+1,
\end{gathered}
$$
with nonnegative weights. For a positive limiting group weight, after retaining the limits of the finitely many $\kappa_{ja}$ the limiting $\kappa>0$ and the coarea-weighted law is the probability $d\rho(H)=T_Hd\Lambda(H)/\kappa$. For $\rho$-almost every cap its allocated full section mean is $\bar Y=\kappa^{-1}\sum_a\kappa_aY_a$, and $\int u\,d\rho=0$. Every support cap passes through all of the group's limiting contacts and has a proper section there. The support caps cover the whole continuous space at every one of those bases. If $Q$ is separately identified with ordinary maximal depth and the marks are ordinary deepest, those through-mark caps are critical.

pk-intake-symmetric-base-pyramid-balance.relation_to_goal: Exact ordinary-volume conclusion for this uniform-body family. The stationary balanced menus split, so no conclusion for irreducible full-rank menus of general bodies follows.
pk-intake-symmetric-base-pyramid-balance.statement:
Under the hypotheses of the symmetric-base pyramid centroidal section classification, choose finitely many inward unit normals $u_i$ to through-zero sections whose Euclidean area centroid is zero. Let $S_i$ be the section areas. If $\theta_i\ge0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$, and $\sum_i\theta_iS_i u_i=0$, then
$$
\sum_i\theta_i\,|K\cap\{x:u_i\cdot x\ge0\}|=\frac{|K|}{2}.
$$
The apex-facing and opposite horizontal cap fractions are $[H/(H+1)]^d$ and its complement. At $H=d-1$ each vertical cap has fraction $1/2$, and the vector balance splits into the line of horizontal-section normals and the subspace of vertical-section normals. In particular the mean fraction strictly exceeds $(d/(d+1))^d$.

pk-intake-symmetric-base-pyramid-centroi.relation_to_goal: Uniform pyramid with an arbitrary centrally symmetric base and height in (0,d−1]. Does not classify sections for arbitrary bases or larger heights.
pk-intake-symmetric-base-pyramid-centroi.statement: Let $d\ge2$, let $D\subset\mathbb R^{d-1}$ be a centrally symmetric convex body with center zero, and fix $0<H\le d-1$. Put $K=\operatorname{conv}(D\times\{-1\},\{(0,H)\})$. Every oblique through-zero section of $K$, meaning neither horizontal nor vertical, has strictly negative mean height with respect to Euclidean section area. The horizontal section has centroid zero. Every vertical section has centroid $(0,(H-(d-1))/d)$. Thus the horizontal section is the only through-zero section whose centroid is zero for $H<d-1$; at $H=d-1$, all vertical sections and the horizontal section have centroid zero.

pk-intake-symmetric-base-truncated-proje.relation_to_goal: Supplies a sharp ordinary ratio for truncated centrally symmetric convex bases.
pk-intake-symmetric-base-truncated-proje.statement:
Let $D\subset\mathbb R^m$ be a convex body centrally symmetric about zero, $m\ge1$. Let $A=D\cap\{b:a\cdot b\le T\}$ for $a\ne0$, $T>0$, and put $v=|A|/|D|$. Define the projective energy at zero by
$$
E_A(0)=\inf_{\ell:\,1+\ell\cdot b>0\ \text{on }A}\int_A(1+\ell\cdot b)^{-m-1}\,db.
$$
Then
$$
2v-1\le\frac{E_A(0)}{|D|}\le\frac{2v-1}{v},
\qquad
\frac49\le\frac{v}{1+E_A(0)/|D|}\le\frac12.
$$
The lower ratio $4/9$ is attained for $m=1$, $D=[-1,1]$, $A=[-1,1/3]$. For $m\ge2$ and $v<1$, the lower ratio inequality is strict.

pk-intake-symmetric-planar-ear-strict-lo.statement: For $x,u,v>0$ and $\delta\ge0$ let $K$ be the convex hull of $(2v,-v),(-x,x+u),(-x-\delta,(x+\delta)/2),(-x,-u)$. pk-intake-symmetric-proper-block-at-regu.relation_to_goal: An all-length necessary condition for a regular through-mark minimizing tilt in continuous dimension one, with endpoints excluded from its regularity hypothesis.
pk-intake-symmetric-proper-block-at-regu.statement: Let the positive interval fibers $[l_i,h_i]$ at consecutive integer bases $0,\ldots,N$ have a convex lower roof and a concave upper roof. A cap boundary $x=y+a(z-p)$ passes through an actual mark $(p,y)$ and misses every sampled endpoint. The proper sections form a consecutive block $l,\ldots,r$ containing $p$. If the mass of the cap $x\ge y+a(z-p)$ is locally minimized in $a$, then $l+r=2p$. Thus the block has odd size, can contain the right endpoint only for $p\ge N/2$, the left endpoint only for $p\le N/2$, and both only for even $N$ and $p=N/2$.
