pk-intake-two-corner-one-double-edge-exa.relation_to_goal: Exact ordinary planar frontier for the specified two-loss branch. The cap ceiling is a separate condition if required by an application.
pk-intake-two-corner-one-double-edge-exa.statement:
In the fixed-ray setting of the reciprocal sector-change lemma, assume exactly two positive unique reciprocal losses $\ell_i,\ell_j$. All double gains other than the one on their common edge must vanish. For proposed areas satisfying the same positive finite area and core bounds and with those other gains zero, let $g$ denote the remaining gain, let $\theta_i,\theta_j$ be the positive entries of the corresponding triangle kernels at its two endpoints, and let $\lambda_i,\lambda_j$ be their block scales. The data are realizable if and only if
$$
g\left(\frac{\theta_i^2}{\ell_i}+\frac{\theta_j^2}{\ell_j}+\frac1{\lambda_i}+\frac1{\lambda_j}\right)\le1.
$$
Write $g_*$ for the reciprocal of the bracket and $Y^T$ for this double sector's original area. When $g_*<1/(2Y^T)$, the maximum finite double area is $Y^T/(1-2Y^Tg_*)$. When $g_*\ge1/(2Y^T)$, this frontier imposes no further finite upper bound. At finite equality the matrix has rank four and there is an exact quadrilateral realization.

pk-intake-two-endpoint-optimized-cap-qua.relation_to_goal: The endpoint contribution for two opposite tilt shifts at one continuous normal.
pk-intake-two-endpoint-optimized-cap-qua.statement:
Let $A,C\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies, $d\ge1$, of volumes $0<a\le c$. Fix a unit vector $u$ and write $U_A(t)=|A\cap\{u\cdot x\ge t\}|$ and $U_C(t)=|C\cap\{u\cdot x\ge t\}|$. Set $K(t)=\inf_{v\in\mathbb R}[U_A(t+v)+U_C(t-v)]$. Write $q_A,q_C$ for their decreasing upper-cap quantiles at masses in $[0,a]$ and $[0,c]$, taking the upper and lower support endpoints at mass zero and full mass respectively. For $0<r<a$, the unique threshold with $K(t)=r$ is
$$
q_K(r)=\frac12\min_{0\le s\le r}\bigl(q_A(s)+q_C(r-s)\bigr).
$$
The root $K^{1/d}$ is concave on its entire positive set, including the left constant plateau. If a convex body $B$ contains $(A+C)/2$, then $K(t)\le2|B\cap\{u\cdot x\ge t\}|$ for every real $t$.

pk-intake-two-endpoint-sector-envelope.relation_to_goal: A planar sector bound from two actual chord endpoints.
pk-intake-two-endpoint-sector-envelope.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a convex body with $0$ in its interior. Suppose the endpoints of the $K$ chords on the negative $y$-axis and on the positive-$x$ ray of $x+y=0$ are $(0,-\beta)$ and $(\rho,-\rho)$, with $\beta,\rho>0$. In the coordinates $u=-y$, $v=x+y$, the sector $K\cap\{y<0<x+y\}$ lies in
$$
u>0,\qquad v>0,\qquad \beta u+(\beta-\rho)v\le\beta\rho.
$$
When $\beta>\rho$, its area is at most $\beta\rho^2/[2(\beta-\rho)]$. Equality holds exactly when the closure of the sector in $(u,v)$ is the corresponding closed triangle. This bound is attained for each $\beta>\rho$. When $\beta\le\rho$, the two endpoints alone give no finite uniform area bound for the sector.

pk-intake-two-interval-affine-buffer-esc.relation_to_goal: Fixed body and positive affine multiplier optimization. The larger singleton has weight $3/2>M/2=5/4$ and violates its proper-minor quota. Its ordinary raw maximum $3/4$ exceeds the sharp $n=d=1$ target $M/4=5/8$.
pk-intake-two-interval-affine-buffer-esc.statement:
Let $C$ be the trapezoid obtained as the convex hull of centered intervals of lengths $a=1$ and $b=3/2$ at the consecutive bases $0$ and $1$. Use mixed length $M=5/2$, pooled within-fiber variance $\Sigma=7/48$ and $c^2=\Sigma/M=7/120$. For a centered interval of length $V$ use projective energy $E_V(y)=V-4y^2/V$ on $[-V/2,V/2]$, extended by zero at the endpoints. Impose positive affine multipliers with $\ell_a^2\ell_b^3=1$. At the mark $(i,y)$ in the interval of length $V$, move the threshold of every through-mark cap with continuous coefficient of unit magnitude outward by $\delta_i(y)=\varepsilon c\sqrt{\ell_i E_V(y)}$, leaving pure-base caps unchanged. The exact buffered raw depth is $\min\{V,V/2-|y|+\delta_i(y)\}$, and the fiber maximum is $\min\{V,V/2+\varepsilon c\sqrt{\ell_i V}\}$, achieved at the midpoint and uniquely so when the latter value is below $V$.

Define $\varepsilon_*^{10}=120^5/(221184\cdot7^5)$. For $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_*$ the buffered maximum over both fibers has a unique minimizing multiplier. Its optimal value $q_\varepsilon$ is the unique root in $(3/4,1)$ of
$$
(q-1/2)^4(q-3/4)^6=(3/2)^3(\varepsilon c)^{10}.
$$
At the minimizing multiplier,
$$
\ell_a=\frac{(q_\varepsilon-1/2)^2}{\varepsilon^2c^2},
\qquad
\ell_b=\frac{(q_\varepsilon-3/4)^2}{(3/2)\varepsilon^2c^2}.
$$
The only buffered maximizing marks are the two midpoints and their minimizing nonvertical own cuts are proper. As $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, $q_\varepsilon\to3/4$, $\varepsilon^2\ell_a\to15/14$, $\ell_b\sim(14/15)^{2/3}\varepsilon^{4/3}$, and the midpoint shifts tend to $1/4$ and $0$, respectively. The ordinary maximum is $3/4$, attained only at the larger midpoint.

At $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_*$ the optimal value is $1$ and the two unsaturated formulas meet at shifts $1/2$ and $1/4$. For every $\varepsilon>\varepsilon_*$ the optimal value is again $1$, with an optimizer whose shifts are strictly greater than $1/2$ and equal to $1/4$, respectively. At these specified optimizing multipliers for $\varepsilon\ge\varepsilon_*$ a minimizing nonvertical cap captures the whole smaller interval, as does a pure-base isolating cap. The smaller own trace is supporting at the specified crossing multiplier for $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_*$.

pk-intake-two-parity-forced-midpoint-den.statement: In $\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R$, let $\gamma_1$ be unit Lebesgue measure on each interval $\{0\}\times[0,1]$ and $\{1\}\times[0,1]$, and let $\gamma_2$ be unit Lebesgue measure on each interval $\{2\}\times[0,1]$ and $\{1\}\times[0,1]$. pk-intake-two-piece-integer-centroid-loc.relation_to_goal: Already for n=d=q=1, the example refutes a per-piece local-depth strengthening of integer-centroid partition existence. The original body satisfies the sharp bound at the middle-fiber midpoint, so it also satisfies the locked weak bound.
pk-intake-two-piece-integer-centroid-loc.statement:
Let $C=\{(z,x)\in\mathbb R^2:0\le z\le2,\ 0\le x\le z+1\}$ and let $\mu$ be the restriction of $\mathcal H_1$ to $C\cap(\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R)$, equivalently the sum of the lengths on the three integer fibers. Suppose at most two closed convex subsets of $C$, each of positive $\mu$-mass, partition the mixed set up to $\mu$-null omissions and overlaps, and each has a true mixed centroid with integer base coordinate. Then there are exactly two pieces, $D$ and $E$, of masses $4$ and $2$ and base centroid coordinates $1$ and $2$, respectively. The true mixed centroid $y_D=\mu(D)^{-1}\int_D (z,x)\,d\mu$ lies on the boundary of a closed ambient halfspace $H$ with $\mu(D\cap H)=7/4$ and $\mu(E\cap H)=0$. Hence its normalized halfspace depth in $D$ is at most $7/16<\gamma_1=1/2$.

Such partitions exist even with full-dimensional pieces covering all of $C$. This body therefore disproves the assertion that every mixed-integer convex body admits an exhaustive partition into at most $2^n$ positive-mass closed convex pieces whose true mixed centroids have integer bases and each have normalized depth at least $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ within their own pieces.

pk-intake-two-plane-inverse-moment-escap.relation_to_goal: The example concerns a fixed inverse moment and a single interval. A strictly positive limit can fail for these representatives.
pk-intake-two-plane-inverse-moment-escap.statement:
For $0<e<1$ on $[0,1]$ let $H_e(x)=\min(1,e+x/e^2)$ and $I_e=1+e(1-e)^2$. The two-plane positive concave functions $L_e=\sqrt{I_e}H_e$ satisfy $\int_0^1 L_e^{-2}=1$. They converge to $1$ locally uniformly on $(0,1]$, while $L_e(0)\to0$. For the marked interval energy $E(x)=4x(1-x)$, the functions $\sqrt{L_e E}$ converge uniformly to $\sqrt E$, so the fixed-scale covariance-buffered depths converge uniformly to those for multiplier one. More generally for each fixed $r>1$, replacing the slope by $A=e^{-r}$ gives
$$
\int_0^1\min(1,e+Ax)^{-r}\,dx
=1+\frac{e^{1-r}-1}{A(r-1)}-\frac{1-e}{A}\longrightarrow1,
$$
and for $r=1$ take $A=e^{-1}$ and replace the first correction by $\log(1/e)/A$. Normalizing by the $1/r$ power of this integral likewise gives positive two-plane weights with a vanishing endpoint value.

pk-intake-two-positive-envelope-equal-co.relation_to_goal: An equal-coordinate scalar critical point location, with all integer dimensions covered by the polynomial sign argument.
pk-intake-two-positive-envelope-equal-co.statement:
For every integer $m\ge2$ and $0<x<1$, set $E=(1-x)^{-m}-1$, $\rho=(1+E)^{-1}$, $Z=E((m+1)x-1)+mx$, and $h_c=x+Z/E$. On the open interval $x<h<1$, the function
$$
R(h)=\rho(E+h)\left[1-\frac{(E+h)(h-x)^m}{h^{m+1}}\right]
$$
has exactly one critical point, its maximum. That point satisfies $h<h_c$.

pk-intake-two-positive-envelope-pair-sta.relation_to_goal: A conditional local-minimum threshold for the positive-coordinate scalar gap.
pk-intake-two-positive-envelope-pair-sta.statement:
For an integer $m\ge1$ and $0\le x_j\le h<1$ with some $x_j>0$, put $\rho=\prod_j(1-x_j)$, $E=\rho^{-1}-1$, and
$$
L=\left(1-\frac{\sum_j x_j}{E}\right)\prod_j(1+x_j/E),\qquad
R=\rho(E+h)\left[1-\frac{(E+h)\prod_j(h-x_j)}{h^{m+1}}\right].
$$

Suppose $m\ge2$ and $x_1=\cdots=x_m=x$ with $0<x<h<1$ is a local minimum of $L-R$ in the full open domain and $L-R\le0$. In particular $E=(1-x)^{-m}-1$. Put $Z=E((m+1)x-1)+mx$, $A=Z+x(E+x)$, $h_c=x+Z/E$, and $h_b=EA/[(E+1)(E-mx)]$. Then
$$
h\ge h_b>h_c>x,\qquad h_b-h_c=\frac{Z^2}{E(E+1)(E-mx)}.
$$

pk-intake-two-positive-scalar-envelope-u.relation_to_goal: Scalar upper faces obtained by sending a single raw negative phase to infinity before taking any additional coordinate limits.
pk-intake-two-positive-scalar-envelope-u.statement:
For an integer $m\ge1$ and $0\le x_j\le h<1$ with some $x_j>0$, put $\rho=\prod_j(1-x_j)$, $E=\rho^{-1}-1$, and
$$
L=\left(1-\frac{\sum_j x_j}{E}\right)\prod_j(1+x_j/E),\qquad
R=\rho(E+h)\left[1-\frac{(E+h)\prod_j(h-x_j)}{h^{m+1}}\right].
$$

Also set $Q=\prod_j(1+x_j/E)$, $B=\sum_j x_j/(1-x_j)$, $C=B/(1-\rho)-1$, and $W=(1-h)CQ$.

If some $x_j=h$, both $L\ge R$ and $W\ge R$. On a face with exactly one coordinate equal to $h$, both inequalities are strict if another coordinate is positive and both are equalities if all other coordinates are zero. Deleting zero coordinates preserves both gaps. For $m=1$ and $0<x=x_1\le h<1$, the smaller-omission gap is
$$
W-R=\frac{x(h-x)(1-h)(2h+x-hx)}{h^2(1-x)} .
$$

pk-intake-two-positive-simplex-section-v.relation_to_goal: Ordinary simplex section with two unequal positive heights. The identities preserve the original section's coarea means and compare its two exact variance gaps.
pk-intake-two-positive-simplex-section-v.statement:
For an integer $m\ge1$ and $0\le x_j\le h<1$ with some $x_j>0$, put $\rho=\prod_j(1-x_j)$, $E=\rho^{-1}-1$, and
$$
L=\left(1-\frac{\sum_j x_j}{E}\right)\prod_j(1+x_j/E),\qquad
R=\rho(E+h)\left[1-\frac{(E+h)\prod_j(h-x_j)}{h^{m+1}}\right].
$$

Let $T$ be a $d$-simplex, $d\ge2$, with affine vertex heights $p>q>0$ at two vertices, $-r_j<0$ at $m\ge1$ other vertices, and arbitrary remaining zero heights. Let $F$ be the volume fraction on the closed nonnegative side, $b_i$ the barycentric coordinates of the uniform section centroid, and $V$ the signed sum of independent unit-rate exponentials with these coefficients. Put
$$
h=1-q/p,\quad x_j=\frac{hr_j}{q+r_j},\quad s_j=\frac{p}{p+r_j},
\quad X=\prod_j s_j,\quad \rho=\prod_j(1-x_j),\quad E=\rho^{-1}-1.
$$
Use these $L,R$ at this vector and threshold, let $Q=\prod_j(1+x_j/E)$, $B=\sum_jx_j/(1-x_j)$, $C=B/(1-\rho)-1$, and $W=(1-h)CQ$. Write $\mu_i=d b_i$ and use $p,q$ to denote the two positive indices. Then
$$
\begin{aligned}
F&=\frac{X\rho(E+h)}h=\frac{(E+h)\prod_j(h-x_j)}{h^{m+1}},
& f_V(0)&=\frac{X(1-\rho)}{p-q},\\
\mu_q&=\frac{1-\sum_j x_j/E}{h},
&\mu_p&=\frac{(1-h)C}{h},\\
\mu_j&=s_j(1+x_j/E)\quad(c_j=-r_j),
&\mu_i&=1\quad(c_i=0),\\
\prod_{i\ne p}\mu_i-F(1-F)&=\frac Xh(L-R),
&\prod_{i\ne q}\mu_i-F(1-F)&=\frac Xh(W-R).
\end{aligned}
$$
For any two negative indices $i,j$, with $h,E$, the other coordinates and $k=(1-x_i)(1-x_j)$ fixed, $W-R$ is a quadratic with strictly negative second derivative in $T_0=(1-x_i)+(1-x_j)$ on its feasible range.

pk-intake-two-positive-simplex-variance-.relation_to_goal: Actual finite-volume caps and section centroids of ordinary simplices with exactly two positive heights.
pk-intake-two-positive-simplex-variance-.statement:
Let $T$ be a $d$-simplex, $d\ge2$, and let an affine height cut its interior, with exactly two strictly positive vertex values $p\ge q>0$, at least one strictly negative vertex value, and any remaining vertex values zero. Let $F$ be the fraction of the simplex on the closed nonnegative side and $b$ the barycentric coordinates of the uniform section centroid. For each of the two positive indices $k$,
$$
F(1-F)\le d^d\prod_{i\ne k}b_i .
$$
Both comparisons are strict if $p>q$.

pk-intake-two-rate-affine-defect-and-spl.relation_to_goal: Actual unweighted volume and actual negative-log boundary measures. The marks satisfy affine contact conditions without a physical stationarity hypothesis.
pk-intake-two-rate-affine-defect-and-spl.statement:
Let $I$ be any nontrivial closed interval strictly inside $[0,1]$, put $t=x+y$, and take
$$
K_j=\{0\le s\le1,\ x,y\ge0:\ j^{-1}+e^{-j}\operatorname{dist}(s,I)\le t\le1\},\qquad
L_j=c_j(t-j^{-1}+e^{-2j})
$$
with volume-mean logarithm zero. Then $K_j\to[0,1]\times\{x,y\ge0,\ t\le1\}$, $M_j=|K_j|\to1/2$ and $c_j\to c=e^{1/2}$. On the exposed zero edge, with normal $n_0=(0,-1,-1)/\sqrt2$, the boundary negative-log defect and normalized reciprocal-volume defect have tangential densities $\sqrt2(1+\mathbf1_I)$ and $(2/c)(1+\mathbf1_I)$, respectively. They have full support and fail log-concavity. There is a single exact affine contact row with a uniformly interior mark and marked value bounded below, and its original-volume reweighting is uniform on $K_j$.

For $\rho>0$, use rates $r_j=(\rho/j)(-\log L_j)_+$. In physical coordinates $(s,0,0)$ the boundary defect with rate retained is
$$
\sqrt2\,\mathbf1_{[0,1]\setminus I}\,ds\,\delta_\rho
+2\sqrt2\,\mathbf1_I\,ds\,\delta_{2\rho},
$$
and the positive-rate inverse conditionals have density $2/(c\rho)$ on $[0,1]$ for $0<r<\rho$, the same density on $I$ for $\rho<r<2\rho$, and zero for $r>2\rho$. In particular the surface law at the single rate $\rho$ has disconnected tangential support. For $I=[1/3,2/3]$ the one-row mark tends to $(1/2,3/28,3/28)$ and its value to $3c/14$. With anchor $o=(1/2,1/3,1/3)$ the radial reciprocal-rate surface tail and $M L(o)$ times the inverse conditional both have density $2/(3\rho)$ on the indicated intervals.

A geometric active cell of a finite affine minimum with coefficientwise convergence and a uniformly positive-height anchor has the decreasing $1/(d-1)$-concave conditional law of the positive-rate slice theorem if its limiting affine gradient is nonzero and its inverse mass is uniformly bounded. For that same symmetric $I$, split the affine row into $s\in[0,1/4]\cup[3/4,1]$ and its complement, normalize each inverse restriction and take its own mean as its mark. The resulting two exact affine contact rows retain uniform interior source balls and positive limiting weights and values. Their original-volume reweightings, with the row weights, partition original volume. For $0<r<\rho$ the first row has a disconnected positive-rate conditional, although the full geometric affine slice has a convex conditional support.

pk-intake-two-residue-midpoint-packing-o.relation_to_goal: A packing inequality for specified inputs and an existing cover, with a common parity hypothesis.
pk-intake-two-residue-midpoint-packing-o.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$ for compact convex $C$, with positive mixed $d$-volume $W=\mu(S)$. Let finitely many open ambient halfspaces $U_j$ cover $S$, and suppose their closed versions each have mixed cap mass at most $\tau W$. For nonempty index sets $I,J$, let $A,B$ be compact positive-mass subsets of $S$ such that $A$ avoids every $U_j$ outside $I$ and $B$ avoids every $U_j$ outside $J$. Suppose both inputs lie in one common base parity class. Write $a=\mu(A)$ and $b=\mu(B)$. Then
$$
\left(\frac{a^{1/d}+b^{1/d}}2\right)^d\le |I\cup J|\tau W.
$$
If $A$ and $B$ are respectively in distinct classes modulo four, still with common parity, then
$$
a+b+\left(\frac{a^{1/d}+b^{1/d}}2\right)^d\le |I\cup J|\tau W.
$$

pk-intake-two-sided-arithmetic-radial-ca.relation_to_goal: Exact identities for original mixed volume and the true centroid; the chart densities retain the central boundary mass separately.
pk-intake-two-sided-arithmetic-radial-ca.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, be a compact convex body of positive mixed $d$-volume with true mixed centroid $(0,0)$. Write $K_z$ for its fiber at $z$. For $k\ge1$ set $Q_k^+=K_k/k$ and $Q_k^-=-K_{-k}/k$, with missing fibers represented by empty sets. Each family is decreasing. Set
$$
f_\pm(s)=\sum_{k\ge1} k^d\mathbf1_{Q_k^\pm}(s),\qquad
g_\pm(s)=\sum_{k\ge1} k^{d+1}\mathbf1_{Q_k^\pm}(s).
$$
For any closed halfspace $H=\{az+u\cdot x\ge0\}$, its mixed mass in $C$ is
$$
|K_0\cap\{u\cdot x\ge0\}|+
\int_{a+u\cdot s\ge0} f_+(s)\,ds+
\int_{a+u\cdot s\le0} f_-(s)\,ds .
$$
The centroid equations become
$$
\int g_+=\int g_-,\qquad
\int s(g_+-g_-)\,ds+\int_{K_0}x\,dx=0.
$$
Writing $F_j(m)=\sum_{k=1}^m k^j$ and $R_\pm(s)=\max\{r\ge0:(\pm r,\pm rs)\in C\}$, one has $f_\pm=F_d(\lfloor R_\pm\rfloor)$ and $g_\pm=F_{d+1}(\lfloor R_\pm\rfloor)$, including exact integer endpoints.

pk-intake-two-source-buffered-base-tilt-.relation_to_goal: Two marks with a common physical cap and a buffer offset fixed during pure base tilt, in one integer coordinate.
pk-intake-two-source-buffered-base-tilt-.statement:
Let a finite family of positive-volume compact convex $d$-fibers, $d\ge1$, be sampled at integer bases $z$ in one integer coordinate, with summed $d$-volume. Let $a<b$ be integer bases of two marks at which the same closed nonvertical buffered cap minimizes the cap mass, at least locally under base-tilt changes keeping the respective buffer offsets and the continuous normal fixed. Let $S_z,A_z,B_z$ denote the section $\mathcal H^{d-1}$ divided by the continuous normal length at proper, outside-supporting and inside-supporting traces respectively, with zero for each other status and with counting measure for $d=1$. Then
$
(b-a)\sum_z S_z+\sum_z B_z[(z-a)_++(b-z)_+]
\le \sum_z A_z[(a-z)_++(z-b)_+].
$

pk-intake-two-triangle-equal-fixed-cap-b.relation_to_goal: An actual two-fiber fixed-cap local maximum with equal noncritical global budgets. It neither varies the cap thresholds nor asserts stability under arbitrary convex-body perturbations or at the actual critical depth budget.
pk-intake-two-triangle-equal-fixed-cap-b.statement:
Let $T$ be a $2$-simplex of area $V>0$ with barycentric functions $\xi_i$, $i=0,1,2$. The actual source $[0,1]\times T$ has two positive integer fibers. Fix the six ambient caps
$$H_i^L=\{\xi_i\ge 1/10+(7/10)z\},\qquad H_i^H=\{\xi_i\ge 4/5-(7/10)z\}.$$
They cover the source on the integer bases and each has mass $17V/20$. In the chart independently varying both physical labeled triangles and keeping these caps fixed, the original pair is a strict local total-volume maximum under the six cap inequalities at that common budget. With all six multipliers $5/11$, the normalized Lagrangian Hessian in either physical block has characteristic polynomial
$$\frac{(11x+6)(11x+7)(121x^2+143x+27)^2}{1771561}.$$
The actual maximum raw mixed depth of the reference source is $4V/9$, or $2/9$ of total mass, whereas the common cover budget is $17/40$ of total mass.

pk-intake-two-unit-fractional-exponentia.relation_to_goal: A scalar fixed-count exponential probability comparison for the two-unit fractional family. The cap interpretation is restricted to the corresponding coefficient pattern in a simplex.
pk-intake-two-unit-fractional-exponentia.statement:
For every integer $m\ge2$ and real $p\in[0,1]$, let
$$
P_m(p)=\Pr\!\left(X+pE_+\ge E_0+\frac{1+p}{m}Y\right),
$$
where $X\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(2,1)$, $Y\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(m,1)$, and $E_+,E_0$ are mean-one exponentials, all independent. The gamma laws have scale one. Then $P_m(p)\ge\min\{P_m(0),P_m(1)\}$.

pk-intake-uncut-free-facet-buffered-dual.statement: In the regular singleton response setting take $\eta_i\ge0$ summing to one. Assume the corresponding separator satisfies $\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}\Xi_zv_z\,dS\le0$ for every admissible response of its actual signed cone. Suppose $d\ge2$ and one old polytopal fiber has a facet $F$ on which that cone contains the isolated inward speeds $1,-1,-T$, where $T$ is the unit-height centroid pyramid tent on $F$ and all three speeds vanish surface-almost everywhere off $F$. The two-direction forced-contact isolation condition is sufficient for these three paths to be actual. Suppose also that for every cap with $\eta_i\theta_{ij}>0$ its selector on $F$ is constant surface-almost everywhere. Then for every $\eta_i>0$ and every $j$, the continuous covector $u_{ij}$ annihilates the tangent space of $F$. The same holds for the own energy covector of any such group whose source is in that fiber. In particular no such separator exists if every available group has two nonparallel continuous covectors.

pk-intake-unequal-dilation-ambient-cap-i.relation_to_goal: The lower certificate is for actual endpoints and all ambient normals, including pure integer normals. The balanced comparison is confined to the stated single-fiber or binary product class.
pk-intake-unequal-dilation-ambient-cap-i.statement:
Let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}$ be compact and convex, let $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$ be nonempty, and put $q=\dim_H S$, $\mu=\mathcal H_q|_S$. Fix an actual $Y\in S$ and $0<t<1$. Define $L_t=t(S-Y)\cap[-(1-t)(S-Y)]$, $G_t(Y)=\mathcal H_q(L_t)$, $A_t=Y+L_t/t$, and $B_t=Y-L_t/(1-t)$. For every closed ambient halfspace $H=\{X:a\cdot(X-Y)\ge0\}$ with $a\ne0$,
$$
t^q\mu(A_t\cap H)+(1-t)^q\mu(B_t\cap H)
=G_t(Y)+\mathcal H_q(L_t\cap a^\perp).
$$
Every closed containing halfspace has mass at least $G_t(Y)/(t^q+(1-t)^q)$. At $t=1/2$ this is $\mathcal H_q(S\cap(2Y-S))/2$.

If $S$ consists of one positive intrinsic $q$-dimensional convex fiber with $q\ge1$, or is the product of a binary base cube and a common such fiber, the certificate at any $Y$ is maximized over $0<t<1$ at $t=1/2$. In the trapezoid product of the reflection-selector example, maximizing jointly over $Y$ and $t$ gives $5/8$, attained only at balanced weight and the points $(p,c_*)$.

pk-intake-unequal-endpoint-selector-actu.relation_to_goal: A necessary condition for the maximum of actual closed-cap depth on this prescribed selector at base zero. It yields no ambient cap-mass lower bound from the effective sections.
pk-intake-unequal-endpoint-selector-actu.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, and place convex bodies $A,B,C\subset\mathbb R^d$ at bases $-1,0,1$. Assume $(A+C)/2\subseteq B$ and write $a=|A|$, $b=|B|$, $c=|C|$, $M=a+b+c$, with $0<a<c$, $c<a+b$, and $b<a+c$. Use summed original fiber volumes $\mu$ and let $f(y)=\inf_{H\ni(0,y)}\mu(H)$ for closed ambient halfspaces. Write $g_K$ for the uniform centroid of $K$ and set
$$
Y=\left\{\frac{b g_B+a g_A+\int x\,d\sigma}{b+2a}:0\le\sigma\le\mathbf 1_C dx,\ \sigma(C)=a\right\}.
$$
This set is nonempty, compact, convex and uniformly inside $B$, and $f$ attains its maximum there. For every maximizer $y_*$ with $D=f(y_*)<M/2$, there are $k\le d+1$ actual minimum caps $H_j=\{(z,x):u_j\cdot(x-y_*)+v_jz\ge0\}$, $\lVert u_j\rVert=1$, $\mu(H_j)=D$, and positive weights $\omega_j$ of sum one. Each cap has effective section measures $\tau_{jz}$ on its trace in $K_z$, where $(K_{-1},K_0,K_1)=(A,B,C)$. They are ordinary $H^{d-1}$ on a proper trace, zero on an empty or $H^{d-1}$-null trace, and $\theta_{jz}H^{d-1}$ on a supporting facet with a measurable $0\le\theta_{jz}\le1$. Write $S_{jz}=\int d\tau_{jz}$, $S_j=\sum_z S_{jz}$ and $X_j=\sum_z\int x\,d\tau_{jz}$. Then
$$
S_j>0,\qquad S_{j,-1}=S_{j,1},\qquad X_j=S_jy_*,\qquad
\bar u\cdot(y-y_*)\ge0\quad(y\in Y),\qquad
\bar u=\sum_j\omega_j S_j u_j .
$$
When $\bar u\ne0$, the selector density producing $y_*$ is uniquely the indicator, up to volume-null sets, of the actual lower $\bar u$-cap in $C$ of volume $a$. When $\bar u=0$, the displayed sum gives a positive section-weighted normal balance.

pk-intake-unequal-homothetic-pair-triang.statement:

$$
r^2 F(t/r)+s^2 F(-t/s)<\min\{\min(r^2,s^2),2(4/9)((r+s)/2)^2\}.
$$
For $r=1,s=11/10$, a supporting cut gives cost $91/100<49/50$ and a cut with both endpoint traces proper gives cost $41189/45000<49/50$. Both are costs divided by $V$ from actual endpoint fibers at integer bases $-1,1$ of a convex hull, cut through the centroid of its middle fiber.

pk-intake-unequal-scale-homothetic-paire.relation_to_goal: Absolute two-source cap bounds for dilates of a single centered convex body at a specified mark. The supplied array has only the two endpoint sources, and a total-mass normalized bound for arbitrary bodies is outside this setting.
pk-intake-unequal-scale-homothetic-paire.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, and let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body of volume $V>0$ and volume centroid zero. Let $0<r\le s$, and for $u\ne0$ define $F_u(t)=|K\cap\{x:u\cdot x\ge t\}|/V$, where $|\cdot|$ is $d$-dimensional volume.

Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ and $c_d=(2\Gamma_d)^{1/d}$. Define
$$
\Phi_d(r,s)=
\begin{cases}
r, & d=1,\\
\left[r c_d+\dfrac{s-r}{d-1}(1-c_d)\right]^d, & d\ge2,\ r\le s\le dr,\\
r^d, & d\ge2,\ s\ge dr.
\end{cases}
$$
The two $d\ge2$ branches agree at $s=dr$.

For every $u\ne0$ and $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$
r^dF_u(t/r)+s^dF_u(-t/s)\ge\Phi_d(r,s).
$$
If $d\ge2$ and $s>r$, then $\Phi_d(r,s)>2\Gamma_d r^d$. For each fixed $u\ne0$ the minimum of the left side over $t\in\mathbb R$ is at most $r^d$. It equals $r^d$ and is attained at a finite threshold if $s\ge dr$, which includes every $0<r\le s$ in dimension one.

For the supplied array with just $rK$ at base $-1$ and $sK$ at base $1$, the raw source depth at $(0,0)$ is at least $V\Phi_d(r,s)$, and is exactly $Vr^d$ if $s\ge dr$. Here raw source depth is the infimum, over closed ambient halfspaces containing $(0,0)$, of the sum of the volumes captured from the two supplied sources.

pk-intake-unequal-scale-retained-midpoin.relation_to_goal: Local raw depth bound for one specified actual lattice point from three disjoint retained subbodies. Its budget is expressed in their volumes and does not give a fixed fraction of the full body's mixed volume.
pk-intake-unequal-scale-retained-midpoin.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$ and let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body. For $z\in\mathbb Z^n$ write $C_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$. Let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be full-dimensional, compact and convex with volume centroid zero and volume $V>0$. Suppose that for $p\in\mathbb Z^n$, $v\in\mathbb Z^n\setminus\{0\}$, $a_-,a_+\in\mathbb R^d$ and $0<r\le s$, the actual fibers $C_{p-v}$ and $C_{p+v}$ contain $a_-+rK$ and $a_++sK$, respectively. Put $g=(a_-+a_+)/2$ and $q=(r+s)/2$. Then $g+qK\subseteq C_p$.

Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ and $c_d=(2\Gamma_d)^{1/d}$. Define
$$
\Phi_d(r,s)=
\begin{cases}
r, & d=1,\\
\left[r c_d+\dfrac{s-r}{d-1}(1-c_d)\right]^d, & d\ge2,\ r\le s\le dr,\\
r^d, & d\ge2,\ s\ge dr.
\end{cases}
$$
The two $d\ge2$ branches agree at $s=dr$.

Every closed ambient halfspace $H$ containing $(p,g)$ captures total $d$-volume at least
$$
V\bigl[\Phi_d(r,s)+\Gamma_d q^d\bigr]
$$
from the three retained copies on the distinct bases $p-v,p,p+v$. In particular this lower bounds the raw depth of $(p,g)$ for $C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$.

pk-intake-unequal-simplex-facet-pair-exa.relation_to_goal: Exact only for the two opposite facet orientations of the untruncated simplex axial law. This does not optimize over other directions or convex bodies.
pk-intake-unequal-simplex-facet-pair-exa.statement:
For an integer $d\ge1$, let $F_+$ be the closed tail of the density $d x^{d-1}$ on $[0,1]$ centered at $A=d/(d+1)$, and set $F_-(q)=1-F_+(-q)$. These are the two opposing axial tails of a full $d$-simplex in a fixed facet-normal direction, with its scalar support before centering scaled to length one. For $0<r\le s$, write
$$
E=r^d-\left[\frac{(dr-s)_+}{d+1}\right]^d,\qquad
V_*=2\left(\frac{d}{d+1}\right)^d\left(\frac{r+s}{2}\right)^d.
$$
For the cost $r^dF_\pm(t/r)+s^dF_\pm(-t/s)$ over real $t$, the two respective minima are $E$ and $\min\{r^d,V_*\}$. Thus the minimum over those two orientations and thresholds is $\min\{E,V_*\}$.

pk-intake-unequal-truncated-affine-power.relation_to_goal: Finite exact profile at each fixed truncation and pair of scales. No optimization over the truncation or over all convex bodies.
pk-intake-unequal-truncated-affine-power.statement:
For an integer $d\ge1$ and $0\le a<1$, let $m=d(1-a^{d+1})/[(d+1)(1-a^d)]$ be the mean of the law of density $d x^{d-1}/(1-a^d)$ on $[a,1]$. Its centered closed tail is $F(q)=[1-\operatorname{clip}(m+q,a,1)^d]/(1-a^d)$, where clipping is projection onto $[a,1]$. For $r,s>0$ set $C(t)=r^d F(t/r)+s^d F(-t/s)$ and $W=r^d+s^d$. Form the finite set
$$
\mathcal E=\{r^d,s^d\}\cup
\left\{C(t):t\in\{r(a-m),r(1-m),s(m-1),s(m-a),m(s-r)/2\}\right\}.
$$
The exact minimum over real thresholds and the two reflected orientations is $\min\{\min\mathcal E,W-\max\mathcal E\}$. All entries are rational when $a,r,s$ are rational.

pk-intake-uniform-covariance-buffered-de.relation_to_goal: The fixed-base result is uniform over all base tilts and applies to uniformly corresponding multipliers, including the unweighted source.
pk-intake-uniform-covariance-buffered-de.statement:
Let \(P\subset\mathbb R^n\) be finite and nonempty, \(n\ge0\), and \(d\ge1\). For every \(z\in P\), let the convex bodies \(K_z^{(j)}\subset\mathbb R^d\) converge in Hausdorff distance to a convex body \(K_z^{(0)}\). Let \(M_j\) be their total \(d\)-volume, \(g_z^{(j)}\) their fiber centroids, and define the within-fiber covariance
$$
\Sigma_j=\frac1{M_j}\sum_{z\in P}\int_{K_z^{(j)}}(x-g_z^{(j)})(x-g_z^{(j)})^{\mathsf T}\,dx.
$$
Let \(\ell_j\ge0\) be continuous on the lifted union of the \(j\)-th fibers. Write \(\delta_j=\max_z d_H(K_z^{(j)},K_z^{(0)})\), and assume
$$
\sup_{\substack{p\in P,\ y_j\in K_p^{(j)},\ y\in K_p^{(0)}\\
\lVert y_j-y\rVert\le\delta_j}}\lvert\ell_j(p,y_j)-\ell_0(p,y)\rvert\longrightarrow0.
$$
Set \(f_j(p,y)=(\ell_j(p,y)E_{K_p^{(j)}}(y)/M_j)^{1/(d+1)}\), using the boundary value zero for the projective energy. For \(\epsilon_j\ge0\) with \(\epsilon_j\to\epsilon_0\), let \(b_j(p,y)\) be the infimum of the \(j\)-th summed fiber masses in the closed caps
$$
a\cdot(z-p)+u\cdot(x-y)+\epsilon_j f_j(p,y)\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_j u}\ge0,
\qquad (a,u)\ne(0,0).
$$
Then \(b_j(p,y_j)\to b_0(p,y)\) uniformly on the displayed correspondences. Each \(b_j\) attains a maximum on its lifted union, and both the maxima and the maxima divided by \(M_j\) converge. The comparison includes pure-base caps and arbitrary oblique base tilts. When \(P\) is the complete positive integer support of compatible actual fibers, the maxima are their actual mixed buffered maxima.

pk-intake-uniform-diagonal-deficit-expan.relation_to_goal: An exact expansion of the discrete affine-radius scalar envelope at small positive slopes for each fixed dimension. The expansion and its constants hold without a sign assumption on the continuous gain.
pk-intake-uniform-diagonal-deficit-expan.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$ and put $t=1/(d+1)$ and $\Gamma=(dt)^d$. For $a>0$, $0\le\beta\le at$ and $h\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$, set $r_h=(1-ah)_+$, $q_h=t-\beta h$ and $p_h=t+\beta(h+1)$, where $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$. The diagonal-envelope deficit is
$$
D(a,\beta)=\Gamma\sum_{h\ge0}r_h^d
-d^d\sum_{\substack{h\ge0\\r_h>0}}
  \left[q_h^{d-1}(r_h-dq_h)_++p_h^{d-1}(r_h-dp_h)_+\right].
$$
Both sums have only finitely many nonzero terms. Whenever $r_h>0$, one has $q_h\ge tr_h>0$ and $p_h\ge t>0$.

For $0\le a\le1/(2d)$ and $v\in[0,1]$, let
$$
\begin{aligned}
L_v(x)&=(1-vx)^{d-1}[1-(d+1-dv)x]_+,\\
R_{a,v}(x)&=(1+av+vx)^{d-1}[1-dav-(d+1+dv)x]_+ .
\end{aligned}
$$
The kernels are defined for $x\ge0$ and set to zero beyond the positive-part supports. Let $I_R(a,v)=\int_0^\infty R_{a,v}(x)\,dx$, $J_d(v)=\partial_a I_R(0,v)$ (the right derivative), and $G_d(v)=\int_0^\infty L_v(x)\,dx+I_R(0,v)-1/(d+1)$. Then $J_d$ and $G_d$ are continuous on $[0,1]$ and both vanish at $0$. For $0<v\le1$, with $f(z)=(1+z)^{d+1}/(1+dz/(d+1))^d$,
$$
G_d(v)=\frac{f(v)+f(-v)-2}{dv^2}-\frac1{d+1}.
$$
Set
$$
\begin{aligned}
V_d&=3d(3d+1)2^{d-3},&
T_d&=\frac{2^{d-3}(9d^2-7d+2)}{d+1},&
B_d&=(d+2)2^{d-4},\\
C_d&=\frac{V_d}{4}+\frac d8+\frac{T_d}{2}+B_d,&
K_d&=\frac{d(2d+1)}{(d+1)^2}\left(1+\frac1{d+1}\right)^{d-2}.
\end{aligned}
$$
For every $0<a\le1/(2d)$ and every $v\in[0,1]$,
$$
\frac{D(a,atv)}{\Gamma}=-\frac{G_d(v)}a-J_d(v)-\frac12+\rho_d(a,v),
\qquad
|\rho_d(a,v)|\le C_d a,\qquad |J_d(v)|\le K_d v .
$$

pk-intake-uniform-face-contact-row-likel.relation_to_goal: This is a one-sided comparison of original-volume and tilted probabilities at actual contact rows.
pk-intake-uniform-face-contact-row-likel.statement:
Let actual compatible convex $d$-fibers over a fixed finite real base $P$ be contained in $RB_d$. At a mark $Y=(p,y)$ with $B(y,r_s)\subset K_p$, let $L\ge0$ be concave on the canonical hull and $A\ge L$ an affine majorant with $A(Y)=L_i=L(Y)>0$. Let $\rho$ be a probability on the sampled fibers with mean $Y$ and $\int L\,d\rho=L_i$. For each $u\in P\cap F_p$ fix an anchored representation of $p$ with positive weight at $u$ and let $t_*>0$ be the minimum of these weights. Then $\rho$ is supported over $F_p$, $L=A$ $\rho$-almost everywhere, and $d\bar\rho=(L/L_i)d\rho$ is a probability with
$$
\frac{d\bar\rho}{d\rho}\le C_0=\frac{r_s+2R}{t_*r_s}\quad \rho\text{-almost everywhere},
\qquad 0\le D(\bar\rho\|\rho)\le\log C_0.
$$
Any probability-weighted average of rows satisfying a common $C_0$ has the same entropy bound.

pk-intake-uniform-nearby-simplex-cap-los.relation_to_goal: Ordinary full-dimensional volume and convex functions on simplex facets. The bound applies to affine halfspaces with arbitrary thresholds within the stated margin tolerance.
pk-intake-uniform-nearby-simplex-cap-los.statement:
Let $F$ be a $k$-dimensional simplex, $k\ge1$, with normalized volume $\mu_F$, and let $t$ be one of its barycentric coordinates. For $b\in(0,1)$ put $r=\frac14\min\{b,(1-b)/k\}$. Every continuous nonnegative convex function $f$ on $F$ satisfies
$$
\int_{\{|t-b|\le\eta\}} f\,d\mu_F
\le \frac{2\eta}{r}\int_F f\,d\mu_F,\qquad 0\le\eta\le r.
$$

Let $S$ be a full-dimensional simplex in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, with centroid $g$ and barycentric functions $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$. Put $m=d+1$, $b=1/m$, and $C_i=\{x:\lambda_i(x)\ge b\}$. Suppose $K$ is a compact convex body with $g+(1-\delta)(S-g)\subseteq K\subseteq S$ for $0\le\delta<1$. Write $\tau=1-|K|/|S|$ and $R_i=|(S\setminus K)\cap C_i|/|S|$, where $|\cdot|$ is $d$-dimensional volume. For any affine margin $\phi$ with $H=\{x:\phi(x)\ge0\}$, if $\sup_{x\in S}|\phi(x)-(\lambda_i(x)-b)|\le\eta\le(1-\delta)/(4m)$, then
$$
\frac{|(S\setminus K)\cap(H\mathbin{\triangle}C_i)|}{|S|}
\le 8m\eta(1-\delta)^{-d-1}\tau .
$$
In particular, $|(S\setminus K)\cap H|/|S|\le R_i+8m\eta(1-\delta)^{-d-1}\tau$. The affine margin may have any threshold satisfying the stated bound.

For the radial formula used to obtain this bound, let $F_j=\{\lambda_j=0\}\cap S$, let $\rho$ be the Minkowski gauge of $K-g$, and put $f_j(z)=\rho(z-g)-1$ and $w_j(z)=1-\rho(z-g)^{-d}$ on $F_j$. Each $f_j$ is continuous, convex and nonnegative, and $d(1-\delta)^d f_j\le w_j\le d f_j$. For a measurable $A\subset F_j$, the missing volume on rays from $g$ towards $A$ equals $(|S|/m)\int_A w_j\,d\mu_{F_j}$. In particular $\tau=m^{-1}\sum_j\int_{F_j} w_j\,d\mu_{F_j}$.

pk-intake-uniform-outward-smoothing-atta.relation_to_goal: Positive-width approximation and compactness on a given original-depth sublevel. This does not prove such a sublevel for arbitrary fixed bases or a sharp depth bound.
pk-intake-uniform-outward-smoothing-atta.statement:

Use threshold $c=N\cdot Y-\varepsilon f(Y)\Gamma(u)$ at a sampled mark $Y=(p,y)$, and retain ordinary closed pure-base caps. Write $\beta_{\varepsilon,h}$ for the normalized maximum of the through-mark infimum, with the closed ordinary or buffered cap at $h=0$.

For every cap $T_h(N,c)=h^{-1}\int_0^h\mu\{N\cdot w\ge c-s\Gamma(u)\}\,ds$, and globally $\beta_{\varepsilon,h}\ge\beta_{\varepsilon,0}\ge\beta_{0,0}$. For positive families in a fixed containing ball with $M=1$, the raw pointwise excess over width zero is at most $C h$, uniformly over all marks and tilts. The raw depth is continuous under simultaneous positive-fiber Hausdorff and feasible mark convergence at fixed $\varepsilon,h$, and so is its normalized maximum.

Assume additionally a strict ordinary trial $\beta_{0,0}<b$ and the invariant compact normalized original-depth sublevel at $b$ with positive volume, inradius and covariance floors, as in 4bf4936eff4d698d. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon\ge0$ and $h>0$, the unrestricted infimum over the fixed complete compatible family class is attained. Each deepest mark has a uniform own interior ball, and each closed pure-base cap there has a uniform positive reserve over the raw maximum. For each such mark the infimum is attained by a nonvertical cap. After $\Gamma(u)=1$, there is one compact domain of base tilts and continuous normals containing a replacement for every nonvertical through-mark cap on the normalized class. Replacement preserves the full ramp profile and strip data on every old fiber. At every deepest mark the active representatives form a nonempty compact set, with $0<S_{\min}\le S=\int\psi((N\cdot w-c)/h)\,d\mu/h\le S_{\max}$ and $-hS\le A=\int[(N\cdot w-c)/h]\psi((N\cdot w-c)/h)\,d\mu\le0$, uniformly for the indicated parameters.

pk-intake-uniform-own-properness-before-.relation_to_goal: A uniform small-buffer choice gives proper own cuts for every maximizing mark in the stated representative family.
pk-intake-uniform-own-properness-before-.statement:
Let \(P\subset\mathbb R^n\) be finite and nonempty, \(n\ge0\), and \(d\ge1\). At every buffered maximizing mark \((p,y)\),
$$
b_0(p,y)\ge\gamma_d M/m-\epsilon LG,\qquad
\operatorname{dist}(y,\partial K_p)\ge b_0(p,y)/L .
$$
In particular, if \(\epsilon G<\gamma_d M/(4mL)\), every such mark lies in its own fiber interior and every shifted own cap with nonzero continuous normal cuts that fiber properly. The same \(\epsilon\) works uniformly on any collection with a common \(P,M,L,G\) and these hypotheses.

pk-intake-uniform-physical-buffer-vanish.relation_to_goal: An asymptotic result for actual global or asymptotically optimal joint choices on a fixed base with a compact original-depth frame and limit quotas. It concerns sampled parameters and frame-normalized physical displacements.
pk-intake-uniform-physical-buffer-vanish.statement:
Fix $d\ge1$, $N=d+1$, $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, and a finite complete affine-lattice base $P$ with $k$ occupied parities. Let $\beta_0^*$ be the infimum of the normalized ordinary closed-halfspace maximum over all actual positive compatible $d$-fibers on $P$. Assume $\beta_0^*<b<\gamma_d/k$ and assume the entire original sublevel $\{\beta_0\le b\}$ admits a compact frame of positive representatives under invertible maps $(z,x)\mapsto(z,Ax+s(z))$ with $s$ affine. Each representative has total sampled volume $M=1$, fiber volumes bounded below by $v>0$, and all fibers contained in $R B_d$. Assume every limit of the framed sublevel satisfies $V(T)\le k(T)/k$ for every nonempty proper closed minor $T=P\cap\operatorname{conv}(T)$, with $V(T)=\sum_{z\in T}|K_z|$ and inherited parity count $k(T)$.

For an actual canonical hull $C$ of the sampled fibers let the parameter $L$ be positive continuous concave on $C$ with $\sum_z\int_{K_z}\log L(z,X)\,dX/M=0$. At scale $\varepsilon>0$ use through-mark nonvertical caps with margin $a\cdot(z-p)+u\cdot(X-y)$ increased at mark $(p,y)$ by
$$
\varepsilon\left(\frac{L(p,y)E_{K_p}(y)}{M}\right)^{1/N}G_K(u),\qquad
G_K(u)=\left(\frac1M\sum_z\int_{K_z}(u\cdot(X-g_z))^2\,dX\right)^{1/2},
$$
where $g_z$ is the centroid and projective energy is extended by zero to the own boundary. Pure-base caps are unchanged. Write $\beta_\varepsilon(K,L)$ for the normalized buffered maximum. Let $\varepsilon_j\downarrow0$ and let $(K_j,L_j)$ be admissible pairs with $\beta_{\varepsilon_j}(K_j,L_j)-\inf_{K,L}\beta_{\varepsilon_j}(K,L)\to0$, taking each infimum over the whole stated class. Then
$$
\beta_{\varepsilon_j}(K_j,L_j)\to\beta_0^*,
\qquad
\max_{z\in P,\ X\in K_{j,z}}\varepsilon_j^N L_j(z,X)\to0.
$$
The physical cap displacements also tend to zero uniformly on sampled fibers and Euclidean unit continuous normals in the bounded representative frame. These assumptions on the original sublevel and quotas hold for a base selected by 26d27b0f77ea4ac9 using the parity budget with $\tau=\gamma_d$.

pk-intake-uniform-simplex-opposite-inter.relation_to_goal: Ordinary barycentric probability and normalized continuous volume, with a finite-dimensional bound for the aligned-simplex depth estimate.
pk-intake-uniform-simplex-opposite-inter.statement:
For $N\ge2$, let $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_N)$ be uniform on the standard simplex $\{x_i\ge0,\ \sum_i x_i=1\}$ in its affine hyperplane. For every $c\in[0,1]$,
$$
\Pr(X_i\le c\text{ for every }i)\le [1-(1-c)^{N-1}]^N.
$$
For a centroid-zero $d$-simplex $T$, set $\rho_d=|T\cap(-T)|/|T|$. Then $\rho_d<1/3$ for every $d\ge5$. The exact values for $1\le d\le7$ are $1,2/3,1/2,46/125,22/81,3364/16807,151/1024$ in that order.

pk-intake-uniform-single-fiber-interval-.relation_to_goal: Exact test for a single-fiber uniform interval law dominated by twice the original mixed-length probability in every closed cap.
pk-intake-uniform-single-fiber-interval-.statement:
Let finitely many positive interval fibers $I_j=[l_j,u_j]$ at distinct integer bases $j$ have lengths $w_j$ and total mixed length $M$. Let $\mu$ be the summed length divided by $M$, fix an actual fiber $k$, and put $[r]_0^w=\min(w,\max(0,r))$. Define the raw cap envelopes
$$
L_k(t)=\inf_s\sum_j[t+s(j-k)-l_j]_0^{w_j},\qquad
R_k(t)=\inf_s\sum_j[u_j-t-s(j-k)]_0^{w_j}.
$$
There is a nondegenerate uniform interval law $\nu$ on a subinterval of $I_k$ with $\nu(H)\le2\mu(H)$ for every closed ambient halfspace if and only if $\sum_{j<k}w_j,\sum_{j>k}w_j\le M/2$ and there are real $a,b$ with $a l_k+b\le0$, $a u_k+b\ge1$, and
$$
\begin{aligned}
at+b&\le 2L_k(t)/M &&\text{where } t\in I_k,\ 2L_k(t)/M<1,\\
at+b&\ge 1-2R_k(t)/M &&\text{where } t\in I_k,\ 1-2R_k(t)/M>0.
\end{aligned}
$$
Then $a\ge1/w_k$ and the target is uniform on $[-b/a,(1-b)/a]$. The envelopes are continuous piecewise affine with finitely many pieces. The conditions reduce to a finite linear feasibility problem in $a,b$, with rational coefficients for rational fiber endpoints.

pk-intake-uniform-triangle-exact-row-cap.relation_to_goal: Ordinary uniform barycentric triangle and a nonnegative row, without any column-stochastic constraints.
pk-intake-uniform-triangle-exact-row-cap.statement:
Let $\Xi$ be uniform on the probability triangle, and let $0\le x\le y\le z$ be the sorted entries of a row. Set $G(c)=\Pr((x,y,z)\cdot\Xi\le c)$. Then
$$
\left(\inf_{c>0,G(c)>0}\frac{c}{\sqrt{G(c)}}\right)^2=z(x+y)-xy.
$$
In particular the result includes tied and zero entries.

pk-intake-unique-eligible-hull-pair-shar.relation_to_goal: Refutes nonincrease of maximum fractional convex-hull packing under every positive eligible mass-preserving merge, even with one eligible pair. The source already satisfies the nominal M/4 packing threshold.
pk-intake-unique-eligible-hull-pair-shar.statement:
Let $P$ be the pentagon with consecutive vertices $A=(0,0)$, $B=(3,0)$, $C=(4,2)$, $D=(3,3)$, $E=(0,3)$, and $S=P\cap\mathbb Z^2$. Give each vertex weight one and each other point of $S$ weight $\varepsilon=1/1200$. The total weight is $M=501/100$, every point weight is strictly below $M/4$, and the only same-parity pair of hull vertices is $A,C$. For the fractional packing value $f_w$ of the comparison lemma and $m=(A+C)/2=(2,1)$, one has
$$
 \max_{z\in\mathbb Z^2} f_w(z)=f_w(m)=2+4\varepsilon=\frac{601}{300}.
$$
For every $0<\delta\le1$, the mass-preserving merge $w'=w-\delta e_A-\delta e_C+2\delta e_m$ satisfies
$$
 \max_{z\in\mathbb Z^2} f_{w'}(z)=f_{w'}(m)=\frac{601}{300}+\delta .
$$
At $\delta=1$ the equality persists when the zero-capacity endpoints are deleted from the source set.

pk-intake-unit-negative-exponential-half.relation_to_goal: Constrains the scalar capped signed exponential optimization used in the restricted angular problem.
pk-intake-unit-negative-exponential-half.statement:
Let $E_j,F_i$ be independent unit exponentials. Let $m\ge1$ be an integer and $0\le p_i\le1$ be a finite list with $\sum_i p_i=m$. Then
$$
\Pr\{\textstyle\sum_i p_i E_i\ge\sum_{j=1}^m F_j\}\ge\frac12 .
$$

pk-intake-universal-zero-convex-hull-ess.relation_to_goal: An abstract rank consequence for a fixed family of menus satisfying the universal balance condition. A depth application requires the actual circuit and variation hypotheses.
pk-intake-universal-zero-convex-hull-ess.statement:
Let $X_1,\ldots,X_k$ be nonempty subsets of a finite-dimensional real vector space $V$, with $k\ge1$. Assume that $0\in\operatorname{conv}\{x_1,\ldots,x_k\}$ for every choice $x_i\in X_i$. Let $I$ be any inclusion-minimal nonempty set of indices for which this property holds on its own. Then
$$
\dim\operatorname{span}\bigcup_{i\in I}X_i\le |I|-1.
$$
In particular, when the sets lie in a dual space, the joint kernel of all covectors in this block has codimension at most $|I|-1$ in the original space.

pk-intake-unrestricted-diagonal-envelope.relation_to_goal: Gives the unrestricted maximum for the scalar envelope governing the affine simplex chain model.
pk-intake-unrestricted-diagonal-envelope.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ be an integer, $t=1/(d+1)$, and $\Gamma=(dt)^d$. For $a>0$ and $0\le\beta\le at$, put $r_h=(1-ah)_+$, $q_h=t-\beta h$, and $p_h=t+\beta(h+1)$ for integers $h\ge0$, where $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$. For $r,q>0$ set $E_d(q,r)=d^dq^{d-1}(r-dq)_+$. The diagonal-envelope deficit is
$$
D_d(a,\beta)=\Gamma\sum_{h\ge0} r_h^d-
\sum_{\substack{h\ge0\\r_h>0}}\bigl[E_d(q_h,r_h)+E_d(p_h,r_h)\bigr].
$$
Every term in the second sum has positive thresholds. For $1\le H\le d$ put
$$
a_H=\frac{H+1}{H(d+1)},\qquad
W_{d,H}=\sum_{h\ge0}(1-a_Hh)_+^d,\qquad
K_{d,H}=\sum_{h=0}^{H-1}(1-h/d)^{d-1}(1-h/H).
$$
The unrestricted maximum of $D_d(a,\beta)$ on the specified domain is attained and satisfies
$$
0<\max_{\substack{a>0\\0\le\beta\le at}}D_d(a,\beta)
=\Gamma\max_{1\le H\le d}(W_{d,H}-K_{d,H})
<\frac{\Gamma}{6}.
$$
Equivalently, the envelope sum for every admissible $(a,\beta)$ is strictly larger than $\Gamma\sum_h r_h^d-\Gamma/6$.

pk-intake-unrestricted-signed-buffer-gap.relation_to_goal: Fixed-body obstruction to a uniformly vanishing signed regularization, measured in original mixed volume.
pk-intake-unrestricted-signed-buffer-gap.statement:
Use the actual centered three-interval family of lengths $1/8,1,1$ at $-1,0,1$ and original measure $\mu$ of mass $17/8$. For a direct signed concave buffer of original mean one and physical shifts $\varepsilon f_\varepsilon(z,x)$ in unit continuous normals, the affine choice
$$
f_\varepsilon(z,x)=1+\frac{z-7/17}{8\varepsilon}
$$
has global raw buffered maximum $39/68+\varepsilon$ for every $0<\varepsilon\le10^{-4}$, whereas its ordinary raw maximum is $5/8$. The difference of these limits is $7/136$. With a fixed positive interval norm one can rescale the slope to get the same limiting gap. Replacing the constant term by a fixed bounded nonnegative concave mean-one buffer leaves the signed limit unchanged.

pk-intake-vanishing-buffer-ordinary-boun.relation_to_goal: A bounded-test estimate and limit for the actual aggregate selector, without identifying individual limiting cap allocations or reciprocal-volume defects.
pk-intake-vanishing-buffer-ordinary-boun.statement:
Let finitely many sampled positive convex $d$-fibers $K_z^j\subset RB_d$ with a common inball radius $r_b>0$ converge in Hausdorff distance to positive $K_z$. Write $dm_j$ and $dS_j$ for their summed mixed volume and boundary area, with endpoint counting if $d=1$. Let $M_j\ge M_*>0$ and let the pooled within-fiber covariance satisfy $\Sigma_j\ge\lambda_* I$. At each index use the same-coefficient contact data and exact physical density $\Xi_j$ of 80c8de4539fbc253. Assume $\Delta_j>0$, $\Delta_j\le S_{\max}\varepsilon_j$, $\varepsilon_j\downarrow0$, a uniform own ball radius $r_s$ at the positive contact sources, and $L_{j,\max}\le H\varepsilon_j^{-N}$ with $N=d+1$ and $H\ge1$. Write $B_j=-(\Delta_j/(NM_j))\log L_j$, let $S_*,S_{f,*}$ bound the total and individual fiber surface areas, and put $E_*=\kappa_d r_s^d$ for unit ball volume $\kappa_d$. Then, with $W_j$ the exact allocated cap load and $\beta_j$ the buffered maximum,
$$
\int_{\partial S_j}|\Xi_j-(W_j-\beta_j)|\,dS_j\le
\Delta_j\left(\frac{N^{N-1}S_{f,*}}{E_*}+\frac{2R^2S_*}{M_*\lambda_*}+\frac{(N+2)S_*}{2NM_*}\right)
+\int_{\partial S_j}|B_j|\,dS_j.
$$
This is $O(\varepsilon_j(1+\log(1/\varepsilon_j)))$. On every bounded speed $v$ in the same cone, the integral of $(W_j-\beta_j)v$ is at most the displayed bound times $\|v\|_\infty$. Assume moreover $\beta_j\to\beta_0$ and that each fixed globally finite convex function $\Phi(z,X)$ belongs to each common tested cone as an inward speed. Then on a subsequence $W_j dS_j\rightharpoonup w_0 dS_0$, $0\le w_0\le1$, and
$$
\int_{\partial S_0}\Phi(z,X)(w_0-\beta_0)\,dS_0\le0
$$
for every such $\Phi$. Affine tests of both signs give equality of the mass and full first moments of $w_0dS_0$ and $\beta_0dS_0$.

pk-intake-variable-barycentric-density-c.relation_to_goal: Selection for fixed compact marginals under a prescribed density envelope. A geometric application needs its own physical density comparison and any necessary capacity sharing.
pk-intake-variable-barycentric-density-c.statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge1$, and $k\ge1$ be integers. For finite $Q\subset\mathbb R^n$ write $\sigma_Q=\sum_{q\in Q}\delta_q\otimes\mathcal L^d$. Let $P_i\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and let $\gamma_i$ be finite nonnegative Borel measures of common mass $M$, supported on compact sets $K_i\subset P_i\times\mathbb R^d$. Suppose $\gamma_i\le f_i\sigma_{P_i}$ for finite nonnegative Borel $f_i$ on $K_i$, extended by zero off $K_i$. Take positive weights $\lambda_i$ with sum one and write $b(w)=\sum_i\lambda_i w_i$, $K=\sum_i\lambda_iK_i$, and $P=\sum_i\lambda_i P_i$. Let $g:K\to[0,\infty]$ be Borel with $\int_K g\,d\sigma_P<\infty$, extended by zero off $K$. Suppose there are Borel $E_i\subset K_i$ of full $\gamma_i$ measure such that for every $w\in\prod_i E_i$ with every $f_i(w_i)>0$,
$$
g(b(w))\ \ge\ \left(\sum_i\lambda_i f_i(w_i)^{-1/d}\right)^{-d}.
$$
For every coupling $\pi_0$ of the $\gamma_i$ there is one coupling $\pi$ of the same marginals such that $b_\#\pi_0\preceq_{\rm cx}b_\#\pi$ and $b_\#\pi\le g\sigma_P$. Convex order tests every finite convex function on $\mathbb R^{n+d}$. If every base tuple occurring in $\prod_i E_i$ with all $f_i(w_i)>0$ has an integer barycenter in its base coordinates, then the selected output is supported on integer bases.

pk-intake-vertical-preserving-block-affi.relation_to_goal: Normalization and exact covariance for full-dimensional mixed sources, with no conclusion about the size of the transformed lattice covering radius.
pk-intake-vertical-preserving-block-affi.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, $d\ge0$, $N=n+d$, and let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior. There is an invertible affine map $F(z,x)=(Az+t,Bz+Tx+c)$, with $A,T$ invertible on their respective spaces, such that
$$
B_2^N\subseteq K=F(C)\subseteq R B_2^N,\qquad R=N(N+2).
$$
For a Borel set $E$ put $\mu(E)=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}|(C\cap E)_z|_d$ and $\nu(E)=|\det A|\sum_{\lambda\in A\mathbb Z^n+t}|(K\cap E)_\lambda|_d$. Then $\nu(F(E))=|\det A|\,|\det T|\,\mu(E)=|\det DF|\,\mu(E)$. The map takes the original sampled source bijectively to $K\cap((A\mathbb Z^n+t)\times\mathbb R^d)$ and preserves normalized depth whenever the total mass is positive. For $d=0$, use counting measure on $\mathbb R^0$ and $|\det T|=1$.

pk-intake-wedge-simplex-outside-selector.relation_to_goal: PK's explicit n=1, d=5 wedge example only. This is a point of the original middle fiber outside the failed selector hull; it is not a centroid or a retained-body result. The theorem does not identify the maximum depth or resolve the locked weak target.
pk-intake-wedge-simplex-outside-selector.statement:
Let $B$ be the standard $5$-simplex, of volume $V=1/120$, with centroid $g$ and barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_5$, where $\lambda_i=x_i$ for $i\ge1$. Set
$$
r=\frac{497}{3000},\qquad \ell=\frac{1027}{6000},\qquad T=\frac{3979}{6000}.
$$
Let $D$ be the simplex with vertices $p=(0,11/12,0,0,0)$, $b_0=(r,\ell,0,0,0)$, and $b_0+T e_i$ for $2\le i\le5$, where $e_i$ are the coordinate vectors. Put $m=rT^4$, $q=m^{-1/5}$, $A=(2-q)D$, $C=qD$, and $a=(2m^{1/5}-1)^5$. Let $K$ be the convex hull of the lifts of $A,B,C$ at levels $-1,0,1$, respectively. These are its exact integer fibers, of volumes $aV,V,V$, with $0<a<10^{-5}$. Write $\mu_K$ for their summed five-dimensional volume, regarded as a measure on the ambient space.

Let $y$ be the interior point of $B$ with
$$
\lambda_1(y)=\frac16-\frac a3,\qquad \lambda_i(y)=\frac16+\frac a{15}\quad(i\ne1).
$$
Then $y\notin\operatorname{conv}(\{g\}\cup D)$.

Writing $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, the infimum of $\mu_K(H)$ over all closed ambient halfspaces $H$ containing $(0,y)$ is strictly greater than $\Gamma_5(1+a/2)V$. Thus $(0,y)$ has normalized depth strictly greater than $\Gamma_5/2$ in $K$.

pk-intake-weight-two-mass-dependent-cent.relation_to_goal: Ordinary cap depth at the prescribed centroid of volume plus twice a dominated submeasure, with the scalar positivity proved for every real parameter d≥1.
pk-intake-weight-two-mass-dependent-cent.statement:
For real $d\ge1$, set $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, $A_d=1/\Gamma_d$, and $L_d=4A_d/3-1$. Write $t_+=\max(t,0)$ and define

$$
\Delta_d=2+(1+1/d)(1+A_d/3)
   -2(1+1/(2d))^{d+1}-2(1-L_d/(2d))_+^{d+1},
\qquad \varepsilon_d=\frac{d}{d+1}\Delta_d.
$$

Then $\Delta_d>0$. For each integer $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, let $0\le\eta\le\mathbf 1_K\,dx$, and let $g$ be the centroid of $\mathbf 1_K\,dx+2\eta$. Then $g\in\operatorname{int}K$, and every closed halfspace $H$ containing $g$ satisfies

$$
|K\cap H|+\eta(H)\ \ge\
\frac{3\Gamma_d}{4}(|K|+\eta(K))
+\frac{3\Gamma_d^2\varepsilon_d}{4\cdot3^d}|K|.
$$

pk-intake-weight-two-midpoint-centroid-f.statement:
For $d\ge2$, let $K=B$ be a volume-one $d$-simplex with apex $P$, and let $t$ be its affine height, one at $P$ and zero at the opposite facet. Take $A=P+\varepsilon(K-P)$, $a=\varepsilon^d$, $0<\varepsilon\le1/(10d)$, at the left endpoint of the actual three-fiber hull $A,K,B$ at $-1,0,1$. Its prescribed weight-two midpoint source is $y=[g_K+a(g_A+g_B)]/(1+2a)$ on the middle fiber. The height of $y$ is $g=[1+a(d+2-d\varepsilon)]/[(d+1)(1+2a)]$. The closed cap $t+(g-1)z\ge g$ through this source has raw mass
$$
Q=\gamma_d[(1+a(1+\varepsilon))/(1+2a)]^d+a,\qquad
\gamma_d(1+a/2)-Q\ge3a/50>0.
$$
For $K=\operatorname{conv}((0,0),(2,0),(0,1))$ and $\varepsilon=1/100$ this gives $g=166733/500100$, $Q=11115856669/25010001000$, and target gap $159443/15631250625$.

pk-intake-weighted-affine-hyperplane-con.relation_to_goal: A quantitative implication from affine hyperplane fractions to lattice covering radius, with a sharp rank-one calibration and a counterexample to replacing vanishing by a fixed sub-half fraction.
pk-intake-weighted-affine-hyperplane-con.statement:
Let $L\subset\mathbb R^r$, $r\ge1$, be a full-rank lattice of Euclidean covering radius $\rho(L)$ and dual shortest nonzero length $\lambda_1(L^*)$. With $\kappa_r=|B_2^r|_r$ and $C_r=r2^{r-1}/\kappa_r$,
$$
\rho(L)\lambda_1(L^*)\le C_r\le r^{r+1}/2.
$$
Let a positive finite measure have fine base projection supported in $(a+L)\cap(q+RB_2^r)$ for some $q$ and $R>0$, and let $\xi<1$ be the maximum fraction of its mass on an affine fine-base hyperplane. Then
$$
\rho(L)\le \frac{2C_r R\xi}{1-\xi}.
$$
For a section law with $s$-volume on the continuous fibers and common weight per lattice base, an invertible block affine map with linear part $(u,x)\mapsto(Au,Bu+Cx)$ preserves these hyperplane fractions, including for $s=0$ with counting. Thus vanishing $\xi$ in uniformly bounded block frames forces the transformed radii to vanish. In dimension one the quantitative bound can be attained by an actual convex hull of its three equal sampled fibers.

pk-intake-weighted-centroid-tails.relation_to_goal: An ordinary directional marginal and measurable-subset theorem for one convex body and one cut direction.
pk-intake-weighted-centroid-tails.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional convex body, $d\ge1$, with volume $V$ and centroid $g$. For $u\ne0$ write $F(s)=|K\cap\{x:u\cdot(x-g)\ge s\}|/V$, and set $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. For every $s\in\mathbb R$,
$$
F(0)+F(s)+\frac12F(-s)\ge\gamma_d+\frac12.
$$
The right-hand side is attained. Equivalently, for every Lebesgue-measurable $A\subseteq K$ of volume $a$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$
|K\cap\{u\cdot(x-g)\ge0\}|+
|A\cap\{u\cdot(x-g)\ge t\}|+
|K\cap\{u\cdot(x-g)\ge-t\}|
\ge \gamma_d V+\frac a2.
$$

pk-intake-weighted-common-simplex-envelo.relation_to_goal: Ordinary weighted envelope volume over shared orientations of a fixed family.
pk-intake-weighted-common-simplex-envelo.statement:
Let $A_i\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a finite family of nonempty compact convex sets with positive weights $w_i$, and assume at least one member $A_*$ has nonempty interior. Using the envelopes $P_U(A_i)$ in the preceding definition, the objective $F(U)=\sum_i w_i|P_U(A_i)|$ attains a minimum over all simplex orientations. On the sublevel $F(U)\le M$, a member with an inball $B(x_i,\rho_i)$ has every envelope vertex $v$ bounded by
$$
\|v-x_i\|\le dM/(w_i\kappa_{d-1}\rho_i^{d-1}),
$$
where $\kappa_{d-1}$ is the unit ball volume and $\kappa_0=1$. If $P_U(A_i)=a_i+r_iP_U(A_*)$ and $|A_i|>0$, then
$$
(w_*|A_i|/M)^{1/d}\le r_i\le (M/(w_i|A_*|))^{1/d}.
$$
On the sublevel, a sequence has a subsequence with convergent anchor vertices, orientations and labeled vertices of every envelope. Its limit orientation has full-dimensional anchor envelope, and objective values converge. The full-dimensional member hypothesis cannot in general be omitted.

pk-intake-weighted-finite-barycentric-at.relation_to_goal: Finite physical barycentric coupling and atom ceilings. The result supplies no depth bound.
pk-intake-weighted-finite-barycentric-at.statement:
Let $P_i\subset\mathbb R^N$ be finite, $1\le i\le k$, and let $\gamma_i$ be finite nonnegative measures on $P_i$ of common mass. Let $\lambda_i>0$ sum to one, let $b(x)=\sum_i\lambda_i x_i$, and suppose $\gamma_i(\{x\})\le a_i(x)$ for finite nonnegative functions $a_i$ on $P_i$. Define
$$
c(z)=\max_{b(x)=z,\ x_i\in\operatorname{supp}\gamma_i}\ \min_i a_i(x_i),
$$
with the empty maximum zero. For any old coupling $\pi_0$ of the $\gamma_i$, one coupling $\pi$ of the same marginals satisfies $b_\#\pi_0\preceq_{\rm cx}b_\#\pi$ and $(b_\#\pi)(\{z\})\le c(z)$ for every $z$. Any fixed output atom ceiling dominating the displayed product envelope may also be used. Convex order tests all finite convex functions on the physical space.

pk-intake-weighted-hausdorff-normal-cone.relation_to_goal: Transfers nonnegative Borel mass under actual translations, with an exact affine-span exclusion and one retained baseline. In mixed lattices, the translations preserve the lattice in sum coordinates.
pk-intake-weighted-hausdorff-normal-cone.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be nonempty compact sets, $V$ a linear subspace, $q\ge0$ with $\mathcal H_q(A)<\infty$, and $Z=V+\operatorname{conv} B$. Suppose nonnegative Borel functions $F$ on $\mathbb R^m$ and $g$ on $A$ satisfy $F(a+b)\ge g(a)$ for all $a\in A$, $b\in B$. Then
$$
\int_{(A+B)\setminus Z}F\,d\mathcal H_q\ge\int_{A\setminus V}g\,d\mathcal H_q.
$$
For any one compact $P\subseteq A$ contained in an affine subspace $L$ this gives
$$
\int_{A+B}F\,d\mathcal H_q\ge
\int_{P+B}F\,d\mathcal H_q+\int_{A\setminus L}g\,d\mathcal H_q.
$$
The inequalities allow extended integrals and include $q=0$. If $A,B$ lie in $\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, the translated source pieces lie in that lattice as actual sum points.

pk-intake-weighted-homothetic-shell-inci.relation_to_goal: An ordinary shell estimate for fixed proper-cut halfspaces in any dimension. It does not assert a dimension-independent depth bound.
pk-intake-weighted-homothetic-shell-inci.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body and let the finitely many closed halfspaces $H_i=\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge b_i\}$ cover $A$ and cut it properly. Write $w_i>0$, $U_i=|A\cap H_i|$ and $\sigma_i=\mathcal H^{d-1}(A\cap\{v_i\cdot x=b_i\})/\lVert v_i\rVert$. If $\sum_{i:x\in H_i}w_i\ge\tau$ almost everywhere on $A$, then every $p\in A$ satisfies
$$
\sum_i w_i\bigl[dU_i+(b_i-v_i\cdot p)\sigma_i\bigr]\ge d|A|\tau.
$$
If all singleton-capture regions with indices in a set $E$ are null, a valid $\tau$ is the minimum of the singleton weights $w_i$ for $i\notin E$ and all pair sums $w_i+w_j$ with $i\ne j$, taking the minimum over the combined nonempty list.

pk-intake-whole-fiber-capture-and-exact-.relation_to_goal: A criterion at a fixed mark of a buffered family.
pk-intake-whole-fiber-capture-and-exact-.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and nonempty, $n\ge0$, and let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, be compact convex bodies of positive volume, with $\sum_z\lambda_z K_z\subset K_p$ whenever $\lambda_z\ge0$, $\sum_z\lambda_z=1$ and $\sum_z\lambda_z z=p\in P$. Let $\mu$ sum $d$-volume on the lifted fibers and let $b_{\rm base}(p)$ be the minimum weight of a closed base halfspace containing $p$, using weights $|K_z|$. Include the whole-base trace, which is the sole trace in rank zero. Every closed ambient halfspace that contains $\{p\}\times K_p$ has mass at least $b_{\rm base}(p)$.

Fix $y\in\operatorname{int}K_p$, a positive definite matrix $\Sigma$ and $\delta>0$. Write $\Gamma(u)=\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma u}$ and let $b_\delta(p,y)$ be the infimum of masses of the caps
$$
a\cdot(z-p)+u\cdot(X-y)+\delta\Gamma(u)\ge0,\qquad u\ne0,
$$
and the pure-base caps. For $R(p,y)=\max_{X\in K_p}\sqrt{(X-y)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}(X-y)}$,
$$
b_\delta(p,y)<b_{\rm base}(p)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\delta<R(p,y),\qquad
b_\delta(p,y)=b_{\rm base}(p)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\delta\ge R(p,y).
$$
Under the strict gap, every minimizing cap is nonvertical and its boundary cuts the interior of $K_p$.

pk-intake-whole-fiber-ownership-componen.relation_to_goal: This is an unequal-mass partition counterexample to a stronger component bound when full-fiber ownership is permitted.
pk-intake-whole-fiber-ownership-componen.statement: There is a compact convex body in $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R$ with three positive integer fibers occupying $k=2$ parities and forming one component in the hypergraph that joins each distinct same-parity pair to its midpoint. Its mixed source has an almost-everywhere partition into $r=4$ original closed caps of masses $(1,1,6,2)$, and one of these caps contains an entire positive fiber. Thus $r=2k>2c(P)$ and $r>2(k-1)$ despite $|P|>k$, where $c(P)$ counts midpoint components.

pk-intake-whole-fiber-sparse-minimax-cer.relation_to_goal: This tests actual pointwise coverage of one compact fiber and retains its own boundary normal.
pk-intake-whole-fiber-sparse-minimax-cer.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty compact convex and $L_i(x)=u_i\cdot x+v_i$ be a nonempty finite family of affine margins. For the support function $h_K(w)=\max_{x\in K}w\cdot x$ and the probability simplex $\Delta_N$, one has the attained identity
$$
F=\min_{x\in K}\max_i L_i(x)
=\max_{\lambda\in\Delta_N}\left(\sum_i\lambda_i v_i-h_K\left(-\sum_i\lambda_i u_i\right)\right).
$$
Closed coverage of $K$ by $\{L_i\ge0\}$ is equivalent to $F\ge0$. If $F=0$, every primal minimizer $x_*$ and dual maximizer $\lambda$ satisfy $L_i(x_*)\le0$, $\lambda_i L_i(x_*)=0$, and $-\sum_i\lambda_i u_i\in N_K(x_*)$, where $N_K(x)=\{v:v\cdot(y-x)\le0\ \text{for all }y\in K\}$. There is a dual maximizer with at most $d+1$ positive entries.

pk-intake-whole-group-projected-helly-qu.relation_to_goal: A bounded selection of original circuit groups and its exact nearby upper comparison. A smooth local depth lower bound additionally requires feasible signed mass directions.
pk-intake-whole-group-projected-helly-qu.statement:
Let a nonempty finite base $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ carry positive compact convex $d$-fibers compatible with their common convex hull. Use the sum of fiber Lebesgue measures, let $q_z$ be maximal raw depth on the fiber at $z$, and let $Q=\max_z q_z$. Choose one actual critical circuit at a restricted maximizing mark at each $z$. For group $i$ at $z_i$, use its unit continuous normals $u_{ij}$, base normals $v_{ij}$, original thresholds $b_{ij}$, and positive circuit weights $\rho_{ij}$ summing to one. Let $A_i=\sum_j\rho_{ij}v_{ij}$ and $h_i=\sum_j\rho_{ij}b_{ij}=A_i\cdot z_i$. Then the projected halfspaces $G_i=\{w:A_i\cdot w\ge h_i\}$ cover $P$, and group $i$ covers the whole continuous plane over every $w\in G_i$. At most $h(P)$ whole groups suffice to cover $P$, where $h(P)$ is the relative Helly number for finite convex-set families on $P$. The selected groups with $q_{z_i}=Q$ cover every deepest base by their projected halfspaces.

For any locally Hausdorff-Lipschitz family of positive fibers at the same bases near the old parameter, keep the ambient normals fixed and continue each chosen group by its equal-mass quantile with weighted threshold sum $h_i$. Then the same projected halfspaces and the same group assignment persist. The maximum of the selected deepest-origin groups' common mass ratios is an upper bound on actual maximal normalized depth near the old parameter, with equality at that parameter. The same continuation conclusion holds when the individual local actual quantile inverses are supplied as jointly continuous strictly decreasing functions, even without a quantitative Hausdorff bound.

pk-intake-whole-line-hinge-regression-sh.relation_to_goal: Sharpness of a regression coefficient for actual whole-line covers at budgets at least one half.
pk-intake-whole-line-hinge-regression-sh.statement:
Let $L>1/2$, and at the binary bases $z\in\{0,1\}^2$ take the intervals $K_z=[\epsilon_z L-1/2,\epsilon_z L+1/2]$, where $\epsilon_{00}=\epsilon_{11}=1$ and $\epsilon_{10}=\epsilon_{01}=-1$. These are the actual integer fibers of their lifted convex hull and have total mass $M=4$. Use exactly two caps with unit continuous normals, required to cover the whole continuous line at each binary base, and impose cap mass at most $\tau M$. Feasibility holds exactly for $\tau\ge1/2$, and the minimum total hinge is $v(\tau)=4L$ throughout that range.

The minimizing pair $x\ge0,x\le0$ has an objective-one mass and moment stress with zero cap-budget multipliers, balanced weights $(1/2,1/2)$ and contact $x=0$ at each base, and $\eta_z=1$. The identity $M\sum_i r_i=-v'(\tau)=0$ holds for $1/2<\tau<1$. The source measure $\nu$ obtained by summing the cap restrictions of mixed volume is the original mixed volume. Label its two parts by their continuous normal $U=\epsilon_z$. If $x$ is projected in $L^2(\nu)$ onto the affine base features, the prediction is identically zero. For $A=\int U^2\,d\nu$, $Q=\int xU\,d\nu$, and $R_x=\int x^2\,d\nu$,
$$
A=4,\quad Q=4L,\quad R_x=4L^2+1/3,\qquad
R_x-QA^+Q=1/3,\quad \frac{R_x}{QA^+Q}=1+\frac{1}{12L^2}.
$$
Consequently no coefficient greater than one can hold uniformly in the source regression bound $R_x\ge QA^+Q$, even within these actual minimizing whole-line covers.

pk-intake-whole-space-cover-balanced-hin.relation_to_goal: Whole continuous space is covered over each sampled base. Hinges and budgets are evaluated only on the fixed source.
pk-intake-whole-space-cover-balanced-hin.statement:
Fix $n\ge0,d\ge1$, finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$, and full-dimensional compact convex fibers $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$. Write $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$, $\mu=\sum_z\delta_z\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_z})$ and $M=\mu(S)$. A cap has margin $L_i(z,x)=a_i\cdot z+u_i\cdot x-b_i$ with $\|u_i\|=1$, threshold $t_{iz}=b_i-a_i\cdot z$, mass $c_i=\mu\{L_i\ge0\}$, and hinge $\Psi_i=\int_S(L_i)_+\,d\mu$. For each $z$ the traces cover $\mathbb R^d$ if and only if there are simplex weights $\lambda_{zi}$ with $\sum_i\lambda_{zi}u_i=0$ and $\sum_i\lambda_{zi}t_{iz}\le0$. Equivalently the epigraph LP has finite attained value
$$
F_z=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^d}\max_i L_i(z,x)
=\max_{\lambda\in\Delta,\ \sum_i\lambda_i u_i=0}-\sum_i\lambda_i t_{iz}\ge0.
$$
At any feasible budget $\tau$ with $c_i\le\tau M$, the finite positive minimum of $\Psi=\sum_i\Psi_i$ over such whole-space covers is attained for a fixed cap count. This holds whether all unit normals are variable or some normals are prescribed, in particular with $N$ variable normals and a fixed frame of $2d$ normals $+e_l,-e_l$. Every cap has free offsets and base tilts and contributes to both objective and budgets.

pk-intake-whole-space-cover-value-right-.relation_to_goal: Sensitivity of the fixed-source fixed-cap-count optimization value. The integrated stress formula uses the framed polytopal case.
pk-intake-whole-space-cover-value-right-.statement:
The attained hinge value for whole-space covers is right-continuous at every feasible budget, in the fixed-count framed or unframed class with the full-dimensional compact convex source fibers of the whole-space attainment theorem. In the framed polytopal setting, for interior feasible $a<b$,
$$
w(a)-w(b)=M\int_a^b \sum_i r_i(t)\,dt+\sum_{a<t\le b}\big[w(t-)-w(t)\big],
$$
where the integral uses the normal stress budget multipliers at regular budgets through their unique total $-w'(t)/M$. The jump sum has finitely many nonzero terms.

pk-intake-whole-zonotope-cap-polynomial.relation_to_goal: The projected measures belong to one and the same actual cap. Its denominator is the total-mass polynomial at lengths $2k_i$.
pk-intake-whole-zonotope-cap-polynomial.statement:
Use the hypotheses and coefficients of the arithmetic zonotope polynomial. Set $Z=\sum_i[-k_i,k_i](v_i,0)$. For every closed ambient halfspace $H$,
$$
\mu_{n,d}((C+Z)\cap H)
\ge\sum_{I\ {\rm independent}}m(I)\mu_{n-|I|,d}(\pi_I(C\cap H))\prod_{i\in I} k_i .
$$
For a generator orthogonal to the integer component of the normal of $H$, replace its factor $k_i$ by $2k_i$ in the terms where it occurs. For a single primitive generator the coefficient one of $k\,\mu_{n-1,d}(\pi_v(C\cap H))$ is sharp even with a nonzero continuous normal and a nonzero pairing of the integer normal with $v$.

pk-intake-width-hinge-affine-covariance.relation_to_goal: Width gauge for fixed-measure, nonvertical full-cover hinge objectives.
pk-intake-width-hinge-affine-covariance.statement: For a centrally symmetric convex body $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ with $0\in\operatorname{int}D$, write $h_D(u)=\max_{v\in D}u\cdot v$. For nonvertical affine margins $L_i(z,x)=a_i\cdot z+u_i\cdot x-b_i$, define $\Psi_D=\sum_i\int_S(L_i)_+\,d\mu/h_D(u_i)$ on the finite positive-volume integer fibers with summed volume $\mu$ and mass $M$. Each margin may be positively rescaled to $h_D(u_i)=1$ without changing its contribution or its cap. Let $K_z$ be the fibers over the finite set $P$ of integer bases carrying positive volume, and set $D_{\rm int}=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(K_z-K_z)$. For fibers of a convex body $C$, put $D_{\rm all}=\{v:(0,v)\in C-C\}$. Both bodies are compact, convex, centrally symmetric and full-dimensional, and $D_{\rm int}\subseteq D_{\rm all}$. Under the map $(z,x)\mapsto(Uz+k,Ax+Bz+b)$ with $U$ integral unimodular, $k$ integral and $A$ invertible, each of these two bodies transforms to $AD$. For either choice of body, the ratio $\Psi_D/M$ and the normalized cap masses are invariant.

pk-intake-width-hinge-attainment.relation_to_goal: Attainment for a given feasible cap budget and fixed gauge.
pk-intake-width-hinge-attainment.statement: For a centrally symmetric convex body $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ with $0\in\operatorname{int}D$, write $h_D(u)=\max_{v\in D}u\cdot v$. For nonvertical affine margins $L_i(z,x)=a_i\cdot z+u_i\cdot x-b_i$, define $\Psi_D=\sum_i\int_S(L_i)_+\,d\mu/h_D(u_i)$ on the finite positive-volume integer fibers with summed volume $\mu$ and mass $M$. Assume $n,d,N\ge1$, every fiber $K_z$ is compact, convex and full-dimensional, and $0<\tau<1$. If there is a full cover of $S$ by $N$ closed nonvertical ambient caps each of mass at most $\tau M$, the minimum of $\Psi_D$ over these covers is attained. If $D\subset R B_d$ and $r_z>0$ are inball radii of the respective fibers, then every such cover satisfies $\Psi_D\ge\kappa_{d-1}\sum_z r_z^{d+1}/[(d+1)R]>0$, where $\kappa_j$ denotes Euclidean unit $j$-ball volume and $\kappa_0=1$.

pk-intake-width-hinge-same-real-base-mom.relation_to_goal: Conditional bound for a stress with actual cap, section and contact measures.
pk-intake-width-hinge-same-real-base-mom.statement: Let $C\subset\mathbb R^{n+d}$ be a compact convex body with positive-volume integer fibers and mixed volume $\mu$ on those fibers. Write $D_{\rm all}=\{v:(0,v)\in C-C\}$. Take a cap with affine margin $L_i(z,x)=a_i\cdot z+u_i\cdot x-b_i$ and $h_{D_{\rm all}}(u_i)=1$. Let $\Psi_i=\int (L_i)_+\,d\mu$ and let $\mu_i=\mu|_{\{L_i\ge0\}}$ have mass $c_i$. Suppose a finite nonnegative section measure $\sigma_i$ on $C\cap\{L_i=0\}$ has mass $S_i$ and a finite nonnegative contact measure $\nu_i$ is also supported on $C\cap\{L_i=0\}$. If for $\alpha_0,r_i\ge0$ the measures $\alpha_0\mu_i+r_i\sigma_i$ and $\nu_i$ have common mass $W_i=\alpha_0c_i+r_i S_i$ and common base first moment, then $\alpha_0\Psi_i\le W_i$. In particular, in a normalized stress with $\alpha_0=1$ and contact masses $\sum_z\eta_z\lambda_{zi}$ for $\lambda_z\in\Delta_N$, this gives $\Psi_i\le c_i+r_iS_i$ and $\Psi_D\le\sum_z\eta_z$.

pk-intake-width-hinge-simplex-product-st.relation_to_goal: Sharp-product width value and explicit normal stress, including nonregular simplices.
pk-intake-width-hinge-simplex-product-st.statement:
Let $C=[0,1]^n\times K$ with $n,d\ge1$ and $K$ a $d$-simplex of volume $v$. Use $D=K-K$, which is both same-base difference bodies, and let $M=2^n v$, $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. At cap budget $\gamma_d v$ and cap count $2^n(d+1)$, the exact width-normalized hinge value of every full cover is $M\gamma_d d/(d+1)$, and it is attained.

For any such cover, in the normalization $h_D(u_i)=1$ there is a width contact stress with objective multiplier $\alpha_0=1$ and all cap-budget multipliers zero. On each fiber $p$ use the simplex centroid $g$, probability weights $1/(d+1)$ on that fiber's canonical caps, and $\eta_p=(d+1)\gamma_d v$. For the cap of vertex $v_j$ take $R_j=v_j-g_j$ with $g_j$ the centroid of its opposite facet. If $c_i,P_i,m_i$ are raw cap mass and moments, the stress identities are
$$
c_i=\sum_p\eta_p\lambda_{pi},\qquad
P_i=\sum_p\eta_p\lambda_{pi}p,\qquad
m_i=\sum_p\eta_p\lambda_{pi}g+\Psi_iR_j,
$$
where $\Psi_i=\int_S(L_i)_+\,d\mu$ in the width representatives, $R_j$ maximizes $u_i\cdot v$ over $D$, and the fiber weights give zero minimax margin with genuine contacts at $g$.

pk-intake-width-one-centroid-slab.relation_to_goal: Gives a quantitative ordinary cap gain from lowering a threshold below the centroid level.
pk-intake-width-one-centroid-slab.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, $d\ge2$, with centroid $g$, and let $X$ be uniform on $K$. Fix a linear functional $\ell$ of width one on $K$. Write $p$ for the density of $\ell(X)$ given by section volumes, $m=\ell(g)$, and $A=m-\min_K\ell$. Then $p\le d$ and $p(m)\ge1$. Lowering a cap threshold by $a\ge0$ increases its normalized mass by at most $da$. For $0\le a\le A$,
$$
\mathbb P\{m-a\le\ell(X)\le m\}\ge a/d.
$$
In particular, if $y\in K$ and $\ell(g-y)\ge0$, then
$$

pk-intake-zero-active-hinge-defects-forc.relation_to_goal: Identifies the extra active-hinge equalities sufficient for identity on a given full-capacity menu.
pk-intake-zero-active-hinge-defects-forc.statement:
Let $\eta$ be a finite nonzero capacity measure on a compact subset of a Euclidean physical space, let $L_i$ be a finite list of affine margins, and set $W_\theta=\sum_i\theta_i\mathbf1_{\{L_i\ge0\}}$ for $\theta_i\ge0$. Fix $\beta>0$ and suppose $\mu_\theta=(W_\theta/\beta)\eta$ has the same total mass as $\eta$. Suppose neither measure charges the boundaries $\{L_i=0\}$ of the active margins ($\theta_i>0$). Assume there is a physical martingale from $\mu_\theta$ to $\eta$ and write $J_i=\int[L_i]_+\,d(\eta-\mu_\theta)$. The following conditions are equivalent.
- $\sum_i\theta_iJ_i=0$.
- $J_i=0$ for every active $i$.
- $\mu_\theta=\eta$.
- Every physical martingale between the two measures is concentrated on the identity.

The equivalence also holds for martingales required to preserve a given measurable label when at least one such martingale exists and the two measures are understood on the labelled space with $\mu_\theta=(W_\theta/\beta)\eta$. Identity here refers to the full physical coordinate.

pk-intake-zero-diagonal-geometric-mean-s.relation_to_goal: Exact duality for the auxiliary zero-diagonal geometric-mean image.
pk-intake-zero-diagonal-geometric-mean-s.statement:
For $d\ge1$ and $m=d+1$, let $D_d$ consist of all $v\in\mathbb R_+^m$ for which there exists a nonnegative zero-diagonal column-stochastic $m\times m$ matrix $Y$ satisfying $v_i\le \operatorname{GM}_d((Y_{ij})_{j\ne i})$ for every $i$, where $\operatorname{GM}_d$ is the geometric mean of $d$ entries. The set $D_d$ is compact, convex, and downward in the nonnegative orthant. For every $c\ge0$ its support function satisfies the attained identity
$$
h_{D_d}(c)=\min\left\{\sum_j\lambda_j:\ \lambda\ge0,\ c_i\le d\left(\prod_{j\ne i}\lambda_j\right)^{1/d}\ \text{for every }i\right\}.
$$
In particular, $v\ge0$ belongs to $D_d$ if and only if
$$
\sum_jp_j^d-d\sum_i v_i\prod_{j\ne i}p_j\ge0\qquad\text{for every }p\ge0.
$$
This gives $D_1=[0,1]^2$ and $D_2=\{v\ge0:\sum_i v_i^2+2v_1v_2v_3\le1\}$. For positive $\lambda$ with $\sum_j\lambda_j=dT$ and each $\lambda_i\le T$, the choice $c_i=d(\prod_{j\ne i}\lambda_j)^{1/d}$ gives an attaining primal matrix $Y_{ii}=0$ and $Y_{ij}=(T-\lambda_i)/\lambda_j$ for $i\ne j$.
