pk-intake-zero-endpoint-facet-moment-and.relation_to_goal: One fixed cap in a compatible chain. Moment membership characterizes directional first-order inequalities. It does not assert local minimality from first-order conditions.
pk-intake-zero-endpoint-facet-moment-and.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, with positive compact convex fibers $A,K,B$ at $-1,0,1$ and $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. For a cap $u\cdot(x-y)+\alpha z\ge0$ through $y\in\operatorname{int}K$, $u\ne0$, suppose the $A,K$ cuts are proper with areas $t,s>0$ and centroids $c_A,c_K$, and the $B$ cut is at an outside supporting facet $F$ of area $M>0$. Use intrinsic surface measure $dS=d\mathcal H^{d-1}|_F$. Let $\mathsf M_t(F)$ be the set of means of densities $0\le\theta\le1$ on $F$ of mass $t$, defined for $0<t\le M$. Put $b_*=(2t+s)y-tc_A-sc_K$. The inequalities
$$
t[w\cdot(c_A-y)-\beta]+s\,w\cdot(c_K-y)+\int_F[w\cdot(x-y)+\beta]_+\,dS\ge0
\qquad(w\in\mathbb R^d,\ \beta\in\mathbb R)
$$
are equivalent to $t\le M$ and $b_*\in t\mathsf M_t(F)$. The equivalent selector equation is
$$
t(c_A-y)+s(c_K-y)+\int_F\theta(x)(x-y)\,dS=0,\qquad \int_F\theta\,dS=t.
$$
For $t<M$, any admissible prescribed mean is attained by a convex combination of at most $d$ indicators of actual intrinsic volume-$t$ caps of $F$. At a relative boundary mean every selector is the same such indicator almost everywhere. For $t=M$ the selector is the full facet, and if also $s=t$ then $E_A,F$ are translates, $E_K=(E_A+F)/2$, and $y=c_K$.

For $0<t\le M$ and $b_*\notin t\mathsf M_t(F)$, let $p$ be its nearest point in that set and put $w=b_*-p$. With $\delta$ any minimizer of $\int_F[w\cdot x+\delta]_+\,dS-t\delta$, choose $\beta=\delta+w\cdot y$. This perturbation at the fixed mark has right capture derivative $-\|b_*-p\|^2/\|u\|$. Its continuous-normal increment $w$ is tangent to the facet, and the perturbed cap has strictly smaller mass for all sufficiently small positive sizes.

pk-intake-zero-right-index-knot-deficit.relation_to_goal: Pointwise bound for the scalar diagonal-envelope deficit at admissible zero-right-index knots. Selection of a maximizing knot and any application to actual mixed-integer halfspace depth require separate arguments.
pk-intake-zero-right-index-knot-deficit.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and $1\le H\le d$ be integers. Put $t=1/(d+1)$ and $\Gamma=(dt)^d$. At the zero-right-index double knot let
$$
a_H=\frac{H+1}{H(d+1)},\qquad \beta_H=\frac{1}{d(d+1)}.
$$
Write $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$. For each integer $h\ge0$ put $r_h=(1-a_H h)_+$, $q_h=t-\beta_H h$, and $p_h=t+\beta_H(h+1)$. For $r,s>0$ let $E_d(s,r)=d^d s^{d-1}(r-ds)_+$, and let $E_d(s,0)=0$ for every real $s$. The thresholds are positive on positive radii. Define the finite diagonal-envelope deficit and the two normalized sums by
$$
\begin{aligned}
D_d(a_H,\beta_H)&=\Gamma\sum_{h\ge0}r_h^d-\sum_{h\ge0}\bigl[E_d(q_h,r_h)+E_d(p_h,r_h)\bigr],\\
W_{d,H}&=\sum_{j\ge0}(1-a_H j)_+^d,\\
K_{d,H}&=\sum_{j=0}^{H-1}(1-j/d)^{d-1}(1-j/H).
\end{aligned}
$$
The normalized left envelope sum is $K_{d,H}$, the right envelope sum vanishes, and $D_d(a_H,\beta_H)/\Gamma=W_{d,H}-K_{d,H}<1/6$.

projected-depth-hit-range-lift.relation_to_goal:
Accepted fact `4e868f774de77608` proves joint concavity and upper
semicontinuity of \(\delta_C^{1/d}\), convex compact depth bundles, and
attainment and concavity of the maximal depth root \(g\). The present
subgoal packages those facts into a one-extra-coordinate convex lift and
adds the new hit-range convexity, exact weighted mass identity, fiberwise
hit domination, and point-lifting implication.

If a later theorem produced an absolute \(\beta>0\) and a point
\(q\in B\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R)\) with
\[
D_{\mathrm{hit}}(q)\geq\beta2^{-n}|\eta|,
\]
then this depth-lift and \(\gamma_d>1/e\) would imply the locked target with
any fixed \(c_0<\beta/e\). That range-centerpoint assertion is not part of
this subgoal and is currently unsupported. Ordinary mixed centerpoint
theorems control halfspaces in \(B\), whereas the sets
\(\mathcal A_H\) are convex projections and need not be halfspaces.

The accepted affine-selector results are a special compatible regime of
this framework, but they do not prove the general hit-range statement.
The present theorem is therefore a structural reduction, not a solution or
a renamed form of the locked target.
projected-depth-hit-range-lift.statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, and for
\((z,x)\in C\) define
\[
\delta_C(z,x):=
\inf\left\{
\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z\cap J):
J\subseteq\mathbb R^d\text{ is a proper closed halfspace and }x\in J
\right\}.
\]
Put
\[
g(z):=\max_{x\in C_z}\delta_C(z,x)^{1/d},
\qquad
B:=\{(z,u):z\in\operatorname{proj}_{\mathbb R^n}C,\ 0\leq u\leq g(z)\}.
\]
On \(B\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R)\), define the finite measure
\(\eta\) fiberwise by
\[
d\eta(z,u):=d\,u^{d-1}\,du.
\]
For every closed halfspace
\(H\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}\), define
\[
\mathcal A_H:=
\left\{
(z,u)\in B:
\exists x\in C_z\cap H_z
\text{ with }\delta_C(z,x)\geq u^d
\right\},
\]
where \(H_z:=\{x:(z,x)\in H\}\).

Prove the following exact depth-lift theorem.

1. \(B\) is compact and convex, every \(\mathcal A_H\) is compact and
convex, and
\[
|\eta|
=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}\max_{x\in C_z}\delta_C(z,x)
\geq
\gamma_d\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z),
\qquad
\gamma_d:=\left(\frac d{d+1}\right)^d.
\]

2. Every closed ambient halfspace satisfies
\[
\eta(\mathcal A_H)
\leq
\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z\cap H_z).
\]

3. For \(q\in B\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R)\), define
\[
D_{\mathrm{hit}}(q):=
\inf\{\eta(\mathcal A_H):H\text{ is a closed halfspace and }
q\in\mathcal A_H\}.
\]
If \(q=(m,u)\) and \(x\in C_m\) satisfies
\(\delta_C(m,x)\geq u^d\), then
\[
h_S((m,x))\geq D_{\mathrm{hit}}(q).
\]

The theorem must not assert an unconditional lower bound for
\(\sup_qD_{\mathrm{hit}}(q)\).

projected-depth-logconcave-selection.relation_to_goal:
This is a continuous closure interface for the accepted
autocorrelation/metronoid routes.

Accepted fact `725defc391f9d55d` proves the metronoid support-function
characterization for a discrete mixed marginal, but its selected
submeasure need not be log-concave.  Accepted facts
`ecdcb5a24b2eac2c` and `0a2b4c19d781e819` give different depth bounds
for specific barycentric constructions and retain a minimum-coefficient
or effective-support loss.  The present statement asks whether ordinary
log-concavity removes those losses while preserving a prescribed base
coordinate.

If a future alignment mechanism supplies a log-concave block of mass
\(\beta2^{-n}W\) dominated by the original mixed measure and whose base
marginal has an integer point of depth \(\alpha\) within that block, the
present conclusion gives an admissible mixed point with depth
\[
\frac{\alpha\beta}{e}\,2^{-n}W.
\]
All losses are explicit and dimension-free.  The still-missing step is
the construction of that ordinary log-concave dominated block; this
subgoal does not assert it.

The statement is independent of the lattice target and is strictly
weaker than the locked conjecture.  A counterexample would kill the
proposed entropy/logistic continuous closure without threatening the
locked target.
projected-depth-logconcave-selection.statement:
Let \(N=n+d\) with \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).  Let \(\rho\) be a nonzero
compactly supported log-concave finite Borel measure on
\(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\), let \(M:=|\rho|\), and let
\[
P(z,x):=z,\qquad \pi:=P_\#\rho.
\]
Fix \(z_0\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1]\).  Assume that every
closed base halfspace \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) containing \(z_0\)
satisfies
\[
\pi(Q)\geq\alpha M.
\]

Prove or disprove that there is a compactly supported log-concave finite
measure \(\sigma\) on \(\mathbb R^{n+d}\) such that
\[
0\leq\sigma\leq\rho,\qquad
|\sigma|=\alpha M,
\]
and the base coordinate of the barycenter of \(\sigma\) is exactly
\(z_0\).

Consequently, prove or disprove that there is \(x_0\in\mathbb R^d\) such
that \(p=(z_0,x_0)\) satisfies
\[
\rho(H)\geq\frac{\alpha}{e}M
\]
for every closed ambient halfspace \(H\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}\)
containing \(p\).

The statement must include log-concave measures supported on a proper
affine subspace, the cases \(\alpha=1\) and \(z_0\) on the boundary of
the level-\(\alpha\) metronoid, and closed halfspaces carrying positive
\(\rho\)- or \(\sigma\)-mass.

shallow-active-balance-compression.statement:
Fix \(\kappa:=1/16\). Prove or disprove that there is an absolute integer
\(K\geq 1\) with the following property.

Let \(n\geq2\), \(d\geq1\), and let
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}\) be a convex body with positive mixed mass
\[
W:=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z)>0.
\]
Let \(z_0\in\mathbb Z^n\) have \(w_{z_0}>0\) and weighted marginal
halfspace depth at least \(2^{-n}W\), and let
\(y_0\in\operatorname{int}C_{z_0}\) maximize
\(h_{C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)}((z_0,y))\) over
\(y\in C_{z_0}\). Put
\[
t:=h_{C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)}((z_0,y_0)).
\]
Then at least one of the following holds:

1. \(t\geq\kappa\,2^{-n}W\).
2. There are \(1\leq r\leq n\), a primitive rank-\((n-r)\) sublattice
   \(L\leq\mathbb Z^n\), and \(a\in\mathbb Z^n\) such that
   \[
   \sum_{z\in a+L}w_z\geq2^{-r}W.
   \]
3. For every \(\varepsilon>0\), there are \(1\leq s\leq K\), Euclidean
   unit normals \(u_i=(a_i,b_i)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\),
   positive weights \(\lambda_i\) summing to one, and closed halfspaces
   \[
   H_i=\{(z,x):
   a_i^\top(z-z_0)+b_i^\top(x-y_0)\geq0\}
   \]
   such that
   \[
   \mathcal H_d\bigl(C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\cap H_i\bigr)
   \leq t+\varepsilon
   \quad(1\leq i\leq s),
   \qquad
   \sum_{i=1}^s\lambda_i b_i=0.
   \]

The assertion concerns ordinary closed caps through the common anchor. The
constant \(K\) must be independent of \(n,d,C,z_0,y_0\), and
\(\varepsilon\).

simplex-depth-one-vertex-cap-formula.statement:
Let \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let
\[
\Delta_d:=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_d\}
\]
be a full-dimensional simplex, and let
\(\lambda_0(x),\ldots,\lambda_d(x)\) be the barycentric coordinates of
\(x\in\Delta_d\). For \(x\in\Delta_d\), define its normalized halfspace
depth
\[
\operatorname{depth}_{\Delta_d}(x):=
\frac1{\operatorname{vol}_d(\Delta_d)}
\inf\left\{
\operatorname{vol}_d(\Delta_d\cap H):
H\subseteq\mathbb R^d\text{ is a proper closed halfspace and }x\in H
\right\}.
\]

For \(i\in\{0,\ldots,d\}\) and \(x\) in the relative interior of
\(\Delta_d\), define the one-vertex cap value
\[
V_i(x):=
\min\left\{
\prod_{j\ne i}t_j:
0<t_j\leq1,\quad
\sum_{j\ne i}\frac{\lambda_j(x)}{t_j}\leq1
\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, this is the smallest relative volume of a cap of the form
\[
\Delta_d\cap
\left\{
y:\sum_{j\ne i}\frac{\lambda_j(y)}{t_j}\leq1
\right\}
\]
that contains \(x\) and whose distinguished contained vertex is \(v_i\).

Prove or disprove the exact formula
\[
\operatorname{depth}_{\Delta_d}(x)
=\min_{0\leq i\leq d}V_i(x)
\qquad(x\in\operatorname{relint}\Delta_d).
\]

As part of a positive proof, establish the exact water-filling evaluation:
for every \(i\), there is a unique \(\mu_i>0\) satisfying
\[
\sum_{j\ne i}
\frac{\lambda_j(x)}
{\min\{1,\mu_i\lambda_j(x)\}}
=1,
\]
and
\[
V_i(x)=
\prod_{j\ne i}\min\{1,\mu_i\lambda_j(x)\}.
\]
Extend the result continuously to the boundary, where the halfspace depth
is zero, and prove the affine-invariant version for an arbitrary
full-dimensional simplex.

simplex-subset-beta-cap-envelope.statement:
Let \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let
\[
\Delta_d:=\left\{y\in\mathbb R^d:
y_i\ge0,\ \sum_{i=1}^d y_i\le1\right\},
\]
and write the \(d+1\) barycentric coordinates of \(y\in\Delta_d\) as
\[
\lambda_0(y):=1-\sum_{i=1}^d y_i,\qquad
\lambda_i(y):=y_i\quad(1\le i\le d).
\]
For \(x\in\Delta_d\), define its absolute halfspace depth
\[
\delta_{\Delta_d}(x):=
\inf\{\operatorname{vol}_d(\Delta_d\cap H):
H\subseteq\mathbb R^d\text{ is a proper closed halfspace and }x\in H\}.
\]

For every nonempty proper subset
\(I\subsetneq\{0,\ldots,d\}\), put
\[
k:=|I|,\qquad
s_I(x):=\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i(x),
\]
and
\[
F_{d,k}(s):=
\frac{d!}{(k-1)!(d-k)!}
\int_0^s t^{k-1}(1-t)^{d-k}\,dt
\qquad(0\le s\le1).
\]
Prove the exact polynomial identity
\[
F_{d,k}(s)
=\sum_{j=k}^{d}\binom dj s^j(1-s)^{d-j}
\]
and the subset-cap depth bound
\[
\frac{\delta_{\Delta_d}(x)}
{\operatorname{vol}_d(\Delta_d)}
\le
\min_{\varnothing\ne I\subsetneq\{0,\ldots,d\}}
\min\{F_{d,|I|}(s_I(x)),\,1-F_{d,|I|}(s_I(x))\}.
\]
The proof must identify the two proper closed halfspaces through \(x\)
whose exact relative volumes are the two displayed Beta tails.

full-dimensional simplex, using its barycentric coordinates.

simplex-transportation-centroid-core.statement:
Let \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let
\[
T=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_d\}
\]
be a full-dimensional \(d\)-simplex, and let
\[
x=\sum_{i=0}^d\lambda_i v_i,\qquad
\lambda_i\ge0,\qquad\sum_{i=0}^d\lambda_i=1.
\]
Put
\[
L(x):=\{i:(d+1)\lambda_i<1\}
\]
and use the empty-product convention.

Prove that there is a possibly degenerate simplex
\[
Q_x=\operatorname{conv}\{w_0,\ldots,w_d\}\subseteq T
\]
whose centroid is \(x\) and whose relative volume is
\[
\frac{\operatorname{vol}_d(Q_x)}{\operatorname{vol}_d(T)}
=
\prod_{i\in L(x)}(d+1)\lambda_i.
\]
Consequently, for normalized halfspace depth with proper closed halfspaces,
\[
\operatorname{depth}_T(x)
\ge
\left(\frac d{d+1}\right)^d
\prod_{i\in L(x)}(d+1)\lambda_i.
\]

The construction must be affine invariant and valid on the boundary, where the displayed product and the \(d\)-volume may vanish.

six-cone-continuum-uniform-core.statement:
Put
\[
p(x,y):=|x|+|y|+|x+y|,
\qquad
\overline H:=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:p(x,y)\leq1\},
\]
\[
\Delta_{30}:=\left\{u\in\mathbb R^{30}:
u_i\geq0,\ \sum_{i=1}^{30}u_i\leq1\right\},
\]
\[
K_{x,y}:=
\bigl(|x|,|y|,|x+y|,0,\ldots,0\bigr)
+(1-p(x,y))\Delta_{30}
\qquad((x,y)\in\overline H).
\]
For \(v\in K_{x,y}\), define
\[
\delta_{x,y}(v):=
\inf\left\{
\operatorname{vol}_{30}(K_{x,y}\cap J):
J\subseteq\mathbb R^{30}\text{ is a proper closed halfspace and }v\in J
\right\}.
\]
For an affine map \(s:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^{30}\) and
\(\tau\geq0\), put
\[
D(s,\tau):=
\left\{
(x,y)\in\overline H:
s(x,y)\in K_{x,y},\
\delta_{x,y}(s(x,y))\geq\tau
\right\}.
\]
Define the continuum rank-two uniform affine-core capacity
\[
\mathfrak U_\infty:=
\sup_{\substack{s:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^{30}\text{ affine}\\\tau\geq0}}
\frac{\tau}{4}\operatorname{area}D(s,\tau),
\]
and
\[
W_\infty:=
\frac1{30!}\int_{\{p<1\}}(1-p(x,y))^{30}\,dx\,dy
=\frac3{1984\cdot30!}.
\]

Prove or disprove the exact inequality
\[
\mathfrak U_\infty\geq\frac{W_\infty}{64}.
\]

support-lifted-congestion-ledger.statement:

236e5d1f3c2efa28 and 637b5f7874d8c875. Define

\[
\mathcal U_\beta
:=
\max_{s:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^d\ {\rm affine}}
\sum_{\substack{e:\beta_e^{\mathrm{cong}}>0\\
s(m_e)\in L_e}}r_e.
\]

\[
\boxed{C_\beta\le\mathcal U_\beta\le R}
\]

and the strengthened legal ledger

D+R+R_{\mathrm{sel}}(C)
\ge
A+\max\{Q-\Omega,\mathcal U_\beta\}

support-safe-flat-pair-depth.statement:
Prove a support-safe flat-pair lower bound for every halfspace through a fiber anchor. Let \(a(z)=|C_z|_d\), let \(x_0\in C_{z_0}\) have positive absolute fiber depth \(\delta_0\), put \(\beta=\delta_0/a(z_0)\), \(q=(1-\beta)^{1/d}\), and \(g=a^{1/d}\). Show that whenever
\[
2g(z_0)-g(z_0+w)-g(z_0-w)\le(1-q)g(z_0),
\]
the two fibers at \(z_0\pm w\) contribute at least
\(\beta\min\{a(z_0+w),a(z_0-w)\}\)
to every boundary-through-\((z_0,x_0)\) halfspace. Deduce the corresponding depth bound for any family of pairwise disjoint symmetric pairs.

support-safe-pair-energy.relation_to_goal:
Accepted fact `92b530e0a2281d6e` proves a pair contribution
\[
\beta\min\{a(z_0+v),a(z_0-v)\}
\]
under an additional flatness hypothesis. Its proof already identifies the two cases that matter here: when both opposite-cap endpoint fibers have positive volume, root concavity gives a capped sum budget; when one endpoint disappears from the positive support, one entire original endpoint fiber is retained.

The registered statement asks for the exact capped optimization without a flatness hypothesis. The minimum with \(A^d\) and \(B^d\) is meant to make the estimate support-safe and also valid for vertical halfspaces. If both removed endpoint fibers have positive volume, the pair contribution should be at least \(\Phi_{d,S_0}(A,B)\). If one is absent, or if the ambient halfspace is vertical, the unconditional contribution is only \(\min\{A^d,B^d\}\). These cases must not be conflated by extending a root-concave cap profile by zero.

The untruncated formula proposed in the consultation is suspect even for \(n=d=1\): an exact trapezoidal or conical body with affine fiber lengths at \(-1,0,1\) can make a vertical halfspace through the middle-fiber anchor smaller than
\[
\delta_0+\Phi_{d,S_0}(A,B).
\]
A valid packet should either prove such a calibration exactly or show why this smoke test is wrong.

The support-safe theorem would strengthen `92b530e0a2281d6e` by removing its flatness assumption and recording the exact remaining pair energy. It still does not close the target: one must prove a dimension-uniform global lower bound for the sum of the \(\Psi\)-terms or obtain a primitive heavy slice through `314b32bda8a0b01e`.
support-safe-pair-energy.statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}\) be a convex body, and write
\[
C_z:=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:(z,x)\in C\},\qquad
a(z):=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z).
\]
Fix \(z_0\in\mathbb Z^n\) and \(x_0\in C_{z_0}\) with absolute fiber depth
\[
\delta_0:=
\inf\{\operatorname{vol}_d(C_{z_0}\cap J):
J\subseteq\mathbb R^d\text{ is a closed halfspace and }x_0\in J\}>0.
\]
Put
\[
\beta:=\frac{\delta_0}{a(z_0)},\qquad
q:=(1-\beta)^{1/d},\qquad
R:=a(z_0)^{1/d},\qquad
S_0:=2qR.
\]
For \(A,B\geq0\), define
\[
\Phi_{d,S_0}(A,B):=
A^d+B^d-
\max\{s^d+t^d:0\leq s\leq A,\ 0\leq t\leq B,\ s+t\leq S_0\},
\]
and the support-safe contribution
\[
\Psi_{d,S_0}(A,B):=
\min\{\Phi_{d,S_0}(A,B),A^d,B^d\}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal P\) be any family of pairwise disjoint symmetric pairs
\[
\{z_0+v,z_0-v\}\subseteq\mathbb Z^n,\qquad v\neq0.
\]
Prove or disprove
\[
h_{C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)}((z_0,x_0))
\geq
\delta_0+
\sum_{\{z_0+v,z_0-v\}\in\mathcal P}
\Psi_{d,S_0}\!\left(
a(z_0+v)^{1/d},a(z_0-v)^{1/d}
\right).
\]

The strongest natural packet should also give the explicit endpoint formula for \(\Phi_{d,S_0}\) and an exact full-dimensional convex-body calibration showing that the truncation by \(A^d\) and \(B^d\) cannot simply be deleted from the universal statement.

\[
B:=\left\{m+\sum_{i=1}^qk_iu_i:-L_i\le k_i\le L_i,\ k_i\in\mathbb Z\right\}
\]
and its corners \(v_\varepsilon=m+\sum_i\varepsilon_iL_iu_i\). If for every \(\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}^q\) there is \(x_\varepsilon\in C_{v_\varepsilon}\) with absolute fiber depth at least \(s\ge0\), prove that
\[
p:=\left(m,2^{-q}\sum_\varepsilon x_\varepsilon\right)\in S
\]
and
\[
h_S(p)\ge s\prod_{i=1}^q(L_i+1)\ge2^{-q}s|B|.
\]
As a calibration, verify that the shifted-corner \(3\times3\) example in the attachment can have no affine selector through all four depth-\(s\) corner cores when \(M>2-4s\), while this certificate gives mixed depth at least \(9s/4\).

symmetric-kernel-depth-certificate.statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, let
\[
S:=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d),
\]
and let \(\mu_C\) denote mixed-integer volume on \(S\). For
\(p=(m,x)\in S\), define
\[
A_p:=C\cap(2p-C),\qquad
J_C(p):=\mu_C(A_p).
\]
For \((z,x)\in C\), define the local symmetric overlap
\[
s_C(z,x):=
\operatorname{vol}_d\bigl(C_z\cap(2x-C_z)\bigr).
\]

Prove the following exact package.

1. For every \(p\in S\),
\[
h_S(p)\geq\frac12J_C(p).
\]
Moreover,
\[
h_S(p)\geq
2^{-n-1}\operatorname{vol}_{n+d}\bigl(C\cap(2p-C)\bigr).
\]

2. The function
\[
(z,x)\longmapsto s_C(z,x)^{1/d}
\]
is concave on \(C\), with the value zero permitted on
lower-dimensional fibers.

3. Consequently, for every finite family
\((z_i,x_i)\in C\), coefficients \(\alpha_i\geq0\) with
\(\sum_i\alpha_i=1\), and
\[
m:=\sum_i\alpha_i z_i\in\mathbb Z^n,\qquad
x:=\sum_i\alpha_i x_i,
\]
one has \((m,x)\in S\) and
\[
h_S((m,x))
\geq
\frac12
\left(
\sum_i\alpha_i s_C(z_i,x_i)^{1/d}
\right)^d.
\]

As part of assertion 1, prove self-containedly the sampling statement
needed for the continuous-volume comparison: if
\(K\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) is a compact centrally symmetric convex set
whose center belongs to \(\mathbb Z^q\), then
\[
\operatorname{vol}_q(K)\leq2^q|K\cap\mathbb Z^q|,
\]
and derive the corresponding layer-cake inequality for a nonnegative
function whose positive superlevel sets are centrally symmetric convex
sets with one common lattice center.

two-level-simplex-depth.statement:
Let
\[
\Delta_{30}:=\left\{u=(u_0,\ldots,u_{30})\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{31}:
\sum_{i=0}^{30}u_i=1\right\}
\]
be regarded as a 30-dimensional simplex in its affine hull, with normalized halfspace depth
\[
\operatorname{depth}_{\Delta_{30}}(q):=
\frac{1}{\operatorname{vol}_{30}(\Delta_{30})}
\inf\left\{\operatorname{vol}_{30}(\Delta_{30}\cap H):
H\text{ is a proper closed halfspace of the affine hull and }q\in H\right\}.
\]
For \(0<b\le1/31\), put
\[
a:=\frac{1-2b}{29}
\]
and let \(q(a,b)\in\operatorname{relint}\Delta_{30}\) have twenty-nine barycentric coordinates equal to \(a\) and the remaining two equal to \(b\). Define
\[
F_{30,2}(s):=\sum_{j=2}^{30}\binom{30}{j}s^j(1-s)^{30-j}.
\]

Prove or disprove the exact formula
\[
\operatorname{depth}_{\Delta_{30}}(q(a,b))
=
\min\left\{(1-a)^{30},F_{30,2}(2b)\right\}
\qquad(0<b\le1/31).
\]

The two displayed quantities are the relative volumes of explicit proper closed subset-coordinate caps through \(q(a,b)\). The claim is that no multi-level or generic oblique cap through this two-level point has smaller volume.

weighted-planar-simplex-depth-eleven-six.statement:
Let \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^2\) be a compact convex set, and let \(F:K\to[0,\infty)\) be concave and upper semicontinuous. Put
\[
D:=\{z\in K\cap\mathbb Z^2:F(z)>0\},
\qquad
M(z):=F(z)^d\quad(z\in D),
\]
and assume \(D\neq\varnothing\). Fix \(z_0\in D\), and define its weighted planar halfspace depth by
\[
\Delta_M(z_0):=
\inf_{\substack{
Q\subseteq\mathbb R^2\text{ a proper closed halfspace}\\
z_0\in Q}}
\sum_{z\in D\cap Q}M(z).
\]

For \(q\in\{0,1,2\}\), let \(v_0,\ldots,v_q\in D\) be affinely independent, put
\[
T:=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_q\},
\]
and suppose \(z_0\in T\). If \(q=0\), define \(\kappa(T,z_0):=1\). If \(q>0\), define
\[
\kappa(T,z_0):=
\min_{\substack{
Q\subseteq\operatorname{aff}(T)\text{ a proper closed halfspace}\\
z_0\in Q}}
\#(T\cap Q\cap\mathbb Z^2).
\]

Prove or disprove that there always exist \(q\in\{0,1,2\}\) and such a lattice simplex \(T\) satisfying
\[
\min_{0\le i\le q}M(v_i)\,\kappa(T,z_0)
\ge \frac{11}{64}\,\Delta_M(z_0).
\]
